SC networks derived from deformation-based morphometry (DBM) were evaluated against three complementary biological benchmarks: age-related individual differences, fractional-anisotropy (FA)-based microstructural connectivity of regionally-specific thalamocortical connections, and Allen Human Brain Atlas gene expression. Each algorithm demonstrated underlying sensitivity to differing aspects of neurobiology: PCA and OPNMF showed the strongest associations between participant-level component weights and age. NMF, OPNMF, and \textit{k}-means showed greater spatial overlap between positive cortical SC and tractography-derived projections. ICA and PCA showed stronger correspondence between thalamic and cortical gene-expression profiles across the transcriptome, whereas NMF, OPNMF, and \textit{k}-means more often identified thalamic components with relatively high core-matrix gene expression. This study emphasizes that algorithmic constraints effectively act as biological priors and decomposition methods do not provide neutral compression of the data. We conclude that it is critical to consider whether the algorithmic objective matches the representational geometry of the neurobiology being studied. Overall, our findings suggest that SC studies should select and justify algorithms according to the biological question, explicitly considering whether their constraints favour distributed gradients, overlapping regional parts, or discrete clusters. Meanwhile, interpretations of SC findings could also be informed by the specific algorithmic constraints used to derive them.

papers.title: Spatially resolved single-cell atlas reveals cortical glial reactivity associated with regions of neuronal growth programs in both hemispheres after stroke
papers.authors: Kenwood M, Betz D, Guttierez-Kuri E, Derebery B, Rhoton P, Palavicinni JP, Ramirez DMO, Goldberg MP.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke recovery relies on structural remodeling of neuronal circuits in both the spared ipsilesional and contralesional cortices. RNA sequencing studies have identified distinct states of glial reactivity after stroke, but how these states are spatially organized at the single-cell level in relation to neuronal responses remains unknown. Consequently, it remains unclear which reactive states are lesion-restricted versus remote regions, such as the contralesional cortex, and how remote glial responses relate to the neuronal growth programs that support circuit repair. To address this, we used imaging-based subcellular spatial transcriptomics to profile ~650,000 cells across both hemispheres in male and female mice 7 days after cortical ischemic stroke, a critical timepoint for neuroplasticity. Reactive glial states differed significantly in their spatial organization from the lesion: scar-forming astrocytes and infiltrating pro-inflammatory myeloid cells were confined to the perilesional rim, whereas a reactive microglial state and a reactive astrocyte state extended into remote gray and white matter of the contralesional hemisphere. Mapping neuronal growth-associated gene expression across the entire cortex, we found substantial activation in both the perilesional and homotopic contralesional cortex, and these same regions showed significantly increased proportions of reactive microglia and astrocytes. Together, these findings identify spatially organized neuronal growth and glial activation states in both hemispheres after stroke and nominate regions for investigating spatial relationships between complex cell types and functional recovery.

papers.title: Mental replay rescales the subjective duration of past events via alpha and theta oscillations
papers.authors: Yue WWY, Mu Z, Yao Z, Chen D, Zhang Y, Liu J, Hu X.
papers.abstract: Human memory recall is flexible in time, allowing past events to be mentally replayed at variable speeds. However, it remains unclear whether temporally rescaled replay distorts the perceived duration of remembered events, and whether such distortion is tied to changes in the retrieved content. Here we instructed participants to mentally replay previously encoded naturalistic videos at compressed, expanded, or self-paced (free) speeds while recording scalp electroencephalography (EEG). Replaying an event at an expanded pace lengthened participants' subsequent judgments of its original duration relative to free and compressed replay, and the longer an event had been replayed, the longer it was judged to have lasted. Crucially, recalled memory content was unaffected, with gist accuracy and recalled detail comparable across speed conditions. During replay, alpha and theta power were reduced under compression, and both interacted with the speed instruction in predicting reported duration. Specifically, alpha power exhibited a stronger positive relationship with duration judgments under compressed replay than under free or expanded replay. Conversely, the relationship between theta power and reported duration was significantly more positive under expanded replay than under free or compressed replay. Neural pattern similarity between instructed and later spontaneous replay varied with replay speed, yet this reinstatement neither predicted reported duration nor mediated the oscillatory effects. These findings suggest that remembered duration is not read out from the amount of content retrieved but reconstructed at retrieval through oscillatory dynamics, decoupling the subjective scaling of time from the content of memory.

papers.title: Behavioral Markers of Essential Tremor Correlate with Distributed Alteration of Brain Functional Connectivity
papers.authors: Blondiaux Pirson F, Kim C, Colmant L, Lebrun L, Jankovski A, Gaëtan D, Dricot L, Bernard H, Crevecoeur F.
papers.abstract: Essential Tremor (ET) is a common motor disorder characterized by involuntary oscillations of the upper limbs during voluntary movement. Although increasing evidence implicates dysfunction of the cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathway, ET remains a diagnosis of exclusion, as no definitive biological marker currently exists. To better characterize ET, we recently hypothesized that impaired compensation of sensorimotor delays within the long-latency feedback pathways may generate the tremor-like oscillations observed in ET. This theory suggests that the mean spectral amplitude (MSA), derived from limb kinematics, may serve as a potential marker of ET. Here we investigated the relationship between MSA, standard clinical assessment (Fahn Tolosa Marin Tremor Rating Scale; FTM-TRS), and brain connectivity derived from resting state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI). Using seed-based analyses, we replicated previous findings of reduced functional connectivity between the dentate nucleus and components of the cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathway in ET patients compared with neurologically intact (NI) age-matched participants. Graph-theoretical analyses of whole-brain functional networks revealed distributed alterations in network topology across motor-related cortical and subcortical regions. Several graph metrics correlated with FTM-TRS scores and/or MSA, particularly within motor-related cortical and subcortical circuits, including the thalamus, basal ganglia, and cerebellum in ET. These findings indicate that ET is characterized by distributed alterations in functional brain networks beyond reduced connectivity of dentate nucleus and highlights MSA as a candidate quantitative marker linking altered brain connectivity to sensorimotor delay-driven tremor oscillations.

papers.title: Pre-stress functional brain connectivity is associated with subsequent anxiety during war-related stress
papers.authors: Boshnak N, Danan N, Keren H.
papers.abstract: Individuals exposed to major real-world stressors show markedly different psychological outcomes, but whether this heterogeneity is associated with pre-existing neural characteristics remains unclear because neuroimaging is rarely performed beforehand. We acquired resting-state fMRI in healthy adults before the unforeseen onset of war-related stress. Approximately 13 months later, during ongoing war-related stress, participants (n = 31) were assessed for anxiety, depressive symptoms, perceived stress and post-traumatic stress symptoms. Among 144 associations spanning 36 predefined corticolimbic and reward-related connections and four outcomes, lower baseline functional connectivity between the right nucleus accumbens and right amygdala was associated with greater subsequent anxiety. This association survived permutation-based family-wise error correction and adjustment for baseline depressive symptoms, age and sex. These findings provide preliminary prospective evidence that pre-existing functional organization of threat- and reward-related circuitry is associated with individual differences in anxiety during prolonged adversity.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-powered solutions for environmental sustainability in medical imaging: a scoping review.
papers.authors: Stogiannos N, Konstantinidis K, Ursprung S, Afat S, Kalari S, Karavasilis E, Herrmann J, Nikolaou K, Shelmerdine SC, Rockall A, Küstner T, Malamateniou C.
papers.abstract: Purpose Growing evidence shows that medical imaging has a substantial environmental impact. With the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical settings, it is important to explore how this technology may support environmental sustainability. Methods Literature searches were performed across eight databases (PubMed, Wiley Online Library, Embase, Web of Science platform, the Cochrane Library, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature Ultimate, Google Scholar, and MedRxiv) for the period January 2020-June 2026. Full-text sources in the English language were eligible for inclusion. The Joanna Briggs Institute checklists were employed for risk of bias assessment. All data were analyzed using a textual narrative synthesis. Results In total, 23 studies were deemed eligible for inclusion. The literature proposed that AI tools in medical imaging could be used to minimize energy consumption by optimizing patient scheduling, decreasing scanner idle times and workstation use, reducing computed tomography over-scanning, contrast agent usage, and radiation dose, harnessing low-field magnetic resonance imaging, and curtailing low-value imaging. However, AI technologies may also impact the environment in harmful ways. Conclusion Although AI-powered solutions hold promise for improving sustainability in medical imaging, the true environmental impact remains largely unexplored. Clinical significance The findings of this work further strengthen the dual role of AI adoption in medical imaging related to environmental sustainability.

papers.title: Constantin von Economo (1876-1931): cytoarchitectonic roots of modern network neuroscience.
papers.authors: Can F, Ozturk S, Sahin C, Yavuz AY.
papers.abstract: Constantin von Economo (1876-1931) is widely remembered for his seminal description of encephalitis lethargica, yet his broader contribution to cortical organization remains underappreciated. Beyond clinical neurology, von Economo and Georg Koskinas, a neurologist-psychiatrist, contributed to the broader cytoarchitectonic tradition by developing one of the most detailed architectonic frameworks of the human cerebral cortex, emphasizing laminar heterogeneity, regional transition, and structural specialization. These concepts can be reconsidered in relation to contemporary models of large-scale brain organization. In particular, cortical territories associated with von Economo's work, including the anterior insula and anterior cingulate region, are now recognized as key hubs in salience processing and contain the distinctive spindle-shaped neurons later termed von Economo neurons. Recent advances in connectomics, cortical gradient mapping, and laminar neuroimaging have renewed interest in the relationship between cortical microstructure and distributed functional networks. From this perspective, von Economo's work may be viewed not simply as a landmark in classical neuroanatomy, but as a historically important structural framework that can be reinterpreted in relation to modern ideas of structure-function coupling and network-level brain organization. This historical vignette revisits his life, scientific contributions, and enduring relevance to contemporary neuroscience and neurosurgical thinking.

papers.title: Stage 2 DBS without the wait: safety of same-day low-amplitude activation in a predominantly unilateral cohort.
papers.authors: Uppalapati SC, Qushair FA, Bentley JN, Thum J, Coleman J, McCullough B, Walker HC, Holland MT.
papers.abstract: Postoperative deep brain stimulation (DBS) programming schedules vary across institutions. At some centers, patients may experience an additional post-stage 2 interval without stimulation before the first outpatient programming visit. In the present study, authors evaluated the safety and operational feasibility of a standardized same-day low-amplitude activation protocol on the day of stage 2 DBS surgery compared with a historical delayed-programming pathway at their center. A retrospective single-center study was conducted using a propensity score-adjusted cohort of consecutive stage 2 DBS procedures performed between 2019 and 2024. Stage 1 denoted intracranial lead implantation, whereas stage 2 signified implantable pulse generator and extension wire insertion. Cases were divided into 2 cohorts, a historical delayed-activation group and an immediate-activation group (same day, conservative current ceilings, fixed contact selection, patient-programmer guardrails). The primary endpoint was the composite 6-month post-stage 2 adverse events rate (surgical, device, or stimulation related). The study included 561 consecutive procedures (273 delayed, 288 immediate); all had ≥ 6 months of follow-up. In the immediate cohort, the median interval from stage 1 to 2 was 3.0 days (Q1-Q3: 2.5-3.5 days), and the median interval from stage 1 to activation was also 3.0 days (2.5-3.5 days) because of same-day activation. In the delayed cohort, the median interval from stage 1 to 2 was 4.0 days (2-9 days) while the median from stage 1 to activation was 18.0 days (13-29, IQR 16 days). In propensity-adjusted analyses, immediate activation met the noninferiority criterion (upper 95% CI for risk difference < 5%); point estimates favored immediate activation. Unadjusted adverse event rates were 3.8% (11/288) for the immediate cohort versus 20.5% (56/273) for the delayed cohort (risk difference -16.7%, 95% CI -22.0 to -11.4). No device-related deaths occurred. Program stability was greater with immediate activation: at 6 months after the first full programming visit, retention of the settings established at that initial visit was 78.5% in the immediate cohort versus 54.9% in the delayed cohort, and the time to first change favored immediate activation (HR 2.28, 95% CI 1.89-2.73 for delayed vs immediate). Kaplan-Meier curves showed separation persisting to 36 months. In exploratory analyses, bilateral cases had higher short-term speech and altered mental status events, without differences in infection, hemorrhage, erosion, or lead migration. In a large consecutive, propensity score-adjusted cohort, same-day low-amplitude activation after stage 2 was at least as safe as delayed activation, coinciding with fewer early post-stage 2 adverse events and more durable programming. This protocol shortens the early no-stimulation gap and can be implemented in programs employing unilateral implantation. However, these findings do not establish the safety of immediate full therapeutic activation or comparative motor efficacy. Prospective multicenter evaluations should confirm durability, patient-reported outcomes, and resource use.

papers.title: Heterogenous Aging of Local Tissues Is a Major Contributor to the Age-Related Decline in Glycosaminoglycans and Fracture Toughness of Cortical Bone
papers.authors: Heath S, Ridoutt A, Reyes M, Ye K, Jiang JX, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Abstract Bone fragility fractures increase with age as bone toughness declines, potentially in part due to the loss of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). However, the mechanisms linking GAG depletion to bone quality remain unclear, partly due to the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of bone remodeling during aging. During bone remodeling, newly formed secondary osteons and older interstitial tissue are randomly distributed throughout the bone, each with distinct material properties. This microstructural heterogeneity adds complexity to studying age-related changes in bone quality that cannot be explained by donor age alone. This study hypothesized that the age-related decline in bulk bone fracture toughness originates from changes in local tissue GAGs with tissue aging and is amplified by an increasing proportion of old tissue relative to new tissue with advancing donor age. To test this, local tissues in human cortical bone samples across different ages and sexes were analyzed using Raman spectroscopy, DMMB, Alcian blue, histomorphometry, microcompression, and fracture toughness testing. The results showed that compositional and mechanical properties of local tissues changed significantly with tissue age, but not with donor age or sex. The volume fraction of old tissue as well as GAG heterogeneity (FWHM) increased significantly with donor age. Furthermore, age-related changes in bulk bone GAG content were strongly correlated with bone fracture toughness. These findings suggest that age-related loss of bone quality arises from the combined effects of tissue age-dependent deterioration in local properties and donor age–dependent accumulation of older tissue.

papers.title: CSF1R inhibition during cranial radiotherapy reshapes the immune environment and glial dynamics
papers.authors: Leter YM, Heijningen CLv, Tolboom ZJ, de Gooijer MC, Compter AC, Tellingen Ov, Schagen SB, Kuil LE.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Cranial radiotherapy (cRT) induces long-lasting alterations in the brain microenvironment, including changes in glial populations and loss of neurogenesis. Pharmacological depletion of microglia via colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R) inhibition has been proposed as a strategy to modulate radiation-induced neuroinflammation, but its effects on other glial populations remains incompletely understood. Methods: Nine-week-old male C57BL/6JRj mice (n=60) received either a CSF1R-inhibitor supplemented diet (pexidartinib, PLX3397) or a control diet prior to and continued for 10 days after fractionated CT-guided cRT (3x10 Gy, 30 Gy). Brain tissue was assessed at multiple time-points up to six months post cRT using immunohistochemistry for markers of microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and proliferating cells. Microglial identity and repopulation dynamics were assessed using IBA1, F4/80 and the homeostatic microglial marker P2RY12, complemented by morphometric analysis. Results: Pexidartinib alone resulted in partial microglial depletion, whereas its combination with cRT led to near-complete loss of P2RY12+ homeostatic microglia at early time points. After discontinuation of the diet this was accompanied by increased IBA1+;F4/80 high ;P2RY12 neg cell densities, consistent with replacement of the microglial niche by monocyte-derived cells. Over time, these cells exhibited gradual morphological adaptation but remained largely P2RY12 neg , indicating incomplete restoration of a homeostatic microglial phenotype. Combined treatment accelerated astrocytic reactivity compared to cRT alone and did not prevent cRT-induced loss of neurogenesis or OPCs. At later time points, partial OPC recovery was observed in selected regions in the combined treatment group. Conclusion: CSF1R inhibition during cRT profoundly alters the composition and temporal dynamics of the brain’s myeloid compartment, characterized by sustained loss of homeostatic microglia and replacement by monocyte-derived cells. Under these experimental conditions, microglial depletion did not mitigate key histopathological features associated with radiation-induced brain injury and was associated with accelerated astrocytic responses. These findings highlight the importance of timing, extent of depletion, and repopulation dynamics when considering microglia-targeting strategies in the context of cranial radiotherapy.

papers.title: Embedded True Proportional Navigation Guidance for a High-Dynamic Flight Vehicle: Real-Time MIL--HIL Validation
papers.authors: Khalifa AM, Safwat E, Mohamed MS, Hassan MA.
papers.abstract: Abstract Real-time embedded implementation can produce substantial differences between theterminal performance predicted by numerical simulation and that realized by aphysical guidance-and-control processor. This study characterizes that gap througha controlled Model-in-the-Loop (MIL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) evaluation ofterminal guidance for a high-dynamic flying vehicle. The two environments use thesame nonlinear six-degree-of-freedom plant, aerodynamic database, actuator model andconstraints, fixed-step plant solver, controller update rate, and paired seededvon K\'arm\'an turbulence realizations. True Proportional Navigation Guidance (TPNG)and a gain-scheduled modified PI autopilot with direct angular-rate damping areexecuted on an STM32F429 ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller at 50 Hz, while the nonlinearvehicle and disturbance models are propagated on a real-time target computer. Forthe four investigated disturbance realizations, the MIL configuration yields planarterminal errors of 0.027--0.460 m, whereas the HIL experiments yield137.6--1865.6 m. The embedded guidance-and-control computation requires an averageof 0.356 ms within the 20 ms control interval, corresponding to 1.78% execution-timeoccupancy. Thus, computational overload is excluded as the direct source of theobserved degradation. The results demonstrate that end-to-end implementation effects,including communication, task scheduling, sample alignment, and data representation,must be treated as part of the closed-loop guidance design. The current experimentsquantify their aggregate effect; causal attribution to individual mechanisms requirescontrolled delay and interface-ablation tests.

papers.title: Heterogeneous structural deficits across lower-leg agonist– antagonist muscle groups in children with cerebral palsy: a cross-sectional imaging study
papers.authors: Liu Z, Handsfield G.
papers.abstract: Abstract Structural alterations in skeletal muscle in cerebral palsy (CP) directly contribute to joint stiffness and impaired motor control, and govern the outcome of rehabilitative interventions. Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) has established architectural alterations in individual lower-limb muscles, but previous work has focused on a small subset of plantarflexor muscles in isolation, leaving their antagonists uncharacterized despite the reciprocal relationships between muscle pairs crossing the same joint. Because imbalance between such pairs is linked to gait limitations, characterizing whether architectural deficits in CP are proportional across agonist-antagonist pairs, or instead reflect atypical antagonist co-activation, is important. In this study, MRI and DTI data from nine children with CP (10.6 ± 2.2 years, GMFCS I–III) and nine age- and sex-matched typically developing controls from a previous study were used to assess muscle size and architecture in seven muscles and muscle groups in the leg. Volume and muscle length were determined from segmented surface meshes; physiological cross-sectional surfaces (PCSS), fascicle length, and angle were computed from DTI tractography; fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity were determined from diffusion tensor data. Normalized muscle volume of examined muscles was 38.8% lower in CP (g = − 2.71) and PCSS 27.2% lower (g = − 2.18, both p < 0.001). Volume (− 29.2% to − 41.3%) and muscle length (− 9.5% to − 12.2%, all p_fdr ≤ 0.004) were reduced in all four functional muscle groups of the leg, but the composition of that loss differed: dorsiflexor volume fell almost entirely through cross-sectional thinning (PCSS − 26.6%, fascicle length − 0.9%), the invertor almost entirely through fascicle shortening (− 3.4%, − 26.1%), and the plantarflexors through both (− 28.6%, − 31.5%). Plantarflexor:dorsiflexor and invertor:evertor size ratios did not differ, though the sample supports only effects of g ≥ 1.41. Individually, 33% of CP participants exceeded |z| > 2 on invertor:evertor ratio, driven by an undersized evertor, and volume z-scores exceeded |z| > 2 in 41% of muscle-participant combinations. Fascicle orientation was more uniformly aligned in tibialis anterior, and more dispersed in posterior soleus. Muscle deficits in CP were pervasive but heterogeneous, with clinically relevant imbalance emerging at the individual level despite proportional group averages.

papers.title: A Robust and Explainable Radiomics Pipeline for Small Multimodal Datasets to Predict Metastasis in Patients with Soft Tissue Sarcoma
papers.authors: Ubaldi L, Loi M, Banini M, Greto D, Arilli C, Casati M, Calusi S, Lizzi F, Marrazzo L, Zani M, Mangoni M, Ciccarone A, Livi L, Pallotta S, Retico A, Talamonti C.
papers.abstract: Preoperative radiotherapy and surgery are standard treatments for high-risk soft tissue sarcomas (STS), yet distant metastasis remains a significant clinical challenge. This study aims to develop a robust and interpretable multi-omics predictive model for metastasis, specifically addressing the limitations of small datasets. A retrospective analysis included 40 STS patients (23 with metastasis) treated with preoperative radiotherapy and surgery. Using PyRadiomics, 107 radiomic and dosiomic features were extracted from CT scans, dose distributions, and post-treatment contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI. A Logistic Regression classifier with L1 regularization was identified as optimal and rigorously evaluated via Stratified 5-Fold Cross-Validation repeated 100 times. Single-modality models demonstrated limited predictive performance, yielding mean AUC-ROC values of 0.52 for CT, 0.59 for dose distribution, and 0.62 for normalized MRI. Integrating these features into a combined multi-omics signature substantially improved the mean AUC-ROC to 0.75. Furthermore, model explainability was ensured using Log-Odds to identify key predictive features. Combining anatomical, dosiomic, and MRI-derived features significantly enhances the prediction of metastatic relapse in STS patients. This interpretable approach shows strong potential for guiding personalized clinical treatments.

papers.title: Evaluator Sex Modulates Stress Network Connectivity During Praise and Criticism
papers.authors: Elgendy A, Fandel H, Kogler LM, Blechert J, Reichenberger J, Derntl B, Kogler L.
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Social evaluation engages neural systems involved in stress and social information processing, with responses potentially depending on valence and evaluator characteristics. We investigated how valence and evaluator sex are reflected in functional connectivity (FC) within a meta-analytically derived stress network in women. (2) Methods: Sixty-three healthy women underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging while receiving praise, criticism, and neutral statements from unfamiliar male and female evaluators. Task-based FC was examined within the stress network. (3) Results: Participants reported less positive affect during criticism and more positive affect during praise, with both effects more pronounced for male than female evaluators. Stress-network FC differed by valence and evaluator sex. Both praise and criticism were associated with greater left insula-–right inferior frontal gyrus FC than neutral statements, while criticism was associated with greater left superior temporal gyrus–right amygdala FC than praise and neutral statements. Furthermore, evaluator sex modulated valence-dependent FC across several FCs involving prefrontal, striatal, medial temporal, thalamic, and posterior midline regions. Post-hoc comparisons revealed evaluator-sex differences in FC during criticism and praise, as well as opposing valence-dependent FC patterns between male and female evaluators. Exploratory analyses showed that associations between FC and self-related positive affect also depended on valence and evaluator sex. (4) Conclusions: Stress-network FC during the perception of praise and criticism delivered by strangers depended on evaluator sex. Importantly, stress-network involvement was not restricted to criticism, indicating that praise may also engage stress-related neural processes depending on social context, particularly when voiced by a male.

papers.title: A self-supervised reconstruction framework for segment-level detection of task-induced deviations in multi-channel EEG.
papers.authors: Saavedra LA, Quintero-Rincón A, Batatia H.
papers.abstract: Understanding brain activations during mental arithmetic tasks provides valuable insights into cognitive processing. However, analyses of the same electroencephalogram (EEG) dataset have produced inconsistent findings about the cortical regions involved, raising methodological questions about global signal treatment. Detecting task-related activations without pre-labelled datasets further remains challenging when supervised approaches are not applicable. This study presents a self-supervised framework for segment-based anomaly detection using deep learning to identify EEG signal outliers during mental arithmetic. Using a hierarchical variational auto-encoder, the study reconstructed multichannel EEG data segmented into 1-second intervals and trained exclusively on resting-state recordings. The study assessed reconstruction quality using multiple error metrics, including dynamic time warping, short-time Fourier transform loss, and signal-to-noise ratio, applied individually to channel segments. Outlier segments were detected based on the elevated reconstruction error relative to the resting baseline, using an unsupervised detection method. By analysing deviations at the segment level rather than treating the signal globally, the proposed framework captured transient cortical dynamics that may otherwise be obscured. The results demonstrated that these outlier segments exhibited distinct temporal and spectral characteristics, particularly within the delta, theta, and beta bands, and were most frequently located in peripheral electrodes such as Fp2, O1, O2, P3, and T6. Additionally, co-occurrence analysis uncovered functional patterns of simultaneous anomalies across specific electrode pairs and triplets, suggesting temporally dynamic and spatially distributed cognitive processes during arithmetic reasoning. Overall, the proposed framework provided a fine-grained temporal and spatial characterisation of EEG deviations during mental arithmetic and offers a methodological perspective that helped explain discrepancies in previously reported electrode-level findings.

papers.title: Interpretable embeddings of speech explain and enhance the brain encoding performance of audio models.
papers.authors: Shimizu R, Antonello RJ, Singh C, Mesgarani N.
papers.abstract: Speech foundation models (SFMs) are increasingly hailed as powerful computational models of human speech perception. However, since their representations are inherently black-box, it remains unclear what drives their alignment with brain responses. To remedy this, we built linear encoding models from six interpretable feature families: mel-spectrogram, Gabor filter bank features, speech presence, phonetic, syntactic, and semantic features, and contextualized embeddings from three state-of-the-art SFMs (Whisper, HuBERT, WavLM), quantifying electrocorticography (ECoG) response variance shared between feature classes. Variance-partitioning analyses revealed several key insights: First, the SFMs' alignment with the brain can be mostly accounted for by their ability to learn and encode simple interpretable speech features. Second, SFMs exhibit a systematic trade-off between encoding of brain-relevant low-level and high-level features across layers. Finally, our results show that SFMs learn brain-relevant semantics which cannot be accounted for by lower-level speech features, with this capacity increasing with model size and context length. Together, our findings suggest a principled approach to build more interpretable, accurate, and efficient encoding models of the brain by augmenting SFM embeddings with interpretable features.

papers.title: Clinical Reasoning: A 60-Year-Old Woman With Progressive Dysarthric Speech and Gait Instability.
papers.authors: Cao S, Du J, Wu T, Chang Y, Ren H, Qi X.
papers.abstract: A 60-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of progressive dysarthric speech and gait instability, accompanied by chronic constipation and significant weight loss. Neurologic examination revealed cerebellar ataxia and diffuse hyperreflexia with bilateral Hoffman signs, concurrent with significant orthostatic hypotension. Initial investigations demonstrated cerebellar, left temporal, and hippocampal atrophy on brain MRI, alongside an inflammatory CSF profile. Although routine commercial antibody panels for paraneoplastic and autoimmune cerebellar ataxias yielded negative results, tissue-based assays (TBAs) identified an intense anti-neural antibody tissue-staining pattern, providing objective evidence of an underlying autoimmune etiology. As the disease evolved, the emergence of bilateral blepharospasm and slow saccades provided further diagnostic clues. Specialized testing in a neuroimmunology laboratory ultimately revealed the diagnosis. Readers will navigate a stepwise clinical reasoning approach to subacute cerebellar ataxia, which illustrates the importance of recognizing systemic red flags and monitoring phenotypic evolution as well as how specialized testing based on positive TBA results can resolve diagnostic dilemmas when commercial assays remain unrevealing.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal fluid p62/SQSTM1 is associated with tau pathology, brain structural alterations, and cognitive impairment in adults without dementia.
papers.authors: Yao MY, Guo HH, Li QY, Huang LY, Tan L, Wang HF, Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe involvement of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) Sequestosome-1 (SQSTM1, commonly known as p62), an autophagy-related scaffold protein, in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis is not well established in human populations.ObjectiveTo investigate the associations of baseline CSF p62/SQSTM1 levels with cognitive function, AD biomarkers, brain structure, and incident dementia in non-demented individuals.MethodsWe included 557 dementia-free participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohort. Multivariate regression and interaction analyses examined associations of CSF p62/SQSTM1 with cognition, AD biomarkers, and brain volumes and their modification by age, sex, APOE genotype, and diagnostic status. Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses assessed dementia-free survival and incident dementia risk. Mediation analysis tested whether AD pathology and brain structure mediated the association between p62/SQSTM1 and cognition.ResultsElevated CSF p62/SQSTM1 levels correlated with poorer cognition, heightened tau pathology, increased sTREM2 and PGRN levels, and decreased whole-brain and fusiform gyrus volumes. Age modified p62/SQSTM1 associations with cognition and whole-brain volume. Subgroup analyses revealed that significant associations between p62/SQSTM1 and cognitive function (MMSE, MEM) were primarily observed in the middle-aged group. Longitudinal analyses further showed that participants in the highest quartile (Q4) exhibited an increased risk compared to the lowest (Q1) (HR = 1.78, 95% CI 1.16-2.73). Mediation analysis indicated that tau pathology and reduced brain volumes mediated the association between p62/SQSTM1 and cognition.ConclusionsHigher p62/SQSTM1 levels were associated with tau pathology and an elevated risk of AD. Tau-related pathological changes and brain structural alterations might be involved in the relationship between the p62/SQSTM1-related autophagy processes and cognition.

papers.title: Sex Differences in Stress Reactivity and Dementia Risk: A Pilot Study of Older Adults With Problematic or Frequent Cannabis Use.
papers.authors: Benitez A, Hickey R, Baker N, Thorn K, Watson Z, Nunn L, McRae-Clark A.
papers.journal: Journal of geriatric psychiatry and neurology
papers.abstract: IntroductionWe conducted a pilot study of older cannabis users with problematic or frequent (i.e. ≥4/7 days/week) use as a preliminary test of the hypothesis that compared to men, women would demonstrate greater stress reactivity and dementia risk.Methods47 participants ages 50-75 (55.3% male, 68% with cannabis use disorder) completed the Trier Social Stress Test, neuropsychological testing, 3T brain MRI, and blood draw.ResultsMen demonstrated: greater salivary cortisol, systolic blood pressure, and craving post-stress induction; worse memory and executive function; greater risk of heart disease or stroke and white matter hyperintensity volumes. There were no sex differences in Alzheimer's disease plasma biomarkers.ConclusionsAmong non-treatment-seeking older adults with problematic or frequent cannabis use, men may have greater risk for dementia due to stress reactivity and vascular risk factors. Future work must replicate and verify this unexpected sex difference and the specificity of these effects to cannabis use.

papers.title: Beyond the skull: Neuropsychological rehabilitation and Extended/Distributed Cognition.
papers.authors: Salas C, Rossi A, Rojas-Líbano D, Kausel L, Parada FJ.
papers.abstract: BackgroundNeuropsychological Rehabilitation has traditionally relied on models that conceptualize cognition primarily as a property of the individual brain. However, many established rehabilitation practices extend beyond the individual, involving cognitive artifacts (e.g., tools), modifications of the physical environment, and the coordinated contribution of other people. This creates a potential mismatch between how cognition is theoretically conceptualized and how rehabilitation is practiced.ObjectiveIn this conceptual article, we examine how Extended and Distributed Cognition may help address this discrepancy. Drawing on the historical work of Kurt Goldstein, contemporary cognitive science, and evidence-based rehabilitation practice, we distinguish Extended Cognition , which emphasizes how external resources can become integrated into an individual's cognitive processes, from Distributed Cognition , which examines how cognitive activity is organized across people, artifacts, and environments.ImplicationsWe argue that these perspectives broaden both the unit of analysis and the potential targets of rehabilitation: intervention may involve not only changing cognitive processes within the individual, but also introducing or reorganizing cognitive artifacts, modifying environments, and changing how other people interact with the person. Established practices including external compensatory strategies, communication partner training, environmental modification, and the coordinated organization of rehabilitation teams illustrate the clinical relevance of this perspective.ConclusionExtended and Distributed Cognition may therefore provide a complementary theoretical framework for understanding how cognition is supported and reorganized in everyday life after brain injury, helping to bridge the persistent gap between neuropsychological mechanisms and everyday functioning.

papers.title: Endothelial Cell-Expressed Prion Protein Prnd/Doppel Promotes Long-Term Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
papers.authors: Wang T, Kim S, Morales JE, McCarty JH.
papers.abstract: Background Recovery after ischemic stroke is limited by persistent cerebrovascular dysfunction, but the mechanisms regulating vascular repair remain poorly understood. Prnd (Prnd/Doppel) is a prion family protein expressed in the cerebrovascular endothelium during development. We tested the hypothesis that endothelial Prnd promotes vascular repair and functional recovery in the adult brain after stroke. Methods Using middle cerebral artery occlusion in mice, we compared wild-type and Prnd-null mice and evaluated endothelial-specific Prnd overexpression. Functional recovery was assessed by behavioral testing, while infarct volume, brain atrophy, vascular architecture, blood-brain barrier integrity, and macrophage/microglia infiltration were evaluated histologically. Vascular signaling and endothelial cell junctional proteins were examined mechanistically. Results Acute infarct volumes were comparable between wild-type and Prnd-null mice, indicating that Prnd does not substantially affect initial ischemic injury. During recovery, however, Prnd-null mice exhibited disrupted cerebrovascular architecture, increased blood-brain barrier disruption, greater brain atrophy, and increased macrophage/microglial infiltration. Conversely, endothelial Prnd overexpression improved long-term functional recovery without altering acute infarct size and was associated with enhanced blood-brain barrier integrity and vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, Prnd manipulation was associated with enhanced VEGF-A (vascular endothelial growth factor-A) signaling and increased endothelial cell tight junction protein expression. Conclusions Prnd is dispensable for acute ischemic injury but promotes cerebrovascular remodeling, blood-brain barrier restoration, and functional recovery after stroke. These findings identify endothelial Prnd as a regulator of poststroke vascular repair and a potential therapeutic target for enhancing long-term recovery.

papers.title: Intrinsic cellular persistent firing sustains hippocampal spatial representations during working memory.
papers.authors: Saber Marouf B, Reboreda A, Theissen F, Kaushik R, Sauvage M, Dityatev A, Yoshida M.
papers.abstract: Neurons are the fundamental units of cognitive processing. The prevailing view holds that neurons are input-output units that fire action potentials only upon receiving sufficient synaptic input. Here, we demonstrate that this may not be the sole operational mode of neurons in vivo during cognitive tasks, by showing that hippocampal place cells actively maintain firing and preserve spatial information through molecularly defined intrinsic mechanisms. Using in vitro and in vivo recordings coupled with molecular manipulation in mice, we reveal that hippocampal persistent firing during spatial working memory is supported by individual neurons via TRPC4 ion channels. Despite the general belief that persistent activity maintains working memory content, we demonstrate that persistent firing instead maintains immediate spatial representations, potentially supporting the encoding of spatial information to guide behavior. These findings position individual neurons as active contributors to information retention, extending their traditional role as passive input-output units and potentially broadening our understanding of neural computation.

papers.title: Electrophysiological properties of mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive.
papers.authors: Voerman S, Wang X, Wang X, Bosman LWJ, Broersen R, De Zeeuw CI.
papers.abstract: The neocortex has the largest volume, whereas the cerebellum houses the most neurons of the mammalian brain, underscoring paramount functions for interactions between them. Neocortical projections to the cerebellum involve both the mossy fibre and climbing fibre systems; mossy fibres find their origin predominantly in the pons, whereas the climbing fibres are relayed via subnuclei of the inferior olive (IO) that receive cortical input via the mesodiencephalic junction (MDJ). Given that climbing fibres regulate cerebellar plasticity in a timing-dependent manner, the MDJ-IO pathway probably contributes to both sensorimotor and cognitive learning. However, the physiological properties of IO-projecting MDJ neurons remain largely unknown. Here, we made targeted whole-cell recordings in brain slices of the mouse MDJ, separating IO- from non-IO-projecting neurons following retrograde tracing. We show that IO-projecting neurons are, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, highly spontaneously active and capable of high-frequency bursts of ≤350 Hz during current injections. Optogenetic stimulation shows that excitatory neocortical inputs to IO-projecting MDJ neurons can be integrated directly with excitatory inputs from the cerebellar nuclei. Moreover, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, IO-projecting MDJ neurons depolarize and repolarize quickly, and hyperpolarizing inputs consistently trigger rebound action potentials upon stimulus offset. This hyperpolarization is probably induced predominantly by inhibitory inputs from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey, which provide prominent bilateral inputs to MDJ neurons, as revealed by viral tracing in Gad2-Cre mice. Our results highlight how neocortical inputs to the MDJ can be transformed into diverse IO firing patterns and thereby contribute to the required specifics of cerebellar learning. KEY POINTS: The mesodiencephalic junction is an important brainstem region connecting the cerebral cortex with the cerebellum through its projection to the inferior olive, the sole source of the climbing fibres that drive cerebellar learning. We find that mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive represent a population of physiologically distinct neurons, capable of high firing frequencies and rebound activity following hyperpolarization. We reveal that mesodiencephalic junction neurons receive prominent excitatory inputs from neocortex and cerebellar nuclei, whereas their main inhibitory inputs are derived from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey. These findings shed light on how the activity of neurons in the mesodiencephalic junction can be regulated and how these neurons might influence activity in the inferior olive, and thereby cerebellar learning.

papers.title: LLM Detoxification via Transition-Aware Reward-Guided Representation Sampling.
papers.authors: Liu A, Xiao Y, Liu X, Huang Y, Liang S, Ying Z, Qu Y, Yang J, Yang Y, Tao D.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
papers.abstract: Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have showcased remarkable capabilities across diverse tasks, their susceptibility to producing harmful or toxic content underscores the urgent need for effective detoxification strategies to ensure their safe and ethical deployment. Test-time detoxification methods, which often involve directional steering within LLM representations during inference, have emerged as one of the most promising approaches due to their flexibility and minimal invasiveness. However, current approaches often rely on static or coarse interventions and suffer from imprecise guidance, largely due to their limited ability to model the transition process between toxic and non-toxic generations. To address this challenge, we propose Transition-Aware Reward-Guided Representation Sampling (TARGRS), a test-time detoxification framework that learns reward guidance directly over toxicity transitions in the latent representation space. Rather than relying on sparse toxic or non-toxic representations, our method performs progressive directional steering during generation to trace representation trajectories that span the transition from non-toxic to toxic states. Each trajectory is assigned toxicity scores, converting sparse annotations into dense, listwise supervision over fine-grained transitions. Based on this formulation, we train a token-level reward model whose predictions are explicitly transition-aware, enabling accurate control over representation sampling during inference. During exploration, steering along the toxicity direction constructs transition trajectories for reward learning; during inference, TARGRS performs coarse-to-fine sampling along the opposite, non-toxic direction to obtain detoxified representations. Specifically, coarse sampling first identifies the intervention required to reach non-toxic regions, followed by refinement to select the optimal representation with minimal perturbation. Comprehensive experiments on 10 widely used LLMs across the RealToxicityPrompts, BOLD, and AttaQ benchmarks demonstrate that TARGRS achieves consistent and strong detoxification performance, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. For instance, TARGRS reduces toxicity by up to 69.38 Additionally, TARGRS preserves the model's core capabilities with minimal impact. Furthermore, benefiting from intervention in the language decoder space, TARGRS can be seamlessly extended to Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), where it also demonstrates strong effectiveness, reducing toxicity by up to 64.23 https://github.com/xiaoyisong/TARGRS.

papers.title: Capturing Class Differences in EEG Connectivity with Class-discriminative Multivariate IMagInary Coherency (CMIMIC).
papers.authors: Vidaurre C, Aguirre J, Eguinoa R, San Martin R, Nolte G, Nikulin VV.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.abstract: A major challenge in EEG/MEG analysis is to characterize task-dependent functional connectivity in a way that is statistically robust and spatially interpretable, without prior source modeling or region-of-interest selection. Comparing connectivity between conditions is statistically demanding due to the high dimensionality of connectivity estimates, and spatial interpretability is compromised when effects are fragmented across many tests. Here, we introduce Class-discriminative Multivariate ImagInary Coherency (CMIMIC), a multivariate method that maximizes differences in the imaginary part of coherency between two classes, enabling the robust identification of condition-specific functional interactions while minimizing spurious connectivity due to volume conduction. We evaluated CMIMIC using simulations and resting-state EEG data of young and older adults in eyes open and eyes closed conditions. In simulations, CMIMIC recovered both the temporal dependencies between sources and their underlying generating networks. On empirical data, the CMIMIC-based pipeline consistently outperformed those based on traditional imaginary coherence (ImCoh) across classifiers and conditions. All methods performed better with eyes open than closed, but CMIMIC showed only a modest performance drop, in contrast to substantial losses for ImCoh. Feature stability analyses revealed that CMIMIC identifies a core set of informative sources largely shared across conditions, whereas ImCoh features were more condition-specific. CMIMIC also provides spatially interpretable source configurations that align well with known neurophysiological effects, offering a reliable, interpretable, and condition-robust approach for extracting discriminative connectivity features from EEG data.

papers.title: Longitudinal PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0 response assessment in vorasidenib-treated IDH-mutant gliomas: the VORAFET study.
papers.authors: Lombardi G, Bosio A, Librizzi G, Anglani M, Ius T, Caccese M, Padovan M, Cavallin F, Maccari M, Volpin F, Pasqualetti F, Simeone R, Parisi A, Salvalaggio A, Bellu L, Denaro L, Lonardi S, Preusser M, Albert NL, Cecchin D.
papers.abstract: Background Conventional MRI may not fully reflect the biological activity of vorasidenib. PET may detect treatment-related metabolic changes before structural changes become evident on MRI. We evaluated longitudinal PET and MRI changes in patients with IDH-mutant gliomas receiving vorasidenib. Methods VORAFET is a longitudinal study of adults with IDH-mutant gliomas treated with vorasidenib. Eligible patients had predominantly non-enhancing WHO grade 2 or 3 gliomas, had not received prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was longitudinal metabolic and structural imaging response according to PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0. Integrated [¹⁸F]FET PET/MRI was performed at baseline and every 3 months. Results Thirty-nine patients were included; at baseline, 23 and 29 had PET and MRI-measurable disease. As best response, PET RANO 1.0 identified 2 complete and 12 partial responses, yielding an ORR of 60.9%; median time to first response was 4.5 months (range 3-12 months). RANO 2.0 showed no complete or partial responses, whereas 5 patients achieved minor response at a median of 9 months (range 6-12 months). Progressive disease occurred in 6 of 39 patients (15.4%) according to PET RANO 1.0 and in 1 of 39 (2.6%) according to RANO 2.0. Patients with PET-PD more often had subtle contrast enhancement and showed higher baseline FLAIR volume, MTV, TBRmax, and TBRmean. Conclusions PET RANO 1.0 identified metabolic changes during vorasidenib treatment that were not always reflected by RANO 2.0 assessment. Longer follow-up is needed to clarify the relationship between PET metabolic changes and MRI findings and to determine their clinical significance.

papers.title: Delineating neural contributions to electroencephalogram-based speech decoding.
papers.authors: Sato M, Hatakeyama E, Inoue M, Kabe Y, Nobe S, Yoshida A, Yamamoto A, Kita Y, Shimizu M, Tomeoka K, Cohen MX, Sasai S.
papers.abstract: Objective . Speech brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have emerged as a pivotal technology in facilitating communication for individuals with speech impairments. Utilizing electroencephalography (EEG) for noninvasive speech BCIs offers an accessible and affordable solution, potentially benefiting a broader audience. However, EEG-based speech decoding remains controversial especially for overt speech, due to difficulties in separating speech-related neural activities from myoelectric potential artifacts generated during articulation. Moreover, because paradigms for collecting covert speech data are inherently less scalable than those for overt speech, whether the neural dynamics underlying EEG-based decoding of overt speech are also present during covert speech remains an open and practically important question.Approach . Here we aim to delineate the extent of the neural contributions to EEG-based speech decoding, and the degree to which the underlying neural dynamics are shared across overt and covert speech, by employing Explainable AI techniques to a convolutional neural network predicting spoken words based on signals obtained by ultra-high-density (uhd)-EEG.Main results . We found that electrode-wise contributions to the decoding cannot be explained by their mutual information with electromyography (EMG). Furthermore, contributing periods of speech to EEG-based decoding are distinct from those to decoding solely relying on EMG. Contributing periods of EEG-based decoding partially overlapped between overt and minimally overt speech. Notably, the denoising process successfully enhanced the decoding contribution from electrodes within speech-related brain areas for all speech conditions.Significance . Altogether, our findings support the idea that, with appropriate preprocessing, EEG becomes a valuable tool for decoding spoken words based on underlying neural activities.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注基于脑电的语音解码在多大程度上依赖真实神经活动，以及这种神经动态是否在出声与默读语音间共享。作者用可解释人工智能方法分析超高密度脑电训练的卷积神经网络，发现对解码有贡献的电极无法用其与肌电的互信息解释，且脑电解码所依赖的时段与仅靠肌电解码的时段不同；而出声和默读条件下，对脑电解码有贡献的信号时序存在明显重叠。去噪处理还能增强所有语音条件下语音相关脑区电极的解码贡献，提示脑电语音解码包含可分离于肌电伪迹的神经成分，并可能跨发声条件共享部分动态。

papers.title: Adaptive physics-inspired angular-spatial modeling for multi-shell diffusion MRI denoising.
papers.authors: Suchao M, Yuanjun W.
papers.abstract: Objective . Multi-shell diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) provides rich q-space information but is susceptible to noise, which can disrupt spatial anatomy, intra-shell directional relationships, inter-shell signal attenuation, and downstream diffusion parameter estimation. We aim to develop a denoising method that jointly preserves spatial structure, directional information, and shell-specific signal characteristics.Approach . We propose ASD-NCSM, an adaptive physics-inspired angular-spatial framework with a fixed three-stage alternating architecture. It combines intra-shell differential angular graph message passing with 2.5D spatial residual refinement. Noise-Conditioned Shell Modulation (NCSM) adaptively regulates angular updates according tob -value, spatial residual and angular dispersion proxies, and local gating. A Shell-wise Physical Attenuation and Angular Relation Consistency objective further constrains shell-wise signal fidelity, logarithmic attenuation, and local angular structure. The model was evaluated on Human Connectome Project multi-shell dMRI with simulated noise and independently acquired realin vivo brain dMRI data.Main results . Across five simulated noise levels from 2% to 10%, ASD-NCSM achieved the best overall DWI restoration among MPPCA, 1D-CNN, ECDM, SAN2N, and dMRI-Swin, with consistent subject-level advantages in PSNR, SSIM, and NRMSE. At 6% noise, principal-direction angular nRMSE was 32.68 ± 2.76%, with significant differences from all five baselines after Holm correction. ASD-NCSM also achieved the lowest mean MAE for FA, MD, AD, and RD, and the lowest relative MAE for ODI and FISO, while NDI was comparable to 1D-CNN and dMRI-Swin. For real data without noise-free references, Q-PEFT yielded the lowest angular cross-fit inconsistency (2.29 ± 0.10%) across three test subjects while maintaining limited signal and downstream-parameter changes.Significance. ASD-NCSM jointly preserves spatial continuity, directional geometry, and shell-level attenuation, providing balanced signal recovery, directional preservation, and downstream parameter stability for multi-shell dMRI denoising.

papers.title: Exact analytical PGSE signal for diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface using a spectral Laplacian formalism.
papers.authors: Canales-Rodríguez EJ, Tax CMW, Górriz JM, Jones DK, Thiran JP, Rafael-Patiño J.
papers.abstract: Objective. To derive an exact analytical expression for the diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) signal arising from diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface under finite rectangular pulsed-gradient spin-echo gradients, and to develop computationally efficient strategies for repeated model evaluations.Approach. The Bloch-Torrey equation was solved using a spectral matrix formalism of the Laplace operator in the eigenbasis of the cylindrical surface. The resulting signal is expressed as a product of non-commuting matrix exponentials and is valid for arbitrary rectangular gradient durations and separations, without approximations to the diffusion propagator or spin phase distribution. A reduced real spectral basis was introduced to decrease the dimensionality of the problem. Accelerated implementations based on Strang splitting and Gauss-Legendre quadrature were developed for repeated signal evaluations and computation of the spherical mean. The analytical signal was validated against Monte Carlo diffusion simulations.Main results. The exact formulation showed excellent agreement with Monte Carlo simulations over a wide range of cylinder radii and acquisition parameters. The spectral expansion converged rapidly with mode order, and the reduced basis substantially decreased computational cost without loss of accuracy. The accelerated implementations provided large additional speed-ups while retaining controllable errors relative to the exact solution.Significance. The proposed framework extends exact finite-pulse solutions of the Bloch-Torrey equation to diffusion confined to cylindrical surfaces and provides practical implementations for directional and orientationally averaged diffusion MRI signals. It therefore offers an approximation-free reference for assessing faster signal approximations and for applications requiring large numbers of model evaluations.

papers.title: A case study of early-emerging prosopometamorphopsia.
papers.authors: Fortner S, Mello A, Stehr D, Kodiweera C, Jung H, Kerns S, Bujarski K, Wager T, Duchaine B.
papers.abstract: Prosopometamorphopsia (PMO) is a rare perceptual disorder characterized by facial distortions. This report presents the first thorough study of early-emerging PMO. Zed, who was 15 years old when first tested, has experienced lifelong, dynamic facial distortions in which features move, droop, disappear, expand, and rotate. He also experiences identity misrecognitions, perceiving familiar faces as strangers and vice versa. Behavioural assessments indicate Zed's distortions persist across different viewpoints, visual field positions, picture-plane orientations, and visual angles. Neuropsychological testing revealed deficits in face identity recognition, yet Zed performed normally on tests requiring fine-grained perception of facial age and sex. While structural MRI showed no lesions, MRI revealed reduced face-selectivity in right posterior face-selective areas, and diffusion tensor imaging indicated lower white matter integrity in the left inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus. This case offers novel insights into the manifestations of early-emerging PMO, its co-occurrence with other face-processing disorders, and its underlying neural correlates.

papers.title: In-context learning as a retraining-free paradigm for constitutive modeling.
papers.authors: Li L, Li Z, Li S, Zhan K, Gao H, Chen CQ, Yang L.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Constitutive modeling is fundamental to computational solid mechanics, yet most existing approaches remain material-specific and require retraining or recalibration when materials change. Here we introduce In-Context Modeling (ICM), a retraining-free paradigm for constitutive modeling that infers constitutive behavior from physical context rather than material-specific optimization. Using hyperelasticity as a testbed, we demonstrate that ICM can be trained once on equilibrium deformation fields spanning diverse materials, geometries, and boundary conditions, enforcing physical equilibrium without stress labels. After training, the same model can be directly deployed on previously unseen hyperelastic materials without retraining. At inference, ICM treats a small set of nonuniform strain fields as physical context to generate constitutive response in a single forward pass. Numerical benchmarks and experimental validation demonstrate accurate stress prediction across out-of-distribution materials and boundary-value problems, together with substantial reductions in deployment cost compared with per-material learning approaches. These results establish in-context learning as a retraining-free paradigm for constitutive modeling, particularly valuable for heterogeneous biological tissues such as the brain, and suggest a pathway toward foundation models for computational mechanics.

papers.title: Hierarchical NiCoP thistles: a promising electrocatalyst for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction.
papers.authors: Lamba N, Meher SK.
papers.abstract: The rational development of efficient and durable electrocatalysts for the alkaline OER is indispensable for the advancement of next-generation energy-conversion and energy-storage technologies. Herein, a slow-growth kinetics favoured synthetic strategy sequenced by solid-state phosphorization was employed to fabricate a synergistically favourable bimetallic NiCoP electrocatalyst possessing a hierarchical thistle flower-like microarchitecture. The physicochemical characteristics of the resultant NiCoP exhibit significant mesoporosity, interconnected hierarchical mesopore channels, small crystallite dimensions, a specific surface area of 52.9 m2 g-1 , multivalent Ni/Co redox centers and catalytically active phosphide nanodomains along with amorphous phosphate layers constituting phosphide/phosphate heterointerfaces on the surface of NiCoP thistles. The electrochemical investigations reveal highly reversible redox characteristics, elevated electrocatalytically active sites, a substantial electrochemically active surface area (357 cm2 , corresponding to a C dl value of 14.3 mF or 72.9 mF cm-2 ), a low onset potential and favourable interfacial charge-transfer kinetics toward the alkaline OER. Consequently, the NiCoP electrocatalyst displays remarkable OER activity with an overpotential of 285 ± 2.65 mV (at 10 mA cm-2 ), a Tafel slope of 113 mV dec-1 , a low charge-transfer resistance of 4.6 Ω and an apparent turnover frequency of 6.72 s-1 , along with excellent operational durability over 18 h amperometric i -t and 24 h chronopotentiometric operations. The superior electrocatalytic efficacy is attributed to the electrochemical synergism between multivalent Ni and Co species, abundant catalytically accessible low-dimensional phosphide active sites, and hierarchically interconnected mesoporous channels that collectively facilitate electrolyte-ion diffusion, rapid charge transport, enhanced OH- adsorption kinetics, and efficient release of evolved oxygen bubbles during prolonged OER operation. Furthermore, the robust mesoporous microstructural framework effectively mitigates electrochemical degradation and stabilizes the partially reconstructed catalytically active phase under anodic OER conditions. Overall, the present study establishes hierarchically architectured and synergistically favourable bimetallic phosphides as promising non-noble alternatives to conventional OER electrocatalysts for advanced alkaline oxygen electrochemistry and sustainable energy technologies.

papers.title: TNF signaling at the brain-heart interface: neurovascular injury and cardiovascular vulnerability in epilepsy.
papers.authors: Sha A, Wu Y, Peng HR, Jin B, He B, Zhao ZK, He F, Cao Y, Gan L.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is increasingly viewed as a systemic disorder in which recurrent seizures intersect with vascular, autonomic, respiratory, and cardiac processes to influence cardiovascular vulnerability. Seizure-related neuroinflammation involves multiple interacting mediator pathways, including HMGB1/TLR4-RAGE signaling, inflammasome/IL-1β activation, IL-6/IL-6R-gp130 signaling, albumin/TGF-β signaling following blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α)/TNF receptor (TNFR) signaling. Within this inflammatory network, TNF/TNFR signaling represents a mechanistically distinct and translationally relevant framework for examining how immune activation intersects with endothelial-barrier dysfunction, neurovascular unit injury, autonomic disturbance, inflammatory communication across neural and cardiovascular compartments, and cardiac vulnerability. This review integrates direct evidence from epilepsy studies with mechanistic insights from related experimental studies of BBB injury, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, cardioprotection, and brain-heart communication. TNF biology is determined by ligand form, receptor subtype, cellular compartment, and disease context. Soluble TNF preferentially engages TNFR1-associated inflammatory and injury-amplifying pathways, whereas transmembrane TNF/TNFR2 signaling may support regulatory or reparative responses in selected settings. In epilepsy, seizure-associated inflammation, BBB dysfunction, glial activation, and autonomic imbalance may interact to increase susceptibility to arrhythmogenic stress, myocardial injury, adverse cardiac remodeling, and cardiorespiratory instability relevant to sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP). However, epilepsy-specific evidence directly linking TNF/TNFR signaling to cardiovascular outcomes remains limited, and many mechanistic connections currently rely on converging evidence from neurovascular and cardiovascular research. Future studies should integrate compartment-resolved inflammatory profiling with autonomic, respiratory, electrocardiographic, and cardiac phenotyping to distinguish inflammatory signatures of disease severity from modifiable contributors to cardiovascular risk. Such approaches may enable phenotype-specific strategies to better understand and ultimately mitigate the brain-heart consequences of epilepsy.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates chronic pain and comorbid depression through Gut-Metabolite-Brain axis remodeling to restore mPFC Glu/GABA balance.
papers.authors: Li S, Huang J, Lin D, Luo D, Fu W, Liu J.
papers.abstract: The comorbidity of chronic pain and depression is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder involving dysregulated microbiota-gut-brain communication. Although electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for both pain and depression, the mechanisms linking peripheral microbial-metabolic remodeling to central neurotransmitter regulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach in a spared nerve injury (SNI) rat model to investigate the gut-metabolite-brain mechanisms underlying EA's efficacy. EA significantly alleviated mechanical hypersensitivity and depressive-like behaviors while restoring mPFC Glu/GABA balance, accompanied by normalization of the glutamate transporter EAAT2 and the GABA-synthesizing enzyme GAD67. Metagenomic analysis showed that EA remodeled the gut microbial ecosystem by increasing microbial diversity, suppressing opportunistic pathobionts, including Bacillus cereus, Alistipes onderdonkii, while enriching SCFA-associated genera, including Butyricimonas and Romboutsia. These alterations were accompanied by coordinated remodeling of amino acid and butanoate metabolism. Correlation network analysis identified Pipecolic acid as a central metabolic node linking gut microbial alterations with mPFC GABAergic neurotransmission and behavioral recovery. Although individual bacterial genera did not significantly mediate its restoration, causal mediation analysis demonstrated that the Pipecolic acid-GABA axis significantly mediated improvements in both mechanical allodynia and anhedonia, supporting Pipecolic acid as a functional metabolic hub linking peripheral metabolic remodeling to central GABAergic regulation. Collectively, these findings identify peripheral metabolic remodeling as a key mechanistic interface through which EA coordinates gut microbial ecology and central neurochemical homeostasis, providing a systems-level framework for understanding the therapeutic mechanisms of acupuncture in pain-depression comorbidity.

papers.title: A Crh-defined insular cortex-brainstem-thalamic circuit regulates anxiety-related behavioral states.
papers.authors: An ZY, Liu MZ, Yuan JY, Song MY, Yang XM, He Y, Mu D.
papers.abstract: Anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent and debilitating psychiatric conditions, yet the neural circuits underlying anxiety-related states remain incompletely understood. Here we identify a cortical-brainstem-thalamic pathway in which Crh-expressing neurons in the anterior and middle insular cortex (a/mIC) engage the parabrachial nucleus (PBN), which in turn recruits the posterior paraventricular thalamic nucleus (pPVT) to contribute to anxiety-related behavior. Single-cell calcium imaging reveals that the predator odorant 2-methyl-2-thiazoline (2-MT) and footshock recruit partially overlapping populations of PBN-projecting a/mIC neurons; neurons activated by both stimuli exhibit increased activity during open-arm approach in the elevated plus maze. Exposure to 2-MT increases corticotropin-releasing factor (CRF) signals in the PBN, where CRF enhances PBN neuronal excitability and CRF receptor 1 (CRFR1) signaling facilitates a/mIC-terminal-evoked firing. Inhibition of Crh⁺ a/mIC-PBN projections, Crh knockdown in the a/mIC, or blockade of CRFR1 signaling within the PBN attenuates 2-MT-induced anxiety-like behavior. Human neuroimaging further reveals stronger functional coupling within a putative homologous aIC-PBN-pPVT network in individuals with anxiety symptoms, and the strength of this coupling correlates with anxiety severity. Together, these findings define a molecularly specified insular circuit that contributes to anxiety-related behavioral states.

papers.title: Laser-Fabricated Ordered Tri-Level Hemispherical Microstructures for Flexible Pressure Sensors with Ultrahigh Sensitivity over a Wide Linear Range.
papers.authors: Wu L, Zhang Y, Lin Y, Xiong X, Lin W, Zhou W, Qiao Y.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of embodied intelligence and soft robotics demands flexible pressure sensors that simultaneously achieve high sensitivity, a broad linear response range, and excellent long-term stability. However, the inherent compression hardening effect of soft materials imposes a fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and linear range, severely limiting their practical applicability in complex dynamic environments. Inspired by the hierarchical tactile perception mechanism of human skin and guided by Archard's contact theory, we propose a piezoresistive sensor incorporating an ordered tri-level hemispherical microstructure array. The sensing layer, composed of a graphite powder/multiwalled carbon nanotubes/polydimethylsiloxane (GP/MWCNT/PDMS) conductive composite, is patterned via a rapid, scalable, and mask-free three-dimensional (3D) dynamic focusing laser processing technique. Finite element analysis (FEA) guides the optimization of geometric parameters, confirming that the tri-level configuration exhibits the highest compressibility and the greatest rate of contact area change among single-level, dual-level, and tri-level designs. The sensor operates through a graded deformation mechanism: under low pressure, the smallest hemispheres deform first to rapidly increase contact area, under medium pressure, the intermediate hemispheres engage to sustain sensitivity; under high pressure, the largest hemispheres provide structural support, ensuring continuous contact area expansion over a broad pressure range. Consequently, the sensor achieves an ultrahigh sensitivity of 12.8 kPa-1 over a wide linear range of 0-369 kPa (R2 = 0.998), with fast response/recovery times (20/21 ms) and excellent cycling stability (15,000 cycles). Beyond single-point sensing, we further construct a 4 × 4 sensor array that successfully discriminates spatial pressure distributions, as demonstrated by recognition of "M"-shaped and "U"-shaped loading modules. Practical applications include precise monitoring of finger joint bending angles and real-time plantar pressure distribution during walking and running, and shape-resolved tactile imaging, highlighting its great promise for applications in embodied intelligence, wearable health monitoring, human-machine interaction, and related fields.

papers.title: Vulnerability of the Brainstem-Cerebellar Respiratory Network in Extreme Prematurity.
papers.authors: Gauda EB, Williams E, Prabhakar N, Cizmeci M.
papers.abstract: Survival of extremely preterm infants has significantly improved over the past decades, shifting critical stages of respiratory and brain development into the extrauterine environment. This transition exposes the vulnerable preterm infant to abrupt changes in oxygen tension, intermittent hypoxemia, inflammation, and oxidative stress, which contribute to maldevelopment of the structure and function of immature organs, including the brain and brainstem, with short- and long-term adverse consequences. This review examines how adverse intrauterine and extrauterine exposures during critical developmental periods in extremely low gestational age neonates (ELGANs) born <28 weeks of gestation disrupt the structure and function of key components of the central respiratory network, supporting epidemiological evidence that premature infants have a substantially increased risk of sudden unexpected infant death (SUID) during the first year of life and sleep disordered breathing across the lifespan. ELGANs are born during a period of rapid brainstem and cerebellar development, increasing the vulnerability of these regions to oxidative and inflammatory injury that can cause direct tissue damage and dysmaturation. The medullary serotonergic network and cerebellar fastigial nucleus regulate cardiorespiratory responses at rest and during progressive hypoxia and hypercapnia. We propose that adverse intrauterine and extrauterine exposures during critical developmental windows damage the macro- and microstructures, neurochemistry of these regions, impair protective respiratory responses, and mechanistically contribute to the two- to threefold higher risk of SUID in ELGANs than in term infants. We review fetal neuroprotective responses to hypoxia; the mechanisms and vulnerability of brain injury in ELGANs; the development and intrinsic hypoxic chemosensitivity of central respiratory control; and brainstem and cerebellar dysmaturation. Together, this framework provides a biological basis linking extreme prematurity to impaired ventilatory control, disordered breathing, and increased vulnerability to sudden death during infancy and beyond.

papers.title: Repeated cocaine exposure and prolonged withdrawal drive morphological and molecular remodeling of hippocampal microglia in response to acute stress.
papers.authors: Mottarlini F, Miglioranza P, Zweistra EE, Parolaro S, Rizzi B, Da Dalt L, Moregola A, Norata GD, Caffino L, Fumagalli F.
papers.abstract: Repeated cocaine exposure during adolescence disrupts physiological brain maturation, inducing persistent neuroplastic adaptations that evolve throughout withdrawal. Because stressful experiences are among the most powerful triggers of relapse during abstinence, uncovering how cocaine withdrawal affects the neurobiological mechanisms of stress adaptation and emotional responses remains a critical challenge in addiction research. Here, we investigated whether prolonged withdrawal from adolescent cocaine exposure alters hippocampal neuroimmune responses to a subsequent stressful challenge. Male adolescent rats received cocaine (5mg/kg, s.c.) for 15 consecutive days followed by a 14-day withdrawal period. At the end of withdrawal, animals were exposed to acute restraint stress (ARS) and assessed for anxiety-like behavior. Our findings demonstrate that prolonged withdrawal from adolescent cocaine exposure impairs emotional adaptation to acute stress, accompanied by persistent neuroimmune dysregulation across both central and peripheral compartments. Within the hippocampus, a key limbic hub integrating contextual drug-associated memories, emotional processes and stress adaptation, cocaine withdrawal altered microglial homeostasis while reshaping stress-responsive neuro-glial communication pathways in a region-specific manner, particularly the CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis within the ventral subregion. Stress exposure revealed distinct microglial and synaptic, structural and molecular, adaptations in cocaine-withdrawn rats, characterized by the recruitment of a surveillance-like microglial phenotype and an altered pattern of neuron-microglia communication. These central alterations were accompanied by peripheral lymphopenia and a blunted lymphocyte response to the challenge. Together, these findings support the existence of a latent neuroimmune vulnerability induced by cocaine withdrawal that becomes apparent under challenging conditions potentially driving maladaptive stress processing.
