papers.title: Multiscale DCE-BOLD MRI reveals vascular uncoupling patterns for IDH genotyping in adult glioma: A prospective habitat-based study.
papers.authors: Song D, Wang Y, Li B, Liu Y, Guo P, Mi Y, Qu H, Nie S, Jiang Y, Song Y, Fan G, Lin Z, Chang M.
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.abstract: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-wildtype gliomas exhibit heterogeneous vascular dysfunction, but whole-tumor analyses may obscure regional variation in vascular permeability and functional reserve. We developed a multiscale habitat framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-derived volume transfer constant (Ktrans) and resting-state blood oxygen level-dependent functional MRI (rs-BOLD-fMRI)-derived relative cerebrovascular reactivity (rCVR), including a 10-mm peritumoral margin, for noninvasive IDH genotyping. This prospective single-center cohort included 132 patients (52 IDH-mutant and 80 IDH-wildtype), divided chronologically into training (n = 92) and internal test (n = 40) cohorts. Gaussian mixture modeling partitioned the continuous joint Ktrans-rCVR distribution into three overlapping imaging-defined intratumoral subregions; the anatomically defined peritumoral region was analyzed separately. The Habitat-Peri10mm model yielded the highest internal test area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) point estimate of 0.914 (95% confidence interval, 0.831-0.997), compared with 0.854 for the Habitat model and 0.753 for the Whole-tumor model. Pairwise DeLong tests were nonsignificant (p = 0.173 and 0.054, respectively). A Subregion 2 Ktrans first-order Entropy feature ranked highest in the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis and correlated with Ki-67 (r = 0.57) and microvessel density (r = 0.27). The habitat-derived intratumoral heterogeneity score was higher in IDH-wildtype than IDH-mutant tumors (0.79 vs. 0.40, p < 0.001; AUC = 0.824), although grade imbalance limited IDH-specific interpretation. This DCE-BOLD multiscale habitat framework characterizes IDH-associated patterns of vascular heterogeneity and shows potential for noninvasive IDH genotyping.

papers.title: Robust joint estimation of regional brain activity and inter-regional source covariance via full-structure covariance learning.
papers.authors: Cai C, Deng W, Zhao K, Ke H, Wu W, Nagarajan SS.
papers.abstract: Uncovering the mechanisms underlying cognition and brain disorders requires accurate regional source imaging and reliable characterization of inter-regional statistical dependencies. Traditional methods typically follow a two-stage pipeline that first performs source imaging and then calculates inter-regional dependence measures separately. Such a decoupled framework can propagate source-reconstruction errors to covariance-based network analyses, leading to biased source localization and distorted dependency patterns. To address these limitations, we propose a joint estimation method for regional brain source activity and source covariance via full-structure covariance learning, termed Joint Activity-Covariance Estimation via Full-Structure Covariance Learning (JAC-FS). JAC-FS constructs a Gaussian probabilistic model at the brain-region level and employs a full-structure source covariance matrix to represent regional source variance and inter-regional dependencies. In this covariance representation, diagonal entries encode marginal regional source variance, whereas off-diagonal entries quantify symmetric zero-lag covariance-based dependencies. These estimates are statistical associations and do not by themselves establish direct, directional, or causal physiological communication. A median-weighted covariance statistic suppresses high-energy artifacts, and convex surrogate optimization provides closed-form updates for source activity and source covariance. In addition, constrained noise estimation with diagonal floor protection, low-rank correlation constraints, and phased damped updates limits signal absorption and spurious covariance structure. Simulations showed that JAC-FS outperformed conventional algorithms in regional source localization, temporal recovery, source-covariance recovery against the simulated ground truth, and recovery of predefined short- and long-range covariance edges. In real MEG analyses, JAC-FS produced focal evoked source distributions and representative time courses together with evoked source-covariance patterns. These results establish JAC-FS as a unified framework for regional source imaging and zero-lag source covariance estimation.

papers.title: Multidimensional EEG Feature Fusion and Interpretable Machine Learning for Identifying Cognitive Impairment in Depression.
papers.authors: Bin Zhou, Wang X, Wang T, Shi J, Huang B, Zhang Y, Li G, Cao X.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment is a clinically important dimension of depression that remains insufficiently assessed using objective measures. Existing assessments largely rely on scale-based screening, whereas EEG-based computational studies are often limited by the use of single-feature representations, window-level data leakage, class imbalance, and limited interpretability. In this study, we developed an interpretable subject-level machine learning framework based on resting-state EEG to identify cognitive impairment in patients with depression and investigate potential electrophysiological markers. A total of 142 patients with depression were categorized as having depression without cognitive impairment (D-NCI) or depression with cognitive impairment (D-CI) based on their Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores. Using 16-channel resting-state EEG recordings, phase lag index, relative power, and fuzzy entropy features were extracted across five frequency bands to characterize functional connectivity, spectral activity, and signal complexity. Five-fold stratified cross-validation at the subject level, ensemble undersampling, and a two-stage SHAP-based feature selection strategy implemented within the training procedure were used to reduce the risk of data leakage, mitigate class imbalance, and improve interpretability. The final model achieved an accuracy of 80.39 ± 7.91%, sensitivity of 83.29 ± 8.30%, specificity of 73.89 ± 15.75%, F1-score of 85.67 ± 5.91%, and AUC of 83.74 ± 9.63%. The retained features were mainly distributed in the beta1 and beta2 bands and reflected alterations in interregional phase synchronization, local oscillatory activity, and signal complexity. These findings support the feasibility of an interpretable EEG-based framework with subject-level data partitioning to assist in identifying cognitive impairment in depression.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Classification Models for Cognitive Function in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease Based on MRE and Machine Learning.
papers.authors: Chen X, Kang Y, Yang M, Zhu X, Zhang J, Huang Y, Yuan J, Tan W.
papers.abstract: Early identification of cognitive impairment is crucial for preventing dementia progression. Magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), combined with traditional imaging markers, provides a novel dimension for cognitive assessment in cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD). To develop machine learning-based classification models for cognitive function in CSVD patients by integrating MRE brain mechanical parameters, white matter hyperintensity burden, and clinical indicators, and to analyze sex differences in model performance. 100 CSVD subjects underwent MRI scanning including FLAIR for white matter hyperintensities, T1WI for hippocampal atrophy assessment, and MRE for measuring brain mechanical properties across 12 regions. Data were split 8:2 (train:test, stratified); within the training set only, candidate features were ranked by Spearman correlation with MoCA score and a final 13-feature subset was selected by Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). Subjects were stratified by sex (all-sex: n=100; male: n=42; female: n=58), and 10 machine learning models were compared for each group using 5-fold cross-validation (cvAUC), with SHAP analysis used to interpret feature importance. A 13-feature subset was identified, predominantly MRE stiffness parameters. Naive Bayes performed best in the overall cohort (cvAUC=0.704, 95% CI 0.652-0.756), Extra Trees in males (cvAUC=0.828, 95% CI 0.635-1.000), and XGBoost in females (cvAUC=0.617, 95% CI 0.370-0.863). The female subgroup's confidence interval spanned chance-level discrimination. Using the same feature set, classification accuracy was numerically higher in males than in females. SHAP analysis showed atrophy and white matter hyperintensity burden markers dominated in males, whereas right angular gyrus stiffness and other MRE parameters dominated in the overall cohort and in females. Using an identical feature set and modeling pipeline, machine learning models integrating MRE showed markedly different performance between sexes, indicating that a single sex-agnostic model does not generalize equally to men and women. This performance gap, together with divergent SHAP patterns, underscores the need for sex-stratified modeling in MRE-based cognitive screening for CSVD.

papers.title: Brain systems supporting the narrative self and psychopathology.
papers.authors: Steward T, Tashjian SM, Kung PH, Felmingham KL, Ney L, Davey CG, Harrison BJ.
papers.abstract: Disturbances in the narrative self are implicated across psychiatric disorders, with abnormalities in the neural systems supporting its generation and regulation constituting a transdiagnostic risk factor for mental illness. This review highlights how alterations in these brain systems underlie prevalent clinical features, including diminished, rigid, and sustained negative beliefs within the narrative self. The narrative self is framed as a higher-order construct that emerges from multiple systems, with reward, punishment, and motivational signals biasing which experiences are encoded as self-defining and which self-beliefs are reinforced over time. We discuss recent evidence demonstrating how the narrative self is supported by distributed brain networks in which subcortical inputs from the basal forebrain, habenula and mediodorsal thalamus modulate default mode network activity, with the salience, frontoparietal, cingulo-opercular, and hippocampal-parahippocampal networks regulating how self-beliefs are established or updated. Adolescence is emphasized as a developmental period uniquely vulnerable to disturbances in the formation of a coherent, flexible narrative self, wherein asynchronous subcortical and cortical development and pubertal changes interact to confer risk for diminished and rigid self-beliefs. Belief-updating tasks, hierarchical computational models, and ecological momentary assessment are proposed as approaches to quantify how self-beliefs form and shift across time, linking neural signatures of the narrative self to momentary variability. We propose that treating the narrative self as a primary level of explanation for psychopathology positions it as a testable target for future neuroimaging research, providing a clearer bridge from self-referential cognition to interventions in daily life.

papers.title: Association of Neighborhood Opportunity and Abdominal Obesity with Brain Development and Cognitive Function in Adolescents: A Prospective Cohort Analysis.
papers.authors: Cadenas-Sanchez C, Nascimento-Ferreira MV, Virostko J, Savitz SI, Oliveira TA, De Moraes ACF.
papers.abstract: To investigate the longitudinal associations between neighborhood opportunity and brain structure and cognitive performance among adolescents, and to explore whether these associations differ by sex, maturational status, race/ethnicity, and abdominal obesity trajectory. Prospective data from ABCD Study participants with complete baseline data (n = 9,375; ages 9-10 years, 47% girls; 21 U.S. sites), followed from 2016-2018 to 2020-2022, were analyzed; outcome-specific analytic samples were 9,121 at 2 years and 3,048 at 4 years. Neighborhood opportunity was measured with the Childhood Opportunity Index (COI) 2.0, subcortical volumes with MRI, and cognition with the NIH Toolbox. Mixed-effects models adjusted for baseline outcome, age, sex, race/ethnicity, population density, and time-varying waist-to-height ratio; sex differences were tested directly. Mean (SD) baseline age was 9.9 (0.6) years, and 54.4% were White. Very-high versus very-low COI was associated with larger subcortical volumes (e.g., amygdala 25.33 mm³; 95% CI 11.98 to 38.69, at 2 years) and higher memory scores at 2 years (5.56 points; 4.55 to 6.57) and 4 years (6.68; 4.44 to 8.91). Associations with the amygdala (2 years) and caudate (both waves) were larger in girls than in boys; cognitive associations did not differ by sex. Four-year estimates were similar to or larger than 2-year estimates; loss of statistical significance reflected the smaller 4-year samples. Adolescents from socioeconomically disadvantaged environments experience significant disparities in brain structure and cognitive function, which exploratory stratified analyses suggesting variation by abdominal obesity and sociodemographic characteristics including sex, maturational status, and race/ethnicity.

papers.title: Greater Lifetime Alcohol Consumption is Associated with Smaller Hippocampal Volumes in Adults with Low-Level Alcohol Intake.
papers.authors: Durazzo TC, Evangelista ND, Jester DJ, McNerney MW, Furst AJ, Adamson MM, Ashford JW, Adeli E, Humphreys K, Meyerhoff DJ.
papers.abstract: For decades, low-level alcohol consumption, operationalized as no more than two standard drink equivalents/day for males and one standard drink equivalent/day for females, was indicated to carry minimal systemic health risks. However, the neurobiological correlates of low-level drinking in healthy adults are not well characterized. To date, no study has concurrently assessed the associations of lifetime low-level alcohol consumption, modeled as a continuous rather than categorical or ordinal variables, with hippocampal volumes in healthy adults. This study examined the associations between recent and lifetime alcohol consumption and magnetic resonance-derived measures of bilateral hippocampal volumes in healthy non-smoking adults (22-70 years of age) with no history of alcohol use disorder or other conditions know to affect brain structure. All participants consumed ≤ 60 standard drink equivalents/month over the 1 year preceding study and median lifetime average drinks/month were 21. Greater lifetime average drinks/month were significantly related to smaller right and average of left and right hippocampal volumes. Findings indicated that lifetime alcohol consumption considered "low risk" for adults may have implications for the integrity of the hippocampi. Increased rate of hippocampal atrophy in cognitively normal middle-aged to older adults is clinically relevant as it may serve as surrogate biomarker for future cognitive decline or progression to mild cognitive impairment. These results may have implications for current harm reduction strategies and alcohol consumption public health guidelines.

papers.title: Impact of post-traumatic stress disorder on brain structural connectivity: A bidirectional Mendelian randomization study with meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Chen M, Tang X, Zhang L, Gang B, Peng L, Zhao G.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) has a tremendous impact on health and well-being, yet the bidirectional effects between it and structural connectivity (SC) of brain networks remain unexplored. Using SC data of European populations in the UK Biobank and PTSD genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets from FINNGEN, UK Biobank, PGC, and Neale lab, we performed bidirectional MR analysis using the inverse variance weighted (IVW) method as the primary approach, supplemented by other methods for validation. We used the MR Egger intercept and Cochrane's Q test for pleiotropy and heterogeneity analysis. We defined positive findings as phenotypes that satisfied all MR assumptions and demonstrated statistical significance (P < 0.05) in the meta-analysis. Of the 206 SC analyzed, five showed nominally significant forward associations with PTSD: left limbic network (L-LN) to right dorsal attention network (R-DAN), left visual network (L-VN) to the left control network (L-CN), L-VN to the L-DAN, L-VN to the left sensorimotor network (L-SMN), and R-DAN to the right salience/ventral attention network (R-SN/VAN). Additionally, no SC phenotype showed a nominally significant reverse association with PTSD in meta-analysis, and no reverse MR association survived correction for the effective number of independent tests. These findings provide preliminary evidence for bidirectional associations between PTSD and SC. However, no associations survived multiple testing correction using the effective number of independent tests (Meff) in either direction, suggesting these results are hypothesis-generating and require independent replication.

papers.title: AGE-RELATED BIOMECHANICAL AND STRUCTURAL REMODELING OF HUMAN MIDDLE CEREBRAL ARTERIES.
papers.authors: Halvorsen SC, Mlawer SJ, Then RM, Stein TD, Connizzo BK, Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Proper cerebral artery function is essential for maintaining the brain's microenvironment. The multilayered organization of cellular and extracellular matrix (ECM) constituents enables large cerebral arteries to accommodate pulse pressure and ensure both effective blood distribution and protection of the microcirculation. However, aging and disease induce compositional and structural remodeling in cerebral arteries, such as the middle cerebral artery (MCA), which can alter biomechanical properties and increase susceptibility to cerebrovascular conditions including atherosclerosis and aneurysms, both major contributors to stroke. Understanding how age-related changes in arterial structure and composition influence biomechanical behavior is critical for improving prediction of cerebrovascular risk. In this study, we characterized the age-dependent elastic and viscoelastic properties of human MCAs and related these changes to ECM structure and composition using imaging and biochemical assays. Our results demonstrate that aging is associated with increased stiffness and stress relaxation in MCAs. Biochemical analyses revealed age-related increases in collagen and glycosaminoglycan (GAG) content, both of which correlated with altered mechanical properties. Histological staining further showed denser collagen organization within the adventitia and elevated GAG presence, consistent with mechanical and biochemical findings. Additionally, multiphoton imaging under mechanical loading provided insight into layer-specific collagen reorganization in the adventitia. Collectively, these findings elucidate key age-dependent alterations in the structure-function relationship of human cerebral arteries and provide a mechanistic basis for increased cerebrovascular risk with aging. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Age-related remodeling of the extracellular matrix is a fundamental driver of tissue dysfunction, yet its effects on human cerebral artery mechanics remain poorly understood. In this study, we combine biomechanical testing, biochemical assays, histology, and multiphoton microscopy to characterize structural and functional remodeling of human middle cerebral arteries across a broad age range. We demonstrate that aging is associated with increased arterial stiffness and viscoelastic relaxation, accompanied by elevated collagen and glycosaminoglycan content. By directly linking extracellular matrix composition and organization to biomechanical function, this work provides new insights into the mechanisms governing cerebrovascular aging. These findings establish an important structure function framework for understanding vascular tissue remodeling and have broader implications for age related vascular dysfunction, mechanobiology, and biomaterials research.

papers.title: Clinical impact of enhanced leaf modelling on multi-metastatic intracranial SRT delivered on Halcyon: a modest but consistent dosimetric effect.
papers.authors: Ashburner M, Gandhi A, Ali O, Scarlet B.
papers.journal: Physical and engineering sciences in medicine
papers.abstract: Enhanced Leaf Modelling (ELM), introduced in Varian Eclipse v18, provides a refined representation of MLC transmission by explicitly modelling physical leaf geometry, interleaf leakage, and leaf-tip effects for Halcyon, replacing the traditional dosimetric leaf gap approximation. Unlike C-arm systems, Halcyon employs no collimator jaws, making out-of-field dose more exclusively dependent on MLC transmission characteristics and increasing the relative importance of accurate MLC modelling. Local commissioning supported the implementation of ELM on Halcyon and demonstrated improved agreement between calculated and measured dose distributions in the commissioning tests. These commissioning findings were separate form the present analysis, which characterises the dosimetric impact of ELM in clinically representative multi-metastatic stereotactic radiotherapy (MMSRT) plans rather than independently validating their physical accuracy. Ten MMSRT patients (2-6 lesions) were replanned using two calculation models: the standard Acuros XBv16 and v18 (with ELM). For each, two optimisation strategies were compared, manual and automatic normal tissue optimisation (NTO), to assess robustness across planning methods. The low-dose valley, defined as [Brain-PTVs], represented normal brain between targets. Dose-volume metrics were extracted across V50% to V2% of prescription dose to evaluate low-dose spread. Dose fall-off was quantified using concentric 1 mm rings extending 1-7 mm from the PTV surface, recording mean, median, and maximum doses within each ring. Clinically relevant spread was further evaluated using V12 Gy, V20 Gy, and V24 Gy metrics. Statistical analysis was done using appropriate parametric or non-parametric testing (p<0.05). Enhanced Leaf Modeling (ELM) primarily affected low- and intermediate-dose regions surrounding intracranial targets in MMSRT plans delivered on Halcyon. Statistically significant differences in normal brain volume were observed between ELM and the conventional MLC model (XB16), particularly beyond 3 mm from the PTV and at lower dose levels (V12-V24 Gy). ELM consistently reported higher low-dose volumes, with the largest effects observed for V20 Gy and V24 Gy within proximal rings, especially for manually optimised plans. Differences in extreme dose metrics were observed, with ELM associated with increased minimum dose and reduced maximum dose in the peri-PTV region, while mean dose remained largely unchanged. Despite statistical significance, all observed differences were small in magnitude and did not affect clinical acceptability. Enhanced Leaf Modelling (ELM) introduces measurable but clinically small changes in dose distribution for MMSRT delivered on Halcyon treatment units, with effects confined predominantly to low-dose regions and steep dose gradients. These changes did not alter clinical acceptability, target coverage, or conformity in the plans assessed. ELM provides a more detailed physical representation of MLC transmission and leakage than the conventional DLG-based approach. The direction and consistency of the observed differences are compatible with previously reported commissioning and validation findings; however, the present study characterises model-dependent dosimetric changes and does not establish improved physical accuracy for the MMSRT plans analysed.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Alpha-Band Oscillations as Potential Indicators of Executive Subcomponents Dysfunction correlating to the Severity of Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
papers.authors: Zhao M, Lu Y, Guo T, Yang Q, Li X, Wang T, Chen X, Collet JP, Wang D, Dirren E, Guan L, Wang Y.
papers.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) relates to executive dysfunction. While electroencephalography (EEG) alpha-band oscillations are promising biomarkers for cognitive impairment, their relationship with specific subcomponents of executive function in CSVD remains unclear. We aimed to investigate the association between EEG alpha-band oscillations and subcomponents of executive function-inhibitory control and working memory-among patients with CSVD. This was a cross-sectional analysis of an ongoing national registry research of CSVD (KY 2019-140-01). Five-minute resting-state EEG was recorded for analyzing occipital and frontal alpha-band indexes including peak frequency (PFα), occipital-frontal ΔPFα, and neurophysiological cognitive level. Inhibitory control and working memory were respectively evaluated by the Victoria Stroop Test (VST) and Digit Span. Associations and screening performance were assessed through logistic regression and ROC-AUC analysis with bootstrap internal validation. A total of 181 CSVD patients (age=60±12.0 years, male=61.9%) were recruited. After adjusting for age, gender, education, and CSVD severity, all PFα were associated with VST trial-2 completion time and VST composite time, respectively (all p<0.05). PFα(O1) have shown association with VST trial-3 completion time (p<0.05). PFα(O1) and PFα(O2) were associated with the high interference score, respectively (all p<0.05). We have set up fifty-six alpha-band-related models, and twenty-four models were selected with apparent AUC ranging from 0.6 to 0.83. The highest apparent AUC for inhibitory control impairment was 0.83, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.80. Alpha-band oscillations showed no robust association with working memory. In conclusion, resting-state EEG alpha-band parameters were associated with inhibitory control, but had no connection with working memory, in patients with CSVD. These findings suggested that resting-state EEG alpha-band oscillations can serve as an objective, accessible tool for assessing specific executive deficits in patients with CSVD.

papers.title: The impact of pruning iterations on Arcuate Fasciculus morphometry and diffusion features in right-handed adults.
papers.authors: Hoang NT, Hoang XH, Ha TH, Tran HPD, Ngo DHA, Le TB, Nguyen TT.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the utility of a pruning method in refining tractography and to examine the Arcuate Fasciculus (AF) morphometry and diffusion metrics in right-handed adults. Thirty-two healthy, right-handed adults underwent DTI on a 1.5T MRI system. Q-space diffeomorphic reconstruction was performed on a single-shell DTI dataset, and the AF was automatically tracked. Topology-Informed Pruning (TIP) was applied to reduce false-positive streamlines across varying numbers of iterations. Morphometry and diffusion metrics of the bilateral AF were extracted. The associations between these metrics and the number of iterations were evaluated using correlation analysis. The protocol-specific TIP threshold was identified as the knee point using the Kneedle algorithm. Differences in the morphometry and diffusion metrics of the selection AF tractometry by sex and hemisphere were also examined. A pFDR < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. TIP-based pruning was associated with improved tract delineation through the reduction of spurious streamlines. The number of pruning iterations affected the AF's morphometry and diffusion metrics. The selected TIP threshold was 8, and TIPs greater than 8 yielded stable values with minimal variability. Significant differences between hemispheres were observed in diffusion metrics except quantitative anisotropy (QA). For morphometry metrics, significant differences were identified in the number of tracts, span, and curl (pFDR < 0.05). No significant sex-related differences were found after FDR correction. Pruning iterations affect the visualization of AF in the protocol-specific population of right-handed adults. The number of pruning iterations selected should be carefully determined with full awareness and consideration.

papers.title: Quantified Brain Atrophy and Risk of Severe Mass Effect in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
papers.authors: Du Y, Altaf AZ, Ibrahim NJ, Chatzidakis S, Mallinger LA, Reinert AL, Stafford RA, Kumar A, Avula A, Abdalkader M, Cheng H, Greer DM, Dhar R, Ong CJ.
papers.abstract: Large middle cerebral artery (MCA) infarctions can result in life-threatening cerebral edema. Quantitative brain atrophy may improve risk stratification for severe edema. We examined whether quantitative brain atrophy is associated with severe midline shift after large ischemic stroke and whether incorporating atrophy improves prediction beyond established clinical and radiographic predictors. This was a retrospective observational cohort study of patients with greater than or equal to half MCA ischemic infarction, presentation within 24 h of last known well time, and at least one follow-up head computed tomography (CT), admitted to two academic hospitals with comprehensive stroke centers between 2006 and 2024. The study was approved by the institutional review boards of both centers. Brain atrophy was quantified as the inverse of standardized brain volume on admission head CT. The primary outcome was severe radiographic mass effect, defined as midline shift ≥ 5 mm on follow-up CT. The secondary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable regression models assessed associations between quantified atrophy and outcomes. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing models with and without atrophy using measures of goodness of fit, calibration, and discrimination. Among 565 patients (mean age 67.5 ± 15.7 years; 49.9% female), 223 (39.5%) developed severe mass effect. Greater atrophy was associated with lower odds of midline shift ≥ 5 mm [odds ratio (OR) 0.44, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34-0.58], but not with in-hospital mortality. Incorporation of atrophy improved prediction of severe mass effect compared with the baseline model [likelihood ratio test χ2 (1) = 41, p < 0.001; Akaike information criterion (AIC) 703 vs. 741; Bayesian information criterion (BIC) 733 vs. 767; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.68 vs. 0.60]. Quantified brain atrophy is independently associated with a reduced risk of severe mass effect after large MCA stroke and improved the performance of established predictive models. Incorporation of this imaging biomarker may enhance early risk stratification, monitoring, and intervention planning for patients at risk of life-threatening cerebral edema.

papers.title: The effect of acupuncture-rehabilitation therapy on brain functional plasticity in motor aphasia after ischemic stroke: a randomized clinical neuroimaging trial.
papers.authors: Liu TT, Ren M, Wang J, Wang Y, Wang CJ, Tang Q, Yang F, Hou XL.
papers.abstract: Motor aphasia is the most prevalent type of aphasia following ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and underlying neural mechanisms of acupuncture-rehabilitation (A-R) therapy on motor aphasia after IS. Twenty-six patients with post-IS motor aphasia were randomly assigned to either the A-R group or the Conventional Rehabilitation (CR) group in a 1:1 ratio, and matched by age and gender with 26 healthy controls (HCs). The CR group received standard treatment and language training, while the A-R group additionally underwent scalp acupoint cluster acupuncture. Behavioral assessments and Blood Oxygenation Level Dependent functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (BOLD-fMRI) scans were conducted before and after the four-week intervention to evaluate therapeutic outcomes and underlying mechanisms. Compared to HCs, patients exhibited decreased Amplitude of Low Frequency Fluctuations (ALFF) in the right precuneus (p < 0.05) and reduced Regional Homogeneity (ReHo) in the left precuneus/postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). Enhanced functional connectivity (FC) was observed in regions including the left Broca's area and right superior temporal gyrus, left Broca's area and right inferior frontal orbitalis gyrus, left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus, left Broca's area and right postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). After intervention, significant improvements were observed in Aphasia Quotient (AQ) scores and sub-item performance in both patient groups (p < 0.05), with the A-R group showing greater gains in AQ and spontaneous speech scores compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FMRI results indicated a significant increase in mean ALFF (mALFF) in the left inferior temporal gyrus after A-R treatment (p < 0.05) compared to before, and higher szReHo in the left anterior central gyrus compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FC between the left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus decreased in the A-R group (p < 0.05). Additionally, a negative correlation was observed between the right anterior central gyrus and listening comprehension (r = -0.574, p = 0.020). The findings suggest that both A-R and CR therapies enhance language function in patients with motor aphasia post-IS, with A-R therapy demonstrating superior efficacy. The therapeutic mechanism of A-R likely involves activating left hemisphere brain regions, suppressing right hemisphere activity, and restoring hemispheric balance to facilitate functional recovery.

papers.title: Italian guideline on palliative care in adult patients with grade 3/4 gliomas.
papers.authors: Veronese S, Solari A, De Panfilis L, Bertocchi E, Lissoni B, Merli R, Salmaggi A, Silvani A, Rudà R, Fariselli L, Camporeale G, Fausti P, Gianola S, Castellini G, Sgromo S, Iacorossi L, Pace A.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: Background The palliative and supportive care needs of adults with glioma are complex. In 2017, the European Association for Neuro-Oncology (EANO) published the guideline on palliative care (PC) in this population. Objective To develop a clinical practice guideline for the PC of adults with CNS WHO grade 3/4 gliomas by updating and adapting the EANO guideline to the Italian context. Methods The guideline was produced by an interdisciplinary, consumer-inclusive panel appointed by the three main Italian scientific associations for neurology, neuro-oncology and PC, following the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Results The panel formulated two clinical questions, addressed by three recommendations (all based on very-low-certainty evidence) and one Good Practice Statement: (1) We suggest the use of structured communication interventions to convey diagnosis, prognosis, and/or therapeutic and care options (conditional recommendation). (2) We recommend using approaches/tools to facilitate information processing in adults with glioma with reduced decision-making capacity (strong recommendation). (3) We believe it is appropriate to monitor the emotional impact that communication can have, and to provide support to adults with glioma and their caregivers (Good Practice Statement). (4) We suggest offering adults with CNS WHO grade 3/4 glioma a healthcare model that integrates the best anti-tumor and palliative treatments through early, dynamic, interdisciplinary, and multi-professional management of emerging health needs. The integrated model should be aligned with patients' care preferences and caregivers' needs and provided throughout the whole disease trajectory and across all care settings (conditional recommendation). Conclusions This guideline provides recommendations for improving communication and integrated PC for adults with glioma and their caregivers. It also provides indications for future research priorities in this population.

papers.title: Small poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma with concentric periarterial growth causing popliteal arterial stenosis: a case report.
papers.authors: Nagata S, Shouji Y, Sawano M, Negoto S, Hiraoka K, Nakayama M, Tanoue S.
papers.abstract: Soft-tissue sarcomas arising in the popliteal fossa are uncommon but clinically important because of their close relationship to major neurovascular structures. Poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma is an aggressive histologic subtype of synovial sarcoma. We report a case of a small poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma located in the perivascular region of the popliteal fossa that showed concentric periarterial growth with popliteal arterial stenosis. A 68-year-old woman reported a several-month history of heaviness in the right lower extremity. Ultrasonography revealed a 2-cm irregular hypoechoic solid mass circumferentially surrounding the popliteal artery, with no definite internal Doppler flow. The lesion showed intermediate signal intensity on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous intermediate-to-high signal intensity on fat-suppressed T2-weighted images. MRI showed circumferential arterial encasement with stenosis. Non-contrast-enhanced quiescent-interval slice-selective (QISS) MRA helped define the longitudinal extent of popliteal arterial narrowing. Surgical resection required vascular resection and reconstruction bypass of the popliteal artery and vein. Histopathological examination showed nested proliferation of tumor cells with ovoid-to-round nuclei in a hyalinized fibrous stroma. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for SS18-SSX and SSX, supporting the diagnosis of synovial sarcoma. This case illustrates that even a small synovial sarcoma in the popliteal fossa can circumferentially encase the popliteal artery and cause stenosis.

papers.title: Cortical bone geometry and static gravitational loads in neosauropod dinosaurs: Implications for biomechanical constraints on terrestrial gigantism.
papers.authors: Aureliano T, Ghilardi AM, Woodward HN, Alves HWL, Sipahi GM.
papers.abstract: Sauropod dinosaurs achieved unprecedented terrestrial gigantism, raising questions about the biomechanical limits of bone under extreme gravitational loads. We estimated static gravitational pressures (Pg) on appendicular cortical bone in neosauropods, including diplodocoids, brachiosaurids, and titanosaurs. We did this by measuring cortical thickness, estimating body masses, and calculating pressures on limb bones. We compared the results with the theoretical fracture thresholds of composite cortical bone (~150-200 MPa) and pure crystalline hydroxyapatite (~1000 MPa). In the largest specimens, Pg remained two orders of magnitude below the compressive strength of hydroxyapatite. These estimates are a conservative lower bound because they assume simultaneous four-limb support. They are also substantially lower (>15 MPa) than the functional failure threshold of composite cortical bone. Dynamic behaviors raise these values: during slow locomotion, a single hindlimb may briefly support the entire hindquarter load, and the weight distribution between fore- and hindlimbs varies markedly with center-of-mass position. Even so, rearing on the hindlimbs in the largest titanosaurs (>25 metric tons) would remain within safe limits defined by composite-bone failure thresholds. Neosauropod lineages show distinct biomechanical strategies. Diplodocoids kept a posteriorly positioned center of mass compatible with facultative bipedal rearing. Brachiosaurids shifted it cranially through neck and forelimb hypertrophy. Titanosaurs reached extreme sizes through enhanced secondary bone remodeling and extensive postcranial pneumatization. Cortical thickening is consistently associated with increasing gravitational loads across Neosauropoda. However, this static model does not test whether it was the primary evolutionary response, compared with other strategies such as trabecular densification and postcranial pneumaticity.

papers.title: Microduplication Overlapping YY1 at 14q32.2 Narrows the Candidate Interval for Cortical Malformation and Early-Onset Arterial Ischemic Stroke.
papers.authors: Bar-Hakim M, Beslow LA, Frumkin A, Shiran SI, Uliel-Sibony S, Harel T, Hausman-Kedem M.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.abstract: YY1 encodes a zinc-finger transcription factor that regulates chromatin remodeling and plays a critical role in brain development and vascular remodeling. Its nuclear co-activator, YY1AP1, causes Grange syndrome, a systemic arteriopathy with impaired vascular smooth-muscle-cell proliferation and differentiation. Haploinsufficiency of YY1 causes Gabriele-de Vries syndrome, whereas the phenotypic consequences of increased YY1 dosage have not been well characterized. We describe a 3.6-year-old girl with prenatal ventriculomegaly, growth restriction, and complex brain malformations including septo-optic dysplasia, dysgenesis of the corpus callosum, diffuse cortical dysgyria, and focal cortical dysplasia. At 7 months, she presented with acute left hemiparesis due to an acute right striatal/internal capsule arterial ischemic stroke and a subacute left striatal infarct, without clear arteriopathy. Head CT demonstrated bilateral basal ganglia and subcortical white matter calcifications. Echocardiography revealed a patent foramen ovale (PFO) but was otherwise normal; metabolic and thrombophilia workups were normal. She later developed drug-resistant epilepsy requiring hemispherotomy. Examination showed mild microcephaly, hemiparesis, and moderate developmental delay. Chromosomal microarray identified a 14q32.2 duplication encompassing the first exon and promoter region of YY1, classified as a variant of unknown significance. This duplication is the smallest reported copy-number gain overlapping YY1 and therefore potentially narrows the candidate genomic interval, given the reported phenotype. The overlapping phenotype with larger distal 14q duplications that also include YY1 supports the hypothesis that increased YY1 dosage contributes to this phenotype, although other potential mechanisms are plausible. Identification of additional patients and functional studies are necessary to delineate the precise pathogenic role of YY1 in this complex observed phenotype.

papers.title: Affective representations and brain-body dynamics during emotional video viewing
papers.authors: Xu W, Ronkainen P, Parviainen T.
papers.abstract: Emotional events evoke changing neural and bodily responses, but how these responses relate to overall emotional evaluations and how brain and body responses correspond over time remain unclear. Ninety-two participants viewed 25 silent emotional videos, each approximately one minute long, and rated valence and arousal after each video. We recorded brain activity using magnetoencephalography alongside cardiac, electrodermal, respiratory and facial-muscle activity. Representational similarity analysis (RSA) compared source-resolved cortical spectral patterns and peripheral response patterns with participants' valence and arousal ratings, adjusting each affective dimension for the other. Across whole videos, valence similarity corresponded to beta-band power patterns predominantly in left sensorimotor and frontotemporal cortex and to facial-muscle responses. Arousal similarity corresponded to alpha-band power patterns in the right frontoparietal cortex and to phasic electrodermal activity. The neural associations persisted after adjustment for visual and semantic similarities between the videos. Windowed neural correspondence with retrospective valence was significant from around 10 s onwards, with both neural and facial-muscle associations strengthening towards the end of the videos, whereas no significant windowed arousal associations were detected throughout viewing. We further applied dynamic RSA to compare neural and physiological response patterns across videos at different temporal lags. Correspondence exceeded a temporally decoupled reference for facial muscles, heart rate and electrodermal activity, but not respiration rate. On average, corrugator activity preceded corresponding neural patterns by about 1 s, zygomaticus activity occurred at approximately the same time, and heart-rate and electrodermal activity followed about 1.7 s and 4.5 s later, respectively. Together, these findings link overall affective evaluations to complementary neural and peripheral response geometries and reveal signal-specific temporal profiles of ongoing brain-body correspondence.

papers.title: In Utero MRI of Radial Glial Fibers Highlights Their Role in Modulating Fetal Cortical Folding
papers.authors: Chen R, Xu X, Zhu Q, Zheng W, Shen Y, Yu Z, Li M, Zhao Z, Sun C, Zhu K, Wang G, Luo Q, Wu D.
papers.abstract: The process of cortical folding is fundamental to early human brain development. While the differential growth of the cortical layers is a known driver, the biomechanical contribution of key cellular microstructures remains unclear, and there is a lack of direct in vivo markers of cortical microstructures for time-resolved observations. Using a multimodal approach combining in utero and ex vivo fetal brain MRI, histology, and computational mechanical simulation, we investigated whether developmental reorganization of cortical radial microstructures, particularly the radial glial cell (RGC)-associated scaffold, is linked to cortical folding and may modulate its mechanical progression. We characterized this radial organization noninvasively using diffusion MRI-based radial fiber density ( FD rad ). ex vivo fetal brain MRI and histology supported that regional variations in FD rad were strongly associated with vimentin-labelled radial architecture. Our in utero MRI data revealed closely coordinated developmental changes in cortical FD rad and curvature, with their regional timings and spatial patterns significantly coupled across the cortex. Longitudinal in utero MRI data further supported the synchronized within-individual co-development of FD rad and curvature. Furthermore, biomechanical simulations showed that reducing radial reinforcement modulated differential-growth-driven buckling, producing earlier folding and a greater cortical curvature under otherwise matched model conditions. Collectively, this study introduces FD rad as a noninvasive in utero MRI measure sensitive to radial glial fibers. By integrating spatial, temporal, histological, and computational evidence, our findings suggested a model in which developmental disassembly of the radial scaffold may modulate the mechanical response of the fetal cortex to differential growth, thereby contributing to cortical folding.

papers.title: Joint localization and testing reveals spatial context of differential expression
papers.authors: Stotzem N, Chang S, Cai N, Casale FP.
papers.abstract: Multi-subject spatial transcriptomics is increasingly used to identify molecular differences across individuals and conditions while resolving where in tissue those differences occur. Yet subject-level differential expression (DE) analyses commonly require spatial regions to be specified in advance, separating localization from testing. Here we present SpaceDX, a framework that uses gene-specific attention-based spatial weighting to jointly test differential expression and localize the spatial expression patterns contributing to these associations. In simulations, SpaceDX outperforms cluster-based DE methods when differential expression does not align with predefined spatial boundaries. Across two multi-subject mouse brain datasets, SpaceDX detected 45.8% more DE genes than regional DESeq2 pseudobulk in a chronic stress model, while in an Alzheimer's disease model combining SpaceDX with DESeq2 increased discovery by 19.1% relative to DESeq2 alone. Across both datasets, the learned maps provided spatial context for condition-associated expression signals in addition to gene-level significance. In the chronic stress model, for example, oligodendrocyte- and myelin-associated genes showed shared localization to corresponding brain structures. Together, these results show that the spatial context of differential expression can be inferred jointly with gene-level associations, recovering signals obscured by regional aggregation without requiring the relevant tissue context to be defined in advance.

papers.title: Anatomical Connectivity of the Macaque Gaze-following Patch
papers.authors: Chong I.
papers.abstract: The macaque gaze-following patch (GFP) is a specialized region of the temporal cortex implicated in decoding others' focus of attention and guiding gaze-following behavior. Although the GFP has been characterized functionally, its anatomical connectivity remains largely unknown. To investigate how the GFP is embedded within a putative brain network supporting social interactions, we injected a pair of fluorescence labeled anterograde and retrograde tracers into the GFP of one monkey. Analysis of the resulting material revealed reciprocal connections between the GFP and a region of the inferior parietal lobule, likely corresponding to area PFG, as well as sparse retrograde labeling in the amygdala. In contrast to the expectation that the GFP might be subject to cognitive control signals from the prefrontal cortex, we failed to identify convincing retrograde labeling in prefrontal regions. Overall, this connectivity profile is consistent with a network that translates information derived from others' faces into shifts of attention, while providing little evidence for direct prefrontal control of the GFP.

papers.title: Multiscale Spatial Characterization of Glioma MRI with MUSE and Radiomics
papers.authors: Miola M, Cammarasana S.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Characterizing glioma heterogeneity requires measurements that retain the physical scale and orientation of intratumoral intensity dependence. We evaluate the original 3D variographic field produced by the MUSE tool (Modeling Uncertainty as a Support for the Environment) alongside directional radiomics and independent image-based molecular classification. Methods. We analyzed postcontrast T1-weighted magnetic resonance images and enhancing-tumor segmentations from the public UCSF-PDGM collection. Verified MUSE outputs were available for 416 independent baseline patients, of whom 375 had paired directional gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) measurements. Each MUSE field retained 328 original experimental directional variograms with physical lag distances, semivariances, orientations, and voxel-pair support. Agreement was assessed at aligned offsets and through between-tumor comparisons. Patient-level permutation tests evaluated associations with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) status on 2,508 native direction-lag coordinates. A standalone 3D residual convolutional neural network (CNN) provided a separate IDH classification benchmark. Results. At 9,371 geometrically aligned offsets, native MUSE semivariance and half GLCM contrast correlated strongly (Pearson r = 0.954). Across 31,599 eligible between-tumor comparisons, representation-level dissimilarities showed Spearman ρ_S = 0.862, with sensitivity to GLCM feature family and long-offset sampling support. In 364 grade-4 tumors, including 24 IDH-mutant cases, the original MUSE field was associated with IDH after conventional adjustment (global permutation p = 0.00050), but the association was attenuated after primary directional GLCM adjustment (p = 0.256). The independent CNN achieved an out-of-fold IDH ROC-AUC of 0.792 and PR-AUC of 0.414 across 416 patients. Native MUSE examples revealed scale- and direction-dependent spatial behavior, including distances beyond those sampled by the GLCM protocol. Conclusion. Variograms by MUSE provide a physically indexed description of tumor spatial heterogeneity that can accompany radiomic analysis and CNN classification. The observed statistical overlap is substantial, and incremental clinical discrimination beyond directional GLCM features remains unestablished.

papers.title: Pupil size-resting state network coupling in major depressive disorder: a longitudinal iTBS study
papers.authors: Di Giuliano M, Schumann A, Walter M, Schmidt-Samoa C, Goya-Maldonado R.
papers.abstract: Altered central-peripheral autonomic nervous system communication plays a key role in major depressive disorder (MDD). In this context, pupillary dynamics may be considered a non-invasive peripheral proxy of treatment-related changes during intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) in MDD. However, the relationship between spontaneous pupillary fluctuations and the resting-state functional networks (RSNs) involved in MDD is still underexplored. Here, we investigated longitudinal changes in pupil-RSN coupling in patients with MDD undergoing an iTBS intervention. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging with concurrent pupillometry was acquired at four study visits. Group independent component analysis was used to estimate tonic pupil coupling with predefined RSNs of interest, along with a linear mixed-effects model to assess longitudinal changes in pupil size-RSN coupling and, exploratively, the effect of potential clinical and behavioral moderators. Among the examined RSNs, the left executive control network (lECN), including the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex as the cortical target of stimulation, exhibited a sustained reduction in positive pupil size coupling relative to baseline, irrespective of treatment order (active-sham). To determine whether this longitudinal change was accompanied by a more general change in pupil diameter, we additionally examined pupil size independently of RSNs. Pupil diameter decreased significantly from baseline, with greater decreases being positively associated with greater reductions in anxiety scores. Notably, reduction in anxiety symptoms were also positively correlated with reduction in depressive symptoms. Together, these findings suggest that longitudinal reductions in pupil-IECN coupling occur alongside reductions in pupil diameter that are associated with reductions in anxiety symptoms.

papers.title: Executive and language systems competitively shape predictive processing during reading
papers.authors: Martin S, Schuler A, Numssen O, Kroner-Weigl N, Schuckart MM, Obleser J, Hartwigsen G.
papers.abstract: When we read, our brains constantly generate predictions about upcoming words, which is thought to make comprehension faster and more efficient. Yet it remains unclear whether this predictive mechanism relies on the same domain-general executive resources the brain uses for other demanding cognitive tasks, or operates largely independently within the language system. Here we tested this question using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in twenty-five healthy adults, who performed self-paced naturalistic reading, an n-back task, and a dual task of concurrent reading and n-back, allowing us to place competing demands on cognitive resources. In three sessions, we stimulated the left angular gyrus alone, the angular gyrus together with dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, a hub of executive control, or delivered sham stimulation, and used computational modeling of decision-making to isolate how each brain state altered the underlying cognitive processes. Combined stimulation of the angular gyrus and prefrontal cortex selectively weakened the reading-time costs of unexpected words, but only when reading competed with the working-memory task, revealing that linguistic prediction draws on executive resources specifically under cognitive load. Computational models showed that the relationship was bidirectional: Unpredictable words also disrupted concurrent working-memory decisions, slowing the accumulation of evidence and increasing response caution. Together, these findings show that predictive language processing is not a fixed, encapsulated function but is dynamically coupled to executive control when cognitive demands compete. Our results provide evidence that prediction during language comprehension is embedded within a broader, demand-sensitive cognitive architecture that flexibly coordinates linguistic and executive resources.

papers.title: Revealing multiscale architecture of the intact human spine using hierarchical phase contrast tomography
papers.authors: Sharma A, Henderson IC, Parmenter AL, Brunet J, Liebsch C, Greiner-Perth A, Stansby D, Chen J, Zhou Y, Liu J, Purzycka J, Urban T, Dejea H, Delphin A, Lamalle L, Pitsillides AA, Bray TJP, Wilke H, Bellier A, Tafforeau P, Walsh CL, Lee PD.
papers.abstract: Background: Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provide detailed clinical assessment of the human spine; however, their millimeter-scale spatial resolution limits direct visualization of tissue microarchitecture and interfaces. Hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) enables ex vivo non-destructive, micron-resolution imaging of intact human organs without exogenous contrast agents, extending anatomical assessment to spatial scales inaccessible to conventional clinical imaging. Purpose: To evaluate the capability of HiP-CT to visualize macro- to microanatomy of an intact adult human spine ex vivo. Methods: An intact spine (C1-L5) from a 62-year-old male donor without known skeletal disease was formalin-fixed and imaged by HiP-CT at the European Synchrotron. Whole-spine imaging was performed at 16.26 μm isotropic voxels, with selected regions of interest imaged using 2.2 μm voxels. Ex vivo MRI using clinical sequences was performed for anatomical comparison. Three-dimensional segmentation and quantitative analyses included intervertebral disc (IVD) grading, annulus fibrosus fiber tracing, and vertebral trabecular micro-morphometry. Results: HiP-CT enabled high spatial-resolution, multiscale imaging of the intact human spine, simultaneously visualizing vertebral bone and endplate, IVDs, spinal cord and meninges, nerve roots and ganglia, vasculature, ligaments, and musculature. Three-dimensional segmentation and virtual sectioning mapped neurovascular anatomy and vertebral vascular supply, without exogenous contrast enhancement, while preserving their relationships with surrounding tissues. Whole-spine images enabled quantitative analysis of annulus fibrosus fiber organization and vertebral trabecular microarchitecture, permitting the detection of focal posterolateral fiber disruption at the L4-L5 IVD and regional differences in trabecular architecture between cervical and lumbar vertebral bodies. Local tomography resolved annulus fibrosus lamellae, vertebral endplate Haversian systems, and facet joint hyaline cartilage at micron resolution. Conclusions: HiP-CT enables non-destructive, multiscale three-dimensional imaging of the intact human spine while preserving tissue relationships across spatial scales and hard-soft tissue boundaries. HiP-CT could provide an ex vivo microanatomical reference for future correlation with clinical imaging investigations of spinal disease and in the development and validation of imaging biomarkers.

papers.title: Neuro-cutaneous interactions in inflammatory, neuropathic, and metabolic skin diseases.
papers.authors: Zhao J, Cheng X, Li Y, Chen Y, Yang H, Zhu N, You L.
papers.abstract: Abstract The skin and nervous system engage in bidirectional communication. Disruption is implicated in inflammatory, neuropathic and metabolic disorders. To systematically review the structural and functional basis of skin-nerve interactions in health and disease, following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. A systematic search of PubMed (inception to June 10, 2026) combined MeSH and free-text terms for skin innervation, sensory neurons, sympathetic nervous system, neuropeptides, neuroimmune regulation, and skin diseases. Manual supplementation via reference tracing and author searches improved recall. 86 original studies were ultimately included (45 from database search and 41 from manual supplementation). Key findings: (1) Keratinocytes, Merkel, Langerhans and melanocytes form synapse-like connections with nerve endings, establishing a "sensory epithelium." (2) Substance P activates mast cells via neurokinin 1 receptor/mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (neurogenic inflammation); while calcitonin gene-related peptide inhibits dendritic cells (immune tolerance). (3) In atopic dermatitis, stress recruits basophils/eosinophils via sympathetic-beta-2 adrenergic receptor axis; in psoriasis, TRPV1+ neurons activate the interleukin-23/interleukin-17 axis via calcitonin gene-related peptide. (4) Stress induces sensory neurons to release miR-let-7b, exacerbating psoriasis via macrophage Toll-like receptor 7. (5) Postherpetic neuralgia: intraepidermal nerve fiber density < 650 neurites/mm2 correlates with central hyperexcitability ("phantom pain"). (6) Neurofibromatosis type 1 (RAS) and guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(q) subunit alpha (ANGPT2) mutations reveal mechanisms for tumors or vascular malformations. (7) Heat stress induces skin kallikrein-related peptidase 14 to reprogram hypothalamic LRRC7+ astrocytes via blood, forming a "heat memory" that leads to metabolic disorders (reversed by vitamin A). Substance P/neurokinin 1 receptor, sensory nerve-calcitonin gene-related peptide-interleukin-23, sympathetic-beta-2 adrenergic receptor-basophil/eosinophil, and skin-hypothalamic circuits are key translational pathways. Targeting these (neurokinin 1 receptor antagonists, β-blockers, anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide antibodies, and vitamin A) offers therapeutic opportunities for inflammatory skin diseases, neuropathic itch/pain and stress-related metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Hippocampus-biased proteomic remodeling after multiple cerebral infarction: Mechanism of Rehmannia glutinosa extract.
papers.authors: Huang Z, Miao L, Li F, Zhang M, Yao M, Liu J.
papers.abstract: Abstract Rehmannia glutinosa extract has been widely used in the treatment of multiple cerebral infarction, but its neurorepair effects and associated molecular responses remain incompletely characterized. In this study, a rat multiple cerebral infarction model was established by microsphere-induced cerebral ischemia, followed by treatment with Rehmannia glutinosa extract. Neurological function, brain atrophy, neuronal integrity, and hippocampal neurogenic responses were evaluated. Label-free quantitative proteomics was performed separately in the ipsilateral cortex and hippocampus to characterize region-specific molecular responses to Rehmannia glutinosa extract, and proteins showing multiple cerebral infarction-associated alterations that changed in the opposite direction following Rehmannia glutinosa extract treatment were subjected to functional enrichment analysis. Catalpol, a representative constituent detected in Rehmannia glutinosa extract, was subsequently evaluated in oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-injured PC12 cells, and the involvement of Hedgehog signaling was examined using cyclopamine, a smoothened inhibitor. Rehmannia glutinosa extract treatment improved neurological outcomes and reduced brain atrophy following multiple cerebral infarction, accompanied by preservation of neuronal integrity and enhanced early neurogenic responses in the hippocampal dentate gyrus. Proteomic profiling revealed distinct treatment-associated responses in the cortex and hippocampus. In the hippocampus, 102 multiple cerebral infarction-associated proteins exhibited opposite-direction changes following Rehmannia glutinosa extract treatment, with functional enrichment implicating injury and inflammatory responses, gliogenesis, cellular homeostasis, and synaptic-associated processes. In oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-injured PC12 cells, catalpol improved cellular recovery and partially restored neuronal structural and repair-associated markers, including neurofilament light chain, whereas growth-associated protein 43 showed a non-significant recovery trend. Catalpol also modulated Hedgehog pathway-related proteins, and cyclopamine attenuated the catalpol-associated improvement in cell confluence, indicating an association between the cellular response to catalpol and Hedgehog pathway integrity. Collectively, these findings indicate that Rehmannia glutinosa extract promotes hippocampus-predominant proteomic remodeling after multiple cerebral infarction in model mice, accompanied by improved neurological function, attenuated brain atrophy, and enhanced hippocampal neurogenesis. Catalpol may participate in the remodeling-associated neural repair processes by modulating the Hedgehog pathway.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
papers.authors: Wu Q, Hu J, Abuliezi N, Sun Y, Wu Y, Dun X.
papers.abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, and mesenchymal stem cell-treated samples. In this exploratory dataset, the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion samples showed relatively greater representation of inflammatory and antigen-presenting microglial states and elevated expression of selected microglial state-associated genes, including Slfn4, Apoe, and Gpnmb. In the corresponding exploratory comparison, the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample showed relatively greater representation of homeostatic-associated and Lgals3/Spp1-enriched microglial states and lower expression of several inflammatory-associated genes. Spatial mapping further revealed regionally restricted expression of microglial and neuronal markers within the injured tissue. Excitatory neurons displayed preliminary mesenchymal stem cell-associated transcriptional patterns involving mitochondrial transcripts, oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic signaling, calcium-related functions, and apoptosis/autophagy-associated pathways. CellChat analysis computationally predicted relatively high levels of tumor necrosis factor, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, and complement signaling in the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion sample, whereas the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample had relatively high levels of predicted activity of neuregulin, pleiotrophin and selected semaphorin. Together, these integrated datasets provide a hypothesis-generating framework linking microglial state remodeling, neuronal metabolic and synaptic programs, and predicted neuroimmune communication patterns after ischemic stroke. Because each omics condition or time point was represented by one biological sample, all the transcriptomic findings should be considered preliminary and exploratory and should be validated in independently replicated cohorts.

papers.title: Bilateral Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia Caused by Minor Head Injury: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Chen WC, Li CW, Wu BP, Huang P.
papers.abstract: Bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO) is rare, with vascular disease and multiple sclerosis being the most common causes. We report an unusual case of isolated bilateral INO following minor brain injury. A 61-year-old Asian woman developed binocular diplopia after a minor motorbike accident. Neurological examination revealed bilateral INO with impaired adduction in both eyes and abducting nystagmus in the contralateral eye. Initial brain computed tomography was unremarkable, but brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) 2 days later revealed a subtle paramedian pontomesencephalic hyperintensity on T2-weighted imaging, which became more pronounced with contrast enhancement, suggesting the axonal injury secondary to trauma. Minor head trauma can cause bilateral INO due to subtle brainstem injury, even without other deficits. Shear forces may lead to vascular and axonal damage in the medial longitudinal fasciculus. MRI with contrast is essential for detection. Although rare, isolated bilateral INO should be considered posthead trauma.

papers.title: Distinct Patterns of Cortical Atrophy Predict Cognitive Progression in Age-Related Hearing Loss: A Longitudinal MRI Study.
papers.authors: Hong L, Zeng Q, Luo X, Li K, Liu X, Li J, Zhang M, Cui F, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.
papers.abstract: Background and purpose Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) and dementia are common chronic conditions among the elderly, significantly impacting the quality of life of older adults. Additionally, ARHL is an important and modifiable risk factor for dementia. This study aimed to investigate distinct patterns of cortical atrophy in patients with ARHL and mild cognitive impairment (MCI), comparing those with stable cognition (sMCI) with those who progressed to dementia (pMCI), using longitudinal MRI data. Materials and methods We included a total of 93 participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative: 51 sMCI with normal hearing (sMCI+healthy control, group 1), 20 with sMCI with ARHL (sMCI+ARHL, group 2), and 22 with pMCI and ARHL (pMCI+ARHL, group 3). All subjects underwent 3 longitudinal T1-weighted MRI scans at approximately 1-year intervals. Cortical thickness was measured using FreeSurfer 6.0 in regions including the entorhinal cortex, parahippocampal gyrus, and temporal gyri. Repeated-measures ANOVA was used to compare atrophy rates, and receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated the predictive value of significant regions. Results Group 3 showed substantial faster annual atrophy rates in the left entorhinal cortex, left middle temporal gyrus, and bilateral superior temporal gyri compared with group 1. Group 2 also exhibited faster atrophy in temporal regions than group 1. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated that combined use of these regions improved predictive accuracy for cognitive progression. Conclusions Patients with ARHL with progressive cognitive decline exhibit accelerated atrophy in the auditory and early Alzheimer vulnerable regions. Combined cortical thickness measures may serve as a neuroimaging biomarker to predict cognitive progression in populations with ARHL.

papers.title: Which memory does brain stimulation improve? The priming problem
papers.authors: Velioglu HA, çelik mc, Aslan D, Sakiroglu MA, Çiçek Y, Altunc AT.
papers.abstract: Background: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of cortical sites connected with the hippocampus improves scores on episodic memory tests and is being tested for memory decline, including in Alzheimer's disease. These gains are read as gains in intentional retrieval. Objective: To examine whether standard memory outcomes can support this reading and how the contribution of repetition priming can be measured. Methods: Narrative review of hippocampal-network stimulation studies, cognitive and electrophysiological research on priming and processing fluency, stimulation studies of priming and parietal cortex, and clinical trials of TMS for memory decline. Results: Old/new recognition and cued recall present studied items or cues again at test. Repetition priming makes these items easier to process, and this fluency can raise a memory score with intentional retrieval unchanged. The fluency behind word-recognition decisions is largely conceptual, so it persists after a change of surface form. TMS can also alter priming directly, and stimulating the standard parietal target changes the subjective side of recollection. Meta-analytic evidence shows that the gains are specific to episodic memory and largest for recollection tests after stimulation before encoding, but the priming contribution to these gains has not been estimated. Conclusions: Process-level claims about stimulation-related memory gains require the priming contribution to be measured. Five measurement steps, centred on matched indirect tests and process-dissociation procedures, make it measurable in the same participants, including in clinical trials.

papers.title: Graviceptive Neglect treatment in acute stroke using transcranial Electrical stimulation clinical trial (GravNegElect): rationale, objectives, and design
papers.authors: Edwards T, Albuquerque L, Castro J, Elias A, Vilar A, Santos L, Marazzi TBM, Lopes R, Goulart T, Pontes-Neto O, Camilo M, Marques D, Kumar S, Leite J, Salmon C, Santos AC, Edwards DJ.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Stroke is one of the leading causes of disability globally and is often related to poor functional recovery and a high risk of falling. These outcomes correlate closely with an impaired perception of visual verticality (VV), a frequent condition referred to as visual graviceptive neglect (V-GN). Our prior findings indicate that post-stroke VV is most frequently rotated away from the lesioned hemisphere in the roll plane. Furthermore, we demonstrated that a focal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) montage (known as high-definition tDCS; HD-tDCS) can induce a remarkable and sustained rotation away from the stimulated hemisphere when positioned over the temporo-parietal junction (TPJ), a key integrative cortical hub for VV. Therefore, we hypothesize that stimulating the contralesional TPJ in sub-acute stroke individuals will correct their V-GN. Methods: This phase IIa, randomised, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial aims to determine whether HD-tDCS can safely correct V-GN in individuals who have experienced a stroke affecting either hemisphere. Ancillary aims are to investigate whether HD-tDCS influences ocular torsion; explore neuroanatomical characteristics related to V-GN; investigate the relationship between EEG functional connectivity and V-GN; and determine the cerebrovascular reactivity effects of HD-tDCS. A total of 28 individuals diagnosed with acute or early sub-acute unihemispheric ischemic stroke (50% with right hemisphere lesions) will be randomized to receive six 20-minute sessions (conducted within 2 days) of either 2mA cathode-centre HD-tDCS or sham stimulation over the contralesional TPJ. VV will be assessed using the bucket method. The primary outcome is the change in VV from baseline to immediately after the intervention protocol, while the secondary outcome is VV assessed at 1 month post-intervention. Fundus photography (ocular torsion), vascular reactivity using transcranial Doppler, and resting state EEG (functional connectivity) will be assessed at the same time-points as VV. Structural and resting state functional MRI will be performed 2-15 days after stroke onset. Fractional anisotropy within the V-GN network regions-of-interest (ROIs) and transcallosal TPJ tract will be correlated with baseline VV and V-GN response to intervention. Discussion: This trial has the potential for a significant public health impact by providing foundational clinical and physiological evidence to develop future clinical interventions for V-GN. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06747676. Registered on 12 December 2024. Version 2.

papers.title: Panel-Gene Transcriptomic Associations in Multiple Sclerosis: a three-cohort white-matter analysis of a locked 468-gene detoxification panel
papers.authors: McCaulley ME.
papers.abstract: Abstract Multiple sclerosis (MS) was examined with a locked 468-gene redox, metal, xenobiotic-metabolism and barrier panel in three adult white-matter cohorts from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE138614, GSE32915, GSE108000). A DerSimonian–Laird random-effects meta-analysis yielded 442 analyzable genes, 78 at Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.05, and 30 high-confidence genes (FDR < 0.05, measured in ≥ 3 cohorts, direction-concordant in ≥ 70% of contributing cohorts, and nominally significant in ≥ 2 cohorts); 12 were higher in MS, led by CP and PPARG, and 18 lower, led by OPLAH and GAMT. The meta-analysis was reproduced exactly from the per-cohort GEO2R result tables. Panel genes were not more often FDR-significant than the rest of the transcriptome (17.2% versus 15.5%; Fisher P = 0.35), and 18% of 20,000 random sets of 442 measured genes had at least as many FDR-significant genes as the panel. Each cohort contributes several samples per donor; re-fitted with the donor as the unit, 17 genes met the high-confidence rule, 12 of them from the original 30, and adjustment for an oligodendrocyte marker score left 9. Under a Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman test no gene reached FDR < 0.05. In an independent cohort (GSE123496), 25 of the 30 high-confidence genes changed in the same direction (exact binomial p = 0.0003; Pearson r = 0.73). In supporting lesion and grey-matter tiers (not pooled), higher HMOX1 and lower GPX4 (the latter not FDR-significant in the meta-analysis) recurred; oligodendrocyte loss with glial and vascular expansion may explain part of these and other signals. These are transcript-abundance associations in postmortem tissue; enzyme activity, iron content and lipid peroxidation were not measured, and the findings do not establish ferroptosis or a treatment target.

papers.title: The Aging Brain Matrix: Cross-Species Evidence Linking FREM3 to Brain and Cognitive Aging
papers.authors: Clifford KP, Prevot TD, Sumitomo A, Das S, Bansal Y, Marcotte M, Zhou R, Yeung J, Ding M, Felsky D, Nieman BJ, Banasr M, Sibille E, Tomoda T, Nikolova YS.
papers.abstract: Abstract The human extracellular-matrix-related FREM3 gene is strongly age-dependent, enriched in age-sensitive excitatory long-range-projecting neurons, and implicated in neurodegenerative diseases. To establish the first translationally relevant causal evidence for the gene’s roles in brain structure and cognition, we developed an excitatory-neuron-specific Frem3 conditional knockout mouse model ( Frem3 -cKO) and computed genetically regulated expression of FREM3 ( FREM3 -GReX) in humans, enabling convergent neurostructural and cognitive characterizations. Frem3 -cKO mice showed widespread lower global and regional brain volume in middle age vs young adulthood, consistent with drastic age-dependent volume loss absent in wildtype mice. These effects were strongest in cognitively relevant cortical regions and paralleled by lower cognitive performance. In humans, lower FREM3- GReX was associated with lower total surface area, which further mediated an indirect link to lower cognitive performance across multiple age-sensitive domains. We provide the first translationally relevant cross-species evidence supporting a key role for FREM3/Frem3 in maintaining brain and cognitive health across aging.

papers.title: Brain MRI of Dystroglycanopathy Patients in a Chinese Pediatric Cohort: Genotype-Specific Neuroimaging Signatures and Neurodevelopmental Correlates
papers.authors: Song D, Liu Y, Lin S, Luo J, Fu X, Yang H, Zhu Y, Xiong H.
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective To delineate clinical-genetic-neuroimaging correlations in a Chinese cohort of patients with dystroglycanopathy (DGP). Methods This observational cohort study enrolled 90 genetically confirmed DGP patients. Brain MRI was available for 63 patients; 38 high-quality scans underwent blinded phenotyping. Patients were classified into Group 1 (combined supratentorial and infratentorial malformations), Group 2 (isolated infratentorial malformations), and Group 3 (normal/non-specific findings).
