Clinical assessments included motor milestones, intellectual disability, expressive language, receptive language, and epilepsy. Spearman’s correlation and network analyses were performed. Results The genetic spectrum included POMGNT1 (12), CRPPA (7), POMT1 (6), FKRP (5), FKTN (4), POMT2 (2), and B3GALNT2 (2). Commonest MRI abnormalities were cerebellar dysplasia (71%), brainstem hypoplasia (63%), and cerebellar microcysts (58%). Group 1 \(\:\text{n=19}\) had severe intellectual disability (100%) and global motor delay; 63% were preverbal/early verbal, 32% had limited phrases, and only 5% achieved basic conversation; epilepsy occurred in 53% and mortality in 16%. Group 2 \(\:\text{n=9}\) had milder intellectual (56%) and language impairment (44%); 67% achieved basic conversation, 89% comprehended simple commands, and epilepsy occurred in 33%. Group 3 \(\:\text{n=10}\) had the mildest phenotype; no epilepsy or mortality occurred, 80% achieved basic conversation, and 100% comprehended simple commands. Imaging severity correlated strongly with clinical phenotype \(\:\text{ρ=0.756,P<0.001}\). Expressive language was the most connected clinical hub, but partial correlations adjusting for supratentorial lesions rendered infratentorial associations non-significant (all P>0.05). Receptive language deficits correlated specifically with lissencephaly \(\:\text{ρ=0.62,P<0.001}\); cerebellar dysplasia independently correlated with epilepsy (partial r=0.351, P=0.033). Genotype dictated distinct correlation spectra: POMGNT1 almost exclusively drove Group 1 (83%); CRPPA uniformly showed cerebellar dysplasia; POMT1/POMT2 exhibited “functional-structural dissociation”; FKRP showed the broadest heterogeneity and weakest imaging-clinical alignment. Conclusions Receptive language deficit is highly specific and strongly associated only with lissencephaly, whereas expressive language is the most widespread and sensitive clinical indicator. Genotype-guided neuroimaging assessment is essential for precise prognostication.

papers.title: A Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman Kernel Framework for Multimodal Brain Connectome Analysis
papers.authors: Razzetta C, Garbarino S.
papers.abstract: Abstract We introduce a Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman (WWL) graph-kernel framework for the joint analysis of weighted structural graphs and continuous node attributes, together with a regularized fractional-Laplacian extension of the underlying graph propagation operator. The proposed fractional operator provides non-local propagation across the entire graph, with influence decaying as a power law with graph distance, while remaining anchored to the subject-specific structural topology. This extends the standard finite-range Weisfeiler Lehman propagation scheme to a controlled long-range setting without introducing an externally prescribed coupling between structural and functional information. We formulate the framework for multimodal brain connectivity by representing each subject as a single attributed graph: diffusion tractography defines the weighted structural edges, while resting-state functional connectivity profiles are encoded as continuous node attributes. We evaluate the method on a synthetic cohort of $900$ subjects in three ordered clinical groups along the Alzheimer's disease spectrum, generated from multiple structural templates and characterised by a spatially structured loss of resting-state network segregation with age. Under nested cross-validation, the WWL kernel achieves a balanced accuracy of $0.651\pm0.028$, significantly outperforming both a raw-feature SVM and a histogram-based WL-kernel baseline. Controlled ablations separate the contribution of the Wasserstein representation from that of structural propagation. Replacing the propagation operator by the identity yields essentially identical classification performance, whereas a structure-only representation approaches chance, showing that the discriminative gain in this benchmark is primarily associated with the Wasserstein point-cloud representation rather than structural propagation. Conversely, experiments across distinct signal regimes show that the fractional extension is signal-dependent: non-local propagation can improve continuous prediction for diffuse whole-brain coupling signals, but provides no consistent advantage for network-segregation signals. We further identify a connectivity artefact induced by fixed-percentile structural sparsification and establish a threshold preserving graph connectivity across subjects. The results clarify the respective roles of Wasserstein geometry, structural propagation, and non-locality in multimodal graph representations and provide a controlled framework for assessing when fractional graph propagation is expected to be beneficial.

papers.title: Chemically Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Electronics for Neurochemical Homeostasis
papers.authors: Wang T, Peng S, Xu Q, Zou H, Chen Z, Song G, zhang f, Xia L, Zhou R, Hao W, Tang Z, Li T, Zhao X, Gao L, Weng L, Ji J, Wang M, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic devices excel at emulating synaptic and neuronal computation, yet their states are predominantly programmed by electrical signals, limiting their ability to directly perceive and adapt to the molecular signals that govern biological neural function. Here we introduce chemical reconfiguration into neuromorphic electronics and develop a chemically reconfigurable neuromorphic healer (CR-NeuroHealer), in which molecular inputs directly reprogram synaptic plasticity to couple neurochemical perception with adaptive regulation. The CR-NeuroHealer responds distinctly to dopamine (DA) and Fe 3+ , enabling the chemical environment to reconfigure the device between healthy-like and pathological synaptic states. When interfaced with neuron-like PC-12 cells, the device establishes a biohybrid synapse through molecular communication, sensing presynaptic DA while providing adaptive chemical feedback. Pathological iron accumulation weakens synaptic transmission and triggers deferiprone (DFP) release, which chelates excess iron and restores dopamine-responsive plasticity, completing a chemically reconfigurable regulatory cycle. We further demonstrate this chemical perception in vivo using a miniaturized neuromorphic OECT implanted in a 6-hydroxydopamine-induced Parkinsonian mouse model. The implanted devices respond to endogenous DA modulation and pathological iron accumulation with distinct synaptic-like outputs that discriminate neurochemical states and guide DFP-mediated intervention, accompanied by recovery of motor performance and device responses. These results establish chemical reconfiguration as a neuromorphic design principle for therapeutic brain–computer interfaces that operate through the molecular language of the nervous system.

papers.title: Multi-scale effects of single-dose psilocybin in the macaque brain
papers.authors: Wang J, Chen J, Sun W, Yang Z, Luo C, Yang F, Zhu Y, Wang H, Zhang X, Masthay J, Baek S, Li J, Zhuo Y, Wang X, Wu Y, Ma Y, Sun Q, Ji W, Chang S, Wang X, Zhu X, Hu J, Chen Y, Yuan T.
papers.abstract: Abstract Psilocybin holds strong therapeutic promise for treating major depressive disorder. However, the cellular and molecular substrates underlying its action have not been fully elucidated, especially in the primate brain. We combined multimodal MRI, magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomics and metabolomics, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to map the multiscale temporospatial dynamics induced by a single dose of psilocybin in cynomolgus macaques. Psilocybin increased the integration of the frontoparietal network (FPN) with the default-mode and limbic networks, transiently reduced integration of the FPN with the somatomotor network, and induced global network segregation. Several regions in the cortex, striatum, and thalamus as well as certain of the frontoparietal white matter pathways showed persistent enhancement lasting 1 week. Notably, these changes were accompanied by a CSF multi-omics shift from acute prostaglandin-dominated inflammation to a sustained enrichment of an omega-3 fatty acid-associated anti-inflammatory state together with a bidirectional reorganization of extracellular matrix (ECM)-related signatures, characterized by increased CD44 and decreased fibulin-family proteins. In addition, we found lasting upregulation of TCA-cycle and NAD(P)-dependent redox enzymes. This was further supported by sustained elevations of glutamate/glutamine and total creatine in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), which was found using in vivo MRS. At the cellular level, psilocybin promoted HTR2A selective upregulation in deep-layer excitatory neurons along with a widespread enhancement of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation centered on the complex I subunit ND3 across diverse excitatory and inhibitory neuronal subtypes in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Glial-state remodeling, including a shift of astrocytes toward ECM remodeling states and microglia toward an anti-inflammatory state, also occurred. Collectively, these findings provide evidence in the primate brain that psilocybin induces functional integration and segregation of brain networks, enhances energy metabolism and synaptic plasticity, and modulates neuroimmune signaling. All the data will be shared as an integrated resource for primate psilocybin research.

papers.title: From Static Scaffolds to Adaptive Language Support: A Framework for Accessible Communication
papers.authors: Frido R, Santos LR, Bruno C.
papers.abstract: Assistive language technologies increasingly offer multimodal supports for reading and communication, yet these supports are generally presented in predefined formats that do not account for differences in individual abilities or changing task demands. This paper outlines a framework for personalizing language assistance through the selection of linguistic and visual scaffolds. The proposed system combines a user profile with ongoing behavioral feedback to select among four presentation formats, ranging from unmodified text to sentence segmentation with pictograms and keyword labels. An optional neural component incorporates calibrated EEG features to investigate whether cognitive-state information can further improve adaptation. We propose a staged evaluation encompassing content validation, behavioral personalization, and the incremental contribution of neural measurements. By comparing fixed, behavior-adaptive, and neuroadaptive interfaces, the project aims to determine when additional support is beneficial and whether EEG provides meaningful advantages beyond observable user performance.

papers.title: Area MT carries acceleration information in a quickly and directly decodable representation.
papers.authors: Chen PS, Huk AC.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: We sought to better understand the neural representation of visual motion acceleration. A straightforward estimation of acceleration would involve calculating the rate of change of velocity, which itself would be calculated from change in position over time. As it is well-established that neurons in area MT encode velocity, the brain could thus indirectly estimate acceleration by calculating the change in MT's velocity representations. An alternative mechanism, however, could operate more rapidly and directly. In this case, the brain could exploit interactions between MT's standard motion encoding and idiosyncratic temporal dynamics of neural responses. Such direct decoding would thus exploit nonlinearities usually ignored in studies of MT coding. We tested between these two theories by measuring from ensembles of MT neurons while two male awake fixating macaques viewed linearly accelerating motion stimuli. Direct decoding of acceleration from MT was possible on faster time scales, and could be done with higher fidelity, than indirect decoding. Distinct motion acceleration information could thus be efficiently read out from rich and heterogeneous MT ensemble responses, regardless of the mechanisms that give rise to various forms of motion tuning that it exhibits. A similar analysis of activity in the medial superior temporal area (MST) did not suggest that this later stage of motion processing has a more refined acceleration representation. Together, these results suggest that the brain may opportunistically exploit nonlinear idiosyncrasies of neural responses to efficiently extract behaviorally relevant information on fast time scales, instead of performing explicit calculation of certain variables.Significance Statement This study aims to understand if linear acceleration information of visual motion is extracted and represented in primate visual motion areas MT and MST. By combining large-scale multi-area neuronal recordings, population-level analyses, and a rich set of moving stimuli, we show that linear acceleration can be decoded from MT activity. Specifically, our results demonstrate that (1) motion acceleration is encoded in MT, and can be directly and quickly decoded from MT ensemble activity, and (2) area MST, despite being a later stage of motion processing, does not refine acceleration representations. These findings call for revisiting how brain areas might efficiently extract behaviorally relevant information from the environment and highlight the importance of temporal dynamics in visual motion processing.

papers.title: PTPRO restricts higher-order branching of terminal arbors through TrkB dephosphorylation.
papers.authors: Li J, Yasumura M, Iguchi T, Taniguchi M, Oka Y, Tsai CY, Sato M.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The structural complexity of axon collateral terminal arbors shapes synaptic connectivity. In corticospinal projections, individual axon collaterals exhibit distinct patterns of terminal arborization, ranging from sparse local branches to dense, highly complex arbors in target regions such as the pontine nuclei. How this complexity is controlled remains poorly understood. Here, using corticopontine projections in male and female mice, we show that protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type O (PTPRO) selectively restricts higher-order branching of terminal arbors in the pontine nuclei without affecting collateral number. This function requires the intracellular phosphatase domain of PTPRO but not its extracellular region. We demonstrate that PTPRO dephosphorylates tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), and that the excessive terminal arborization caused by acute PTPRO loss is rescued by TrkB depletion or phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) inhibition. Together, these findings reveal that PTPRO-mediated TrkB dephosphorylation acts as a molecular brake on corticopontine terminal arbor elaboration.Significance Statement How individual axons regulate terminal branching within target regions is a fundamental question in neural circuit development. This study identifies protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type O (PTPRO), a receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase that negatively regulates signaling through tyrosine phosphorylation, as a selective regulator of higher-order branching in corticopontine terminal arbors. PTPRO dephosphorylates tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), a neurotrophin receptor tyrosine kinase that promotes neuronal growth and branching, thereby restricting terminal arbor complexity without affecting collateral number from the main axon. Given that terminal arbor architecture determines the synaptic territory of each cortical input, PTPRO-dependent constraint on arbor elaboration may represent a general principle by which projection-specific arbor complexity is established across long-range circuits in the central nervous system.

papers.title: Macaque Area LIP Reflects Confidence-Dependent Changes in Decision Policy.
papers.authors: Tu MS, Vivar-Lazo M, Fetsch CR.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The process of forming a decision gives rise to an estimate of its quality or likelihood of success. This graded sense of confidence is important for guiding subsequent decisions, but a neural mechanism linking subjective confidence to formation of the next decision has not been identified. We trained two male rhesus macaques to report a perceptual choice and simultaneous confidence judgment in a reaction-time (RT) motion discrimination task. Monkeys were more likely to repeat a rewarded choice when they reported low confidence on the previous trial, and showed greater changes in RT after a surprising outcome (low-confidence correct or high-confidence error). Neural activity in the lateral intraparietal area (LIP) encoded the previous trial's choice and confidence more strongly after a low-confidence correct trial, and the strength of history encoding was correlated with a trial-by-trial estimate of choice bias. Ramping dynamics of the decoded decision variable also depended systematically on the conjunction of confidence and reward on the previous trial, in a manner that reflected individual differences between animals. The findings suggest that LIP not only reflects the formation of the current decision but could participate in confidence-guided learning via adjustments of the subsequent decision process.Significance statement Decision confidence is of primary interest in the study of metacognition, yet it also plays a key role in learning, serving as a graded prediction of accuracy that modulates the response to feedback. Reanalyzing data from nonhuman primates performing a reaction-time (RT) motion discrimination task with explicit confidence reports, we found that adjustments of choice bias and RT were gated by the animal's self-reported confidence on the previous trial. The interaction of confidence and outcome (reward or punishment) was reflected in the activity of parietal (LIP) neurons on the subsequent trial, in ways largely consistent with the behavioral effects. The results and accompanying computational model suggest plausible functional links between the neuronal substrates of perceptual decision making and reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Hexagonal modulation of theta rhythmic attentional sampling of visual space.
papers.authors: Kienitz R, Moroz M, Martini J, Helfrich RF.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Spatial attention improves visual perception by selecting behaviorally relevant sensory signals. Traditionally, attention has been conceptualized as a static spotlight, while recent evidence posited that attention operates as a moving spotlight that samples visual space sequentially in discrete snapshots that are clocked by theta rhythms (∼3-8 Hz). While theta rhythmic attentional sampling has mainly been observed in fronto-parietal and occipital areas, theta oscillations also hallmark entorhinal-hippocampal grid-cell networks, which encode physical space in hexagonal patterns that guide overt exploration and navigation. We hypothesized that visual attention might rely on the same underlying principles and sample visual space in a hexagonal, grid-like configuration. To test this hypothesis, twenty participants (10 females and 10 males) performed a cue-guided attention task that probed behavioral performance as a function of space and time. Reaction times were assessed as a function of spatial location and varying cue-target intervals, which displayed spatially-structured theta rhythms. Specifically, higher theta power occurred at spatial locations that were aligned to multiples of 60°, consistent with an underlying hexagonal organization. Participants that exhibited stronger hexagonal sampling relied less on the spatial cue to guide their attentional allocation. In sum, these findings suggest that covert visual attention is organized in a hexagonal pattern that might be consistent with the grid-like structure known from the entorhinal-hippocampal system and highlight that theta rhythms could reflect a common organizing principle for spatial cognition.Significance Statement Attention prioritizes sensory inputs to optimize behavior. But how does attention sample the environment in space and time? Here, we demonstrate that attentional sampling of visual space is not uniform, but might preferentially explore locations that are oriented along a hexagonal pattern, reminiscent of the spatial configuration of entorhinal-hippocampal grid cells. Moreover, covert attentional sampling exhibited oscillatory theta signatures (3-8 Hz). In sum, these findings suggest that spatial attention and navigation may share a common organizing principle, and indicate that theta rhythms may orchestrate sampling behaviors in space and time as a unifying principle underlying spatial cognition.

papers.title: Perception of tones versus tone streams under random multi-tone masking and its representation in auditory cortex.
papers.authors: Kistenmacher F, Doll L, Gutschalk A.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: When repeated tones are presented among random masker tones, their perceptual organization is often variable. In some trials, they cannot be segregated from the masker tones. In other trials, often with a delay, they form coherent streams, segregated from the masker tones. A strong awareness-related negativity is evoked by each segregated tone of the stream in auditory cortex. A similar negative-going response has been observed when subtle, isolated tones are detected versus missed, raising the question of whether target tones that do not form a stream under informational masking are still perceived or not. Here a paradigm is introduced to probe this question while activity in auditory cortex was recorded with magnetoencephalography. Human listeners (13 female, 8 male) were instructed to indicate when they detected an isochronous stream of tones under multi-tone masking while listening to the stimulus. Thereafter, they indicated if a cue tone, presented subsequently to each trial, was comprised in the target and masker combination. Results confirmed that target tones could still be perceived in the subset of trials where they did not form a coherent stream, but the detectability in the cued frequency report was higher for tones forming a stream. A prominent awareness-related negativity was only observed when the tones formed a stream, suggesting that this response reflects the perceptual organization of the tones into streams and beyond the pure perception of the tones themselves. We speculate that the perceptual organization into a stream further enhances the detectability of the tones comprised in the stream.Significance Statement Tone sequences may form streams that segregate from competing aspects of the auditory scene, a phenomenon considered comparable to visual object grouping. In multi-tone masking, hearing out streams of repeated tones seemingly enhances tone detectability by a degree that makes it difficult to judge whether these tones could at all be perceived if they had not formed a coherent stream. We present a paradigm that allows for probing both, the perception of target-tone frequency and the formation of coherent streams in the same trials. Applying this setup in magnetoencephalography showed that the perceptual organization into a stream is more strongly represented in auditory cortex than the ability to correctly detect a tone frequency within a random tone masker.

papers.title: Bivalent habenula modulation of human monoaminergic midbrain and cortical pathways.
papers.authors: Hudson LJ, Davey CG, Steward T, Kung PH, Dai Y, Unsworth L, Jamieson AJ, Moffat BA, Glarin R, Harrison BJ.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The habenula is implicated in signaling negative reward prediction errors (RPE), yet direct evidence demonstrating its influence on downstream human brain circuits is limited. Using ultra-high field (7T) fMRI and dynamic causal modelling across two negative RPE-inducing experimental tasks, we characterize habenula-directed connectivity with monoaminergic midbrain and cortical pathways in healthy adults (n = 47, 24 males and 23 females; n = 43, 23 males and 20 females). Negative feedback drove habenula inhibition of ventral tegmental area and dorsal raphe nucleus activity, while positive feedback had an excitatory effect. These core effects are replicated across reversal learning and perceptual decision uncertainty tasks, establishing a generalizable mechanism for behavioral adaptation. Task-specific modulatory effects emerged in pathways between the subcortical and cortical regions (ventral tegmental area→dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, dorsal raphe nucleus→medial prefrontal cortex, and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex→habenula), revealing context-dependent cortical elaboration of negative RPE-driven habenula signals. This provides the first evidence in humans, using model-based effective connectivity, for bivalent modulation of habenula function on monoaminergic midbrain and cortical pathways, demonstrating how the brain integrates negative and positive signals to guide adaptive behavior.Significance Statement The habenula - an epithalamic brain region - plays a key role in the encoding of reward and punishment. Animal studies have demonstrated the habenula to be bivalently modulated by aversive and appetitive stimuli, resulting in the bidirectional modulation of monoaminergic brain region activity. Despite this evidence, the directional impact of bivalently modulated habenula activity on its circuitry has yet to be investigated in humans. This study leverages ultra-high field (7T) fMRI and dynamic causal modelling to reveal the impact of bivalent habenula modulation on monoaminergic midbrain and cortical regions across two distinct tasks. Through these methodologies, we demonstrate the habenula to have a key role in guiding adaptive behavior.

papers.title: Transient feedforward communication between somatosensory and premotor cortex supports goal-directed behavior.
papers.authors: Ranjbar-Slamloo Y, Kamigaki T.
papers.abstract: Goal-directed behavior requires sensory information to be transformed into motor commands, yet the precise temporal structure of communication between sensory and motor cortices during this process remains poorly understood. By simultaneously recording spiking activity from primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and secondary motor cortex (M2) in mice performing a tactile delayed go/no-go task, we identified a brief, stimulus-triggered communication window that predicted behavioral success. Time-shifted canonical correlation analysis revealed a sharp, feedforward surge in S1 → M2 coupling peaking at a short latency, as expected for a potentially direct transmission pathway. This transient interaction conveyed stimulus-selective information such that the S1 → M2 communication subspace aligned with stimulus-coding axes in both regions. In contrast, M2 → S1 feedback interactions were weaker and delayed. Brief optogenetic suppression of S1 reduced both M2 stimulus selectivity and behavioral discriminability, consistent with a functional role of the transient S1 → M2 coupling. These findings demonstrate that sensorimotor transformation is supported not by sustained linear coupling along the stimulus- or choice- axis, but by a short-lived and highly selective feedforward communication channel that rapidly transmits reliable sensory representations into motor-planning circuits.

papers.title: Establishing Potosi Virus as a Human Pathogen: Fatal Neuroinvasive Disease in a B-Cell-Depleted Patient.
papers.authors: Abbatemarco JR, Begum F, Villalba JA, Davis E, Bhatnagar J, Brault AC, Calvert AE, Chomyk A, Gould CV, Isada CM, Jung JU, Jones SE, Kang S, Ko Y, Li Y, Nakamura K, Najm L, Staples EJ, Trapp BD, Tipping P, Yeaney GA, Fox RJ.
papers.abstract: Objectives To establish Potosi virus, a mosquito-borne member of the family Peribunyaviridae , as a neuroinvasive human pathogen. Methods Case report. Results A 37-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis on long-term rituximab developed rapidly progressive dementia. Serial MRI demonstrated progressive generalized atrophy. CSF showed transient, minimal lymphocytic pleocytosis. Extensive infectious, autoimmune, and prion evaluations were unrevealing, but CSF metagenomic sequencing detected all 3 genome segments for Potosi virus. Postmortem examination revealed diffuse meningoencephalitis with T-cell-predominant leptomeningeal and perivascular inflammation. Molecular analyses confirmed multiple nucleotide sequences with >99+% concordance with a known Potosi strain, with widespread viral infection confirmed by immunohistochemistry demonstrating intracellular and extracellular viral antigen. Electron microscopy demonstrated particles of a size consistent with the Peribunyaviridae family. Metagenomic sequencing of RNA extracted from frozen brain tissue identified all 3 Potosi virus gene segments without other infectious entities. Findings were concordant across multiple laboratories and institutions. Discussion Potosi virus can cause fatal neuroinvasive disease in humans, as evidenced by convergent postmortem neuropathologic, molecular, and ultrastructural evidence. Chronic B-cell depletion may increase susceptibility to severe disease with arboviral infections, which may present without conventional CNS inflammatory markers. CSF metagenomic sequencing should be considered in immunocompromised patients with unexplained progressive neurologic decline.

papers.title: Resting-State Functional MRI and Clinical Outcomes After Acute Disorders of Consciousness: A Systematic Review.
papers.authors: Kazazian K, Czink D, Iansavitchene A, Owen AM, Norton L.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Accurate assessment and prognostication of patients with acute disorders of consciousness (DoC) after severe brain injury remain a substantial clinical challenge. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) measures spontaneous, temporally correlated brain activity in the absence of external stimulation and provides objective insight into the integrity of large-scale neural networks that support brain function. Emerging evidence suggests that assessing neural integrity using rs-fMRI may improve outcome prediction in patients with acute DoC. This review summarizes the current evidence of rs-fMRI as an assessment tool during the acute phase of severe brain injury. Methods Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature search using MEDLINE and Embase databases from January 2006 to March 2026. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed empirical investigations of adult patients with acute DoC (<28 days postinjury) that examined associations between rs-fMRI measures and clinical outcomes. The systematic review protocol was registered in the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251085923). Results Of 396 studies screened, 30 met eligibility criteria. Across these studies, a total of 800 patients (mean age = 48, 69% male) were scanned at a weighted average of 9.31 days after intensive care unit admission. Ten studies included patients exclusively with traumatic brain injury, 8 with cardiac arrest, 2 with encephalopathy, and 10 included mixed etiologies. The most frequently assessed resting-state networks were the default mode (n = 20) and executive control networks (n = 11), followed by visual (n = 6), salience (n = 6), sensorimotor (n = 6), and auditory (n = 5) networks. Across studies, significant associations between rs-fMRI measures and outcome were consistently reported, despite heterogeneity in methodology. The most commonly reported patient outcomes were functional or neurologic status, assessed at hospital discharge or between 3 and 12 months postinjury. Discussion Current evidence consistently demonstrates that rs-fMRI acquired during the acute phase of brain injury is associated with neurologic and functional outcomes in patients with DoC. In addition, rs-fMRI may help identify patients more likely to recover consciousness and achieve favorable functional outcomes by characterizing the integrity of large-scale brain networks. However, substantial heterogeneity and small sample sizes limit comparability across studies. Standardized acquisition and analysis frameworks, along with larger prospective studies, are needed to validate the clinical utility of rs-fMRI and support translation into an assessment tool after brain injury.

papers.title: Cenobamate in Focal-Onset Refractory and Super-Refractory Status Epilepticus: A Multicenter Cohort Study With Matched Analysis.
papers.authors: Campos-Fernandez D, Abraira L, Vila-Sala C, Sansa G, Sala Padró JX, San-Pedro-Murillo E, García-Díaz AI, Quílez A, Quintana M, López-Maza S, Garcés-Pellejero M, Bellido Castillo E, Fonseca E, Toledo M, Santamarina E.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Cenobamate (CNB) is an antiseizure medication (ASM) with demonstrated efficacy in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but its role in status epilepticus (SE) remains unclear. Emerging evidence suggests that it may achieve early clinically meaningful seizure control at relatively low doses, with an acceptable safety profile, supporting its potential utility as an urgent adjunctive therapy in severe refractory epilepsy. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of CNB for the treatment of focal-onset refractory SE (RSE) and super-refractory SE (SRSE) in real-world clinical practice. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained registry including adult patients with focal RSE and SRSE treated between January 2022 and October 2025. Clinical, EEG, and treatment data were collected. The primary outcome was sustained SE termination (>24 hours) with electroclinical resolution attributable to CNB. A secondary propensity score-matched analysis (1:2) compared CNB-exposed patients with matched nonexposed controls from the same registry (2011-2025), using target trial emulation principles. Results Thirty-one patients received CNB (mean age 61 ± 21 years; 54.8% male); 45.2% met criteria for SRSE. CNB was initiated a median of 4 days (interquartile range [IQR] 2-12) after SE onset after failure of 5 ASMs (IQR 4-5), at a median starting dose of 50 mg/d (IQR 25-50). Sustained SE resolution occurred in 26 patients (83.9%), including all patients with RSE (17/17) and 64.3% with SRSE. Response occurred after a median of 2 days (IQR 1-6). In the matched cohort analysis (28 CNB exposed vs 56 controls), SE resolution was higher in CNB-treated patients (82.1% vs 57.1%; p = 0.02). In multivariable analysis, CNB exposure was independently associated with SE resolution (adjusted odds ratio 5.9, 95% CI 1.2-30, p = 0.03). No serious CNB-related adverse events occurred. Mild adverse events were observed in 51.6%, most commonly somnolence. In-hospital mortality was 22.6% with no deaths attributed to CNB. Discussion In this multicenter real-world cohort, CNB was associated with high rates of sustained SE termination in RSE and SRSE and improved outcomes compared with matched controls, without serious safety signals. These findings support CNB as a potential adjunctive therapeutic option in refractory focal SE. Classification of evidence This study provides Class IV evidence that CNB is effective as an adjunctive therapy for the control of focal-onset RSE and SRSE in adult patients.

papers.title: Persistent Skeletal Deficits Following Weight Restoration in a Rodent Model of Anorexia Nervosa.
papers.authors: Jafari M, Brooks DJ, Swanson B, Bouxsein ML, Breithaupt L, Kaiser UB, Rutkove SB, Rosa-Caldwell ME.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
papers.abstract: Purpose: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is associated with significant changes in bone density and microstructure. However, the extent and nature of skeletal recovery following weight restoration is unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate these changes in bone during simulated AN in rats across short- and long-term recovery. Methods : Female Sprague Dawley rats were exposed to 50-60% food restriction for 30 days to simulate AN, followed by recovery periods of 5, 15, and 30 days. Bone parameters were assessed longitudinally using peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) and micro-computed tomography (µCT). Bodyweight and muscle strength were correlated with bone parameters. Results: AN resulted in significant reductions in total and trabecular bone density, as well as impairments in cortical and trabecular microarchitecture. Even with weight restoration, these deficits persisted and the compensatory responses were not sufficient for bone recovery. Bodyweight showed an association with total and trabecular bone density. Measures of muscle strength also correlated with total and trabecular density and were additive in multiple regression analysis prediction of total and trabecular bone density when combined with bodyweight. Conclusion: Recovery from AN-induced bone disorders is incomplete even after weight restoration and likely requires targeted interventions beyond nutritional rehabilitation. Furthermore, muscle function is an important predictor of bone health when combined with bodyweight.

papers.title: Untangling time and prematurity in brain development.
papers.authors: Kelly-Goss MR, Crouch EE.
papers.abstract: Cerebellar developmental differences between preterm- and term-born children persist into early childhood.

papers.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth.
papers.authors: Sanidas G, Simonti G, Ghaemmaghami J, Woyshner K, Polyviou A, Vidva R, Lowe C, Vij A, Bittel D, Triantafyllou M, Wolff N, Cardenas R, Chen H, Almeida F, Sudhakar S, Mankad K, Koutroulis I, Pettersen HS, Stein-O'Brien G, Sidiropoulos DN, Gallo V, Kratimenos P.
papers.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

papers.title: DuMeta++: Spatiotemporal Dual Meta-Learning for Generalizable Few-Shot Brain Tissue Segmentation Across Diverse Ages.
papers.authors: Sun Y, Shu J, Ma J, Wang F.
papers.abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain tissues from MRI scans is critical for neuroscience and clinical applications, but achieving consistent performance across the human lifespan remains challenging due to dynamic, age-related changes in brain appearance and morphology. While prior work has sought to mitigate these shifts by using self-supervised regularization with paired longitudinal data, such data are often unavailable in practice. To address this, we propose DuMeta++, a dual meta-learning framework that operates without paired longitudinal data. Our approach integrates: (1) meta-feature learning to extract age-agnostic semantic representations of spatiotemporally evolving brain structures, and (2) meta-initialization learning to enable data-efficient adaptation of the segmentation model. Furthermore, we propose a memory-bank-based class-aware regularization strategy to enforce longitudinal consistency without explicit longitudinal super-vision. We further characterize the convergence of the dual meta-learning pipeline under standard smoothness assumptions. Extensive experiments on the iSeg-2019 and ADNI datasets under one- and five-shot settings demonstrate that DuMeta++ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both segmentation accuracy and longitudinal consistency. Code will be available at https:// github.com/ladderlab-xjtu/DuMeta++.

papers.title: GeoMind: Dancing with Geometric Brain Rhythm on Symmetric Positive Definite Manifolds.
papers.authors: Dan T, Huang X, Cao Y, Ding J, Yang Y, Wu G.
papers.abstract: State space model (SSM) is a powerful tool in neuroscience field to characterize the dynamic nature of brain functions by elucidating the mechanism of how brain system transits between brain states and how underlying states give rise to the observed neural activities. Although tremendous efforts have been made to lend the power of deep learning and mathematical insight of SSM in various functional neuroimaging studies, current state-of-the-art methods lack a holistic view of brain state evolution as a self-organized dynamical system where each part of the brain is functionally inter-connected. Since the topological co-activation of functional fluctuations exhibits an intrinsic geometric pattern (symmetric and positive definite, SPD) on the Riemannian manifold, the call for understanding how a selective set of functional connectivities in the brain supports diverse behavior and cognition emerge a new machine learning scenario of manifold-based SSM for largescale functional neuroimages. To that end, we propose a geometric neural network of SSM, coined GeoMind, designed to uncover evolving brain states by tracking the trajectory of functional dynamics on a high-dimensional Riemannian manifold of SPD matrices. GeoMind demonstrates promising results in identifying specific brain states on task-based functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) data, as well as in diseases early diagnosis for Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease and Autism, by using resting-state fMRI. These results highlight the applicability of GeoMind in neuroscience research. To further evaluate generalizability of GeoMind, we applied GeoMind to electroencephalography (EEG) emotion datasets, outperforming competing methods and demonstrating scalability across neuroimaging modalities.

papers.title: Genetic architecture of cichlid brain morphology.
papers.authors: Morris J, Rivas-Sánchez DF, Elkin J, Hickey A, Fischer B, Marconi A, Durbin R, Turner GF, Santos ME, Montgomery SH.
papers.abstract: How evolutionary and developmental processes interact to determine axes of neural variation that produce behavioural diversity has been debated for many decades, with alternative hypotheses giving differential emphasis to functional coupling, which favours co-evolution, and developmental constraint, which enforces it. A critical omission is data on the genetic architecture of brain size and structure, which more closely illuminates the shared developmental dependencies between components of an integrated system. Here, we exploit ecological divergence between Astatotilapia calliptera and Aulonocara stuartgranti, two closely related cichlid species from Lake Malawi, to explore the genetic architecture of brain evolution. Using computer vision and machine learning techniques to extract volumetric data from micro-tomographic images, we first demonstrate significant divergence in brain composition between these species. Genomic and micro-tomographic imaging data from a population of hybrids generated between the two species were used to investigate genetic factors shaping this differentiation. We show that the majority of brain components are integrated phenotypically in hybrids, but genetic correlations between them are generally weaker. We further show that variation in multiple brain components is associated with variation in largely structure-specific quantitative trait loci, rather than determined by genetic factors with broad effects across the entire brain. These results suggest a genetic architecture that can facilitate modular changes in brain structure, and imply that individual components are independently evolvable.

papers.title: Imaging of the inferior alveolar nerve using dental-dedicated MRI at 0.55 T: Comparison of a deep learning-based accelerated sequence with a conventional sequence.
papers.authors: Hinsen M, Kopp M, Zeilinger M, Mathy CS, Uder M, Greiser A, Weber M, Willershausen I, Hellwig K.
papers.abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to investigate the feasibility of low-field dental MRI in the evaluation of the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) and the acceleration of image acquisition with a deep learning (DL)-based sequence. Therefore, overall image quality (OIQ), image artefacts and delineation of the IAN were investigated. Methods In this single-centre retrospective study, we enrolled 39 patients who underwent dental MRI using a dedicated dental coil on a 0.55 T MRI system. A conventional T1-weighted gradient-echo 3D sequence and a T1-weighted gradient-echo 3D sequence with advanced DL-based reconstruction were acquired. Both sequences were evaluated for OIQ, image artefacts in and conspicuity of the IAN using a Likert scale from 1 to 5. Interrater agreement was assessed using weighted Cohen's κ coefficients. As quantitative measurements, the apparent signal-to-noise ratio (aSNR) and the diameter of the IAN were determined. Results Thirty-three examinations were included, OIQ was rated higher for the accelerated sequence compared with the conventional sequence for both readers (p < 0.01). Image artefacts were lower in the accelerated sequence for both readers (p < 0.001). Accordingly, the delineation of the IAN was improved for both sides (p < 0.001) in the accelerated sequence. Interrater agreement between readers was substantial/good to almost perfect/excellent across all measures. aSNR was increased in the accelerated sequence (p < 0.001), whereas IAN diameter did not differ. Conclusions This study demonstrates that a DL-accelerated T1-weighted gradient-echo 3D sequence for dental-dedicated MRI is feasible for imaging of the IAN with improved image quality while reducing acquisition time by 50%. Advances in knowledge Reduction of scan time and superior image quality could help establish dental-dedicated MRI as a radiation-free alternative for dentomaxillofacial imaging.

papers.title: The amygdaloid complex: from morphology to neurodegeneration.
papers.authors: Rodrigo H, Rábano A, Vyas S, Herrero MT.
papers.abstract: The amygdaloid complex is one of the most structurally and functionally heterogeneous regions of the mammalian brain, acting as an integrative node between sensory, mnemonic and visceral systems. It comprises a set of subnuclei whose cytoarchitectural differentiation, neurochemical profiles and anatomical boundaries have been debated since the earliest descriptions. This heterogeneity is established during ontogenetic development, assembling progenitors from pallial and subpallial domains, and preoptic and hypothalamic territories, resulting in a highly connected network. Maturation is not complete at birth, the amygdala changes through childhood and adolescence, leaving a protracted window of environmental sensitivity. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have added a molecular layer to this framework, resolving populations that no single marker separates, and set explicit limits on the resolution at which rodent-derived subdivisions can be transferred to the human amygdala. Together these levels of description provide a structural framework for understanding its functions, which include emotional regulation and conditioned fear, social and sexual behaviours, decision-making, reward and punishment processing, empathy and memory modulation. Cross-species comparison reveals further variation, particularly the expansion of the basolateral complex in primates and the redistribution of neurons towards the lateral nucleus in humans. In summary, the amygdala acts as a densely connected hub with a broad role not only in physiological and psychological health but also in disease states; indeed, the amygdala is affected early in several neurodegenerative disorders, and in some (notably limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy and argyrophilic grain disease) it is among the first regions in which pathology is detected.

papers.title: Cerebellar subregions support social cognition in early behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Chatzidimitriou E, Yang WFZ, Leng F, Syed F, McEachen B, Ivry RB, Rosen HJ, Seeley WW, Gorno-Tempini ML, Kramer JH, Miller BL, Rankin KP.
papers.abstract: Social cognitive deficits manifest early in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), compromising individuals' ability to interpret social cues, empathize, and maintain interpersonal relationships. Current neurobiological models emphasize cortical network disruption, particularly within the salience, semantic appraisal, and default mode networks, as primary contributors to social dysfunction. However, despite the increasingly recognized role of the cerebellum in higher-order cognitive and socioemotional processes, its contributions to social deficits remains underexplored in bvFTD. Here, we investigated the unique and network-level influences of cerebellar subregions on social cognition across experimental and real-world assessments in early-stage bvFTD. A total of 107 individuals with bvFTD and 100 healthy controls were evaluated across three social domains: theory of mind (ToM) (The Awareness of Social Inference Test-Social Inference-Enriched, TASIT-SIE; Cognitive Emotional Perspective Taking Test), emotion reading (Dynamic Affect Recognition Test; TASIT-Emotion Evaluation Test; Comprehensive Affect Testing System), and real-life empathy (Revised Self-Monitoring Scale; Interpersonal Reactivity Index). Using a functional cerebellar parcellation, we extracted volumes of posterior cerebellar subregions implicated in social-linguistic and multiple-demand networks from participants' structural MRIs. To address the high collinearity between cerebellar and cortical atrophy patterns, we applied sequential regression, partial least squares correlation, and dominance analysis to characterize brain-behavior relationships. Additionally, supplementary structural equation modelling (SEM) examined whether the associations between cerebellar integrity and social cognition was mediated by executive functioning. Our results showed that cerebellar subregional integrity contributed to social cognitive deficits in individuals with early-stage bvFTD. Cerebellar subregions, particularly right Crus I and II, showed the strongest and most selective contribution to high-level inferential Theory of Mind performance. Tasks involving dynamic emotion stimuli exhibited a more distributed pattern of cerebello-cerebral involvement. By contrast, questionnaire-based measures of real-world social functioning were less prominently represented in the latent covariance structure. SEM further showed that cerebellar integrity remained directly associated with social cognition after accounting for executive functioning, whereas the indirect association through executive functioning was not significant. These findings highlight the task-dependent nature of cerebellar involvement in social cognition, and demonstrate that time-limited experimental tasks, particularly those involving inferential reasoning about beliefs and affect, are likely to be especially valuable in detecting subtle cerebello-cerebral network dysfunction that questionnaire-based measures may overlook. Our results extend cortex-centric models of social dysfunction in bvFTD by demonstrating that cerebellar subregions contribute to distributed cerebello-cerebral systems associated with social cognitive performance. These findings provide a foundation for future longitudinal and mechanistic studies of cerebello-cerebral dysfunction in neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Alzheimer's pathology mediates arteriolosclerosis and cerebral amyloid angiopathy associations with cognition.
papers.authors: Hayes CA, Dharmapuri A, Agwu C, Ramirez V, Newman J, Chambers M, Odden MC, Younes K.
papers.abstract: Vascular and neurodegenerative pathologies frequently co-occur in aging brains, yet the mechanisms linking vascular neuropathologies to cognitive impairment remain incompletely understood. We examined whether Alzheimer's disease neuropathologic change (ADNC) and Lewy body disease (LBD) mediate or modify associations between vascular neuropathologies and domain-specific cognitive performance. The analytic sample included 1,269 decedents (mean age at death, 84.3 ± 9.1 years; 43.3% female; 94.7% White). At the last evaluation prior to death, 22.5% were cognitively normal, 2.4% were impaired but not mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 14.9% had MCI, and 60.2% had dementia. Vascular neuropathologies included arteriolosclerosis, atherosclerosis of the circle of Willis, cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), gross infarcts/lacunes, and microinfarcts. Multivariable linear regression models evaluated associations with harmonized memory, executive function, and language z-scores adjusting for age at death, sex, education, and apolipoprotein E ε4 status. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was tested. Mediation models estimated indirect and direct effects of vascular neuropathologies on cognition through ADNC or LBD using 5,000 bootstrap samples. Greater arteriolosclerosis severity was associated with worse memory (β=-0.16, 95% CI -0.23 to -0.09), executive function (β=-0.18, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.11), and language (β=-0.18, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.12; all p<0.001). CAA was strongly associated with poorer cognition across domains, including memory (β=-0.26, 95% CI -0.33 to -0.19; p<0.001). Atherosclerosis and infarcts showed more limited associations, while microinfarcts were not significantly associated with cognition. Mediation analyses indicated that ADNC statistically accounted for approximately 13-29% of the associations between arteriolosclerosis and cognition across domains and 64-91% of the associations between CAA and cognition. Direct effects of arteriolosclerosis remained significant, whereas CAA effects were largely explained by ADNC. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was limited, although LBD attenuated associations of arteriolosclerosis and CAA with executive function. Mediation through LBD was not observed. This novel evidence shows that vascular neuropathologies influence cognition through defined pathways with statistically significant patterns of associations. In this autopsy-confirmed cohort, vascular neuropathologies showed different patterns of association with domain-specific cognitive performance and ADNC. A larger proportion of the association involving CAA was statistically accounted for by ADNC, whereas direct associations remained more apparent for arteriolosclerosis. This study clarifies how vascular and neurodegenerative processes interact to shape cognitive impact and inform mechanistic preventions.

papers.title: Altered medial prefrontal-striatal connectivity and plasticity in humanized CBLN2 mice.
papers.authors: S Narasimhan KK, Chettiar PB, Sabnis SS, Kola PK, Thakur SS, Shelkar GP, Asati DG, Gawande DY, Jadhav SR, Dravid SM.
papers.abstract: Deciphering processes that are responsible for differences in brain development and architecture among species may provide clues to the species-specific program and may facilitate a mechanistic understanding of vulnerability to neuropsychiatric disorders. It has recently been shown that the promoter of the CBLN2 gene, which codes for a synaptogenic factor, cerebellin 2 (Cbln2), has a repressor element in mice but not in humans. A humanized mouse lacking this repressor (hCbln2) reproduces higher spine density in medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) neurons and higher corticothalamic connectivity observed in humans. Cbln2 is part of a trans-synaptic complex that includes glutamate delta-1 receptor (GluD1) and neurexins (Nrxn) (GluD1-Cbln2-Nrxn). Interestingly, we have previously reported a contrasting striatal patch-matrix expression pattern of GluD1 in mouse versus monkey, suggesting a potential role of the GluD1-Cbln complex in species differences. In this study, we examined the synaptic organization and function in the cortex and dorsal striatum of hCbln2 mice. Consistent with previous reports, hCbln2 mice exhibited increased vGluT1 expression in the mPFC, indicating enhanced intracortical connectivity. Electrophysiological recordings further revealed an increased mEPSC frequency along with a reduced mIPSC frequency in layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons, suggesting an increase in excitatory/inhibitory balance. These changes were accompanied by enhanced mTOR signalling and autophagic deficits in the mPFC. Contrasting synaptic changes were observed in the striatum with an increase in vGluT2 and a reduction in vGluT1, together with a decrease in GluD1-Cbln1 and an increase in hevin. Importantly, corticostriatal dysfunction characterized by a reduction in cortical contribution to mEPSCs and impaired DHPG-induced synaptic depression was observed in the hCbln2 medium spiny neurons. Further, hCbln2 mice displayed increased repetitive behaviour together with social and affective-like deficits, consistent with autism-relevant phenotypes. Collectively, these findings identify humanized Cbln2 regulation as a driver of divergent cortical and striatal synaptic remodelling, disrupted corticostriatal synaptic function, and behavioural abnormalities relevant to neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: Upper-limb accelerometry in children with cerebral palsy: a scoping review.
papers.authors: Youngsub H, Choe Y, Kwon JY.
papers.abstract: Purpose Among children with cerebral palsy (CP), gains on standardized upper-limb (UL) capacity measures do not necessarily translate into greater spontaneous arm use in everyday environments. This scoping review mapped how UL accelerometry - predominantly bilateral wrist-worn accelerometry - is used in children and adolescents with CP to examine (i) construct validity against standardized UL measures and (ii) intervention monitoring in treatment settings and everyday environments. Methods Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance, PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL were searched for English-language studies published between January 2000 and May 16, 2026. Peer-reviewed studies were included if they involved children and adolescents (0-18 years) with CP that used UL-worn accelerometers to report quantitative metrics in standardized or free-living settings. Results Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. In construct-validity studies, asymmetry-focused metrics showed the most consistent associations with standardized bimanual measures and manual ability classifications, with the strongest relationships observed in standardized sessions and weaker, context-dependent associations in free-living monitoring. In intervention studies, accelerometry was consistently sensitive to within-session dose and immediate behavioral change during intervention sessions. However, translation to spontaneous everyday arm use was heterogeneous, with several studies showing improved clinical scores without parallel gains in free-living accelerometry metrics. Conclusion UL accelerometry provides objective performance information to complement assessment and neurorehabilitation monitoring in children with CP, especially when asymmetry-oriented metrics are matched to the clinical question and recording context. Its clearest current role is as a complement to standardized assessment and as a tool to quantify in-session engagement, whereas evidence for sustained transfer to everyday arm use remains inconsistent. Future studies should consistently report device model and placement, wear protocol, valid wear time, preprocessing methods, and metric definitions.

papers.title: Outcomes of multidisciplinary cognitive and social communication traumatic brain injury rehabilitation in Qatar: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Kareem Abughalieh BMA, Al Barghothi MBH.
papers.abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) often leads to long-term social and cognitive dysfunction, and even more so in Arabic-speaking communities due to the lack of culturally appropriate rehabilitation programs. Aims This study examines the efficacy of a structured multidisciplinary cognitive-social rehabilitation program on cognitive functioning, communication, and vocational reintegration in TBI patients in Qatar. Method Retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data of TBI patients 15-65 years old admitted to the Adult Day Rehabilitation Unit, Qatar Rehabilitation Institute, from January 2022 to December 2024. All the participants had cognitive and communication impairment and were treated with a multidisciplinary rehabilitation program consisting of individualized speech-language therapy and occupational therapy. Outcome measures included the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) of cognitive function, Functional Communication Measures (FCMs) of social interaction and communication, "the Ability to participate in social roles and activities (Neuro-QoL short form)," and the Functional Independence Measure (FIM) of global functional status and return-to-work or school. The measures were assessed at baseline, mid-intervention, post-intervention, and follow-up. Results Post-rehabilitation evaluations reported improvement in all areas of outcome. Participants showed greater improvements in MoCA (+4.3 vs + 1.3, p < .001), FIM (+14.45 vs + 5.1, p < .002), the Neuro-QoL scores improved by (+11.23 points), and FCMs (+7.0 vs + 2.2, p < .001) pre and post program. Return-to-work was achieved in 68.8%. Effect sizes were large (Cohen's d > 1.0). Conclusions The results suggest the effectiveness of combined cognitive-social rehabilitation for TBI patients, emphasizing concurrent speech and occupational therapist intervention benefits. The intervention also demonstrated functional improvement in daily life, supporting the significance of multidisciplinary interventions to recovery and social reintegration after TBI.

papers.title: Italian guidelines for speech and language therapy in patients with stroke or primary progressive aphasia. Recommendations from the Italian neuropsychological society.
papers.authors: Papagno C, Cappa S, Cruciani F, Difonzo T, Ferroni L, Miceli G, Mitrova Z, Quaranta D, Romani C, Saulle R, Soda M, Vecchi S, Viganò M, Trojano L.
papers.abstract: Background Aphasia can be frequently observed after left hemisphere stroke, but also in neurodegenerative diseases, as in primary progressive aphasia (PPA). Aphasia strongly impacts on quality of life, and rehabilitation of People with Aphasia (PWA) presents clinicians with complex challenges. Aims An ad-hoc Scientific Panel, including 20 members (neurologists, physiatrists, psychologists, therapists, nurses, PWA representatives), selected 4 questions not addressed by current international guidelines: (1) effectiveness of SLT for post-stroke aphasia provided by professionals vs non-specialized personnel; (2) effectiveness of SLT in the chronic phase vs no treatment; (3) effectiveness of non-invasive neuromodulation combined with SLT vs stand-alone SLT for PWA after stroke; (4) effectiveness of non-invasive neuromodulation combined with SLT vs stand-alone SLT for PPA patients. Methods The Scientific Panel and experienced methodologists followed common guidelines for systematic reviews and the PICO framework for scrutinizing several databases (last search: March 2023). Recommendations were based on evidence analysis according to the GRADE methodology. Key findings The Scientific Panel suggested one strong and three conditional recommendations, although quality of evidence was low or very low. Conclusions The present guidelines, published by the Italian Higher Institute for Health on December 19, 2023, supplement the most recent international guidelines, particularly in tackling PPA.

papers.title: Traumatic brain injury history moderates age-related episodic memory change in older veterans: the DOD-ADNI longitudinal cohort study.
papers.authors: Saltiel N, Howard E, Lee AJ, Moody JN, Hayes JP, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative*.
papers.abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) has been associated with increased risk of dementia and cognitive decline, but its relationship with age-related cognitive trajectories remains unclear. This study examined associations between TBI history and age-related changes in cognitive function in aging military veterans. Methods Data from the Department of Defense-Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (DOD-ADNI) repository were used to evaluate whether TBI history moderates the relationship between age and longitudinal change in domain-specific cognitive performance. To investigate these relationships, this study utilized data from neuropsychological assessments collected at baseline and 12-month timepoints from a sample consisting of 203 Vietnam War veterans, 99% of whom were male, aged 60-84 years, with varying TBI histories. Results Results revealed that TBI history moderated the association between age and change in episodic memory. Older age was associated with greater memory decline among individuals with TBI. No interaction effects were observed for executive functions or language. Conclusions These findings suggest that TBI history is associated with differences in age-related episodic memory change and highlight the importance of considering TBI history in studies of cognitive aging. Considering the modest proportion of variance explained by the interaction and homogeneous veteran sample, additional research is warranted.

papers.title: Hospital mortality and discharge destination prediction after fall-related traumatic brain injury in older adults.
papers.authors: Osong B, Armstrong M, Williams H, Sribnick EA, Groner JI, Xiang H.
papers.abstract: Objective Develop prediction models to support care for older adults with fall-related traumatic brain injury (TBI). Summary of background Fall-related TBI is a leading cause of hospitalization and death among older adults. Prognostication remains challenging in this population because frailty and comorbidity burden greatly influence recovery trajectories. Tailored prognostic models to support individualized patient care remain limited. Patients and methods Data from 179,287 older adults (≥65 years) hospitalized with fall-related TBI in the NTDB (2017-2021) were analyzed. MARS models were developed to predict in-hospital mortality and discharge destination (home, rehabilitation, or care facility). Predictor selection was guided by clinicians' input, and model performance was evaluated using discrimination and calibration measures. Results The mortality model showed high discrimination (AUC 0.88, 95% CI 0.87-0.89; balanced accuracy 79%). The discharge model demonstrated moderate-to-good discrimination across discharge destinations (AUCs 0.77-0.85; balanced accuracies 70%-77%). Both models showed good calibration and were implemented as interactive web-based tools. Conclusion This study developed two prognostic models that provide individualized outcome probabilities to support prognostic communication and care planning for older adults hospitalized with fall-related TBI.

papers.title: Primary language as a moderator of social integration and functional independence after traumatic brain injury in U.S. older adults.
papers.authors: Jung W, Taylor J, Vazquez CE, Ogawa E, Yoo-Jeong M, Singer J, Hwang D, Smith ML.
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examined whether primary language moderates the relationship between social integration and functional independence among older adults in the U.S. following traumatic brain injury (TBI). Methods A secondary analysis was conducted using data from the Traumatic Brain Injury Model System National Database (TBIMS-NDB), including 1,030 individuals aged 65-88 with mild, moderate, or severe TBI. Of these, 88.3% reported English as their primary language, while 11.7% reported a non-English language. Social integration was assessed using the Participation Assessment with Recombined Tools-Objective, and functional independence was measured via the Functional Independence Measure. Primary language was categorized as English or non-English. Hayes's PROCESS macro was used for moderation analysis. Results Social integration significantly predicted functional independence (β = 15.94, p < .001), controlling for demographics and TBI severity. A significant interaction between social integration and primary language (β = 10.05, p < .01) indicated that the relationship was stronger among non-English speakers. Conclusion Primary language plays a moderating role in the link between social integration and functional independence post-TBI. These findings highlight the need for culturally and linguistically tailored interventions to improve outcomes for older adults with TBI.

papers.title: A sulfotyrosine motif in the human TrkB extracellular domain is required for activation by the agonist antibody ZEB85.
papers.authors: Briggs DC, Duffy RT, Ateaque S, Maslen S, Nagaraj H, Barde YA, DiStefano PS, Lindsay RM, Armstrong PC, Peach CJ, McDonald NQ.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: The brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) signaling axis is a key effector of synaptic plasticity and neuroprotection. While TrkB activation is a major target to prevent neural dysfunction, stimulation with exogenous BDNF administration has not proven tractable given the unfavorable physiochemical properties of BDNF. In addition, BDNF also activates a cell death pathway by binding to the neurotrophin receptor p75. The TrkB agonist antibody ZEB85 provides an alternative route to the selective activation of TrkB. To understand the ZEB85 mechanism of action, we mapped the binding site for ZEB85 to the TrkB extracellular juxtamembrane domain and found a sulfotyrosine modification at residue 400 crucial for ZEB85 interaction and activation of TrkB signaling. We determined the structures of ZEB85 and BDNF bound to their respective binding sites on human TrkB suggesting independent sites for each ligand, despite prior evidence of direct competition. Using structure-guided BDNF- and ZEB85-binding deficient TrkB mutants, we assessed their ability to sequester ligands from full-length TrkB in cultured human neurons. We found that the BDNF binding site extends into the juxtamembrane domain of TrkB but does not require the sulfotyrosine 400 to activate TrkB. Together with biophysical analysis and AlphaFold modeling, these results explain how BDNF can displace ZEB85 from TrkB through an overlapping epitope. Our findings reveal unique features of TrkB, not present in the related neurotrophin receptors TrkA and TrkC and suggest future directions to explore the role of sulfotyrosine in TrkB signaling.

papers.title: Toward Culturally Responsive Clinical Practice: Intercultural Speech-Language Pathology Services for Acquired Pragmatic Communication Disorders in Traumatic Brain Injury and Right-Hemisphere Damage.
papers.authors: Brown WC, Fullwood SP, Fannin DK, Hardin KY, Minga J.
papers.abstract: Purpose Acquired pragmatic communication disorders following traumatic brain injury and right-hemisphere damage can disrupt patient-provider interactions that are essential for effective health care. This clinical focus article explores how these disorders intersect with sociocultural factors such as race, language access, and health literacy, contributing to disparities in health care engagement and outcomes to offer culturally specific considerations. Method This clinical focus article integrates evidence from neurogenic communication disorders, intercultural pragmatics, and health disparities to inform assessment and intervention considerations for acquired pragmatic communication disorders across diverse cultural communication contexts and structural barriers in health care systems. Results Impairments in pragmatic communication can affect discourse management, conversational participation, and comprehension, reducing opportunities for shared understanding during clinical encounters. When these impairments intersect with cultural communication differences or limited health literacy, patients may experience greater difficulty navigating health care systems and participating in medical decision making. Current speech-language pathology assessment practices and rehabilitation models often fail to capture these contextual influences on communication. Considerations for speech-language pathology service improvements related to assessment and treatment are offered. Conclusions Advancing equitable neurogenic rehabilitation requires integrating intercultural pragmatics and sociocultural perspectives into assessment and treatment. Approaches such as dynamic assessment, holistic assessment, and telehealth offer practical pathways to improve assessment practices for individuals with acquired social communication disorders.

papers.title: Characterizing Narrative Discourse in Posttraumatic Amnesia and Early Recovery After Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.authors: Steel J, Vazirani A, Hoffman R, McKay A, Checklin M.
papers.abstract: Purpose Following severe traumatic brain injury (TBI), individuals experience a transient period of confusion known as posttraumatic amnesia (PTA). Few empirical speech-language pathology studies have described language and cognitive-communication features during PTA or examined their early recovery. International guidelines recommend routine monitoring of communication during PTA; however, standardized speech-language pathology assessments are generally unsuitable for use during PTA. Narrative tasks offer a structured and repeatable approach to capture clinically meaningful changes. The purpose of this research was to describe narrative discourse characteristics in adults with severe TBI during PTA and examine how performance changed following PTA resolution. Method Nine adults with severe TBI admitted to an inpatient rehabilitation setting completed a narrative task during PTA and again after resolution of PTA. Language samples were analyzed across multiple levels, with descriptive analyses used to characterize performance and patterns of change. Discourse performance during PTA was compared descriptively to published data, providing reference data for microlinguistic measures and story grammar in adults without brain injury and adults with TBI who were not in PTA, where data were available. Results All participants demonstrated confused, disorganized narratives during PTA, although the degree and profile of impairment varied markedly across individuals. Macrostructural analyses provided the most meaningful and sensitive indicators of change, with several participants showing clearer narrative structure and increased production of relevant content post-PTA. Conclusions A narrative task has the potential to provide insight into the communication ability of patients in PTA, particularly in relation to change over time. This may help to guide decisions about the most appropriate timing for formal speech-language pathology assessment and intervention.

papers.title: Rehabilitation of Swallowing and Language Ability in Patients With Severe Acquired Brain Injury: An Online International Survey.
papers.authors: Regnier A, Gosseries O, Mélotte E, Gillet S, Magliacano A, Bottaeva Z, Hakiki B, Schnakers C, Cassar P, Thibaut A, Majerus S, Noé E, Llorens R, Maurer-Karattup P, Pérez LN, Fufaeva E, Formisano R, Estraneo A, Aubinet C.
papers.abstract: Purpose Patients with severe acquired brain injury and disorders of consciousness (DoC) are noncommunicative and present with severe dysphagia. To characterize current practices, identify gaps, and explore emerging approaches in postcomatose rehabilitation, the DoC Special Interest Group of the International Brain Injury Association conducted an international survey on speech-language therapy (SLT) practices. Method An online questionnaire, available in seven languages, was disseminated to clinicians involved in swallowing and/or language and communication rehabilitation of patients with DoC. The survey captured (a) sociodemographic and practice setting information, (b) general postcomatose SLT practices, (c) swallowing assessment and management, and (d) language and communication assessment and management. Results Responses were obtained from 166 clinicians, predominantly speech-language pathologists (74%), working in acute/subacute care (38%) or in longer-term rehabilitation (71%). Most assessed (74%) and managed (74%) swallowing disorders, and 25% created or adapted their own assessment tools. For language and communication, most respondents reported assessing (82%) and managing (76%) these abilities, with frequent use of augmentative and alternative communication (71%). Family input was considered central, for identifying motivating stimuli (96%) and involving relatives in therapy (87%). While 29% developed their own language assessment tools, 51% did so for intervention tools, reflecting limited validated resources. Conclusions Clinicians worldwide assess and manage swallowing and communication in patients with DoC but report a lack of validated tools. Practice often relies on individualized approaches and clinician-developed materials, with family involvement. These findings highlight the need for enhanced training and standardized, evidence-based instruments to strengthen SLT practices across the continuum of care. Supplemental material https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34741404.

papers.title: Tryptophan metabolism within the gut-brain axis in depression: mechanisms, association with heterogeneity, and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.authors: Qin Z, Lei T, Yi T, Zhang S, Tang Y, Xiang Y, Zhou Z, Mei Z, Qiu F, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Depression is a highly heterogeneous psychiatric disorder, characterized by substantial variability in clinical manifestations, treatment responses, and disease progression, thereby posing significant challenges to precision diagnosis and therapeutic intervention. Accumulating evidence indicates that dysregulated tryptophan metabolism, mediated through dynamic crosstalk with the gut microbiota and the gut-brain axis (GBA), plays a pivotal role in both the pathophysiology and biological heterogeneity of depression. In this review, we delineate the contributions of the three principal tryptophan metabolic pathways-the kynurenine, serotonin, and microbial indole pathways-in modulating neuroimmune signaling, neurotransmitter function, and gut-brain communication.
