The guidelines are openly available as a living guideline document on a webpage (\href{https://trust-guidelines-v01.readthedocs.io/en/latest/}{\textbf{trust-guidelines-v01.readthedocs.io}}), with git-versioning infrastructure that makes changes transparent and enables discussion. To validate the guidelines, we implemented the German Lexicon Project, providing an empirical feedback loop to test our suggestions. The living, open nature of the guidelines invites broader community feedback. It also enables future extension to other languages, groups (e.g., dyslexics), and methods (e.g., brain imaging), as it is openly available and includes instructions for hosting an adapted version at no cost. Thus, we provide a document intended to raise research standards in reading research worldwide, as a service to the community, potentially increasing replication rates and generalizability of relevant effects and phenomena.

papers.title: Which memory does brain stimulation improve? The priming problem
papers.authors: Velioglu HA, çelik mc, Aslan D, Sakiroglu MA, Çiçek Y, Altunc AT.
papers.abstract: Background: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of cortical sites connected with the hippocampus improves scores on episodic memory tests and is being tested for memory decline, including in Alzheimer's disease. These gains are read as gains in intentional retrieval. Objective: To examine whether standard memory outcomes can support this reading and how the contribution of repetition priming can be measured. Methods: Narrative review of hippocampal-network stimulation studies, cognitive and electrophysiological research on priming and processing fluency, stimulation studies of priming and parietal cortex, and clinical trials of TMS for memory decline. Results: Old/new recognition and cued recall present studied items or cues again at test. Repetition priming makes these items easier to process, and this fluency can raise a memory score with intentional retrieval unchanged. The fluency behind word-recognition decisions is largely conceptual, so it persists after a change of surface form. TMS can also alter priming directly, and stimulating the standard parietal target changes the subjective side of recollection. Meta-analytic evidence shows that the gains are specific to episodic memory and largest for recollection tests after stimulation before encoding, but the priming contribution to these gains has not been estimated. Conclusions: Process-level claims about stimulation-related memory gains require the priming contribution to be measured. Five measurement steps, centred on matched indirect tests and process-dissociation procedures, make it measurable in the same participants, including in clinical trials.

papers.title: Effects of rs2738880 Genotype on Symptom-Associated White Matter Networks in Schizophrenia: A Computational Connectomics Study.
papers.authors: Wang S, Peng Z, Gao X, Zuo T, Li F, Yang Y, Gao H.
papers.abstract: Objective The Disrupted-in-Schizophrenia 1 (DISC1) gene is a well-established genetic risk factor for schizophrenia (SCZ) and has been implicated in the pathogenesis of abnormal white matter (WM) development in this disorder. rs2738880, a common single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) within DISC1, has been linked to a spectrum of neurobiological alterations in SCZ. However, its specific impact on WM network in SCZ remains unclear. This study utilized magnetic resonance imaging and genotyping to investigate these mechanisms. Methods We recruited 332 Han Chinese participants, used magnetic resonance imaging scanning to assess WM integrity, and constructed a WM network for each individual. Besides that, we used imLDRTM SNP typing technology to determine the genotypes of SNPs at rs2738880. Furthermore, we used two-way analysis of covariance and partial correlation analysis (gender and age as covariates) to investigate the effects of rs2738880. Results While no significant main effects of genotype were observed, a significant diagnosis×genotype interaction on network local efficiency (Elocal) was identified (F(1,190)=7.353, p=0.007, η2p=0.037). Post-hoc tests revealed that patients carrying the G allele (AG/GG genotypes) exhibited significantly lower Elocal compared to other groups. Furthermore, Elocal was negatively correlated with symptom severity in the patient group (r=-0.194, p=0.038). Conclusion Our study suggests that the DISC1 rs2738880 G allele might be associated with network vulnerability and symptom severity in SCZ. However, the biological pathways through which the G allele influences WM network properties warrant further investigation.

papers.title: Impact of Chatbot-Based Cognitive Training on Cognitive Function and White Matter Integrity in Cognitively Unimpaired Older Adults: Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Kim BR, Kim E, Lim SM, Kim J, Jeong JH, Kim GH.
papers.abstract: Background Cognitive training may enhance cognition and support brain health during aging, but few trials have evaluated readily accessible chatbot-based programs with neuroimaging outcomes. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the effects of a chatbot-based cognitive training program on white matter microstructural organization and cognition in cognitively unimpaired older adults. Methods In a single-blind randomized controlled trial, 72 cognitively unimpaired older adults were assigned to chatbot-based cognitive training (30 min/day, 5 days/week for 12 weeks; n=37) or a no-intervention control (n=35). Diffusion tensor imaging at baseline and 12 weeks quantified fractional anisotropy (FA) in predefined white matter tracts, and cognition was assessed with the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery. Results Groups were comparable at baseline. After 12 weeks, the training group showed significantly less FA reduction than controls in the bilateral tapetum and right posterior thalamic radiation, surviving false discovery rate control (P<.05). The training group also improved on Paired Associates Learning (PAL), an episodic memory measure (P=.04). PAL improvement was positively associated with FA change in the right posterior thalamic radiation and right sagittal stratum (false discovery rate-adjusted P=.04 for each). Conclusions These findings suggest that a 12-week chatbot-based cognitive training program may support episodic memory and the relative maintenance of white matter microstructural organization in selected pathways in cognitively unimpaired older adults, consistent with a brain-maintenance framework. Trial registration CRIS KCT0004630; https://tinyurl.com/4xfesb68.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Radiology Report Quality Assurance: Real-World Multicenter Evaluation.
papers.authors: Wang L, Zhang Y, Peng L, Liu P, Wang L, Cui Y, Chen Y, Li X, Tao Y, Gong X, Zhao X, Song Y, Chen J, Zhao S, Wang F, Ma J, Zhao X.
papers.abstract: Background Radiology reports serve as the definitive clinical record of imaging diagnoses, with their accuracy being directly critical to patient safety. However, amid escalating workloads, manual review remains inadequate for capturing subtle errors in reports on a large scale. Although large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated considerable promise in medical text processing, previous studies have predominantly been confined to radiology report text from a single imaging modality or datasets with synthetic errors. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, accuracy, and generalizability of general-purpose LLMs for quality assurance of radiology report text from multiple imaging modalities (x-ray, computed tomography [CT], and magnetic resonance imaging [MRI]), multi-anatomical regions, and multicenter clinical settings, with head-to-head comparisons conducted against radiologists of varying seniority. Methods Radiology report texts from 3 aforementioned imaging modalities and 5 anatomical regions (head, chest, abdomen, spine, and knee) were retrospectively collected from center 1 (March 2025-May 2025) and reviewed using a clinician-annotated 5-category error taxonomy (type 1: interpretive; type 2: factual). Five LLMs (Qwen3, GPT-5.4 Pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Llama 4, and DeepSeek-V3.1) were benchmarked on 10,000 randomly selected reports, and the best-performing model was evaluated on the full cohort. A blinded head-to-head comparison with 3 radiologists (3-10 years of experience) used a modality-stratified, error-enriched challenge set. The radiologists subsequently rated the model-generated explanations using a 5-point Likert scale. Cross-center performance was evaluated in an independent external cohort. The same 2 senior radiologists labeled reports from both centers using the same protocol, resolving disagreements by consensus. Results In total, 4.6% (4431/95,582) of the reports in center 1 contained at least one confirmed text internal error. Qwen3, the selected model, achieved a report-level sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and F 1 -score of 0.99, 0.99, 0.90, and 0.94, respectively, with high performance across reports from the 3 imaging modalities and multiple anatomical regions and better detection of factual than interpretive errors. In the error-enriched challenge set, its error instance exact category recall exceeded that of the radiologists (0.96 vs 0.45-0.67; P <.001), with a shorter mean task completion time (5.80 vs 55.80-67.80 seconds per report). Explanations had a mean Likert score of 4.57, and all inter- and intraobserver intraclass correlation coefficients exceeded 0.89. In center 2, balanced accuracy was 0.94 (95% CI 0.92-0.95). Before consensus, Cohen κ for report-level error presence was 0.783 (center 1) and 0.850 (center 2). Conclusions This study suggests that LLMs can serve as efficient adjunctive tools for text-level quality control of radiology reports, particularly for detecting explicit factual errors. Performance remained stable across centers. In the text-only review task, the model achieved higher exact category recall and shorter task completion times than the participating radiologists. These findings support the potential value of LLM-assisted radiology report text review in real-world clinical environments.

papers.title: Permeability of the extracellular space in the rat, mouse, and human brain
papers.authors: Ranjan A, Guo Y, Thomas JH, Kelley DH, Boster KAS.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Brain tissue is a highly complex, heterogeneous, porous medium containing neurons, glial cells, blood vessels, and fluids. The interstitial spaces surrounding cells, referred to as the extracellular space (ECS), are critical transport pathways whose disruption is believed to play a role in neurological diseases. Therefore, understanding ECS fluid dynamics and the factors modulating flow there, such as permeability, is essential. Furthermore, because brain morphology, scale, and cellular density vary across species, understanding how permeability varies between species is critical for accurate physiological modeling. Methods: In our study, we investigated ECS permeability by performing computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations on three-dimensional electron microscopy data from rat, mouse, and human. We artificially varied the ECS volume fraction to investigate associated permeability variations, since volume fraction changes with arousal state. We also used a mesoscale computational model to simulate the waste clearance from the brain tissue. Results: The mean permeabilities of the ECS in rat, mouse, and human brain tissues, averaged across sampled locations, were approximately 18, 34, and 10 nm2, respectively. We compared our computational results with those predicted by the Kozeny-Carman equation, which consistently underestimated permeability. We developed an empirical relation to describe the variation of permeability with volume fraction within the range relevant to brain tissue. Conclusion: Our results show that the ECS permeability is of the same order of magnitude, approximately 10 nm2 across all species but varied several-fold across datasets. Hence, for models incorporating ECS permeability, a reasonable range of ECS permeability values for rats, mice, and humans is 10 nm2 - 100 nm2.

papers.title: Multi-Dataset Deep Learning for Automated Multiple Sclerosis Lesion Segmentation in Multimodal Brain MRI
papers.authors: Elsayed M, Elhoshy M, Bishri N, Saleh AI.
papers.abstract: Abstract Automated segmentation of multiple sclerosis (MS) lesions from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can support quantitative assessment, but performance remains sensitive to lesion heterogeneity, severe class imbalance, and variation across imaging sources. This study evaluates a multi-dataset deep learning framework for MS lesion segmentation using multimodal brain MRI. T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences are combined as a three-channel input to a UNet++ network with deep supervision. Training incorporates a hybrid Dice--Tversky objective, lesion-aware augmentation, and hyperparameter optimization. Comparative experiments assess architecture, encoder backbone, loss formulation, and modality fusion. On the held-out test split, the proposed model achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.722 \((\pm)\) 0.082, lesion-wise sensitivity of 0.783 \((\pm)\) 0.109, and lesion-wise F1-score of 0.738 \((\pm)\) 0.089. Small-lesion sensitivity reached 62%, representing a 29% relative improvement over the 2D U-Net baseline. A complementary resource-constrained ImageMask experiment compared U-Net, UNet++, and a SegNet-like architecture using a separate two-dimensional FLAIR pipeline. The results support multimodal representation and imbalance-aware optimization while highlighting the need for patient-level external validation before clinical deployment.

papers.title: The Ectodermal-Brain Memory to Explain the Methylation Pattern of the ASD Gene Matrix
papers.authors: kirdar z, Hamad HY, Auda IG.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The methylation of the genes in Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is now the most controversial topic. A large cohort of ASD individuals was genetically intact. This fact was a hallmark of the epigenetic regulation of ASD, especially the promoter region of the genes. DNA methylation is a challenging subject to study, as it is influenced by multiple factors. The brain is not a touchable tissue; postmortem brain tissue could give false positives because of apoptosis bias. Therefore, the study selected the ectodermal brain memory by collecting buccal swabs. Methods Pre-diagnosed ten individuals with ASD and two neurotypical controls were selected for buccal swab collection, DNA extraction, and NGS-based whole genome bisulfite sequencing. To avoid sex bias, we separated male ASD as A2 and female ASD as A3, while A1 represents all ASD. All ASD cohorts were compared with neurotypical controls. To avoid sex bias and germline bias, we made comparisons between two neurotypical controls, male and female A4 (negative control). Results The study screened about 8209 differentially methylated regions (DMRs), 4,234 genes, and 1,121 DMR-anchored promoter region genes in the A1 cohort. 12,353 DMRs, 5,247 genes, and 1,564 DMR-anchored promoter region genes in the A2 cohort. 7,761DMRs, 4,195 genes, and 1,329 DMR-anchored promoter region genes in the A3 cohort. 10,676 DMRs, 4,820 genes, and 1485 DMR-anchored promoter region genes in A4. SFARI overlap is consistently higher in the broader GO lists than in the promoter subsets, while A3 (female cohort) shows the highest promoter SFARI overlap at the descriptive count level. The study suggested that the following genes showed aberrant methylation overlaps in the SFARI database: high confidence like CACNA2D3, ATRX, MECP2, SKI, CASK, GRIA2; s trong candidates ADORA2A, CHARNA7, RPS6KA3, CACNA1B, MAOB, PIK3CG, LHX2, PITX1; suggestive evidence NPFFR2, PDHA1, POLR2A, KDM2A, TCEAL1; syndromic genes ZBTB18, HUWE1, HCFC1, RALA and the paralogs of SFARI genes PLCB1 (PLCB2) and WNT1 (WNT3). These genes, CALML3, GNG4, MYL9, WNT10B, MSH 5, are biomarkers in DNA methylation in ASD. About 2511 genes were shared between A1, A2, and A3, which were not recorded in the SFARI database. These genes were candidates for ASD biomarkers, including ADAM8, ASIC2, ASIC4; unclassified genes such as Chromosome Open Reading Frame C19orf44, C1orf159, C9orf3, Long Intergenic Non-Protein Coding RNA LINC00299, LINC01056; and FAM genes FAM19A5 and FAM171A1. Conclusion Individuals with ASD have a distinct epigenetic signature from NT. A large number of genes were differentially methylated and overlapped with the SFARI database. The mutation and methylation are critical to developing ASD. Most of the genes and their paralogs were involved in synaptic differentiation. The aberrant methylation is of embryonic origin, and other environmental factors influenced the severity of the cases.

papers.title: Zika-Related Microcephaly in the First 5 Years After Birth.
papers.authors: Ramos RCF, de Barros Miranda-Filho D, Martelli CMT, de Araújo TVB, Rocha MÂW, de Carvalho MDCG, da Silva PFS, Montarroyos UR, Brickley E, Rodrigues LC, de Souza WV, de Albuquerque MFPM, da Silva Oliveira DM, de Oliveira Ventura LMV, de Alencar Ximenes RA, Microcephaly Epidemic Research Group.
papers.abstract: Objective To characterize clinical manifestations and complications of children with Zika-related microcephaly in the first 5 years after birth. Methods A cohort of children with Zika-related microcephaly were observed up to age 60 months as part of the Microcephaly Epidemic Research Group Pediatric Cohort. Results Among the 181 children, 43.1% were male and 77.2% were born at term. The median birth weight was 2700 g, with 64.8% classified as small for gestational age. Notably, 22.3% were diagnosed with microcephaly after birth, and 48.8% had severe microcephaly. Most common phenotypic characteristics were craniofacial disproportion (54.1%), arthrogryposis (35.9%), and exacerbated occipital protuberance (35.5%). Approximately one-third (33.1%) presented with dysphagia (n = 151 evaluated at median age of 28.2 months), and 13.3% of children had gastrostomies (median age of 24 months). Hearing anomalies were detected in 9.7% (n = 93 evaluated at median age of 30 months). In ophthalmological evaluation, 30.4% showed changes in the retina and 28.5% in the optic nerve; strabismus was observed in 53.4%. During neurological assessment (median age at first assessment of 15.9 months), 73.8% presented with abnormalities. Imaging examinations showed ventriculomegaly and cortical atrophy in 75.3% and 64.4% of the children, respectively. Electroencephalography was performed based on clinical indication in 84 children, of whom 92.9% had pattern alterations. Over the 5 years, 62.4% were hospitalized, mainly for respiratory problems and seizures. Conclusions The study highlights the severity of Zika-related microcephaly. Future research should prioritize continued systematic monitoring of these children to understand the frequency and timing of late-onset manifestations and complications, including death.

papers.title: Synchronous Activity in the Auditory Forebrain Represents Temporal Landmarks in Vocal Communication Signals.
papers.authors: Ahmadi A, Robotka H, Gahr M, Theunissen F.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Precise temporal segmentation of sound is critical for identifying and interpreting complex acoustic signals such as human speech (Pisoni and Luce, 1987) and bird song (Gentner, 2008). Using the zebra finch model system, we investigated the neural coding of the songs' temporal features. We recorded neural activity from avian primary and secondary auditory cortex-like brain areas using electrode arrays in awake birds (four males and three females) exposed to conspecific songs. By applying a deep-learning approach with bidirectional long short-term memory networks (Daly, 2023), we demonstrate that not only the amplitude envelope of song stimuli but also discrete, time-locked envelope landmarks can be decoded from multichannel neuronal responses to songs. The times of envelope peak amplitude and peak slope were decoded with average accuracies of 40% and maximum accuracies of 70% at 20 ms timescales. The decoding of these landmarks enabled the segmentation of song into syllables with maximum accuracy of 90% at 10 ms timescales. Decoding accuracy for temporal events was greater in the primary auditory than in the secondary auditory area, suggesting a serial processing of the segmentation and identification operation. These findings reveal that neural entrainment to salient temporal events in vocal communication signals is a ubiquitous, specialized feature of the vertebrate primary auditory forebrain (Mesgarani et al., 2009; Heelan et al., 2019) providing a mechanism for segmenting continuous acoustic streams into behaviorally relevant units for higher-order processing.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究以斑胸草雀为对象，在清醒状态下记录其初级与次级听觉皮层样脑区对同种鸣唱的多通道神经反应，并用深度学习解码歌曲的时间特征。结果显示，不仅歌曲的振幅包络，包络峰值和峰值斜率等离散、锁时的事件也能从神经反应中解码，且这些时间标志可用于把连续鸣唱切分为音节；初级听觉区对时间事件解码的准确性高于次级听觉区。作者据此认为，对发声交流信号中显著时间事件的神经锁相是脊椎动物初级听觉前脑的专门特征，可能为把连续声流切分为行为相关单元、供更高阶加工提供机制，并推测这种功能组织对应先分段后识别的串行加工顺序。

papers.title: Learning from Error Predictions Rather Than Prediction Errors: A Perspective on Self-Supervised Learning in the Brain.
papers.authors: Meirhaeghe N.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Humans learn by doing and observing but also by imagining the result of simulated actions in their mind. When learning from executed or observed actions, traditional theories posit that behavior improves by minimizing the difference between (1) the perceived outcome derived from sensory feedback and (2) the desired outcome (performance error) or the outcome predicted by an internal model (prediction error, PE). Supporting these theories, decades of electrophysiological studies have documented the role of the dopaminergic system and cerebellum in generating activity patterns compatible with the hypothesized error signals. In comparison, our understanding of the neural basis underlying the ability to learn from simulated actions is far more limited. Here, I argue that this form of self-supervised learning is best described in terms of a quantity known as the predicted performance error (PPE), theorized more than 30 years ago and yet largely overlooked ever since. Complementary to PEs, PPEs reflect "error predictions" between predicted and desired outcomes. Unlike PEs, however, PPEs exist even in the absence of sensory feedback and can in principle serve to evaluate actions without executing them, based on an efference copy of the underlying motor plan. I review evidence supporting the computation of PPEs in the brain and propose a network implementation based on a cortico-basal ganglia loop interacting at multiple timescales with prefrontal, parietal, and hippocampal areas. I then connect PPEs to recent discoveries on motor planning and formulate novel predictions linking PPEs to various high-level brain functions such as metacognition, problem-solving, and deception.

papers.title: Ventral Tegmental Area Dopamine Neuron Dynamics during Postpartum Scarcity-Adversity Depend on Caregiving Quality and Pup Proximity.
papers.authors: Nguyen CH, Jayamohan S, Rincón-Cortés M.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Maternal behaviors are evolutionarily conserved yet sensitive to environmental factors such as resource availability. Scarcity-adversity, modeled by providing dams with reduced bedding and nesting materials, reliably induces changes in sensitive and insensitive pup-directed maternal behaviors. Ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopamine (DA) neurons are activated by pup interactions and are required for the expression of normal maternal behaviors. However, the effects of postpartum scarcity-adversity on dam VTA DA neuron activity during caregiving alterations remain unexplored. We conducted in vivo fiber photometry recordings of VTA DA neuron activity using Cre-dependent GCaMP7f in postpartum female TH-Cre rat dams in control or scarcity-adversity conditions. Dams were assigned to control or scarcity-adversity conditions on postpartum day (PD) 2 and underwent daily fiber photometry recordings during naturalistic maternal behavior observation sessions and a food pellet reward retrieval task through PD 5. Scarcity-adversity dams showed significantly elevated VTA DA neuron activity during insensitive caregiving, reflected by increased area under the curve, with no group differences during sensitive care. Additionally, scarcity-adversity dams exhibited a decrease in frequency of peaks when separated from their pups (i.e., out of nest), with no group differences during pup contact or nursing. Critically, alterations in VTA DA neuron activity in scarcity-adversity dams were not observed during food reward retrieval, suggesting that postpartum scarcity-adversity selectively disrupts VTA DA dynamics within the maternal caregiving context. These findings show that postpartum resource scarcity induces context-specific alterations in VTA DA neuron activity and provide a foundation for future investigation of projection-specific mechanisms underlying adversity-induced maternal behavior deficits.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注产后资源匮乏逆境如何影响母鼠在照料行为中的中脑腹侧被盖区（VTA）多巴胺神经元活动，采用TH-Cre母鼠的在体光纤记录，在自然育幼观察和食物奖励任务中比较资源匮乏组与对照组。结果显示，资源匮乏母鼠在不敏感照料期间VTA多巴胺神经元活动升高，而在敏感照料期间两组无差异；与幼崽分离（离巢）时其活动峰值频率下降，但接触或哺乳幼崽时无组间差异。关键的是，这些变化未出现在食物奖励提取任务中，提示产后资源匮乏对VTA多巴胺动态的影响具有情境特异性，主要局限于育幼情境，而非广泛改变奖赏加工。作者据此提出，逆境可能通过情境依赖的多巴胺活动改变母性照料的动机结构，为理解产后不良环境损害照料质量提供了神经生物学线索，但相关机制仍需进一步研究。

papers.title: Dissociable Roles of Prelimbic and Orbitofrontal Cortices in the Flexible Use of Model-Based Associations.
papers.authors: Dawson A, Wilson D, Taira M, Wilcher M, Abiero AR, Leake J, Sharpe MJ.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Our environment is complex and to navigate it effectively, we organize conceptual and spatial information into a coherent cognitive map. This allows us to be flexible and make novel inferences to maximize the procurement of the things we need and minimize negative events. Decision-making based on such cognitive maps is generally described as model-based behavior, which refers to an ability to simulate likely paths to reward via a transitional structure of the task. We have previously modeled how different prefrontal regions contribute to deploying cognitive maps to facilitate flexible behavior. We hypothesized that the prelimbic region-as analogous to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in humans-is necessary to upload the current relevant map, while the orbitofrontal cortex tracks position within the map as subjects traverse it. To test this, we developed a sequential biconditional discrimination task allowing optical inhibition during either map upload or position tracking in male and female rats. We show this task engenders a detailed model-based cognitive map, fostering the ability to make novel inferences. Consistent with our framework, optical inhibition of the orbitofrontal cortex disrupts rats' ability to track their current position in the map. In contrast, optical inhibition of the prelimbic cortex reduces performance when rats must upload the current map. While rats without prelimbic activity during map upload still show discriminative performance, their discrimination is uncoupled from that seen during training and lacked outcome specificity, suggesting a compensatory mechanism. Together, these data reveal dissociable contributions of the orbitofrontal and prelimbic cortices to cognitive map deployment.

papers.title: Normalization Accounts for Temporal Dynamics in the Human Somatosensory Cortex.
papers.authors: Bloem IM, Li L, Badde S, Groen IIA, Schellekens W, Ramsey N, Flinker A, Devinsky O, Devore S, Doyle W, Dugan P, Friedman D, Petridou N, Landy MS, Winawer J.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Sensory processing is fundamentally shaped by stimulation history. For example, in the visual cortex, neural responses are reduced for repeated or sustained stimuli (adaptation). These phenomena are well characterized and effectively modeled by divisive normalization. We asked whether these same computational principles govern somatosensory processing. We used fMRI (six participants, all female) and intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG, two participants, both male) to measure responses to time-varying vibrotactile stimuli in the human somatosensory cortex. Stimuli consisted of single and paired pulses with durations and interstimulus intervals ranging from 0.05 to 1.2 s. We extracted BOLD time courses to capture neural response amplitudes and high-frequency iEEG broadband envelopes to capture fast neural dynamics. In both experiments, we observed pronounced subadditive temporal summation. Responses to longer or repeated stimuli were consistently lower than predicted by linear integration. Computational modeling revealed that divisive normalization models outperformed linear models in cross-validated accuracy across both datasets. These results demonstrate that somatosensory temporal dynamics closely mirror those in the visual system. Our findings suggest that the nervous system employs similar computational principles across modalities to encode sensory information across time.

papers.title: Micro-online and Micro-offline Learning Reflect Stable Yet Randomly Distributed Strategies in Motor Skill Acquisition.
papers.authors: Fricke C, Muehlberg C, Juettner P, Psurek F, Hermsdorf F, Classen J, Rumpf JJ.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Motor learning is traditionally conceptualized as gains emerging during and after practice, over minutes to days. However, learning can also occur on much shorter timescales, within (micro-online) and between (micro-offline) practice blocks over seconds. It remains unclear whether micro-learning reflects an intrinsic property of the learning brain, arises from mechanisms such as reactive inhibition, or instead reflects transient fluctuations, stable individual traits, or chance. We pooled data from five motor sequence learning experiments (146 participants of either sex), including healthy younger and older adults and patients with Parkinson's disease (PD). Participants practiced motor sequences across repeated blocks separated by short rests. Using linear mixed-effects models, we quantified micro-online and micro-offline learning, related them to macro-learning, and assessed effects of age, PD, and dopaminergic medication. Micro-online learning predominated early in training, while micro-offline learning became the primary driver of later gains; neither modality alone predicted macro-learning. Individual preferences for one modality were stable across sessions, indicating trait-like profiles. However, the strong negative correlation typically reported between the two modalities was largely explained by how they are mathematically derived, rather than a genuine behavioral trade-off. Older participants relied more heavily on micro-online learning in early stages and showed stronger modality preferences, despite comparable total learning to younger adults. Patients with PD off medication showed reduced micro-online but enhanced micro-offline learning, a shift not observed under dopaminergic medication. However, group-level effects were modest relative to pronounced interindividual variability, and the observed micro-learning patterns may partly reflect measurement properties rather than distinct learning processes.

papers.title: Equidistance between Primary Sensory-Motor Landmarks Shapes Functional Specialization in the Human Brain.
papers.authors: Marin-Marin L, Wang X, Smallwood J, Margulies DS, Jefferies E.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The human cortex is organized around primary sensory-motor landmarks, but the way these distances shape large-scale functional organization remains unclear. Using geodesic measures in males and females, we show that global minimum distance to sensory-motor landmarks aligns with the principal gradient of intrinsic connectivity, reflecting the shift from unimodal to heteromodal cortex, while equidistance between landmarks captures complementary organizational patterns. Heteromodal networks, including default mode, control, and limbic systems, occupy cortical regions that are both distant from primary systems and relatively balanced between them. Subsystems within these networks exhibit distinctive spatial embeddings: core default mode regions sit equidistant between visual and somatomotor cortex, frontotemporal default mode regions favor auditory cortex but remain relatively balanced, and medial temporal regions are biased toward visual cortex. Control network subsystems also vary: the control-DMN subsystem occupies the most distant and equidistant positions, core control is closer to motor regions, and medial control is closer to visual cortex, reflecting their different functional specializations. At the parcel level, greater equidistance predicts stronger task-evoked activation, particularly in heteromodal border zones. These findings highlight two complementary spatial principles-proximity and balance-that structure the cortex, shaping both the location and functional profile of heteromodal networks.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨初级感觉运动皮层之间的空间距离如何塑造人脑大规模功能组织，利用测地距离分析男女被试的皮层几何与内在连接。结果显示，到感觉运动标志点的全局最小距离与内在连接的主梯度一致，对应从单模态到异模态皮层的过渡；而各标志点之间的等距性则刻画了互补的组织模式。默认模式、控制与边缘等异模态网络位于既远离初级系统、又在各标志点间相对均衡的区域，其内部子系统呈现不同的空间嵌入方式；在脑区层面，等距性越高，任务诱发激活越强，尤其在异模态边界区。作者据此提出邻近性与均衡性两个互补的空间原则，认为皮层几何与认知功能相关，但这是关联性证据，尚不能说明因果关系。

papers.title: New insights of oligodendrocytes in the etiology of Parkinson's disease.
papers.authors: Wang JR, Zhou N, Dong YR, Zang CX, Li FF, Yang Y, Jiang YQ, Chen QZ, Yang X, Zhou MC, Cao SP, Zeng SX, Bao XQ, Zhang D.
papers.abstract: Oligodendrocytes (OLs) are myelin-forming cells in the central nervous system (CNS), providing nutritional and metabolic support to axons. They also interact with other glial cells to regulate the microenvironment of the CNS. Recent clinical studies have revealed that OL dysfunction and white matter changes occur at an early stage of Parkinson's disease (PD) and may be associated with dopaminergic neuronal damage, postural, and gait disorders. However, whether these changes are primary drivers or secondary consequences of neurodegeneration remains to be determined. Biochemical and genetic studies have provided evidence for OL dysfunction in PD pathology. Mechanistic studies have shown that OL damage can disrupt neuronal integrity through communicating with neurons, and the aggregation of α-synuclein (α-Syn) in OLs also accelerates dopaminergic neuronal death. Emerging evidence suggests that OLs may play a significant role in the pathogenesis and progression of PD through their involvement in mitochondrial damage, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. In this review, we summarized current understanding of oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs), OLs, myelination, and white matter in the pathogenesis of PD and discussed the potential therapy by targeting OLs for PD.

papers.title: Individualised electrophysiological neural field models for the assessment of thalamocortical function in disorders of consciousness: A multicentre study.
papers.authors: Cóngyǔ L, Tewarie P, Alnagger NLN, Mindlin I, Van der Lande GJM, Belloli L, Laureys S, Naccache L, Rohaut B, Thibaut A, Annen J, Gosseries O, Núñez P, Sitt JD.
papers.abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying disorders of consciousness (DoC) remains a major challenge, particularly in distinguishing limited awareness in minimally conscious state (MCS) and complete unawareness in unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, also coined vegetative state (UWS/VS). In this multicentre study, we fitted a biophysically informed corticothalamic neural field model to high-density EEG data from two large independent datasets, comprising 203 UWS patients, 270 MCS patients and 74 healthy controls. We then used the fitted parameters to simulate EEG time series on a per-subject basis and compared empirical and simulated complexity metrics. The model reliably captured the spectral features across different states of consciousness and revealed reduced corticothalamic integrity in DoC patients that was more pronounced in UWS than in MCS, supporting the mesocircuit hypothesis. Furthermore, the simulated EEG reproduced the complexity patterns of the empirical recordings, with permutation entropy emerging as a sensitive marker capable of distinguishing between MCS and UWS for both real and simulated time series.

papers.title: Modeling reaction-diffusion processes in simplified to complex astroglial branchlet geometries using different simulation tools.
papers.authors: Keto L, Seppälä S, Ndubuaku D, Mäki A, Mäki-Marttunen T, Linne ML, Manninen T.
papers.abstract: Computational modeling of spatial biochemical processes in neuroscience is increasingly important as advances in experimental and imaging techniques provide detailed insights into cellular organization. Reaction-diffusion models are commonly used to study the diffusion and interactions of ions and molecules within neuronal cells, and multiple open-access simulation platforms have been developed to support such analysis. However, a comprehensive analysis of commonly used simulation tools, including MCell, STEPS, NeuroRD, and NEURON, remains lacking, particularly for realistic glial cell geometries, as these tools were originally developed for neurons. Here, we present a systematic analysis of these four simulation environments by implementing equivalent calcium diffusion and calcium-calmodulin reaction-diffusion models across a range of spatial domains. These include simplified geometries (cylinders and rectangular cuboids) as well as biologically realistic astroglial morphologies derived from electron microscopy data, including mouse Bergmann glia and mouse and human cortical astrocytes. Using matched kinetic parameters and diffusion constants, we examine simulation outputs and morphological variations across platforms under comparable conditions. We find that all tools produce overall consistent results for the systems considered, indicating that each can reliably capture diffusion and reaction-diffusion dynamics in simplified and complex geometries. At the same time, we show that the structural heterogeneity of branchlets from human astrocytes and mouse Bergmann glia gives rise to distinct calcium signaling, demonstrating that fine-scale morphology critically shapes astroglial dynamics and must be accurately captured by simulation frameworks. In addition, notable differences emerge in geometry representation, implementation strategies, computational aspects, and usability of the tools. By highlighting key trade-offs between geometric fidelity, flexibility, and computational cost in modeling intracellular biochemical processes, these findings provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate simulation tools. More broadly, our results support the use of reaction-diffusion modeling in morphologically realistic astrocytic environments and contribute to enabling mechanistic studies of localized signaling events at synaptic and perisynaptic sites.

papers.title: Teaching Video NeuroImage: Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome With Appropriate Sodium Correction Causing Isolated Basal Ganglia Demyelination and Reversible Parkinsonism.
papers.authors: Dolan E, Donlon E, Fearon C.

papers.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Beyond the Bone Marrow-VEXAS Syndrome Presenting as Subacute Encephalomyelitis.
papers.authors: Ferrari A, Divenuto I, Martire MS, Gallia F, Absinta M, Fasano A, Liberatore G.
papers.abstract: Vacuoles, E1 enzyme, X-linked, Autoinflammatory, Somatic (VEXAS) syndrome is an adult-onset autoinflammatory disease caused by acquired somatic UBA1 mutations, typically presenting with systemic inflammation and myelodysplastic syndrome. Although infrequent, neurologic manifestations can include peripheral neuropathy, stroke, or encephalopathy. Notably, spinal cord involvement remains poorly documented. Here, we present the case of a 70-year-old man with myelodysplastic syndrome and confirmed VEXAS (UBA1 p.Met41Thr) presenting with subacute ascending paresthesia, Lhermitte sign, and urinary hesitancy suggestive of myelopathy. 3T MRI demonstrated multifocal T2-hyperintense spinal cord and brain lesions, some with contrast enhancement, consistent with inflammatory encephalomyelitis. CSF analysis showed mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (33 cells/µL), elevated protein (55 mg/dL), and numerous CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands. Negative infectious PCR testing and the absence of aquaporin 4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibodies argued against infection or other inflammatory demyelinating condition. The patient received high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g/d for 3 days), resulting in rapid clinical improvement. Follow-up MRI performed 1 month after presentation showed resolution of contrast enhancement and partial disappearance of spinal T2 hyperintense lesions.

papers.title: Deep learning models to detect neurodegenerative diseases across different modalities, datasets, and stages: A systematic review.
papers.authors: Poddar K, Wahi C.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.abstract: BackgroundNeurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's pose significant diagnostic challenges because they are incurable. Their symptoms often overlap with those of normal ageing and involve progressive neuronal loss. This makes early prediction, proper diagnosis, and ongoing monitoring crucial at every stage of the disease. Deep learning has become a useful tool for handling different types of data. However, the performance of these models relies heavily on the availability and variety of data, making it important to characterize datasets.ObjectiveThis PRISMA-based systematic review looks at 111 studies from 2019 to April 2026, organized into three clinical stages of neurodegenerative diseases: early prediction, diagnosis, and progression.MethodsEach study is assessed across four dimensions: data type (neuroimaging or non-neuroimaging), datasets (open-access, self-created, or hybrid), deep learning model architecture, and the use of explainable AI.ResultsMRI is the only imaging modality that spans all three stages. Speech is the most common non-neuroimaging method for diagnosis, while gait is used only for diagnosis and progression. The ADNI and PPMI datasets are the most commonly used. Self-created datasets introduce new modalities such as ECG and iPSCs, which are not found in open-access datasets. CNNs are the leading models for neuroimaging tasks, while LSTMs and RNNs capture temporal patterns in longitudinal datasets. Survival models are exclusively used for ALS and LATE. Fewer than 6% of the studies used confirmed XAI. Only 2 of the 111 studies validated their results on an independent external cohort.ConclusionThis review is the only one that covers all three disease stages across multiple neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Autonomic Function and Cerebral Hemodynamics in Relation to Cognitive Function in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
papers.authors: Li X, Zhao M, Lu Y, Yang Q, Guo T, Wang T, Liu C, Ren L, Wang Y, Hu G, Guan L.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
papers.abstract: Background Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is linked to cognitive impairment. This study examined associations of autonomic function and cerebral hemodynamics with cognitive function in patients with CSVD. Methods In this cross-sectional study, patients with white matter hyperintensity and recent subcortical small infarction were recruited from January 2020 to March 2022. Cognitive function was assessed using education-adjusted Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), autonomic function using heart rate variability (HRV), and cerebral hemodynamics including cerebral autoregulation (CA), cerebrovascular reactivity, and neurovascular coupling (NVC). Logistic and linear regression and ROC analyses were performed. Results Among 206 patients (median age 63 years; 130 men), 167 (81.1%) had cognitive impairment. Patients with cognitive impairment showed reduced HRV and impaired cerebral hemodynamics, including dynamic CA and NVC. Mean Holding LF Phase and Mean Holding CBFv remained significantly associated with cognitive impairment in multivariable models. Hemodynamics-based models showed AUCs of 0.776-0.850 for LF Phase-based models and 0.917-0.924 for CBFv-based models. In sensitivity analyses excluding HFnu, Mean Holding CBFv remained significantly associated with cognitive impairment. Conclusions Impaired autonomic function and cerebral hemodynamic responses may contribute to cognitive dysfunction in CSVD. Assessing parasympathetic function and cerebral hemodynamics may help identify cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Understanding the Perception of Pain in People with Parkinson's Disease: A Qualitative Study.
papers.authors: González-Zamorano Y, García-Bravo C, Güeita-Rodríguez J, Peláez I, Fernández-Carnero J, Romero JP.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo describe the experience of pain among people with Parkinson's disease, including its characteristics, psychological effects, and impact on daily life.DesignQualitative descriptive study.SettingCommunity-based study using semi-structured individual interviews.ParticipantsFifteen people with Parkinson's disease (11 women) diagnosed according to the United Kingdom Parkinson's Disease Society Brain Bank criteria and experiencing Parkinson's disease-related pain based on the Parkinson's Disease Pain Classification System.InterventionNot applicable.Main measuresSemi-structured interviews were conducted to explore participants' experiences of pain. Data were analysed using an inductive thematic analysis based on a hybrid approach combining artificial intelligence-powered coding through ChatGPT-4 with manual triangulation.ResultsThree main themes were identified: (1) experiences and perceptions of pain, including the nature and characterization of pain and its relationship with Parkinson's disease; (2) the impact of pain on daily life; and (3) feelings associated with pain, including emotional changes related to pain and its broader psychological impact.ConclusionsPain in people with Parkinson's disease is an interconnected and context-dependent experience extending beyond its physical manifestations. The patient-centred narratives provide contextual insight into how pain interacts with motor and non-motor symptoms, daily functioning, emotional well-being, and participation, supporting individualized and comprehensive approaches to pain assessment and management.

papers.title: Effects of External Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation on Neurocognitive Functioning in Children and Adolescents With ADHD: A Phase 2b Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Eraydin IE, Marhenke R, Stringer D, Conti AA, Bozhilova N, Johansson L, Mason L, Bilbow A, Mehta MA, Santosh P, Fiori F, Carter B, Cortese S, Rubia K.
papers.abstract: Objective Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with atypical cognition and related autonomic nervous system regulation. Trigeminal nerve stimulation (TNS) received U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance as neuromodulation treatment for ADHD based on findings of clinical improvements from a pilot trial that were not confirmed in the authors' larger multicenter UK trial. Effects of TNS on cognition in ADHD, however, are relatively unknown. The authors therefore tested secondary outcomes, that is, short- and longer-term effects of active versus sham TNS in youths with ADHD on a broad neurocognitive task battery, physiological indicators of autonomic nervous system regulation, and head motion. Methods In the first confirmatory, multicenter, double-blind, parallel-group, phase 2b randomized sham-controlled trial, 150 youths with ADHD (ages 8-18 years) were assigned to 4 weeks of nightly active (N=75) or sham (N=75) TNS. Cognitive performance was assessed using a comprehensive battery of executive function and attention tasks (inhibition, sustained attention, time estimation, processing speed, and intrasubject response variability) at baseline, posttreatment, and 6-month follow-up. Autonomic nervous system regulation (heart rate, heart rate variability, and electrodermal activity) was measured via a wristband device and head motion with an eye tracker during rest or cognitive testing. Results Intention-to-treat analysis showed no significant differential treatment effects between active and sham TNS on any cognitive or physiological outcomes after 4 weeks of treatment or on cognitive measures at 6-month follow-up. Conclusions TNS does not appear to improve neurocognitive performance, autonomic regulation, or head motion in youths with ADHD, extending negative clinical findings. The findings do not provide evidence to support TNS as a viable treatment to improve cognitive or autonomic nervous system functioning in youths with ADHD.

papers.title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release.
papers.authors: Jain A, Dong R, Kroll J, Webster JF, Moss J, Bikbaev A, Ultanir SK, Gonzalez-Sulser A, Rosenmund C, Heine M, Liu J, Cousin MA, Ivanova D.
papers.abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

papers.title: An oxidized ribonucleotide 8-oxoGTP drives neuroinflammation and accelerates cognitive decline.
papers.authors: Li J, Wang ZH, Pan JX, Jiang ZL, Li R, Gao XF, Sheng G, Wang ZH, Ma YQ, Wang ZL, Wang T, Huan R, Zeng LT, Zhang W, Dai DP, Cui J, Zhou XY, Zhang LQ, Su W, Chen HB, Hu GX, Qi RM, Cai JP.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress is a hallmark of aging and a key driver of neurodegenerative diseases. While much attention has been given to oxidative damage of macromolecules, the functional consequences of oxidizing the abundant nucleotide triphosphate (NTP) pool remain largely unknown. Here, we identify oxidized GTP (8-oxoGTP)-a major product of NTP oxidation-not as a mere marker of damage, but as an endogenous signaling molecule that drives microglial activation and neuroinflammation. 8-oxoGTP accumulated in the aging mouse brain, and its elevation was sufficient to induce synaptic dysfunction, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline. Mechanistically, 8-oxoGTP functioned as a potent activator of heterotrimeric G proteins, binding more strongly to Gα subunits than GTP itself, triggering Src kinase/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB signaling in microglia, leading to pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reactive oxygen species generation, and neurotoxicity. Pharmacological inhibition of Src family kinases rescued the neuroinflammatory and cognitive phenotypes induced by 8-oxoGTP. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking nucleotide oxidation to age-associated neurodegenerative processes.

papers.title: Development and validation of a low-cost, wearable near-infrared spectroscopy system for quantifying tissue water fraction in the human brain.
papers.authors: Wu KC, Renna M, Otic N, Starkweather Z, Kierul OS, Smith C, Franceschini MA, Robinson MB.
papers.abstract: Significance Cerebral water fraction is physiologically relevant to brain fluid dynamics, glymphatic function, cerebral edema, and dehydration, yet it is not routinely measured in wearable neuroimaging. Aim We aimed to develop and validate a low-cost, wearable, light-emitting diode (LED)-based continuous-wave near-infrared spectroscopy system capable of concurrently monitoring changes in cerebral hemoglobin concentration and water fraction from the forehead. Approach Our device, called the GS-FlexNIRS, contains nine LEDs spanning 740 to 1050 nm mounted on a flexible printed circuit board. Three of these wavelengths (i.e., 910, 940, and 1050 nm) fall within the water absorption window. A wavelength-weighted fitting algorithm incorporates measured LED emission spectra and photodiode responsivity to enable accurate chromophore recovery despite spectrally broad LED illumination. Performance was characterized in liquid phantoms and in five healthy participants during respiratory maneuvers. Results The system achieved a dynamic range of ∼100 dB , gain linearity ( R2>0.99997 ), and signal-to-noise ratio of 67 to 90 dB. Phantom experiments confirmed independent tracking of hemoglobin deoxygenation and water fraction changes. Hemoglobin responses in human measurements were consistent with prior work. Conclusions The GS-FlexNIRS ( ∼$350/unit ) and its wearable design may support future longitudinal and naturalistic monitoring of cerebral hemodynamics and brain fluid dynamics, enabling investigation in sleep, glymphatic research, and cerebral edema monitoring.

papers.title: MRI BRAIN lesions and growth after antenatal steroids in preterm infants: Does timing matter?
papers.authors: Malova M, Caruggi S, Pozzi F, Massirio P, Vinci F, Bonato I, Calandrino A, Minghetti D, Calevo MG, Prefumo F, Resaz M, Paladini D, Severino M, Tortora D, Rossi A, Ramenghi LA.
papers.abstract: Introduction Antenatal corticosteroids (ACS) are widely used to improve outcomes in preterm infants, with known benefits on respiratory morbidity and intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH). However, the effect of ACS timing on brain injury and development remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the impact of a complete course of ACS (ccACS), with particular attention to timing, on brain lesions, growth, and neurodevelopment in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Material and methods In this historical cohort study, all VLBW infants admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between January 2019 and December 2021 were included. Clinical data, including timing of ACS administration, were collected. The primary outcome was the occurrence of brain injury on MRI at term-equivalent age, including IVH, white matter lesions (WML), and cerebellar hemorrhage (CBH). Secondary outcomes were brain growth and maturation on MRI and neurodevelopment at 2 years assessed using the Griffiths Mental Development Scales. Outcomes were compared between infants with and without ccACS and according to different administration-to-birth intervals. Results A total of 189 infants were included, of whom 139 (73.5%) received ccACS. Infants exposed to ccACS had a lower incidence of WML (p = 0.02) and moderate/severe IVH (p = 0.04). In extremely preterm infants (<28 weeks), IVH was significantly less frequent when ccACS was administered within 7 days before birth (p = 0.006). No significant differences were observed in brain growth, maturation, or neurodevelopmental outcomes at 2 years. Conclusions A complete course of ACS was associated with unadjusted lower rates of brain injury in VLBW infants, particularly when administered within 7 days before birth in extremely preterm infants, without adverse effects on brain growth, maturation, or neurodevelopment at 2 years.

papers.title: Osteohistological analysis reveals unusual bone tissue patterns in Temminck's ground pangolin (Smutsia temminckii).
papers.authors: Mamabolo P, Parrini F, Botha J.
papers.abstract: Temminck's ground pangolin is one of Africa's most threatened mammals, yet little is known about its skeletal biology. This study provides the first osteohistological analysis of its limb bones, documenting patterns of growth, remodelling and skeletal reinforcement. Limb bones exhibit extensive cortical remodelling, with substantial portions of the cortex being composed of compacted coarse cancellous bone, endosteal bone and secondary osteons, together with abundant resorption cavities. Growth marks occur in all elements, but the absence of outer circumferential lamellae and persistence of open vascular canals indicate continued growth and a lack of skeletal maturity despite the presence of up to four annual growth cycles. Extensive skeletal reinforcement occurs throughout the limbs, although elements employ distinct osteohistological patterns. Comparison with the aardvark reveals alternative pathways of skeletal reinforcement, with ground pangolins showing relatively greater secondary remodelling in the hind limb. Ground pangolins are further distinguished by abundant, incompletely infilled resorption cavities extending into the middle and outer cortex, suggesting an unusual pattern of intracortical remodelling. The exceptionally low basal metabolic rate of S. temminckii may contribute to these patterns, although this relationship remains to be tested. These findings provide new insights into the skeletal biology of this poorly studied mammal.

papers.title: Clinical Trajectories and Cardiac Phenotypes in Danon Disease.
papers.authors: Tsirelman K, Frishman WH, Aronow WS.
papers.abstract: Danon disease is a rare X-linked lysosomal cardioskeletal myopathy caused by loss-of-function variants in LAMP2, which impair autophagosome-lysosome fusion and lead to accumulation of autophagic vacuoles in cardiomyocytes. Although cardiac penetrance is high in both sexes, the natural history differs markedly by sex. Males typically present in childhood or adolescence with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and intellectual disability, and often progress to heart failure or ventricular arrhythmias by early adulthood. Females typically present later in life with a cardiac-predominant phenotype that more often evolves to dilated cardiomyopathy, although a subset develops an early onset, severe phenotype reminiscent of male hemizygotes. Pooled case data suggest that cumulative rates of death, heart transplantation, or ventricular assist device implantation are similar between sexes but occur approximately 2 decades later in females, indicating that women may be delayed rather than spared. Ventricular preexcitation, mediated by fasciculoventricular or extranodal accessory pathways, and a characteristic cardiac magnetic resonance pattern of late gadolinium enhancement with mid-basal septal sparing can support the diagnosis, although septal sparing is less frequent in females. Heart transplantation remains the established treatment, and a phase 1 trial of AAV9-LAMP2B gene therapy has provided early proof-of-concept in males.

papers.title: mPFC-Dependent Valuation Shapes Information Sharing: Causal Evidence from tDCS and a Dyadic Social Media Paradigm.
papers.authors: Li Y, Zhang Y, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Information sharing drives the spread of both accurate and misleading content, yet its psychological and neural mechanisms remain unclear. We investigated whether perceived self- and social relevance influence sharing through downstream content evaluations, and whether this process depends on medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) function. In a dyadic social media paradigm, 186 participants were assigned to anodal, cathodal, or sham tDCS over the mPFC. Senders judged 30 science news items (15 true and 15 false) on truthfulness, self-relevance, social relevance, interestingness, and importance before deciding whether to share each item with a real receiver. Structural equation modeling showed that self- and social relevance predicted sharing indirectly through evaluations of interestingness, importance, and truthfulness. mPFC stimulation did not reliably change sharing rates, but altered evaluative processing: it reduced perceived interestingness, and anodal stimulation produced a significant negative indirect pathway to sharing through reduced interestingness. Multi-group analyses indicated that these valuation pathways were invariant across true and false news. On the receiver side, social endorsement increased reading of shared items but had little effect on post-reading evaluations. Together, these findings support a causal contribution of mPFC-targeted neuromodulation to evaluative processing relevant to sharing, with limited evidence for a direct effect on sharing behavior.

papers.title: Is it truly patient-centered? Doctor-patient communication in remote programming for Parkinson's disease.
papers.authors: Xu S, Zhang W, Cheng Y.
papers.abstract: Purpose Patients with Parkinson's disease require frequent programming after deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery to maintain therapeutic efficacy. Although remote programming promises a more patient-centered and accessible healthcare model, the transition from in-person to virtual visits may introduce unique barriers that compromise this innovative care model. From a doctor-patient communication perspective, this study explores these specific communication barriers and their subsequent impact on programming outcomes and patient experience. Methods Non-participatory observation and in-depth interviews were used to understand the experiences of patients, caregivers, and doctors regarding communication during remote programming of DBS. Thematic analysis was applied to analyze the qualitative data. Results A total of 49 participants were enrolled. Three themes were identified: Structural changes in doctor-patient communication; Expanded patient responsibility; and Weakened emotional support. Findings indicate that Parkinson's patients face new barriers to communication access, heavier burdens of self-expression, and poorer outcomes in emotional communication. Conclusion The shift in programming models has introduced numerous new challenges for patients and their caregivers, including mastering digital devices, ensuring that home environments are suitable for online consultations, accurately describing symptoms, and accepting the absence of emotional comfort.

papers.title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.
papers.authors: Mukherjee U, Basu B, Suryavanshi P, Beyer SE, Ghodsi S, Robillard N, Vanrobaeys Y, Taylor EB, Glykys J, Abel T, Chatterjee S.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions. Through genetic manipulations, we show that reducing hippocampal Kcr levels impairs memory, while increasing Kcr levels by means of crotonate administration enhances long-term memory. Single-nuclei transcriptome and chromatin accessibility analyses reveal that crotonate facilitates activation of genes regulating glutamate signaling. Cell-cell communication analysis further suggests a strengthening of glutamatergic signaling within hippocampal excitatory neurons following crotonate administration. Real-time fluorescence imaging with genetically encoded sensors functionally validates our multiomics and computational findings-demonstrating the role of Kcr in regulating presynaptic glutamate release and neuronal activity. In summary, our findings elucidate a key mechanism underlying long-term memory consolidation and excitatory neurotransmission, linking epigenetic events to synaptic function and behavior.

papers.title: Forniceal deep brain stimulation improves memory in Rett syndrome mice by promoting the maturation of newborn hippocampal neurons.
papers.authors: Wang Q, Tang B, Wu Z, Zoghbi HY, Tang J.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is associated with an increase in hippocampal neurogenesis and memory benefits, but the causal mechanism is unclear. Here, we use a mouse model of Rett syndrome, a severe learning disability syndrome caused by MECP2 loss of function, to find that DBS promotes the maturation and integration of newborn dentate granule cells (DGCs) into the neural circuit. Suppressing hippocampal neurogenesis prevented DBS from improving learning and memory. Newborn methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2)-deficient DGCs in Rett syndrome mice showed attenuated development and synaptic dysfunction, but DBS rescued DGC dendritic arborization, synaptogenesis, and long-term synaptic plasticity. DBS achieves this, at least in part, by increasing the protein level and shifting the phosphorylation of potassium chloride cotransporter 2, thereby restoring the conversion of GABAergic signaling from depolarization to hyperpolarization, a process that is otherwise delayed by MeCP2 deficiency. This study pinpoints one mechanism by which chronic DBS promotes neuronal maturation and enhances memory.

papers.title: Emotion regulation capacity lacks a shared neural signature.
papers.authors: Sicorello M, Zaehringer J, Kraynak TE, Gianaros PJ, Nebe S, Paschke LM, Steimke R, Stelzel C, Walter H, LaBar KS, Graner JL, Kim SH, Wessa M, Sandner M, Weinmar F, Derntl B, Huneke NTM, Fagan HA, Fernández G, Yan L, Marín-Morales A, Verdejo-Román J, Steward T, Harrison BJ, Davey CG, Dörfel D, Neta M, Pierce J, Stolz DS, Kissler J, Benzait A, Erk S, Berboth S, van Reekum CM, Tupitsa E, Bratec SM, Sorg C, Müller-Pinzler L, Sokołowski A, Dragan WŁ, Folkierska-Żukowska M, Jentsch VL, Merz CJ, Scheffel C, Diers K, Nashiro K, Min J, Mather M, Heinke S, Gärtner A, McRae K, Powers JP, Doren N, Maier SU, Dziobek I, Guendelman S, Gaebler M, Daniels JK, Burghart M, Schmidt SNL, Hofhansel L, Habel U, NIDER Consortium, Kohn N, Morawetz C.
papers.abstract: Cognitive reappraisal refers to changing how one thinks about a situation to alter its emotional impact. It is central to well-being1 and engages prefrontal regulatory circuits2 , prompting the assumption that their activity reflects a person's capacity to regulate emotions3-5 . Yet evidence for this assumption remains inconclusive and has not been established at scale. Here we analysed 40 task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) datasets in a preregistered consortium with 2,175 participants and show that three widely used indicators of reappraisal capacity-trait questionnaires, task-based affective ratings and amygdala down-regulation-do not converge on a common core. Moreover, none of the three indicators showed the expected association with canonical prefrontal regulatory circuits. Trait questionnaires showed no detectable neural associations across the brain and task-based affective ratings were instead associated with responses in the amygdala and sensorimotor cortices. At the process level, canonical control circuits were engaged during both emotion generation and reappraisal, challenging their presumed specificity for emotion regulation. These findings caution against using activation in putatively regulatory brain regions to infer how well a person regulates emotions, with implications for neural biomarkers, interventions and psychoeducation that link emotion regulation difficulties to specific regional brain deficits.

papers.title: Presynaptic homeostasis mediated by exocytosis of a SNARE protein.
papers.authors: Xu H, Rao L, Edwards RH.
papers.abstract: The neural plasticity that underlies adaptation and learning requires countervailing homeostatic mechanisms to maintain the stability and responsiveness of neural circuits. Previous work has described several forms of synaptic homeostasis1 , but the mechanisms that detect changes in activity and transduce these into altered neurotransmission have remained poorly understood. Here we show that high-frequency stimulation alters the subsequent properties of neurotransmitter release to confer a presynaptic form of homeostasis, independent of postsynaptic receptors. The mechanism involves vesicular SNARE protein (v-SNARE) VAMP7 (vesicle-associated membrane protein 7), which reduces neurotransmitter release by inhibiting the entry of Ca2+ specifically through P/Q-type presynaptic Ca2+ channels. Previous work has implicated target SNARE proteins (t-SNAREs) in the inhibition of Ca2+ channels2 , but without clear physiological rationale. We show that the activity-dependent regulation of release mediated by VAMP7 requires the t-SNARE syntaxin. Although VAMP7 acts at the plasma membrane to inhibit P/Q-type channels, it localizes predominantly to a subset of synaptic vesicles made by adaptor protein-3 (AP-3) that respond specifically to high-frequency stimulation3,4 . The localization of VAMP7 to AP-3-derived synaptic vesicles thus provides a mechanism for the activity-dependent delivery of VAMP7 to the plasma membrane, where it associates with syntaxin to inhibit P/Q-type Ca2+ channels and transmitter release. This homeostatic form of metaplasticity operates at multiple excitatory synapses, and in its absence, the fraction of FOS+ neurons increases several fold, revealing a general property of excitatory neurotransmission that might also maintain the sparsity of neural connections.

papers.title: Meta-study sparks questions about what it means to be good at regulating emotions.
papers.authors: Kober H, Ochsner K.

papers.title: Design Strategy of T1-Weighted MRI Contrast Agents for High Relaxivity Based on a Self-Folding Macromolecular Architecture.
papers.authors: Gao S, Miura Y, Sumiyoshi A, Iiyama M, Ma L, Maehara N, Ono S, Bonnet CS, Aoki I, Nishiyama N, Osada K.
papers.abstract: Conjugation of gadolinium chelates to macromolecular nanoplatforms has emerged as a promising strategy for developing high-performance contrast agents for T1-weighted MRI. However, conventional macromolecular gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) typically achieve limited enhancement of longitudinal relaxivity merely by tethering Gd chelates to macromolecular platforms to slow their global rotational motion. Here, we present a rational design strategy based on a self-folded macromolecular contrast agent (SMCA), formed through intramolecular self-folding of a single amphiphilic polymer chain incorporating a minimized amount of Gd chelate. The SMCA forms a nanosized micellar structure with a hydrophobic core and a hydration shell, while positioning the Gd chelates at the core-shell interface. Experimental results suggest that the rigid architecture of SMCA may contribute to relatively slow global motion, while the PEG shell may restrict segmental dynamics, potentially contributing to the enhanced longitudinal relaxivity. Systematic structural modulation, including control of the degree of polymerization and hydrophilic chain length, enables enhanced relaxivity while ensuring renal clearance. The optimized Gd-DOTA-conjugated SMCA exhibits a longitudinal relaxivity of 31.5 mM-1 s-1 at 0.47 T, representing an 8.5-fold increase over clinically used Gd-DOTA. In a proof-of-concept MRI study, SMCA enhances strong and long-lasting vascular contrast even at one-eighth of the Gd-DOTA dose, yielding a 2.7-fold higher peak signal intensity while maintaining favorable clearance. This work would contribute to establishing mechanistic guidance for designing next-generation macromolecular GBCAs with high relaxivity and ensured safety.

papers.title: Free-breathing Pulmonary Relaxometry at 0.55T.
papers.authors: Panos P, Bieri O, Pradella M, Hostettler KE, Bauman G.
papers.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the feasibility of an integrated, free-breathing workflow for automated 2D pulmonary relaxometry (T1, T2) at 0.55T. Methods A 2D inversion recovery balanced steady-state free precession (IR-bSSFP) sequence was adapted to achieve high-temporal sampling of its transient phase at 0.55T. IR-bSSFP relaxometry was validated in manganese-doped phantoms using reference methods and tested in eight healthy volunteers as well as one patient. A fully automated pipeline was developed, featuring multi-contrast registration for motion correction and deep learning-based lung segmentation to enable voxel-wise nonlinear fitting for T1 and T2 map generation. Results Phantom results were in agreement with reference scans. The proposed free-breathing framework effectively mitigated respiratory motion, yielding quantitative maps in close agreement with breath-hold references. Average healthy lung parenchyma relaxation times were T1 = (920 ± 40)ms and T2 = (90 ± 8)ms. In a patient case, the method successfully distinguished a solid lung mass from surrounding parenchyma, with the lesion showing elevated T1 (950 vs 800ms in the surrounding parenchyma). Conclusions Simultaneous free-breathing T1 and T2 mapping of the lung is feasible at 0.55T using a fully automated pipeline. By eliminating breath-holds and external gating, this approach may improve patient compliance, demonstrating technical feasibility in a clinical setting and offering potential for future clinical evaluation.

papers.title: Elaborative processing before retrieval practice enhances semantic organization and long-term memory.
papers.authors: Dai J, Zhu Y, Zhao C, Sun M, Guo C.
papers.abstract: One longstanding goal in psychology is to identify more effective ways of learning. Recent work has shown that elaborative processing can amplify the memory benefits of retrieval practice, yet the mechanisms underlying this advantage remain unclear. Using electroencephalography (EEG), the present study examined how elaborative processing before retrieval practice influences later memory and encoding-related neural processing and representations, relative to context processing. Behaviorally, memory performance was better for elaborative processing plus retrieval practice than for context processing plus retrieval practice. During the first encoding phase, elaborative processing elicited a more negative N400, whereas context processing elicited a more positive LPC. Moreover, the N400 and LPC differences between elaborative and context processing during encoding were significantly correlated with the corresponding differences in 7-day recognition performance. Representational similarity analyses further showed stronger semantic-category organization and greater representational reorganization across repeated encoding under elaborative processing than under context processing. These findings suggest that elaborative processing before retrieval practice enhances long-term memory and is associated with broader semantic processing and stronger semantic organization during encoding. More broadly, the results suggest that richer connections with pre-existing semantic knowledge may be one way in which encoding variability supports long-term memory.

papers.title: HDAC3 inhibition alleviates neuroinflammation and white matter injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage through modulation of BDNF/TrkB/NF-κB signaling.
papers.authors: Yang H, Hu Z, Zhuang H, Chen S, Zhou S, Sun M, Lian L, Zhou C, Gao X, Huang Y.
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.abstract: White matter injury (WMI) is a major contributor to neurological deficits after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) is an established modulator of inflammatory responses, yet its contribution to post-SAH white matter pathology remains poorly understood. We used a rat endovascular perforation model and treated animals with RGFP966, a selective HDAC3 inhibitor. Clinical data, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and transmission electron microscopy were integrated to evaluate cellular remodeling and structural integrity. Short- and long-term neurological recovery was assessed using a systematic battery of behavioral tests, while the underlying BDNF/TrkB/NF-κB signaling axis was validated through gain- and loss-of-function experiments. HDAC3 levels were elevated in both the CSF of SAH patients and rat brain tissues, inversely correlating with myelin basic protein (MBP) expression. RGFP966 treatment effectively preserved WMI, evidenced by reduced axonal injury and improved myelin shielding, and translated to superior long-term cognitive performance. ScRNA-seq analysis identified a profound shift in the microglial and oligodendrocyte-lineage landscapes after SAH. HDAC3 inhibition effectively curbed the expansion of pro-inflammatory microglial subsets while restoring homeostatic signatures and enhancing pro-myelination programs. Mechanistically, RGFP966 upregulated BDNF expression and restored TrkB phosphorylation, thereby suppressing NF-κB-mediated neuroinflammation. Notably, BDNF knockdown abolished the protective effects of HDAC3 inhibition, whereas exogenous BDNF mimicked the anti-inflammatory and myelin-protective phenotype induced by RGFP966. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that HDAC3 is a pivotal driver of post-SAH neuroinflammation and WMI. Inhibition of HDAC3 exerts neuroprotection by recalibrating the microglial immune microenvironment and restoring the BDNF/TrkB axis.

papers.title: Individualized structural brain network and transcriptomic characterization of heterogeneity in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.authors: Wang H, Xu J, Wu Y, Du X, Zhang Y, Zhai Y, Zhang Z, Wu Q, Lei M, An Q, Cai W, Peng Y, Liu F, Zhang Q.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a heterogeneous metabolic disorder that also affects the brain, yet prior neuroimaging studies have predominantly focused on group-level comparisons, obscuring interindividual variability in brain structural organization. To capture this heterogeneity, we constructed individualized differential structural covariance networks for 156 individuals with T2DM using 148 healthy controls as a normative reference.
