Significance of results It highlights the importance of early psycho-oncological integration, shows how the generative document can extend into communal legacy work, and demonstrates that meaningful psychological support can continue beyond verbal communication. Prospective investigation of DT in brain tumor populations is warranted.

papers.title: Myelin as an emerging dimenpsysion of neuroendocrine brain plasticity: lifelong neuroactive steroid regulation and sex-specific mechanisms.
papers.authors: Schumacher M, Ghoumari AM.
papers.abstract: Neuroactive gonadal steroids and their metabolites are major regulators of brain development, function and plasticity. Their actions on neurons, astrocytes and microglia have been extensively studied, whereas their contribution to the lifelong regulation of myelin has received less attention. This question has acquired new significance with the recognition that myelin remains dynamic throughout life, undergoing activity- and experience-dependent remodeling and regeneration after injury or disease. Here, we review how progesterone and its neuroactive metabolites, estrogens and androgens regulate developmental myelination and myelin repair, and consider the emerging possibility that they may also influence adaptive myelination and maintenance of established myelin. We examine steroid-sensitive checkpoints of oligodendrocyte lineage progression and emphasize that steroid regulation of myelination extends beyond direct actions on oligodendroglial cells to multicellular interactions involving neurons, astrocytes and microglia. Remyelination provides particularly compelling evidence for such regulation: physiological gonadal steroid signaling can be required for efficient oligodendrocyte-mediated repair, and emerging studies indicate that males and females may recruit partly distinct cellular and molecular pathways to achieve similar regenerative outcomes. We further propose that adaptive myelination represents an overlooked dimension of neuroendocrine brain plasticity, potentially linking the changing steroid environment across the lifespan to experience-dependent remodeling of neural circuits. Integrating developmental, adaptive and regenerative myelination into neuroendocrinology may broaden the relevance of neuroactive steroids from demyelinating diseases to neurodevelopmental, neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders and provide new opportunities for sex- and endocrine-state-informed therapeutic strategies and biomarkers.

papers.title: Associations Between Dietary Carotenoids and Cognitive Performance in Older Hispanic/Latino Adults are Stronger in Men and Smokers.
papers.authors: Krause CA, Woods SP, Litson K, Ledoux T, Medina LD.
papers.abstract: Background Dietary intake is associated with age-related cognitive decline and neurodegenerative disease. Carotenoids, fruit-and-vegetable-derived nutrients, support brain health through anti-oxidative and anti-inflammatory properties in non-Hispanic White samples. However, their relevance to ethnoracially diverse populations, including the rapidly growing and aging Hispanic/Latin American (H/L) population, remains unclear. We sought to elucidate the relationship between carotenoids, cognition, and inflammation in adult H/Ls. Methods Cross-sectional data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey represented participants (Mage =67.5±5.9y) of Mexican American (n=2,078,580; 42% Spanish-preferring) and Other H/L heritage groups (n=2,244,252; 51% Spanish-preferring). Regression models adjusted for age, education, smoking status, BMI, acute inflammation, and total energy intake examined the relationship between carotenoid intakes (MTotal Carotenoid =9.47±9.05mg), and a cognitive composite score. Inverted mediation tested whether three systemic inflammation indices (i.e., systemic inflammation response index, SIRI; systemic immune-inflammation index, SII; and pan-immune-inflammation value, PIV) mediated these relationships. Results Regression results reflect sensitivity analyses that removed (n=61) extreme carotenoid intake values identified by Mahalanobis and Cook's distances. Regression models revealed that total carotenoids (β=0.26), α-carotene (β=0.22), β-cryptoxanthin (β=1.0), lutein+zeaxanthin (β=0.21), and lycopene (β=0.19) were significantly (all ps ≤ 0.04) associated with cognitive performance. Ethnicity/Language-stratified analyses demonstrated significant associations between total and individual carotenoids exclusively among English-preferring H/Ls. However, these associations did not remain significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction (all FDR-adjusted ps ≥ 0.09). Significant interactions suggested associations between a-carotene and cognitive performance differed by sex (χ2 (1)=7.02; p=0.029) and smoking (χ2 (1)=8.33; p =0.018). Post-hoc analyses revealed stronger effects for men (β=0.34) and smokers (β=1.64), respectively (all ps ≤ 0.001). Results did not support mediation effects of the systemic inflammation indices. Conclusion Findings revealed nuanced associations between carotenoids and cognition among H/Ls, varying by sex and smoking. Future diet-brain health work should prioritize culturally-informed, community-based approaches to address disparities at the intersection of culture, cognition, aging, and diet.

papers.title: Lesion characterization in magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound for essential tremor using quantitative susceptibility mapping.
papers.authors: Didier M, Pyatigorskaya N, Santin M, Bardinet E, Pouget P, Vidailhet M, Lehéricy S, Grabli D, Aubry JF, Karachi C, Galléa C, Hainque E.
papers.abstract: Background Focused ultrasound (FUS) thalamotomy targeting the ventral intermediate nucleus (VIM) is an increasingly adopted treatment for essential tremor. Although conventional T1/T2-weighted imaging is routinely used for post-treatment lesion segmentation shortly after the intervention, these modalities can be confounded by transient edema. Consequently, alternative sequences may offer refined tissue-level specificity regarding cytotoxic necrosis. Objectives We investigated the use of quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) as a tool to characterize the thermal lesion and explored the association between QSM-derived measures and clinical outcomes. Methods Fifteen essential tremor patients had clinical evaluation, T1, T2-FLAIR, QSM and diffusion images acquisition one week before and three months after FUS-thalamotomy. We assessed clinical improvement using the Clinical Rating Scale for Tremor, alongside sensory and cerebellar adverse effects. Lesions were segmented on individual QSM maps to extract volume and mean magnetic susceptibility. Using automatic region segmentation of the VIM and probabilistic tractography, we reconstructed the dentato-rubro-thalamo-cortical tract and the medial lemniscus, quantifying their spatial overlaps and adverse effect risks. Results QSM revealed lesions in 100% of cases, compared to 47% and 60% for T1- and T2-weighted images respectively. Mean magnetic susceptibility correlated with clinical improvement. Sensory adverse effect was related to lesion overlap with medial lemniscus, whereas cerebellar symptoms mapped to regions receiving cerebello-thalamic fibers. Conclusions QSM is a reliable method for lesion segmentation. Magnetic susceptibility reflects the microstructural changes and tissue damage produced by FUS thalamotomy, serving as an important determinant of therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of intracranial lesions assessed with MRI in infective endocarditis patients: Data from the Vesuve study.
papers.authors: Clottes P, Fontaine J, Hermier M, Eker OF, Cho TH, Mechtouff L, Nighoghossian N, Delahaye F, Thibault H, Derex L, Ong E.
papers.abstract: Background Infective endocarditis (IE) is a life-threatening disease. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is efficient to detect cerebral IE related lesions, which are known to worsen prognosis. Systematic use of MRI remains controversial due to insufficient scientific evidence. This work was aimed at clarifying the prognostic value of this imaging method in the context of IE. Methods The VESUVE study is a retrospective registry of patients with definite IE according to the modified Duke criteria, who had a brain MRI and were hospitalized between the 1st of November 2015 and the 15th of February 2019 in a Lyon University Hospital. All MRI were analyzed by the same senior neuroradiologist. Prognosis was evaluated by the mortality rate at 6 months. Results Among 212 patients, 162 were considered to have an abnormal MRI (76.4%). Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) was present in 125 patients (60.4%), intracranial hemorrhage in 8 patients (3.8%), hemorrhagic transformation in 41 patients (19.5%), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) in 26 patients (12.4%), cerebral microbleed in 130 patients (62.5%), intracranial mycotic aneurysm in 10 patients (5.1%), sulcal microaneurysm in 45 patients (23.6%) and abscess in 3 patients (1.5%). Mortality rate at 6 months was 19% (37 patients deceased). AIS (26.9% mortality, 31 patients deceased, OR 5.11) and SAH (44% mortality, 11 patients deceased, OR 4.32) were linked to mortality. Conclusion The presence of AIS or SAH on brain MRI is independently linked to mortality in IE patients. This strengthens the prognostic value of MRI in the assessment of IE.

papers.title: Sex-Related Multivariate Organization of Glymphatic MRI Markers in Healthy Adults.
papers.authors: Wang R, Wu S, Xu J, Huang X, Zhang S, Gong Q, Sun H.
papers.abstract: Sex may influence MRI-derived markers related to brain fluid and perivascular processes, but sex differences across glymphatic-related MRI markers remain unclear. We investigated sex differences in individual and multivariate glymphatic-related MRI markers in healthy adults. The Human Connectome Project (HCP) was used as the discovery dataset (n = 971; 521 females), and the Chinese Human Connectome Project (CHCP) was used as an independent validation dataset (n = 307; 157 females), from which a range of glymphatic-related MRI markers was derived. Sex differences in these glymphatic-related markers were examined, followed by principal component analysis (PCA) to characterize their multivariate organization. We found that males showed higher choroid plexus volume fraction, perivascular space volume fraction, and white-matter free-water fraction, but lower values for the index of diffusivity along the perivascular space and the index of periventricular diffusivity than females. PCA identified two dominant components explaining 63.45% of the total variance. Most glymphatic-related MRI markers showed consistent sex-related patterns in CHCP, and sex differences in HCP-projected component scores were directionally consistent with HCP. PCA performed separately in HCP and CHCP showed high similarity of the retained two-dimensional subspaces, with differences in individual component loading patterns. Together, these findings characterize sex-related variation in glymphatic-related MRI phenotypes at the individual-marker and multivariate levels.

papers.title: From field of view to point of view: integrating virtual reality as a tool to inform experiential learning in MRI education.
papers.authors: Hudson DM, Heales C.
papers.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences
papers.abstract: Introduction Newly qualified radiographers are required to perform a range of MRI examinations. Achieving proficiency involves more than technical capability; it also requires learners to demonstrate effective person-centred care. This includes the ability to recognise, understand and appropriately support claustrophobic and/or anxious patients, who are frequently encountered in the MR environment. The aim of this pilot was to examine whether a combined approach with the integration of a virtual reality (VR) experience, shifted the awareness and understanding of patient needs in MRI. Method An educational session was delivered consisting of an immersive MRI-based VR experience, framed by evidence-based, seminar-style teaching focused on patient experience, communication, and strategies for supporting individuals. Data were gathered using a survey comprising closed and open-ended questions, administered at both the start and end of the teaching session. Evaluation adhered to institutional review processes. Results Eight apprentice radiographers participated, demonstrating increased self-rated agreement across the assessed domains (between 0.59-1.44 mean increases). Open responses indicated a clearer appreciation of both the emotional challenges faced by patients and the radiographer's role in providing reassurance and support. Feedback consistently highlighted the value of undergoing the VR experience in enhancing perspective awareness and enacting empathy, with the seminar content perhaps having more influence over informing practice. Participants regarded both elements of the session as complementary and mutually reinforcing. Conclusion Teaching methods that strengthen awareness of patient experience are essential. This pilot suggests that VR, when integrated with evidence-based theoretical teaching, offers an alternative educational approach for promoting empathic MRI practice. Plain language summary MRI scans can be difficult for people who feel anxious or uncomfortable in small spaces. This study gave apprentice radiographers a virtual reality MRI experience along with teaching about patient care and communication. This study found that participants gained a better understanding of patient experiences and felt more aware of how to provide support and reassurance. This matters because helping future radiographers understand patients' needs may improve care and make MRI scans a more positive experience.

papers.title: Low-dose ketamine modulates brain entropy in treatment-resistant depression: Results from two neuroimaging clinical trials.
papers.authors: Liou YJ, Cheng LK, Lin WC, Su TP, Chen LF, Tu PC, Li CT, Bai YM, Tsai SJ, Chen MH.
papers.abstract: Background Several studies have reported entropy reductions in regions of the brain associated with affective-regulatory and reward- and motivation-related processes in patients with major depressive disorder. However, whether low-dose ketamine modulates this reduction remains unclear. Methods We analyzed resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from two single-infusion low-dose ketamine trials. Data at baseline and 3 days after infusion were analyzed. In Trial 1, patients with treatment-resistant depression were randomized to receive 0.2 or 0.5 mg/kg ketamine or normal saline. In Trial 2, patients with treatment-resistant depression and suicidal ideation were randomized to receive either 0.5 mg/kg ketamine or 0.045 mg/kg midazolam. Sample entropy was calculated from the spontaneous blood oxygenation level-dependent time series of 166 regions of interest defined by the automated anatomical labeling atlas 3. Results In Trial 1, increased brain entropy was observed in the gyrus rectus, cerebellar vermis I/II, substantia nigra, red nucleus, and bilateral locus coeruleus after low-dose ketamine infusion. In Trial 2, the ketamine group exhibited higher brain entropy in the left amygdala compared with the midazolam group. Discussion Low-dose ketamine rapidly increases brain entropy (from baseline to day 3) in frontolimbic, cerebellar, and ascending neuromodulatory regions, including the gyrus rectus, cerebellar vermis I/II, substantia nigra, red nucleus, bilateral locus coeruleus, and left amygdala. Changes in brain entropy after low-dose ketamine infusion may be associated with its rapid antidepressant and antianhedonic effects, although this relationship requires further investigation.

papers.title: Large language models for gait classification and treatment recommendation in cerebral palsy.
papers.authors: Çelik M, Ertan-Birsel S, Demirci E, Doğan O, Inan M.
papers.abstract: Background Large language model (LLM)-based artificial intelligence systems are increasingly being explored for the interpretation of clinical and biomechanical data. However, their ability to classify cerebral palsy gait patterns and support treatment-related decision-making remains unclear. Research question How accurately can commonly used LLM-based AI systems classify sagittal gait patterns in children with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy using kinematic graphs and three-dimensional skeletal gait videos, and how well do their treatment recommendations agree with expert decisions? Methods Fifteen children with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy, including three cases from each Rodda sagittal gait pattern, were retrospectively evaluated. ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude independently classified each case using bilateral sagittal-plane kinematic graphs and three-dimensional skeletal gait model videos and provided treatment recommendations. Expert consensus served as the reference standard. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa, together with classification accuracy. Results Classification accuracy was higher in the graph-based condition than in the video-based condition. Claude showed the highest graph-based performance (73.3% accuracy; κ=0.67), while ChatGPT and Gemini each achieved 46.7% accuracy (κ=0.33). Video-based accuracy decreased to 26.7% for ChatGPT and Gemini (κ=0.08) and 20.0% for Claude (κ=0.00). Inter-model agreement was fair for graph-based classification (κ=0.31) but poor for video-based classification (κ=-0.07). Treatment recommendation agreement was generally low across models and modalities. Significance Under the tested conditions, LLMs achieved higher accuracy with kinematic graphs, although the difference cannot be attributed to input modality alone. Graph-based classification showed promising performance; however, limited treatment concordance indicates that current LLMs should be considered supportive rather than independent clinical decision-making tools.

papers.title: Default mode network connectivity and temperament are associated with internalizing symptoms in early childhood.
papers.authors: Miller H, Chajes J, Grossmann T.
papers.abstract: This study investigates neural and temperament precursors to internalizing psychopathology. Increased default mode network (DMN) functional connectivity and decreased frontoparietal network (FPN) connectivity are established neural signatures of internalizing disorders in adults, but it is unknown if these patterns represent early-emerging vulnerability. In a community sample of typically developing children aged 4-6 years, we examined the concurrent associations of resting-state functional connectivity and temperament with internalizing symptoms. Of the 78 children retained following fNIRS quality control, 66 were included in the analytic sample (age range = 48-83 months; 38 female, 28 male; 78% White; predominantly high SES), We hypothesized that increased DMN connectivity, decreased FPN connectivity, and temperament traits of high negative affect and low surgency would be associated with higher internalizing problems. Functional connectivity was measured using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), a child-friendly neuroimaging technique. Internalizing symptoms and temperament were assessed via parent report using the Child Behavior Checklist and Child Behavior Questionnaire. A multiple linear regression revealed that greater DMN connectivity, higher negative affect, and lower surgency were significantly and independently associated with internalizing symptoms. FPN connectivity was not significantly associated with internalizing symptoms. These findings suggest that a key neural signature of adult depression-DMN hyperconnectivity-is associated with subclinical symptoms in early childhood, supporting its role as a primary vulnerability marker. The absence of an FPN association may reflect the protracted maturation of this cognitive control network, though longitudinal data are required to test whether neural risk factors for internalizing disorders emerge on distinct developmental timetables.

papers.title: Environment-specific virtual head direction representation in the human anteroventral thalamus during memory-guided spatial orientation.
papers.authors: Lv P, Chen D, Zhang C, Zhang K, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Knowing which way you are facing is essential for navigation. In animals, a dedicated set of neurons-head direction cells-acts as an internal compass: each cell fires most strongly when the animal faces a particular direction. The anterior thalamus is a key hub for this system. In humans, however, direct electrophysiological evidence for a comparable head direction signal remains limited. To address this gap, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography (EEG) from the anteroventral thalamus (AVT) in patients with epilepsy while they performed a virtual navigation task. We analyzed neural activity during in-place rotation to isolate virtual head direction (vHD) information. Using inverted encoding models applied to multi-band neural activity, we reconstructed continuous vHD within two distinct virtual environments. Critically, the decoders failed to generalize across environments, indicating that the AVT vHD representation is environment specific rather than a fixed, universal map. This encoding was observed in the AVT and was temporally specific to rotation epochs; no significant encoding was detected in the pulvinar, another thalamic subregion not part of the classic head direction network in rodents. Together, these findings suggest that the human AVT carries environment-specific vHD information, bridging a gap between animal models and human navigation and highlighting a potential link to spatial disorientation disorders.

papers.title: Predictive value of EEG/ECG biomarkers for treatment response in depression.
papers.authors: Provaznikova B, de Bardeci M, Altamiranda E, Ip CT, Monn A, Weber S, Jungwirth J, Rohde J, Prinz S, Kronenberg G, Brühl A, Bracht T, Olbrich S.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: Major depressive episodes frequently show limited response to first-line treatments, motivating the search for objective biomarkers. EEG/ECG-based support tools aggregating electrophysiological predictors may guide treatment selection. We examined whether antidepressant treatments concordant with an EEG/ECG-biomarker report were associated with higher response rates. We retrospectively analyzed adults with ICD-10 depressive disorder or bipolar depression treated with electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), (es)ketamine, or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) between 2022 and 2024. Resting-state EEG with simultaneous ECG generated individualized biomarker reports with modality-specific response likelihoods. Treatment chosen by clinical teams was classified as concordant or non-concordant; response was derived from routinely collected clinical scales. Among 153 patients (ECT n = 53, rTMS n = 48, (es)ketamine n = 36, SSRIs n = 16), response rates were higher for concordant vs non-concordant treatments: ECT 70% vs 50%, rTMS 30% vs 13%, (es)ketamine 31% vs 10%, and SSRIs 100% vs 11%. Overall, 46% (42/92) of concordant vs. 26% (14/54) of non-concordant patients responded (absolute difference + 20 percentage points; relative increase ≈77%; number needed to treat ≈5). Concordance with EEG/ECG biomarkers correlated with higher treatment response, warranting confirmation in prospective trials. EEG/ECG-based decision support may enhance antidepressant treatment response in everyday clinical practice.

papers.title: Magnetic resonance imaging and radiotherapy: Precision begins with imaging.
papers.authors: Gouel P, Autret D, Tournier A, Lapierre A, Baude J, Barateau A, Dufreneix S, Fitton I, Rétif P, Marchesi V, Moreau-Noblet C.
papers.journal: Cancer radiotherapie : journal de la Societe francaise de radiotherapie oncologique
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging has played an increasingly important role in radiotherapy, both before and during treatment. Before irradiation, its excellent soft-tissue contrast has provided a major advantage over simulation computed tomography by improving the visualization of tumour volumes and organs at risk, and by reducing delineation uncertainties, particularly in high-precision treatments such as stereotactic radiotherapy. Beyond morphological information, magnetic resonance imaging has also provided access to functional and quantitative data, such as diffusion-weighted imaging, apparent diffusion coefficient maps, perfusion and T1/T2 mapping, which may contribute to the biological characterization of tissues and to the early assessment of treatment response. During irradiation, onboard magnetic resonance imaging has helped overcome some of the limitations of cone beam computed tomography, owing to improved soft-tissue visualization, motion monitoring, and adaptation of the treatment plan to inter- or intrafraction anatomical variations. The development of magnetic resonance-only workflows, based on synthetic computed tomography generation, could also reduce dependence on planning computed tomography. However, these benefits have imposed specific requirements: acquisition under treatment-position conditions, geometric distortion control, reproducibility of quantitative acquisitions, accurate computed tomography-magnetic resonance imaging registration, and rigorous validation. Their implementation requires harmonization of practices, strengthened coordination between imaging and radiotherapy, and official recommendations, or even a dedicated regulatory framework.

papers.title: High-Intensity Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation for Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: A Triple-Blind Randomized Trial.
papers.authors: Ai Y, Zhang S, Huang L, Chen Q, Liu Y, Yin M, Zheng F, Wu S, Ye Z, Zheng H, Zhang L, Hu X.
papers.abstract: Background Non-invasive neuromodulation for post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) holds promise, but high-level evidence is lacking, partly due to the challenge of targeting single brain regions in a condition with diverse lesions and multi-network dysfunction. Objective The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of high-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (Hi-tACS) on cognitive function in patients with PSCI. Methods In this triple-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial, PSCI patients were randomized to receive either active or sham Hi-tACS. The tACS group received active Hi-tACS at 15 mA and 77.5 Hz for 40 minutes, twice daily, 5 days a week for 2 weeks. The sham group used identical devices without current delivery. The primary outcome was the change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary outcomes included Digit Span Test and cerebral oxyhemoglobin (HbO) concentration changes measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Results The tACS group (n=34) showed higher MoCA response rates than the sham group (n=34) immediately after treatment (73.5% vs 38.2%, P=0.003) and at the 4-week post-treatment follow-up (88.2% vs 55.9%, P=0.003). Improvements in forward and backward digit span were also greater in the tACS group at both assessments. The intention-to-treat analysis of all 70 randomized participants yielded results consistent with the per-protocol analysis. Exploratory fNIRS analyses identified greater HbO increases in the left, right, and medial prefrontal regions in the tACS group at T1 after FDR correction (all q=0.033), whereas no regional difference remained significant at T2. Conclusion Hi-tACS improved global cognition and working memory in patients with PSCI and was generally well tolerated. Exploratory fNIRS findings suggested possible accompanying changes in cortical activation and network organization but did not establish a neurophysiological mechanism. Importantly, as a broad-network stimulation approach, Hi-tACS may reduce reliance on selecting a single precise target, a potential practical advantage in heterogeneous PSCI.

papers.title: Analysis of the dynamic evolution and immunosuppressive functions of myeloid cells in gliomas based on single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Yuan H, Yang J, Bai Z, Wang H, Tong J, Chen P, Gong S.
papers.abstract: Background Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and lethal primary brain tumor. However, the dynamic evolution of myeloid cells within its microenvironment and their role in immune suppression remain unclear. This study aims to elucidate the heterogeneity and immune regulatory mechanisms of myeloid cells, particularly tumor-associated neutrophils, through single-cell transcriptomic analysis. Methods We integrated single-cell transcriptomic data from 4 cases of GBM and 4 cases of low-grade glioma (LGG) to systematically analyze the myeloid cell landscape and identify neutrophil subpopulations and their differentiation trajectories. Utilizing CellChat cell-cell communication analysis, pseudotime trajectory analysis (performed on CD8 + T cells), and functional scoring, we revealed the interaction network between SRGN + neutrophils and CD8 + T cell subpopulations. Furthermore, based on the TCGA cohort, we constructed a SRGN + signature-based prognostic model to evaluate immune infiltration, immune checkpoints, TIDE immune evasion, and temozolomide sensitivity. Results Neutrophils were specifically enriched in GBM. A SRGN + subpopulation highly expressed S100A8/A9, IL1B, and PMN-MDSC-related genes, with elevated inflammation and S100 scores. Functional scoring indicated that this subpopulation exhibited pro-inflammatory and immunoregulatory characteristics. Among CD8 + T cells, three exhausted subsets were defined: Tex_PD1, Tex_NKG2A, and Tex_TIM3. CellChat-based ligand-receptor analysis predicted preferential chemotactic signaling from SRGN + neutrophils toward Tex_PD1 cells via CCL pathways and toward Tex_TIM3 cells via CXCL pathways, as well as potential inhibitory signaling toward Tex_NKG2A and Tex_TIM3 cells via the HLA-E-NKG2A axis. A 12-gene risk model stratified GBM patients into high- and low-risk groups. High-risk patients showed shorter overall survival but greater temozolomide sensitivity (reduced IC50 predicted by oncoPredict analysis), alongside an immune phenotype of "increased T-cell infiltration yet functional exhaustion." TIDE analysis confirmed elevated dysfunction scores, reduced exclusion scores, and low MDSC phenotype scores, consistent with SRGN + neutrophils lacking classic MDSC markers. Conclusion This study systematically characterizes the dynamic evolution and immunosuppressive functions of myeloid cells, particularly SRGN + neutrophils, in GBM, suggesting a potential dual "chemotactic recruitment and selective suppression" mechanism by which they may shape the landscape of CD8 + T-cell exhaustion. The risk model constructed based on this subpopulation demonstrated prognostic stratification value within the TCGA-GBM cohort, pending validation in independent cohorts, and suggests a potential therapeutic strategy combining targeting of the HLA-E-NKG2A axis with temozolomide.

papers.title: Individualized brain mapping for neurosurgical planning.
papers.authors: Voets NL.
papers.abstract: The need for personalised approaches in neurosurgery arises from marked variations in the distribution and performance of functional networks among individual brains. Functional MRI and diffusion tractography have been widely adopted for neurosurgical planning. However, the way in which neuroimaging results are used clinically remains largely qualitative. This review explores how personalised neurosurgical mapping can move toward quantitative, patient-specific predictions by adopting techniques from the field of neuroscience. Exciting potential comes from extending our largely static measures of network organisation with metrics probing the dynamic nature of information processing in the brain. Such multidimensional approaches show promise to capture aspects of complex behaviour relevant to everyday function beyond the mainstream focus on language and motor skills. Yet, translation of advanced approaches into the clinic faces many challenges. Progress will require validated metrics capturing individually-unique patient profiles, methods for robust multimodal integration, clinically usable analytical tools, and outcomes that better capture real-life performance. By combining spatial, structural and temporal features of brain networks, neuroimaging may evolve from a 'localisation' tool into a platform for personalised neurosurgical prediction, intervention and longitudinal care.

papers.title: A Sensorimotor-Interoceptive Model for Sensory Phenomena in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Neural and Computational Mechanisms.
papers.authors: Zhang G, Han H, Cheng J, Luo Q, Stern ER, Wang Z.
papers.abstract: Classical models of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) grounded in cognitive-affective processes do not fully account for sensory phenomena (SP), including bodily discomfort, incompleteness, and not-just-right experiences that often precede or accompany compulsive behavior. To address this gap, we propose a sensorimotor-interoceptive model for the sources, generation, and maintenance of SP and SP-driven compulsions in OCD. Specifically, the posterior insula may integrate external sensory signals with internal bodily signals within the perceptual module. These integrated signals are subsequently processed by the salience module centered on the anterior insula and anterior cingulate cortex, where heightened error monitoring may assign excessive salience to integrated signals and recruit the supplementary motor area and primary motor cortex to initiate corrective actions. Dysfunction of a cerebellum-centered forward system may then produce persistent mismatches between predicted and actual action outcomes, which are re-entered into the perceptual module and sustain a recurrent feedback loop. The framework therefore conceptualizes SP-driven compulsions as maladaptive attempts to resolve persistent sensory errors. Predictive coding and active inference provide a computational account of these processes. We underscore that this sensorimotor-interoceptive model, intended to complement existing models, provides an account of symptoms in which SP are prominent and may therefore contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of OCD.

papers.title: Role of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in the diagnosis of chronic constrictive pericarditis revealed by Pick's syndrome: A case report.
papers.authors: Sall F, Meneas C, N'Cho Mottoh MP, Akatchi R, Vy L, Boka BC, Adoubi A.
papers.abstract: Introduction Chronic constrictive pericarditis (CCP), or Pick's syndrome, is a rare but severe inflammatory disease of the pericardium, often difficult to distinguish from restrictive cardiomyopathy without multimodality imaging. In sub-Saharan Africa, tuberculosis remains the leading cause. Case presentation We report the case of a 37-year-old woman with a history of post-partum hypertension, admitted for a three-month history of exertional dyspnoea, lower-limb oedema and retrosternal chest pain in a febrile, tuberculosis-suggestive context. Examination revealed isolated right heart failure with a pericardial knock. Echocardiography and cardiac MRI showed pericardial thickening and circumferential detachment, bi-atrial dilatation and a septal bounce, with late gadolinium enhancement and T1/T2 mapping consistent with active pericardial inflammation, confirming an evolving, inflammatory form of CCP. Coronary CT angiography excluded coexisting coronary disease and revealed tuberculous pulmonary sequelae. Under corticosteroids, antituberculous therapy and symptomatic management, the patient improved clinically, allowing pericardiectomy to be deferred. Conclusion This case highlights the value of cardiac MRI in the early diagnosis of inflammatory, potentially reversible forms of CCP, helping to avoid upfront surgery and guide targeted medical management, particularly in tuberculosis-endemic regions.

papers.title: Imaging Features and Prognosis of Anti‑Sez6l2 Encephalitis: A Longitudinal Cohort Study and Literature Review.
papers.authors: Dong S, Tu S, Chen S, Meng H.
papers.abstract: Anti-Seizure-Related 6 Homolog Like 2 (Sez6l2) encephalitis is a rare autoimmune disorder characterized by cerebellar ataxia and cognitive impairment. The 13 previously reported cases included in our systematic analysis focus on adults, leaving gaps in pediatric demographics, longitudinal multimodal imaging markers, and effective management of refractory cases. This study aimed to expand the clinical spectrum, evaluate multimodal imaging in localizing neuroinflammation/monitoring response, and assess the efficacy of combined first- and second-line immunotherapy. We analyzed a longitudinal cohort of five Sez6l2-antibody-positive patients (aged 15-72 years) alongside a systematic review (N = 18). Clinical severity (mRS, CASE, MMSE, MoCA), structural MRI, and 18 F-DPA714 PET/MRI mapped neuroinflammation and monitored therapeutic response. Our cohort features the first documented adolescent case. All five patients presented with ataxia and cognitive deficits. While MRI revealed cerebellar atrophy in three patients, 18 F-DPA714 PET/MRI detected microglial activation in the cerebellum (n = 4) and bilateral mesial temporal lobes (n = 1), mapping precisely to clinical phenotypes. Longitudinally, clinical improvement paralleled a 7%-8% reduction in cerebellar tracer uptake in Case 1. Patients receiving combined first- and second-line immunotherapy (efgartigimod, ofatumumab; n = 3) achieved pronounced cognitive and psychiatric recovery. Conversely, first-line therapy alone yielded limited efficacy in the 66-year-old patient with established atrophy, while the adolescent showed more favorable responsiveness. The systematic review (N = 18) confirmed universal ataxia (100%), frequent cognitive impairment (72%), and significant residual disability (median mRS 4). This study expands the demographic spectrum of Sez6l2 encephalitis to adolescents and provides cohort-based evidence for multimodal imaging in localizing neuroinflammation/monitoring response, highlighting combined immunosuppressants as possible new therapeutic options.

papers.title: Astrocyte-Regulatory T Cell Communication in Neuroinflammation: From Glial Reactivity to Immune Modulation.
papers.authors: Juárez-Solano AH, Pérez-Osorio IN, Adalid-Peralta L, Guevara-Salinas A, Torres-Ramos MA.
papers.journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
papers.abstract: The interaction between astrocytes, microglia, and regulatory T cells (Tregs) is essential for maintaining immune homeostasis in the central nervous system (CNS). During neuroinflammation, communication between astrocytes and reactive microglia promotes the upregulation of chemokines that induce T cell infiltration and differentiation into Th17 cells through RORγt activation in response to IL-1β. Effector Th17 cells secrete IL-17 A and IL-17 F, which act on astrocytes and reactive microglia to induce the secondary release of TNF-α and IL-6. This establishes a paracrine feed-forward loop in which glia-derived IL-6 promotes further polarization of T cells toward the Th17 phenotype. In turn, TNF-α acts synergistically with IL-17 to promote the expansion of neurotoxic reactive astrocytes and contributes to disease progression. In contrast, sustained pro-inflammatory cytokine signaling induces CD69 expression on T cells, which, upon interaction with the S100A8/A9 complex secreted by reactive astrocytes, suppresses RORγt and promotes the generation of immunoregulatory Tregs. These CD69⁺ Tregs secrete IL-10 and amphiregulin (Areg), attenuating astrogliosis by inhibiting the STAT3-IL-6 pathway and helping to restore cerebral homeostasis. The persistence and dynamic regulation of Tregs underscore their homeostatic and therapeutic relevance. Additionally, communication between the gut microbiota (GM) and the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is a key modulator of the Th17/Treg axis. Although its role in T cell differentiation within the CNS still requires further investigation, it represents a promising therapeutic strategy to modulate glial activation in chronic neuroinflammatory diseases.

papers.title: A PTN+ glioblastoma subclone orchestrates immune reprogramming to drive distant recurrence.
papers.authors: Yan X, Hu J, Hu Y, Xu M, Gao S, Han X, Zhao D, Li Q, Zhou L, Hu S.
papers.abstract: Aims Distant recurrence (DR) represents a distinct and lethal trajectory in glioblastoma (GBM), characterized by the colonization of spatially isolated neural niches. The mechanisms by which disseminated tumor cells remodel the microenvironment to overcome anatomical and immunological barriers remain poorly understood. This study aimed to decode the immune ecosystem of DR and elucidate the intercellular crosstalk driving this lethal dissemination. Methods We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on paired primary and DR tumor specimens from GBM patients, alongside an independent local recurrence (LR) control cohort, to map dynamic cellular shifts. Bioinformatic analyses, including differential abundance testing (Milo), cell-cell communication inference (CellChat), and copy number variation (CNV) analysis, were integrated with clinical co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) validation, bidirectional in vitro co-culture assays, and an orthotopic xenograft mouse model. Results Our high-resolution atlas revealed a profound remodeling of the microenvironment in DR lesions, characterized by a specific expansion of anti-inflammatory monocyte-derived tumor-associated macrophages (Anti_infl-TAM) and a paradoxical co-enrichment of CD8 + T cells and Tregs. Mechanistically, an OPC-like subpopulation of PTN+ tumor cells acted as a "paracrine architect," promoting Anti_infl-TAM polarization through the interaction between PTN and NCL. Co-IP assays confirmed direct physical binding of these two proteins in human DR tissues. Functional and bidirectional knockdown assays demonstrated that decoupling this cellular communication, achieved by targeting either PTN in tumor cells or NCL in macrophages, significantly attenuated glioma cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and macrophage polarization. In vivo, silencing PTN markedly reduced Anti_infl-TAM infiltration, suppressed intracranial tumor burden, and prolonged overall survival in tumor-bearing mice. Conclusion This study establishes that DR GBM is defined by a reconfigured immune niche rather than mere genetic drift. The paracrine crosstalk between PTN+ tumor cells and Anti_infl-TAM serves as a critical engine of this permissive soil, offering a promising therapeutic target to disrupt the supportive microenvironment in distant recurrent GBM.

papers.title: A Reproducible MRI-to-FE Workflow for Generating Population-Specific and Subject-Specific Finite Element Head Models.
papers.authors: Saludar CJA, Tayebi M, Kwon E, Mathew J, McGeown J, Schierding W, Mātai mTBI Research Group, Wang A, Fernandez J, Holdsworth S, Shim V.
papers.abstract: Purpose Finite element (FE) models are widely used to study traumatic brain injury, but most are based on single-subject scans or generic atlases that may not represent specific cohorts, introducing variability in biomechanical outputs. This study presents a reproducible framework for generating a cohort-specific MRI-derived template brain and constructing a representative FE head model. Methods A cohort-specific template was created from T1-weighted and diffusion-weighted MRI scans of collision sport athletes (n = 78). An FE head model was then generated from this template, with material properties mapped using MRI-derived microstructural information. The anatomical accuracy of the template was evaluated using deformation-based morphometry against standard brain atlases. The FE model was validated against cadaveric head impact experiments. Subject-specific FE models were also developed to test the pipeline's applicability and model performance. Results Registration of an external non-collision sport controls (n = 20) to the template showed reduced deformation compared with registration to the MNI152 and an existing adolescent atlas, indicating improved cohort representation. Validation against cadaveric data demonstrated small to moderate correlations between simulated and experimental nodal displacements. The subject-specific model showed significantly different strain distributions from isotropic and fiber dispersion-informed models at both impact intensities; the two template models did not differ significantly. Conclusion The proposed framework enables reproducible construction of cohort-specific FE brain models using open-access tools. Results highlight the importance of subject- and cohort-specific modeling for accurately characterizing brain biomechanics. This approach improves the anatomical and microstructural realism of FE models and supports more precise mapping of mechanical strain to clinical outcomes in TBI.

papers.title: T2 mapping of individual fascicles of the sciatic nerve at 7 T using multi-echo spin-echo.
papers.authors: Sleight E, Piredda GF, Grouiller F, Romanin L, Gariani K, Lascano AM, Gui L, Jende JME, Lovblad KO, Hilbert T, Kurz FT, Karampinos DC.
papers.abstract: Objective Neuropathies can selectively affect individual fascicles within peripheral nerves, but diagnosis is limited by MRI spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratio. This feasibility study aimed to leverage 7 T MRI to measure sub-millimetric T2 maps of sciatic nerve fascicles in healthy subjects. Materials and methods Accelerated multi-echo spin-echo sequences were acquired in six healthy volunteers at 7 T. Acceleration included generalised autocalibrating partially parallel acquisition (GRAPPA) and GRAPPATINI, which integrates GRAPPA with model-based accelerated relaxometry. Extended phase graph (EPG) modelling of signal decay was used to compute T2 maps. Quantitative maps were visually assessed and T2 values were extracted from regions of interest. Results High-resolution imaging (0.4×0.4x3.0 mm3 ) enabled visualisation of individual fascicles. T2 values were lower in fascicles (57.0 ms) than in the non-fascicular intraneural compartment (76.2 ms) and intermuscular fat (132.7 ms). Compared with GRAPPA alone, GRAPPATINI reduced acquisition time (11:05 to 3:35 min) while maintaining fascicle depiction and T2 consistency (mean difference: 1.45 ms). Overlaying T2 on S0 maps enhanced fascicle delineation, facilitating anatomical interpretation. Discussion This approach demonstrated the feasibility of high-resolution T2 mapping of peripheral nerve fascicles at 7 T, offering a potential tool for improved assessment of nerve microstructure and early neuropathy detection.

papers.title: Heterogeneous decision-making in ADHD: computational subtypes and their distinct prefrontal connectivity patterns.
papers.authors: Hong H, Yu Z, Li H, Wang Y, Liu L, Qian Q.
papers.abstract: Children with ADHD exhibit decision-making deficits characterized by lower efficiency in evidence accumulation and a preference for smaller, sooner rewards in intertemporal choices. This study aimed to preliminarily explore computational subtypes of ADHD in children and to investigate differences in prefrontal functional connectivity between ADHD subtypes. A total of 94 children with ADHD and 63 typically developing children matched for sex, age, and IQ were included. All participants completed the Two Choice Impulsivity Paradigm (TCIP) and the ADHD Symptom Rating Scale, and 43 children with ADHD underwent resting-state fMRI. A hierarchical drift diffusion model was applied to analyze TCIP task performance, followed by two-step cluster analysis to identify decision-making subtypes. Differences in prefrontal functional connectivity among ADHD decision-making subtypes were then compared. The ADHD group showed fewer square selections in the TCIP (p < 0.001), lower drift rates (pBayes < 0.001), and shorter non-decision times (pBayes = 0.002). Two decision-making subtypes were identified: a decision-making deficit subtype and a decision-making normal subtype, characterized by lower and higher drift rates, respectively. The ADHD decision-making deficit subtype exhibited stronger functional connectivity between the left medial superior frontal gyrus and both the right middle frontal gyrus and the right postcentral gyrus, as well as between the right medial superior frontal gyrus and the right postcentral gyrus (all p < 0.05). The results reveal decision-making deficits and internal heterogeneity in children with ADHD during intertemporal choice, with this heterogeneity possibly associated with abnormal functional connectivity between the medial superior frontal gyrus and the middle frontal gyrus/postcentral gyrus.

papers.title: Next-Generation Brain Health Monitoring Enabled by Integrated Wearable AI Infrastructure.
papers.authors: Masrur MH, Khan B, Khalid RT, Sumaira, Abdullah S.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are difficult to detect during their pre-symptomatic stages, when intervention is most effective. Advances in wearable biosensors, artificial intelligence (AI), and neuroscience now enable continuous monitoring of brain-related physiological signals in real-world settings. However, progress in sensing technologies, signal analytics, and machine learning remains fragmented, limiting the biological specificity, robustness, and clinical translation of many digital biomarkers. This review presents an integrated framework that links molecular pathology and neural circuit dysfunction to sensor-detectable digital phenotypes across sleep, autonomic regulation, gait, speech, and ocular dynamics. We evaluate emerging wearable platforms, including bioelectric, optical, and neuromotor sensors, and discuss critical design considerations such as signal quality, user-centered form factors, and ultra-low-power edge AI systems. We further examine how self-supervised learning, federated AI, mechanistic modeling, and fairness-aware validation can improve biomarker reliability, interpretability, and generalizability. To facilitate clinical deployment, we introduce the Personalized Brain-Health Operating System (pBH-OS), a privacy-preserving reference architecture for scalable digital phenotyping. The framework maps conceptual layers to existing technologies while identifying key validation gaps. We also address practical challenges, including adherence, device dropout, informative missingness, regulatory compliance, and accountability. Together, these advances provide a pathway toward biologically grounded and regulation-ready systems capable of identifying neurodegenerative risk years before clinical symptom onset.
keywords: Bio‐Signal Monitoring, And Remote Patient Monitoring

papers.title: Perivascular Diffusivity and Periventricular Susceptibility Changes in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Combined DTI-ALPS and QSM Study.
papers.authors: Revanth RB, Smitha KA, Jithin SS, Meena P, Nair SS, Jayadevan ER, Thomas B, Kesavadas C.
papers.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
papers.abstract: Background Progressive periventricular damage in multiple sclerosis (MS) has been linked to impaired perivascular clearance and to susceptibility changes attributed to iron deposition and myelin loss. Their relationship is unclear. Purpose/hypothesis To compare diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) and periventricular quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) between relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) patients and healthy controls; and to evaluate their correlation and relationships with clinical disability (Expanded Disability Status Scale, EDSS). Study type Retrospective case-control study. Population/subjects Thirty one patients with RRMS (mean age, 34.6 ± 8.4 years) and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age, 34.2 ± 8.1 years). Field strength/sequence 1.5 T; Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and multi-echo gradient-echo (GRE) sequences. Assessment DTI-ALPS index and periventricular QSM values were measured from manually placed bilateral regions of interest (ROIs). Standardized Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI)-space coordinates were used for DTI-ALPS analysis, and QSM ROIs in periventricular normal-appearing white matter were reviewed by a neuroradiologist. Disability was assessed using the EDSS. Statistical tests Groups were compared using independent-samples t-tests and Cohen's d. Correlations were assessed using Pearson's r, with Spearman's rho as a sensitivity analysis (p < 0.05, two-tailed). Results DTI-ALPS was lower in MS patients than controls (1.27 ± 0.22 vs. 1.45 ± 0.22; d = 0.828), whereas periventricular QSM was higher (-15.35 ± 4.92 vs. -21.70 ± 6.40 ppb; d = 1.116). A strong negative correlation between the two biomarkers was observed across all subjects (r = -0.738). Both measures correlated with EDSS (DTI-ALPS r = -0.509; QSM r = 0.501) and differed between EDSS subgroups (EDSS > 2.0 vs. ≤ 2.0: DTI-ALPS 1.160 vs. 1.364; QSM -12.33 vs. -17.83 ppb). Data conclusion Reduced DTI-ALPS and higher periventricular QSM-derived susceptibility were each moderately associated with disability in RRMS. The negative DTI-ALPS-QSM correlation in both groups indicates an association between perivascular diffusivity, a putative marker of glymphatic function, and periventricular QSM-derived susceptibility; causality cannot be established from this cross-sectional design. Level of evidence: 3 Stage of technical efficacy 2.

papers.title: Maternal microbiota shapes brain and neuroendocrine development in piglets.
papers.authors: Wang L, Yan C, Li L, Deng Y, Shao H, Long K, Long C, Zhu Y, Chen M, Huang J, Jiang J, Lin Z, Yao Y, Yang T, Guo W, Ge L, Sun J, Ding Y, Liu Z, Yin M, Yin Y.
papers.abstract: The maternal microbiota plays a critical role in early-life development, yet how maternal microbiota exposure shapes cellular and neuroendocrine programs during mammalian development remains poorly understood. Here, leveraging germ-free (GF) and maternal microbiota transplantation (MMT) models, we generated an integrated multi-organ porcine atlas by combining multi-regional single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk RNA sequencing of intestinal tissues, and metabolomics. Across five brain regions and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, we profiled 673,623 high-quality nuclei and revealed microbiota-dependent remodeling of neuronal and glial states across early postnatal developmental stages. MMT reshaped neuronal maturation programs, altered the distribution of immature neuronal states, and elicited region-specific transcriptional responses in glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons. MMT also reorganized neuron-glia interaction networks, accompanied by trends toward increased plasma glutamic acid and glutamine levels. Across the gut-brain-neuroendocrine axis, MMT was associated with coordinated remodeling of HPA-axis cellular communication, stress-response transcriptional programs, and immune signatures, together with reduced circulating cortisol levels. Integrated intestinal analyses revealed segment-specific transcriptional and metabolic remodeling, including alterations in tryptophan/indole-related metabolites and immune-associated pathways. Cross-species stratified linkage disequilibrium score regression further identified enrichment of human cognitive and neuropsychiatric trait-associated genetic signals within cell-type-specific gene signatures derived from microbiota-responsive porcine cell populations. Our study establishes a large-animal cellular atlas linking maternal microbiota-responsive remodeling across the brain, gut, and neuroendocrine axis, providing a translational framework for understanding how early-life microbial signals shape mammalian developmental physiology.

papers.title: Digital completion time relates more strongly to Alzheimer's disease-type atrophy than to vascular burden in a community cohort.
papers.authors: Iwasa K, Omori N, Ishida M, Tanaka T, Nagai A.
papers.abstract: Introduction Slowing on digital cognitive testing may reflect Alzheimer's disease (AD)-type atrophy, small-vessel disease, or both. Single-outcome studies cannot determine whether slowing preferentially reflects one type of brain change or general brain health. We tested whether response-time features from the tablet-based Cognitive Assessment for Dementia, iPad version 2 (CADi2) were more strongly associated with AD-type atrophy than with vascular burden. Methods In 1163 community-dwelling adults undergoing brain-health screening (Izumo cohort, 2019-2025), CADi2 response-time features predicted two primary MRI markers from one framework under repeated nested cross-validation: Alzheimer's disease likelihood score (ADLS; similarity to an AD-type atrophy pattern) and normalized white matter lesion (WML) volume. The primary metric was the incremental observed-predicted correlation (ΔR ) over age and sex. Silent brain infarcts, microbleeds, and a composite small vessel disease score were additional vascular outcomes. Results CADi2 features improved prediction of ADLS (ΔR = +0.054, 95% confidence interval [CI] +0.010 to +0.095) but not WML (ΔR = -0.006). The improvement reflected completion time, not accuracy. Because predictive headroom differed, we repeated the comparison in residual space. There, the increment correlated about twice as strongly with ADLS as with WML (r = 0.160 vs. 0.080; p = 0.044), although both remained significant. A parallel contrast against the composite vascular score gave Δr = 0.100 (p = 0.008). Discussion Digital completion time was preferentially, but not exclusively, associated with AD-type atrophy (neurodegeneration axis) relative to vascular burden. Because ADLS indexes an atrophy pattern rather than amyloid or tau pathology, these cross-sectional findings characterize a structural phenotype.

papers.title: Maternal Hyperglycemia Disrupts Cerebral Cortex Development Through the Foxp1-Dll1-Notch Axis.
papers.authors: He L, Jin Y, Liu G, Liu H, Zhu X, Xu W, Li W, He M, Shen Y, Li B, Yang X, Wang X, Han S.
papers.abstract: Maternal hyperglycemia is associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in offspring, but the mechanisms by which it affects fetal brain development remain incompletely understood. Using a mouse model of pregestational diabetes mellitus (PGDM), we found that maternal hyperglycemia was associated with reduced cortical thickness and altered cortical lamination. These abnormalities were accompanied by changes in neural stem cell differentiation and asymmetric division, as well as impaired neuronal migration and dendritic development. Transcriptomic analysis identified the transcription factor Foxp1 as markedly downregulated in the PGDM embryonic cortex. Restoring Foxp1 expression in vivo substantially alleviated the observed cortical abnormalities. Mechanistic experiments showed that Foxp1 represses transcription of the Notch ligand Delta-like 1 (Dll1) and attenuates Notch signaling. Together, these findings implicate the Foxp1-Dll1-Notch axis as one pathway contributing to disrupted corticogenesis in the PGDM model and provide insight into how an adverse intrauterine metabolic environment affects embryonic brain development.

papers.title: CNTN2 Deficiency Disrupts Ascending Auditory Neuroglial Interactions and Redox Homeostasis in Neural Presbycusis.
papers.authors: Chen P, Zhu J, Huang S, Xu B, Duan M, Lv J, Chen J, Yang J, Hou S.
papers.abstract: Neural presbycusis disrupts auditory timing and speech perception, yet its molecular basis remains poorly understood. This study identifies Cntn2 as the Ranvier's nodal molecule significantly downregulated in aged auditory nerves. Cntn2 heterozygous knockout (Cntn2+/- ) mice showed elevated auditory brainstem response thresholds and prolonged wave latencies and interpeak intervals, whereas distortion product otoacoustic emission thresholds were largely preserved. Hair cell and ribbon synapses were preserved, with no obvious ultrastructural changes, suggesting that overt hair cell loss or synaptic structural loss is unlikely to be the main cause of the early phenotype. Instead, transmission electron microscopy revealed myelin outfoldings and aberrant node of Ranvier morphology in myelinated auditory nerve fibers, accompanied by increased Schwann cell density. Multiplex immunofluorescence and Western blot analysis showed disruption of nodal molecular organization along the ascending auditory pathway from cochlea to auditory cortex. Transcriptomic profiling and oxidative stress assays further linked CNTN2 deficiency to altered neuroglial interaction and redox imbalance. Early unilateral AAV-mediated CNTN2 restoration partially improved threshold and latency abnormalities. These findings identify CNTN2-dependent neuroglial integrity as an important contributor to auditory conduction of neural presbycusis and may provide a new direction for future therapeutic studies.

papers.title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large-Area Tin-based Perovskite Solar Cells.
papers.authors: Zhang W, Li T, Huang X, Zhang D, Jin Z, Wang P, Nie J, Lin S, Cao W, Wang Y, Wang Y, Li Z, Fu Y, An M, Liang J.
papers.abstract: Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p-type small molecule, 4,4'-(5,6-bis(2-methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole-4,7-diyl)bis(2,5-difluoro-N,N-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic-angle spinning 1 H NMR, 1 H-1 H double-quantum-single-quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning-rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high-quality Sn-based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap-assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG-PEDOT:PSS-based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1-cm2 devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04-cm2 devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N2 atmosphere.

papers.title: Changing Patterns of Transient Ischemic Attack Evaluation in US Emergency Departments.
papers.authors: Mamer LE, Cranford JA, Li J, Kocher KE, Zahuranec DB, Korley FK, Scott PA.
papers.abstract: Importance For US patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with transient ischemic attack (TIA), guidelines recommend resource-intensive multimodal evaluation to optimize secondary stroke prevention. These resources are not available in all EDs, and national patterns of ED TIA care are not well described. Objectives To evaluate national trends in ED TIA care, including discharge practices, imaging use, and associated costs, and to assess patient- and hospital-level factors associated with these patterns. Design, setting, and participants This was a retrospective repeated cross-sectional study of ED visits using the 2013-2021 National Emergency Department Sample of the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project, a weighted, nationally representative annual sample of ED visits in the US. TIA and stroke encounters during the study period were identified among patients aged 18 years or older by a first-listed International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision or Tenth Revision code for TIA or stroke diagnosis. Analyses were performed from October 2024 to April 2026. Exposures Calendar year. Main outcomes and measures ED discharge; imaging use among discharged TIA encounters; and inflation-adjusted ED cost per discharged encounter. Results This study included 2 151 408 (95% CI, 2 107 855-2 194 960) weighted ED visits for TIA (1 194 630 [55.5%] female; mean [SEM] age, 69.8 [0.05] years). Adjusted models found the predicted probability of discharge increased from 45% (95% CI, 43%-46%) in 2013 to 66% (95% CI, 64%-68%) in 2021 (P < .001 for trend). During this time, mean ED charges increased from $1746 (95% CI, $1662-$1830) to $2755 (95% CI, $2674-$2836) per encounter (P < .001 for trend). Imaging use among discharged TIA encounters increased substantially, including computed tomography angiography (predicted probability, 4% [95% CI, 3%-4%] in 2013 vs 45% [95% CI, 42%-47%] in 2021; P < .001 for trend) and magnetic resonance imaging (predicted probability, 17% [95% CI, 16%-19%] in 2013 vs 53% [95% CI, 50%-55%] in 2021; P < .001 for trend). Rate of discharge was higher in rural encounters than in urban encounters for all years studied, and the rate of magnetic resonance imaging use was lower. Conclusions and relevance This cross-sectional study demonstrates a shift in TIA care over time that suggests increased use of the ED to expedite evaluation for TIA that previously occurred during a brief hospitalization. This approach has consequences in terms of cost and ED throughput and may not be as feasible in rural hospitals as it is in urban hospitals.

papers.title: Gain-of-Function Variants in PLAAT4 and Spinal Predominant Demyelinating Leukodystrophy.
papers.authors: Zeng YH, Chen B, Shi Y, Jiang J, Zhang Z, Ma MM, Wu S, Fu J, Zhang S, Lin J, Ye P, Chen S, Yan X, Zhu J, Xie J, Lin S, Dong E, Cheng X, Wang N, Ke R, Li R, Shui G, Yong VW, Chen WJ, Lin X.
papers.abstract: Importance Leukoencephalopathies are clinically and etiologically heterogeneous disorders, and establishing a specific diagnosis remains challenging. Patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and brain white matter hyperintensities (WMH) may be misdiagnosed as having multiple sclerosis, potentially exposing them to unnecessary immunosuppressive therapy. Objective To define the clinical, radiological, and genetic features of spinal predominant demyelinating leukodystrophy with leg spasticity (SPDMLS). Design, setting, and participants This case series involved participants from 4 tertiary referral hospitals within the China Alliance for Rare Diseases during the period July 2019 to August 2025. The study design integrated clinical evaluations and whole-exome sequencing (WES), as well as targeted plasma lipidomics correlated with SPATAX-EUROSPA disability stages. Variant pathogenicity was evaluated using an oligodendrocyte-specific knock-in mouse model. Participants were patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and central nervous system (CNS) WMH and available family members, including presymptomatic carriers. Exposures WES, genetic characterization, testing. Main outcomes and measures Identification of disease-associated gene and characterization of clinical, radiological, and genetic features of SPDMLS. Results Twenty-six individuals from 11 unrelated families were included; 4 patients underwent longitudinal follow-up for up to 5 years. Recurrent heterozygous PLAAT4 (phospholipase A and acyltransferase 4) variants (p.I14T and p.A96V) were associated with a novel autosomal dominant leukoencephalopathy, named SPDMLS. Age at onset was 11 to 51 years (median [IQR], 22 [15-29] years), with patients predominantly developing spastic paraplegia. Symbol Digit Modalities Test scores ranged from 11 to 70 in 6 available patients. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated slow progression with heterogeneous brain WMH and a stereotyped pattern of symmetric, long-segment "girdle-like" spinal cord WMH accompanied by atrophy. Somatosensory- and motor-evoked potentials indicated dysfunction of the dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts, respectively. In presymptomatic carriers, spinal cord signal alterations preceded brain involvement. An oligodendrocyte-specific knock-in mouse model provided in vivo functional evidence supporting a role of PLAAT4 gain-of-function in driving demyelination, informing SPDMLS pathogenesis. Patient plasma lipidomics suggested accumulation of arachidonic acid-related lipids correlating with disability stage. Conclusions and relevance This study found that PLAAT4 variants delineated SPDMLS, a clinically distinct leukodystrophy that should be considered in patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and CNS WMH. Arachidonic acid-related lipids represent a candidate biomarker for disease progression.

papers.title: Histological morphometric correlates of MRI-defined cortical thinning in temporal lobe epilepsy
papers.authors: Bartkiewicz J, Xiao F, Lim YM, Ryniejska M, El Hachami H, Mrzyglod A, Liu J, Miserocchi A, McEnvoy AW, Duncan JS, Koepp M, Thom M.
papers.abstract: Large-scale MRI studies have consistently demonstrated progressive and age-accelerated neocortical thinning in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE). These findings are frequently interpreted as evidence of cumulative neurodegeneration. However, the histopathological substrates underlying MRI-confirmed cortical thinning in epilepsy remain poorly defined. In particular, it is unknown whether cortical thinning reflects irreversible neuronal loss or potentially reversible epilepsy-related network alterations in cortical microstructure. We analysed the resected middle temporal gyrus from 117 individuals undergoing surgery for temporal lobe epilepsy, including cases with (n= 74) or without hippocampal sclerosis (HS) and 12 cases with additional temporal lobe sclerosis (TLS, or Focal Cortical Dysplasia IIIa), defined by a distinct pattern of cytoarchitectural reorganisation and gliosis involving superficial layers. All cases were stratified by the presence or absence of pre-operative MRI-defined cortical thinning of the middle temporal gyrus, quantified using CAT12 relative to healthy controls. On NeuN-immuno-labelled sections using automated image analysis we assessed neuronal spatial distributions relative to their size and packing density; relative cortical layer thickness and sulcal-gyral cytoarchitectural variation were also quantified. MRI-defined cortical thinning was not associated with diffuse neuronal loss. Instead, thinning correlated with increased neuronal density and altered cell-size spatial organisation in superficial and deep layers, particularly in right temporal lobe epilepsy cases with HS. There was limited evidence of layer-specific laminar thinning, being confined to layer VI in the right TLE/HS group only. Of note, TLS cases did not show either cortical thinning on MRI or laminar thinning on histology compared to cases without TLS but altered neuronal densities and composition that was not confined to the superficial cortex. MRI cortical thinning was also characterised by attenuation of normal sulcal/gyral cytoarchitectural variations suggesting disruption of cortical architectural gradients. In contrast, cases with HS but without MRI cortical thinning demonstrated loss of the expected inter-hemispheric cytoarchitectural asymmetry, indicating a distinct pathological process dissociated from thinning. Clinical-pathological correlations were lateralised, including age of onset, further supporting distinct mechanisms contributing to MRI cortical thinning between left and right TLE. These findings challenge the prevailing assumption that MRI-defined cortical thinning in epilepsy reflects progressive neuronal degeneration. Rather than laminar neuronal loss and atrophy, thinning was associated with altered neuronal packing and cell-size distributions between layers. This points towards altered neuropil volumes, including myelin content and dendritic remodelling, in turn suggesting potentially reversible dynamic seizure- or network-related processes.

papers.title: Cellular and mitochondrial correlates of regional glucose metabolism in the human cortex
papers.authors: Murgaš M, Habernig S, Milz C, Graf S, Reed MB, Eggerstorfer B, Falb P, Schmidt C, Briem E, Schlosser G, Mayerweg A, Al Barede K, Pörnbacher I, Nics L, Rasul S, Hacker M, Rujescu D, Hahn A, Lanzenberger R.
papers.abstract: Regional differences in human brain glucose metabolism reflect local energy demands, but their cellular and mitochondrial determinants remain unclear. We combined [ 18 F]FDG positron emission tomography in healthy human participants with estimates of cellular composition and mitochondrial density to unravel (sub)cellular correlates of heterogeneity in brain glucose metabolism. By correcting for RNA content and differential gene expression due to postmortem sampling, we addressed methodological shortcomings in multimodal neuroimaging integration. We introduce transcriptionally derived cytoarchitectonic maps of the human cortex that are consistent with histological findings, providing a biologically grounded framework for relating in vivo neuroimaging signals. Accordingly, mitochondrial distribution showed strong association with the intrinsic energy requirements at resting state. In contrast, relations between metabolism and neuronal composition were driven by sensory input and mitochondria-sparse thin-axon neurons, suggesting that stimulation-induced energy demand is met rather by neuronal processes that are independent of mitochondrial abundance to maintain efficient information processing.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注人脑皮层葡萄糖代谢区域差异的细胞与线粒体基础，将健康参与者的[18F]FDG正电子发射断层扫描与细胞组成和线粒体密度的估计相结合，并校正RNA含量及死后采样导致的基因表达差异。作者据此构建了与组织学发现一致的皮层细胞构筑图谱，发现线粒体分布与静息状态下的内在能量需求密切相关；而代谢与神经元组成的关系则受感觉输入和线粒体稀疏的薄轴突神经元驱动，提示刺激诱发的能量需求可能更多由不依赖线粒体丰度的神经元过程来满足，以维持高效的信息处理。这些结果强调了细胞和线粒体特征在解释脑代谢异质性中的作用。

papers.title: Brain synchrony between interacting sibling pairs during real-time cooperation: an fMRI hyperscanning study
papers.authors: Hernandez-Pena L, Taebi A, Koch J, Mathiak K, Wagels L.
papers.abstract: Siblings typically represent the longest-lasting social relationships. Second-person neuroscience provides a framework for studying the neural mechanisms of real-time, reciprocal social interactions. Yet, most studies have focused on simplified coordination tasks, limited brain regions, and did not investigate neural dynamics between siblings. In the first study investigating brain synchrony between siblings to date, we used fMRI hyperscanning to simultaneously record brain activity in 50 same-sex healthy young adult sibling pairs while they played a complex collaborative problem-solving Tetris game requiring continuous non-verbal complementary coordination. Brain synchrony was quantified using inter-subject correlation across 36 regions of interest (ROIs) of the social brain atlas. The interacting sibling pairs showed significantly higher brain synchrony than randomly permuted non-sibling pairs in 19 ROIs (FDR-corrected p < .05). These regions were primarily located within the higher-level theory of mind subnetwork (including bilateral temporo-parietal junction, precuneus and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex), and intermediate-level subnetwork (including anterior insula, inferior frontal gyrus). Greater synchrony in the left temporo-parietal junction significantly predicted better cooperative performance, suggesting that shared neural modelling of a partner's intentions supports effective collaboration. Synchrony in frontal and temporal regions was weakly modulated by cooperative and competitive sibling relationship characteristics; however, these effects did not survive correction for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously (uncorr. p < .05). This study provides first evidence that real-time cooperation between siblings is supported by inter-brain synchrony in core social brain networks. We highlight the value of ecologically valid hyperscanning approaches for investigating neural mechanisms of cooperation in long-term relationships, advancing the field of relational neuroscience.

papers.title: Sex-Related Differences in Regional Homogeneity and Intolerance of Uncertainty in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Resting-State fMRI Study.
papers.authors: Wang A, Zhao S, Guo Q, Wu J, Fang W, Zheng S, Zhu C, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Background Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) is a cognitive vulnerability associated with symptom severity in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Evidence also suggests that IU and OCD symptom profiles may differ by sex; however, the neural correlates of IU in male and female patients with OCD remain insufficiently characterized. Methods In this cross-sectional observational study, 63 patients with OCD and 40 healthy controls (HCs) underwent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Regional homogeneity (ReHo) was used to examine diagnosis- and sex-related differences in intrinsic brain activity. Imaging data were analyzed using a full-factorial model in SPM, with diagnosis and sex as factors and age, years of education, and mean framewise displacement (FD) as covariates. Statistical significance was defined using a voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 followed by cluster-level family-wise error (FWE) correction at p < 0.05. Significant effects were characterized using post hoc contrasts. Four exploratory partial correlations controlling for age, years of education, and mean FD were examined; their p values were not corrected for multiple comparisons. Results The final sample comprised 63 patients with OCD (37 males and 26 females) and 40 HCs (25 males and 15 females). Patients with OCD showed lower ReHo in visual processing regions, including the right calcarine cortex and right middle occipital gyrus, compared with HCs. Across diagnostic groups, the whole-brain factorial analysis revealed a significant main effect of sex, with males showing higher ReHo in visual and sensorimotor regions and females showing higher ReHo in prefrontal regions. No significant diagnosis-by-sex interaction was observed. Exploratory partial correlations showed that higher IU was associated with lower ReHo in the left inferior frontal gyrus in the female OCD, and that lower ReHo in the right middle occipital gyrus was associated with greater obsession severity in the overall OCD sample. These uncorrected associations are preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Conclusions These findings suggest potential sex-related differences in regional neural synchrony in OCD and identify an exploratory association between IU and left inferior frontal gyrus ReHo within the female OCD subgroup. Given the cross-sectional observational design, these findings should be interpreted as associative and hypothesis-generating rather than as evidence of distinct sex-specific neural mechanisms.

papers.title: Association of CT-Derived Skeletal Muscle Radiodensity and Index With Cerebral Small Vessel Disease: A Community-Based Study.
papers.authors: Yuan Y, Cai X, Wang L, Yang Y, Ren L, Wang M, Zhang D, Pan Y, Wang Y.
