papers.abstract: Aims Skeletal muscle composition is linked to metabolic health, but its association with cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) remains unclear. We examined associations of CT-derived skeletal muscle radiodensity (SMD) and skeletal muscle index (SMI) with CSVD. Materials and methods This cross-sectional analysis included 2395 adults from the PRECISE study. SMD and SMI were measured on abdominal CT at L3. CSVD was assessed using Wardlaw and Rothwell scores. Individual MRI markers included lacunes, white matter hyperintensities, basal ganglia enlarged perivascular spaces (BG-EPVS) and cerebral microbleeds (CMBs). Logistic and ordinal logistic regression models were used, with additional covariate adjustment examined in sensitivity analyses. False discovery rate correction was applied to marker-specific analyses. Results The mean age was 60.9 ± 6.6 years (56.8% women). In primary multivariable analyses, each 1-SD decrement in SMD was associated with CSVD presence (Wardlaw: OR: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.03-1.31; Rothwell: OR: 1.12, 95% CI: 1.00-1.25) and burden (total: cOR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.06-1.33; modified total: cOR: 1.14, 95% CI: 1.03-1.27). With broader covariate adjustment, most of these associations were attenuated, with only Wardlaw total burden remaining statistically significant. The SMD-BG-EPVS association was similarly attenuated. Lower SMI was associated with CMB presence and burden, whereas no consistent association with overall CSVD was observed across models. Conclusions Lower SMD was associated with overall CSVD in primary analyses, but most associations were attenuated after broader adjustment. Lower SMI was consistently associated with CMBs, whereas its association with overall CSVD was less consistent across models.

papers.title: Psychometric validation of a clinician-reported clinical severity assessment in STXBP1-related disorder.
papers.authors: Abbott M, Jacoby P, Angione K, Benke TA, Downs J, Miele A, Stringfellow M, Helbig I, Demarest S, STARR Working Group.
papers.abstract: Aim To adapt a validated clinician-reported measure from CDKL5 deficiency disorder for use in STXBP1-related disorders and evaluate the psychometric properties of the resulting STXBP1 Clinical Severity Assessment (S-CSA). Method In this multicenter, prospective, natural history study, the S-CSA was adapted from the CDKL5 Clinical Severity Assessment through expert consensus sessions with STXBP1 clinicians. Revisions addressed gaps in the motor and vision domains, adding tremor and vision items. The measure was administered to 123 individuals with STXBP1-related disorders (50% males, median age 7 years 8 months). Psychometric evaluation included confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency, composite reliability, average variance extracted, and distinctiveness, compared with recommended thresholds. Results Analyses supported a three-domain structure (motor, communication, vision) with factor loadings greater than 0.5 and strong internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha >0.7; composite reliability >0.88). Model fit and variance metrics met the recommended standards, and domains demonstrated distinctiveness. No ceiling or floor effects were observed. Minimal skew was seen in the motor (0.34) and communication (-0.16) domains; positive skew in vision (2.2) was observed, identifying patients with and without cortical visual impairment. Interpretation The S-CSA demonstrates strong validity and reliability in STXBP1-related disorders and may show utility in clinical trials for STXBP1-related disorders and potentially other severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

papers.title: HINT1 in ventral hippocampal GABAergic neurons mediates depressive-like behaviors.
papers.authors: Li SF, Liu DY, Zhang H, Wen RC, Hu HL, Xv JM, Cheng D, Dang YH.
papers.abstract: Depression is a complex psychiatric disorder with multifaceted etiologies, and its underlying molecular mechanisms are incompletely elucidated. Although histidine trimeric nucleotide-binding protein 1 (HINT1) has been implicated in major depressive disorders (MDD), its precise role and regulatory mechanism remain unclear. This study investigated the role of HINT1 in depression-associated phenotypes. In mice subjected to chronic social defeat stress (CSDS), stress-susceptible individuals exhibited significant upregulation of HINT1 in the hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex. Targeted overexpression of HINT1 in ventral hippocampus (vHip) demonstrated that HINT1 directly induced depressive-like behaviors, whereas its knockdown exerted a robust antidepressant-like effect. Pharmacological inhibition of HINT1 with the selective inhibitor Tryptamine guanosine carbamate (TpGc) in vHip also reversed behavioral deficits and normalized neuronal activity in the CSDS-exposed mice. Cell-type-specific analyses demonstrated that HINT1 overexpression in vHip GABAergic neurons, including somatostatin-positive (SST+ ) and parvalbumin-positive (PV+ ) subtypes, exacerbated depressive-like phenotypes and disrupted neuronal activity. Proteomics analysis identified that HINT1 overexpression in the vHip significantly upregulated the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) E3 ligases chromobox 4 (CBX4). Further overexpression of CBX4 in the GABAergic neurons of vHip induced depressive-like behaviors. Mechanistically, HINT1 interacted with and inhibited the phosphorylation of protein kinase C-β1 (PKCβ1), suppressing its downstream MEK1/2-ERK1/2 signaling and thereby increasing CBX4 levels. CBX4 promoted the SUMOylation of the glutamate N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor subunit 2 A (GluN2A) and affected its phosphorylation and trafficking. These findings demonstrated HINT1 as a key regulator of GABAergic signaling in vHip and highlighted its therapeutic potential for depression.

papers.title: Resting-state functional brain changes in temporal lobe epilepsy with comorbid depression: A meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Fu J, Zhou X, Wei L, Kong Z, Cai L.
papers.abstract: Objective To compare the differences in functional brain activity between patients with temporal lobe epilepsy comorbid with depressive disorder (TLE-D) and those with temporal lobe epilepsy without depressive disorder (TLE-ND) via a meta‑analysis of resting‑state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) studies, and to explore the functional brain activity features associated with depressive symptoms. Methods Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Data from database inception to September 2026 to identify cross-sectional studies comparing rs-fMRI-derived differences in functional brain activity between patients with temporal lobe epilepsy comorbid with depressive disorder (TLE-D) and those without depressive disorder (TLE-ND). Eligible rs-fMRI metrics included regional brain activity indices and functional connectivity indices. A meta-analysis of studies reporting regional brain activity indices was performed using anisotropic effect-size signed differential mapping (AES-SDM). Due to their limited number, studies reporting functional connectivity indices were only described narratively. Study selection and data extraction were then completed, and a voxel-based meta-analysis of the included studies was performed with AES-SDM. Results A total of six studies yielding nine datasets met the inclusion criteria, involving 100 patients with TLE-D and 108 patients with TLE-ND. Meta-analysis showed that, compared with the TLE-ND group, the TLE-D group had significantly increased spontaneous brain activity in the right precuneus, right angular gyrus, right superior frontal gyrus, left middle frontal gyrus, and left cerebellum (analyzed via AES-SDM with an initial exploratory threshold of uncorrected voxel-level P < 0.005 and cluster size ≥10 voxels, and validated by leave-one-out sensitivity analysis). No brain regions with significantly decreased spontaneous brain activity were detected. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest that, compared with patients with TLE-ND, patients with TLE-D show distinct patterns of functional brain activity in multiple key nodes of the default mode network, including the precuneus and angular gyrus, as well as in prefrontal-related regions. These differences may provide preliminary neuroimaging evidence for understanding the neural mechanisms underlying depressive symptoms associated with temporal lobe epilepsy.

papers.title: Mechanisms and therapeutic strategies for central and peripheral remyelination.
papers.authors: Zhan J, Jo J, Cristobal CD, Jeong DJ, Park HT, Lee HK.
papers.abstract: Myelin sheaths are produced by myelinating glia and provide metabolic support to neuronal axons while accelerating electrical signal conduction. Myelinating glia, which include oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system (CNS) and Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system (PNS), have distinct developmental origins and biological characteristics that profoundly influence their capacity for myelin regeneration following demyelinating insults. In various demyelinating diseases, loss of myelin and myelinating glia resulting from autoimmune disorders, inflammation, or genetic defects causes neurological dysfunction. Beyond removing disease-causing factors, inducing and accelerating remyelination represents a critical therapeutic goal for demyelinating diseases. In this review, we first summarize and compare molecular mechanisms underlying CNS and PNS remyelination, including extracellular signaling pathways, transcriptional regulation, and intercellular communication. We then highlight current treatments and ongoing clinical trials for common demyelination disorders, including neonatal white matter injury, multiple sclerosis, and inherited peripheral neuropathies.

papers.title: Global synchrony moderates sad mood and is associated with emotional Stroop interference and somatic symptoms.
papers.authors: Mabel-Kenzie STST, Wong NML, Lee TMC.
papers.abstract: Mood-congruent attention in depression has been studied via emotional interference tasks, including tasks comparing responses to sad and happy stimuli. Mood induction offers a way to experimentally induce sad mood in non-clinical samples and examine its association with subsequent emotional interference, including Sad-Happy interference. Previous studies have separately linked resting-state global neural dynamics (synchrony, metastability) to depressive symptoms and attentional processing. However, whether individual differences in baseline global synchrony and metastability relate to how individuals respond to sad mood remains largely unclear. This study therefore examined the relationship between neural dynamics, sadder mood after induction, and Sad-Happy interference. Depressive symptoms also encompass somatic domains alongside cognitive-affective domains, though these are rarely distinguished in neuroimaging studies. We further examined whether baseline neural dynamics and their association with sadder mood and Sad-Happy interference were related to depressive symptoms (total, cognitive-affective, and somatic). Forty-six non-clinical individuals completed resting-state neuroimaging, mood induction (sad or non-sad), and an emotional Stroop task. We found in a cross-sectional moderated mediation model that sadder mood after induction was associated with greater interference from sad compared to happy stimuli at medium and high levels of global synchrony, particularly in exploratory path models that included somatic symptoms. Findings suggest that individual differences in resting-state global synchrony may be a neural correlate of sadder mood after induction and Sad-Happy interference in non-clinical individuals. This study offers preliminary associations linking neural dynamics, sad mood, emotional interference, and somatic symptoms, providing insights into the role of neural dynamics in emotional and attentional processing.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation attenuates post-stroke dysphagia by modulating microglial polarization via the endothelial VWF/PI3K-Akt axis.
papers.authors: Yu F, Feng Y, Miao Y, Xu G.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke dysphagia is a common complication with limited treatment options. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (ta-VNS) has shown neuroprotective effects. This study investigated whether ta-VNS improves swallowing function and alleviates neuroinflammation by modulating microglial M1/M2 polarization, examining the role of von Willebrand factor (VWF) in endothelial-microglial crosstalk. A rat model of transient bilateral middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was established. Rats received ta-VNS for 3 weeks, and swallowing function, neurological deficits, and inflammatory markers were assessed. Microglial M1 (CD16) and M2 (CD206) polarization in the white matter was examined by immunofluorescence. RNA-seq was used to identify candidate genes. In vitro, an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model was applied to hCMEC/D3 endothelial cells co-cultured with HMC3 microglia, and VWF was knocked down using shRNA to evaluate its effect on microglial polarization and inflammation. ta-VNS significantly improved body weight, food/water intake, and swallowing function (reduced latency and increased swallowing frequency) in transient middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. ta-VNS reduced levels of TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, and IL-10, attenuated microglial activation, suppressed M1 (Iba-1+ CD16+ ) microglia, and enhanced M2 (Iba-1+ CD206+ ) polarization in rat whiter matter. RNA-seq revealed downregulation of VWF after ta-VNS, with enrichment in the PI3K-Akt pathway. In vitro, OGD/R upregulated VWF, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, endothelial apoptosis, and permeability. Knockdown of VWF in endothelial cells shifted co-cultured microglia from M1 toward M2 phenotype and reduced TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β while increasing IL-10. ta-VNS can improve post-stroke dysphagia and reduce neuroinflammation by promoting M2 microglial polarization. Endothelial VWF may be a key downstream mediator of this process.

papers.title: Delayed cerebral myelination in a patient with isodicentric chromosome 18 [psu idic(18)(q21.2)] mosaicism: a case report.
papers.authors: Inoue S, Matsumoto H, Takane T, Mitani S, Moriya K, Ohashi H, Imai K.
papers.abstract: Introduction Isodicentric chromosome 18 is a rare structural chromosomal abnormality, with few reported cases. When the breakpoint occurs on 18q, the phenotype may overlap with 18p trisomy, proximal 18q trisomy, 18q deletion syndrome, and Pitt-Hopkins syndrome. Nonmosaic isodicentric chromosome 18 (idic18) causes a severe and often lethal phenotype; therefore, most surviving patients are mosaic. However, mosaic idic18 with an 18q breakpoint is rare, and its neuroimaging features remain poorly characterized. Case presentation A 10-month-old girl was referred for developmental delay and esotropia. She had achieved head control at 3 months but could not sit or crawl. She also had microcephaly and right esotropia. Brain MRI at 12 months of age showed delayed myelination of the anterior limb of the internal capsule and the cerebral white matter on T2-weighted images. G-banding revealed mosaicism: 46,XX,psu idic(18)(q21.2)[5]/46,XX[25], and chromosomal microarray demonstrated duplication of 18p11.32q21.2 and deletion of 18q21.2q23 (mosaic level 26-30%), confirming mosaic idic18 with a 18q21.2 breakpoint. She achieved independent walking at 2 years and 2 months, but the Kinder Infant Development Scale at 2 years and 5 months showed a developmental quotient of 48. Conclusion Mosaic idic18(q21.2) is a rare disorder that may present with delays in motor and language development without obvious dysmorphic features. T2 hyperintensity in cerebral white matter on brain MRI, which overlaps with findings seen in 18q deletion syndrome, may aid diagnosis. The phenotype appears to be influenced by the breakpoint location and degree of mosaicism.

papers.title: The macrophage as a neuroimmune sensor and effector: neural control of inflammation across tissues and disease.
papers.authors: da Cruz RS, Lopes LS, Pachiega ANS, Colombari DSA, Colombari E, Zoccal DB, Katayama PL.
papers.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
papers.abstract: Background Once viewed mainly as scavengers of innate immunity, macrophages are now recognized as constitutive partners of the nervous system. In neural tissue their identity is instructed by neurons and glia, and in turn they shape neural function - pruning synapses, tuning neuronal excitability, and executing the autonomic commands that restrain inflammation. Purpose Here we advance a mechanistic model built on three principles: that neural and glial signals specify macrophage identity on a shared myeloid template; that the macrophage is a bidirectional sensor-effector node within autonomic reflex arcs, both relaying neural output and generating the cytokine signals that afferent nerves detect; and that this sensor-effector arc is modular, recurring across brain, spleen, gut, heart, and adipose tissue. We give particular attention to the afferent limb of the inflammatory reflex, which now extends beyond the vagus to nociceptors and to the carotid body, an arterial chemoreceptor that senses circulating inflammatory signals and recruits a sympathetic anti-inflammatory pathway, and to the stress-responsive circuitry through which sympathetic outflow drives myelopoiesis, neuroinflammation, and sickness behavior. We then turn to disease, in which macrophage function is altered by a diseased or aged niche in neurodegeneration, chronic pain, gut-brain disorders, and metabolic disease. Conclusions Whether the neuroimmune circuits described here are themselves disrupted in these conditions, rather than merely coexisting with them, is largely untested, and we outline what such evidence would require. We close by arguing that tuning these circuits, rather than broadly suppressing macrophage activity, is the more plausible therapeutic goal.

papers.title: Laser-Structured Nickel Electrodes for Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution Kinetics in Alkaline Media at Elevated Temperature.
papers.authors: Barrientos MS, Zschach LG, Baumann R, Lasagni AF.
papers.abstract: Tailoring the surface morphology of electrocatalysts is one potential opportunity for improving the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in alkaline media. Direct laser interference patterning (DLIP) emerged as a promising surface engineering technique for enhancing the HER performance of nickel electrocatalysts in alkaline media. In this study, DLIP is employed to fabricate periodic line-like microstructures on Ni electrodes using a picosecond-pulsed laser system (λ = 1064 nm, τ = 70 ps). By varying cumulated laser fluence up to 2.4 kJ cm-2 , a maximum structure depth of 2.35 ± 0.04 μm and interfacial area ratio up to 87% is reached. HER is evaluated by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) at 22 and 60 °C. The DLIP-structured electrodes exhibit significantly enhanced HER activity compared with untreated Ni, showing overpotential reductions of up to 28% at 22 °C and 53% at 60 °C, in conjunction with an increase in electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) from 2.24 to 31.04 cm2 at 22 °C and from 1.95 to 74.84 cm2 at 60 °C, respectively. These findings highlight the favorable interplay between DLIP-induced surface modification and thermally enhanced HER kinetics.

papers.title: The b-Value Dependence for Higher-Degree Spherical Harmonic Powers of the Diffusion MRI Signal Follows Stick Model Predictions in White Matter.
papers.authors: Moss HG, Jensen JH, Benitez A.
papers.abstract: Purpose To compare the dependence on b-value of the spherical harmonic powers for the diffusion MRI signal in white matter to theoretical predictions from the stick model of water diffusion within axons. Methods Diffusion MRI data were acquired at 3 T in three healthy adults with 10 b-value shells (b = 1000-10 000 s/mm2 ) and 64 directions per shell. For every b-value, the signal was expanded in spherical harmonics for all even degrees l up to l = 6, and the harmonic power for each degree was calculated. These were compared in selected white matter regions of interest to the theoretical predictions of the stick model, which depend on just two adjustable parameters: the intra-axonal diffusivity and an amplitude factor for each degree. The intra-axonal diffusivity was estimated independently using triple diffusion encoding MRI, leaving the amplitude factor as the sole fitting parameter. Results Close agreement between experiment and theory was found for b ≳ 4000 s/mm2 , the threshold where extra-axonal water signal is expected to be strongly suppressed, for total cerebral white matter as well as separately within the genu, body, and splenium of the corpus callosum. These findings extend prior studies that either considered only the l = 0 harmonic power or treated the intra-axonal diffusivity as a fitting parameter. Conclusion In white matter, the b-value dependence of the diffusion MRI signal's even degree spherical harmonic powers up to l = 6 are relatively well-described by the stick model of axons for b ≳ 4000 s/mm2 .

papers.title: Fabrication Strategies and Performance Optimization Strategies of Flexible Brain-Computer Interface Electrodes.
papers.authors: Sun M, Ma X, Wang X, Bai B, Wang J, Wang H, Wang Y, Huang L, Tang J.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) provides a direct communication pathway between the brain and external devices and has been applied in neurological disease treatment, motor rehabilitation, and human-computer interaction. Electrodes play essential roles in recording and modulating neural signals, and their performance directly affects signal quality, spatial resolution, and long-term stability. Traditional rigid electrodes suffer from mechanical mismatch with brain tissue, which may induce tissue damage and reduce recording stability during long-term implantation. Flexible electrodes offer improved mechanical compatibility and have emerged as promising alternatives. Recent advances in materials science, micro/nanofabrication, and interface engineering have enhanced the electrical, mechanical, and biological performance of flexible BCI electrodes. This review summarizes neural signal characteristics, electrode requirements, fabrication strategies, and performance optimization approaches. The major fabrication methods include microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), printing and transfer, laser processing and thermal drawing, and electrospinning, while deposition and surface modification are discussed as functional enhancement strategies. The review also highlights challenges associated with large-scale manufacturing, long-term stability, and the physical and clinical limitations of invasive, semi-invasive, and noninvasive electrodes. Future directions involving intelligent, wireless, and self-powered systems, together with clinical translation, are discussed to promote the development of flexible electrodes for BCI applications.

papers.title: Limb-localized induction of regeneration reshapes brain and amputation-site transcriptional states in adult Xenopus laevis
papers.authors: Russell SJ, Miller KA, Kaplan DL, Levin M, Murugan NJ.
papers.abstract: Limb regeneration requires coordinated tissue reconstruction and nervous system reintegration, yet whether regenerative induction alters brain responses to limb loss remains unclear. We analyzed transcriptomics from the paired brains and amputation sites of adult Xenopus laevis after hindlimb amputation with or without a 24-hour exposure to localized, pro-regenerative multi-drug treatment (MDT) delivered through a wearable bioreactor device. At 24 hours post treatment (24 HPT), MDT brains showed increased vascular and basement membrane transcripts and enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation and mTORC1 programs. In the limb, an exploratory integrated stress response (ISR) score increased at 11 and 24 HPT and returned to control levels by 7 days post treatment (7 DPT), coinciding with induction of growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15), a cytokine responsive to mitochondrial stress. No corresponding increase in brain ISR score was detected. At 7 DPT, MDT brains showed enrichment of immune, heme metabolism and biosynthetic programs, reduced synaptic transmission gene expression and increased gdf15.L . Relative to an external uninjured reference, MDT and amputation-only brains showed concordant changes, with treatment modifying selected programs. Cross-species comparative analyses identified partial overlap with an axolotl regenerative glutamatergic signature and separation from selected mammalian injury profiles. These findings reveal cross-tissue responses to regenerative induction, identifying candidate mechanisms of brain–body communication in biomedically engineered vertebrate limb regeneration.

papers.title: Overlapping yet distinct spatiomolecular profiles across mood disorders and biological sex in the human prefrontal cortex
papers.authors: Thompson JR, Oh S, Maguire SE, Bach SV, Mulvey BJ, Pertea G, Abramson MR, Miller RA, Kwon SH, Tippani M, Valentine MR, Deep-Soboslay A, Du Y, Nguyen AB, Kleinman JE, Maynard KR, Hyde TM, Han S, Collado-Torres L, Martinowich K, Hicks SC, Page SC.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) exhibit both overlapping and distinct clinical features, including sex differences in prevalence and symptomatology, but how these similarities and differences are reflected at the molecular and cellular level in the human brain remains poorly understood. Here, we applied spatial transcriptomics to the human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex from individuals with MDD, BD, and neurotypical controls to resolve molecular programs associated with diagnosis and biological sex. Our analysis revealed sex- and diagnosis-specific differences across white matter, the neurovascular unit (NVU), and neuronal compartments. Within white matter, we identified female-specific survival-response programs shared in both MDD and BD, and divergent myelin-related gene expression patterns across disorders ( CLDN11 , CNDP1 ). Within the NVU, transcriptional evidence of impaired vascular integrity was accompanied by astrocytic response profiles in females with MDD and males with BD, with inflammatory responses further evident in females with MDD ( IFITM3 , CEBPD , IL1R1 ). In donors with BD of both sexes and in females with MDD, inhibitory neurons exhibited impaired neuropeptide expression ( SST , CORT , CRH ). Integration with donor genotype information highlighted that genetic risk for mood disorders influences MAPK3 expression, implicating altered ERK signaling, which was further supported by disorder-associated changes in Ras/MEK/ERK pathway components in neurons ( MAPK3, DUSP6 , RASD1 , ELK1 ). Together, these findings reveal coordinated, cell type- and spatial domain-specific molecular programs that distinguish shared and disorder-specific transcriptomic changes across mood disorders in a sex-dependent manner.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注重性抑郁障碍与双相障碍在人脑前额叶皮层中既有重叠又有区别的分子特征，以及这些特征如何随生物学性别而变化。作者对患者和神经典型对照的背外侧前额叶皮层开展空间转录组分析，发现白质、神经血管单元和神经元等区域存在诊断与性别特异的转录差异，例如两种障碍共享的女性特异性生存反应程序、不同的髓鞘相关基因表达，以及女性抑郁障碍和男性双相障碍中血管完整性受损与星形胶质细胞反应的伴随出现。抑制性神经元的神经肽表达在部分患者中受损，遗传风险则与MAPK3表达及ERK信号改变相关。这些结果提示，情绪障碍的共享与特异转录变化以细胞类型、空间区域和性别依赖的方式组织，但相关发现仍需进一步验证。

papers.title: A polysynaptic hypothalamus–pelvic ganglion circuit regulates prostate tumor growth via WNT3A
papers.authors: Ran W, Wu P, Qiao Z, Wang S, Yang Q, Yan R, Yan Z, Zhang J, He B, Shao Y, Wang Y, Chu S, Wang Y, Wang H.
papers.abstract: Brain – tumor communication is increasingly recognized. Peripheral autonomic nerves regulate prostate cancer progression, yet how the brain influences local nerve–tumor interactions remains unclear. We identify a polysynaptic circuit linking the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN), dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus (DMV), major pelvic ganglion (MPG) and prostate tumor in mice. Although both nuclei were activated during tumor growth, PVN activity restrained, whereas DMV activity promoted tumor growth. MPG ablation abolished DMV-induced tumor promotion. Combining LMD with Smart-seq2 revealed transcriptional remodeling and increased Wnt3a expression in tumor-innervating, activated MPG neurons under upstream neural control. MPG explants released WNT3A, whose neutralization suppressed explant-induced cancer-cell proliferation. Together, our findings identify a polysynaptic PVN–DMV–MPG circuit that regulates prostate tumor growth and implicate WNT3A as a mediator of the pro-tumor effects of the MPG, highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting the neural circuit and downstream molecular pathway.

papers.title: CDKL5 deficiency alters cell subtype-specific molecular programmes and intercellular signalling in the mouse hippocampus
papers.authors: Villegas-Salmerón J, Egan S, Sanfeliu A, Higgins J, Heiland M, El-Mansoury B, Connolly NM, Henshall DC, Mamad O.
papers.abstract: CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD) is a severe neurodevelopmental condition characterised by epilepsy, intellectual disability, and motor dysfunction. Loss of CDKL5 leads to altered synapse development, excitatory-inhibitory imbalances and glial changes, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood, particularly at the level of individual brain cell subtypes. Here, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on the hippocampus of 12 weeks old heterozygous female Cdkl5 exon 6 deletion ( Cdkl5 tm1.1Joez/J ) and wild-type mice to characterise cell-subtype-specific transcriptional alterations associated with CDKL5 deficiency. Analysis of 11,791 high-quality nuclei revealed cell-subtype-specific transcriptional changes across neuronal and non-neuronal populations. Differential expression was most prominent in intratelencephalic and extratelencephalic (IT–ET) glutamatergic neurons, which showed altered expression of genes involved in neuronal signalling and activity-dependent transcription, and in dentate gyrus (DG) neurons, which exhibited coordinated upregulation of multiple ribosomal protein genes. Gene set enrichment analysis revealed broader molecular alterations, with neuronal populations showing recurrent changes in pathways associated with synaptic organisation, neuronal development, axonal and dendritic processes, and neurotransmission. Altered gene expression was also evident among non-neuronal populations, although these displayed fewer changes. CellChat analysis inferred changes in predicted intercellular communication across excitatory and inhibitory neuronal populations, particularly Sema3c signalling, suggesting reorganization of hippocampal neuronal subtypes. These findings provide a single-nucleus transcriptional atlas of the hippocampus in a CDD mouse model. In our dataset, CDKL5 deficiency was associated with cell-subtype-specific alterations in gene expression, including enrichment of gene pathways related to cellular metabolism, neuronal development and synaptic organisation, alongside alteration in predicted intercellular signalling. This dataset provides a resource for investigating the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying CDD and for prioritising candidate pathways for future therapeutic investigation.

papers.title: Resting state fMRI detects pathological functional brain connectivity in the Ndufs4 knockout mouse model of Leigh syndrome during the pre-symptomatic stage of the disease
papers.authors: Guo CC, van de Wal M, el Bouazzati S, Overwater NM, Remie L, Koopman W, Grandjean J, Homberg JR.
papers.abstract: Leigh syndrome (LS) is a progressive encephalopathy and generally regarded as the most common inborn mitochondrial disease. Mutations in mitochondrial respiratory complex I are common in patients with LS and a mutational hotspot has been identified in the gene that encodes the NDUFS4 subunit of respiratory complex I. The Ndufs4 knockout mouse ( Ndufs4 KO) model of LS closely resembles the phenotypes of LS patients and show like the patient brain lesions when the symptoms are manifested. It is speculated but unproven that brain functional connectivity may precede the onset of symptoms. Therefore, the present study was set out to investigate the progression of brain functional connectives in Ndufs4 KO mice before and after the manifestation of LS-like symptoms using in vivo resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI). Since the brain lesions may be caused by increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the brain, we also examined the potential protective effect of KH176, a small molecular for modulating ROS levels, on brain functional connectivity. Rs-fMRI results showed that in Ndufs4 KO mice the functional connectivity of the piriform cortex, motor cortex, barrel cortex, visual cortex, auditory cortex, prefrontal cortex, lateral striatum, ventral striatum cortex and amygdala was increased, starting from the pre-symptomatic stage (middle stage) to the symptomatic stage (late stage) of the disease. KH176 had no effect on the changes in functional connectivity in the mice. In conclusion, these results show that there are abnormalities in functional connectivity in Ndufs4 KO mice during the pre-symptomatic phase of the disease and that KH176 treatment does not modify the connectivity changes.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究利用静息态功能磁共振成像，考察Ndufs4敲除小鼠在Leigh综合征样症状出现前后脑功能连接的演变，并检验调节活性氧水平的小分子KH176是否具有保护作用。结果显示，从症状前阶段到症状阶段，这些小鼠多个皮层、纹状体及杏仁核区域的功能连接升高，提示功能连接异常可在症状显现前出现；而KH176并未改变这些连接变化。作者据此认为，该模型在症状前期已存在病理性功能连接改变，但所观察的连接异常不受KH176干预影响。

papers.title: Early-Life Environmental Exposures and Brain Structure in Schizophrenia
papers.authors: Stano A, Quinones JF, Fischer DJ, Weber S, Klock L, Amaya I, Lorenz RC, Kühn S.
papers.abstract: Background Schizophrenia is widely considered a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by premorbid alterations in brain structure. Urban upbringing is a well-established environmental risk factor. However, urbanicity is often operationalised using broad population-based measures, leaving unclear which features of urban environments might affect the developing brain. This gap limits progress in understanding the pathways linking urban upbringing to schizophrenia, an increasingly important question as global urbanisation progresses. Cortical gyrification is especially informative in this context, as it is largely established before birth and remains relatively stable thereafter, offering a promising retrospective marker of early-life neurodevelopmental disturbances. Study Design In this case-control MRI study, we examined whether residential environmental exposures at birth were associated with adult brain structure in 51 individuals with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder and 88 healthy controls matched for age, sex and socioeconomic status. Birth addresses were linked to geospatial measures of air pollution, green space, built volume, built surface and population density. Study Results Higher air pollution at birth was associated with lower cortical gyrification in individuals with schizophrenia, but not in healthy controls, particularly in orbitofrontal and inferior frontal regions. No comparable associations were observed for grey matter volume, cortical thickness or surface area. Conclusions These findings suggest that air pollution at birth may be linked to hypogyria in schizophrenia and provide a potential bridge between epidemiological research on urbanicity and neurodevelopmental models of schizophrenia. In turn, this work provides a critical starting point for future work assessing how early urban environments become biologically embedded in schizophrenia risk.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注城市环境中的具体特征是否与精神分裂症患者成年期脑结构相关，采用病例对照MRI设计，将患者与健康对照者的出生住址与空气污染、绿地、建筑量和人口密度等地理空间指标关联。结果显示，出生时空气污染较高与患者皮层脑回化程度较低相关，尤其在眶额区和额下区，而健康对照中未见这种关联；灰质体积、皮层厚度和表面积则没有类似联系。作者据此提出，出生期空气污染可能与精神分裂症中的脑回化不足有关，为城市生活流行病学发现与神经发育模型之间提供了潜在连接，但强调这只是后续研究的起点，尚不能说明因果或临床意义。

papers.title: Age and sex impact resting-state EEG aperiodic activity beyond symptom associations in persistent post-concussive symptoms
papers.authors: Louras M, D’Archambeau G, Meys M, Martens G, Kaux J, Annen J, Thibaut A, Lejeune N.
papers.abstract: 1. Objective to investigate whether resting-state EEG aperiodic parameters (i.e., offset and exponent) are associated with symptom burden and demographic factors in patients with persistent post-concussive symptoms (PPCS) and differ from healthy controls. Methods In this cross-sectional observational study, resting-state eye-closed high-density EEG was recorded in patients with PPCS and in age-matched healthy controls. Aperiodic parameters were extracted from EEG power spectra. In patients, hierarchical multiple linear regression models included age and sex as a base model, with additional demographic and clinical symptoms entered separately. Patient-control differences were assessed using multiple linear regression adjusted for age and sex. Results Seventy patients with PPCS (54 female; 39.57±12.21 y.; 109.5 [76.5; 196] days post-concussion) recruited from a concussion care pathway and 38 healthy controls (17 female; 39.61±13.57 y.) were included. In patients, younger age and male sex were associated with higher offset and exponent values (all p ≤.014). None of the additional demographic and clinical variables improved model fit beyond age and sex (all p ≥.143). After adjustment for age and sex, neither offset ( p =.898) nor exponent ( p =.100) differed between patients and controls. Conclusion Resting-state aperiodic EEG parameters were consistently associated with age and sex, but not with self-reported symptom burden or clinical characteristics in patients with PPCS. Not accounting for these factors may generate apparent group differences attributable, at least in part, to demographic variability. Significance Age and sex are important sources of inter-individual variability in resting-state aperiodic EEG activity and should be systematically considered when investigating such features. Highlights Age and sex significantly impact resting-state EEG aperiodic activity. Aperiodic EEG parameters were not associated with symptom burden in persistent post-concussive symptoms. Aperiodic offset and exponent did not differ between patients with persistent post-concussive symptoms and healthy controls after adjustment for age and sex.
papers.summary_zh: 该横断面观察研究探讨持续性脑震荡后症状患者的静息态EEG非周期参数是否与症状负担及人口学因素相关，并与健康对照比较。研究采集患者与年龄匹配对照的闭眼高密度静息态EEG并提取非周期参数。结果发现，在患者中，较年轻和男性与更高的offset和exponent值相关，而其他人口学和临床变量均未在年龄和性别之外改善模型拟合；校正年龄和性别后，患者与对照在这两项参数上均无差异。这表明静息态非周期EEG活动主要与年龄和性别相关，而非与患者自报症状负担或临床特征相关，忽略这些因素可能产生部分源于人口学差异的表观组间差异。

papers.title: Understanding cognitive function in post-COVID-19 condition with fatigue: an interdisciplinary multimodal investigation
papers.authors: Birberg Thornberg U, Eklund A, Zeiler K, Morberg Jämterud S, León F, Özarslan E, Andersson A, Levi R, Engblom D, Divanoglou A, Blystad I.
papers.abstract: Lingering cognitive symptoms of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) continue to challenge our understanding, highlighting the need for interdisciplinary research. We investigated whether individuals with PCC and fatigue differ from matched controls across neurocognitive, neuroimaging, and immunological measures, integrating these findings with qualitative phenomenological analyses through multimodal cross-analysis. Individuals with PCC and clinically significant fatigue (n=34), and age-, sex-, and education- matched controls recovered from COVID-19 without PCC (n=37) were included. Assessments encompassed physician evaluation, neuropsychological and functional tests, structural and functional MRI, immunological tests, and qualitative phenomenological analysis of interviews. Data were analyzed using established methods and an interdisciplinary cross-analysis to examine persistent cognitive symptoms in PCC. Group comparisons revealed subtle differences between individuals with PCC and controls, while neurocognitive performance and immunological markers remained within normative ranges. Modest differences in white-matter, myelin-related, and global brain measures were observed, alongside differences in associations between network connectivity and neurocognitive performance across groups, suggesting reduced network resilience rather than domain specific deficits. This pattern resonated with qualitative phenomenological findings: altered experiences of concentrating and difficulties to execute decisions and actions, despite preserved performance on standard neurocognitive tests. These findings suggest that cognitive symptoms in post-COVID-19 fatigue are associated with subtle neurobiological alterations not captured by standard cognitive assessments. In this highly fatigued sample, converging neuroimaging, neurocognitive and immunological findings point toward reduced network efficiency rather than overt cognitive impairment. Qualitative phenomenological analysis further highlighted altered modes of being in the world characterized by increased cognitive effort and difficulties executing decisions and actions.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注新冠感染后状况（PCC）伴疲劳者的持续认知症状，将患者与新冠康复但无PCC的匹配对照进行比较，整合神经认知、神经影像、免疫学测量与访谈的现象学分析。组间差异总体细微，神经认知表现和免疫指标多在正常范围内，影像上可见白质、髓鞘相关及全脑指标的轻度差异，且网络连接与认知表现之间的关联模式在两组间不同，作者据此倾向于网络韧性下降而非特定认知域缺损。质性分析也提到，尽管标准测验表现保留，受访者仍感到集中注意和执行决定、行动更费力。研究提示这类认知症状可能与常规认知评估捕捉不到的细微神经生物学改变有关，而非明显的认知损害。

papers.title: Radiological Phenotypes of Acute Brain Injury During Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation on Ultra-Low-Field Portable MRI
papers.authors: Noda K, Ahmed YB, Woo HY(, Khanduja S, Wang Y, Soulé Z, Malfitano M, Wang S, Kim BS, Wilcox C, Gusdon AM, Whitman GJ, Cho S.
papers.abstract: Background Despite the clinical importance of acute brain injury (ABI) during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), the mechanism of ECMO-associated ABI remains poorly understood, partly because conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is incompatible with ECMO devices. Ultra-low-field portable MRI (ULF-pMRI) enables high-quality bedside neuroimaging during ECMO. We aimed to characterize imaging phenotypes of ABI and explore mechanisms underlying lesion distribution across ECMO configurations. Methods In this multicenter retrospective observational study, adults receiving ECMO who underwent bedside ULF-pMRI at Johns Hopkins University and University of Texas–Houston from December 2021 to May 2026 were included. ABI was defined as ischemic stroke (IS), intraparenchymal hemorrhage (IPH), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), or subdural hematoma (SDH). Lesions were characterized according to vascular territory, cortical/subcortical lesion versus deep white matter (WM)/basal ganglia (BG) involvement, laterality, lesion burden, and cerebral small-vessel disease (SVD) using Fazekas scale. Associations between ECMO configuration (central venoarterial [VA], peripheral VA, and venovenous [VV]), echocardiographic findings, and ECMO parameters were examined. Results Among 70 patients analyzed (55.9 ± 16.2 years; 54.3% male), 29 (41.4%) had ABI. IS was the predominant type of ABI (82.8%), with most strokes affecting the frontal lobe (48.3%). All the central VA-ECMO patients with ABI demonstrated predominantly cortical/subcortical lesions, whereas deep WM/BG involvement was more frequent in peripheral VA-ECMO (53.8%). Peripheral VA-ECMO demonstrated left hemispheric predominance (85% vs. 15% right-sided, P =0.002), and deep WM/BG lesions in peripheral were associated with higher ECMO pump flow and lower pulse pressure. Among VV-ECMO patients, bilateral lesions were more common (62.5%), with a high prevalence of deep WM/BG involvement (62.5%) and SVD (75%). Conclusions ULF-pMRI revealed distinct radiological phenotypes of ABI across ECMO configurations; cortical/subcortical lesions in central VA-ECMO, left-sided predominance in peripheral VA-ECMO and frequent deep WM/BG in VV-ECMO. These findings generate mechanistic hypotheses regarding configuration-specific pathways of ABI and may inform future strategies for risk stratification, prevention and monitoring.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注体外膜肺氧合（ECMO）期间急性脑损伤的影像表现，利用超低场便携式磁共振在床旁对接受ECMO的成人进行多中心回顾性观察，并按血管分布、皮层与深部白质/基底节受累、侧别及脑小血管病等特征描述病灶。结果显示，急性脑损伤以缺血性卒中为主，且不同ECMO模式呈现不同影像表型：中心静脉-动脉ECMO以皮层/皮层下病灶为主，外周静脉-动脉ECMO更多累及深部白质/基底节并呈左半球优势，静脉-静脉ECMO则多见双侧病灶和深部受累。作者据此提出，不同ECMO配置可能对应不同的脑损伤机制假设，但该研究为回顾性观察，相关发现尚属机制探索而非因果结论。

papers.title: A digital biomarker of white-matter routing from diffusion MRI as an early biomarker of Alzheimer’s disease
papers.authors: Ghodrat M, Schlachetzki JC, the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is diagnosed after a decade-long phase in which pathology accumulates; current markers show that pathology is present, but not how far it has advanced. Because white-matter structure is altered early, we computed two graph-theoretic indices of periventricular white-matter routing from diffusion MRI in 1,706 OASIS-3 sessions: the Route Concordance Index (RCI), a population-calibrated path-concordance score over 316 routes, and a global conductance from the connectome’s graph Laplacian. RCI was reduced before clinical conversion and declined monotonically across a five-stage trajectory (cross-validated AUC = 0.817 for stable-CN vs. pre-AD; comparable to hippocampal volume and exceeding entorhinal thickness, global conductance, and DTI-ALPS), with degradation concentrated in fronto-striatal circuits. A classifier combining these routing features with demographic, structural-MRI and cognitive covariates detected conversion to MCI or AD up to four years before diagnosis (AUC = 0.831; 0.918 within one year; modest positive predictive value). Findings replicated in ADNI ( n = 609; conductance AUC = 0.805; RCI = 0.797 under frozen external validation) and tracked CSF amyloid- β 42 in the expected direction. Computed from a standard diffusion MRI sequence, RCI is comparable to established structural and demographic biomarkers on preclinical discrimination while, unlike them, declining cleanly and monotonically across the disease trajectory, supporting prospective validation for risk stratification.

papers.title: Post-Learning Reactivation of Memories for Naturalistic Continuous Experiences
papers.authors: Wolf N, Antony JW, Delarazan AI, Reagh ZM, Michelmann S, Ranganath C, Liu XL.
papers.abstract: Memories are not static records of the past; rather, the act of remembering can change how an event is recalled. Intriguingly, several studies also suggest that memories may be reactivated during rest. However, reactivation has largely been studied for spatial tasks and discrete stimuli, and we know little about whether spontaneous reactivation occurs for long timescale naturalistic events and how reactivation affects retention. Using fMRI, we show that neural activity patterns in the hippocampus and the Default Mode Network during encoding of narrative events were spontaneously reactivated during rest. Contrary to predictions, reactivation did not strengthen recall of movie details, and instead exploratory analyses suggested that reactivation in the hippocampus was associated with more gist-like recall one week later. These findings support the idea that memories for complex events may be spontaneously reactivated, but they suggest that rather than simply strengthening episodic memories, reactivation might help transform them. Significance statement We tend to think of memory as a process of recording and later playing back those experiences during retrieval, but some prior evidence suggests the brain may use downtime to process memories to help consolidate them. This paper uses functional MRI to show that the brain activation patterns present while people view films are spontaneously reactivated afterwards during rest. While there was no evidence to suggest that this reactivation strengthened memories, reactivation may be associated with more gist-like memory one week later. These findings suggest that the resting brain processes memories for complex events, but the results call for theories that account for transformations of memories beyond strengthening.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注自然连续经历的记忆在休息时是否会被自发重激活，以及这种重激活如何影响后续保持。研究者用fMRI记录被试编码叙事事件时的神经活动，发现海马和默认模式网络的活动模式在休息期间自发重现。与预期相反，重激活并未增强对影片细节的回忆；探索性分析提示，海马重激活与一周后更偏概要式的回忆相关。作者据此认为，复杂事件的记忆确实可能自发重激活，但其作用或许不是简单强化情节记忆，而是促进记忆表征的转化。

papers.title: Longitudinal fMRI reveals altered developmental trajectories of functional network organisation associated with adolescent cannabis use
papers.authors: Davies EJ, Ertl N, Freeman TP, Borissova A, Thorne RL, Ofori S, Petrilli K, Mokrysz C, Curran HV, Lawn W, Wall MB.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a critical period of brain development during which the endocannabinoid system continues to mature. These developmental changes may contribute to age-related differences in the association between cannabis use and large-scale functional network organisation, yet this association remains incompletely characterised. We hypothesised that regular cannabis use would be associated with differential one-year changes in resting-state functional connectivity between adolescents and adults. Resting-state fMRI data at two time points, one year apart, were analysed from 66 participants (31 aged 16-17 years; 35 aged 26-29 years) including 29 with regular cannabis use and 37 age-matched cannabis-naïve controls. Seed-to-voxel analyses examined longitudinal changes in functional connectivity across age and cannabis-use groups. Year change, age × user-group interactions were identified in salience and default mode network connectivity, including divergent changes in anticorrelations with medial prefrontal, thalamic, cerebellar and juxtapositional regions. Directionality of effects differed by network and region. Additional main effects of user group were observed for executive control and associative striatal connectivity, with the cannabis-use group showing decreased positive connectivity and reduced anticorrelation, respectively. Changes in functional connectivity were developmentally dissociable and predominantly observed in regions contributing to attentional and transmodal processing. These findings suggest that cannabis may be associated with alterations in the maturational refinement of higher-order neural systems, potentially reflecting age-related differences in neurobiological sensitivity to cannabis exposure. Considering developmental stage may therefore be important for characterising cannabis-related neurobiological differences and may have implications for understanding age-dependent vulnerability to cannabis-related psychiatric outcomes.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注青少年期规律使用大麻是否与静息态功能网络组织的发育轨迹存在关联，并比较青少年与成人一年间的变化。研究者对66名参与者（含规律使用者和年龄匹配的未使用者）在两个时间点进行静息态fMRI扫描，分析种子点至全脑的功能连接变化。结果显示，使用组与年龄组在凸显网络和默认模式网络连接上存在交互，与内侧前额叶、丘脑、小脑等区域的反相关变化方向因网络和区域而异；使用组在执行控制和纹状体连接上也表现出主效应。作者据此提出，大麻可能与高阶神经系统成熟优化的改变有关，提示发育阶段对理解大麻相关神经生物学差异及年龄依赖易感性可能很重要，但相关关联不能直接解释为因果或临床效应。

papers.title: Muscarinic signaling sustains delay-period selectivity in prefrontal cortex by preserving thalamic drive
papers.authors: Kim Y, Kim J, Choi IS, Lee J, Yang Y, Choi JH, Choi J, Rah J.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Short-term memory (STM) requires the temporary maintenance of task-relevant information in prefrontal cortex (PFC). Reciprocal interactions between the mediodorsal thalamus (MD) and PFC have been implicated in sustaining this activity, but how thalamofrontal communication is maintained despite the biophysical constraints of repetitive synaptic transmission remains unclear. Here, we show that MD–PFC synapses exhibit profound frequency-dependent short-term depression, causing repetitive thalamic input to progressively lose its ability to drive PFC neurons. During STM performance, acetylcholine (ACh) levels in PFC rose rapidly following cue presentation and remained elevated throughout the delay period. Muscarinic ACh receptor (mAChR) activation did not alleviate synaptic depression, but instead increased the intrinsic excitability of PFC neurons, thereby preserving their responsiveness to weakened thalamic input. Conversely, mAChR blockade impaired STM performance and progressively disrupted delay-period directional representations at both the single-neuron and population levels, while largely sparing initial encoding. These findings identify muscarinic signaling as a postsynaptic gain mechanism that compensates for declining thalamofrontal efficacy and sustains task-relevant prefrontal representations during STM.

papers.title: A Double Challenge: Cerebral Blood Flow During Concurrent Breath-Hold and Motor Task
papers.authors: Jakobsen K, Daiu M, Critchley H, Colasanti A, Asllani I.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background/Hypothesis Challenging the brain with simultaneous global and local demands may reveal functional constraints not apparent with either challenge alone. Here, we combined breath-holding with a motor task to investigate how a global vascular challenge modifies the local neurovascular response. Methods Fourteen healthy adults underwent arterial spin labelling magnetic resonance imaging during three conditions: finger tapping with normal breathing, 25-second inspiratory breath-holding, and finger tapping during breath-holding. Cerebral blood flow responses were assessed using whole brain voxelwise analyses and motor regions of interest. Results In the primary motor cortex, the increase in cerebral blood flow relative to baseline was approximately halved during the combined breath-holding and motor task challenge compared with motor task alone (26.5% vs 51.3%; p<0.001). Supplementary motor area responses were also smaller (23.2% vs 41.2%), but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.092). Regional perfusion reductions were less extensive during the combined challenge than during breath-holding alone. These regional effects occurred without significant global grey- or white-matter perfusion changes from baseline. Conclusion/Interpretation Combining global and local challenges revealed constraints on task-evoked perfusion increases not apparent during motor activation alone. This approach could help assess whether impaired cerebrovascular reserve compromises the brain’s capacity to meet local functional demands.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在健康成人中结合屏气与手指运动任务，用动脉自旋标记磁共振成像考察全局血管挑战如何改变局部神经血管反应。结果显示，与单独运动任务相比，屏气同时进行运动时初级运动皮层血流相对基线的增幅约减半，辅助运动区的反应也较小但差异未达显著；联合挑战时的局部灌注下降范围比单独屏气时更小，且这些局部效应未伴随全脑灰质或白质灌注的显著变化。作者认为，同时施加全局与局部挑战可揭示单独运动激活时未显现的任务诱发灌注增长受限，这一思路或有助于评估脑血管储备受损是否影响大脑满足局部功能需求的能力。

papers.title: Predicting alcohol consumption from resting-state functional connectivity: Feature relevance and the potential of meta-matching
papers.authors: Bottino M, Smolka MN, Böhmer J, Yeo BT, Bach P, Kiefer F, Lenz B, Heinz A, Spitta G, Rosenthal A, Ritter K, Rane RP, Garg S, Schwarz E, ReCoDe Consortium, Walter H, Marxen M.
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is among the most prevalent mental disorders. Associations between resting-state fMRI functional connectivity (FC) and AUD have been reported but rarely replicated. In this preregistered study, we investigated the extent to which FC predicts alcohol consumption, as measured by the AUDIT-C score, in a large sample of non–treatment-seeking alcohol consumers (N = 739), including 528 participants with varying degrees of AUD severity. To optimize performance, we compared kernel ridge regression (KRR) trained directly on this sample with transfer-learning models based on multilayer meta-matching embeddings, from which we derived data-driven relevance maps at the connection, region, and network levels. We tested split-half reliability, reproducibility across cohorts, and outcome specificity of the relevance maps. Both models predicted AUDIT-C scores moderately but significantly ( r ≈ 0.15). Meta-matching did not outperform KRR in prediction. Relevance maps showed limited split-half reliability, consistent with the modest predictive performance, but reproduced moderately well across two independent cohorts. These maps indicate reduced connectivity among limbic regions, the anterior middle temporal gyrus, the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and dorsal attention network regions. In contrast, hypothesized hyperconnectivity patterns involving the striatum, anterior cingulate cortex, and precuneus were less reliable and mostly non-significant. Overall, our findings suggest that resting-state FC contains reproducible but weak signals related to alcohol consumption. Transfer learning improved relevance-map reliability but not prediction performance and reduced outcome specificity. These results support the utility of interpretable machine learning for identifying connectivity patterns related to drinking behavior, while also highlighting current limitations in its predictive power.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在大量非寻求治疗的饮酒者中考察静息态功能连接能否预测酒精消费（以AUDIT-C衡量），并比较了直接训练的核岭回归与基于多层元匹配嵌入的迁移学习模型。两种模型对AUDIT-C的预测均达到中等但显著的水平，迁移学习并未提升预测表现。数据驱动的相关性图谱显示，边缘系统区域、颞中回前部、背内侧前额叶及背侧注意网络区域间连接降低；而关于纹状体、前扣带和楔前叶连接增强的假设可靠性较低且多不显著。作者据此认为，静息态功能连接含有可重复但较弱的饮酒相关信号，可解释机器学习有助于识别相关连接模式，但其预测能力仍有限。

papers.title: Exploratory brain-wide analyses predicting binge drinking: A machine learning and targeted causal inference pipeline in two adolescent cohorts
papers.authors: Visontay R, Byrne HR, Devine EK, Sunderland M, Fan L, Wen W, Perica MI, Tapert S, Clark DB, Nooner K, Afzali K, Squeglia LM, Mewton L.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background A sizeable literature has found that neuroanatomical differences predict alcohol use outcomes in adolescence. However, due possibly to small samples and inconsistent/limited methodologies, it is still unclear which specific morphometric features are most predictive and if they are also causally implicated in binge drinking onset. Methods To differentially predict abstinence from binge drinking by age 16-17, a SuperLearner ensemble algorithm was fit to structural and diffusion MRI features at age 9-10 in the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development cohort (ABCD). A separate model was fit using the National Consortium on Alcohol and NeuroDevelopment in Adolescence (NCANDA), in which the MRI predictors were measured later (ages 12-17) but the developmental outcome (binge drinking by age 18) remained similar. The top ten predictors were extracted from each model, and the causal role of these features scrutinised using targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE). Results Predictive performance in ABCD was poor (AUC=.585) but was stronger in NCANDA (AUC=.695). There was little overlap in predictive feature rankings between the cohorts. TMLE did not reveal a causal effect of the top ten morphological predictors on binge drinking in either cohort. Conclusions No evidence was found for causal contributions of any discrete macrostructural/microstructural brain feature in late childhood or adolescence to binge drinking. Using more sophisticated metrics of brain structure and function may yield better insights. Adding to previous evidence from youth cohorts, neuroanatomy may have greater predictive value for identifying those at risk of adolescent binge drinking when measured in adolescence, rather than late childhood.

papers.title: [Posterior periventricular white matter lesions as a clue to the diagnosis of folate deficiency with compound heterozygous MTHFR polymorphisms: a case report].
papers.authors: Amano S, Akaiwa Y, Abe Y, Kamiyama K, Nakamura T, Miyamoto T.
papers.abstract: An 18-year-old woman presented with a one-month history of persistent dizziness. Brain MRI revealed bilateral periventricular white matter lesions adjacent to the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles. Subsequently, she developed distal paresthesia of the extremities and was admitted for further evaluation. Neurological examination demonstrated abnormal ocular movements in the primary gaze position, horizontal gaze-evoked nystagmus, gait instability, and distal sensory disturbance. There was no antecedent infection, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis was unremarkable. Based on the clinical course and findings, an autoimmune-mediated brainstem-cerebellar disorder was suspected, and high-dose intravenous corticosteroid therapy was administered, resulting in improvement of ocular abnormalities and gait disturbance. Meanwhile, further investigation of the incidental posterior periventricular white matter lesions-considered unrelated to the presenting symptoms-revealed low serum folate levels and compound heterozygous genotype of the MTHFR gene. Vitamin supplementation was initiated accordingly. Notably, the patient's father was also found to have the same MTHFR gene compound heterozygous genotype. This case suggests that bilateral periventricular white matter lesions adjacent to the posterior horns may represent an early radiological marker of folate deficiency associated with MTHFR gene compound heterozygous genotype, even in the absence of overt folate-deficiency symptoms. Recognition of this imaging pattern may facilitate early diagnosis and intervention, potentially preventing future neurological or systemic complications.

papers.title: REG1B attenuates post-cardiac arrest-induced brain injury identified by integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Li L, Lu L, Wang X, Sun J, Xu S, Zhu Y, Lian Y, Wu Y, Hou J, Lin Q, Li S, Zhang Y, Hou G, Huang K, Yao L, Yu Z.
papers.abstract: Abstract Post-cardiac arrest brain injury is a major determinant of mortality and neurological disability after post-cardiac arrest syndrome. However, effective targeted therapies for post-cardiac arrest brain injury and reliable circulating biomarkers for early neurological prognosis are lacking. This study aimed to identify circulating molecules associated with neurological outcomes after cardiac arrest and to investigate their potential neuroprotective mechanisms. Serum samples collected 24 hours after the return of spontaneous circulation were subjected to integrated proteomic and untargeted metabolomic analyses at Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University, and REG1B was identified as a candidate protein associated with favorable neurological outcomes after cardiac arrest (|log2FC|>1.4; P < 0.05). Moreover, metabolomic profiling revealed distinct metabolic reprogramming between the favorable and unfavorable outcome groups. Additionally, a cardiac arrest/cardiopulmonary resuscitation mouse model was developed. Given that human REG1B and mouse Reg1 are orthologous genes with conserved protein sequences, recombinant Reg1 protein was administered exogenously, followed by comprehensive assessments of neurological deficits and pathological changes. To elucidate the mechanism underlying these effects, we conducted a series of experiments in HT22 cells, and Reg1 gain- and loss-of-function assays, Extl3 knockdown, and protein interaction assays were performed to investigate the underlying mechanisms of oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion-induced neuronal injury. In vivo experiments indicated that recombinant Reg1 administration post-cardiac arrest could attenuate neuropathological damage, enhance neurological function scores, and diminish endoplasmic reticulum stress, along with its associated apoptosis. In vitro validation confirmed that Reg1 overexpression markedly enhanced the morphology and neurite outgrowth of HT22 cells while effectively mitigating endoplasmic reticulum stress and related apoptosis. Conversely, loss of Reg1 function exacerbated neuronal injury. Extl3 knockdown further enhanced the neuroprotective effects of Reg1 and attenuated endoplasmic reticulum stress, suggesting that Extl3 may negatively regulate Reg1-dependent neuronal protection. Protein interaction assays further supported a physical interaction between Reg1 and Extl3. Collectively, our findings revealed that REG1B is associated with favorable neurological outcomes and is linked to the homeostatic adaptation of the endoplasmic reticulum following post-cardiac arrest syndrome. Reg1 may exert neuroprotective effects by promoting neuronal repair and suppressing endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated apoptosis, whereas Extl3 may act as a negative regulator of Reg1-mediated neuroprotection. REG1B may therefore represent a candidate circulating biomarker for neurological prognosis, and modulation of REG1B-associated signaling may provide a potential therapeutic strategy for post-cardiac arrest brain injury.

papers.title: Corticomuscular coupling alterations during task-dependent bimanual coordination after stroke: A multimodal functional near-infrared spectroscopy-surface electromyography analysis.
papers.authors: Liu M, Zheng N, Lin Q, Li Y, Sheng B, Wang X, Xie Q.
papers.abstract: Abstract Post-stroke bimanual coordination dysfunction severely impairs activities of daily living. However, the underlying neurophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood, particularly regarding central-peripheral coupling characteristics under different bimanual coordination tasks and their distinction from aging effects. This study included 32 chronic subcortical stroke patients and 29 healthy controls. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy and surface electromyography signals were synchronously acquired during the execution of symmetrical and asymmetrical bimanual coordination tasks. Analyzed indices included cortical activation patterns, functional connectivity, corticomuscular coupling characterized by transfer entropy, intermuscular coupling, and muscle synergies. Correlations between these indices and the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity and Modified Barthel Index were also evaluated. The results showed that during the symmetrical task, the ascending muscle-to-cortex connectivity was significantly reduced in the patient group, and this index was significantly positively correlated with the Modified Barthel Index. Brain functional connectivity and cortical activation were significantly increased in the patient group, and the connectivity from the ipsilesional prefrontal cortex to the contralesional SAC was significantly negatively correlated with Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity scores. Additionally, intermuscular coupling was significantly weakened, and muscle synergy patterns were abnormal in the patient group. During the asymmetrical task, no significant group differences in corticomuscular coupling were found, but brain functional connectivity and cortical activation were both significantly increased, and the connectivity from the ipsilesional supplementary motor area to the contralesional supplementary motor area was significantly positively correlated with MBI. Intermuscular coupling was significantly weakened, and muscle synergy patterns were abnormal. Attribution analysis suggested that cortical hyperactivation patterns and abnormal muscle synergies mainly reflect stroke effects, while abnormal sensory cortex activation and altered corticomuscular coupling may be influenced by both stroke and aging. This study suggests that post-stroke bimanual coordination impairment is closely related to selective damage to sensory feedback pathways, manifested as task-dependent reductions in ascending (muscle-to-cortex) corticomuscular coupling and compensatory cortical reorganization. Multimodal neurophysiological indicators may serve as potential quantitative tools for assessing upper limb function after stroke, but age-matched control studies are essential to dissociate stroke effects from aging effects.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注卒中后双手协调障碍的中枢-外周耦合特征，同步采集脑功能近红外与表面肌电信号，比较慢性皮层下卒中患者与健康对照在对称和非对称双手任务中的表现。结果显示，对称任务下患者肌肉到皮层的上行耦合减弱，且与日常活动能力正相关；患者皮层激活和脑功能连接升高，部分连接与上肢运动评分相关，同时肌间耦合减弱、肌肉协同模式异常。非对称任务下耦合未见组间差异，但皮层激活与连接仍升高。作者据此提出，卒中后双手协调障碍与感觉反馈通路的选择性受损及代偿性皮层重组有关，并提示多模态指标或可用于评估上肢功能，但需年龄匹配对照以区分卒中与老化影响。

papers.title: Altered intersubject variability of functional connectivity in gray and white matter underlying neurocognition and genetic profiles in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
papers.authors: Huang C, Lu W, Liu J.
papers.abstract: Abstract Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder is an autoimmune disease that causes inflammatory damage to the central nervous system. While alterations in functional connectivity have been reported in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, changes in intersubject variability of functional connectivity within gray matter and white matter are not yet understood. A total of 66 patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and 71 healthy controls were recruited. We compared intersubject variability of functional connectivity between patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and healthy controls and performed subgroup analyses comparing neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder patients with and without a history of optic neuritis. We also examined the associations between intersubject variability of functional connectivity alterations and disease duration, clinical disability, and cognitive scores. We combined our imaging results with those of the Allen Human Brain Atlas to conduct transcriptome-neuroimaging association analyses, identified gene expression profiles linked to intersubject variability of functional connectivity alterations and characterized their potential biological functions. Compared with healthy controls, patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder showed widespread increases in intersubject variability of functional connectivity. Notable gray matter alterations included the precentral and postcentral gyri; extensive occipital areas; and the insula, putamen, and thalamus. The corresponding white matter changes involved the fornix, corticospinal tract, widespread corona radiata, cingulum, and uncinate fasciculus. Compared with patients without optic neuritis, the optic neuritis subgroup exhibited distinct intersubject variability of functional connectivity alterations in specific regions, such as the inferior parietal lobule, angular gyrus, thalamus, fornix, and internal capsule. Clinically, only white matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity correlated significantly with physical disability and cognitive processing speed and was not significantly associated with disease duration. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that genes positively associated with white matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity were enriched in synaptic plasticity and cognition, while negatively associated genes were enriched in oxidative stress. Additionally, genes positively associated with the gray matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity were enriched in myelination and lipid biosynthesis, whereas genes negatively associated with the gray matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity were involved in synapse organization. In conclusion, our study revealed alterations in gray matter- and white matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity across neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and clinical subtypes. We demonstrate that changes in white matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity correlate with clinical disability and neurocognition. Linking these connectivity patterns with gene expression profiles may provide insights into the underlying pathophysiology of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注视神经脊髓炎谱系疾病患者灰质与白质功能连接的受试者间变异性是否改变，比较了患者与健康对照，并结合影像与基因表达数据做转录组关联分析。结果显示，患者灰质和白质多个区域的功能连接受试者间变异性普遍升高，伴视神经炎病史的亚组在部分区域呈现不同模式；其中仅白质变异性与躯体残疾和认知加工速度相关，与病程无关。相关基因分别富集于突触可塑性、认知、氧化应激、髓鞘形成和脂质合成等条目。作者据此提出，白质功能连接变异性的改变可能与临床残疾和神经认知相关，并可能为理解该病病理生理提供线索；这些关联尚属相关性质，不能视为因果或治疗证据。

papers.title: Advances in Multi-Omics Research on Post-Stroke Depression: From Molecular Mechanisms to Therapeutic Strategies.
papers.authors: Feng G, Gao L, Zhao Y, Yu Z, Yang M, Chen Y, Xu X.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a common neuropsychiatric complication after stroke and has a substantial impact on functional recovery, quality of life, and long-term outcomes. Because stroke-related manifestations, including aphasia, cognitive impairment, fatigue, and somatic symptoms, overlap with depressive symptoms, the clinical identification of PSD still largely relies on symptom assessment and clinical interviews, resulting in delayed diagnosis and intervention in some patients. Recent studies indicate that the development of PSD is not driven by a single pathological process but involves multiple mechanisms, including neuroinflammation, neural network alterations, dysfunction of the neurovascular unit, disturbances in energy and lipid metabolism, imbalance of the microbiota-gut-brain axis, and psychosocial factors following brain injury. The advancement of multi-omics technologies has provided new approaches for investigating the biological mechanisms underlying PSD. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in the application of multi-omics approaches in PSD research, focusing on molecular alterations identified across different omics platforms and potential biomarkers. Furthermore, the role of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis in stress response regulation and PSD development is discussed within the context of neuro-immune-metabolic interactions. Overall, multi-omics studies have provided new insights into the molecular basis of PSD and facilitated the identification of potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. However, their clinical utility requires further evaluation through standardized cohorts and validation studies.

papers.title: Neuropsychological and Event-Related Potential Abnormalities Three Months After Brainstem Lacunar Infarction: An Exploratory Case-Control Study.
papers.authors: Wang X, Yang Y, Zhao S, Zhang J, Zhang B, Hou X, Wang X, Liu X, Guo Y.
papers.abstract: Background Though smaller in size, lacunar infarction was reported to cause cognitive impairment. As a common infarction location, brainstem interacts extensively with cortical structures. However, whether brainstem infarction affected cognition and involved cognitive domains remained elusive. In this study, we aimed to comprehensively investigate cognitive changes after brainstem infarction by using neuropsychological and neurophysiological measures. Methods The study was designed as an exploratory case-control analysis and modest sample size was included. Altogether, 29 patients with brainstem lacunar infarction (17 males, mean age 61.83 years) and 24 healthy controls (14 males, mean age 60.25 years) were recruited. Multiple neuropsychological scales and a sensitive visual oddball paradigm comprising standard, target and novel stimuli were employed for cross-sectional assessment of cognitive processing at 3 months following acute infarction. The event-related potential (ERP) components N1, P2, N2 and P3 were measured and analyzed. Primary cognitive outcomes including neuropsychological scores and P3 amplitude/latency were evaluated. Results Brainstem infarction patients exhibited lower scores or longer reaction time in Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Stroop Color and Word Test, Shape Trail Test and Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test. Compared with healthy controls, P3b/P3a amplitudes were attenuated and latencies were prolonged in infarction group, and these changes still existed in subtraction-derived difference waveforms. Moreover, exploratory analyses showed that cognitive data including ERP parameters were significantly correlated with infarction diameter and white matter hyperintensity grade. Conclusions Patients with brainstem lacunar infarction exhibited multi-domain cognitive impairments, with executive function, visuospatial function, memory, attention allocation, orienting response and processing speed involved. These abnormalities should be validated by comparisons with vascular-risk or non-brainstem stroke controls. The cognitive decline after lacunar infarction should be paid critical attention, especially for patients with severe imaging lesions.

papers.title: The Current Landscape of Exosome-Based Strategies for Breast Cancer Brain Metastasis: From Mechanistic Insights to Therapeutic Potential.
papers.authors: Jin S, Jiang Y, Meng L, Ye N, Qiu J, Lin J.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a common malignancy affecting women. Brain metastasis is a serious late-stage complication associated with high incidence and poor prognosis, particularly in patients with triple-negative and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) -positive breast cancer. Currently, surgery and radiotherapy are the primary treatment options for breast cancer brain metastasis (BCBM). However, the effectiveness of conventional chemotherapy and immunotherapy is limited by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the complex tumor microenvironment, and effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. Exosomes are extracellular vesicles with diameters of 30-150 nm that mediate intercellular communication by transporting active molecules such as proteins and nucleic acids. They play crucial roles in tumor development, progression, and metastasis. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that exosomes promote BCBM through various mechanisms, including BBB remodeling to facilitate tumor cell transmigration, initiation of the pre-metastatic microenvironment, and systemic immune escape mediated by exosomal PD-L1. Genetically or chemically engineered exosomes have demonstrated targeting and drug-delivery potential in preclinical models, making them potential candidates for BCBM treatment. This review summarizes the clinical challenges associated with BCBM and the biological characteristics of exosomes and their mechanisms of action in brain metastasis. It also discusses the potential of exosomes as diagnostic markers, therapeutic targets, and drug delivery carriers, providing insights into future research and clinical translation, which remains challenging and requires further validation.

papers.title: Diabetes mellitus accelerates preclinical Alzheimer's disease progression by amplifying the amyloid-to-tau pathway and attenuating brain-cognition resilience.
papers.authors: Jin H, Meng Y, Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.
papers.abstract: BackgroundDiabetes mellitus (DM) is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its stage-dependent effects on the ATN framework remain unclear.ObjectiveTo determine whether DM differentially affects clinical progression from cognitively normal (CN) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) versus MCI to AD, how DM modulates the ATN cascade, and the optimal follow-up for detecting structural-cognitive changes.MethodsWe analyzed longitudinal data from 1638 ADNI participants (765 CN, 71 with DM; 873 MCI, 91 with DM). Clinical progression was assessed by Cox regression. Annualized slopes of ATN biomarkers and cognition were estimated. Moderation analyses tested DM × predictor interactions on A→T (amyloid→tau) and N→C (neurodegeneration→cognition) pathways with FDR correction. Piecewise linear mixed models identified the optimal knot for structural-cognitive coupling.ResultsDM increased CN-to-MCI risk (adjusted HR = 1.73, p = 0.028) but not MCI-to-AD progression (adjusted HR = 1.10, p = 0.574). In CN, DM amplified amyloid-driven tau accumulation in entorhinal cortex (A→T interaction β = 0.77, FDR p = 0.043) and attenuated the protective effect of hippocampal volume on cognition (e.g., hippocampal volume slope × DM on MMSE slope: β = -0.19, FDR p = 0.031). These effects were absent in MCI (all FDR p > 0.05).
