A 36-month follow-up was the optimal window for detecting robust structural-cognitive coupling in the CN cohort, independent of DM status.ConclusionsDiabetes accelerates preclinical AD by amplifying A→T and eroding structural-cognitive resilience, but does not hasten progression from established MCI to AD. A minimum 36-month observation period is recommended for early-phase prevention trials.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Cerebral hemodynamic reserve and the prediction of shunt-responsive reversibility in idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.authors: Takase H.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
papers.abstract: The placebo-controlled PENS trial showed that shunting improves gait but not cognition or continence in idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH). This selective response highlights an unresolved problem: even among patients who respond to temporary cerebrospinal-fluid (CSF) drainage, we cannot predict which deficits will reverse after shunting. Static structural and perfusion markers, including white-matter hyperintensity load, cerebral small-vessel-disease burden, and baseline cerebral blood flow, do not predict shunt response. In contrast, impaired cerebrovascular reactivity is associated with a favorable response, yet cerebral autoregulation has not been measured before and after CSF diversion. I propose that reversibility in iNPH reflects recoverable hemodynamic reserve, and that this hypothesis can be tested within the existing diagnostic pathway.
papers.summary_zh: 该文针对特发性正常压力脑积水（iNPH）患者分流术后仅步态改善、认知与控尿未必恢复这一选择性反应问题，提出可逆性反映的是可恢复的脑血流动力学储备。作者指出，白质高信号负荷、脑小血管病负担和基线脑血流等静态结构与灌注指标不能预测分流反应，而脑血管反应性受损却与较好反应相关；但脑自动调节尚未在脑脊液引流前后被测量。文章据此提出可在现有诊断路径中检验该假说，属于观点性论述而非原始实验。

papers.title: Mapping Lifespan Functional Connectivity with Vision Transformer and Attention-Guided Trajectory Analysis.
papers.authors: Cho K, Choi J, Park M, Shin NY, Han S.
papers.abstract: Brain aging involves widespread reorganization of functional networks, yet characterizing these changes across the lifespan remains challenging. This study presents an innovative application of a Vision Transformer (ViT) to resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) functional connectivity for age group classification using the Human Connectome Project (HCP) Lifespan datasets. A ViT model was fine-tuned on [Formula: see text] ROI-to-ROI connectivity matrices to perform three binary age group classifications (Young versus Old, Adult versus Aging, Young versus Aging). The model achieved accuracies of 91%, 71%, and 93%, respectively, under five-fold cross-validation. To interpret model decisions, attention weight maps from the final transformer encoder layer were extracted using attention rollout and thresholded with a scree plot analysis, identifying 48 high-salience connections across 28 brain regions. These features were analyzed across the lifespan using generalized additive models (GAM), and k-means clustering of the trajectories revealed three dominant lifespan connectivity patterns: Age-Declining, Mid-Life Peaking, and Age-Increasing. This study demonstrates the viability of the ViT for functional connectome analysis and shows that attention-based interpretability combined with GAM trajectory analysis can enrich insights into age-related changes in brain network connectivity, offering a framework for interpretable brain-age modeling.

papers.title: Adapted physical activity enhances cortical surface area and modulates functional connectivity of default-mode and frontoparietal networks in schizophrenia.
papers.authors: Leroux E, Lerosier B, Tréhout M, Quarck G, Dollfus S.
papers.abstract: Background Adapted physical activity (APA) may benefit patients with schizophrenia (SZPs), but neurobiological effects remain underexplored. We investigated whether a 16-week web-based APA program (e-APA) induces brain plasticity in SZPs and whether brain changes relate to cardiorespiratory fitness and clinical symptoms. Methods In secondary analyses of a randomized controlled trial, 31 SZPs were assigned to e-APA (n = 16) or e-health education (e-HE, n = 15), matched to 23 healthy controls (HCs). Structural and resting-state functional MRI were acquired pre- and post-intervention to assess cortical surface area, thickness, and functional connectivity (FC). Relationships with VO2 max and symptom changes were examined. Results Compared to SZPs-HE, SZPs-APA showed greater surface area changes in the left superior frontal, right precentral and right cuneus cortices. Separately, within SZPs-APA, VO2 max improvement was associated with changes in the left precentral and inferior temporal cortices and right insula, while reductions in apathy and positive symptoms were associated with changes in the right fusiform, rostral middle frontal, inferior temporal cortices and left supramarginal cortex. Greater FC changes within the frontoparietal network (FPN) were observed in e-APA versus e-HE, and within the default-mode network in SZPs-APA versus SZPs-HE, at the uncorrected level (neither survived multiple-comparison correction). FPN changes were associated with VO2 max gains. No significant structural and functional differences occurred between SZPs-APA and HCs-APA. Conclusions e-APA induced cortical plasticity in motor, visual, and associative regions in SZPs. Brain changes were associated with improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness and clinical symptoms, while uncorrected FC findings require cautious interpretation. e-APA may represent a promising adjunct to the treatment of schizophrenia.

papers.title: Resting-state frontostriatal dysconnectivity and cognitive impairment in alcohol use disorder.
papers.authors: Chen J, Song X, Chen T, Liu S, Zou W, Fan N.
papers.abstract: Background Alcohol use disorder (AUD) involves persistent craving and cognitive deficits, reflecting an imbalance between reward/habit systems and cognitive control. This study used resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) to identify prefrontal-striatal circuits related to cognitive and clinical dimensions in AUD. Methods Sixty-six male patients with AUD and 43 male healthy controls completed craving assessments, MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery testing, and resting-state fMRI. Seed-based rsFC analyses were conducted for the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), nucleus accumbens, and dorsal striatum (DS). Group differences and correlations with cognition and craving were examined. Results Compared with controls, patients with AUD showed poorer speed of processing, working memory, and reasoning/problem solving (all p < .05), but not verbal or visual learning. AUD was characterized by hypoconnectivity of DS and DLPFC with frontoparietal, temporal, and cerebellar regions. Within AUD, greater craving was associated with lower left DS-right supramarginal gyrus connectivity (r = -.267, p = .030). Poorer speed of processing was associated with greater right DLPFC-left orbital inferior frontal gyrus connectivity (r = -.289, p = .030). Poorer visual learning was associated with greater right DLPFC connectivity with the right middle temporal gyrus (r = -.268, p = .036) and right inferior temporal gyrus (r = -.259, p = .044). Conclusion AUD involves widespread DS- and DLPFC-related hypoconnectivity and distinct circuit-level associations with craving and cognition. These preliminary findings provide initial support for a dimensional circuit-based framework of AUD heterogeneity and suggest that right DLPFC-related connectivity may be relevant to cognitive dysfunction. However, these associations were exploratory and require independent replication before any intervention implications can be considered.

papers.title: Exploring the neural correlates of mental health: associations between cortical folding and mental health problems in youth with prenatal alcohol exposure.
papers.authors: Scholten C, Gilchrist C, Geeraert B, McMorris CA, Gibbard WB, Pei J, Beaulieu C, Landman BA, Tortorelli C, Lebel C.
papers.abstract: Prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) can alter neurodevelopment and cause health and behavioral effects. Mental health challenges disproportionately affect individuals with PAE and are related to brain alterations. Cortical folding (gyrification) is associated with mental health in clinical populations and may help understand mental health difficulties in individuals with PAE. 161 datasets from 125 youth (57 PAE, 59 females) aged 7-21 years were included. T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and the caregiver-report Behavior Assessment System for Children were collected at baseline and 2-year follow-up. Images were processed to extract local gyrification index (LGI) from 20 mental health-related regions. Linear mixed-effects models were used to test the effect of PAE on associations between LGI and mental health symptoms. Youth with PAE had more Externalizing Problems (60.7 ± 15.5) than unexposed youth (54.8 ± 11.1; p < 0.001). PAE moderated the relationship between Internalizing Problems and LGI in the left posterior orbital gyrus and the left subcallosal area, and between Externalizing Problems and LGI in the right frontal pole and left subcallosal area. Higher LGI was associated with higher Internalizing and Externalizing Problems in participants with PAE; this association was weaker or absent in unexposed youth. This indicates a potential neurobiological basis for mental health challenges in individuals with PAE.

papers.title: Common phenomenal and neural substrate geometry in visual motion perception.
papers.authors: Robinson K, Zeleznikow-Johnston A, Wu J, Yoshimura Y, Tsuchiya N.
papers.abstract: What is a possible physical substrate of the qualitative aspects of consciousness (qualia)? Answering this question is a central goal of consciousness research. Due to their subjective and ineffable nature, finding a quantitative way to characterise qualia from verbal description has thus far proven elusive. To overcome the challenge of expressing subjective experience, recent structural and relational approaches have been proposed from mathematics. Yet, as far as we know, no attempts have been made to evaluate the relationship between a certain structure of qualia and the structure of a candidate underlying physical substrate. Towards this ambitious goal of linking the structures of qualia and physical, we set out to make an empirical first step by focusing on experienced dissimilarity of visual motion in human participants and stimulus-evoked neural population response geometry recorded from mouse primary visual cortex. From human participants (N=171), we obtained dissimilarity ratings of visual motion experiences induced by 48 stimuli, spanning 8 directions and 6 spatial frequencies. Analysis revealed a human dissimilarity structure that was not well captured by a simple monotonic function of physical motion-direction difference alone nor by a pure orientation-symmetry account. From nine individual mice, we recorded single-neuron activity (n = 751) with optical imaging in both awake and lightly anaesthetised conditions (isoflurane 0.6-0.8%). From neuron population responses to a similar set of motion stimuli, we computed a distance matrix that is comparable to our human dissimilarity matrix. Quantitative analyses show structural commonalities between a human dissimilarity structure and mouse neural structure, where a categorical organisation of stimulus direction best explained both. These commonalities were similar in awake and anaesthetised recordings, suggesting that this coarse V1 geometry is relatively insensitive to this type of anaesthesia; future work combining behaviour with causal intervention is required to relate such neural structures to conscious experience. Finally, we list several empirical factors that can be improved to promote our qualia structure approach in the future.

papers.title: From Cell to Circuit: Altered Functional Network Topology in iPSC-derived Neuronal Circuits in Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.authors: Issa R, Wein S, Milenkovic VM, Rupprecht R, Wetzel CH, Schwarzbach JV.
papers.abstract: The functional organization of brain networks relies on a delicate balance between segregation and integration, which supports both localized neural processing and global information exchange. While numerous whole-brain imaging studies have linked disruptions in this balanced topology to Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), it remains unclear whether such macroscale alterations are reflected in neuronal circuit dynamics at the cellular level. In this study, we investigated whether neuronal networks derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) of nine MDD patients display a distinct functional topology compared to nine matched controls. We obtained skin biopsies from all participants, cultivated fibroblasts, and reprogrammed these into hiPSCs. We then differentiated hiPSCs into neural progenitor cells (NPCs), which we later developed into neurons. We recorded spontaneous activity in the derived neuronal networks using calcium imaging, and applied graph theory analysis to quantify differences in functional topology between groups. We observed a significant decrease in the clustering coefficient and average node degree in MDD-derived neural networks. Furthermore, global efficiency showed a downward trend across varying thresholds and network sizes in patient-derived lines. Together, these findings demonstrate diminished segregation and reduced overall nodal connectivity in MDD-derived neural networks. This suggests that a predisposition for less efficient functional topology exists in depression at the microscale, highlighting the utility of hiPSC technology in modeling cellular disease mechanisms and exploring potential cellular correlates of network-level phenomena reported in depression.

papers.title: Stratifying heterogeneity in mild cognitive impairment: A multimodal subtype and stage inference approach.
papers.authors: Rodolfo CC, Vinícius SR, Francesca B, Alexandra Y, Neil O, James C, Carlos SG, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.
papers.abstract: This study aims to identify distinct clinical and biological subtypes of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and their progression stages using a data-driven multimodal approach, aimed at improving the stratification and prediction of conversion to Alzheimer's disease (AD). We applied the Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) algorithm to a multimodal dataset from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) to identify distinct MCI subtypes and their progression stages on 558 patients classified as MCI amyloid-positive. Our model incorporated T1-weighted structural MRI (measuring cortical, subcortical, and hippocampal volumes), CSF biomarkers (Aβ1-42 and p-TAU), APOE-ε4 status, and a comprehensive set of neuropsychological scores. We delimited four subtypes, which two exhibited higher risk for conversion to AD. The remaining two were characterized by prominent ventricular enlargement and a significant association with geriatric depression, respectively. Predictive performance was driven mainly by the class of input features: a multimodal model using individual biomarkers alone achieved the best discrimination (AUC 0.865; accuracy 0.810), and adding SuStaIn subtype and stage did not improve it. However, subtype and stage in isolation (two variables rather than sixteen) reached an AUC of 0.811 with the highest recall observed (0.867), statistically indistinguishable from the full model. Thus, applying SuStaIn to multidomain data successfully disentangles the phenotypic heterogeneity of MCI. By separating temporal disease progression (staging) from inherent trait differences (subtyping), this framework provides a more refined diagnostic tool for patient stratification and early intervention in the AD continuum.

papers.title: CSF1R haploinsufficiency reveals subtle and selective age- and sex-dependent vulnerabilities in cognition and white matter without overt neurodegeneration.
papers.authors: Schmidt SD, Guimarães DM, Hogan-Cann AE, Crooks AM, Novikov V, German-Castelan L, Fan J, Cowan MF, Fodor C, Ollen-Bittle NK, Nichols E, Schmitz T, Whitehead SN, Finger E, Bartha R, Saksida LM, Bussey TJ, Prado VF, Prado MAM.
papers.abstract: Adult-onset leukoencephalopathy with axonal spheroids and pigmented glia (ALSP) is caused by autosomal dominant mutations in the colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R), yet the extent to which CSF1R haploinsufficiency alone drives cognitive and neurobiological dysfunction remains unclear. Here, we performed a longitudinal multi-level characterization of behavioral, neuroimaging, cellular, and molecular phenotypes in male and female Csf1r+/- mice to determine the impact of partial CSF1R loss across aging. Cognitive function was assessed using touchscreen-based tasks probing cognitive flexibility, working memory, selective attention, and extinction learning, given that executive function is mainly compromised in ALSP. Brain microstructure was evaluated by diffusion-weighted MRI, complemented by MALDI mass spectrometry imaging to examine regional phospholipid composition. Cell-type quantification and gene expression analyses were performed to identify potential cellular and molecular correlates. Across most domains and ages, Csf1r+/- mice exhibited preserved cognitive performance and cellular composition. Within this broadly intact framework, subtle, age- and sex-dependent vulnerabilities emerged. Aged females showed reduced fractional anisotropy and neurite density in the corpus callosum and left primary motor cortex, along with region-specific alterations in phosphatidylcholine species. Aged males exhibited increased response persistence at the final extinction session and elevated false alarm rates under maximal attentional load. Notably, these changes occurred in the absence of microglial or oligodendrocyte loss, indicating mild microstructural and circuit-level alterations rather than widespread neurodegeneration. Collectively, these findings indicate that CSF1R haploinsufficiency does not recapitulate the severe phenotype of ALSP but instead reveals selective, sex-specific vulnerabilities in white matter and cognitive function. This profile is consistent with a sensitized state in which additional factors may be required to drive disease progression.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究以Csf1r+/-小鼠为对象，结合触摸屏认知任务、扩散加权MRI、质谱成像及细胞和基因表达分析，考察CSF1R单倍剂量不足随年龄增长对认知与脑结构的影响。总体来看，小鼠在多数认知领域和年龄阶段表现正常，细胞组成也基本保留；但在此背景下出现了细微且依赖年龄和性别的易感性：老年雌鼠胼胝体及左侧初级运动皮层各向异性与神经突密度降低，并伴区域磷脂成分改变，老年雄鼠则在消退学习后期表现出反应持续增多、高注意负荷下误报率升高。这些变化未见小胶质细胞或少突胶质细胞丢失，提示为轻度微结构和环路层面改变而非广泛神经退行性变。作者据此认为，CSF1R单倍剂量不足并不复现ALSP的严重表型，而是形成一种选择性的性别相关易感状态，可能还需其他因素推动疾病进展。

papers.title: 4DLoG: Generative modeling of neurodegenerative brain anatomy with 4D longitudinal diffusion model.
papers.authors: Jayakumar N, Deb S, Jafrasteh B, Zhao Q, Zhang M.
papers.abstract: Modeling and predicting neurodegenerative disease progression from medical images remains a major challenge in medical AI, with significant implications for early diagnosis, disease monitoring, and treatment planning. However, most longitudinal neuroimaging datasets are temporally sparse, with substantial gaps and missing follow-up scans for individual subjects. This makes it difficult to learn and accurately capture the continuous anatomical changes associated with disease progression at the level of individual subjects. To address this problem, we propose a novel model, named as 4DLoG, a full 4D (3D×T) Longitudinal Generative framework that effectively models and synthesizes follow-up brain anatomy over time, conditioned on available clinical and demographic variables. In contrast to previous approaches, our 4DLoG features two main contributions. First, it introduces a full 4D generative diffusion framework that jointly models spatial and temporal dependencies across complete longitudinal sequences through dedicated spatiotemporal attention, with robust spatial patch extraction and temporal alignment. Second, it explicitly learns the distribution of topology-preserving spatiotemporal deformations, which captures realistic geometric changes in brain structures over time. These new components enable a better generation of anatomically plausible future states from an imaging scan at any time point, providing greater flexibility for modeling individual longitudinal brain trajectories. We validate our model through both synthetic sequence generation and downstream longitudinal disease classification, as well as brain segmentation. Experiments on two large-scale longitudinal neuroimage datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in generating anatomically accurate, temporally consistent, and clinically meaningful brain trajectories. Our code is available on Github.

papers.title: Age-stratified neuroimaging correlates of psychiatric symptoms in first-episode schizophrenia: Insights from structural and functional MRI.
papers.authors: Wang X, Li Z, Yu J, Zhang R, Cao D.
papers.abstract: To investigate changes in brain structure and function, their correlations with psychiatric symptom severity, and possible neuropathological differences in patients with first-episode schizophrenia (FES) with different ages of onset. A total of 76 patients with FES and 67 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled. Patients with FES were stratified based on the onset age into two subgroups as follows: (i) early adult onset (EOS, 18-25 years) and (ii) young-middle-aged onset (YMOS, 26-45 years). Every participant underwent the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS), along with 3D T1-weighted structural MRI and resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI). Amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) was used to measure spontaneous brain activity. After analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was performed to examine the main effects of age, disease, and their interaction, post-hoc simple effect analysis and Pearson correlation analysis were conducted between differentially expressed indices and PANSS scores. Patients with FES exhibited significantly lower ALFF in the left lingual gyrus and right postcentral gyrus than HCs. ALFF in the right postcentral gyrus was correlated with negative symptom scores. YMOS group showed increased ALFF in the right insula, whereas EOS group showed higher ALFF in the right precuneus. In contrast, YMOS group exhibited lower ALFF in the right precuneus, and this reduction was significantly correlated with positive symptom severity. No significant differences were found in gray matter structural indices of these regions (all p > 0.05). With no comparable macroscopic gray matter structural changes in the affected areas, patients with FES with different onset ages exhibit distinct patterns of spontaneous brain functional abnormalities, which may indicate variations in underlying pathophysiological processes.

papers.title: Pain mechanisms in trigeminal neuralgia: From peripheral pathology to brain network reorganization and neurosurgical implications.
papers.authors: Serhiienko YH, Nekrasova NO, Piatykop VO, Yu Kaliuzhka V.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
papers.abstract: Objectives Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) involves peripheral neurovascular pathology and may also be associated with maladaptive neuroplastic changes in central nervous system networks. This review synthesizes evidence on peripheral and central pain mechanisms, neuroimaging biomarkers, molecular and transcriptomic correlates, and neurosurgical implications, including emerging neuromodulation strategies. Materials and methods This narrative review drew on topic-oriented searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science conducted between June 27 and July 5, 2026, covering literature published through June 2026. Supplementary targeted searches and reference-list screening were used to identify relevant publications. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively. Results Evidence supports a multilevel model of TN involving peripheral pathology and central neuroplastic changes. Neuroimaging studies report structural and functional alterations in sensorimotor, salience, limbic, and default mode networks, alongside disrupted structure-function coupling. Partial restoration of functional connectivity after neurosurgical treatment has been reported, although outcomes vary. Transcriptomic findings link imaging abnormalities to genes involved in ion channel function, synaptic signaling, neuroinflammation, and energy metabolism but remain hypothesis-generating. Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) may provide short-term analgesic benefit; however, evidence is limited and heterogeneous. Conclusions TN may be understood as a disorder involving interactions between peripheral pathology and central nervous system reorganization. Integrating neuroimaging and molecular evidence may inform future patient stratification and neurosurgical decision-making. Individualized neuromodulation remains investigational and requires further clinical validation.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述围绕三叉神经痛从外周病理到中枢网络重组的多层次机制展开，梳理了神经影像、分子与转录组证据及神经外科相关启示。文章指出，证据支持三叉神经痛涉及外周病理与中枢神经可塑性改变的交互作用，影像研究报告感觉运动、突显、边缘及默认模式网络存在结构与功能改变，结构-功能耦合也出现紊乱；手术治疗后功能连接有部分恢复的报道，但结果不一。转录组发现将影像异常与离子通道、突触信号、神经炎症和能量代谢相关基因联系起来，但仍属假设生成性质。作者认为经皮电刺激可能带来短期镇痛获益，但证据有限且异质；个体化神经调控仍处研究阶段，需进一步临床验证。

papers.title: ART-TMJ: Arthroscopic real-time classification system for temporomandibular joint disorders.
papers.authors: Zar K, Janmohamed T, Talisman S, Hanna S, Komath D.
papers.journal: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery
papers.abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) Level II arthroscopy offers unparalleled diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities by enabling direct visualization and manipulation of the articular disc and intra-articular structures. This prospective study introduces a novel, evidence-based classification system that integrates clinical findings, radiological imaging, and arthroscopic assessment to improve diagnostic precision and guide personalized treatment planning. A cohort of 160 patients (295 joints) underwent standardized clinical evaluation, MRI, and Level II and III arthroscopy between 2019 and 2024. Patients were stratified into five stages, reflecting combined clinical, imaging, and arthroscopic findings. The cohort was predominantly female (84.6%) with a mean age of 41 years, and 83.8% had bilateral involvement. Arthroscopic findings frequently revealed more advanced joint pathology than clinical and radiological assessments alone (p = 0.005), underscoring the added diagnostic value of direct joint inspection. Patients' outcomes support the treatment algorithm. This integrated classification system bridges existing gaps in TMJ disorder staging by encompassing anatomical, functional, and pathological parameters, thereby facilitating tailored stage-specific interventions ranging from conservative management to advanced arthroscopic procedures and joint reconstruction. By enhancing diagnostic accuracy and treatment alignment, this system serves as a practical tool to optimize outcomes and improve communication among TMJ surgeons in minimally invasive joint surgery.

papers.title: Exosomes in remote ischemic preconditioning-mediated organ protection: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
papers.authors: Randhawa PK, Hanifa M, Suri M, Bajgai B, Jaggi AS, Bali A.
papers.abstract: Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is an endogenous protective strategy that confers resistance against sustained ischemia-reperfusion injury in distant organs. RIPC induces protective responses through complex neuronal, humoral, and systemic signaling pathways. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes may serve as important mediators of humoral inter-organ communication during RIPC. Exosomes are small extracellular vesicles released by donor cells that transport biologically active molecules, including lipids, proteins, messenger RNAs, and microRNAs, to recipient cells, thereby modulating cellular responses to injury. Emerging evidence indicates that RIPC-associated exosomes and their molecular cargo contribute to protection against ischemia-reperfusion injury in organs such as the heart, brain, kidney, and spinal cord. Several exosomal molecules, including miRNAs, HSP90, HIF-1α, and NOX2, have been implicated in the regulation of cellular pathways associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, mitochondrial function, and tissue survival. In particular, alterations in exosomal miRNAs and protein and metabolite profiles following RIPC suggest that exosomes may participate in the transmission of protective signals from remote ischemic tissues to target organs. The therapeutic potential of exosomes is further supported by their ability to transport multiple bioactive molecules and their potential application as biomarkers or delivery vehicles for therapeutic cargo. However, the specific exosomal components responsible for RIPC-mediated protection and their causal contribution to inter-organ signaling remain to be fully established. Therefore, the present review summarizes the emerging evidence on the role of exosomes in RIPC-mediated organ protection, with particular emphasis on cardiovascular and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, the molecular cargo involved, underlying protective mechanisms, and their potential therapeutic and translational applications.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning model based on radiomic features of hippocampal subfields for classifying zoster-associated pain.
papers.authors: Wen X, Peng R, Wang M, Yu M, Liu S, Zhang D, Ren C, Chen G.
papers.abstract: Postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), the most common complication of herpes zoster (HZ), is difficult to prevent due to limited understanding of the mechanisms underlying the transition from acute to chronic pain and the lack of objective neuroimaging biomarkers for individualized risk stratification. In this study, we aimed to develop interpretable machine learning models based on hippocampal subfield radiomics to classify zoster-associated pain (ZAP) patients and identify neuroimaging biomarkers reflecting microstructural alterations in hippocampus associated with ZAP. High-resolution 3D T1-weighted MR images were obtained from 28 PHN patients, 25 Hz patients, and 21 healthy controls (HCs). We extracted radiomic features of ten hippocampal subfields and used five machine learning classification algorithms to identify the most contributive subfield and robust model for classifying ZAP patients. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the optimal model. In distinguishing ZAP patients from HCs, the SVM_Linear model based on the left subiculum radiomics achieved the highest performance with an AUC of 0.739, whereas the Logistic_L1 model based on the right CA4-DG and left SR-SL-SM radiomics showed the best performance with an AUC of 0.799 in distinguishing PHN patients from HZ patients. SHAP analysis revealed that SmallAreaEmphasis from the right CA4-DG subfield was the dominant feature for identifying PHN patients, followed by ClusterShade from the left SR-SL-SM subfield. Furthermore, both features showed strong associations with disease duration. These results suggest that hippocampal subfield radiomics can effectively stratify ZAP phases. Specifically, right CA4-DG radiomic features may serve as effective neuroimaging biomarkers associated with disease chronicity and have the potential for early risk stratification and intervention of ZAP.

papers.title: Functional connectivity and white matter microstructural alterations of thalamic subregions in benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
papers.authors: Yang K, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Li M, Yun Y, Xing J, Wang Y.
papers.abstract: Objective Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) is a common peripheral vestibular disorder. Although the thalamus serves as a key node in vestibular pathways, its role in the central regulation of BPPV remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the functional and structural alterations of thalamus in patients with BPPV. Methods The study recruited 52 BPPV patients and 52 age- and gender-matched healthy volunteers. Seed-based analysis was used to explore functional connectivity (FC) alterations between thalamic subregions and the whole brain in patient group. Probabilistic fiber tracking was then employed to analyze white matter structural differences in brain regions with functional alterations. Additionally, correlation analysis was conducted to investigate the relationship between abnormal imaging metrics and clinical scales. Results Compared to controls, patients with BPPV exhibited increased FC and higher fractional anisotropy (FA) values of some thalamic subregions to certain cerebral cortices. As a confirmatory finding, decreased FC but increased structural connectivity was displayed between the rostral temporal thalamus and cerebellum in BPPV. Furthermore, the FA value of the rostral temporal thalamus-cerebellar tract showed a correlation with the score of the impact of event scale. The mediation analysis showed emotional distress mediated the relationship between vertigo and FA of the rostral temporal thalamus-cerebellar tract. Conclusions In BPPV, the thalamic subregions and certain cerebral cortices exhibit synergistic functional and structural enhancement, whereas a distinct dissociation pattern is observed in the cerebellum. This differentiated reorganization may characterize the neural process in the early stage of BPPV.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨良性阵发性位置性眩晕患者丘脑亚区的功能连接与白质微结构改变，采用基于种子点的功能连接分析和概率纤维追踪，比较患者与年龄、性别匹配的健康对照。结果显示，患者部分丘脑亚区与特定大脑皮层的功能连接增强、各向异性分数升高，而丘脑前颞部与小脑之间则呈现功能连接下降但结构连接增强的分离模式；该纤维束的各向异性分数与事件影响量表得分相关，中介分析提示情绪困扰在眩晕与该指标之间起中介作用。作者据此认为，BPPV早期可能存在丘脑亚区与皮层功能结构协同增强、小脑呈分离性重组的分化性神经重组模式。

papers.title: Characteristics of visual search and prefrontal brain activity in individuals with autism spectrum disorder: functional near-infrared spectroscopy study.
papers.authors: Yano K, Yasumura A, Shin J, Nagai Y, Wada M.
papers.abstract: Introduction The term 'visual search' (VS) is used to describe behaviors such as finding a desired item while shopping or looking for a room key. These behaviors are important in everyday life. Individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have been reported to experience difficulties with VS. However, the characteristics of VS and the associated brain activity remain unclear. Therefore, we investigated these characteristics in detail using a measurement method that combined VS tasks with brain function measurements. Methods Twenty-one individuals with ASD and 42 typically developing (TD) individuals, matched for age and visual intelligence, participated in this study. The characteristics of VS were evaluated using two types of cancellation tasks: structured and random arrays. We evaluated VS performance using various measurements, including the rate of intersections and the best r, which reflect systematicity and directional constancy. We measured brain activity using functional near-infrared spectroscopy in the prefrontal cortex (PFC). Results The ASD group had a significantly higher rate of intersections and a significantly lower best r than the TD group. The right PFC activity was significantly higher than the activity in other PFC regions during the random array task in the TD group. Additionally, the TD group exhibited significantly higher right PFC activity than the ASD group. Conclusion These results suggest that VS in individuals with ASD is characterized by inconsistent search direction and disorganization and that patterns of PFC brain activity during VS may also differ from those observed in TD individuals.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注孤独症谱系障碍（ASD）个体的视觉搜索特征及其前额叶脑活动，采用结构化与随机阵列两种划消任务，并结合功能性近红外光谱测量前额叶活动，比较ASD个体与年龄和视觉智力匹配的典型发育者。结果显示，ASD组的搜索路径交叉率更高、方向恒常性指标更低，提示其搜索方向不一致、组织性较差；在随机阵列任务中，典型发育组右侧前额叶活动高于其他前额叶区域，也显著高于ASD组。作者据此认为，ASD个体的视觉搜索以方向不稳定和组织紊乱为特点，其前额叶活动模式也可能与典型发育者不同，但相关脑活动差异与行为表现之间的因果关系尚不明确。

papers.title: Multimodal evidence associated with 20Hz rTMS in AD: neuroaxonal injury reduction, neural oscillatory rebalancing, and multilayer network integration.
papers.authors: Wang T, Ji Y, Liu S, Wu H, Gu L, Guo M, Wang P, Xu G.
papers.abstract: High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has been demonstrated to enhance cognitive function in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the neurobiological mechanisms associated with neuroaxonal injury, neural oscillatory dynamics, and large-scale network reorganization remain unclear. In this study, we first conducted a randomized, sham-controlled trial with 16 patients with AD to evaluate the efficacy of DLPFC-targeted rTMS, followed by a single-arm multimodal cohort study of 30 patients to explore potential neurobiological mechanisms through cognitive assessments, blood biomarkers, EEG oscillatory activity, and multiplex brain network analysis. In Stage 1, the sham group showed no significant pre-post changes in MMSE or MoCA scores (MMSE: Z = -0.738, Cohen's r = 0.26; MoCA: Z =-0.853, Cohen's r = 0.30). The active rTMS group showed improvements in MMSE (Z = -2.124, Cohen's r = 0.75) and MoCA (Z = -2.108, Cohen's r = 0.75). In stage 2, rTMS was associated with improvements in MMSE (Z = -2.863, Cohen's r = 0.523) and MoCA (t = -6.137, Cohen's r = 0.752) scores. Biomarker analyses indicated a significant decrease in NfL concentrations (Z=-2.371, Cohen's r=0.484). EEG recordings revealed a decrease in delta power in the left temporal lobe (t=2.158, Cohen's r=0.372) and increases in beta power in the right parietal lobe and gamma power in the temporal lobe (beta: Z=-2.088, Cohen's r=0.381; gamma: Z=-2.129, Cohen's r=0.389). Network analysis showed reduced modularity and enhanced global efficiency across theta, alpha, and beta bands, accompanied by increased degree of overlap in frontal, parietal, and occipital regions. Importantly, MoCA improvement correlated with gamma-band global efficiency (R=0.389, P=0.034) and multilayer clustering coefficients in the left frontal and right occipital regions (R=0.478, P=0.008; R=0.398, P=0.029). Overall, rTMS exposure was associated with cognitive improvements in patients with AD, together with changes in neurodegeneration-related biomarkers and EEG network organization. These findings suggest that cognitive changes following rTMS may be associated with oscillatory modulation and large-scale network remodeling. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registration number: ChiCTR2500095949; Registration Date: 2025-01-15.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究以阿尔茨海默病患者为对象，先通过随机假对照试验评估靶向背外侧前额叶的高频rTMS对认知的效应，再用单臂多模态队列结合认知量表、血液标志物、脑电振荡和多层脑网络分析探讨相关神经生物学变化。结果显示，活性rTMS组认知评分改善而假刺激组未见明显变化；rTMS还与神经轴突损伤标志物NfL浓度下降、部分脑区振荡功率改变以及theta、alpha和beta频段网络模块化降低、全局效率提高相关。认知改善与gamma频段全局效率及部分区域多层聚类系数相关，提示rTMS后的认知变化可能与振荡调节和大规模网络重组有关，但相关结果不能说明因果关系。

papers.title: Diffusion MRI reveals stage-dependent microstructural responses to early ferroptosis inhibition in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
papers.authors: Tao J, Du R, Xiong J, Wang M, Cao Z, He G, Li Y, Zeng C.
papers.abstract: Background Neurodegeneration drives irreversible disability in multiple sclerosis (MS). Ferroptosis has been implicated in MS and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), but its spatiotemporal dynamics and imaging correlates remain unclear. Methods We combined 7.0 T diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) with histopathological and molecular analyses to evaluate the effects of Liproxstatin-1 (Lip-1) in mice with EAE induced by myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein peptide 35-55 (MOG35-55 ). Sixty-five female C57BL/6 mice were assigned to control, EAE, early-treatment (Early-Tx; Lip-1 from day 12), and late-treatment (Late-Tx; Lip-1 from day 18) groups. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and tissue analyses were performed at days 20 and 30 post-immunization. Results Early-Tx reduced clinical severity at day 30 (vs. EAE; p < 0.001) and limited body weight loss. At peak disease, voxel- and ROI-based DTI showed increased mean diffusivity and radial diffusivity in the corpus callosum, internal capsule, and thalamus, which were attenuated by Early-Tx. At the chronic stage, EAE showed persistent fractional anisotropy reduction in periventricular white matter and corpus callosum, whereas Early-Tx largely prevented these abnormalities. Histology demonstrated that Early-Tx suppressed inflammatory infiltration, microglial activation, and demyelination while preserving myelin integrity. Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) upregulation and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) downregulation preceded overt iron deposition, whereas iron accumulation emerged mainly at the chronic stage and colocalized with activated microglia and demyelinated lesions. Conclusions Ferroptosis-related molecular alterations are associated with stage-dependent inflammatory demyelinating injury in EAE. Early Lip-1 treatment provides greater microstructural protection than delayed treatment. High-field DTI sensitively detects treatment-responsive microstructural injury and may help monitor ferroptosis-related pathology in demyelinating disease.

papers.title: Visual-linguistic cues in manual communication: Neural and behavioral responses to Mouthings in sign-naïve perception.
papers.authors: Krebs J, Wilbur RB, Roehm D, Malaia EA.
papers.abstract: Gesture serves as a foundational modality for conveying event structure, providing critical visual information about transitivity and participant roles. Sign languages integrate manual (hand-based) and non-manual (face, torso, head) articulations to encode complex linguistic information. Among these, mouth movements provide phonological and lexical cues, but their role in sign-naïve individuals remains underexplored. This study investigates how sign-naïve individuals process non-manual markers (mouthings) in unfamiliar signed verbs, to explore how linguistic information is extracted from visual stimuli sharing properties with both gesture and sign language. Using EEG, we examined whether lip-reading functions as a linguistic cue or a general perceptual enhancement in non-signers viewing Austrian Sign Language (ÖGS) and non-ÖGS stimuli. Findings reveal distinct neural signatures for manual signs presented with and without congruent mouthings. An early posterior negativity followed by a late posterior positivity suggests that mouthings facilitate lexical access by providing phonological cues that activate stored lexical representations. Conversely, stimuli without mouthings elicited increased anterior activity, reflecting heightened cognitive control demands. Further, telic verbs, which inherently encode event endpoints, showed earlier and stronger facilitation from congruent mouthings compared to atelic verbs. These findings align with the Event Visibility Hypothesis and reinforce the role of visual cues in linguistic comprehension.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察从未学过手语的个体如何加工不熟悉手语动词中的口动线索，用脑电记录其观看奥地利手语及非手语刺激时的反应。结果显示，手动手势配合一致口动时出现早期后部负波和晚期后部正波，提示口动通过提供语音线索促进词汇通达；缺少口动则引起前部活动增强，反映认知控制需求上升。此外，有界动词比无界动词更早、更强地受益于一致口动，作者据此认为结果支持事件可见性假说，并强调视觉线索在语言理解中的作用。

papers.title: Cognitive reserve reconsidered: Asymmetry across proxies challenges a domain-general mechanism.
papers.authors: Paap KR, Majoubi J, Won JH.
papers.abstract: Cognitive reserve (CR) is a broad framework for explaining why individuals differ in cognitive functioning in the face of aging and neuropathology. One influential mechanistic account proposes that cognitively demanding life experiences such as education, occupational complexity, and cognitively stimulating activities augment a domain-general cognitive capacity that subsequently provides resilience. We refer to this more specific claim as cognitive reserve augmentation (CRA). This narrative and conceptual review evaluates the inferential strength of the evidence for CRA, emphasizing prospective cohort studies as the strongest available observational design for evaluating causal hypotheses. Across meta-analyses, several putative reserve-building experiences show consistent protective associations; however, comparison across prospective cohort studies reveals a striking asymmetry: whereas education, occupational complexity, and cognitively stimulating activities predict reduced risk or delayed clinical diagnosis of dementia, bilingualism-also proposed as a reserve-building cognitive experience-does not. This pattern constrains the assumption that diverse cognitive experiences augment a common reserve mechanism. Life-course evidence further indicates that associations between traditional CR proxies and later cognitive functioning can be substantially attenuated when earlier cognitive ability is measured directly. We argue that these findings are compatible with multiple pathways involving selection, correlated socioeconomic and health factors, domain-specific knowledge and expertise, processing efficiency, and effects on brain and physical health, as well as possible changes in cognitive capacity. Distinguishing among these alternatives requires specifying what experience is proposed to change, which experiences should and should not produce that change, and which outcomes would challenge the proposed mechanism. CR may therefore remain useful as a broad descriptive framework even when evidence for CRA or another specified reserve mechanism is incomplete.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述重新审视认知储备增强假说，即教育、职业复杂性和认知刺激活动等经历是否通过提升一般认知能力来提供韧性。作者比较前瞻性队列研究后发现明显不对称：教育、职业复杂性和认知刺激活动与痴呆风险降低或临床诊断延迟相关，而双语经验并无此关联；生命历程证据还显示，直接测量早期认知能力后，传统储备代理与后期认知功能的关联会明显减弱。作者认为这些结果可由选择、社会经济与健康因素、领域特定知识、加工效率及脑与身体健康等多条路径解释，因此认知储备仍可作为宽泛的描述框架，但支持特定增强机制的证据尚不完整。

papers.title: siRNA-Mediated RNF213 Depletion Aggravates Inflammatory Hypoxia-Induced Endothelial Dysfunction and Alters Endothelial-Smooth-Muscle Communication in an In Vitro Model Relevant to Moyamoya Disease.
papers.authors: Gao T, Zhao L, Wang L, Liu Z, Li C.
papers.abstract: Moyamoya disease is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder associated with variants in ring finger protein 213 (RNF213), endothelial dysfunction and pathological arterial remodelling. However, the relationship between reduced RNF213 abundance, inflammatory hypoxia and endothelial-smooth-muscle communication remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated RNF213 depletion in primary human brain microvascular endothelial cells exposed to combined hypoxia, tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) and interferon gamma (IFN-γ). Endothelial viability, proliferation, apoptosis, migration, angiogenic network formation and barrier integrity were evaluated. Conditioned-medium and indirect co-culture systems were subsequently used to examine responses in primary human brain vascular smooth muscle cells. Combined RNF213 depletion and inflammatory hypoxia reduced endothelial viability and proliferation, increased apoptosis, impaired migration and network formation, and compromised barrier integrity. Barrier impairment was demonstrated by decreased transendothelial electrical resistance, increased dextran permeability and disruption of vascular endothelial cadherin (VE-cadherin), zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), claudin-5 and occludin. RNF213 depletion also enhanced endothelial inflammatory activation. Conditioned medium from RNF213-depleted inflammatory-hypoxic endothelial cells was associated with increased smooth-muscle-cell proliferation, migration and colony formation. These responses were accompanied by reduced contractile-marker expression and increased secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), Krüppel-like factor 4 (KLF4), fibronectin 1 (FN1) and matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9), consistent with transition toward a synthetic, matrix-remodelling phenotype. The responsible endothelial-derived mediator or combination of mediators was not identified. Selected findings were reproduced using indirect co-culture and an independent siRNA targeting a different RNF213 sequence. These findings support an association between siRNA-mediated RNF213 depletion, endothelial stress susceptibility and altered endothelial-smooth-muscle communication in an in-vitro model relevant to Moyamoya disease. RNF213 re-expression or orthogonal genetic validation will be required to establish RNF213-specific causality.Clinical Trial Number None.

papers.title: Clinical utility of temporal subtraction imaging in head CT: a pictorial review.
papers.authors: Noguchi S, Sakamoto R, Fujimoto K, Yakami M, Emoto Y, Kubo T, Akasaka T, Arizono S, Nakamoto Y.
papers.abstract: Temporal subtraction (TS) imaging highlights interval changes by computing a voxel-wise difference between spatially registered serial CT examinations, converting side-by-side comparison into a single map of change. Although TS head CT has been validated for acute cerebral infarction detection, its application across the broader spectrum of intracranial pathologies has not been systematically described.We present a pictorial review of twelve clinical cases covering hemorrhagic, ischemic, vascular, neoplastic, and degenerative pathologies. TS imaging was particularly effective for lesions near the visual detection threshold, multi-focal interval findings, and bilateral symmetric changes. It also supported exclusion of new lesions in structurally complex backgrounds. Characteristic artifacts from source-image degradation, scanner protocol differences, and retained contrast are also illustrated.TS head CT is a broadly applicable reading aid with potential to improve diagnostic conspicuity across a wide range of intracranial pathologies. Awareness of characteristic artifacts is essential for accurate interpretation.

papers.title: The Multi-Faceted Nature of Limb Apraxia in Neurodegenerative Diseases: a Systematic Review.
papers.authors: Guézouli L, Roy V, Osiurak F, Baumard J.
papers.abstract: This systematic review aims to expand the characterization of apraxia in a spectrum of different neurodegenerative diseases and to explore associations between apraxia, on the one hand, and motor and cognitive disorders, on the other hand. 32 studies were included, representing a total of 430 patients with neurodegenerative diseases (n = 146 cases with CBS; n = 104 cases with SD; n = 66 cases with PD; n = 92 cases with bvFTD; n = 22 cases with PCA). The findings highlight that limb apraxia is multi-faceted in neurodegenerative diseases, as patients show polymorphic praxic performances depending on the cognitive disorders and the patterns of cortical or subcortical atrophy they exhibit. (1) According to a cortico-subcortical axis, patients with CBS are more impaired in gesture production than patients with PD. Whether gesture impairments met in PD are due to motor deficits or "true" apraxia remains an open issue. (2) According to a dorso-ventral axis, there is a double dissociation between gesture production that is better preserved in SD than in CBS, and semantic knowledge that is better preserved in CBS than in SD. (3) According to an antero-posterior axis, more data are needed to explore apraxia and its links with social and visual spatial skills in the behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia and in posterior cortical atrophy. Overall, our review emphasizes the need to adopt a process-based approach to better understand the nature of gesture impairments in each syndrome.

papers.title: Disease trajectory in cerebral amyloid angiopathy: a matter of time.
papers.authors: Zedde M, D'Agostino V, Pezzella FR, Lochner P, Piazza F, Catapano G, Pascarella R.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is a significant contributor to cerebrovascular disease, characterized by the deposition of amyloid-beta in the walls of cerebral small arteries and capillaries. This communication presents a detailed long-term follow-up of a 75-year-old female patient diagnosed with possible CAA in 2016, who demonstrated various clinical and neuroradiological manifestations over an 11-year period. Initial assessments revealed a right prerolandic hyperdense spontaneous convexal subarachnoid hemorrhage (cSAH) and a small vessel disease pattern on MRI. Subsequent imaging highlighted the progression of leptomeningeal involvement and cortical superficial siderosis (cSS), culminating in a lobar intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in 2026. This example shows the complexity and variability of CAA progression, underscoring different phenotypes and disease trajectories associated with CAA, and advocating for a nuanced understanding of its natural history to enhance personalized management strategies.

papers.title: Copy number variants across the developmental epilepsy-developmental and epileptic encephalopathy spectrum: an Indonesian case series.
papers.authors: Triono A, Gunadi, Herini ES.
papers.abstract: Developmental epilepsy (DE) and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) comprise neurodevelopmental disorders in which epilepsy occurs alongside developmental impairment of varying contributions from the underlying etiology and epileptic activity. Advances in genetic testing, including whole-exome sequencing (WES), whole-genome sequencing (WGS), and chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), have facilitated the identification of copy number variants (CNVs); however, data on CNV-associated epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders remain limited in Southeast Asia, including Indonesia. This retrospective case series describes the clinical and genetic characteristics of four Indonesian children across the DE-DEE spectrum with pathogenic CNVs identified at a tertiary referral hospital in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Among 48 patients who underwent WES, CNVs were identified in five; four underwent further genetic characterization and were included in this case series, while one patient died before additional testing could be performed. Clinical manifestations included early-onset seizures, developmental delay or intellectual impairment, and abnormal EEG and/or neuroimaging findings. Genetic findings included a 2q24.3 deletion involving SCN1A in a patient with Dravet syndrome and 15q11.2-q13.1 deletions involving UBE3A in three patients with clinical features of Angelman syndrome. Confirmatory testing using WGS or CMA further characterized the identified CNVs. This case series expands the clinical and molecular data on pathogenic CNVs associated with pediatric epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders in an underrepresented Southeast Asian population and illustrates the complementary roles of sequencing and chromosomal analysis in genetic diagnosis.
papers.summary_zh: 该病例系列报告了印度尼西亚日惹一家三级转诊医院中4名存在致病性拷贝数变异（CNV）的儿童，这些儿童处于发育性癫痫至发育性和癫痫性脑病谱系。在48名接受全外显子组测序的患者中检出5例CNV，其中4例进一步完成遗传学表征并纳入分析。临床表现包括早发性癫痫发作、发育迟缓或智力障碍，以及脑电图和/或神经影像异常；遗传学发现包括1例累及SCN1A的2q24.3缺失（Dravet综合征）和3例累及UBE3A的15q11.2-q13.1缺失（Angelman综合征临床特征），并通过全基因组测序或染色体微阵列分析进一步确认。作者认为，该系列补充了东南亚代表性不足人群中儿童癫痫与神经发育障碍相关致病性CNV的临床和分子资料，并说明测序与染色体分析在遗传诊断中具有互补作用。

papers.title: Cortical and trabecular deficits in patients with recent hip fractures assessed by DXA and 3D-DXA.
papers.authors: Ramírez Stieben LA, Brance ML, Di Gregorio S, Pardo SM, Ortuño PS, Del Río Barquero L, Lombarte M, Brun LR.
papers.journal: Journal of bone and mineral metabolism
papers.abstract: Introduction Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is the standard for osteoporosis assessment, but areal BMD (aBMD) does not fully capture volumetric or microstructural deficits associated with hip fractures. We aimed to characterize cortical and trabecular parameters using 3D-DXA in patients with hip fractures and assess whether these measures improve discrimination of prevalent fracture status beyond aBMD. Material and methods Descriptive analyses included 499 individuals: femoral neck fractures (FNfx, n=110), intertrochanteric fractures (ITfx, n=123), and controls (n=266). Patients were assessed within 15 days of fracture at the contralateral hip. DXA and 3D-DXA provided trabecular volumetric BMD (vBMD), cortical surface BMD (sBMD), and cortical thickness. TBS and FRAX were evaluated descriptively but excluded from penalized models. LASSO models were evaluated in 515 unique participants with complete predictor data. Results Among fractured patients, 51% did not meet densitometric criteria for osteoporosis. In the low bone mass subgroup, fractured individuals showed lower trabecular vBMD, whereas osteoporotic subjects also exhibited reduced cortical sBMD. Exploratory comparisons suggested lower trochanteric trabecular measures in ITfx and lower femoral neck cortical thickness in FNfx, although most differences occurred between fracture groups and controls. Total hip aBMD alone yielded an AUC of 0.646. The LASSO λmin model improved discrimination modestly (AUC 0.692; p<0.001), while the λ1se model achieved an AUC of 0.663 (p=0.034). Conclusion 3D-DXA identified cortical and trabecular deficits in patients with recent hip fractures, including those without densitometric osteoporosis, and provided complementary structural information beyond aBMD. However, the improvement in discrimination was modest and requires prospective external validation.

papers.title: Twenty-five years of progress in Parkinson's disease research: from dopamine replacement to biological definition and regenerative therapy.
papers.authors: Winkler J.
papers.abstract: The first quarter of the twenty-first century has transformed Parkinson's disease (PD) from a predominantly motor, dopamine-deficiency syndrome into a heterogeneous multisystem disorder defined across clinical, genetic and molecular dimensions. This overview follows the trajectory of these advances from the historical foundations established prior 2000 to present concepts of prodromal disease, progression, biological classification and precision medicine. Epidemiological work has established PD as the fastest-growing major neurological disorder, while systematic characterization of non-motor symptoms has shifted diagnosis and attention beyond the nigrostriatal system in PD research. Imaging has progressed from exclusionary structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to quantitative susceptibility, diffusion and molecular approaches, although no single imaging biomarker yet provides a stand-alone diagnosis of PD. The discovery of α-synuclein gene mutations and its presence as protein in Lewy bodies and neurites connected genetics, protein aggregation and selective neuronal vulnerability. Seed amplification assays (SAA) now enable robust detection of pathological α-synuclein in cerebrospinal fluid and have catalysed biologically anchored staging proposals. At the same time, negative phase 2 antibody against α-synuclein trials illustrate the challenges of target engagement, disease heterogeneity and intervention timing. Genetics and cell biology have placed lysosomal proteostasis, in particular glucocerebrosidase 1 (GBA1) dependent pathways, at the center of disease-modification strategies. Dopaminergic therapy remains extraordinarily effective symptomatically, with continuous delivery systems extending its utility for intermediate and late stages of the disease, whereas cell replacement has re-entered clinical development through standardized pluripotent-stem-cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic progenitors. The next phase of PD research will depend less on a single unifying mechanism than on integrating molecular state, the pattern of neuronal injury, clinical phenotype and individual trajectory to select the right intervention at the right biological stage.

papers.title: Impact of clinical risk factors on white matter microstructure in preterm-born infants: investigation with diffusion MRI and tractography at term-equivalent age.
papers.authors: Devisscher L, Leprince Y, Biran V, Elbaz N, Ghozland C, Adibpour P, Chiron C, Neumane S, Gonzalez Carpinteiro A, Elmaleh-Bergès M, Hertz-Pannier L, Héneau A, Barbu-Roth M, Alison M, Dubois J.
papers.abstract: Premature birth occurs during a phase of intense brain maturation, making white matter (WM) particularly vulnerable to injury. Beyond major lesions, subtle and widespread microstructural alterations also contribute to later neurodevelopmental impairments. We aimed to characterize the impact of key clinical risk factors on global and tract-specific WM microstructure at term-equivalent age (TEA), using 3T-diffusion-MRI data of 111 infants born before 33 weeks of gestation. We implemented a tractography pipeline adapted for use in infants with heterogeneous brain anatomy, including macroscopic abnormalities and lesions, and extracted diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics in sensorimotor tracts: corticospinal tract (CST), superior thalamic radiation (STR), frontal aslant tract (FAT), forceps minor (FMI) and middle cerebellar peduncle (MCP). Associations with risk factors were assessed accounting for age at MRI or global WM microstructure. Tractography succeeded in most infants despite marked anatomical variability and/or overt lesions. Being a male, small for gestational age (SGA) at birth, encountering sepsis and having severe Kidokoro radiological score for WM were associated with altered global WM metrics. At the tract level, CST and STR showed the strongest susceptibility to SGA, prolonged parenteral nutrition, and Kidokoro score. In contrast, associations after adjustment for global WM microstructure suggested that FAT might be less vulnerable than other tracts to extreme prematurity, SGA and invasive ventilation. Findings were partially replicated in infants without macroscopic abnormalities, supporting the presence of WM dysmaturation even in the absence of visible injury. DTI metrics thus provide tract-specific biomarkers of early WM microstructure in preterm infants, which are sensitive to risk factors and could inform targeted prevention and intervention.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注早产儿在矫正胎龄足月时，关键临床风险因素如何影响整体及特定白质纤维束的微结构。作者对111名胎龄不足33周的早产儿进行3T扩散MRI和适用于婴儿解剖变异的纤维束成像，提取感觉运动通路的弥散张量指标，并分析其与风险因素的关联。结果显示，男性、出生时小于胎龄、败血症及较重的Kidokoro白质影像评分与整体白质指标改变相关；皮质脊髓束和丘脑上辐射对小于胎龄、长期肠外营养和Kidokoro评分尤为敏感，而额斜束在调整整体白质微结构后似乎较不易受极端早产等因素影响。部分结果在无宏观异常的婴儿中重复，提示即使未见明显损伤也可能存在白质发育异常，这些指标有望作为早期风险分层依据。

papers.title: HARP: HARmonizing In-Vivo Single-Shell Diffusion MRI Using Phantom-Only Training.
papers.authors: Jeong H, Liu Q, Keenan KE, Wilde EA, Schneider W, Pathak S, Zuccolotto A, O'Donnell LJ, Ning L, Rathi Y.
papers.abstract: Purpose Combining multi-site diffusion MRI (dMRI) data is hindered by inter-scanner variability, which confounds subsequent analysis. Previous harmonization methods require large, matched or traveling human subjects from multiple sites, which are impractical to acquire in many situations. This study aims to develop a deep learning-based dMRI harmonization framework that eliminates the reliance on multi-site in-vivo traveling human data for training. Methods HARP employs a voxel-wise 1D neural network trained on an easily transportable diffusion phantom. The model learns relationships between spherical harmonics coefficients of different sites without memorizing spatial structures. Results HARP reduced inter-scanner variability levels significantly in various measures. Quantitatively, it decreased inter-scanner variability as measured by standard error in FA (12%), MD (10%), and GFA (30%) with scan-rescan standard error as the baseline, while preserving fiber orientations and tractography after harmonization. Conclusion We believe that HARP represents an important first step toward dMRI harmonization using only phantom data, thereby obviating the need for complex, matched in vivo multi-site cohorts. This phantom-only strategy substantially enhances the feasibility and scalability of quantitative dMRI for large-scale clinical studies.

papers.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Findings and Demographics Predict Surgical Versus Nonoperative Management of Rotator Cuff Injuries: A Natural Language Processing Analysis.
papers.authors: Keeley TS, Halvorson RT, Niknam K, Ziegeler K, Feeley BT, Link T, Majumdar S, Lansdown DA.
papers.journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
papers.abstract: Purpose To identify pathologic and demographic predictors of treatment selection and timing in patients with rotator cuff injuries using natural language processing of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reports. Methods Data were retrospectively reviewed in our institution's Information Commons database. Adult patients who underwent shoulder MRI within 30 days of rotator cuff injury diagnosis (1996-2023) were identified using International Classification of Diseases codes and categorized by treatment. A Generative Pre-Transformer-4 model analyzed MRI reports using a reference list of shoulder pathologies, with validation against a human reference for 50 reports. χ2 tests evaluated differences in shoulder pathology across treatment groups. Logistic regressions identified predictors of surgery-overall, as initial treatment, and after an initial trial of conservative management-while controlling for age, sex, insurance, race, and other imaging findings. Results A total of 3555 patients were identified, of whom 1139 underwent surgery. Natural language processing achieved 93.9% sensitivity and 99.3% specificity. Full-thickness supraspinatus tears predicted surgery overall (odds ratio [OR] 3.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.54-4.17, P < .001) and after an initial trial of conservative management (OR 3.14; 95% CI, 2.23-4.41, P < .001). Full-thickness subscapularis tears also predicted surgery overall (OR 1.74; 95% CI, 1.14-2.66, P = .011). Female sex decreased the odds of surgery (OR 0.76; 95% CI 0.64-0.90, P = .001). No differences in surgical likelihood were observed by race (P = .272-.986) or between Medicare and private insurance (P = .735). Conclusions MRI findings and demographics were associated with treatment selection and timing for patients with rotator cuff injuries. Natural language processing analysis of MRI reports enabled the identification of pathologic treatment predictors. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective prognostic cohort study.

papers.title: A robust adversarial learning framework for EEG emotion recognition
papers.authors: Yang H, Chen L, Gao J, Zhang J, Zhang J.

papers.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain.
papers.authors: Fodor J, Murawski C, Suzuki S.
papers.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other semantic models to brain activity in language regions of interest. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformers poorly match human brain representations of sentences that require sensitivity to structural relations such as semantic roles (who did what to whom). Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究用7T fMRI考察Transformer类大语言模型表征句子意义的方式是否与人脑相似，通过分离句子结构与词义，比较了多种模型与人脑语言区表征的对应关系。结果显示，Transformer模型虽优于完全忽略词序的模型，但在需要把握语义角色等结构关系时，其与人脑句子表征的匹配普遍较差，且明显不如显式编码词间结构关系的模型。作者据此强调句子结构在人脑句子意义表征中的关键作用，并对Transformer能类人地表征句义这一说法提出质疑。

papers.title: Mapping the topographic organization of the human zona incerta using diffusion MRI.
papers.authors: Haast RAM, Kai J, Taha A, Liu V, Kasa LW, Gilmore G, Guye M, Khan AR, Lau JC.
papers.abstract: The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an 'immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said'. Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. Using in vivo diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and data-driven connectivity, we identify a topographic organization between the ZI and neocortex. Specifically, our methods identify a rostral-caudal gradient predominantly connecting the frontopolar and ventral prefrontal cortices with the rostral ZI, and the primary sensorimotor cortices with the caudal ZI. Moreover, we demonstrate how clustering and gradient approaches build complementary evidence including facilitating the mapping of a central region of the ZI, connected with the dorsal prefrontal cortex. These results were shown to be replicable across multiple datasets and at the individual subject level, building evidence for the important role of the ZI in mediating frontal lobe-associated tasks, ranging from motor to cognitive to emotional control. Finally, we consider the impact of this topographic organization on the refinement of neuromodulatory targets. These results pave the way for an increasingly detailed understanding of ZI substructures, and considerations for in vivo targeting of the ZI for neuromodulation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究利用在体扩散磁共振成像和数据驱动的连接分析，考察人类未定带与大脑皮层之间的拓扑组织方式。结果显示，未定带与皮层连接呈现由前到后的梯度：前部未定带主要与额极和腹侧前额叶皮层相连，后部未定带主要与初级感觉运动皮层相连；聚类与梯度方法还共同刻画出一个与背侧前额叶皮层相连的中央区域。这些结果在多个数据集和个体水平上可重复，提示未定带可能参与从运动到认知、情绪控制的额叶相关功能，并为神经调控靶点的细化提供依据。

papers.title: Pediatric brain charts reveal ADHD biotypes with distinct developmental, molecular, and therapeutic profiles
papers.authors: Bu X, Sun L, Fu Z, Zhao Y, Zheng X, Zhang K, Liang X, Cui Z, Gao J, Gong G, Huang R, Li S, Luo L, Men W, Peng Y, Sun L, Sun X, Wang X, Xia M, Zhao T, Zhu L, Zuo X, Wang Y, Dong Q, Cao Q, Yang L, He Y.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) exhibits profound clinical heterogeneity; however, its underlying neurobiological substrates remain unclear. Here, leveraging large-scale structural magnetic resonance imaging data from 12,663 typically developing children and 1,699 children with ADHD across Chinese and United States cohorts, we construct population-specific pediatric brain charts via hierarchical Bayesian normative modeling to quantify individual deviations in cortical morphology. Data-driven clustering identifies two robust, cross-ethnically replicable ADHD biotypes: an infra-normal biotype characterized by widespread cortical thinning and a supra-normal biotype marked by cortical thickening. Multivariate analyses reveal distinct brain–behavior architectures: cortical deviations correlate preferentially with symptom severity in the infra-normal biotype but with both symptom severity and cognitive performance in the supranormal biotype. Clinically, the infra-normal biotype demonstrates a superior response to methylphenidate over atomoxetine, whereas the supra-normal biotype responds comparably to both. Transcriptomic analyses identify biotype-specific molecular signatures converging with ADHD genome-wide association study (GWAS) risk loci but exhibiting distinct expression patterns in the brain. These findings classify ADHD heterogeneity into neurobiologically distinct, clinically informed biotypes, providing a mechanistic framework for precision psychiatry in pediatric ADHD.

papers.title: Slow Ionic Dynamics Reshape Bistability in a Biophysical Mean-Field Model of Brain Activity
papers.authors: Chatterjee S, Maschke C, Petkoski S, Wang H, Depannemaecker D, Jirsa V.
papers.abstract: Brain states such as sleep, seizures, and resting wakefulness are often described in terms of transitions between distinct population states. Biophysically inspired mean-field models that couple neuronal firing statistics to slow ionic homeostasis provide a mechanistic bridge between detailed single-neuron physiology and macroscopic brain activity. Here we examine this issue in a biophysical meanfield model of cortical populations driven by potassium exchange and compare its dynamical repertoire with a matched spiking network across six physiological and pathological regimes. The fast subsystem contains a substantial region in which low- and high-activity fixed points coexist, but this conditional bistability is not inherited by the physiological resting branch of the complete slow-fast system. A generic fast-slow calculation identifies how feedback through a dynamical ionic variable changes the stability conditions of the fast subsystem, and an exact equilibrium reduction of the KIonEx-MF equations yields a single equilibrium on the physiological resting branch over the range examined. This resting state is excitable: perturbations generate intermittent synchronized events in both the mean-field and spiking-network descriptions. The results show how slow ionic dynamics can reshape conclusions drawn from a frozen fast subsystem and provide noise-driven excitability as an alternative route to spontaneous population transitions.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究以受钾交换驱动的皮层群体生物物理平均场模型为对象，并将其动力学行为与匹配的脉冲神经网络在多种生理和病理条件下进行比较。结果显示，尽管快速子系统存在低活动与高活动不动点共存的条件性双稳区，但完整慢-快系统的生理静息分支并未继承这一双稳性；对模型的平衡态约化在考察范围内只给出单一平衡点。作者指出，静息态具有可兴奋性，扰动会在平均场和脉冲网络描述中引发间歇性同步事件，提示慢离子动力学可改变仅依据冻结快速子系统得出的结论，而噪声驱动的可兴奋性可能是自发群体状态转换的另一条途径。

papers.title: The Concise Language Paradigm in left and right hemisphere stroke: a longitudinal source-localized EEG study
papers.authors: Roos NM, Oostenveld R, Piastra MC, Tuladhar AM, Ruiter MB, Kessels RP, Westner BU, Piai V.
papers.abstract: Language recovery after stroke can be supported by neuroplasticity, but its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Most previous studies have either focused on language comprehension or production and/or relied on hemodynamic measures, with limited complementary electrophysiological evidence. Here, we combined a paradigm assessing comprehension and production with individualized electroencephalography (EEG) source reconstruction to investigate post-stroke language function and changes in hemispheric dominance over time. We tested 31 participants: 13 stroke-free controls, 8 individuals with left hemisphere (LH), and 10 with right hemisphere (RH) stroke in the middle cerebral artery territory. Participants with stroke were assessed approximately two and seven months post-stroke. We employed the Concise Language Paradigm (CLaP), which combines auditory sentence comprehension with picture naming, in addition to standardized neuropsychological tests. EEG data were analyzed using event-related potentials and time-frequency representations, followed by source reconstruction based on individual MRI-derived forward models. Laterality indices were calculated to assess changes in hemispheric dominance between sessions. Behaviorally, the LH group showed low performance at two months followed by overall improvement, whereas the RH group mainly improved in visuospatial memory and functional communication. EEG activity was significantly modulated by task condition across comprehension and production contrasts. Source-level results in controls were consistent with established language-related networks, serving as regions of interest for the stroke analyses. In the stroke groups, hemispheric dominance differed between LH and RH stroke participants. Notably, several LH participants shifted from left-to right-hemisphere dominance between sessions, whereas those initially showing right-hemisphere dominance remained stable. Our study provides evidence on comprehension and production performance after stroke using a single paradigm. These findings demonstrate dynamic changes in hemispheric dominance during post-stroke recovery, ultimately highlighting the value of individualized EEG source reconstruction to investigate post-stroke plasticity.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注卒中后语言功能恢复及大脑半球优势随时间的变化，将同时评估语言理解与产出的简明语言范式与个体化脑电源定位EEG结合，在卒中后两个月和七个月两个时间点比较左、右半球卒中患者，并以无卒中对照者的源定位结果作为语言相关网络参考。行为上，左半球卒中组初期表现较差但随后整体改善，右半球卒中组主要在功能性交流方面改善；源水平上，两组的半球优势存在差异，左半球卒中者多出现从左半球优势向右半球优势的系统性转移，若两个月时尚未右偏则尤为明显。作者据此强调个体化EEG源重建对研究卒中后可塑性的价值，但结果来自小样本纵向观察，尚不能直接推及临床康复效果。

papers.title: Endogenous retrovirus activation disrupts postsynaptic organization in human glutamatergic neurons
papers.authors: Davis-Hansson C, Garza R, Piochon C, Johansson JG, Busskamp V, Jakobsson J, Johansson EM.
papers.abstract: Endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) comprise a substantial fraction of the human genome, yet whether their expression can directly alter human neuronal function remains unknown. Because glutamatergic signaling is fundamental to brain function and frequently disrupted in brain disorders, we asked whether activation of the primate-specific ERV-W group, associated with neurological disease, perturbs human glutamatergic neurons. We used CRISPR activation of the LTR17-ERV-W consensus sequence to examine its effects on neuronal and synaptic function, inducing transcription from multiple proviral loci, including five with intact open reading frames. Functionally, ERV-W activation selectively altered the postsynaptic compartment, reducing PSD-95 and NMDA receptor abundance. These changes were accompanied by altered excitatory synaptic transmission and reduced intrinsic excitability, whereas activation of ERVW-1/Syncytin-1 alone did not reproduce the phenotype. Our findings identify ERV-W activation as a modulator of human neuronal function with potential relevance to ERV-associated brain disorders.

papers.title: Unstable word form representations and greater reliance on right hemisphere during word learning in adults with a history of developmental language disorder
papers.authors: Nora A, Yan C, Husa V, Wilkki V, van Vliet M, Service E, Salmelin R.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Impairment in acquiring new vocabulary is a persistent deficit in developmental language disorder (DLD), but its cortical substrates remain unclear. We investigated learning of new words in young adults with DLD and typically developing (TD) control participants using magnetoencephalography (MEG). Participants were exposed to spoken real words and two sets of pseudowords, with shared beginnings, in two MEG sessions. One set of pseudowords was actively trained for three days, paired with fantasy animal pictures. Both groups learned new pseudowords, but adults with DLD recalled fewer items and confused similar sounding pseudowords more often than TD adults. MEG recordings revealed robust left temporal learning effects in both groups, along with left inferior frontal involvement. The DLD group additionally showed stronger right-hemispheric involvement and a significant right temporal learning effect for the newly learned words. Furthermore, only the DLD group showed changes in the left and right temporal responses for the real words after the learning phase, indicating altered lexical access for familiar words after integration of new word forms with overlapping phonology into the mental lexicon.
