A no-MHC student trained with the same full distillation objective achieved essentially the same Dice (0.9141 ± 0.0021) with lower HD95 and lower measured latency, indicating that the full distillation objective, rather than the MHC block alone, explained most of the performance recovery toward the teacher. Replication on the 2026 Medical Lumbar Spine 3D Axial MRI Dataset achieved Dice 0.8960 ± 0.0032 and IoU 0.8224 ± 0.0047. A fixed label-harmonized train-on-primary/test-on-2026 transfer stress test achieved macro Dice 0.7002 ± 0.0181 and foreground Dice 0.6280 ± 0.0225. The results suggest that compact class-aware distillation can support reproducible lumbar MRI segmentation for future computer-aided measurement pipelines, while prospective and strict cross-institutional validation remain necessary.

papers.title: Correction-stage information leakage and target-input asymmetry can distort comparisons of fNIRS short-separation channel correction strategies.
papers.authors: Suzen E.
papers.abstract: Objective We examined how evaluation design affects comparisons of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) short-separation correction strategies. Approach Nearest-SC, All-SC, SC-PCA and an adapted tCCA-GLM were compared in a multimodal resting-state dataset (n = 14), using semi-nested and correction-stage fully nested cross-validation, boundary purging, symmetric leave-one-modality-out (LOMO) evaluation, circular-shift nulls, injected hemodynamic response function (HRF) recovery and a second cohort. Main results In an initial joint-target diagnostic analysis, the adapted tCCA-GLM's absolute out-of-fold R² increased by 42.7 percentage points from semi-nested to purged fully nested evaluation. In a separate fixed-seed purged analysis, its null-adjusted ΔR² was -1.1%. Symmetric LOMO, which evaluates reduced tCCA models, yielded no statistically detected method differences (all paired p ≥ 0.3685), but did not establish equivalence or separately quantify leakage and input-target overlap. Motion-targeted external validation provided partial support for an evaluation-tier × method interaction (Freedman-Lane p < 0.005). SC-PCA had lower mean known-truth normalized root mean square error (nRMSE = 0.037) than the adapted tCCA-GLM (0.121); within-metric Holm-adjusted comparisons were significant for this contrast and for amplitude-bias comparisons with all three SC-based strategies, but not for slopes. Sensitivity analyses included training-fold PCA selection, LOMO boundary/segment-filtering checks, lagged evaluation and longer test blocks. Significance Benchmarks should fit learned correction stages within training data, disclose correction-evaluation overlap and assess signal preservation separately. Findings are specific to the evaluated implementations, outcomes and datasets; the sensitivity analyses do not establish complete removal of preprocessing-related dependence.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察评估设计如何影响fNIRS短距离通道校正策略的比较，在静息态多模态数据中对比了Nearest-SC、All-SC、SC-PCA与改编tCCA-GLM，并采用不同交叉验证方案、对称留一模态评估、零分布检验和注入血流动力学响应恢复等手段。结果显示，评估流程本身会明显改变方法表现：改编tCCA-GLM在未充分嵌套的评估下R²偏高，而在校正阶段完全嵌套并清除边界后，其零校正ΔR²接近零；对称留一模态评估未检出方法间差异，但作者强调这并不等于方法等价，也未分别量化信息泄漏与输入-目标重叠。SC-PCA在已知真值误差上优于改编tCCA-GLM。作者据此建议将学习型校正步骤纳入训练数据内、披露校正与评估的重叠，并单独评估信号保留；结论限于所考察的实现、结局和数据集。

papers.title: The gut-brain axis in Binge Eating Disorder: From microbial dysbiosis to vagal dysfunction and therapeutic intervention.
papers.authors: Rossetti C, Aeschlimann L, Praz L, Boutrel B.
papers.abstract: Binge Eating Disorder (BED), the most prevalent eating disorder worldwide, is characterized by recurrent episodes of uncontrolled food intake accompanied by marked psychological distress in the absence of regular compensatory behaviors. While behavioral and neurobiological frameworks have traditionally dominated research, converging evidence now positions the gut microbiota as a critical mediator of BED pathophysiology through bidirectional microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) communication. This review synthesizes current knowledge of gut microbial remodeling in BED, elucidating how compositional alterations contribute to pathogenesis through disrupted satiety signaling, altered neurotransmitter metabolism, immune-inflammatory cascades, and vagal dysfunction. Recent evidence highlights BED-specific depletion of fermentative taxa, including Pediococcus , Catenibacterium , and Megasphaera , with depletion of Pediococcus correlated with reduced cardiac vagal tone. The mechanistic landscape encompasses short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-mediated appetite modulation, α -MSH mimicry by bacterial caseinolytic protease B, serotonin and GABA pathways, and immune activation via lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Emerging microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategies, including prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), are critically evaluated in light of current evidence from BED and related eating disorders. Despite the promising mechanistic rationale, rigorous clinical trials remain scarce. This review highlights several priorities for future research, and the development of precision medicine strategies integrating established therapeutic approaches with emerging microbiota-targeted interventions.

papers.title: Proposed Role of Prenatal Nicotine Exposure Induced TNF-α Signaling as an Upstream Contributor of Neurodegenerative Diseases: A Systematic Review.
papers.authors: Delgado M, Roja A, Pareek O, Penman SL, Smith D, Thanos PK.
papers.abstract: Background Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) regulates immune responses, neuroinflammatory signaling, and central nervous system (CNS) homeostasis. While physiological TNF-α signaling contributes to normal brain function, dysregulation of this pathway has been implicated in chronic neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative disease progression. Prenatal nicotine exposure (PNE) has been associated with persistent alterations in neuroimmune function, including microglial activationand disruption of TNF-α signaling pathways, potentially contributing to long-term neurological dysfunction. Methods A PubMed literature search was conducted using terms related to prenatal/maternal nicotine exposure, TNF-α, neuroinflammation, microglia, and neurodegenerative disease, following PRISMA guidelines. Peer-reviewed English-language studies published after 1985 that met predefined inclusion criteria were selected, yielding 134 articles. Results Preclinical and clinical studies indicate that PNE alters neuroimmune homeostasis through changes in inflammatory signaling, microglial function, and TNFR1/TNFR2-associated mechanisms. Dysregulated TNF-α signaling emerged as a shared feature across multiple neurodgenerative disorders, contributing to disease progression through distinct yet overlapping mechanisms involving neuroimmune dysfunction and chronic inflammatory signaling. Direct evidence connecting PNE-induced TNF-α dysregulation to the onset of these specific diseases, however, remains limited. Conclusion Current evidence supports a potential link between PNE and TNF-α-mediated neuroinflammation. Further research is needed to clarify the proposed underlying mechanisms connecting early-life nicotine exposure to long-term neurodegenerative risk, as well as their broader clinical and public health implications.

papers.title: Action features dominate cortical representation during natural vision.
papers.authors: Jung H, Jain H, Han X, Feilong M, Han J, Shokeen D, Van Uden C, Hanson I, Connolly AC, Wager TD, Haxby JV, Nastase SA.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Cortical resources are allocated into systems specialized for processing ecologically relevant features of the world. These features are typically studied in isolation using controlled experimental stimuli, making it difficult to assess the relative importance of different kinds of features that tend to overlap during natural vision. In the current study, we evaluated the relative contributions of action, agent, and scene features in predicting cortical activity while participants viewed a 1-h nature documentary. We tested four sets of model features: semantic vectors capturing the observed action, agent, and scene features derived from an annotation of the stimulus, as well as low-level visual motion-energy features. We used banded ridge regression to fit vertex-wise encoding models from the combination of all four sets of features. While each set of features predicted neural activity in the expected areas, the action features predicted more widespread activity. A variance partitioning analysis revealed that the action features captured the most unique variance in neural activity across a much larger extent of cortex than the agent or scene features. Our findings suggest that cortical activity during dynamic, natural vision is dominated by features for understanding the actions of others.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注自然观看动态影像时，动作、行动者与场景等特征对皮层活动的相对贡献。研究者让被试观看一段自然纪录片，用标注提取动作、行动者和场景的语义特征，并结合低层视觉运动能量特征，以带状岭回归构建逐顶点编码模型。结果显示，各类特征都能预测其预期区域的活动，但动作特征预测的范围更广；方差分解进一步表明，动作特征在更大范围皮层上捕获了最多的独特方差。作者据此认为，动态自然视觉下的皮层活动主要由理解他人动作的特征所主导。

papers.title: Generalizable neural decoding for clinically scalable brain-computer interfaces.
papers.authors: Gu Y, Yin H, Wang Y, Woon YQ, Wang Y, Teng M, Lu C, Lu Z, Chen J.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces promise restored communication and movement, yet accuracy achieved under development rarely survives new sessions, users, tasks, or hardware. Generalization, not peak performance, determines clinical scalability. Here we examine generalizable neural decoding from development to deployment, organized by the domain held out at evaluation, target-data access, adaptation strategy, and the clinical conditions under which performance persists, identifying benchmarking standards, prospective validation, and hardware-algorithm co-design as prerequisites for durable benefit.

papers.title: A review of self-supervised imaging phenotypes for genome-wide association studies.
papers.authors: Patel K, Zhao X, Xie Z, Zhi D.
papers.abstract: Biobank-scale imaging-genomic cohorts enable genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of organ structure and function. Traditional approaches rely on expert-defined image-derived phenotypes (IDPs), which capture only a fraction of the biological variation in high-content images. Powered by artificial intelligence, self-supervised learning (SSL) learns representations directly from intrinsic image structures, creating scalable, data-driven traits. Here, we review the technical frameworks and challenges of SSL-based imaging genetics and their applications in brain MRI, cardiac MRI, and retinal imaging. Early studies suggest that these data-driven approaches can complement traditional IDPs and may expand the phenotypic space available for discovery of heritable imaging traits, although broader validation across cohorts, ancestries, scanners, and imaging protocols remains needed.

papers.title: The non-inflammatory effect of neuronal NLRP3 on spatial memory after traumatic brain injury.
papers.authors: Tan SW, Xie Q, Zhang J, Li P, Ning YL, Yang N, Wang B, Peng Y, Chen X, Gao RB, Li CH, Du H, Zhou YG, Zhao Y.
papers.abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome has emerged as a critical regulator in neuroinflammatory responses to various brain insults from traumatic, ischemic and neurodegenerative conditions, an effect almost exclusively attributed to microglial NLRP3. Here, we demonstrated that in the absence of changes in inflammatory factors IL-18, IL-1β and TNF-α, neuronal Nlrp3 knockout in hippocampus (nNlrp3-/- ) improved long-term spatial memory performance, with increased synaptic proteins levels and enhanced amplitude of long-term potentiation at 4 weeks after traumatic brain injury (TBI), compared to wildtype littermates. Notably, the nNlrp3-/- mice out-performed microglia-specific knockout and global Nlrp3 knockout mice in cognition and synaptic function. We further identified that NLRP3 structurally and functionally directly interacted with the R1 subunit of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NR1) in hippocampus after TBI. Accordingly, pharmacological inhibition of NLRP3 by MCC950 rescued the decrease in the NMDAR-gated calcium influx by LPS-stimulated hippocampal neurons while selective Nlrp3 knockout in hippocampal neurons partially reversed the decreased phosphorylation level of NR1 after TBI. Collectively, this study provides the first evidence that neuronal NLRP3 constitutes a non-inflammatory response to control synaptic plasticity and cognitive function via NR1-dependent non-inflammatory mechanism in TBI and thus broadens the central role of NLRP3 in neuronal adaptive mechanisms to include both microglial NLRP3-inflammation arm and the neuronal NLRP3-synaptic plasticity arm.

papers.title: Multimodal associations between posterior hippocampus glutamate metabolism, visual cortex connectivity, and intrusive trauma reexperiencing symptoms.
papers.authors: Clancy KJ, Chen X, Song X, Song T, Zhou S, Akman E, Ostrand C, Ren B, Du F, Rosso IM.
papers.abstract: Hippocampal dysfunction is implicated in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), particularly intrusive reexperiencing symptoms, and may be mediated by glutamatergic excitotoxicity. Markers of glutamate dysfunction (higher glutamate to N-acetyl aspartate levels; Glu/NAA) in the hippocampus (HPC) have been linked to reexperiencing symptoms. However, the HPC demonstrates heterogeneity along its anterior-posterior axis, with different functional connectivity patterns and PTSD symptom associations, motivating investigations into glutamate metabolism in anterior and posterior HPC subregions (a/pHPC). To this end, 121 symptomatic trauma-exposed adults with current trauma reexperiencing symptoms completed magnetic resonance spectroscopy and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging to examine the regional specificity of HPC Glu/NAA associations with reexperiencing symptoms and the link to a/pHPC functional connectivity. PTSD symptoms were assessed with the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5. Reexperiencing symptom severity was associated with greater Glu/NAA in the pHPC, but not aHPC. pHPC Glu/NAA was further linked to stronger functional connectivity between the pHPC and visual cortex (VC), which in turn correlated with more severe reexperiencing symptoms. This strengthened pHPC-VC connectivity explained the shared variance between pHPC Glu/NAA and reexperiencing severity, suggesting dysregulated glutamate metabolism in the pHPC may contribute to reexperiencing symptoms through functional connectivity with the VC. These findings replicate prior work linking HPC Glu/NAA to trauma reexperiencing symptoms and provide novel evidence of this association in the pHPC, but not aHPC, which is mediated by its functional connectivity with the VC. This multimodal investigation supports translational models of glutamatergic dysfunction in trauma-related disorders and highlights new targets for pharmacological and neuromodulatory interventions.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在有创伤再体验症状的创伤暴露成人中，结合磁共振波谱与静息态功能磁共振成像，考察海马谷氨酸代谢与再体验症状的关联是否沿前后轴存在区域特异性。结果发现，再体验症状严重程度与后海马而非前海马的谷氨酸/NAA水平相关；后海马该指标还与其和视觉皮层更强的功能连接相关，而这种连接又对应更严重的再体验症状，并可解释后海马谷氨酸代谢与症状严重度之间的共享变异。作者据此提出，后海马谷氨酸代谢失调可能通过其与视觉皮层的功能连接参与再体验症状，为创伤相关障碍的谷氨酸假说提供了多模态证据，但这些关联性发现尚不能确立因果或治疗效果。

papers.title: Distinct profiles of white matter diffusivity in obesity and bipolar disorders: An ENIGMA bipolar disorders study in 2166 individuals.
papers.authors: Dietze LMF, McWhinney SR, Favre P, Abé C, Alda M, Alexander N, Bauer J, Benedetti F, Berk M, Bøen E, Böhnlein J, Boye B, Brosch K, Butler AD, Canales-Rodríguez EJ, Cannon DM, Carruthers SF, Caruana GF, Corley E, Dannlowski U, Díaz-Zuluaga AM, Elvsåshagen T, Fortea L, Fuentes-Claramonte P, Furlong LS, Goldstein BI, Goltermann J, Grotegerd D, Haarman BCM, Hahn T, Howells FM, Mwangi B, Jahanshad N, Jamalabadi H, Jansen A, Kang MJY, Karuk A, Karantonis JA, Kennedy KG, Kircher TTJ, Klahn AL, Kochunov P, Konowski M, Kraus A, Landén M, Leehr EJ, López-Jaramillo C, MacIntosh BJ, Mackinnon ED, Madero S, Mazza E, McDonald C, McIntosh AM, Meinert S, Melloni EMT, Mitchell PB, Nabulsi L, Nenadić I, Opel N, Ortuño M, Phillips ML, Piguet C, Polosan M, Pomarol-Clotet E, Pouchon A, De Prisco M, Radua J, Roberts G, Romaniuk L, Roos A, Rossell SL, Saccaro LF, Salvador R, Scheffler F, Sim K, Soares JC, Stein DJ, Stein F, Straube B, Suo C, Temmingh HS, Teutenberg L, Thomas-Odenthal F, Thomopoulos SI, Usemann P, Valentí M, Van Rheenen TE, Vieta E, Vilajosana E, Whalley HC, Wu MJ, Zunta-Soares GB, Andreassen OA, Ching CRK, Thompson PM, Houenou J, Hajek T, ENIGMA Bipolar Disorder Working Group, ENIGMA BMI-X Working Group.
papers.abstract: Background Bipolar disorders (BD) are associated with a wide range of brain white matter abnormalities, but results vary across studies. This heterogeneity likely relates to effects of additional clinical/diagnostic variables, including medications and obesity, on white matter in BD. In this mega-analysis, we studied the links between relevant clinical variables and four diffusivity measures. Methods We obtained diffusion tensor imaging-derived fractional anisotropy (FA), mean, axial, and radial diffusivity (MD, AD, RD) values from 910 individuals with BD and 1256 healthy controls across 16 research sites in the ENIGMA-BD Working Group. We used principal component analysis to detect patterns of covariance across white matter tracts and studied associations between multivariate patterns of white matter alterations and demographic and clinical variables, including body mass index (BMI), medications, and diagnostic information, using mixed regression models. Results Higher BMI was associated with lower PC1 FA and higher PC1 RD; BD was associated with higher PC1 MD, while treatment with antiepileptic medications was associated with lower PC1 FA, higher PC1 MD, and PC1 RD. Conclusions We found FA and MD are weakly associated, providing complementary information, and there are unique associations between specific diffusivity measures and clinical predictors. Treatment with antiepileptics may inflate the statistical effects of BD on white matter. By using all diffusivity measures and accounting for additional clinical factors, we can gain new insights into brain correlates of severe mental illness.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于ENIGMA双相障碍工作组的多中心扩散张量成像数据，比较双相障碍患者与健康对照者的白质弥散指标，并考察体重指数、药物等临床变量与这些指标的关系。分析显示，较高的体重指数与较低的各向异性及较高的径向弥散相关，双相障碍诊断与较高的平均弥散相关，而抗癫痫药物使用则与较低的各向异性和较高的平均、径向弥散相关。作者指出，各向异性与平均弥散仅呈弱关联、提供互补信息，不同弥散指标与临床预测因素存在各自特异的联系；抗癫痫药物治疗可能放大双相障碍对白质统计效应的影响，提示分析时需纳入全部弥散指标并控制相关临床因素。

papers.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT responses to common questions about rTMS: can ChatGPT support patient education about rTMS?
papers.authors: Kalem B, Gülel HG, Veskoukis T, Meisenzahl E, Kujovic M, Theisen C.
papers.abstract: Objective In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) and its applications have become a compelling topic in psychiatry. This study aimed to investigate whether the AI chatbot ChatGPT is useful for patient education by evaluating the quality, reliability, and readability of its responses to patient questions about repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS). Methods Twenty-five frequently asked questions about rTMS were separately queried to ChatGPT-4 with no follow-up questions. Responses were reviewed by three psychiatrists by using the Global Quality Scale (GQS), DISCERN tool, and Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) Benchmark Criteria. Readability was evaluated by the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and the Gunning Fog, Coleman-Liau, and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook Indexes. Results Overall, the quality of ChatGPT responses was moderate to good, with a mean GQS score of 3.69. The mean DISCERN score was 35.33, which is considered poor, and the JAMA Benchmark Criteria score was 0 for all questions. The mean readability score was high (mean grade level, 10.98). Conclusion Our results show that ChatGPT responses to patient questions about rTMS are of acceptable quality and usefulness. However, the reliability and accuracy of the responses are limited, and a high reading level is required to understand them. Although ChatGPT can support patient education about rTMS, it should be used with caution and under guidance from healthcare professionals.

papers.title: Muscle biomechanical rehabilitation following therapy in Achilles and patellar tendinopathy assessed by MR elastography.
papers.authors: Salimi Majd M, Lerchbaumer M, Kim S, Tzschätzsch H, Agres AN, Sack I, Guo J.
papers.abstract: Tendon healing is the primary goal of tendinopathy therapy. However, the therapeutic response of adjacent muscles remains uninvestigated. MR-elastography (MRE) can assess muscle biomechanical properties and function. This study investigated muscle biomechanical responses in patients treated for patellar (PT) or Achilles tendinopathy (AT). A prospective longitudinal study included 20 athletes, 8 with AT (41 years ± 8; 6 men) and 12 with PT (34 years ± 10; 12 men), who underwent MRI, diffusion-tensor-imaging (DTI), and MRE before and ≥6 months post-treatment. Isotropic (ciso ) and anisotropic stiffness parameters (c‖ and c⊥ ) in tendon-adjacent muscles were derived and analyzed between groups and longitudinally compared with clinical scores and tendon dimensions. At baseline, symptomatic legs with higher tendon dimensions and clinical symptoms exhibited lower muscle stiffness than asymptomatic legs (p<0.05). Post-treatment, AT patients showed increased ciso (4.3±8.5%) in gastrocnemius and posterior soleus (SolP; 4.9±8.6%) in treated legs but decreased SolP stiffness (-3.2±7.2%) in untreated legs (p<0.05). In PT patients, only anisotropic MRE (c‖ : 5.3±15.2% and c⊥ : 10.3±12.7%) in vastus lateralis showed significant increases (p<0.05) post-treatment. In treated legs of AT and PT, increased muscle stiffness post-treatment correlated negatively with tendon dimensions (p<0.05). Post-therapy, tendon-adjacent muscles exhibited increased stiffness in affected leg and decreased stiffness in contralateral leg (particularly SolP), potentially reflecting altered muscle use and loading, respectively. The observed changes in muscle stiffness may help characterize muscle biomechanical changes during rehabilitation and balanced recovery. Furthermore, anisotropic muscle stiffness was more sensitive to tendon structural changes than isotropic stiffness, warranting further validation for clinical assessment.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes and risk factors in pediatric epilepsy associated with focal cortical dysplasia: a retrospective cohort study of 628 imaging-confirmed cases.
papers.authors: Wu J, Xiong M, Yang L, Chen X, Jiang L, Hu Y.
papers.abstract: Objective To investigate the clinical high-risk factors for epilepsy secondary to focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) in children and for progression to drug-resistant epilepsy, and to evaluate the long-term prognosis of affected patients. Methods We retrospectively included 628 children with MRI-diagnosed FCD who were treated at the Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University between February 2006 and September 2025. Risk factors for epilepsy and drug-resistant epilepsy were analyzed using Cox and Logistic regression models, with cluster analysis applied to define clinical subtypes and the stability of the clustering solution was verified by bootstrap resampling. Results The incidence of epilepsy in children with FCD was 79.0% (496/628), of whom 24.0% (151/628) progressed to drug-resistant epilepsy. Among the 81 surgically treated children with medium- to long-term follow-up, 72.8% (59/81) achieved complete seizure freedom. Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that global developmental delay (P=0.004), intellectual disability (P=0.002), paralysis (P=0.014), hypoplasia of the white matter (P<0.001), repetitive epileptiform discharges lasting ≥5 seconds during the interictal period (P=0.003), and continuous irregular slow waves (P=0.016) were independently associated with epilepsy onset. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis showed that the interictal RED type II waveform (P=0.003) was an independent high-risk factor for drug-resistant epilepsy. Cluster analysis classified the patients into three subtypes: a low-risk group characterized by seizure freedom or drug responsiveness, essentially normal intelligence, lesions confined to a single lobe, and no EEG abnormalities; an intermediate-risk group, also predominantly seizure-free or drug-responsive, but frequently accompanied by intellectual disability, with single-lobe lesions and a single abnormal EEG pattern; and a high-risk group dominated by drug-resistant epilepsy, often complicated by intellectual disability, with lesions frequently involving multiple lobes and multiple abnormal EEG patterns. Bootstrap validation indicated moderate stability of the clustering structure (ARI = 0.653). Conclusion Children with FCD show marked clinical heterogeneity, and their prognosis is closely associated with neurodevelopmental deficits, lesion extent, and electrophysiological characteristics. Early identification of these high-risk factors, together with cluster-based stratified management, may be of substantial importance for improving patient outcomes.

papers.title: Impact of cannabis use and cannabis composition on formal thought disorder and related brain networks: An fMRI study in 51 patients with schizophrenia.
papers.authors: Bernabeu T, Argote M, Citterio-Quentin A, Giloux N, Sescousse G, Rolland B.
papers.abstract: Background Formal thought disorder (FTD) is a core dimension of schizophrenia, which has been associated in previous studies with increased brain functional connectivity between temporal gyri and striatal regions as measured with fMRI. Cannabis use is highly prevalent in schizophrenia population as compared with the general population and, in the context of elevated tetrahydrocannabinol/cannabidiol (THC/CBD) ratio, has been found to be associated with increased FTD in schizophrenia. Consequently, in this study, we aimed to investigate whether cannabis consumption in patients with schizophrenia is generally associated with both enhanced functional connectivity and FTD. Methods We explored the functional connectivity between the temporal gyri and striatal regions in 51 schizophrenia patients divided into two groups stratified by cannabis use. FTD was measured using the conceptual disorganization item from the Positive And Negative Syndrome Scale. Region-of-interest (ROI)-to-ROI and seed-based connectivity analyses, correlation tests, and mediation models were conducted using both frequentist and Bayesian approaches. Results No significant difference was found in terms of functional connectivity between cannabis users and non-users. THC/CBD ratio was not significantly associated with cortico-striatal connectivity or FTD. Overall, Bayesian results indicated moderate to strong evidence favoring the null hypothesis across most models. Conclusion Cannabis use was not robustly associated with an altered cortico-striatal connectivity in this sample. The convergence of frequentist and Bayesian evidence suggests that cannabis use may not account for previously reported FTD-related connectivity alterations in schizophrenia. Larger studies considering cannabis composition, dose-response relationships, and symptom dimensions are warranted to refine these findings.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在51名精神分裂症患者中比较使用与不使用大麻者的颞叶与纹状体功能连接，并考察大麻中四氢大麻酚/大麻二酚比值与形式思维障碍的关系。结果显示，两组间功能连接无显著差异，该比值也与皮层-纹状体连接及形式思维障碍无关，贝叶斯分析多数模型支持零假设。作者据此认为，大麻使用在本样本中并未稳定对应皮层-纹状体连接改变，提示其可能不足以解释既往报道的与形式思维障碍相关的连接异常；样本较小，结论仍需更大规模研究验证。

papers.title: Glial lipid reprogramming in brain aging: Lipid identity, organelle stress, and redox vulnerability.
papers.authors: Rana M, Ko WC, Nepali K, Ko CY, Yen TL, Jan JS, Taliyan R, Li CH, Yang CH.
papers.abstract: Brain aging is accompanied by progressive glial dysfunction, impaired metabolic adaptation, oxidative stress, and increased susceptibility to neurodegenerative disease. Although many studies of lipid metabolism in aging and neurodegeneration emphasize lipid abundance, lipid amount alone cannot explain why glia become redox-vulnerable. This review advances a chemistry-resolved integrative framework in which glial lipid reprogramming is understood through aging- and disease-associated changes in lipid identity, composition, oxidation state, storage form, subcellular localization, and lipid-mediated signaling. We discuss evidence from aged brain tissue, human neurodegenerative disease, iPSC-derived glial systems, and mouse models showing that altered lipid handling in microglia, astrocytes, and oligodendrocyte-lineage cells reshapes phagocytosis, inflammatory signaling, myelin processing, astrocytic metabolic support, and neuronal injury. We emphasize that acyl-chain saturation, head-group structure, oxidized lipid species, neutral lipid storage, plasmalogen-dependent redox buffering, peroxisomal lipid metabolism, and compartmental distribution determine how lipids regulate receptor engagement, lipid-droplet dynamics, lysosomal stress, mitochondrial function, ferroptotic susceptibility, and inflammatory redox signaling. Importantly, glial lipid reprogramming is further shaped by extracellular vesicle-mediated neuron-glia communication, regional lipid heterogeneity, and sex-dependent modifiers of glial metabolism. Oxidative stress therefore reflects the convergence of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA)-enriched membranes, oxidized phospholipids, oxysterols, ceramide accumulation, plasmalogen loss, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, lysosomal iron release, peroxisomal dysfunction, and declining glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1), GTP cyclohydrolase 1-tetrahydrobiopterin (GCH1-BH4), and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-dependent protective systems. Finally, we discuss lipid-centered therapeutic opportunities targeting cholesterol efflux, apolipoprotein E (APOE) lipidation, lipid-droplet metabolism, sphingolipid pathways, lipid peroxide defense, plasmalogen support, extracellular vesicle biology, and lipid-based delivery systems. By shifting the focus from lipid accumulation to lipid identity, compartmental handling, and biological context, this review synthesizes glial lipid reprogramming as an integrative framework linking brain aging to redox-sensitive neurodegeneration.

papers.title: State transitions in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: mechanistic convergence and biomarker-guided stratification.
papers.authors: Nasb M, Yang D, Malik TH, Xu D, Dayoub L, Zhou J, Zhao Y.
papers.abstract: Background Biological heterogeneity is a major obstacle to therapeutic development in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Cross-sectional pathway labels do not show whether a mechanism is active or treatment-relevant in an individual patient. Methods We conducted a structured critical narrative review informed by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and CENTRAL were searched for English-language literature published from 1 January 2015 to 7 August 2026; seminal earlier studies were identified by citation tracking. Human genetic, pathological, longitudinal biomarker, multi-omic, imaging, neurophysiological, and interventional evidence was prioritized. Evidence was appraised by human proximity, temporality, replication, mechanistic specificity, and treatment relevance. Results Evidence supports interacting RNA/proteostasis, nucleocytoplasmic-transport, glial-inflammatory, and energetic-metabolic processes, but current evidence does not yet support the use of any candidate state for individual treatment assignment. The most mature temporal example is loss of TDP-43 splicing repression before neurofilament elevation in genetically at-risk individuals. Nucleocytoplasmic-transport evidence is strongest in C9orf72 disease; inflammatory and metabolic signals are confounded by disease burden and systemic illness; and the gut-brain axis remains a context-dependent amplifier. We propose prespecified transition rules, evidence grades, and biomarker-by-treatment interaction tests. Conclusions A state-transition model becomes clinically useful when longitudinal measurements add value beyond clinical predictors and injury markers and prospectively identify differential treatment benefit.

papers.title: Dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal graph fusion for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
papers.authors: Zhang H, Zhao J, Wu S, Szigeti K, Miklós K, Sun J, Qiao J.
papers.abstract: Multi-modal fusion methods have demonstrated potential in integrating complementary information from different data modalities. However, existing methods often rely on static fusion strategies, failing to capture the heterogeneous interactions across modalities. To address this challenge, we propose the dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal interaction graph fusion network (DMTL-Net) for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) diagnosis. The model is designed to extract distinctive and complementary features from brain functional and structural networks while capturing their dynamic topological organization. Specifically, the structural radiomics similarity network (RSN) and functional connectivity network (FCN) are constructed from structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), respectively. Multi-modal graph initialization is performed by the cross-modal inclusive integration and consensus filtering to balance sensitivity and specificity. Then we propose the dynamic topology learning mechanism that integrates multi-scale feature extraction with adaptive channel-wise and spatial-wise fusion, effectively capturing complex inter-modal interactions. Additionally, focal loss is used to reduce the contribution of easy-to-classify samples and emphasize hard examples during optimization. Evaluated on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange dataset, the proposed DMTL-Net demonstrates superior performance and consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Decoding individual differences in mental information from human brain responses predicted by deep neural networks.
papers.authors: Kawahata K, Wang J, Blanc A, Maeda N, Nishimoto S, Nishida S.
papers.abstract: Brain decoding using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has high potential for evaluating unobservable mental information that varies across individuals in everyday situations. Although estimating individual differences in mental information using brain decoding could be effective for social applications, especially in neuromarketing, the physical constraints and high costs of fMRI limit the practical application in real-world settings. To overcome these limitations, we propose a framework to estimate individual differences in decodable mental information using brain responses predicted by deep neural networks (DNNs). In this framework, DNN-based models are trained to predict fMRI responses to natural movie scenes. Then, additional fMRI measurements are no longer required because mental information for new movie scenes can be decoded from the predicted responses instead of the measured ones. A large-scale analysis revealed that the proposed predicted-response decoding captures individual difference patterns consistent with those derived from conventional measured-response decoding across various cognitive domains. Of the 88 cognitive labels associated with movie scenes, individual difference patterns could be captured for more than 70% of the labels. This framework offers a promising approach for evaluating personal mental information with substantially reduced reliance on fMRI, thereby expanding the potential for social applications of brain decoding.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出一种框架，用深度神经网络预测的脑活动替代实际fMRI测量，来解码个体心理信息的差异。模型先学习从自然电影场景预测fMRI响应，之后对新场景即可直接从预测响应中解码，无需再采集fMRI数据。大规模分析显示，这种预测响应解码在多种认知维度上得到的个体差异模式与传统实测响应解码基本一致，在电影场景关联的多数认知标签上都能捕捉到个体差异。作者认为，这有望大幅减少对fMRI的依赖，推动脑解码在社会场景中的应用，但结论基于预测响应与实测响应的对照，尚非实际应用验证。

papers.title: Digital twin control framework uncovers individualized cross-scale links between functional connectivity deviations, communication impairment, and molecular mechanisms in autism.
papers.authors: Liu G, Qiu J.
papers.abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is hallmarked by pronounced inter-individual heterogeneity in brain function and clinical manifestations. Conventional neuroimaging studies yield highly inconsistent findings, as extrinsic confounding factors and intrinsic disease heterogeneity mask ASD-specific functional connectivity (FC) signatures, hampering the identification of individualized neural mechanisms linked to symptom severity. Methods We developed a digital twin control analytical framework based on deep contrastive learning. By comparing each ASD participant with their matched digital twin control, we quantified individual-specific FC deviations. Principal component analysis was applied to extract the core aberrant pattern, followed by multi-dimensional analyzes and validation including clinical correlation, transcriptomic decoding, neurotransmitter and mitochondrial co-localization, as well as disease and cognitive enrichment. Results The model effectively disentangled disease‑related from non‑disease‑related variations. The identified dominant aberrant FC pattern was significantly associated with Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) communication scores, suggesting it is associated with to communication impairment. This pattern showed convergent associations with synaptic pathways, excitatory/inhibitory neuronal signatures, critical developmental windows and subcortical structures, and exhibited negative spatial association with multiple neurotransmitter systems and mitochondrial respiratory complexes. Biological validation further supported its ASD specificity and communication‑related cognitive relevance. Conclusions Leveraging the twin control analytical framework, this study provides an exploratory cross-scale framework linking individualized FC deviations with clinical, transcriptomic, neurochemical, and mitochondrial maps. The findings indicate that communication difficulties in ASD may partly arise from multi-scale disturbances in neural integration, social-perceptual processing and activity-dependent cellular energy regulation.

papers.title: Coarse motor-state structure across paired preoperative fMRI and intraoperative ECoG in patients with brain tumors.
papers.authors: Hu J, Ma J, Guo W, Jiao Y, Yang J, Wang H, Yin Y, He R, Cheng G, Bai H, Zheng H, Liang D, Zhang J, Hu Z.
papers.abstract: Presurgical motor mapping in patients with tumors near eloquent motor cortex is commonly based on task-evoked activation maps, yet local BOLD responses may be difficult to interpret in lesion-affected tissue because of anatomical distortion, altered vascular coupling, and variability in task performance. In this study, we used a four-state motor paradigm spanning Action, kinesthetic motor imagery (IMG), Watch, and recent-action recall (REC) - to test whether coarse task-state relationships are preserved across paired preoperative fMRI and intraoperative ECoG in10 patients with brain tumors. Activation summaries and preoperative task familiarization were used to support task engagement, representational similarity analysis (RSA) was used to characterize within-modality state geometry, and cross-modal RSA was used to assess shared organization. Across modalities, Action and IMG showed relatively similar response patterns, Watch was more distinct, and REC occupied an intermediate position that should be interpreted cautiously because of the fixed task order. Cross-modal RSA showed positive correspondence between fMRI and ECoG representational dissimilarity matrices, supporting a shared coarse state structure rather than fine-grained equivalence between modalities. These findings support a hypothesis-generating, relation-based complementary framework for interpreting functional organization in patients with brain tumors, while the limited state space, clinically determined ECoG coverage, fixed task order, and indirect verification of internally generated states warrant cautious interpretation.

papers.title: The Visual Cortex and Beyond: Investigating Long-Term Cortical Plasticity Following Monocular Deprivation.
papers.authors: Wagner F, Grajewki L, Schmidt A, Ulrike T, Ullsperger M, Finke K, Gaser C, Dahnke R, Klingner CM, Brodoehl S.
papers.abstract: Aim To characterise short- and long-term plastic changes in cortical and subcortical structures induced by ultra-long (five-day) monocular deprivation (MD), and to assess the extent and regional specificity of structural changes and their reversibility following the restoration of binocular vision. Methods In this single-arm longitudinal study, 21 healthy adults underwent five structural MRI sessions: at baseline, during MD on days 1, 3 and 5, and after a seven-day recovery period (day 12). MD was induced by occluding the right eye with a translucent eye patch for five consecutive days. Grey matter volume (GMV) changes were analysed using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain effects and generalised estimating equations (GEE) to model temporal trajectories in predefined cortical and subcortical regions. Results Ultra-long MD induced dynamic GMV changes in primary and higher visual cortices, with exploratory changes also in subcortical and cerebellar structures. VBM showed cumulative volume increases in bilateral occipital cortex, including calcarine, lateral occipital and fusiform regions, and adjacent cerebellar lobules, peaking between days 3 and 5. Region-wise modelling resolved the temporal build-up of these changes across visual, subcortical and sensorimotor regions; after correction for multiple comparisons, a time-dependent effect remained in occipital and ventral occipito-temporal cortex (occipital pole, fusiform and calcarine cortex), converging with the voxel-wise result. Following binocular restoration, an exploratory GMV decrease was observed selectively in the left middle occipital gyrus, while an exploratory increase was observed in the left hippocampus, compatible with persistent plasticity in associative memory networks. Conclusion Prolonged sensory imbalance via ultra-long MD induces rapid, region-specific and possibly persistent GMV plasticity in the adult brain. These changes follow temporally stratified trajectories across visual, subcortical and integrative systems, consistent with models of homeostatic and hierarchical plasticity. Corrected evidence supports cumulative occipital plasticity during deprivation; whether the exploratory extra-visual and post-recovery changes reflect persistent adaptation requires confirmation. MD-based paradigms thus offer a controlled window on structural plasticity in both healthy individuals and clinical populations.
keywords: Monocular Deprivation · Sensitive Period · Volume Effect · Plasticity Model

papers.title: Brain volume analysis-guided basic research in psychiatry.
papers.authors: Tanaka KF, Abe Y.
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) volumetric analysis is among the few tools able to probe the living human brain, offering a route from clinical findings back to basic neuroscience. Here we propose a reverse-translational framework for psychiatric research that links human MRI findings to their underlying molecular mechanisms in model animals. The framework rests on three "liaisons": a species liaison, confirming that a volume change identified in humans is also observed in mice using the same imaging and analytical method; a scale liaison, in which a histological pipeline explains the macroscopic volume change in terms of cell number and cell volume; and a causal liaison, in which molecular or cell-biological intervention converts correlative histological findings into causal evidence by inducing or reversing the volume change. We further propose that unbiased, whole-brain MRI volumetric analysis in mice can serve as an exploratory region-screening method, identifying disease- or treatment-related regions without a predefined region of interest, and capturing the maintained structural outcome of an intervention rather than its immediate functional trace. Together, the three-liaison framework and the region-screening approach outline a general strategy by which MRI-guided reverse and forward translation can uncover the structural and molecular basis of psychiatric diseases and their treatments.

papers.title: Translational evidence for habenula's role in human addiction: A scoping review.
papers.authors: Parisien C, Abidi NH, Khalaf E, Fortin JS, Pat N, Hétu S.
papers.abstract: Addiction is characterized by persistent substance use or engagement in behaviors despite adverse consequences and impaired control, but its expression varies substantially across individuals, substances, and severity. Within one influential neurocircuitry framework, addiction processes are organized into binge, withdrawal, and preoccupation stages. Preclinical research implicates the habenula across these processes but indicates that its contribution varies across drugs, subdivisions, and experimental models. Research on the human habenula in addiction remains fragmented, and the extent to which it converges with preclinical mechanisms is unclear. This scoping review synthesized evidence on the human habenula in addiction and examined its convergence with preclinical findings. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, databases and grey literature were searched in November 2025, with literature surveillance continued through April 2026. Human studies reported reduced fronto-habenula white-matter integrity, elevated habenula-striatal resting-state functional connectivity, withdrawal-related habenula-frontal connectivity, increased habenula blood flow during opioid withdrawal, altered task-evoked responses to reward and feedback, and nicotine-related genetic signals. By contrast, morphological studies found no consistent differences in habenula structure across addiction samples. Most human neuroimaging studies could not distinguish the medial and lateral habenula, limiting direct comparison with subdivision-specific preclinical mechanisms. Overall, across human and preclinical studies, the evidence does not support a unitary habenular alteration across addiction. Cross-species convergence was strongest for withdrawal-related activity, particularly for opioids, and for nicotine-related molecular mechanisms, but remained limited by differences in substances, circuits, measures, and paradigms. Future studies using subdivision-sensitive imaging and more comparable cross-species designs are needed.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述梳理了人类缰核在成瘾中的研究证据，并考察其与临床前发现的吻合程度。人类研究涉及额叶-缰核白质完整性下降、缰核-纹状体静息态功能连接增强、戒断相关的缰核-额叶连接与阿片戒断时缰核血流增加，以及奖赏与反馈相关任务反应改变和尼古丁相关遗传信号；但形态学研究未发现成瘾样本间缰核结构的一致差异，且多数人类神经影像研究无法区分内侧与外侧缰核。作者指出，跨物种证据并不支持成瘾中存在单一的缰核改变，吻合最强的是戒断相关活动（尤其阿片类）和尼古丁相关分子机制，但仍受物质、环路、测量与范式差异限制。

papers.title: Examining reliance patterns on AI advice in medical imaging: a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experiment.
papers.authors: Gaube S, Jussupow E, Kokje E, Koch TK, Khan J, Bondi-Kelly E, Schicho A, Kitamura FC, Ezer T, Mottok J, Lermer E, Ghassemi M, Colak E.
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) holds significant potential to support diagnostic decision making; however, the collaboration between clinicians and AI systems often does not surpass the performance of unaided humans or standalone AI. This study aimed to examine the effect of AI advice on diagnostic decision making among experts and novices, focusing on the occurrence of AI over-reliance and under-reliance and the potential mitigating effect of explainable AI. Methods We used a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experimental design. Participants (50 task experts [radiologists] and 75 novices [non-radiologist physicians and medical trainees]) were randomly assigned in equal proportions to one of six groups, which determined the order in which the three conditions were presented across the three sessions. In each session, participants read 50 head CT scans with or without the presence of an intracranial haemorrhage, under one of three experimental conditions: control, no AI prediction; basic AI advice, AI prediction without annotations; and explainable AI advice, AI prediction with scan annotations. 80% of cases with basic or explainable AI advice received correct advice, and 20% received incorrect advice. The main outcomes were diagnostic performance (the correct identification of intracranial haemorrhage), confidence in the diagnosis, case reading time, and AI advice usefulness ratings. We defined under-reliance as a final decision that did not align with correct AI advice, and over-reliance as a final decision that aligned with incorrect AI advice. All elements of the project were preregistered and are available on the project's Open Science Framework repository. Findings Data were collected between Feb 16, 2023, and Aug 10, 2023. Both over-reliance on incorrect advice and under-reliance on correct advice occurred. Under-reliance was associated with high uncertainty and, in absolute terms, had a more detrimental effect on diagnostic performance than over-reliance. Correct explainable AI advice reduced under-reliance and improved performance (OR=1·84, p<0·0001, 95% CI 1·49-2·28) and confidence (b=0·15, p<0·0001, 0·09-0·22) compared with no advice, particularly when reviewing more difficult cases with intracranial haemorrhage. Correct explainable AI did not reduce reading time compared with the no-advice condition (b=-1·81, p=0·071, -3·78 to 0·16). Explainable AI was perceived as more useful than basic AI advice (b=0·12, p=0·0029, 0·04-0·20), especially among novices. Interpretation The occurrence of both under-reliance and over-reliance highlights the need for efficient counterstrategies beyond classic explainable AI methods to foster appropriate reliance and synergy in AI-supported clinical decision-making. Funding Volkswagen Foundation, Forum for Interdisciplinary Research, and German Federal Ministry of Education and Research.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究用混合方法、随机交叉实验考察影像诊断中专家与新手的AI建议依赖模式，比较无AI、基础AI和可解释AI三种条件。结果显示，对错误建议的过度依赖和对正确建议的依赖不足同时存在；依赖不足与高不确定性相关，且对诊断表现的负面影响在绝对量上大于过度依赖。正确的可解释AI建议能减少依赖不足并提升诊断表现与信心，尤其在较难的颅内出血病例中，但未缩短阅片时间；可解释AI也被认为更有用，新手尤为明显。作者据此指出，仅靠经典可解释AI不足以促成恰当依赖，仍需更有效的对策。

papers.title: Implementation and early experience with tubular retractor-assisted minimally invasive parafascicular surgery for deep brain tumors.
papers.authors: Toyota PR, Liu E, Gould L, Norton J, Slough K, Appendino JP, Persad ARL, Hnenny LP.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
papers.abstract: Minimally invasive parafascicular surgery using tubular retractors (tr-MIPS) has emerged as a strategy to access deep intra-axial lesions while minimizing white matter disruption. However, practical guidance on institutional implementation and integration with modern intraoperative adjuncts remains limited. We describe our early institutional experience with tr-MIPS, with a focus on workflow adoption, multimodal adjunct integration, and feasibility. Demographic, radiographic, operative, and postoperative data were collected, with particular attention to extent of resection, neurological outcomes, and use of adjunctive technologies. Six patients underwent tr-MIPS for deep intra-axial tumors of varied histology. Gross or near-total resection was achieved in four cases. Five patients experienced no new postoperative neurological deficits, and one had transient dysphasia. Median length of stay was 3.5 days. A range of adjuncts including diffusion tensor imaging, 5-aminolevulinic acid fluorescence, intraoperative neurophysiologic monitoring, and depth-electrode electroencephalography were successfully incorporated without workflow disruption. Notably, intraoperative depth-electrode EEG was used to guide resection of an epileptogenic lesion, representing a novel adjunctive application in the tr-MIPS setting. tr-MIPS can be implemented within a modern neurosurgical practice and feasibly integrated with multiple intraoperative adjuncts. We demonstrate feasibility with the addition of this technique to our center's armamentarium. Beyond facilitating access to deep lesions, its compatibility with technologies such as tractography, neurophysiologic monitoring, and EEG expands its functional utility. These findings support the feasibility of a broader adoption of tr-MIPS and highlight opportunities for multimodal, precision-guided minimally invasive neuro-oncologic surgery.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究报道了一个中心在深部脑肿瘤中开展管状牵开器辅助微创经脑室旁手术（tr-MIPS）的早期经验，重点在于工作流程的建立、多种术中辅助技术的整合及可行性。研究纳入数例组织学类型不同的深部脑内肿瘤患者，多数实现全切或近全切，术后多数无新发神经功能缺损，仅一例出现短暂性失语。扩散张量成像、荧光引导、神经电生理监测及深部电极脑电图等辅助手段均顺利融入流程，其中脑电图用于指导致痫病灶切除属新的辅助应用。作者据此认为该技术可在现代神经外科实践中实施并与多种术中技术兼容，但结论限于单中心早期可行性，尚不能说明其疗效优劣。

papers.title: Insular subregional dysfunction in panic disorder: A multimodal MRI study.
papers.authors: Li Y, Wang F, Huang Y, Deng M, Wang G, Yang Z, Feng J, Chen H, Zou Z.
papers.abstract: Background The spatial organization of insular abnormalities across connectional-architecture-defined subregions in panic disorder (PD) remains unclear. We examined structural and resting-state functional measures using the Brainnetome Atlas. Methods Forty-nine medication-naïve patients with PD and Fifty healthy controls underwent structural and resting-state MRI. Gray matter volume (GMV), amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF), and regional homogeneity (ReHo) were assessed across six insular subregions. Four prespecified functional connections were examined, together with exploratory Granger causality analysis between dIg and S1 and an AAL3 whole-insula comparison. Results dIg-S1 functional connectivity was reduced in PD (β = -0.148, 95% CI [-0.248, -0.048], pFDR = 0.017). ALFF showed a Group × Subregion interaction (F(5,578) = 4.162, p = 0.001). Only the ventral agranular insula (vIa) showed significantly higher ALFF after false discovery rate (FDR) correction (pFDR = 0.016), with a larger group effect than other subregions. The interaction persisted after temporal signal-to-noise ratio (tSNR) adjustment (F(5,577) = 2.582, p = 0.025), but the vIa-specific effect was nonsignificant in a separate vIa-only tSNR-adjusted model (p = 0.194). ReHo was directionally lower across all six subregions, but no contrast survived FDR correction. No robust subregional GMV differences or significant group differences in exploratory Granger causality were detected. Adjusted AAL3 whole-insula differences were nonsignificant. Conclusions PD showed measure-dependent insular functional alterations, including reduced dIg-S1 coupling and vIa-predominant ALFF differences, with the latter sensitive to signal quality and spatial smoothing.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注惊恐障碍患者岛叶各亚区的结构与静息态功能异常如何按连接架构分区分布，采用多模态MRI比较未用药患者与健康对照的岛叶亚区指标。结果显示，患者背侧颗粒岛叶与初级感觉皮层间的功能连接减弱，低频波动幅度存在组别与亚区交互，仅腹侧无颗粒岛叶的幅度升高较突出，但该亚区效应在单独校正信号质量后不再显著；局部一致性和灰质体积未见经校正的稳健差异。作者据此认为，惊恐障碍的岛叶功能改变依赖具体测量指标，且部分结果对信号质量与空间平滑敏感，解释时需谨慎。

papers.title: Topography-specific white matter hyperintensities, hippocampal atrophy, and gait slowing as independent and interrelated correlates of late-life depression.
papers.authors: Kim J, Yang HJ, Park S, Kim BS, Park JH.
papers.abstract: Background Late-life depression (LLD) has been linked to cerebrovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and physical dysfunction. This study aimed to investigate the independent and interrelated associations of topography-specific white matter hyperintensities (WMH) burden, hippocampal volume, and gait speed with LLD. Methods We evaluated 366 older adults (LLD n = 112; non-depressed n = 254) using 3 T MRI, neuropsychological testing, and gait speed assessment. WMH were segmented into juxtaventricular (JVWMH), periventricular (PVWMH), and deep (DWMH) regions. Multivariable logistic and linear regressions and structural path analysis were performed. Results JVWMH (OR = 2.98, 95% CI 1.58-5.63, p = 0.001) and PVWMH volume (OR = 2.60, 95% CI 1.61-4.18, p < 0.001), together with slower gait (OR = 0.96, 95% CI 0.95-0.98, p < 0.001) were associated with LLD, whereas DWMH was not. In linear models, JVWMH (β = 0.184, P = 0.001), PVWMH (β = 0.197, P < 0.001), smaller hippocampus volume (β = -0.115, p = 0.038), and slower gait (β = -0.322, p < 0.001) were independently associated with increased depressive symptom severity, whereas DWMH was not. Path analysis demonstrated that JVWMH exerted both direct (β = 0.17, p < 0.001) and indirect effects on depression via gait slowing (β = 0.044, p = 0.007), whereas PVWMH showed only direct effects and DWMH showed no significant pathways. Conclusions This study reveals that LLD is independently associated with regional WMH, hippocampal volume loss, and gait slowing, via topography-specific direct and indirect WMH pathways.

papers.title: Exploring tinnitus-like central hyperactivity in a large language model-based computational analog of hearing loss.
papers.authors: Han SY, Song JJ, Choi BY, Koo JW, Chang M.
papers.abstract: Tinnitus is commonly associated with maladaptive neural plasticity following hearing loss. Although large language models (LLMs) share similarities with the human brain in language processing and representation, their potential for modeling tinnitus-related neural mechanisms remains limited. This study aimed to develop an LLM-based framework to investigate tinnitus-related maladaptive neural plasticity. An LLM was partitioned into eight independently trainable regions. An exploratory computational analogy of deafferentation-related changes associated with peripheral hearing loss was developed by applying token-specific high-frequency attenuation during training on a commonsense reasoning task. Region-specific contributions to tinnitus-like excess activity were quantified using region-wise plasticity ablation, selectively disabling plasticity in one region at a time. Representational relationships among regions were evaluated using centered kernel alignment. The computational deafferentation analog largely preserved task accuracy but showed increased activity. Region 1 was the only region with a net suppressive contribution to excess activity, whereas region 2 exhibited the largest positive contribution; regions 6 and 8 also contributed positively. Regions 1 and 2 remained representationally distinct across all conditions. Deafferentation tended to reduce region 1-region 2 similarity, whereas plasticity ablation in most regions, except for regions 6 and 8, tended to increase it. The proposed LLM-based framework captured network-level functional dissociations consistent with current theories of hearing loss-associated tinnitus, identifying distinct suppressive, transformation, and higher-order modulatory roles. These findings highlight the potential of LLMs to investigate maladaptive neural changes underlying tinnitus. This framework may provide the foundation for constructing patient-specific digital twins.

papers.title: Ultra-high-resolution 5 T MR neurography: first steps.
papers.authors: Martín-Noguerol T, Álvarez-de-Sierra-García B, Luna A, Górriz JM, Gómez-Río M.
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) is an established technique for peripheral nerve assessment, enabling high-resolution visualization of nerves and simultaneous evaluation of adjacent musculoskeletal structures. Although optimized 3 T MRI remains the clinical standard, whole-body 5 T systems have emerged as a potential intermediate platform between 3 T and 7 T imaging. Direct peer-reviewed evidence for peripheral MRN at 5 T remains limited to a single pilot study of the inferior alveolar nerve, with no prospective validation of the brachial plexus, lumbosacral plexus, or limb nerves. Physical and engineering studies suggest that 5 T MRI may provide greater signal availability than 3 T while presenting less severe radiofrequency-related challenges than 7 T; however, the relevance of this theoretical balance to peripheral nerve imaging remains unproven. The additional signal available at 5 T could theoretically be allocated to higher spatial resolution, greater acceleration, or broader anatomical coverage, but these potential gains have not been validated against optimized 3 T MRN. Potential applications include the evaluation of entrapment neuropathies, traumatic nerve injuries, inflammatory neuropathies, peripheral nerve tumors, and the implementation of quantitative approaches such as diffusion tensor imaging, T2 mapping, and T1ρ imaging. Furthermore, artificial intelligence-based reconstruction, denoising, and acceleration strategies may improve the clinical feasibility of ultra-high-resolution neurography by reducing scan times while preserving image quality. This narrative review examines the limited published evidence, physical rationale, technical requirements, preliminary institutional experience, and research priorities for 5 T MRN.

papers.title: Region-specific associations between dual-Layer spectral detector CT-derived carotid plaque parameters and white matter hyperintensity burden in patients with carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.authors: Ye Y, Lin L, Liu Y, Wang Y, Wen X, Xu Y.
papers.abstract: Objective White matter hyperintensities (WMH) exhibit region-specific characteristics. Whether dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLSCT)-derived plaque parameters associate with WMH burden region-specifically remains unclear. Methods This cross-sectional study enrolled 213 patients with carotid atherosclerotic plaques who underwent carotid CTA and brain MRI within 30 days. Seven DLSCT parameters were measured; WMH was segmented into juxtaventricular, periventricular, deep, and juxtacortical subregions. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations with total WMH burden (FDR correction). Nested models evaluated incremental value. Linear mixed-effects models with region-by-parameter interactions assessed region-specific associations. Results In the primary model (Model 2), Z-Zeff was significantly negatively associated with total WMH burden (β = -0.205, 95 % CI: -0.299 ∼ -0.111, FDR-q < 0.001). Adding Z-Zeff to the clinical model significantly increased explained variance (ΔR2 = 0.070, p < 0.001, ΔAIC = -15.09), whereas conventional CTA parameters did not (ΔR2 = 0.001, p = 0.938). Significant region interactions were observed for Z-Zeff, age, and LDL-C. Z-Zeff was negatively associated with all subregions, strongest in periventricular (β = -0.254) and deep (β = -0.172) WMH. Age was most strongly associated with periventricular WMH (β = 0.436). LDL-C and diabetes were associated only with periventricular WMH (β = -0.111 and -0.221, respectively). Conclusion DLSCT-derived Z-Zeff was independently associated with WMH burden in a region-specific manner, with the strongest associations in periventricular and deep white matter, and provided incremental value beyond clinical and conventional CTA parameters. These findings support Z-Zeff as a potential imaging biomarker linking carotid plaque composition to regional cerebral small vessel disease.

papers.title: Asymptomatic congenital CMV infection: long-term cognitive outcome and brain imaging findings.
papers.authors: Kokkola E, Palomäki M, Puosi R, Ritari N, Westerholm-Ormio M, Boppana S, Nieminen T, Saxen H, Puhakka L.
papers.journal: European journal of paediatric neurology : EJPN : official journal of the European Paediatric Neurology Society
papers.abstract: Infants with symptomatic congenital cytomegalovirus infection (cCMV) are at high risk of neurodevelopmental impairments. However, long-term cognitive outcomes in children with asymptomatic cCMV (acCMV) remain unclear. Through universal CMV screening of approximately 20,000 newborns, children with acCMV (n = 36), children with symptomatic cCMV (n = 4), and matched healthy controls (n = 54) were identified and followed prospectively. Brain MRI and neuropsychological assessments were performed in children with acCMV and controls at 6-8 years of age. Brain MRI findings were more common in children with acCMV than in controls (14/23, 60.9% vs. 3/31, 9.7%;p < 0.001). Punctate white matter lesions were the most frequent finding and occurred more often in children with acCMV than in controls (10/23, 43.5% vs. 3/31, 9.7%;p 0.004). Ventriculomegaly, cerebellar cortical malformations, and cerebral cortical malformations were less common and occurred only in children with acCMV. Mean full-scale IQ did not differ significantly between children with acCMV (n = 26) and controls (n = 28) (116.91 ± 11.67 vs. 118.68 ± 13.12, p NS), nor did the mean subtest scores. The full-scale IQ in children with acCMV with brain MRI abnormalities (n = 12) did not significantly differ from those without abnormalities (n = 8) (109.67 ± 13.72 vs. 120.75 ± 9.24, p NS). Neither did the mean subtest scores differ between them. Despite the high frequency of brain MRI abnormalities, predominantly white matter lesions, cognitive outcomes at early school-age did not differ significantly between children with acCMV and controls. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and determine the prognostic significance of brain MRI abnormalities in acCMV.

papers.title: Circuit architecture and regulation of the Drosophila brain neuroendocrine system.
papers.authors: Al-Dailami AN, McKim TH, Zandawala M.
papers.abstract: Insect neurosecretory cells (NSCs), located in distinct regions of the brain and the ventral nerve cord (VNC), are a major source of neuropeptides and peptide hormones (NPHs) that facilitate communication between the nervous system and peripheral tissues. NPHs, in turn, regulate growth and development, and modulate diverse behaviors and physiological processes including feeding, locomotion, social behaviors, metabolism, and reproduction. Given their central role in regulating systemic homeostasis, NSCs are tightly regulated. Recent advances in connectomics and single-cell transcriptomics have enabled comprehensive identification of NSCs in the Drosophila melanogaster brain and identified factors that modulate their activity. Here, we review the current state-of-the-art on insect NSCs and the inputs regulating them, predominantly focusing on adult Drosophila. We highlight: 1) major synaptic inputs, 2) neuromodulatory inputs, 3) gut-derived NPHs, and 4) cell-autonomous internal sensors that influence NSC activity. Finally, we discuss open questions in the field and how advances in omics approaches can bridge the gap in our understanding of NSC regulation between Drosophila and other insects.

papers.title: Clinical, immunological and metabolic features and gut-brain axis markers in children with autism spectrum disorder and TORCH-associated central nervous system involvement.
papers.authors: Khusenova N, Madjidova Y, Mizamov F, Abidova M, Karimova G, Irfan, Mohammad T, Abramyan A.
papers.abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) have heterogeneous etiologies, with TORCH infections potentially contributing to neurodevelopmental disruption through central nervous system injury and gut-brain axis dysfunction. Methods A prospective comparative study enrolled 280 children aged 3-10 years with ASD: 112 with TORCH-associated central nervous system (CNS) involvement (main group) and 168 with idiopathic ASD (comparison group), alongside 25 healthy controls. Assessments included clinical/neurological features, autism severity, gastrointestinal symptoms, pro-inflammatory cytokines, metabolic markers, neuron-specific enolase (NSE), fecal zonulin, and brain MRI. TORCH pathogens were detected by PCR from saliva samples. Results TORCH-associated ASD exhibited a more severe phenotype with greater frequencies of delayed speech, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbance, hyperactivity, emotional-behavioral dysregulation, epileptiform manifestations, and gastrointestinal symptoms. Severe ASD was significantly more common in the TORCH group. Laboratory analyses revealed significantly elevated interleukin-1β, interleukin-8, tumor necrosis factor alpha, homocysteine, ammonia, uric acid, NSE, and fecal zonulin, with reduced folate. Fecal zonulin was positively correlated with inflammatory markers and neuron-specific enolase. MRI more frequently demonstrated periventricular gliosis, ventriculomegaly, subependymal abnormalities, and diffuse residual organic changes. Conclusions In this cohort, ASD with clinical evidence of TORCH-associated CNS involvement was associated with greater clinical severity and higher serum inflammatory, metabolic, neuronal-injury, fecal-zonulin, and structural MRI measures than ASD without such evidence. The cross-sectional design and limitations of salivary PCR preclude causal attribution to TORCH infection.

papers.title: Infant Negative Affect During Mother-Infant Interaction Is Associated with Neonatal Limbic-Prefrontal Connectivity in the First Month of Life.
papers.authors: Posner J, Michael AM, Fay M, Abraham E, Feldman R, Coelho Milani AC, Silva I, Abdala N, Maria de Araújo C, Fanton MR, Lodi A, Duarte CS, Jackowski A.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Background Early caregiving may shape neonatal limbic circuit organization, yet whether microanalytically coded interaction quality relates to neonatal limbic-prefrontal connectivity is unknown. We tested associations between infant and maternal affect during mother-infant interaction and neonatal limbic-prefrontal cortex (PFC) connectivity. Methods At approximately 30 days postnatal, 143 mother-infant dyads from the Healthy MiNDS cohort (São Paulo, Brazil) completed a video-recorded interaction coded with the Coding Interactive Behavior (CIB) system; infant negative affect was the percentage of interaction time in distress. Neonates underwent resting-state fMRI; limbic-PFC connectivity was quantified by principal component analysis of amygdala and hippocampus seed-to-ROI maps. Covariate-adjusted regressions tested associations. Results Infant negative affect was associated with right amygdala-PFC (β = -0.247, p = .003) and right hippocampus-PFC connectivity (β = -0.202, p = .021), both surviving FDR correction and robust across multiple analytic approaches. The amygdala association was limited to infant distress-related behaviors, whereas maternal positive expressiveness showed an independent, opposing association (β = 0.202, p = .019); no other CIB measure was significant. Exploratorily, connectivity was associated with sleep problems at 18-24 months in females (r = -.324, p = .030). Conclusions The emotional quality of early caregiving is associated with neonatal limbic circuit organization: infant distress is selectively associated with weaker amygdala-PFC connectivity, whereas maternal positive affect shows an independent opposing association. These findings identify the mother-infant relationship as a modifiable input to neonatal brain development.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察母婴互动中的情绪质量是否与新生儿期边缘系统—前额叶皮层的功能连接相关。研究者在婴儿约一个月大时，对母婴互动录像进行编码，并以静息态fMRI量化杏仁核和海马与前额叶的连接，随后用回归分析检验关联。结果发现，婴儿负面情绪越强，右侧杏仁核—前额叶及右侧海马—前额叶连接越弱；其中杏仁核的关联仅限于婴儿痛苦相关行为，而母亲积极表达则呈现独立的相反关联。作者据此认为，早期照护的情感质量与新生儿边缘回路组织相关，母婴关系可能是可干预的输入；但这是关联性证据，不能推断因果或治疗效果。

papers.title: Positive-affective and negative-cognitive brain-behavior axes in clinical high risk for psychosis.
papers.authors: Vieira S, Aleman Y, Bici L, Meijer J, Penzel N, Jacobs GR, Yassin W, Alameda L, Bastürk Ö, Pries LK, Kiakos D, Armando M, Klauser P, Abrahamyan-Empson L, Conus P, Wannan CMJ, Dwyer D, Cho KIK, Knight SR, Cecchi G, Polosecki P, Allott K, Addington J, Arango C, Breitborde NJK, Broome MR, Cadenhead KS, Calkins ME, Carrión RE, Castillo-Passi RI, Hai Chen EY, Choi J, Cornblatt BA, Diaz-Caneja CM, Ellman LM, Fusar-Poli P, Gaspar PA, Gerber C, Glenthøj LB, Horton LE, Ming Hui CL, Kambeitz J, Kambeitz-Ilankovic L, Keshavan M, Kim M, Kim SW, Koutsouleris N, Kwon JS, Langbein K, Mamah D, Mathalon DH, Mittal VA, Nordentoft M, Pearlson GD, Perez J, Perkins DO, Powers AR, Roalf D, Rogers J, Sabb FW, Schiffman J, Shah JL, Silverstein SM, Smesny S, Stone WS, Strauss GP, Thompson JL, Tod S, Upthegrove R, Verma SK, Wang J, Wolf DH, Wood SJ, Yung AR, Zhang T, Bouix S, Corcoran CM, Kapur T, Pasternak O, Bearden CE, Kahn RS, Kane JM, McGorry PD, Shenton ME, Woods SW, Nelson B, Accelerating Medicines Partnership® Schizophrenia (AMP® SCZ), Marquand A, Hagmann P.
papers.abstract: Background Individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR) present with heterogeneous combinations of positive, negative, and affective symptoms, cognitive difficulties, and functional impairment. However, reproducible multivariate links between this multidomain phenotype and brain morphology remain limited. This study explored the multivariate brain-behavior associations in CHR using a data-driven approach. Methods Baseline data from 720 CHR participants from the Accelerating Medicines Partnership® Schizophrenia program (AMP® SCZ) were analyzed using sparse canonical correlation analysis to identify associations between 95 regional brain volumes and 28 behavioral variables indexing symptoms, cognition, and functioning. Generalizability was tested using leave-one-network-out cross-validation (PRoNET and PRESCIENT), and stability was assessed using bootstrapping and leave-one-site-out analyses. Associations with demographic, clinical and site-related variables were examined. Results Two brain-behavior dimensions generalized across networks. A positive-affective axis (r=0.21-0.23), linking higher depression, anxiety/stress, positive symptoms and anhedonia with predominantly frontal-cingulate-insular volume reductions and relatively larger corpus callosum and putamen volumes. This axis was associated with comorbid depression, cannabis use and family history of depression or affective psychosis. A negative-cognitive axis (r=0.17-0.18) linked greater asociality, alogia, emotional withdrawal, blunted affect, and motor retardation, poorer cognition and functioning with reduced cerebellar and parietal volumes, and relatively larger lateral ventricles and corpus callosum. This axis was associated with lower IQ and poorer premorbid adjustment. Conclusions Two partially dissociable brain-behavior dimensions were identified: a positive-affective axis capturing the co-expression of affective and attenuated positive symptoms, and a negative-cognitive axis suggestive of neurodevelopmental vulnerability.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注精神病临床高危（CHR）人群中多维症状、认知与功能表型能否与脑形态建立可重复的多元联系，利用数据驱动方法分析了该人群的基线脑区体积与行为变量。结果识别出两个可跨网络泛化的脑-行为维度：一个正性-情感轴将抑郁、焦虑/压力、阳性症状及快感缺失与以额-扣带-岛叶体积减小为主的模式相联系，并与共病抑郁、大麻使用及情感障碍家族史相关；另一个阴性-认知轴将社交退缩、言语贫乏、情感淡漠、运动迟滞及较差的认知与功能与特定脑体积模式相联系，并与较低智商和较差病前适应相关。作者认为这两个部分可分离的维度分别反映情感与弱化阳性症状的共表达，以及提示神经发育易感性的阴性-认知特征；这些关联为横断面观察，尚不能说明因果或临床预测效用。

papers.title: The spectrum within the spectrum: Neural heterogeneity in autism.
papers.authors: Bakul F, Krafick KI, Kana RK.
papers.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) encompasses diverse behavioral, cognitive, and neural profiles that vary widely across individuals. Because diagnosis remains predominantly behavior-based, clinically meaningful within-spectrum differences are often missed. Recent advances in neuroimaging analysis have created opportunities for the identification of distinct neural profiles within ASD. These new avenues provide ways to examine intra-ASD heterogeneity directly, identifying person-specific brain-behavior patterns that group-level comparisons fail to capture. The present systematic review focused on neuroimaging methods (i.e., resting-state fMRI; rs-fMRI, cortical morphology) that emphasized heterogeneity-informed outcomes based on normative modeling, data-driven subtyping, clustering analysis and similar analytic choices. For rs-fMRI, findings showed that differences in connectivity within the default mode and salience networks were linked to social-communication and language impairments, with subtype-specific patterns emerging across samples. In cortical thickness and surface area, studies identified distinct developmental trajectories and individual deviation profiles, with prefrontal and temporal regions often tied to repetitive behaviors and social-communication difficulties. Voxel-based analyses revealed subgroup-specific gray matter alterations, including cerebellar and cortical differences, that aligned with variation in repetitive behaviors and social difficulties. Collectively, this emerging evidence supports the notion that neural heterogeneity in autism is a core feature rather than a limitation. Embracing individual variability can provide crucial insight into the inconsistencies and contradictions of earlier case-control and group-level findings. Moving forward, autism research must prioritize heterogeneity-based methods to establish reproducible subtypes and individualized brain-behavior links.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述聚焦自闭症谱系障碍内部的行为、认知与神经异质性，梳理了静息态功能连接、皮层形态等神经影像研究中采用规范性建模、数据驱动分型与聚类等异质性导向分析的结果。研究发现，默认网络与突显网络内的连接差异同社交沟通和语言障碍相关，并呈现亚型特异模式；皮层厚度与表面积分析揭示出不同的发育轨迹和个体偏离特征，前额叶与颞叶区域常与重复行为和社交沟通困难相联系；基于体素的分析则显示亚组特异的灰质改变，涉及小脑和皮层，并与重复行为和社交困难的变异相吻合。作者据此提出，神经异质性是自闭症的核心特征而非研究局限，重视个体差异有助于理解以往病例对照和组水平研究中的不一致与矛盾，并呼吁未来研究优先采用基于异质性的方法，以建立可重复的亚型及个体化的脑—行为联系。

papers.title: Hearing function in virologically suppressed persons living with HIV: Results from the HELO study.
papers.authors: Moulignier A, Daval M, Guillaume J, Rodach J, Valin N, Ayache D.
papers.journal: European annals of otorhinolaryngology, head and neck diseases
papers.abstract: Aim Hearing function is highly sensitive to aging and may represent a marker of neuro-sensory decline. Whether well-controlled HIV infection is associated with altered auditory function remains uncertain. Material and methods Cross-sectional exposed-non-exposed study including 100 antiretroviral therapy (ART)-treated persons living with HIV (PLHIVs) (≥10 years of infection and ≥5 years of sustained viral suppression <20 copies/mL) and 95 age- and sex-matched HIV-uninfected controls (HUCs). All participants underwent comprehensive audiological assessment including pure-tone audiometry, speech audiometry, auditory brainstem responses (ABR), and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Analyses were adjusted for age using multivariable models. Objectives To assess peripheral and brainstem auditory function in PLHIVs with long-term, tightly controlled virological suppression compared with HUCs. The primary objective was to compare pure-tone hearing thresholds in the better-hearing ear. Results No clinically meaningful differences were observed between groups in pure-tone thresholds, speech audiometry parameters, ABR findings, or MRI small-vessel disease features. Mean air-conduction thresholds were 26.4±10.2dB in PLHIVs and 27.1±9.8dB in HUCs (P=0.52). Age-adjusted analyses showed no association between HIV status and auditory outcomes despite longstanding HIV infection. ABR wave latencies and interpeak intervals were comparable across groups. No significant correlation was found between auditory measures and global cognitive performance. Although some speech audiometry differences reached nominal significance levels, none met the predefined conservative significance threshold used to account for multiple testing. Conclusion Peripheral and brainstem auditory function were similar in virologically suppressed PLHIVs and HUCs. These findings suggest that, under current treatment conditions, well-controlled HIV infection is not associated with clinically meaningful peripheral or brainstem auditory dysfunction.
