In the same feature space, a dataset-origin classifier achieved ROC-AUC = 0.966, demonstrating substantial cross-cohort distribution shift. These findings show that resting-state microstate dynamics contain PD-related information within a cohort, but that the present representation is not sufficiently stable across cohorts. Cross-cohort validation and explicit assessment of dataset shift are therefore essential when evaluating EEG microstate features as reproducible electrophysiological markers.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究检验帕金森病相关的静息态脑电微状态特征能否在不同队列间稳定迁移，采用整合静态描述、定向转移、流动相关指标与序列复杂度的多族表征，并在开发队列交叉验证后锁定外部独立队列测试。结果显示，随机森林在开发队列中能较好区分帕金森病，但外部测试时性能降至接近随机水平；同一特征空间下，数据集来源分类器却高度可区分，提示存在明显的跨队列分布偏移。作者据此指出，该微状态表征虽在单队列内含有疾病相关信息，但跨队列稳定性不足，评估其作为可重复电生理标记时需重视外部验证与数据集偏移问题。

papers.title: Preoperative diffusion-perivascular MRI burden and postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation in Parkinson disease
papers.authors: Niu C, Chen P, Xiong C, Jiang M, Wang S, Zhang C, He H, Si J.
papers.abstract: Abstract Postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation may reflect pre-existing brain vulnerability, but the preoperative imaging correlates of this vulnerability remain uncertain. We examined whether a combined diffusion and perivascular imaging burden was associated with delirium after bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation. This single-centre observational cohort included 100 patients with Parkinson disease undergoing bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation and 32 healthy controls scanned with the same preoperative MRI protocol. Delirium was assessed during postoperative days using the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale with clinical adjudication. Age- and sex-adjusted reference models fitted in healthy controls were used to standardise tract diffusion metrics, diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space, and basal ganglia enlarged perivascular space counts. Directionally aligned diffusion and perivascular scores were averaged with equal domain weights. Patients who developed postoperative delirium (n = 30) had higher combined burden than those who did not (n = 70; 95% CI, 0.584 to 1.526; q<.001). Using Firth penalised logistic regression, higher combined burden remained associated with postoperative delirium after adjustment for age, sex, education, Mini-Mental State Examination score, disease duration, and motor severity (95% CI, 1.49 to 4.25; Wald P<.001). Higher burden was also associated with longer delirium duration and higher peak screening scores among affected patients. Exploratory internal prediction yielded an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.701 after adding burden to clinical variables, compared with 0.538 for clinical variables alone. These findings support preoperative diffusion-perivascular burden as a candidate marker of perioperative neuropsychiatric vulnerability requiring multicentre validation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注帕金森病患者在接受双侧丘脑底核脑深部电刺激后出现术后谵妄的问题，并检验术前弥散成像与血管周围间隙成像所反映的复合负担是否与谵妄相关。研究为单中心观察性队列，比较了接受手术的患者与健康对照，并用健康对照建立的参考模型标准化相关影像指标。结果显示，发生谵妄的患者术前复合负担高于未发生者，这一关联在调整年龄、性别、教育程度、认知评分、病程和运动严重程度后仍然存在；负担较高者谵妄持续时间更长、筛查峰值更高。作者据此提出，术前弥散-血管周围负担可能是围手术期神经精神易感性的候选标志物，但尚需多中心验证，其探索性预测性能也提示目前不宜直接用于临床决策。

papers.title: Translating Imaging-based Brain Age Models for Predicting Accelerated Brain Ageing in African Populations: A Pilot Study on a Nigerian Cohort.
papers.authors: Anazodo U, Olusuyi T, Cakmak J, Soula O, Raymond C, Rajabli R, Umoren C, Oladeji I, Gbadamosi A, Toyobo O, Dako F, Muhammad A, Abba S, Akinola R, Aduluwa H, Eze C, Anyanwu B, Anosike C, Shah J, Udeh-Momoh C, Cole J, Collins D, Fatade A, Adewole M.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Brain age is an emerging imaging biomarker for early detection of neurodegenerative disorders, based on the estimation of the brain’s biological age. Existing predictive models are predominantly trained on Global North (GN) neuroimaging data, limiting their sensitivity when applied to underrepresented populations due to geographic, imaging scanner, and biological heterogeneity. We investigated this bias by adapting the standard Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) method to a population-specific (PS) brain age model. Methods: Using a multi-institutional T1-weighted brain MRI dataset from 309 Nigerian adults, we implemented a robust low-compute image analysis pipeline which includes repurposing clinical scans and high-resolution cortical parcellation with multi-stage quality control. The PS-GPR model was trained on regional brain volumetric features from the Nigerian MRI scans and its performance compared to four common GN pre-trained models. Results: The proposed PS-GPR model showed a significantly lower prediction error (mean absolute error = 9.82 years) without age-bias correction and few seconds inference time compared to GN-trained machine learning models (mean absolute error = 10.00 – 16.70 years). SPARROW, a generalizable deep learning framework achieved an MAE of 7.87 but failed on 6% of the test set. This early work demonstrates the importance of representative data to build resource-efficient clinically viable models. Conclusion: This population-specific model is a step towards sensitive low-compute African brain age models. With the expansion of imaging data beyond Nigeria through the Africa Neuroimaging Archive (AfNiA), we will further develop the PS model to identify individuals with accelerated brain ageing for early intervention in at-risk adults.

papers.title: A Dual-Stream Spatio-Temporal Network with Bidirectional Rectification for Differential Diagnosis of Dementia using EEG
papers.authors: Yu L, Meng M, Gao Y, Xi X.
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate differential diagnosis between Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is of critical importance for the early screening of neurodegenerative diseases. Scalp electroencephalogram (EEG), as a non-invasive neurophysiological detection tool with excellent temporal resolution, has been widely adopted in dementia screening research. However, the inherent low signal-to-noise ratio and non-stationarity of scalp EEG signals, combined with the highly overlapping pathological rhythms between AD and FTD patients, render existing single-domain representation methods incapable of achieving precise pathological differentiation. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a dual-stream spatio-temporal network. In this framework, multiscale temporal features and effective connectivity graph features are extracted in parallel, followed by their integration. However, directly fusing the features from the two streams tends to amplify their respective noises. Therefore, the Spatio-Temporal Feature Fusion Based on Bidirectional Rectification module is proposed to execute dynamic noise suppression on the features and subsequently performs deep feature fusion via a cross-attention mechanism. Furthermore, this paper applies knowledge distillation using attention maps to address the issue of imbalanced sample distributions in the dataset. Experimental results on the ADFTD-RS dataset show that the proposed framework yields a subject-level accuracy of 60.00\% and an F1-score of 57.44\%, showing measurable improvements over several baseline methods. This work offers a feasible approach for the computer-aided differential diagnosis of dementia based on resting-state EEG.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对阿尔茨海默病与额颞叶痴呆患者静息态脑电病理节律高度重叠、信号信噪比低且非平稳，导致单域表征难以精确区分的问题，提出一种双流时空网络，并行提取多尺度时间特征与有效连接图特征，并通过基于双向校正的时空特征融合模块抑制噪声、借助交叉注意力实现深度融合，同时利用注意力图知识蒸馏缓解样本分布不均衡。在ADFTD-RS数据集上，该框架取得受试者水平准确率60.00%和F1分数57.44%，较若干基线方法有可测提升。作者认为这为基于静息态脑电的痴呆计算机辅助鉴别诊断提供了可行途径，但结果仍属初步，尚不能直接等同于临床诊断效能。

papers.title: Aperiodic EEG activity is a domain-specific marker of attentional aging in neurotypical adults.
papers.authors: Cazares C, Rigby A, Kang L, Getzmann S, Arnau S, Wascher E, Voytek B.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Aperiodic neural activity has been reliably shown to be reduced among older adults, and these reductions are associated with age-related cognitive decline. These results suggest that aperiodic activity, as measured by the spectral exponent, might be a viable electrophysiological biomarker for cognitive aging. However, this has not been tested longitudinally, within participants, during normal aging. Here, we used a longitudinal cohort of either sex to test whether changes in aperiodic activity between two sessions, approximately 5 years apart, track behavioral change across two domains: sustained attention (Psychomotor Vigilance Test) and executive function (modified Simon task). We found that aperiodic activity declined within individuals after the interval, independent of age at baseline. This within-person change tracked concurrent changes in reaction times during sustained attention but was not associated with changes in any Simon task measure. Within a resampling framework, the aperiodic-PVT association was stable across cohort resamples and independently fitted partitions, though it was not confirmed in a small, frozen held-out set. These findings suggest the longitudinal decline in aperiodic activity tracks attentional processing speed rather than executive function, supporting its potential as a domain-specific biomarker of attentional aging in neurotypical populations.Significance Statement Aperiodic (non-oscillatory) neural activity, indexed by the aperiodic exponent, is known to decline in older adults, but whether this happens within individuals over just a few years, and in step with cognitive change, remains unclear. Here we leveraged scalp EEG and cognitive-behavioral data from 276 neurotypical adults, tested twice approximately five years apart, and found that the aperiodic exponent declines within individuals over this interval, independent of age at baseline. This decline tracked concurrent slowing on a sustained attention task, but not change on an executive function task, and only in EEG recorded before, not after, cognitive testing. Based on this dissociation, we propose that aperiodic exponent decline indexes attentional processing speed rather than general cognitive decline in neurotypical aging.

papers.title: Probing the neural geometry of conscious object perception in time.
papers.authors: Hachisuka A, Baumgarten TJ, Spector D, Koenig L, He BJ.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Conscious object recognition is a critical brain function, key to making sense of the plethora of visual inputs and guiding adaptive behavior. Yet, the sequence of neural processing underlying conscious object recognition remains unclear. Existing proposals alternatively suggest that conscious object recognition proceeds in a "coarse-to-fine" sequence or a "fine-to-coarse" sequence. Here, we recorded high-density EEG while participants of both sexes performed a threshold-level object recognition task under different viewing conditions. Both superordinate and basic-level category information emerged early in neural activity, followed by a late superordinate category representation in an abstract format that is disentangled from low-level object features. Strikingly, in the early period, while basic-level category information positively correlated with perceptual awareness, superordinate category information negatively predicted perceptual awareness. By contrast, both superordinate and basic-level category information positively correlated with objective categorization accuracy in the early period. In the late period, both levels of category information positively correlated with awareness. These results suggest that neural processing underlying conscious object perception proceeds from the basic to the superordinate category level.Significance statement Despite significant interests, the sequence of neural processing underlying conscious perception remains unclear. Here, we investigated the unfolding of neural events in time that support perceptual awareness of visual objects. Using a threshold-level object perception task involving three image conditions (normal, low-pass filtered, masked) and high-density EEG, we reveal that basic and superordinate category information both emerge early in the neural activity (at ∼100 ms), but only the basic-level category representation positively contributes to awareness. By contrast, the early superordinate category representation negatively correlates with perceptual awareness. At ∼300 ms, an abstract superordinate category representation emerges, which also positively correlates with perceptual awareness. Therefore, category-level neural processing underlying conscious object perception proceeds from the basic to the superordinate level.

papers.title: Early life stress leads to detectable aberrant spread of neuron avalanches in the prefrontal-amygdala network in males but not females.
papers.authors: Kharybina Z, Palva JM, Palva S, Lauri SE, Hartung H, Taira T.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Development of the brain networks is highly vulnerable to stressful events. Early life stress (ELS) has been linked to multifaceted cognitive and emotional deficits in adulthood. Despite a growing body of evidence showing ELS-induced structural and functional changes in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), a circuit crucial for emotional processing, our knowledge of the resulting changes in the network dynamics is incomplete. Here, we investigate how maternal separation (MS) affects prefrontal-amygdala network in terms of neuronal avalanches, spatiotemporal clusters of activity, using simultaneous multielectrode recordings in the medial PFC (mPFC) and the BLA of urethane-anaesthetized juvenile (postnatal day (p) 14 - p15) and young adult (p50 - p 60) rats. Firstly, we show that MS leads to an intensified spread of activity within both regions as reflected in the higher mean branching ratios of the avalanches. Next, we demonstrate that most of the avalanches occur locally in one region, however, a small percentage of avalanches have clusters of activity in both regions simultaneously. We show that in MS animals prefrontal clusters followed by activity in the amygdala tend to be larger compared to controls and each event in the mPFC is followed by smaller number of events in the BLA, pointing towards impaired spread of activity from the mPFC to the BLA. Interestingly, avalanche spread from the BLA to the mPFC remains unaffected by MS. Abovementioned effects manifest only in adulthood and, intriguingly, only in males highlighting prolonged developmental and sex-dependent nature of ELS outcome.Significance statement Brain criticality describes the brain's ability to maintain a balanced state in which neural activity spreads efficiently without becoming too weak or overly chaotic. This balance can be measured through neuronal avalanches, bursts of cascading activity across interconnected neurons. Here, we show that early life stress (ELS) - adverse experiences during early brain development - disrupts the development of avalanche patterns in the connection between the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), brain regions involved in emotion and stress regulation. These effects were detected in males but not females. Our findings improve understanding of how stable brain activity develops in emotional brain networks and suggest that early life stress is an important factor influencing this critical balance.

papers.title: Cell-type dependence of effects from transcranial electric brain stimulation.
papers.authors: Dahle S, Einevoll GT, Ness TV.
papers.abstract: There is an urgent need for better treatment options for many neurological conditions, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, depression, and epilepsy. Transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) is a non-invasive, safe, inexpensive, and promising method that could address some of this unmet need. The therapeutic value of tES has been well demonstrated, but the effect is highly variable. To enable tES to reach its full potential requires a better understanding of how tES modulates neural activity so that tES treatments can be tailored to specific neurological conditions and individual patients. The neural response to tES is, however, highly complex, and the parameter space involved in optimizing tES treatments is daunting. This has made it difficult to obtain general insights into how tES modulates neural activity, and a central challenge lies in the cell-type-specific and frequency-dependent nature of these responses. In this study, we investigated cell-type-specific neuronal responses to tES over a broad frequency range, using a large database of biophysically detailed neuron models. We found that pyramidal cells respond strongly to low-frequency tES, but their responses drop sharply with frequency. In contrast, inhibitory neurons show a smaller reduction and, on average, become more responsive than pyramidal cells above ~60 Hz. By leveraging a reciprocity theorem we demonstrated that the effect of tES on a given cell-type is proportional to the frequency-dependent current-dipole moment that determines the EEG-signal contribution of this cell-type. We further identified the dendritic asymmetry as key in determining tES responses across the frequency spectrum. Counterintuitively, we also found that while total cell length increases tES sensitivity at low frequencies, it can have the opposite effect at high frequencies. Furthermore, we derived an analytical formula for idealized neuron models which can approximately predict the tES sensitivity of different cell types at any given frequency. By characterizing the role of morphology and stimulation frequency in determining tES responses of single cells, this is an important step towards a better understanding of tES at the fundamental level. These results also provide an efficient and accurate method for characterizing and comparing the tES responses of different neural populations across the frequency spectrum, which facilitates optimizing tES for cell-type specific targeting.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注经颅电刺激（tES）为何疗效高度可变，核心问题在于不同细胞类型对刺激频率的响应差异。作者利用大规模生物物理精细神经元模型数据库，考察了广频率范围内不同细胞类型的反应。结果显示，锥体细胞对低频刺激响应较强，但随频率升高迅速减弱；抑制性神经元下降较缓，在约60赫兹以上平均比锥体细胞更敏感。作者借助互易定理表明，某类细胞受tES影响的程度与其决定脑电信号贡献的频率依赖电流偶极矩成正比，并识别出树突不对称性是跨频谱决定响应的关键因素；细胞总长度在低频提高敏感性、在高频却可能相反。研究还给出可近似预测不同细胞类型任意频率敏感性的解析公式，为按细胞类型优化刺激参数提供了依据。

papers.title: A cortical semantic map integrates fractions and integers in the human brain.
papers.authors: Valério D, Debray S, Karami A, Cauté M, Gravel N, Dehaene S.
papers.abstract: How does the human brain represent the meaning of abstract symbols? Some theories postulate the existence of semantic spaces where concepts occupy positions that reflect their conceptual relationships. In the number domain, psychological evidence suggests that integers are represented along a mental number line which, with education, integrates higher-level number concepts such as fractions. To test this hypothesis, we recorded whole-brain 7T fMRI responses to integer and fraction symbols during an active magnitude comparison task designed to engage magnitude processing. Consistent with predictions, we found both behavioral and neural numerical distance effects. Activation vectors in intraparietal, inferior temporal, prefrontal, hippocampal, and parahippocampal cortices formed a two-dimensional semantic space organized by numerical magnitude and domain (fractions versus integers). Gaussian fits revealed a topographic map of numerical preferences in the anterior inferior parietal cortex, common to both domains. Our results suggest that, when educated adults engage in an explicit magnitude comparison task, their brain can construct an ordered representation that integrates fractions and integers, with a topographic organization in the anterior IPS/IPL.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注人脑如何表征分数与整数这类抽象符号的意义，用7T全脑fMRI记录受试者在主动数量比较任务中对两类数字符号的反应。行为与神经层面均出现数字距离效应，多个皮层区域的激活向量构成由数值大小和数字领域（分数与整数）组织的二维语义空间；前部顶下皮层还呈现两个领域共有的数值偏好拓扑图。作者据此认为，受过教育的成人在明确的数量比较任务中可构建整合分数与整数的有序表征，但这一结论限于该任务情境，不宜直接外推为日常理解或临床效果。

papers.title: MOG Antibody Status Is Associated With Distinct Clinical Profiles and Treatment Responses in Chronic Relapsing Inflammatory Optic Neuropathy.
papers.authors: Graure M, Nierobisch N, De Vere-Tyndall A, Pakeerathan T, Ayzenberg I, Gernert JA, Havla J, Ringelstein M, Aktas O, Tkachenko D, Hümmert MW, Trebst C, Cerdá-Fuertes N, Papadopoulou A, Giglhuber K, Wicklein R, Berthele A, Weller M, Kana V, Roth P, Herwerth M.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Chronic relapsing inflammatory optic neuropathy (CRION) is a steroid-dependent form of optic neuritis with incompletely understood pathophysiology. The identification of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibodies (MOG-IgG) in a substantial patient subset has challenged the diagnostic and therapeutic management. The aim of this study was to investigate clinical profiles and treatment outcomes of patients with CRION, comparing MOG-IgG-positive (MOG+) and seronegative (MOG-) subgroups. Methods Patients from 6 European tertiary centers fulfilling diagnostic criteria for CRION were included. All underwent cell-based autoantibody testing. Clinical outcomes (visual acuity and annualized relapse rate), laboratory and imaging findings (MRI, OCT), and treatment responses were retrospectively analyzed. Results Sixty patients were included (median age 33 years; 70% female); 27 (45%) were MOG+. MOG+ CRION was associated with later onset, higher annualized relapse rate (ARR) before treatment (median [IQR] 2 [1-3] vs 1 [1-2], p = 0.023), and a trend toward shorter interrelapse intervals. Additional distinguishing features included higher frequencies of antinuclear antibody positivity, elevated CSF interleukin-6, and extensive enhancement of the optic nerve on MRI. Relapse burden correlated with visual acuity decline and retinal thinning. In MOG+ patients, monoclonal antibody therapy reduced the ARR (n = 21; 2 [1-3] vs 0 [0-2], p = 0.024), primarily driven by tocilizumab (n = 11; 2 [1-3] vs 0 [0-1], p = 0.023). In MOG- patients, rituximab and azathioprine showed a trend toward ARR reduction. Discussion CRION represents a heterogeneous syndrome encompassing distinct subgroups. Although MOG+ patients demonstrate higher disease activity, tocilizumab might represent a therapeutic option, though further validation is needed. Serologic testing is critical for treatment stratification and preventing relapses.

papers.title: Prediction of death by neurologic criteria in patients with non-traumatic acute brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Schoene D, Nicklas M, Altarsha E, Diel NJ, Trabitzsch A, Pleul K, Huttner HB, Barlinn K.
papers.abstract: Background Robust predictors of death by neurologic criteria (DNC) after non-traumatic acute brain injury remain insufficiently defined. We therefore aimed to systematically synthesize the available evidence on prediction of DNC in non-traumatic brain injury. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched to August 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, observational studies, case series and registry data. Studies were included in the quantitative synthesis when sufficient comparable data for the same prognostic factor were available from at least two studies. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Results The database search identified 2,091 records. Eighteen studies comprising reported study cohorts of 9,070 participants were included. Quantitative synthesis included four studies (n=1,738), comprising two post-cardiac arrest and two stroke cohorts. In stroke populations, CT markers of severe intracranial mass effect were associated with a more than threefold increased odds of DNC (pooled OR 3.14, 95%CI 1.98-4.96; p<0.0001; I2=0%), while in post-cardiac arrest cohorts lower gray-white matter ratio values were associated with progression to DNC (pooled mean difference -0.15, 95%CI -0.22 to -0.07; p<0.001; I2=72%). Conclusions Evidence on predictors of DNC after non-traumatic acute brain injury remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous, with only a small number of studies providing robust analyses. Across these studies, CT-based markers - particularly indicators of diffuse cerebral edema or intracranial mass effect - show the most reproducible associations with progression to DNC.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究通过系统综述与荟萃分析，汇总非创伤性急性脑损伤患者进展为神经学标准死亡（DNC）的预测因素。纳入的18项研究覆盖约九千名报告队列参与者，但仅四项研究（含两项心脏骤停后与两项卒中队列）具备可合并数据。结果显示，卒中人群中提示严重颅内占位的CT征象与DNC风险升高相关，心脏骤停后队列中较低的灰白质比值也与进展至DNC相关。作者指出，现有证据仍有限且方法学异质性较大，CT所见的弥漫性脑水肿或占位效应是目前重复性较好的关联指标，尚不能据此确立临床预测或治疗结论。

papers.title: Optimization of copper and tin disulfide based surface plasmon resonance for the detection of brain tumor tissues.
papers.authors: Kumar R, Brahma B, Garia L, Kumar M, Bhoi AK.
papers.abstract: In this study, a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor, including SF5 prism, copper (Cu), Tin Disulfide (SnS2 ), Molybdenum Ditelluride (MoTe2 ), and sensing medium (SM) layers, was designed for the detection of brain lesions. With the remarkable sensitivity of 142.15°/RIU found at 33 nm of Cu, 8 nm of SnS2 , a monolayer of MoTe2, and refractive index (RI) of SM 1.33-1.50. To obtain the sensitivity of the proposed sensor, different brain lesions, including cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), gray matter, oligodendroglioma, low-grade glioma, lymphoma, and metastasis, were used as SM, while the thickness of the Cu layer was varied from 25 to 60 nm. A sharp SPR dip with a minimum reflectance (Rmin ) of 3.9 × 10⁻⁷ a.u. was obtained at a thickness of 33 nm, which also yielded the highest sensitivity (S = 136.47°/RIU) and figure of merit (FoM = 15.01/RIU). The low full width at half maximum (FWHM) at this thickness and the SPR angle shift (Δθres ) further confirmed the improved detection capability of the sensor. According to these results, the proposed SPR sensor is very useful for detecting brain abnormalities in real time and without labels.

papers.title: Atypical Cerebellar Vermis Signal Abnormality in Wernicke Encephalopathy.
papers.authors: Panwala TF, Sakai Y, Schmitt JE, Xu DJ.
papers.abstract: Wernicke encephalopathy is classically associated with signal changes involving the mamillary bodies, medial thalami, and periaqueductal gray matter on MRI. We present a case of a 57-year-old woman with progressive Wernicke encephalopathy with imaging abnormalities in the cerebellar vermis and bilateral cerebellar hemispheres. This case highlights atypical imaging features that can be seen in Wernicke encephalopathy and emphasizes the importance of early clinical recognition to prevent progression.

papers.title: DTI-Associated Blood Biomarkers in a Human Perioperative Brain Perturbation Model.
papers.authors: Liu J, Wang Y, Gao Z, Bao X, Han C, Sun Z, Tong H, Xue Z, Lv W, Xu A, Li M, Song X, Li W, Yang Z, Li S, Duan L, Wu C, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Circulating biomarkers of brain perturbation are rarely evaluated against anatomically localized in vivo imaging measures, limiting biological interpretation. We tested whether perioperative changes in candidate biomarkers were associated with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI)-defined microstructural changes in a controlled human perioperative model. In a paired cohort of 75 patients undergoing left-sided encephaloduroarteriosynangiosis, we obtained matched pre- and postoperative DTI and blood samples. Six biomarkers (ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase-L1 [UCH-L1], glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP], S100 calcium-binding protein B [S100B], neurofilament light chain, neuron-specific enolase, and protein tau) were quantified. Analyses included paired comparisons, region-of-interest-based cross-modal correlations, sparse canonical correlation analysis (sCCA) with bootstrap stability assessment, and patient-grouped regularized logistic regression for state discrimination. DTI showed perioperative changes in bilateral temporal-limbic regions and connected white matter, with the largest effects in left hippocampal and amygdalar territories on the operated side. UCH-L1, GFAP, and S100B showed the clearest paired increases and dominated internal perioperative-state discrimination. Blood-DTI associations were heterogeneous across biomarkers and states, and paired-change associations were not confined to these three markers. An observed three-biomarker panel discriminated perioperative state with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.914 in the test set. Several circulating biomarkers covaried with regional DTI measures in this exploratory perioperative cohort. UCH-L1, GFAP, and S100B were the most perioperatively responsive and state-discriminative markers, but the DTI-association pattern was not specific to this trio. The findings support a structure-associated framework for evaluating blood biomarkers against regional imaging changes; they do not validate these biomarkers for traumatic brain injury, and relevance to traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains hypothesis-generating.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在75名接受左侧脑硬膜动脉血管融通术的患者中，配对采集术前术后血液和弥散张量成像（DTI）数据，考察围手术期候选血液标志物是否与局部脑微结构变化相关。DTI显示双侧颞叶-边缘系统及相连白质出现围手术期改变，手术侧左海马和杏仁核区域效应最大；UCH-L1、GFAP和S100B的配对升高最明显，并在区分围手术期状态上表现最佳，三者组合在测试集中区分状态的曲线下面积为0.914。不过，血液标志物与DTI的关联在不同标志物和状态间并不一致，配对变化关联也不限于这三种标志物。作者据此提出以结构关联为框架评估血液标志物，同时强调这些结果不能用于验证创伤性脑损伤标志物，其与创伤性脑损伤的相关性仍属假设性。

papers.title: Adaptive local temporal weighting for short-window EEG-based SSVEP recognition using FB-eTRCA.
papers.authors: Zhao G, Feng Z, Wang Z.
papers.abstract: To improve short-window SSVEP recognition, we integrated adaptive temporal local weighting (ATLW) with filter-bank ensemble task-related component analysis (FB-eTRCA). ATLW estimates local discriminability from training trials, converts window scores into sample weights, and applies the training-derived weights to training and test trials within each cross-validation fold. Experiments were conducted on two public 40-target SSVEP datasets: the Benchmark dataset containing 35 subjects and six blocks, and the BETA database containing 70 subjects and four blocks. Seven observation windows ranging from 0.2 to 1.4 s were evaluated using subject-specific leave-one-block-out validation, with six folds for the Benchmark dataset and four folds for the BETA database. On the Benchmark dataset, only the 0.2-s accuracy gain remained significant after Holm correction (44.79% vs 44.07%; adjusted p = 0.0300); other windows were nonsignificant. On the Benchmark dataset, ablation analysis showed that adaptive weighting was more stable than fixed temporal weighting. After Holm correction, eTRCA+ATLW significantly outperformed eTRCA at 0.4 s (gain: 0.86 percentage points; adjusted p = 0.0023), but not at 0.2 s, supporting transferability to another TRCA-based decoder. EEGNet and BiLSTM were included as representative CNN and RNN baselines; both performed below the TRCA-family methods under the present subject-specific limited-calibration protocol. On the BETA database, FB-eTRCA+ATLW remained close to FB-eTRCA across all seven observation windows without BETA-specific parameter retuning, but no paired difference was statistically significant. These findings indicate that ATLW is a lightweight temporal refinement that can be applied to more than one TRCA-based decoder. Its measurable benefit may depend on SSVEP signal quality and the amount of available subject-specific calibration data. Accuracy increased with longer windows, whereas the information transfer rate peaked at 0.6 s on the Benchmark dataset. Therefore, no observation window was optimal for both accuracy and communication speed.

papers.title: The electro-MICA toolbox for integrating electrophysiology within multimodal imaging and connectomics workflows.
papers.authors: von Ellenrieder N, Cai Z, Arafat T, Vavassori L, Abdallah C, De Kraker J, Rodriguez-Cruces R, Royer J, Sahlas E, Bautin P, Pana R, Aron O, Frauscher B, Bernhardt BC.
papers.abstract: The integration of electrophysiological recordings with multimodal neuroimaging data holds great promise for advancing our understanding of brain function and neurological disorders. To facilitate this endeavor, we present electro-MICA, an open-access Python toolbox designed to project electrophysiological features from scalp and intracranial electroencephalography (EEG) onto cortical and hippocampal surfaces generated by validated multimodal imaging ecosystems. The toolbox comprises two pipelines: one for intracranial EEG (iEEG) recorded with stereo-EEG depth electrodes and one for scalp EEG source localization. Both pipelines are grounded in numerical solutions to the electromagnetic equations governing electric activity in the brain, solved using the Boundary Element Method. A key methodological contribution is the use of a current density double layer model for neural generators, which avoids the mathematical singularities introduced by conventional dipole-based models when electrodes are near the cortical surface, a situation that can arise in iEEG. Electrode contacts are additionally modeled with non-zero length, improving physical realism. Scalp EEG source localization is performed using eLORETA on a subject-specific three-layer head model derived from the anatomical input. Validation against empirical gamma-band iEEG data from 32 subjects demonstrates that the distributed generator model outperforms both distance-based and dipole-based alternatives. An illustrative clinical example demonstrates the toolbox's capacity to reveal associations between intracranial spike rates, cortical thickness, and anatomical connectivity in an epilepsy patient. Electro-MICA requires no parameter selection from the user, facilitating straightforward multimodal analyses. The toolbox is available at http://github.com/MICA-MNI/electromica with extensive online documentation at http://electromica.readthedocs.io.

papers.title: Interactions between age and sex in multiscale entropy and spectral power changes across the lifespan.
papers.authors: Solomon JP, Dobri SGJ, Shen K, Vakorin VA, Moreno S, McIntosh AR.
papers.abstract: Multiscale entropy (MSE) changes in relation to age, whereby ageing is associated with an increasing bias towards fine scale entropy. This change is thought to represent a shift towards localized information processing in the brain as we age. However, this relationship has not been tested in large sample sizes alongside other demographic factors and cognitive behaviours. This study aimed to replicate previously reported effects of ageing on MSE in an open access database (Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience, N = 587) and expand the findings to include an investigation of the effects of sex and a variety of cognitive behaviours. MSE curves and power spectrum densities (PSD) were calculated for each region of interest from the magnetoencephalography data. Multivariate partial least squares analyses were used to assess the relationship between MSE or PSD and five behavioural/demographic factors including age, sex, fluid intelligence, visual short-term memory, and a generalized measure of cognitive function. Age was associated with increased fine scale and decreased coarse scale entropy, as well as complementary spectral changes, including slowing of peak alpha rhythms, increased beta-band activity, and reduced gamma-band activity, which replicates prior MSE and PSD findings. In both domains, these age-related patterns differentiated based on sex with advancing age. Importantly, the unique effects of sex diverged between MSE and PSD. This result indicates that entropy-based measures can isolate aspects of temporal organization that are not clearly summarized by spectral structure alone.

papers.title: Beta-band dynamics during a naturalistic motor task: An OPM-MEG study.
papers.authors: Gibson J, Fildes J, Kirby A, Holmes N, Rier L, Mullinger KJ, Ison M, Morris PG, Boto E, Hill RM, Brookes MJ.
papers.abstract: Beta oscillations are a fundamental feature of brain activity, linked to long-range connectivity within canonical networks, inhibition of sensorimotor cortices, and the maintenance of a stable sensorimotor state in situations where the external world is predictable. The importance of beta oscillations in brain function is underscored by observations of their perturbation in neurological and psychiatric disorders. However, the precise role played by beta activity, particularly in mediating complex or skilful movements, remains incompletely understood. Here, we used a newly developed wearable optically pumped magnetometer-based magnetoencephalography (OPM-MEG) system to measure beta dynamics as participants learned to play a musical instrument. Twenty-two novice players took part in a study in which OPM-MEG data were recorded during two scanning sessions, while participants attempted to play a tune on a violin. Between the two sessions, participants received a violin lesson from an expert teacher. Results showed that robust data could be acquired during this naturalistic task, with beta oscillations decreasing in amplitude during movement and increasing upon movement cessation, as expected. Moreover, beta power while playing, in the motor and pre-motor areas, was significantly elevated after the lesson compared to before, and the movement-related modulation of beta amplitude was more pronounced after the lesson. These findings align with predictive coding models which suggest that beta amplitude should increase when individuals have greater certainty over the movements they carry out. Our study adds to an expanding literature on the role of beta oscillations and provides further evidence for the utility of OPM-MEG in naturalistic neuroscience.

papers.title: Longitudinal Changes in Brain Connectivity and Structure after MRgFUS VIM Thalamotomy for Essential Tremor.
papers.authors: Pijar J, Crompton DBJ, Elias G, Pancholi A, Iskin S, Loh A, Chow CT, Yang A, Ranjan M, Milosevic L, Schwartz M, Lozano A, Boutet A, Germann J.
papers.abstract: Essential Tremor (ET) is the most common movement disorder. Magnetic Resonance-guided Focused Ultrasound (MRgFUS), an incisionless surgery involving thermal ablation of targeted brain regions, like the Ventral Intermediate Nucleus of the Thalamus (VIM) and surrounding white matter tracts, is an effective treatment option. Fractional Anisotropy (FA), a metric of diffusion tensor imaging, can be used to determine white matter structural integrity and their changes following MRgFUS. This study investigates white matter and morphological brain remodeling after MRgFUS VIM thalamotomy and its association with tremor improvement, assessed by the Clinical Rating Scale for Tremor (CRST), over the first postoperative year. We retrospectively analyzed 56 ET patients who underwent unilateral MRgFUS VIM thalamotomy. Subjects' CRST scores, T1-weighted MRI scans, and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) scans were acquired pre-operatively and at three and twelve months post-operatively. FA maps were generated and registered to a standard space. Voxel clusters that exhibited significant change in FA over time were identified using FSL's cluster tool (p<0.001) and their change in FA value over time was Spearman correlated with relative change in CRST score. Deformation-Based Morphometry of T1-weighted images evaluated changes in structural volume, and a linear mixed-effects model was applied. We permuted these values 1000 times randomly to isolate significant (p<0.01) clusters related to the interaction between time and outcome and Spearman correlated them with relative improvement in CRST. Four main FA clusters demonstrated strong associations between CRST score and time. The insula produced consistent positive correlations at three (R=0.32, p=0.04) and twelve months (R=0.29, p=0.11). Yet, the visual cortex exhibited no significant association at three months (R=0.11, p=0.46), but did at twelve months (R=0.35, p=0.05), suggesting malleable white matter remodeling. Our morphometry analysis revealed two primary clusters located in the pre-supplementary motor area (pre-SMA) and visual cortex. The pre-SMA exhibited the strongest correlations at three months (three months: R=0.34, p=0.03, twelve months: R=0.17, p=0.36), while the visual cortex displayed a similar strength throughout (three months: R=0.20, p=0.18, twelve months: R=-0.22, p=0.23). These findings suggest that MRgFUS VIM thalamotomy is associated with broad structural tract and volumetric changes that extend beyond motor networks. Both analyses demonstrated post-treatment volume growth and increased tract structure in visual and cognitive regions. Correlation with tremor improvement indicates many of these changes may contribute to individual outcomes during the first post-operative year.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究回顾性分析了56名接受单侧MRgFUS丘脑VIM毁损术的特发性震颤患者，结合弥散张量成像的FA指标和基于形变的形态学分析，考察术后一年内白质与脑结构的变化及其与震颤改善（CRST评分）的关联。结果显示，FA变化与CRST评分相关的区域涉及岛叶和视觉皮层，其中岛叶在术后三个月和十二个月呈较一致的正相关，视觉皮层则在十二个月时出现关联；形态学分析发现前辅助运动区和视觉皮层两个主要区域，前者在三个月时相关性最强。作者据此认为，该手术与超出运动网络的广泛结构束和体积改变有关，视觉与认知区域出现治疗后体积增长和纤维结构增强，且这些变化可能与术后第一年的个体震颤改善相关。需注意这些为相关性结果，尚不能确立因果或治疗效应。

papers.title: The cognitive power of the avian brain.
papers.authors: Colombo M, Poutrain-Sorel O.
papers.abstract: Carrion crows make decisions faster than monkeys and humans.

papers.title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain.
papers.authors: Schmidbauer P, Nieder A.
papers.abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows (Corvus corone ) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

papers.title: Infra-slow brain-heart-gut electrophysiological interactions reveal a co-ordinated multisystem physiological network in humans.
papers.authors: Sitti G, Pitti L, Candia-Rivera D.
papers.abstract: Growing evidence indicates that brain continuously interacts with other physiological systems through neural and non-neural pathways. The brain-heart and brain-gut axes play a central role in homoeostasis, allostasis and behaviour, but also in cognitive aspects, including emotion and decision-making. Disruptions in these axes have been linked to a wide range of cardiovascular, neurological and psychiatric disorders. Despite this evidence, triadic crosstalk between the brain, heart and gut remains largely unexplored. Brain activity, cardiac autonomic fluctuations and gastric rhythms all exhibit slow temporal components in resting state, suggesting that brain-heart-gut electrophysiological interactions may occur over time scales from the infra-slow (0.01-0.1 Hz) physiological range. Using open-access electrophysiological recordings from 28 healthy subjects at rest, we extracted time-varying power dynamics describing the activity of the three organs: brain alpha power, cardiac sympathetic and parasympathetic indices, and the power of the gastric rhythm. Statistical associations among these organs were quantified using the maximal information coefficient across the extended temporal delay range. Physiological interactions were confirmed using surrogate-based testing, which allowed us to construct the network topology of interactions between the three organs. Our findings show that triadic brain-heart-gut interactions form a multidirectional network primarily at infra-slow time scales during resting state. This study offers one of the first insights into the physiology of brain-heart-gut interplay, providing a methodological baseline for the development of more comprehensive biomarkers based on network dynamics capable of linking pathological conditions to dysregulation across multiple organ systems. KEY POINTS: First in-human, non-invasive investigation of parallel brain-heart-gut electrophysiological interactions in awake, healthy subjects. We analysed simultaneous electroencephalographic (EEG), electrocardiographic (ECG) and electrogastrographic (EGG) recordings and quantified strength and temporal scale of the derived time series associations to construct a large-scale network of interactions. We found that brain-heart-gut interactions extend into the infra-slow range (0.01-0.1 Hz), indicating that spontaneous fluctuations in the electrophysiological activity of one organ at rest are typically followed by corresponding changes in the other two. We consistently found a robust brain-heart-gut network topology across subjects, with multidirectional interactions and bodily dynamics converging towards midline central-posterior EEG regions. These findings provide one of the first endeavours in characterizing the physiology of brain-heart-gut interactions and a methodology with strong biomarker development potential.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注清醒健康人静息状态下脑、心、胃三者之间的电生理交互，利用同步采集的脑电、心电和胃电记录，提取各器官活动的时变功率动态，并在较宽的时间延迟范围内量化三者之间的统计关联，再用替代数据检验确认交互并非偶然。结果显示，脑—心—胃交互主要发生在超慢时间尺度（约0.01—0.1 Hz），一个器官的自发波动通常随后伴随另外两个器官的相应变化，且三器官构成多方向网络，身体动态向中线中央—后部脑电区域汇聚，这一网络拓扑在受试者间较为一致。作者据此认为，这是对脑—心—胃交互生理特征的初步刻画，并为基于网络动态开发跨器官系统失调的生物标志物提供了方法学基础；相关发现尚属关联性证据，其临床意义有待进一步验证。

papers.title: A Molecular Communication Channel Model for Early Epileptic Seizure Detection via Synaptic Glutamate Dynamics.
papers.authors: Ozcan S, Akan OB.
papers.abstract: Molecular communication (MC) is a bio-inspired paradigm that models information transfer through molecules and provides an approach to analyze biological processes. Positioning neurological signaling within this framework enables a communication-theoretic view of disorders such as epilepsy. Epileptic seizures originate from microscopic neurotransmitter dynamics. Current prediction methods rely on EEG, which captures only macroscopic activity and often misses early preictal buildup. We propose an MC framework that models microscale synaptic glutamate signaling as a channel shaped by diffusion, clearance, and finite-receptor binding. Our Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) and Chemical Master Equation (CME) combined model yields impulse response and validates stochastic binding. Further analysis shows how synaptic parameters influence detection dynamics. Framing seizure prediction as a threshold-crossing detection problem aligns with latency and reliability metrics in communication theory, positioning MC as a promising framework for next-generation molecular-level seizure detection.

papers.title: Multimodal Analysis of Brain Network Abnormalities in Autism Spectrum Disorder: a Graph Neural Network-based Fusion Investigation of EEG and fNIRS.
papers.authors: Li Y, Zhang L, Hou L, Wan L, Zhu G, Yang G, Li R.
papers.abstract: Objective This study aimed to identify brain network abnormalities of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) by analyzing multimodal neuroimaging data through graph neural networks (GNNs), laying a technical foundation for future machine learning-based neuroimaging analysis. Methods We employed combined electroencephalogram (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to capture brain activity of 58 ASD children and 63 age- and gender-matched typically developing (TD) children. The concurrent EEG and fNIRS data were fused using an enhanced GNN to identify ASD with high accuracy. Key connections and regions of interest (ROIs) were identified for each group, followed by graph theory metrics (e.g., local efficiency) and topological data analysis (TDA) to quantify group differences. Results The proposed GNN model achieved 84% accuracy, outperforming the single-modality approach. Analysis of subgraph created by the model showed that the two groups exhibited different neural patterns in motor-language integration and lateralization, a key basis for GNN models to distinguish between the two groups. Individuals with ASD may also have topological defects such as lower average local efficiency and a lack of high-order structures. Conclusion The proposed framework effectively captures quantitative insights ranging from specific connection-level variations to network-level differences, identifying candidate discriminative connectivity patterns within this cohort. Significance This study establishes a multimodal deep learning framework that identifies candidate discriminative topological signatures from fused EEG-fNIRS data, providing preliminary within-cohort classification evidence and an exploratory topological analysis framework.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究用图神经网络融合脑电与功能性近红外光谱数据，分析孤独症谱系障碍儿童与典型发育儿童在脑网络上的差异，并尝试据此区分两组。融合模型在组内分类中表现优于单一模态，其识别依据主要来自运动—语言整合与偏侧化方面不同的神经活动模式；同时，孤独症儿童还表现出局部效率较低、缺乏高阶结构等拓扑特征。作者将这些连接层面和网络层面的差异视为该队列内的候选判别性拓扑标志，并强调结果属于初步的组内分类证据和探索性分析，尚不能直接推广为临床诊断或治疗依据。

papers.title: InFACT: Bridging Visual Variance With Semantic Invariance Via Informed Adapter Tuning for Cross-Subject Video Seizure Detection.
papers.authors: Shu K, Wu L, Jia J, Liu A, Wang L, Qian R, Chen X.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.abstract: Timely seizure detection is vital for patient intervention. Video-based approaches offer a non-contact, patient-friendly alternative to traditional EEG monitoring. However, their effectiveness is fundamentally hindered by the significant visual variance of seizure behaviors both within and across patients. While existing methods attempt to mitigate this via complex feature extraction, they struggle to eliminate the impact of variance, particularly under drastic appearance shifts caused by complex poses or environmental clutter. Crucially, we observe that although pixel-level appearances fluctuate, the clinical semantics of seizure actions can remain invariant across patients sharing similar semiological patterns. To this end, we propose InFACT (Informed Fusion Adapter with Consistent Text), a dual-branch framework that treats text as a semantic anchor to calibrate visual representations. Specifically, an Informed Fusion Adapter fine-tunes a VideoMAE, a pretrained video masked autoencoder, specializing generic motion priors into seizure-specific pathological patterns under textual guidance. Simultaneously, a Consistency-aware Text Encoder extracts stable behavioral descriptions from a Multimodal Large Language Model, filtering out task-irrelevant visual noise. Furthermore, a cross-modal contrastive learning mechanism aligns divergent visual features with these invariant semantic anchors, ensuring tight clustering of seizure classes regardless of patient identity. Experimental evaluations show that InFACT achieves 86.1% sensitivity, 89.6% specificity on the public SAH-ZU dataset, and 94.3% sensitivity, 96.5% specificity on our in-house FAH-USTC dataset, yielding consistent performance improvements over state-of-the-art methods and proving its robustness against cross-subject variability.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对跨被试视频癫痫检测中发作行为视觉差异大、现有特征提取难以消除外观变化影响的问题，提出以文本作为语义锚点校准视觉表示的双分支框架InFACT：借助文本引导的融合适配器将预训练视频模型的通用运动先验特化为癫痫病理模式，同时从多模态大语言模型提取稳定的行为描述，并通过跨模态对比学习对齐视觉特征与语义锚点。在公开数据集和自建数据集上的实验显示，该方法在敏感性和特异性上均优于现有方法，表明利用语义不变性可提升跨被试检测的稳健性；但结果来自特定数据集评估，尚不能等同于临床应用的疗效验证。

papers.title: Isoform Runx2-II is sufficient for the development of calvaria, clavicles, and limb bones in the absence of Runx2-I.
papers.authors: Matsuo Y, Yabuta S, Moriishi T, Sakane C, Komori H, Komori T.
papers.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
papers.abstract: Runx2 is an essential transcription factor for osteoblast differentiation and chondrocyte maturation. Heterozygous mutations in RUNX2 cause cleidocranial dysplasia, characterized by an open fontanel, hypoplastic clavicles, and short stature. Runx2 is transcribed from two promoters, P1 and P2, generating Runx2-II and Runx2-I, respectively. However, the function of Runx2-I remains unclear. To clarify its function, we generated Runx2-I-specific knockout mice by systematically deleting the P2 region while retaining the downstream sequence from the branch site for intron 1 splicing. As the 2.5-kb and 24-kb deletions did not disrupt P2, the deletion was extended to 76 kb (Int1del/+ mice). Because this intron contains Supt3, whose homozygous deletion was lethal on embryonic day 9.5-10.5, we crossed Int1del/+ mice with Runx2+/- mice. Cap analysis of gene expression showed that Runx2-I mRNA was absent in Int1del/+Runx2+/- mice. In newborn calvaria and 6-week-old femurs, real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction analysis showed that Runx2-II mRNA in Int1del/+Runx2+/- mice was upregulated to wild-type levels, whereas the total Runx2 mRNA was comparable to Runx2+/- mice. At E16.5 and the newborn stage, skeletal preparation and histological and micro-CT analyses showed that the impaired development of cranial bones, clavicles, and limb bones in Runx2+/- mice was rescued in Int1del/+Runx2+/- mice, whereas that of the ribs, sternum, and vertebrae was not. In 6-week-old females, reduced femoral cortical thickness in Runx2+/- mice was restored in Int1del/+Runx2+/- mice. Neither Runx2-I nor Runx2-II overexpression exhibited negative autoregulation of endogenous expression. Depending on the cell type examined, their overexpression or Runx2 knockdown differentially affected P1 and P2 reporter activities, which were also influenced by an osteoblast-specific enhancer. These findings indicate that wild-type levels of Runx2-II can substitute for Runx2-I in calvaria, clavicle, and limb bone development. Upregulation of Runx2-II in Int1del/+Runx2+/- mice cannot be explained by negative autoregulation, offering a hypothetical model of reciprocal P1/P2 regulation.

papers.title: Clinically unresponsive patients with acute brain injury activate a brain-computer interface.
papers.authors: Shen Q, Eliseyev A, Kansara V, Neves Briard J, Song YL, Carmona J, Gonzales IJ, Velazquez A, Klein AJ, Agarwal S, Park S, Ghoshal S, Roh D, Connolly ES, Claassen J.
papers.abstract: Brain activation to verbal commands can be detected by EEG in clinically unresponsive patients. These patients with cognitive motor dissociation (CMD) are unable to communicate with the environment despite preserved consciousness. Advanced brain-computer interfaces (BCI) are promising to support motor function in patients with motor neuron disease or spinal cord injury. Our primary objective was to determine if clinically unresponsive patients can control a self-paced, one-way BCI early after acute brain injury. Secondarily, we assessed the association of BCI control with short- and long-term outcomes. We conducted a prospective single-centre cohort study in 41 clinically unresponsive, critically ill and acutely brain injured patients, as well as in a convenience sample of 8 healthy volunteers and 22 conscious critically ill patients. The self-paced BCI analysed EEG in real time and modulated frequency and pitch of a tone that patients controlled by attempting a motor task: patients were provided with instructions 'to make the beep sound faster, keep opening and closing your right hand' alternating with 'to make the beep sound slower, stop opening and closing your right hand'. CMD was detected by applying machine learning to EEG recorded while patients listened to motor commands. Clinical outcomes were recovery of consciousness by hospital discharge, assessed with the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised, and recovery of functional independence at 12 months, defined as a Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended score of 4 or higher (denoting the ability to function independently for 8 h or more). Additionally, we invited conscious patients as well as family members of conscious and clinically unresponsive patients to complete a survey on perceived utility and challenges associated with the BCI. In this study, 13 clinically unresponsive patients (32%) achieved BCI control and 8 of 41 (20%) were CMD-positive. All healthy volunteers and nine conscious patients (41%) were able to control the BCI. Median signal delay for BCI control was 49.8 [interquartile range (IQR) 39.9-75.6] seconds for clinically unresponsive patients, 17.1 (IQR 7.8-19.9) for conscious patients and 15.5 (IQR 12.9-21.2) for healthy volunteers. In the group of 41 clinically unresponsive patients, 4 of 13 patients with (31%) and 1 of 28 without BCI control (4%) recovered clinical consciousness at hospital discharge [odds ratio (OR) 21.2; 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.3-930.7]. At 12 months, 6 of 13 patients with (46%) and 2 of 28 without BCI control (7%) recovered functional independence (OR 9.9; 95% CI 1.8-81.6). None of the patients that were unable to control the BCI and were CMD-negative recovered. Patients with BCI control had shorter times to recovery of functional independence by 12 months than those who did not (hazards ratio 6.0; 95% CI 1.2-30.6). All respondents of the BCI survey (n = 37) expressed strong support for the potential future use of BCI devices. These results suggest that BCI control is a strong predictor of outcomes following acute brain injury and provide initial evidence that a bedside, EEG-based BCI system might permit bidirectional communication in critically ill unresponsive patients.

papers.title: Gray matter volume is associated with pain and masticatory performance in temporomandibular disorders-related myalgia: A longitudinal MRI study.
papers.authors: Chen TC, Lin CS.
papers.journal: Cranio : the journal of craniomandibular practice
papers.abstract: Objective Neuroimaging evidence has increasingly revealed associations between brain mechanisms and temporomandibular disorders (TMD). However, current cross-sectional findings have not elucidated the neural mechanisms underlying dynamic changes in pain and mastication. This longitudinal study investigated gray matter volume (GMV) of the brain in patients with TMD-related myalgia and its associations with pain intensity and masticatory performance. Methods Twenty-one TMD patients were investigated for current pain, muscle pain, and masticatory performance before (T0 ) and after (T1 ) treatment. Among the patients, 13 received structural magnetic resonance imaging. GMV was compared between TMD patients and matched non-TMD controls, and the association between GMV at T0 and clinical variables was investigated in TMD patients. Results Between the TMD and non-TMD groups, no significant GMV differences were found. However, total GMV was significantly lower in T1 compared to T0 . Greater T0 GMV in the superior frontal gyrus and primary motor cortex was associated with greater current pain and better masticatory performance at T0 , respectively. Greater T0 GMV in the anterior insula was associated with a lower muscle pain score at T1 . Conclusion The new findings suggest that individual differences in structural brain features may be associated with pain and masticatory performance before and after TMD treatment.

papers.title: Neuropharmacology of language: ERP evidence for catecholaminergic modulation of syntactic processing.
papers.authors: Tan Y, Lewis AG, Schmits IC, Verkes RJ, Cools R, Hagoort P.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: A few studies have shown that brain catecholamines are implicated in language comprehension. However, the specific cognitive processes they modulate remain underexplored. We hypothesized that catecholamines enhance the unification of syntactic roles and word meanings into coherent multiword structures. This study combined electroencephalography and psychopharmacology to examine the effects of a catecholaminergic stimulant (methylphenidate) on processing sentences containing local syntactic ambiguities. Methylphenidate amplified the P600 event-related potential effect, which has been linked to the recruitment of cognitive resources for processing sentences with increased syntactic load. The drug's impact on semantic processing was subtler, showing a suggestive attenuation of the N400 effect to ambiguous sentences. Furthermore, the increase in the P600 effect under methylphenidate was most pronounced in participants with lower working memory capacity. This study provides evidence for linking catecholamine activity to syntactic unification in healthy individuals. Elevated catecholamine levels appear to increase the cognitive effort invested in syntactic unification, and to support the dynamic prioritization of syntactic information when contextual demands require it.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注儿茶酚胺如何调节语言理解中的句法加工，结合脑电与精神药理学方法，在健康个体中考察儿茶酚胺类兴奋剂哌甲酯对含局部句法歧义句子的影响。结果显示，哌甲酯增强了与句法负载加工资源投入相关的P600效应，而对语义加工的影响较弱，仅提示歧义句的N400效应可能减弱；P600效应的增强在工作记忆容量较低的参与者中更为明显。作者据此认为，儿茶酚胺水平升高可能增加句法统一加工中投入的认知努力，并在情境需要时支持句法信息的动态优先处理，为儿茶酚胺活动与健康人句法统一加工的关联提供了证据。

papers.title: Neural sensitivity to peer rejection predicts depressive symptoms and daily mood in adolescents.
papers.authors: Kim N, Treves IN, Li LY, Sarkas SE, Durham K, Pagliaccio D, Allen NB, Shankman SA, Auerbach RP.
papers.abstract: Understanding the role of peer feedback, particularly rejection, is critical for adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the neurophysiological markers core to peer feedback, especially those that may presage risk for depression, are unclear. Adolescents (N = 179; ages 13-18; healthy controls n = 62, remitted MDD n = 80, current MDD n = 37) completed a baseline clinical assessment and a revised Chatroom Task during EEG recording, from which the P3 to peer acceptance and rejection feedback was quantified. Over 12 months, daily mood and keyboard inputs from adolescents' smartphones were passively obtained. Linear models evaluated whether the P3 difference between rejection and acceptance (ΔP3) prospectively predicted depressive severity and average daily mood. Exploratory natural language processing examined whether friendship-focused social communication moderated the association between neural sensitivity to peer feedback and subsequent clinical outcomes. Group and feedback type interacted in predicting P3 amplitude (F(2176) = 4.84, p = 0.009): adolescents with current MDD showed larger P3 amplitudes to rejection than acceptance, whereas remitted MDD showed elevated amplitudes to both feedback types relative to controls. In a general linear model adjusting for age, sex, site, and baseline depression severity, the Group × ΔP3 interaction was significant in predicting severity at follow-up (b = 0.092, p = 0.045); higher ΔP3 predicted higher follow-up severity in current MDD, but not in remitted MDD or healthy controls. Across the full sample, larger ΔP3 was associated with lower average daily mood over 12 months (b = -1.673, p = 0.045). These findings suggest that enhanced neural sensitivity to peer rejection may be deeply engrained in adolescent depression, shaping both the longitudinal course of depressive symptoms and daily mood.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察青少年对同伴接纳与拒绝反馈的神经敏感性（以脑电P3波幅衡量）能否前瞻性预测抑郁症状和日常情绪，对象包括健康青少年、抑郁缓解者与当前抑郁者，并结合智能手机被动采集的日常情绪数据。结果显示，当前抑郁青少年对拒绝反馈的P3波幅大于接纳反馈，而缓解者对两类反馈的波幅均高于健康对照；对拒绝的相对敏感性越高，随访时抑郁越重，这一关联仅见于当前抑郁组，且在全样本中与随后一年平均日常情绪较低相关。作者据此认为，对同伴拒绝的神经敏感性增强可能已深植于青少年抑郁之中，并与其症状走向和日常情绪相关，但研究属预测性关联，尚不能说明因果或治疗效应。

papers.title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex.
papers.authors: Chakravarthula LNC, Ito T, Tzalavras A, Cole MW.
papers.abstract: Flexible cognition requires the brain to generalize across tasks while preserving task-specific information. Previous work showed that task representations are compressed in the association cortex and expanded in sensory and motor systems, but the mechanisms underlying these transformations are unclear. Here we test whether the geometry of intrinsic brain connectivity constrains how representations change between cortical regions. We analyzed functional MRI acquired during 16 diverse cognitive tasks together with activity flow modeling, finding that connectivity dimensionality predicts representational changes across the cortex. Low-dimensional connectivity compressed task representations and increased similarities across tasks, whereas high-dimensional connectivity expanded representations and supported conjunctive coding of task features. Activity flow modeling reproduced the observed compression-to-expansion pattern along the sensory-association-motor hierarchy and generated representational geometries that more closely matched targets than sources, consistent with transformation rather than transfer of information. These findings identify network geometry as a systems-level principle that shapes cortical representations and supports flexible cognition.

papers.title: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease.
papers.authors: Harasymiw L, Kuang A, Xu D, Scheffler A, George E, Peyvandi S, McQuillen P.
papers.abstract: Background Infants with critical congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk for abnormal brain development and later neurodevelopmental impairment. We hypothesized that the trajectory of perioperative whole-brain network development would predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood. Methods This prospective longitudinal cohort of neonates with critical CHD (n = 97) underwent preoperative and/or postoperative brain MRI with diffusion imaging. Whole-brain network measures were derived from structural connectomes from 80 infants, and 50 had neurodevelopment assessed at 1-4 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development. Results White matter injury was associated with a slower perioperative increase in global efficiency (p = 0.013), a measure of network integration, whereas cardiac physiology was not associated with network development. Infants with greater perioperative increases in global efficiency had higher cognitive (p = 0.001), language (p < 0.001), and motor (p = 0.008) scores. For each 1-standard deviation increase in the trajectory of global efficiency, cognitive scores increased by 8.2 points (95% CI: 3.64-12.78), independent of brain injury and socioeconomic factors. Conclusion In infants with critical CHD, longitudinal whole-brain network development was associated with neurodevelopment across multiple domains. Early network development may serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience in this population. Impact In infants with critical congenital heart disease, perioperative increase in whole-brain network integration was associated with cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood. White matter injury was associated with a slower increase in network integration, whereas cardiac physiology subtype was not associated with network development. This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注危重先天性心脏病新生儿围手术期全脑网络发育轨迹能否预测早期神经发育结局，对患儿在术前和/或术后进行扩散成像并构建结构连接组，部分患儿在幼儿期接受发育评估。结果显示，围手术期全脑网络整合（全局效率）增长较快的患儿，其认知、语言和运动得分更高，且这一关联独立于脑损伤和社会经济因素；白质损伤与网络整合增长较慢相关，而心脏生理类型与网络发育无关。作者据此认为，纵向追踪新生儿全脑网络发育而非单次影像，可能作为该人群神经发育风险与韧性的潜在生物标志物，但相关发现尚属关联性证据，其临床用于风险分层和干预仍需后续研究验证。

papers.title: Neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulation: A systematic review of task-based neuroimaging studies.
papers.authors: Pu M, Ma Q.
papers.abstract: Objective Adequate sleep is essential for physiological, cognitive, and mental functioning. While epidemiological and behavioral studies show that sleep restriction or sleep deprivation is associated with altered responses to food stimuli, the neural mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. The preregistered systematic review synthesized evidence from task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging studies examining neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulations, including sleep deprivation or sleep restriction. Method Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and American Psychological Association PsycInfo, yielding 11 eligible studies, including nine with adult samples and two with adolescent samples. We extracted the data, assessed the risk of bias, and conducted a qualitative synthesis. Results Across studies with adult samples, six visual food-cue studies generally reported stronger brain activity following sleep deprivation or sleep restriction, particularly in the striatum, insula, anterior cingulate cortex, and inferior frontal gyrus. Two food valuation studies, including a willingness-to-pay and food-desire task, showed enhanced neural activity in the amygdala and hypothalamus during food valuation. Moreover, one study using a food odor perception paradigm showed that sleep deprivation altered chemosensory and interoceptive processing by enhancing food odor encoding in the piriform cortex. Two adolescent studies reported distinct neural findings. Conclusions Together, these findings highlight that experimentally induced sleep deprivation or sleep restriction does not uniformly enhance reward-related brain activity; rather, it is associated with task-dependent changes in neural responses to food-related stimuli. However, the limited and heterogeneous evidence limits conclusions regarding common neural mechanisms. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Adult aphasic status epilepticus: A systematic review and patient-level synthesis of clinical phenotypes and multimodal diagnostic evidence.
papers.authors: Chu QC, Do TT.
papers.abstract: Background Aphasic status epilepticus (ASE) is an uncommon manifestation of focal status epilepticus in which aphasia is the sole or predominant clinical feature. Recognition may be difficult because consciousness can be relatively preserved, convulsive activity may be absent, and the presentation can mimic acute stroke. Objective To characterize diagnostic phenotypes of adult ASE and synthesize clinical, electrographic, and neuroimaging features across published cases. Methods We conducted a systematic review and patient-level synthesis of adult ASE cases. Eligible patients were adjudicated as definite or probable ASE using prespecified criteria. Clinical phenotype, electroencephalographic (EEG) findings, neuroimaging, initial diagnostic impressions, treatment, and language outcomes were extracted. Results Ninety-nine publications contributed 168 adults with ASE, including 89 definite and 79 probable cases. Aphasia was the sole manifestation in 42.9% and predominant in 57.1%, while consciousness was preserved in 78.0%. Ictal EEG activity or electrographic status epilepticus was documented in 53.0%, and 41.7% had supportive epileptiform abnormalities. Among cases with interpretable EEG laterality, 92.7% were left-lateralized. Peri-ictal MRI abnormalities occurred in 41.2% of performed interpretable studies. Among 55 patients with interpretable functional perfusion or metabolic imaging, hyperperfusion was reported in 32. FDG-PET hypermetabolism was treated as a distinct metabolic finding. Stroke or transient ischemic attack was the most frequent reported initial impression (44.2%). Complete language recovery was reported in 77.4% of evaluable patients. Conclusions Published adult ASE cases show a heterogeneous phenotype in which recognition commonly rests on concordance between language disturbance and focal EEG abnormalities, with peri-ictal imaging providing complementary evidence. These findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy of individual features or multimodal combinations.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究通过系统综述与患者层面汇总，分析成人失语性癫痫持续状态的临床表型及诊断特征。共纳入已发表病例，多数患者意识保留、无惊厥发作，失语可为唯一或主要表现，脑电图常见左侧偏侧化癫痫样异常，部分患者出现围发作期影像学改变。作者指出，该病识别常依赖语言障碍与局灶性脑电图异常的对应，影像学提供补充证据，但现有资料尚不能确定单一特征或多模态组合的诊断准确性。

papers.title: Gamma-band network segregation links corollary discharge dysfunction and anomalous self-experiences in schizophrenia.
papers.authors: Beño-Ruiz-de-la-Sierra RM, Arjona-Valladares A, Osorio-Iriarte E, Sobrino-Conde L, Rodríguez V, Núñez P, Poza J, Roig-Herrero A, Díez Á, Molina V.
papers.abstract: Anomalous self-experiences (ASEs) are a core feature of psychotic disorders and reflect disturbances in ipseity. Impairments in corollary discharge mechanism have been proposed as a neurobiological substrate of ASEs, and an imbalance between brain network integration and segregation, may impair the coherent flow of mental contents, thereby disrupting their fluid and implicit character. However, the relationship between corollary discharge and functional network properties has not been directly examined. This link was assessed in thirty participants with schizophrenia and thirty healthy controls. Functional network was computed using the Phase Locking Value (PLV) from resting-state EEG in the gamma band and two parameters were calculated: the clustering coefficient (ClC, as a proxy for segregation) and the path length (PL, as a proxy for integration); corollary discharge was indexed by N1 suppression in a talk-listen paradigm; and ASEs were evaluated using the 'Inventory of Psychotic-Like Anomalous Self-Experiences' (IPASE) total score. Patients with schizophrenia showed significantly greater gamma-band network segregation and lower integration than healthy controls. Moreover, higher segregation in this band was associated with reduced N1 suppression and greater ASEs severity in patients, whereas network integration was not associated with N1 suppression nor ASEs. These findings suggest that excessive gamma-band network segregation may be correlated with disrupted corollary discharge functioning and may compromise the distinction between self-generated and external stimuli. Therefore, it may alter the sense of ipseity by interfering with the integration of mental contents into the flow of consciousness, thereby contributing to greater severity of ASEs.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察精神分裂症中复制放电（corollary discharge）功能与静息态脑功能网络组织之间的关系，以及二者如何与异常自我体验（ASEs）相关联。研究比较了精神分裂症参与者和健康对照者，用脑电gamma频段的功能连接计算网络分离与整合指标，以听-说范式中的N1抑制作为复制放电的指标，并用IPASE量表评估异常自我体验。结果发现，患者gamma频段网络分离程度更高、整合程度更低；在患者中，分离程度越高，N1抑制越弱、异常自我体验越严重，而整合程度与这两者均无关联。作者据此提出，gamma频段网络过度分离可能与复制放电功能受损相关，进而影响对自我生成刺激与外部刺激的区分，并可能通过干扰心理内容融入意识流而改变自我感，从而与更严重的异常自我体验相关；这些均为相关性发现，尚不能说明因果关系。

papers.title: Reduced short-lag autoregressive carry-over in resting-state latent dynamics in major depressive disorder.
papers.authors: Yamaki N, Churiki T.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is increasingly characterized as a disorder of brain dynamics, but the temporal scale on which resting-state activity differs from healthy controls remains unclear. We analyzed resting-state fMRI data from 71 participants (51 MDD, 20 controls; OpenNeuro ds002748) using bilateral grid-extracted left-right difference signals projected into a control-defined latent space. Across 30 analysis configurations spanning five denoising pipelines, three latent dimensionalities, and two left-right correction settings, MDD showed reduced mean lag-1 autocorrelation in 24 of 30 configurations (integrated β = -0.0321, p = 0.036) and reduced AR(1) gain φ in 24 of 30 (β = -0.0316, p = 0.037), both robust to adjustment for pipeline, age, sex, and head motion. The broader autocorrelation area under lags 1-10 was not significantly reduced (β = -0.0099, p = 0.22), and lag-by-lag analysis localized the group difference specifically to lag 1. A model-comparison analysis identified AR-gain reduction as one of three competing candidate generative transformations rather than the unique winner. MDD is thus associated with a focal short-lag autoregressive carry-over reduction, a candidate latent-dynamical phenotype rather than a fully identified mechanism.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注重性抑郁障碍患者静息态脑活动在何种时间尺度上与健康人不同，利用静息态功能磁共振数据，将左右差异信号投影到对照定义的潜在空间后分析其时间动态。结果显示，患者在多个分析配置下普遍表现出滞后一阶自相关和自回归增益降低，而更长滞后范围的自相关未见显著减弱，提示差异集中在短滞后时间尺度上。模型比较进一步表明，自回归增益降低只是若干竞争性候选生成变换之一，并非唯一解释。作者据此提出，短滞后自回归延续性减弱可能是抑郁的一个潜在动力学表型，但尚不能视为已确定的机制。

papers.title: Altered Cortico-cerebellar effective connectivity of the Visuo-attentional system is associated with READ1 deletion in developmental dyslexia.
papers.authors: Korkmaz G, Lorenzi RM, Lampis V, Peruzzo D, Arrigoni F, Pischedda D, D'Angelo E, Palesi F, Mascheretti S, Gandini Wheeler-Kingshott CAM.
papers.abstract: Developmental dyslexia (DD) is a heritable neurodevelopmental disorder associated with altered brain connectivity. The influence of genetic risks on cortico-cerebellar effective connectivity (EC) remains unclear. The present study investigates how reading proficiency and the READ1 deletion (READ1d) in the DCDC2 gene modulate visuo-attentional network dynamics. Functional MRI data were acquired in 78 children (DD and typical readers, with/without READ1d) performing a coherent motion detection task. EC within a seven-region visuo-attentional network, including magnocellular, ventral attention, and cerebellar (crus I) regions, was estimated using Dynamic Causal Modelling. Group-level effects were assessed using Parametric Empirical Bayes within a hierarchical Bayesian framework, testing reading proficiency, READ1d status, and their interaction (posterior probability threshold, Pp > 0.95). Reading proficiency was associated with increased cerebellar influence on visual and frontal regions, alongside reduced intra-cortical connectivity within dorsal stream pathways. The presence of READ1d was associated with reduced EC from primary visual and cerebellar regions to magnocellular and ventral attention networks, and increased intra-cortical interactions. The interaction between DD and READ1d revealed further reductions in cortico-cerebellar connectivity and altered network dynamics. Group-level analyses revealed EC differences in cortico-cerebellar pathways, which are reported as exploratory findings. Cortico-cerebellar EC is modulated by both reading proficiency and genetic susceptibility. Altered cerebellar contributions to visuo-attentional processes may represent a potential imaging-genetic signature of dyslexia, warranting replication in independent samples and validation through longitudinal and multimodal approaches.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注发展性阅读障碍中遗传风险如何影响视觉注意系统的皮层—小脑有效连接，对78名儿童（含阅读障碍与典型阅读者、携带或不携带DCDC2基因READ1缺失）在相干运动检测任务中的功能磁共振数据，用动态因果模型和分层贝叶斯方法估计七区域网络的有效连接。结果显示，阅读能力与更强的小脑对视觉和额叶区域的影响以及背侧通路内连接减弱相关；READ1缺失则与初级视觉和小脑区域向大细胞及腹侧注意网络的连接减弱、皮层内交互增强相关，二者交互还伴随进一步的皮层—小脑连接下降和网络动态改变。作者将这些组水平差异作为探索性发现，认为小脑对视觉注意过程的贡献改变可能是阅读障碍的潜在影像—遗传标志，但尚需独立样本重复及纵向和多模态验证。

papers.title: Structural brain correlates of symptom severity in stress-induced exhaustion.
papers.authors: Björnsdotter M, Cully SA, Hermansson M, McCulloch S, Petrovic P.
