Neither finding was observed in the placebo group (p=0.211 and p=0.161, respectively), although the correlation did not differ significantly between groups (p for interaction=0.728). Other clinical, sociodemographic, psychological and psychophysical variables were not associated with response. In the subsample with peripheral neuropathic pain and structural MRI (n=37), lower left precentral cortex volume was associated with response to methadone (p=0.041), and lower right paracentral volume with response to placebo (p=0.003). Conclusions Baseline expectation may influence treatment outcomes, supporting its inclusion as a covariate to improve the precision of treatment effect estimates in trials, and its use in clinical practice to help tailor treatment to individual patients. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies. Significance statement Predictors of opioid response in chronic neuropathic pain remain poorly understood, and treatment expectation has received little attention in this setting. In this study, a single baseline rating of expected improvement identified methadone responders more consistently than pain phenotype, conditioned pain modulation or other psychological traits. These results support considering patient expectation both when interpreting opioid trials and when discussing likely benefit with patients before starting treatment.

papers.title: Revisiting Parakinesia Brachialis Oscitans: You Yawn, I Move! A Scoping Review.
papers.authors: Vasireddy RP, Vivanco RA, Koppanatham A, Lenka A.
papers.journal: Tremor and other hyperkinetic movements (New York, N.Y.)
papers.abstract: Background Parakinesia brachialis oscitans (PBO) is a rarely reported phenomenon in which a paretic limb moves involuntarily during yawning. The literature consists predominantly of case reports and small series, with limited comparative evidence. Methods We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from inception to 28 August 2026, with backward citation searching. Eligible reports described one or more patients with an involuntary, stereotyped, yawn-locked movement of a paretic limb after a focal central nervous system lesion, with the lesion site reported on neuroimaging. Data included demographics, movement description, latency, lesion site, etiology, and outcome. Results Twenty-two reports describing 31 patients met the inclusion criteria. Most patients were men (67.7%), with a mean age of 56.1 years. PBO involved the upper limb alone in 29 patients (93.5%). Acute ischemic stroke was the most common etiology (83.9%). Lesions were often seen in the internal capsule (44.4%) and the corona radiata or subcortical white matter (40.7%). Onset ranged from immediate to four months after the lesion. Complete resolution was documented in 10 patients (32.3%), PBO persisted for up to three years in five, and outcome was not reported in 15 (48.4%). Discussion PBO is associated with focal lesions affecting distributed voluntary motor-control networks, frequently involving subcortical motor pathways. Although no mechanism has been established, the observations suggest a release of preserved brainstem and extrapyramidal circuits. Outcome was unreported in almost half the cases; prospective, standardized reporting is needed to clarify its course and prognostic significance. Highlights This scoping review gathered 22 reports describing 31 patients with PBO after a focal brain injury.PBO involved the upper limb alone in 29 patients and lesions were most commonly subcortical, involving the internal capsule.Onset ranged from presentation to four months and PBO persisted for up to three years. However, the outcome was not reported in half of the included cases.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述系统梳理了打哈欠时瘫痪肢体不自主运动的文献，共纳入22篇报告、31例患者，多数为男性，以急性缺血性卒中后上肢受累为主，病灶多位于内囊及放射冠或皮层下白质。作者指出，这类现象与累及随意运动控制网络、尤其是皮层下运动通路的局灶性病变相关，但机制尚未确立，现有观察提示脑干和锥体外系环路可能被释放。由于近半数病例未报告结局，作者强调需要前瞻性、标准化的报告来明确其病程和预后意义。

papers.title: A Cell Culture Insert-Based Protocol for Constructing a Simplified Multicellular In Vitro Blood-Tumor Barrier Model of Breast Cancer Brain Metastasis.
papers.authors: Du B, Zhang Q, Li B, Qiu Y, Bai X, Cheng M, Gu N, Zhu S, Li X.
papers.abstract: Effective treatments for breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM) remain limited, largely because the blood-tumor barrier (BTB) restricts the entry of many chemotherapeutic and targeted agents into metastatic lesions within the central nervous system. To model selected features of this complex microenvironment in vitro, this study presents a standardized protocol for constructing a simplified multicellular three-dimensional BTB model. The method comprises three core steps. First, a blood-brain barrier (BBB) compartment is constructed using cell culture inserts with a 0.4 μm pore size. Human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs) are seeded on the basal side of the porous membrane, and 1 day later, human astrocytes (HA) and human microglial HMC3 cells (HMC3) are seeded on the apical side.Using SK-BR-3 cells as an example, breast cancer cells are cultured by the hanging drop method to form uniform, regularly shaped 3D tumor spheroids after 3 days of culture. The spheroids are then transferred to the apical side of a basement membrane matrix-coated porous membrane, which provides physical separation while allowing chemical communication between the barrier cells and tumor spheroids during co-culture. This platform enables precise control of the experimental timeline and produces astrocytic morphological and marker changes consistent with a peritumoral reactive response while allowing assessment of endothelial barrier integrity and paracellular permeability.

papers.title: Clinical Phenotypes, Neuroimaging, and Outcomes in Prolonged and Persistent Non-Motor Migraine Aura: A Systematic Review and Episode-Level Synthesis.
papers.authors: Meiramova A, Ainabekova B, Tursynbet Y, Akhmetova Z.
papers.abstract: Background/objectives Prolonged and persistent migraine aura may mimic cerebral ischemia, but its clinical course and neuroimaging features are poorly characterized. We synthesized episode-level evidence on non-motor aura lasting more than 60 min without reported established infarction. Methods This systematic review (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews [PROSPERO] CRD420261461238) followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to August 2026 and the searches were rerun with an extended strategy on 5 October 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching. Eligible reports provided individual-episode clinical data and temporally related neuroimaging. Owing to publication selection, heterogeneous reporting, and clustering, the synthesis was descriptive. Results Forty-eight studies described 80 episodes in 79 individuals (49 prolonged; 31 persistent). Visual aura occurred in 63/80 episodes. Although magnetic resonance imaging was performed in 77/80 episodes, patient-level informative diffusion imaging was available in only 28/80 and imaging-based perfusion data in 28/80. Five of the 28 episodes with informative diffusion imaging were diffusion-positive (17.9%); the acute apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) was reduced in 3, non-restricted in 1, and unreported in 1, and all diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) abnormalities resolved on follow-up. Unusual imaging findings are more likely to be published; this proportion is therefore hypothesis-generating rather than a frequency estimate. In the longer-follow-up stratum, aura improvement was reported in 36/36 prolonged and 18/22 persistent episodes, with complete resolution in 35/35 and 15/22, respectively; a nerve-block series with a fixed 24-h assessment (14 episodes) was analyzed separately. Conclusions Published cases show heterogeneous phenotypes and cannot support estimates of prognosis or treatment effectiveness. Standardized prospective data collection should incorporate symptom-level duration, imaging timing, DWI/ADC reporting, treatment timing, and protocol-defined follow-up.

papers.title: Song Patterns and Stridulatory Movements in Conocephalus Species (Orthoptera: Tettigonioidea: Conocephalidae) of the Eastern Hemisphere: A Review with Some New Data.
papers.authors: Heller KG, Ali A, Jaiswara R.
papers.abstract: Conocephalus is a speciose, worldwide distributed genus of small bush-crickets (=katydids; Orthoptera, Tettigonioidea). While some of its species have huge ranges covering several continents, forms occurring in both hemispheres are not known. Partly due to their large ranges and because of morphological similarity, the correct identification of species is often not easy. Here, we present a review of the acoustic communication of all species with known songs in the eastern hemisphere. The species-specific amplitude pattern of the calling songs offers a helpful tool to find out which species are involved. Our results-using data from published sound files on compact discs, internet resources and conventional papers-show that species have the same species-specific songs all over their range. In addition to some misidentifications and situations which require further studies, however, we recover the widespread Conocephalus maculatus as a species complex with an Asiatic taxon (C. maculatus s.str.) and an African taxon (could be called Conocephalus continuus ), both differing in song. The Indian Conocephalus hilli is considered a synonym (form) of C. maculatus.

papers.title: Association of Mandibular Morphological and Trabecular Bone Characteristics with Long-Term Outcomes Following First Permanent Molar Extraction: A Retrospective Study.
papers.authors: Bas Ozturk A, Urvasizoglu G, Abdulkader R, Sariyeva N, Sengul F.
papers.abstract: Background/Purpose: This study aimed to evaluate mandibular morphological, trabecular, dental, and periapical factors associated with favorable long-term outcomes following early mandibular first permanent molar (FPM) extraction. Methods: This retrospective study included 60 patients with pre-extraction and ≥5-year follow-up panoramic radiographs. Patients were classified into favorable (FO; n = 30) and unfavorable (UFO; n = 30) outcome groups according to residual space and second permanent molar (SPM) axial position. Gonial angle (GA), antegonial notch depth (AND), notch angle (ANA), cortical thickness (ACT), and corpus and angulus fractal dimensions (FD) were assessed. Initial SPM and second premolar (SP)angulations, primary second molar (PSM)-SP status, and FPM periapical index (PAI) scores were also evaluated. Analyses included Bonferroni correction, exploratory multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results: AND was greater in the FO group (Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.015) and remained associated with FO after adjustment (OR = 2.22 per millimeter; 95% CI: 1.19-4.15; p = 0.012). An extracted PSM with an unerupted SP was associated with higher odds of FO than a retained PSM (adjusted OR = 9.51; 95% CI: 1.45-62.50; p = 0.019). AND demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC = 0.728; 95% CI: 0.600-0.856); a ≥2.0-mm threshold yielded 86.7% sensitivity and 53.3% specificity. Other morphological and fractal parameters did not differ significantly between groups; angulations and PAI were not significantly associated with outcome. Conclusions: AND and PSM-SP status were associated with FO. These exploratory findings require validation in larger, independent cohorts before clinical application, particularly given the wide confidence intervals for categorical estimates and the limited specificity of the proposed AND threshold.

papers.title: Auditory Stimulation-Evoked Frontoparietal Theta Asymmetry for Subtype Classification and Long-Term Prognosis Prediction in Disorders of Consciousness.
papers.authors: Chen C, Hu Y, Wang S, Zhang X, Zheng S, Han J, Wang K.
papers.abstract: Background : Quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG) facilitates the objective assessment of residual brain function in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC), which addresses the intrinsic limitations of behavioral assessment methods. Nevertheless, the characteristics of frontoparietal neural oscillation asymmetry between resting state and auditory stimulation state have not been fully elucidated, and its incremental prognostic value for DOC subtype classification and outcome prediction remains to be confirmed. Methods : Fifty-seven patients with DOC and 23 healthy controls completed qEEG recordings at baseline and during auditory stimulation. Interhemispheric asymmetry indices of the frontal lobe and parietal lobe were calculated for the theta band and alpha band. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) were adopted to test the main effects and interaction effects of diagnosis, brain region and stimulation condition. The correlations between asymmetry indicators, Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R) scores and 6-month Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) scores were analyzed. Nested logistic regression and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed to quantify the incremental prognostic value of oscillatory asymmetry beyond conventional clinical variables; odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for all predictive indicators. Internal leave-one-out cross-validation and external cohort validation were performed to assess the generalizability and robustness of the final prognostic model. Results : Significant diagnosis × region interaction effects were observed in both frequency bands. Vegetative state (VS) patients presented with frontal-dominant asymmetry, while minimally conscious state (MCS) patients showed parietal-dominant asymmetry; this dissociative pattern was significantly amplified after auditory stimulation. Only stimulation-evoked theta asymmetry showed consistent correlations with clinical status and prognosis: frontal theta asymmetry was negatively correlated with CRS-R scores, while parietal theta asymmetry was positively correlated with CRS-R scores and 6-month GOS outcomes. Incorporating stimulated frontoparietal theta asymmetry significantly improved prognostic performance, and the area under the curve (AUC) of the optimal model reached 0.930. Conclusions : VS and MCS present distinct frontoparietal oscillatory asymmetry phenotypes, which are specifically enhanced by auditory stimulation. Stimulation-evoked theta band asymmetry can reflect residual conscious function and provides incremental prognostic value for long-term functional recovery, with robust generalizability verified by internal and external validation.

papers.title: Biological and Clinical Applications of Dimethyl Sulfoxide: Evidence and Safety Considerations.
papers.authors: Huang Z, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is a polar aprotic solvent used in biomedical research, pharmaceutical formulation, some clinical applications, and cryopreservation. Here we review molecular activity related to DMSO and selected clinical applications including interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS), musculoskeletal and traumatic injury, central nervous system (CNS) trauma, cardiovascular and ischemic injury, historical oncology research, local applications, cryopreservation and safety. Of the applications discussed, intravesical DMSO has the clearest contemporary clinical support in selected patients with IC/BPS, particularly those with Hunner-type disease, although its role in non-Hunner disease remains uncertain. This concentration may partly reflect DMSO's limited regulatory approval for therapeutic use, rather than comparative evaluation across indications. Mixed findings have been reported for other applications: modest pain relief has been observed in knee osteoarthritis, whereas no benefit has been found in systemic sclerosis ulcers, where substantial skin intolerance has also been reported. Small uncontrolled clinical series reported reductions in intracranial pressure following intravenous DMSO administration. Walker's monograph separately described neurological recovery after CNS trauma, but concurrent treatment and incomplete documentation limit causal attribution. Reduced intracranial pressure alone does not establish long-term neurological benefit. Historical oncology reports described DMSO-containing hematoxylin preparations, including "haematoxylon", but evidence of antitumor efficacy remains insufficient. Historical ocular and otic applications involved diverse formulations but limited controlled clinical assessment. Cardiovascular protection remains supported mainly by preclinical research. DMSO is an effective cryoprotectant but residual exposure may cause infusion reactions and removal after thaw adds to the processing burden and potential cell loss. Biological activity and risk vary with concentration, route, duration, formulation, material quality, and biological setting. Historical narratives identify questions for further study but do not establish clinical efficacy. This review summarizes reported DMSO effects and risks, examines study limitations, and identifies unresolved research questions.

papers.title: Age-Related Decrease in Interthalamic Adhesion Thickness in Cats Without Apparent Cognitive Dysfunction.
papers.authors: Kerbrat-Copy R, Thérier O, Fusellier M.
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.abstract: Feline cognitive dysfunction syndrome (FCDS) is an age-associated disorder for which objective imaging markers remain limited. This study evaluated the association between age and interthalamic adhesion thickness (IAT) in cats without apparent cognitive dysfunction and described IAT across feline life stages. MRI examinations from 112 client-owned cats aged 4 months to 18 years were retrospectively reviewed. Cats were classified as kittens (<1 year), young (1 to < 7 years), mature (7 to <11 years) and senior (≥11 years). Cats with intracranial lesions or reported behavioral changes suggestive of cognitive dysfunction were excluded. Two blinded observers measured IAT on transverse T1W and T2W images. Analyses included linear regression adjusted for brain height, brain width, sex/neuter status, breed group, and scanner; exploratory quadratic age modeling; and comparisons among life stages. Interobserver agreement was high. Age was negatively associated with IAT on T1W (B = -0.071 mm/year) and T2W images (B = -0.067 mm/year; both p < 0.001). This association persisted after multivariable adjustment (T1W: B = -0.074 mm/year; T2W: B = -0.067 mm/year; both p < 0.001) and after excluding kittens or brachycephalic cats. Senior cats had lower IAT than all other life stages on both sequences. A quadratic term suggested a steeper decline at older ages on T1W images only; this finding remains exploratory. These findings support a group-level association between age and IAT, rather than individual-level diagnostic use. Its potential diagnostic value for FCDS requires prospective evaluation with standardized behavioral assessment and age-matched controls.

papers.title: Age and sex differences in T1 relaxation times and volumetrics in segmented brain and upper cervical spine in healthy participants using MP2RAGE protocol at 3.0 T.
papers.authors: Nguyen VS, Welch T, Penano S, Matache IM, Arndt N, Bydon M, Carroll TJ, Javed A.
papers.abstract: Background and purpose To examine the influence of age and sex on T1 relaxation and volume in brain and upper cervical cord using MP2RAGE, which offers high contrast-to-noise ratio, uniform tissue contrast, and superior anatomical resolution alongside T1 mapping. This provides an accurate analysis of the magnitude of the effects of these covariates on the outcomes. Materials and methods 208 MP2RAGE scans from the Max Planck Institute Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body LEMON dataset were segmented and labeled using FreeSurfer and Spinal Cord Toolbox. The influences of age and sex on dependent variables were analyzed using linear regression and group difference were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. Results T1 values of cortical gray matter (GM), cerebral white matter (WM), thalamus, caudate, putamen, hippocampus, amygdala, and anterior corpus callosum (CC) varied significantly with age. Cortical GM and cervical C1 T1 showed statistical significance with sex, with latter lower in the females compared to males. T1 values of the posterior CC were significantly lower than the anterior portion. GM, WM, thalamus, caudate, putamen, hippocampus and anterior CC volumes were significantly affected by age. Spine cross-sectional area (CSA) showed statistically significant differences with sex but not age. Conclusions T1, regional brain volumes, and spinal CSA vary according to anatomical location, age, and sex, reflecting physiological differences associated with aging and sex. These results can operate as a normative baseline to gauge the magnitude of effect of these covariates on future studies in health or disease.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于健康参与者的MP2RAGE扫描，结合脑与上颈髓分割，考察年龄和性别对T1弛豫时间及体积的影响。结果显示，多个皮层灰质、白质及皮层下结构的T1值随年龄变化，皮层灰质和颈髓C1的T1值存在性别差异，女性C1的T1值更低；多个脑区体积受年龄影响，而脊髓横截面积与性别相关、与年龄无关。作者认为这些差异反映了衰老和性别相关的生理变化，可作为未来健康或疾病研究中评估协变量效应大小的参考基线。

papers.title: The Association Between Cardiorespiratory Fitness and White Matter Integrity Across the Lifespan: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: de Oliveira RM, Lox C.
papers.abstract: White matter deterioration is a hallmark of cognitive aging and a core feature of manyneurodegenerative disorders. Cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) has emerged as a modifiable factorthat may support white matter integrity across the adult lifespan. This systematic review, using anarrative synthesis, examined findings from 24 studies, identified through a systematic search ofPubMed, Web of Science, and PsycINFO databases, examining the association betweenobjectively measured CRF and neuroimaging-based white matter structure. Results revealed aconsistent positive relationship between higher CRF and stronger microstructural integrity,particularly in late-myelinating tracts such as the corpus callosum, cingulum, and longitudinalfasciculi. These associations were minimal in young adulthood, mixed in midlife, and mostrobust in adults over 60, suggesting an age-dependent neuroprotective effect that strengthensacross the lifespan. Higher CRF was also linked to reduced white matter hyperintensity (WMH)burden in older populations. While cross-sectional evidence for this relationship was largelyconsistent, findings from randomized controlled trials were considerably more mixed, with mostintervention studies failing to detect group-level improvements in white matter microstructuredespite confirmed fitness gains. These findings underscore the potential of CRF as a nonpharmacological strategy to preserve brain health and mitigate cognitive decline with age. Futureresearch should adopt longitudinal and multimodal designs to clarify causal mechanisms andidentify age-specific moderators of these effects. Keywords: cardiorespiratory fitness, white matter, fractional anisotropy, aging, aerobic exercise
papers.summary_zh: 该综述系统检索并叙述性整合了24项研究，考察客观测量的心肺适能与基于神经影像的白质结构之间的关联。结果显示，较高的心肺适能与更强的白质微结构完整性呈较一致的正相关，尤其在胼胝体、扣带束和纵束等晚髓鞘化纤维束中；这种关联在青年期很弱，中年期结果不一，在60岁以上成人中最明显，提示可能存在随年龄增强的神经保护作用，老年人中较高适能还与较低的白质高信号负担相关。横断面证据较为一致，但随机对照试验结果明显更混杂，多数干预研究尽管体能确有提升，却未检测到组水平白质微结构改善。作者据此强调心肺适能作为非药物策略的潜力，同时指出因果机制尚待纵向和多模态研究澄清。

papers.title: Patient Satisfaction with MRI Department Service and Staff in Public and Private Hospitals in Aseer, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.authors: Alelyani M.
papers.abstract: Purpose Patient satisfaction (PS) is a measure of the quality of healthcare. There is little documented evidence for PS regarding MRI services in the Aseer region of Saudi Arabia. This study aimed to evaluate the satisfaction of patients using MRI services in private and public hospitals in Aseer, Saudi Arabia, focusing on departmental services and staff performance. Patients and methods A descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted with 203 adult patients who had undergone an MRI at selected private and public hospitals in the Aseer region. The data were collected using a self-administered, structured questionnaire and analysed using SPSS software programme version 23. A five-point Likert scale was used to rate the responses. Results The mean patient satisfaction score was high (mean = 3.69, SD = 0.51). Satisfaction was significantly associated with staff providing patients with clear explanations about the MRI procedures, risks, and possible discomforts (p < 0.001); the provision of ear protection (p < 0.001); the cleanliness of the MRI facilities (p < 0.001); the speed of the registration process (p < 0.001); staff professionalism (p < 0.001); and the waiting time (p < 0.001). No significant associations were noted between satisfaction and patient demographic variables (p < 0.05). There was a highly significant correlation between satisfaction with MRI staff and satisfaction with the department services (r = 0.82, p < 0.001). Conclusion Most patients from the Aseer region reported high satisfaction with MRI services and staff. There is a need to develop and refine communication with patients, increase administrative efficiency, and introduce measures that enhance patient comfort.

papers.title: GWAS of Active Music Engagement Frequency in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging
papers.authors: Henechowicz T, Wolford B, Nitin R, Mekki Y, Scartozzi A, Coleman P, Tio E, Schlicht G, Nayak S, Thaut M, Felsky D, Gordon R.
papers.abstract: Abstract Active music engagement (AME), i.e., playing a musical instrument or singing, is moderately heritable and may support resilience to age-related functional decline. To understand AME’s genetic architecture, we conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (n=23,782 with genetically inferred European ancestry). SNP-based heritability was estimated at 11%, revealing 21 independent loci at suggestive significance (p<5×10⁻⁵). Post-GWAS analyses showed enrichment in regulatory regions of adult brain cells and genetic correlations with musical rhythm ability, language, and cognition. Secondary genetic correlation analyses (bivariate-GREML) linked AME to enhanced cognition, motor function, social engagement, and resilience to psychological distress, but also increased mood disorder risk. Lastly, bi-directional Mendelian randomization indicated that individuals who have greater genetic propensity for musical rhythm abilities are more likely to have more frequent musical instrument or singing engagement. Overall, these findings suggest that the polygenic architecture of AME is enriched for neurobiological function, specifically promoter of astrocyte function, and shares genetic variation with healthy aging.

papers.title: Multimodal mediators connecting APOE4 to dementia
papers.authors: Chen Z, Lin F, Yang K, Tang W, Li J, Niu J, Shi Y, Zhou S, Petersen JD, Huang B, Liu J, You Y.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: APOE ε4 ( APOE4 ) is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic dementia. Nevertheless, it remains unclear to what extent shared and disease‑specific cerebral and peripheral traits mediate APOE4 ‑associated dementia risk across major dementia subtypes. Methods: We integrated multimodal datasets, including neuroimaging (n = 58,876), plasma proteomics (n = 51,623), and plasma metabolomics (n = 267,627), from the UK Biobank to systematically disentangle brain structural and peripheral molecular mediators that connect APOE4 carriage to incident all-cause dementia (ACD), Alzheimer’s disease (AD), and vascular dementia (VaD). We applied multivariable logistic regression for APOE4 allele dose‑response risk estimates, counterfactual causal mediation analysis to identify neural and molecular mediators, and receiver operating characteristic‑based predictive modelling stratified by APOE4 zygosity. Results: We revealed graded, allele dosage‑dependent risk elevations for ACD, AD and VaD among APOE4 carriers, whereby homozygous carriers exhibited substantially higher incident dementia risk relative to heterozygous carriers and non‑carriers across all three clinical endpoints. Bilateral hippocampal and left thalamic gray matter atrophy selectively mediated APOE4 -associated ACD and AD risk without detectable indirect effects on VaD, while widespread white matter microstructural degeneration mediated increased risk across all three dementia subtypes. At the peripheral molecular level, circulating GFAP served as a shared protein mediator for ACD, AD and VaD, whereas distinct proteomic and metabolomic profiles underpinned subtype-specific pathways for AD and VaD, respectively. Combined models integrating plasmamediators outperformed clinical-only models for predicting incident dementia in both APOE4 heterozygotes and homozygotes. Conclusions: Collectively, this study delineates coordinated central brain structural and circulating molecular mediators of APOE4 -associated dementia risk, and provides potential subtype-specific mechanistic insights and therapeutic targets for AD and VaD.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于英国生物银行的多模态数据，结合神经影像、血浆蛋白组和代谢组，考察APOE4携带者中连接该基因与全因痴呆、阿尔茨海默病及血管性痴呆风险的中枢和外围中介因素。结果显示，APOE4的风险随等位基因剂量递增，纯合子风险明显高于杂合子和非携带者；海马和丘脑灰质萎缩选择性地中介全因痴呆和阿尔茨海默病风险，而白质微结构退化则中介三类痴呆的风险，血浆GFAP是三者共有的蛋白中介，AD和VaD还各有特异的蛋白与代谢通路。整合血浆中介物的模型预测表现优于仅用临床信息的模型，作者据此提出亚型特异的机制线索和潜在干预靶点，但中介分析结果仍需进一步验证。

papers.title: The Influence of Contralesional Brain Age Gradients on Chronic Stroke Aphasia Severity and Treatment Response.
papers.authors: Riccardi N, Martin A, Rangus I, Busby N, Rorden C, Fridriksson J, Bonilha L.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The adult brain follows normative aging trajectories, yet stroke abruptly disrupts this process. Beyond the focal lesion, undamaged regions can deviate from expected aging due to diaschisis or pre-existing vulnerabilities, reflecting tissue health that may constrain recovery. Chronic post-stroke aphasia, a persistent language disorder, shows wide individual variability in severity and treatment response, and these differences are not fully captured by lesion characteristics or demographic factors. Further, prior imaging biomarkers have been difficult to scale because they rely on specialized acquisitions or nonstandardized analytical pipelines. Here, we used a standardized, lifespan-informed brain age model (volBrain) trained on large public datasets to quantify regional deviations from normative aging using only routine structural MRI (T1-weighted). In 188 individuals with chronic stroke (67 female, 121 male), regional aging deviations in the contralesional hemisphere explained aphasia severity beyond lesion volume, lesion location, and basic demographics. In a treated subgroup, baseline brain aging patterns also predicted language gains that persisted 6 months after therapy, indicating prognostic value. By characterizing how individual brains diverge from expected aging, this approach captures variation in tissue integrity that is relevant for both impairment and recovery. This provides a scalable framework that can be integrated across sites and studies, linking normative aging models with post-stroke prognostics and informing precision neurorehabilitation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注慢性卒中后失语症的严重程度和治疗反应为何存在较大个体差异，并检验对侧半球区域偏离正常脑老化轨迹能否提供病灶之外的信息。研究利用基于常规结构MRI的标准化脑龄模型，在慢性卒中人群中量化各脑区相对预期老化的偏差。结果显示，对侧半球的区域老化偏差在病灶体积、位置和基本人口学因素之外仍能解释失语严重程度；在接受治疗的亚组中，基线脑老化模式还能预测治疗后持续数月的语言改善，提示其预后价值。作者据此提出，这一可扩展的框架将规范老化模型与卒中后预后评估联系起来，有望用于精准神经康复，但相关预测价值仍需进一步验证。

papers.title: Conflict-Dependent Gain Control in Area VIP during Visual-Vestibular Self-Motion Processing.
papers.authors: Sun H, Wang R, Zeng F, Chen A.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Visual and vestibular signals are continuously integrated to estimate self-motion, yet these sensory cues are often inconsistent under natural conditions. How cortical circuits regulate multisensory interactions under cue conflict while preserving stable heading representations remains poorly understood. Here, we recorded neurons in male macaque ventral intraparietal area (VIP) during passive movement stimulation while systematically varying visual-vestibular heading offsets. VIP neurons exhibited strong conflict-sensitive gain modulation: congruent cues enhanced neuronal responses, whereas increasing cue offsets progressively suppressed response gain. This effect was observed not only in multisensory neurons but also in neurons classified as predominantly visual or vestibular, indicating widespread cross-modal interactions across the population. In contrast, preferred-heading shifts remain modest, suggesting that cue conflict primarily modulated response gain rather than altering heading tuning. Despite substantial suppression at the single-neuron level under large cue offsets, population Fisher information was largely preserved, indicating robust heading discriminability. Further analyses revealed flexible sensory weighting in VIP, with visual and vestibular contributions shifting as cue conflict increased. Finally, a feedforward-gated normalization model substantially improved the characterization of VIP responses by allowing cue conflict to dynamically regulate the effective normalization pool, thereby capturing both multisensory enhancement at small visual-vestibular heading offset and suppression under large cue conflict. Together, these findings show that VIP exhibits conflict-dependent regulation of multisensory gain, preserving robust self-motion representations under sensory conflict.

papers.title: Regulation of Protein Kinase Pathways in Primary Neuron Model of Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis.
papers.authors: Joo Y, Ciryam P, Zhang T, Huang W, Dean CA, Lawrence AP, Vu TH, Gooya N, Dessain SK, Kane MA, Benavides DR.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The most common form of autoimmune encephalitis is associated with antibodies that target N -methyl-d-aspartic acid receptors (NMDARs). NMDARs play a pivotal role in neurotransmission and synaptic plasticity. Mounting evidence has shown that antibody targeting of the NMDAR GluN1 subunit, as in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, leads to NMDAR cross-linking and receptor internalization. However, the underlying signaling pathways affected by antibodies targeting NMDARs remain to be explored. We previously demonstrated that a human GluN1 monoclonal antibody 5F5 (GluN1 mAb 5F5) rapidly localizes to and regulates synaptic NMDAR function at native synapses of primary hippocampal neurons. Here, we sought to explore signaling targets of GluN1 mAb 5F5 in primary cortical neurons of either sex using subcellular fractionation, Western blotting, and label-free quantitative phosphoproteomics by mass spectrometry. We find that human GluN1 mAb 5F5 does not change NMDAR abundance or surface levels of GluN1 on primary cortical neurons at 2 h. Despite this, we observe that GluN1 mAb 5F5 alters the phosphoproteome in synaptoneurosomes and regulates numerous synapse-related biological processes and protein kinase activities. Bioinformatic analyses suggest that these phosphoproteomic changes are positively correlated with NMDAR activation and negatively correlated with NMDAR inhibition. Together, these data suggest that GluN1 mAb 5F5 alters intracellular kinase signaling pathways in primary cortical neurons, likely by activating the NMDAR. These studies may help to identify novel therapeutic strategies for anti-NMDAR encephalitis and other antibody-mediated encephalitides targeting cell surface antigens.

papers.title: Hippocampal-Dependent Navigation without Outcome-Sensitive Control.
papers.authors: Wang S, Grgurich R, Blair HT.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Goal-directed decisions depend on predictions of future outcomes and are thus sensitive to revaluation of expected outcomes, whereas habitual decisions depend on cached action values or stimulus-response associations and are insensitive to outcome revaluation. Hippocampal neurons encode future states (potentially supporting prediction of future outcomes during goal-directed choice) as well as present states (potentially supporting retrieval of state-dependent action values during habitual choice). Prior studies suggest the role of the hippocampus in goal-directed, outcome-sensitive decision-making, but few studies have examined its role in outcome-insensitive action selection. Here, we tested this using a two-outcome spatial navigation task in which identical turning actions (left or right) led either to preferred milk or nonpreferred water outcomes, depending on the spatial location at which the choice was made. Rats (20 males, 22 females) were trained under conditions that either required hippocampal-dependent discrimination between choice points or allowed hippocampal-independent navigation using visual beacons. Rats then underwent 24 h water restriction, during which separate cohorts underwent Contingency Updating (CU), in which rats re-experienced the maze action-outcome contingencies while thirsty, or Incentive Learning (IL), in which rats received only a two-bottle preference test while thirsty without re-experiencing maze contingencies. Both cohorts were later tested under thirst on an unbaited maze. CU rats shifted their choices toward water-associated responses, whereas IL rats perseverated on milk-associated responses, even when navigation depended on the hippocampus. These results provide novel evidence that hippocampal-dependent navigational decisions can show insensitivity to outcome revaluation, a widely used behavioral criterion for habitual control.

papers.title: ASCL1 and OLIG2 Expression Dynamics Control Glial Cell Fate and Regional Diversity in the Dorsal Forebrain.
papers.authors: Paez-Beltran LE, Chen H, Villicana E, Liyanapathirana M, Myers BL, Duan J, Fletcher DE, Esparza AC, Riega A, Vue TY.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Gliogenesis is a multistep process in which glial progenitors are specified into migrating and proliferating precursor cells that subsequently differentiate into mature astrocytes and oligodendrocytes. How these developmental processes are coordinated to generate the diverse glial lineages across gray matter (GM) and white matter (WM) regions remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factor ASCL1 serves as a direct mechanistic link between these processes in the dorsal forebrain. Notably, ASCL1 is dynamically expressed in glial progenitor cells, initiating in the ventricular zone, peaking in the intermediate zone, but is downregulated once glial cells enter the cortical plate. Lineage tracing of ASCL1+ progenitors demonstrates that they subsequently coexpress OLIG2 to generate both astrocytes and oligodendrocytes in an "outside-in" pattern starting from the upper cortex inward to the corpus callosum, the opposite pattern of neurogenesis. ASCL1 gain-of-function combined with OLIG2 loss-of-function reveals that sustained levels of ASCL1 are essential to induce sufficient levels of OLIG2 required to specify oligodendrocyte precursor cell (OPC) fate. Interestingly, a persistent ASCL1 expression also maintains OPCs in an undifferentiated, preneoplastic state into postnatal stages, in part by suppressing their differentiation into postmitotic oligodendrocytes. Together, these findings establish ASCL1 as a key regulator of the spatiotemporal order of glial lineage diversity in cortical GM and callosal WM and highlight ASCL1 dysregulation as an underlying developmental mechanism in the pathogenesis of gliomas.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在小鼠背侧前脑的胶质细胞谱系中，考察ASCL1与OLIG2的表达动态如何协调胶质前体细胞的命运指定与区域多样性。谱系追踪显示，ASCL1阳性前体细胞随后共表达OLIG2，以“由外向内”的顺序生成星形胶质细胞和少突胶质细胞，与神经发生的方向相反；功能获得与缺失实验表明，持续水平的ASCL1是诱导足够OLIG2、进而指定少突胶质前体细胞命运所必需的。作者还发现，ASCL1持续表达会使这些前体细胞在出生后仍维持未分化状态，部分通过抑制其向终末少突胶质细胞分化，并将ASCL1失调与胶质瘤发病机制联系起来。

papers.title: Dopamine Modulates Striatal Activity When Controlling the Output of Working Memory.
papers.authors: Nielsen NM, Calcott RD, van den Bosch R, Olraun HS, Spronkers FS, Verkes RJ, den Ouden HEM, Cools R.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Cognitive control depends on capacity-limited mechanisms that require selection. Working memory (WM) therefore relies on an input-gate to filter information into WM and an output-gate to transform current WM representations into a prioritized state to guide behavior. According to current theory, such WM gating processes are modulated by dopamine in the striatum, yet empirical evidence for this hypothesis remains sparse. We fill this gap by directly testing the role of dopamine for both WM input- and output-gating in a double-blind, placebo-controlled within-subject functional magnetic resonance imaging study (N = 34; 23 female, 11 male human subjects), using a 400 mg oral dose of the dopamine D2 receptor antagonist sulpiride. In our cued delayed-response task, which separated input- from output-gating, sulpiride altered neural activity in the striatum during output-gating. This effect was accompanied by a sulpiride-induced decrease in the neural stimulus-selectivity of gated sensory representations in visual association cortex, with greater decreases in stimulus-selectivity correlating with reduced behavioral accuracy in the task. Together, the results establish a role for striatal dopamine during the control of cortical outflow of WM.

papers.title: Association Between Plasma N-Terminal Tau, Cognitive Decline, and Neurodegeneration in the ADNI Cohort.
papers.authors: Rao Y, Liu L, Ostaszewski BL, Anderson AK, Pinilla V, Shirzadi Z, Laho EM, Stern AM, Yau WW, Yang HS, Buckley RF, Ashton NJ, Denkinger MN, Sperling RA, Selkoe DJ, Chhatwal JP, Schultz SA, Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Blood-based biomarkers offer a cost-effective, minimally invasive alternative to neuroimaging and CSF biomarkers. Newly developed fluid biomarkers, including the N-terminal tau fragment (NT1), show promise for identifying individuals at risk for Alzheimer disease (AD) and for monitoring disease progression. Here, we determine whether NT1 levels are associated with key clinical and biomarker measures in a large, well-characterized cohort. Methods Participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort with available plasma NT1, β-amyloid (Aβ)-PET, MRI, and clinical measures (Clinical Dementia Rating) were included in this observational study. NT1 was measured using the Quanterix Simoa HD-X platform. PET, MRI, clinical, and other plasma measures were obtained using established ADNI procedures. A subset also had NULISA-based plasma measures of amyloid and tau and tau-PET assessed. Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between NT1 and clinical or biomarker measures, adjusting for relevant covariates. Multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was performed to evaluate the association between baseline NT1 levels and risk of clinically diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD. Mediation analysis was conducted to examine whether hippocampal atrophy mediates the relationship between NT1 and memory decline. Spearman correlations were used to examine continuous relationships between plasma NT1 and continuous fluid and neuroimaging markers. Results A total of 755 participants (mean age: 72.9 [7.0], female: 375 [50%]) were included in the study. Plasma NT1 levels were elevated in MCI/AD individuals (BMCI/AD [SE] = 0.09 [0.022], p = 1.98 × 10-4 ) and were cross-sectionally associated with worse memory performance (B [SE] = -0.25 [0.09], p = 0.005). Aβ moderated the association between elevated NT1 and greater cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory: B [SE] = -0.17 [0.074], p = 0.022; executive function: B [SE] = -0.24 [0.082], p = 0.004; language: B [SE] = -0.21 [0.075], p = 0.006). NT1 levels were negatively associated with hippocampal volume (B [SE] = -264.49 [125.99], p = 0.036) and predicted longitudinal atrophy (B [SE] = -42.00 [16.90], p = 0.013). Accelerated hippocampal atrophy largely mediated the association between higher baseline NT1 level and greater memory decline (B [95% CI]indirect effect = -0.082 [-0.135 to -0.03], p = 0.003, B [95% CI]proportion mediated = 70.1% [32.6%-155.3%], p = 0.004). Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p 's < 5.01 × 10-6 ) and Simoa-Based pTau181 (p < 4.51 × 10-15 ) and neurofilament light chain (p < 5.34 × 10-7 ). Discussion Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

papers.title: The Paradoxical Effect of Levetiracetam: A Case of Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus Following Stereoelectroencephalography Implantation.
papers.authors: Lian H, Dan W, Jiang L, Liang X.
papers.abstract: The paradoxical effect of levetiracetam (LEV) refers to the paradoxical aggravation of epileptic seizures during clinical application. In this case, we report for the first time a patient with MRI-negative drug-resistant frontal lobe epilepsy who developed nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE) following LEV dose escalation, as documented by stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG). The SEEG findings suggested that paradoxical activation of mesial temporal structures may be involved in the occurrence of LEV-induced paradoxical effects.
keywords: Drugresistant Epilepsy Seeg Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus Frontal Lobe Epilepsy
papers.summary_zh: 该病例报告首次记录了立体脑电图（SEEG）监测下的一例MRI阴性耐药性额叶癫痫患者，在左乙拉西坦剂量增加后出现非惊厥性癫痫持续状态。SEEG结果提示，内侧颞叶结构的反常激活可能参与了左乙拉西坦所致反常效应的发生。这一发现为理解左乙拉西坦在个别患者中加重癫痫的反常现象提供了颅内电生理证据，但作为单例观察，其机制推测仍需更多研究验证。

papers.title: Diagnostic Utility of Velopharyngeal MRI in Children With Unexplained Velopharyngeal Insufficiency.
papers.authors: Sherrod EK, Black J, Mason KN.
papers.journal: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the utility of velopharyngeal MRI in contributing additional diagnostic information for patients with velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) of unknown etiology.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingTertiary children's hospital.ParticipantsChildren with clinically significant VPI without a confirmed etiology.InterventionsStandardized perceptual speech assessment with nasometry, non-sedated MRI, and multidisciplinary review for treatment planning.Main Outcome MeasuresMRI-informed etiologic classification, anatomic and functional contributors to VPI, and management recommendations.ResultsAmong 89 children, six (6.7%) presented with clinically significant VPI of unknown etiology on routine examination. MRI identified occult submucous cleft palate or atypical levator veli palatini morphology in five (83.3%) and adenoid-supported VP closure in three (50%). Involution was expected to unmask increased pharyngeal depth in two (33.3%). MRI supported patient-specific recommendations for speech therapy, surgical interventions, and longitudinal monitoring.ConclusionsMRI provided clinically meaningful diagnostic information beyond routine examination and informed management decisions for children with VPI.

papers.title: Confounds in Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Part II: Modifiers.
papers.authors: Inglis B, D'Esposito M.
papers.abstract: In the first part of this three-part series, we reviewed the mechanisms that cause nuisance signals in fMRI data. Here, in the second part of the series, we review "human factors" that modulate these confounding mechanisms. The modulators may be trait characteristics such as age or bodyweight, or they may be state dependencies that alter the relative contributions of nuisance signals in the fMRI data. A wide array of psychological (e.g., motivation/arousal, cognitive strategy, task engagement), lifestyle (e.g., exercise, sleep, and dietary habits), experimental (e.g., scanner anxiety, task-related movement), and situational (e.g., prandial state, time of day, menses) factors can affect the brain state directly as well as via changes in systemic physiology mediated by autonomic nervous responses.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Effect of Intranasal Breast Milk-Derived Exosomes in a Neonatal Rat Model of Periventricular Leukomalacia.
papers.authors: Pekal Y, Koyuncu E, Topel G, Avci E, Baris Mogul C, Turgut M, Özdemir ÖMA, Pekal AB, Yalçin N.
papers.abstract: Background Periventricular leukomalacia (PVL) is a major cause of neurodevelopmental impairment in premature infants and is characterized by inflammation-associated white matter injury. Breast milk-derived exosomes have regenerative and immunomodulatory properties. Methods Experimental PVL was induced in neonatal Sprague-Dawley rats by maternal lipopolysaccharide administration. Animals were assigned to control (n=10), PVL (n=9), PVL + saline (n=10), and PVL + exosome (n=9) groups. Breast milk-derived exosomes were isolated, characterized according to MISEV2018 criteria, and administered intranasally on postnatal days 1, 3, and 5. Histopathological and biochemical analyses were performed on postnatal day 7. Results Significant differences were observed among groups in microcystic injury, myelin basic protein (MBP) staining, and tyrosine hydroxylase staining (p<0.05). Exosome treatment reduced microcystic white matter injury and preserved MBP staining intensity compared with untreated PVL groups. Tyrosine hydroxylase staining was also higher in the exosome-treated group. No significant differences were observed in GFAP staining intensity, histopathological inflammation scores, or IL-6 levels. IL-1β and TNF-α showed altered profiles, suggesting immunomodulatory effects. PKH26 labeling demonstrated exosome-associated fluorescence in the frontal cortex and hippocampus after intranasal administration. Conclusions Intranasal breast milk-derived exosomes attenuated white matter injury and preserved markers of myelin and neuronal integrity in experimental PVL, supporting further investigation in larger models with functional outcome assessments. These findings support a potential cell-free neuroprotective strategy for inflammation-associated neonatal brain injury. However, the use of human breast milk-derived exosomes in rats and the absence of long-term functional outcomes warrant further comparative and longitudinal studies before clinical translation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在母体脂多糖诱导的新生大鼠脑室周围白质软化模型中，经鼻给予母乳来源外泌体，并以组织病理与生化分析评估其作用。结果显示，外泌体处理减轻了白质微囊性损伤，并较好保留了髓鞘碱性蛋白和酪氨酸羟化酶染色所反映的髓鞘与神经元完整性标志；炎症评分、GFAP染色强度及IL-6水平未见显著差异，而IL-1β和TNF-α谱发生变化，提示可能存在免疫调节作用。作者据此认为，经鼻母乳外泌体在该模型中具有减轻白质损伤的潜力，但所用为人母乳来源外泌体、且缺乏长期功能结局，尚需更大模型和纵向比较研究后再考虑临床转化。

papers.title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice.
papers.authors: Shee S, Huang M, Baghel MS, Zheng Y, Lun S, Yadav SK, Yadav NN, Ruiz-Gonzalez CE, Tyagi S, Nuermberger E, Jain SK, Bhujwalla ZM, Slusher BS, Wong PC, Bishai W.
papers.abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer's disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2-magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer-MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

papers.title: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia.
papers.authors: Wei HT, Boutet D, Dou R, Ahrens J, Zeramdini N, Voppel A, Gonzales-Aste F, Abboud F, Baillet S, Palaniyappan L.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注精神分裂症患者的感知、动作与语言障碍是否共享同一神经生理基础，用脑磁图在多感觉与运动任务中比较患者与健康人的事件相关β频段调制。结果显示，患者在感觉加工和动作完成阶段的β变化减弱，提示其更新内部模型的灵活性下降；这一神经模式与视听同时性判断行为、自然言语的组织性以及临床严重程度相关。作者据此提出，分布式的β调制可能作为跨领域候选标记，关联精神分裂症的感知、运动与语言异常，但相关关系不等于因果，其预测性更新机制仍需未来研究直接检验。

papers.title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Chen C, Song X, Guo Y, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization-selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

papers.title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex.
papers.authors: Thorat S, Doerig A, Kroner A, Amme C, Kietzmann TC.
papers.abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain's visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出，自然场景中的物体共现与空间关系可能通过主动视觉中相邻注视点之间的时间规律以自监督方式习得，并用循环神经网络构建“注视预测网络”，训练其沿类人扫视路径预测下一注视片段的嵌入表示。结果显示，这类模型能提取物体共现和空间布局等复杂场景信息，并整合跨注视片段的信息；其表征与人类视觉皮层中高级区域的fMRI反应高度对齐，且常优于其他先进人工神经网络模型。作者据此认为，预测下一注视片段可能是形成与大脑对齐的场景表征的一条生物学上合理的途径，但这一结论主要基于表征相似性，尚不涉及因果机制或临床应用。

papers.title: Gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine with and without aura: A multimodal MRI and JuSpace analysis.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Luo Y, He Z, Xie H, Su Y, Chen D, Miao Y, Pu R, Jiang J.
papers.abstract: Objective To characterize gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine without aura (MwoA) and migraine with aura (MwA) relative to healthy controls (HC), test direct differences between the migraine groups, and examine spatial associations between voxel-based morphometry findings and molecular and cellular reference templates. Background Structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have reported gray and white matter abnormalities in migraine, but findings vary across cohorts, imaging methods, and clinical subgroups. Whether migraine with and without aura show distinct structural patterns remains uncertain, and the molecular and cellular context of these alterations is incompletely understood. Methods This cross-sectional group-comparison analysis was embedded in an ongoing prospective single-center study at The First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University in Dalian, China, and included participants recruited from August 2025 to March 2026. Thirty HC, 40 participants with MwoA, and 15 participants with MwA underwent T1-weighted and diffusion MRI. Diffusion tensor imaging, neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging, and diffusional kurtosis imaging metrics were analyzed using tract-based spatial statistics; gray matter microstructure and volume were assessed using gray matter-based spatial statistics and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). JuSpace Toolbox correlated unthresholded VBM statistical parametric t (spmT) maps with neurotransmitter- and cell-related templates. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education; VBM additionally adjusted for total intracranial volume; and direct MwoA-versus-MwA sensitivity models included Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Results Relative to HC, MwoA showed higher mean and radial diffusivity and lower neurite density index, whereas MwA showed lower free-water fraction (all threshold-free cluster enhancement-family-wise error [FWE], p < 0.05). No diffusional kurtosis imaging or corrected gray matter-based spatial statistics result was significant. VBM showed lower gray matter volume in MwoA in left cerebellar Crus I (77 voxels; peak-level whole-brain family-wise error (FWE)-corrected p value (pFWE) = 0.022) and right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (6 voxels; pFWE = 0.025), and in MwA in right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (85 voxels; pFWE = 0.019). Direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant in primary and Patient Health Questionnaire-9-adjusted models. JuSpace identified seven and 11 false discovery rate (FDR)-significant neurotransmitter-related associations for MwoA-versus-HC and MwA-versus-HC, respectively; no cell-related template survived FDR correction for MwoA-versus-HC, whereas nine survived for MwA-versus-HC (q < 0.05). No region of interest-clinical association survived Bonferroni correction. Conclusion Multimodal MRI identified gray and white matter alterations in both migraine groups relative to HC, whereas direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant. JuSpace provided complementary spatial context for the VBM findings. These results broaden the structural characterization of migraine but do not establish imaging differences between the two migraine groups.
keywords: Neurite Orientation Dispersion And Density Imaging
papers.summary_zh: 该研究比较无先兆偏头痛和有先兆偏头痛患者与健康对照者的灰质和白质结构改变，并检验两种偏头痛之间是否存在直接差异。参与者接受弥散与结构MRI，研究还用JuSpace将基于体素的形态学结果与神经递质及细胞相关模板做空间关联。结果显示，两组偏头痛患者相对健康对照均出现白质弥散指标异常和局部灰质体积降低，但无先兆与有先兆偏头痛之间的直接比较未达显著。JuSpace分析为形态学发现提供了神经递质和细胞层面的空间参照，但影像指标与临床特征的相关未通过校正，因此结果扩展了偏头痛的结构特征描述，尚不能确立两种亚型之间的影像差异。

papers.title: EEG Edge-Centric Dynamics Reveal Distinct Post-Stroke Somatosensory Network Responses to Vibratory and Electrical Stimulation.
papers.authors: Lin L, Liao J, Huang Y, Qing W, Ye F, Rong W, Li W, Jiao J, Hu X, Ma T.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.abstract: Stroke-induced somatosensory deficits disrupt sensorimotor integration (SMI) and limit motor recovery, yet the immediate network-level effects of different somatosensory interventions remain unclear, hindering patient-specific rehabilitation planning. We propose an informatics framework based on edge-centric dynamic connectivity (ECDC) to characterize transient, whole-brain EEG network responses to sensory-level focal vibratory stimulation (FVS) and neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES). We analyzed EEG recordings from 15 chronic stroke participants and 15 healthy controls during forearm stimulation and quantified temporal network dynamics, spectral network organization, and interhemispheric interactions from instantaneous overlapping functional networks. Compared with NMES, FVS in stroke participants induced a distinct neurophysiological profile, including (i) shorter global theta-network latency, suggesting faster attentional engagement; (ii) higher contralesional alpha network diversity, indicating enhanced somatosensory recruitment; and (iii) reduced theta-alpha phase-amplitude coupling, reflecting decoupled interhemispheric interactions that may support adaptive reorganization. These findings provide interpretable network signatures for differentiating stimulation-specific brain responses and suggest a data driven route toward personalized SMI rehabilitation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注卒中后感觉障碍患者在接受不同感觉刺激时，全脑网络层面的即时反应有何差异，并为此提出基于边中心动态连接（ECDC）的脑电分析框架，比较局灶振动刺激（FVS）与神经肌肉电刺激（NMES）下的网络动态。结果显示，与NMES相比，FVS在卒中参与者中呈现出不同的神经生理特征：全局theta网络潜伏期更短，提示注意参与更快；对侧alpha网络多样性更高，提示感觉募集增强；theta-alpha相位-幅值耦合降低，反映半球间交互解耦，可能有利于适应性重组。作者认为，这些网络特征可用于区分不同刺激引起的大脑反应，并为数据驱动的个体化感觉运动整合康复提供线索，但尚属初步探索。

papers.title: Regional blood-brain barrier dysfunction maps to lower performance in cognitive ageing.
papers.authors: Mirloo S, Shpilberg S, Druker N, Saar-Ashkenazy R, Prager O, Neustaedter SB, Ben-Arie G, Shelef I, Kamintsky L, Serlin Y, Sandsmark DK, Friedman A, Shalev H.
papers.abstract: Age-related cognitive decline is a common and growing public health challenge, associated with loss of independence, reduced quality of life, increased caregiver burden and substantial healthcare and societal costs. Yet cognitive decline in ageing is heterogeneous, and current clinical constructs do not reliably capture the underlying biological mechanisms or predict progression to dementia. This cross-sectional study examined whether blood-brain barrier dysfunction (BBBD) provides a biologically supported correlate of cognitive performance beyond clinical diagnosis. The study included 46 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 46 age-matched controls and 43 young controls. BBBD was assessed using dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI in 42 patients with MCI and all controls, alongside volumetric brain analysis. Standardized NeuroTrax cognitive assessment data were analysed for 41 MCI patients and 19 age-matched controls. BBBD was analysed using the BBBdetect software (Emagix Inc, Nova Scotia, Canada), quantifying voxelwise and region-wise blood-brain barrier permeability; volumetric analysis was performed using the Volbrain software; and cognitive performance was stratified into low- and high-performance subgroups based on modified z-scores. Compared with young controls, the older cohort (MCI patients combined with age-matched controls) showed significantly greater BBBD volume and regional extent. Permeability increased with age and showed marked inter-individual variability. Across participants, lower cognitive performance was associated with a greater number of regions exhibiting BBBD. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified domain-specific spatial patterns of BBBD linked to poor performance in memory, executive, attention, verbal and motor domains, implicating frontal, cingulate, hippocampal, basal ganglia and cerebellar regions. In contrast, volumetric analyses revealed expected age-related reductions in grey and white matter and cortical thickness along with increased ventricular volume; however, these structural changes showed weak to no associations with cognitive performance. These findings suggest that BBBD is widespread in ageing and that regional BBBD maps to domain-specific cognitive deficits. BBBD thus emerges as a biologically relevant biomarker of age-related cognitive impairment and a potential therapeutic target for preserving cognitive function in ageing.
papers.summary_zh: 该横断面研究考察血脑屏障功能障碍能否在临床诊断之外为认知表现提供有生物学依据的关联。研究比较了轻度认知障碍患者、年龄匹配的老年对照与年轻对照，用动态对比增强MRI评估血脑屏障通透性并结合脑体积分析。结果显示，老年群体的血脑屏障功能障碍范围和区域更广，且随年龄增加并存在明显个体差异；认知表现较低者出现血脑屏障功能障碍的脑区更多，不同认知域对应不同的空间模式，而灰白质体积和皮层厚度等结构变化与认知表现的关联较弱甚至缺失。作者据此认为，区域性的血脑屏障功能障碍与特定认知域缺损相对应，可能作为年龄相关认知损害的生物学标志物及潜在干预靶点，但相关发现尚属关联性证据。

papers.title: Serum β-synuclein predicts dementia conversion and mortality beyond amyloid-β and phospho-tau.
papers.authors: Oberstein TJ, Schwarz J, Rudtke L, Jablonowski J, Marterstock DC, Schmidt MA, Doerfler A, Kiesel J, Klement N, Schulz P, Lewczuk P, Maler JM, Kornhuber J, Oeckl P, Otto M.
papers.abstract: Synaptic dysfunction is among the earliest pathological events in Alzheimer's disease and among the strongest neuropathological correlates of cognitive impairment, yet blood-based synaptic biomarkers are lacking. Whether serum β-synuclein provides prognostic information independent of established amyloid-β (A; CSF Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio) and tau (T1; CSF pTau181) biomarkers has not been determined. We studied 259 non-demented individuals with subjective or mild cognitive impairment from a single-centre memory clinic, classified by CSF biomarkers using externally validated cut-offs into A-T1- controls (n = 97), A-T1+ PASSED ('pTau and Aβ surge with subtle deterioration', n = 65), and A + T1+ Alzheimer's disease (n = 97), with parallel analyses using Aβ40-normalised pTau181. Endpoints comprised dementia conversion (n = 185, median follow-up 4.1 years), all-cause mortality (n = 258, median 7.0 years), longitudinal MMSE trajectories (n = 185), and regional brain volumes (n = 137). Independence from CSF biomarkers was quantified through systematic effect attenuation analysis. Serum β-synuclein was selectively elevated in the Alzheimer's disease group (Cohen's d = 0.69 vs controls, P < 0.001) but not in PASSED individuals (P = 0.40), and was more strongly associated with CSF pTau181 (r = 0.36) than with the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio (r = -0.20) across the cohort. Each standard deviation increase was associated with higher risk of dementia conversion (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.40; 95% CI: 1.11, 1.77; P = 0.005), faster cognitive decline (-0.11 SD/year, 95% CI: -0.18, -0.04, P = 0.002, corresponding to -0.20 MMSE points/year), and higher mortality (HR = 1.33; 95% CI: 1.07, 1.65; P = 0.010). For dementia conversion and mortality, adjustment for continuous CSF pTau181 and Aβ42/Aβ40 produced minimal attenuation (≤13%). Both associations were preserved under Aβ40-normalised T1 staging but not against continuous pTau181 normalised to CSF Aβ40. For cognitive decline, β-synuclein's effect remained significant after Aβ42/Aβ40 adjustment (25% attenuation; P = 0.007) but was substantially attenuated by pTau181 (58.5%; P = 0.186). Serum β-synuclein was associated with lower bilateral temporal lobe volume-the only lobar regions to survive hierarchical testing-with sub-regional involvement spanning the hippocampi, entorhinal cortex and parahippocampal gyrus, and explained 5.0-8.9% of unique variance beyond CSF biomarkers. Plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) showed a strong association with β-synuclein, estimated in the PASSED subgroup (β=0.34 per SD, P < 0.001). Serum β-synuclein provided prognostic information largely independent of CSF Aβ42/Aβ40 across all endpoints and of pTau181 for survival outcomes, while sharing substantial prognostic variance with pTau181 for cognitive trajectory, supporting its candidacy as a blood-based synaptic complement to core Alzheimer's disease biomarkers.

papers.title: Improved quality and reproducibility of cerebral cortical organoids under microfluidic culture conditions: a proof-of-concept study.
papers.authors: Castiglione H, Madrange L, Brás N, Setien C, Baquerre C, Renault J, Maisonneuve BGC, Bourgeois M, Lemonnier T, Deslys JP, Chessel A, Honegger T, Yates F, Rontard J, Vigneron PA.
papers.abstract: Cerebral organoids have emerged as advanced three-dimensional in vitro models capable of recapitulating essential aspects of human brain development, thereby offering new opportunities for studying brain physiology and disease. Nonetheless, their use in preclinical settings remains limited by their high variability. Microfluidic devices offer a promising alternative to conventional culture supports by enabling improved recapitulation of the cellular microenvironment; however, most cerebral organoids-on-chips rely on custom-made academic prototypes, limiting their scalability and translatability. Here, we established a brain organoid-on-chip model by combining a regionalized cortical organoid differentiation protocol with a commercial, standardized and industrially-compatible microfluidic device (Duplex™, NETRI). Cortical organoid quality and reproducibility were evaluated using a previously established multi-criteria Quality Control (QC) framework based on a scoring system. To enhance objectivity and throughput, the non-invasive morphometric QC criteria were automated using deep learning-based image analysis. Using a single human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) line, we assessed whether microfluidic culture conditions could improve the quality and reproducibility of cortical organoids within a controlled genetic background. Compared with conventional cultures, on-chip cortical organoids demonstrated improved inter- and intra-batch reproducibility across multiple scales, including morphology, size, cytoarchitectural organization, and transcript expression, together with higher QC scores and reduced QC failure rates. Finally, the QC framework was adapted for neurotoxicity assessment using a decision tree to classify compounds according to their neurotoxic risk. While this study represents a proof-of-concept within this cellular background, the integrated brain organoid-on-chip platform and standardized QC evaluations provide a flexible and translatable framework for preclinical and industrial studies, and may facilitate future cross-line validation of reproducible cortical organoid cultures.

papers.title: Towards semantic brain-computer interfacing: The graded inventory of semantic triggers (GIST) paradigm.
papers.authors: Podmore JJ, Radman M, Poli R, Paulmann S, Daly I.
papers.abstract: Objective Semantic Brain-Computer Interfaces (sBCIs) aim to decode conceptual information directly from neural activity, enabling more efficient and natural communication for individuals with severe motor impairments. However, existing approaches are often confounded by stimulus-driven perceptual processes and lack a reliable means of tagging the moment of concept formation. We introduce the Graded Inventory of Semantic Triggers (GIST), a novel electroencephalography (EEG) paradigm designed to elicit semantic retrieval from graded verbal clues with precise temporal alignment. Approach: EEG data were recorded from 14 participants performing the GIST task across three semantic categories (food, musical instruments, and body parts). Target neural activity was aligned to each participant's self-reported moment of semantic retrieval (spacebar press), enabling response-locked analysis. Here, we propose a staged framework where the first comprises a Conformer-based encoder trained on pooled data using a hybrid contrastive objective that combines instance-level consistency and cross-participant class alignment with domain-adversarial learning to reduce participant-specific information. In the second stage, the frozen encoder is transferred to a held-out participant whose data played no part in Stage 1, and a support vector machine is calibrated on that participant's own labelled items under a nested leave-one-item-out protocol. Results: Above-chance semantic decoding was achieved in all three pairwise tasks. Mean accuracies were 73.4% (Body vs. Food), 70.7% (Body vs. Music), and 68.2% (Food vs. Music). Participant-level permutation tests were significant in 9/11 participants for Body vs. Food and 8/11 for each of the other tasks (p < 0.05). The pre-response interval at [-1.5s, -0.5s] was the most discriminative. Significance: The GIST paradigm enables controlled elicitation and temporal alignment of semantic processing while reducing perceptual confounds. Combined with cross-participant representation pretraining and participant-specific calibration, the results demonstrate above-chance decoding of semantic categories from EEG in individuals excluded from representation learning, supporting the feasibility of sBCIs.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出GIST范式，用分级言语线索诱发语义提取，并将脑电活动对齐到受试者自报的语义提取时刻，以减少刺激驱动的知觉混淆。14名受试者完成食物、乐器、身体部位三类语义任务；分析采用跨受试者预训练的Conformer编码器，再在未参与预训练的受试者数据上做个体化校准。结果显示，三组两两分类均高于随机水平，反应前一段时间的区分度最高，但个体层面并非全部显著。作者据此认为，该范式结合跨受试者表征预训练与个体校准，可在未参与表征学习的个体中实现语义类别解码，为语义脑机接口的可行性提供了初步支持。

papers.title: The relationship between binocular vision components and visual evoked potentials with reading difficulties in elementary school children.
papers.authors: Jamali A, Ahangarani R, Khabazkhoob M, Mirzajani A, Jafarzadehpour A, Mohamadi A, Jafarzadehpur E.
papers.abstract: Purpose To assess the relationship between visual function and neural processing with reading/writing defects in elementary school children. Methods This case-control study included 28 boys (8-12 years old) with poor academic performance (study group) and 14 healthy, age-matched controls. All participants underwent a comprehensive optometric evaluation, including visual acuity, refractive error, heterophoria, accommodation and convergence facility, fusional reserves, and monocular Visual evoked potentials (VEPs) using 15- and 60-checkerboard patterns (ISCEV standards). Results No significant differences were found in uncorrected or best-corrected visual acuity between groups (p > .05). However, the study group demonstrated significantly greater hyperopia (+0.07 ± 0.61 D vs. -0.12 ± 0.23 D, p = .025), reduced monocular (6.93 vs. 9.07 cycles/min, p < .001) and binocular (6.04 vs. 8.00 cycles/min, p < .001) accommodative facility, as well as lower vergence facility (6.93 vs. 8.71 cycles/min, p < .001). The study group also exhibited greater exophoria at near (4.61 Δ vs. 2.57 Δ, p < .001) and a reduced distance base-out blur point (10.36 Δ vs. 11.71 Δ, p = .043). VEP measurements revealed a significantly prolonged P100 latency at the 15' check size (112.86 vs. 109.07 ms, p = .043) and higher Fmod values at both 15' (p = .029) and 60' (p = .031) in the study group compared to controls. Conclusion Children with reading difficulties exhibit distinct subclinical visual deficits, particularly in accommodative function, alongside delayed neural processing despite normal visual acuity. Binocular functional assessments and neurophysiological tests should be integrated into assessments of poor academic performance.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注小学儿童阅读困难与双眼视觉功能及视觉诱发电位之间的关系，采用病例对照设计，比较学业表现不佳儿童与年龄匹配健康儿童的眼科检查和单眼视觉诱发电位。结果显示，两组在视力上无显著差异，但学业不佳组表现出调节与聚散功能下降、近距离外隐斜更大，且视觉诱发电位P100潜伏期延长、部分频率指标升高，提示其存在亚临床视觉功能缺陷和神经加工延迟。作者据此认为，对学业表现不佳的儿童进行评估时，应纳入双眼视觉功能与神经生理检查；但这是组间关联，不能据此推断因果关系或治疗效果。

papers.title: Naturalistic spatial education engages distinct neural processes for mental rotation, cognitive load, and linguistic demands.
papers.authors: Gacetta EB, Laws ML, Aulet LS, Ozaydin TS, Tsay JS, Zapanta C, Cantlon JF.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Neuroscience studies typically isolate spatial cognition using simplified tasks targeting a single cognitive process. However, during formal spatial education, the brain rarely performs one cognitive operation at a time. Here, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to assess neural systems involved in dynamically processing an educational spatial visualization lesson. We quantified lesson content using an instructional-design framework capturing variation in spatial complexity, cognitive load, and verbal density. We then characterized how instructional demands modulated brain function using content-evoked responses, functional connectivity, and network-centrality. Spatial transformations during instruction robustly recruited parietal and premotor regions, which were linearly modulated by spatial complexity. This parietal dominance aligns with theories that these areas encode geometric and quantitative dimensions. In contrast, domain-general frontal activity tracked overall processing demands, and language regions tracked verbal density. Activity also varied with learners' spatial abilities: higher spatial performers showed stronger modulation of parietal and premotor regions as spatial demands increased, and greater domain-general modulation across content types. Thus, the same circuitry representing spatial transformations during instruction also reflects individual variation in spatial cognition. Parietal regions showed the highest centrality and strongest within-network coherence, marking them as the central hub of the system, and distinguishing them from less central and less coherent domain-general regions.
