Together, the findings reveal how the brain dynamically decomposes complex spatial instruction, preserving parietal-centered spatial processing, while coordinating support from premotor, domain-general, and language systems. These findings begin to reveal how spatial cognition operates within the complexity of formal instruction.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注在正式空间教育中，大脑如何同时处理空间变换、认知负荷和语言需求，而不是在简化任务中只完成单一认知操作。研究者用功能磁共振成像记录学习者观看一段空间可视化教学课程时的脑活动，并用教学设计框架量化课程内容的空间复杂度、认知负荷和语言密度。结果显示，空间变换主要稳定招募顶叶和运动前区，且其活动随空间复杂度线性变化；一般性额叶活动更多跟随整体加工需求，语言区则跟随语言密度。空间能力较高的学习者在空间需求增加时，顶叶和运动前区的调制更强，一般性区域的调制也随内容类型变化更明显。顶叶区域中心性最高、网络内一致性最强，处于该系统的核心位置。作者据此认为，大脑在复杂教学情境中会保留以顶叶为中心的空间加工，同时协调运动前区、一般性认知和语言系统的支持。

papers.title: C1ql2 gates stress vulnerability by regulating microglia-mediated synaptic pruning in the BLA-vHPC circuit.
papers.authors: Wang CY, Liu WZ, Liao SM, Niu J, Pan HQ, You WJ, Zhao K, Ma B, Lu MF, Zou JX, Hu P, Zhang WH, Pan BX.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Synaptic remodeling in emotional circuits contributes to the development of stress-related emotional disorders. However, such remodeling generally exhibits considerable heterogeneity across specific neuronal populations and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identified C1ql2 as a key molecular regulator that governs projection-specific synaptic vulnerability within basolateral amygdala (BLA). Transcriptional profiling revealed that C1ql2 expression is enriched in BLA neurons projecting to ventral hippocampus (BLA→vHPC PNs), but not in those projecting to nucleus accumbens (NAc), and is significantly down-regulated following chronic social defeat stress (CSDS). Gain- and loss-of-function manipulations demonstrated that C1ql2 regulates stress-induced neuronal remodeling in BLA→vHPC PNs, including dendritic hypertrophy, synaptic outgrowth, and enhanced glutamatergic transmission, thereby shaping susceptibility to anxiety-like behavior. We further found that CSDS-induced C1ql2 loss impairs microglial engulfment of BLA→vHPC PNs synapses, leading to aberrant synaptic accumulation. Our findings establish C1ql2-mediated neuron-microglia cross talk that critically regulates circuit-specific synaptic pathophysiology in stress-related disorders.

papers.title: A New Web-Based Word-Picture Matching Test Reveals Psycholinguistic Effects on Word-Level Reading and Auditory Comprehension in Aphasia.
papers.authors: Laks AB, Kim Y, Kelly CR, DeMarco AT, Turkeltaub PE.
papers.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
papers.abstract: Purpose Word reading comprehension deficits, often measured by word-to-picture matching (WtPM) tasks, are common in aphasia and alexia. To specify the nature of comprehension deficits, WtPM tasks should manipulate psycholinguistic features, have matched written and auditory versions, and provide normed scores measuring speed and accuracy. Here we present a novel web-based WtPM task that meets those needs. We use it to assess word comprehension deficits in left-hemisphere stroke survivors (LHSS). Method We examined scores for the novel auditory and written WtPM task in a normative sample (n = 62) and an LHSS sample (n = 63). Mixed-effects models examined accuracy and response time in both groups, and an analysis of variance compared efficiency between the groups. Correlations compared written WtPM performance and item difficulty to auditory WtPM, written lexical decision, and oral reading. A k -means clustering analysis examined deficit patterns in the LHSS group. Results WtPM performance was modulated by modality, frequency, and regularity and was impaired in the LHSS group. Written WtPM performance and item difficulty were correlated with auditory WtPM and written lexical decision in both groups and with oral reading in the LHSS group. Over half of the LHSS sample had frank deficits on at least one WtPM task. Comprehension deficits in individual LHSS were often modulated by input modality, word frequency, and regularity. Conclusions We present a clinically accessible WtPM task that captures individual patterns of word comprehension impairment in both written and auditory modalities. The use of efficiency scores allows for the assessment of mild impairments that are missed by ceiling effects on currently available tasks. Input modality, frequency, and regularity affect word comprehension as measured by WtPM. Individual stroke survivors present with different combinations of these effects, which may help to identify specific deficits and spared abilities that can guide reading comprehension treatment. Supplemental material https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33968839.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究开发了一项基于网络的词—图匹配测试，可同时评估书面与听觉词汇理解的速度和准确性，并在健康参照组与左半球卒中幸存者中比较表现。结果显示，两组的表现均受输入通道、词频和规则性影响，卒中组的词—图匹配成绩整体受损，且过半个体至少在一项任务上存在明显缺陷；书面与听觉版本的成绩及条目难度相互关联，个体缺陷模式也可按这些因素区分。作者认为，该测试能捕捉现有任务因天花板效应而遗漏的轻度理解障碍，并帮助识别卒中后阅读理解的特定缺陷与保留能力，为治疗提供参考。

papers.title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits.
papers.authors: Woo J, Williamson MR, Choi D, Akdemir E, Zlatkov T, Yu K, Kwon W, Maleki E, Ko Y, Sanchez K, Maleki H, Choi JM, Serin-Harmanci A, Deneen B.
papers.abstract: Astrocytes perform a diverse range of tasks that facilitate brain physiology, raising the possibility that these diverse astrocytic roles are enabled by functionally distinct subtypes1,2 . Recent studies identified molecular diversity among astrocytes3 ; however, whether this molecular heterogeneity reflects specialized astrocyte subpopulations with distinct functions remains unclear. Here, on the basis of previous molecular and functional studies4 , we generated a CD51-FLP mouse line that enables direct comparison of the functional properties between CD51+ and CD51- astrocyte subpopulations in neural circuits in vivo. We show that CD51+ and CD51- astrocytes have unique morphological, physiological and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. Functional studies demonstrate that CD51+ astrocytes selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex and circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, we found that CD51+ astrocytes function through glypican 6 to promote synapse formation in the cortex, while CD51 itself drives circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Applying these findings to brain injury, we found that CD51+ astrocytes promote functional recovery after stroke through enhanced synaptic remodelling. Taken together, our studies identify specialized astrocyte subpopulations that exhibit distinct functional properties in the developing, mature and injured brain.

papers.title: Functional architecture of the human insula.
papers.authors: Quabs J, Pantis S, Chen G, Huang W, Ma E, Del Vecchio M, Lyu D, Wang C, Avanzini P, Buch V, Ramayya AG, Caspers S, Vogel H, Parvizi J.
papers.abstract: The insular cortex has a central role in pain1,2 , interoception3,4 and feelings5,6 , yet its functional architecture and causal electrophysiological relationships among its subregions remain poorly understood. Here we combine intracranial electrical stimulation and task-based electroencephalography recordings with connectivity mapping within a cytoarchitectonic atlas of the human insula7-10 in 87 participants implanted with intracranial electrodes, and identify a quadripartite functional architecture comprising four distinct regions: (1) a dorsal-posterior region encoding somatotopically organized nociceptive/thermoceptive and somatosensory signals; (2) a ventral-posterior region with access to somatic information across multiple body parts; (3) a mid-anterior region associated with visceral sensations and anxiety states; and (4) an anterior-polar region, largely silent to direct stimulation, yet showing robust activation during salience detection and change of action mode. Critically, this anterior region, with its strong connections with the prefrontal cortex, including the anterior cingulate cortex, exerts strong and direct influence over other insular regions, while receiving less-strong indirect inputs from them, revealing an electrophysiological pathway for cognitive modulation of pain and bodily perception. Together, these findings define a functional architecture of the human insula that links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

papers.title: Breast carcinoma amplified sequence 2 rescues adult hippocampal neurogenesis and cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's disease via regulating BDNF/TrkB signaling.
papers.authors: Ma H, Liu C, Liu W, Liu J, Hou Y, Song Q, Wang Y, Wang P.
papers.abstract: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN) occurs throughout lifespan of humans and rodents and is correlated with memory performance and cognitive plasticity. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), AHN is impeded, while the molecular basis behind this impairment remains to be elucidated. Here we identified Breast carcinoma amplified sequence 2 (BCAS2), a core component of the CDC5L/Prp19 spliceosome complex, regulating AHN in AD. Using Bcas2 conditional knockout mice, AD mouse model APP/PS1 mice, established mouse primary adult neural stem cells and single cell sequencing, we demonstrate that BCAS2 replacement in adult mouse hippocampus promotes NSC activation and differentiation to neuron, restore AHN and relevant memory deficits through BDNF/TrkB signaling. Our findings corroborate the significance of AHN in AD and reveal the possible therapeutic potential of targeting BCAS2 in neurodegeneration.

papers.title: ADHD symptom positivity and its association with medication adherence and psychiatric burden in adults with epilepsy.
papers.authors: İlgen Uslu F, Özyalçın M, Kizek Ö, Elmalı AD, Bebek N.
papers.abstract: Background Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms are increasingly recognized in adults with epilepsy (AwE) and may contribute to psychiatric burden, seizure-related outcomes, and treatment adherence. We therefore investigated the frequency of ADHD symptom positivity and its associations with medication adherence, psychiatric symptoms, seizure burden, and neurophysiological findings. Methods This cross-sectional study included 100 AwE and 94 healthy controls. ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS-v1.1). Anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated using the Beck Anxiety Inventory and Beck Depression Inventory, respectively. Medication adherence was assessed using the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8). Participants were classifiedas ASRS-positive or ASRS-negative according to the six-item ASRS Part A screener. Clinical, psychiatric, electroencephalographic, and magnetic resonance imaging findings were compared between groups. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with ADHD-symptom-positivity. Results ADHD-symptom-positivity was significantly more frequent in AwE than in healthy controls (50.0% vs. 25.5%, p = 0.001). Within the epilepsy cohort, ASRS-positive participants demonstrated lower medication adherence (p = 0.010), higher rates of poor adherence (70.0% vs. 48.0%, p = 0.042), higher anxiety (p = 0.002), and depression scores (p < 0.001). Clinically significant anxiety and depression were also more common among ASRS-positive participants (p = 0.027 and p < 0.001, respectively). In multivariable analysis, depression score was independently associated with ADHD-symptom-positivity (OR = 1.147, 95% CI 1.039-1.267, p = 0.007). Conclusions ADHD-symptom-positivity is common in AwE and is associated with poorer medication adherence in the between-group analysis, but this association did not remain statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, while greater psychiatric symptom burden was observed. Routine screening for ADHD-related symptoms may facilitate identification of adults with epilepsy at increased riskfor adverse clinical outcomes and support more comprehensive epilepsy care.
papers.summary_zh: 该横断面研究比较了成人癫痫患者与健康对照的ADHD症状阳性率，并分析其与服药依从性、精神症状、癫痫负担及神经生理指标的关系。结果显示，癫痫患者中ADHD症状阳性更为常见，且阳性者的服药依从性更差、焦虑和抑郁症状更重，临床显著的焦虑与抑郁也更普遍。多变量分析中仅抑郁评分与ADHD症状阳性独立相关，服药依从性的组间关联经调整后不再显著，提示癫痫患者中ADHD相关症状与精神负担相伴，但依从性关联需谨慎解读。

papers.title: The mediating effect of circulating C-reactive protein on the association between depression and brain cortical dysconnectivity.
papers.authors: Shahi S, Hu Z, Zhang Q, Ma D, Li M, Xu Y, Deng Y, Liu K.
papers.abstract: Chronic low grade systemic inflammation is associated in the pathophysiology of major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the specific cortical structural connectivity changes associated with peripheral inflammation in MDD remains poorly understood. In this case-control study, 113 MDD patients and 107 healthy controls underwent 3T MRI and measurement of high sensitivity C-reactive protein (CRP). Fiber connectivity density (FiCD) mapping, a data driven whole-cortex pipeline combining cortical surface reconstruction with diffusion tractography, was used to examine depression and CRP interaction effects on cortical connectivity. A subgroup of MDD patients completed a six-week antidepressant follow-up with repeat MRI. A significant interaction between depression and CRP was identified in the left rostral middle frontal cortex (LRMF). FiCD in the LRMF was significantly lower in MDD patients than controls and negatively correlated with CRP in patients but not controls. Following six weeks of antidepressant treatment, FiCD in LRMF increased significantly, and this increase was negatively correlated with baseline. Peripheral inflammation is possibly associated with disrupted cortical connectivity in MDD and disturbs the brain structural recovery process during antidepressant treatment. The left rostral middle frontal cortex possibly serves as an important target.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注外周炎症是否参与重性抑郁障碍患者皮层结构连接异常，采用病例对照设计，比较抑郁患者与健康对照的皮层纤维连接密度，并检测循环C反应蛋白水平。结果显示，抑郁与C反应蛋白在左侧额中回前部存在交互作用：患者该区域连接密度低于对照，且与C反应蛋白呈负相关，而对照中未见此关联。部分患者接受抗抑郁治疗后该区域连接密度升高，且升高幅度与基线水平负相关。作者据此推测，外周炎症可能与抑郁患者的皮层连接受损及治疗中的脑结构恢复过程有关，左侧额中回前部可能是重要靶点；但相关结果尚不能确立因果关系。

papers.title: Resting-state EEG functional connectivity changes following memantine administration in children with autism spectrum disorder: an exploratory pre-post study.
papers.authors: Sharifzadeh M, Bajestani GS, Ashrafzadeh F, Karimzade M.
papers.abstract: Despite the widespread use of memantine in modulating excitatory/inhibitory balance, the precise changes in the topology of brain networks following memantine administration in preschool children remain clearly undefined. The objective of this study is a quantitative evaluation of brain functional connectivity changes associated with memantine administration in using EEG-based network analysis. In this research, 22 preschool ASD children underwent treatment with memantine for one month. Resting-state electroencephalogram (EEG) signals were recorded before and after the intervention. functional connectivity matrices were extracted using the Phase Locking Value (PLV) index. Individual-level analysis revealed a Neurophysiological heterogeneity pattern, consisting of a 64% Subgroup with increased network integration (n = 14) with increased connectivity and 36% with decreased connectivity. SPN analysis identified distinct spatial components of network reorganization: (1) localized connectivity suppression in the fronto-central (Fz, F3) and left occipital (O1) regions captured by lower-order spatial filters, and (2) reinforcement of long-range functional coupling and enhanced nodal centrality in the right parietal (P4) and left temporal (T3) regions in higher-order filters. These findings suggest spatial network reorganization patterns associated with memantine administration, characterized by a complementary balance between localized phase decoupling and long-range functional integration.

papers.title: Depression in the prodromal phase of Parkinson's disease: Clinical manifestations, biomarker evidence, and predictive implications.
papers.authors: Zhou ZD, Elvira R, Ng JH, Tamakoshi D, Hiraga K, Xiao B, Katsuno M, Tan EK.
papers.abstract: Depression is one of the earliest and most frequent non-motor symptoms in the prodromal phase of Parkinson's disease (PD), often preceding motor signs by years to decades. This review synthesizes epidemiological, neuroimaging, biomarker, and genetic evidence to clarify whether depression is a risk factor, a direct prodromal manifestation, or both. Meta-analyses consistently show a two-fold increased risk of subsequent PD in individuals with depressive symptoms or major depressive disorder (MDD), with the highest risk occurring within 1-2 years of diagnosis but persisting for up to 25 years. Late-onset depressive syndrome (after age 50-60) is associated with dopaminergic deficits on dopamine transporter imaging in 24-79% of cases, supporting it as a prodromal symptom, whereas early-onset depression may act through shared genetic vulnerability or chronic inflammatory pathways. Neuroimaging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) reveals that depression correlates with caudate atrophy, frontostriatal white matter disruption, and brainstem monoaminergic dysfunction, but not simply with nigrostriatal denervation. Depression frequently coexists with RBD, autonomic dysfunction, and olfactory impairment, likely reflecting shared brainstem pathology. Genetic forms of PD (GBA1, SNCA, LRRK2, PRKN) show variable depression prevalence, providing mechanistic insights into lysosomal, inflammatory, and proteostatic pathways. Emerging evidence implicates IL-17A, sIL-2R, and α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregation as convergent points linking depression and prodromal α-synucleinopathy, with gut-brain axis dysfunction potentially amplifying this process. Current Movement Disorder Society prodromal PD criteria include depression but have limited sensitivity in general populations. No disease-modifying trials have tested whether treating prodromal depression alters phenoconversion risk. We conclude that proximal, late-onset depressive syndrome is a robust prodromal marker, while distant or early-onset depression, including MDD, identifies a chronically elevated risk population. Future studies should integrate multimodal biomarkers and test therapeutic interventions in prodromal cohorts.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述整合流行病学、神经影像、生物标志物和遗传学证据，探讨抑郁在帕金森病前驱期究竟是风险因素、前驱表现还是两者兼有。作者指出，抑郁症状或重性抑郁障碍者日后患帕金森病的风险约为一般人群的两倍，且晚发性抑郁综合征常伴随多巴胺能缺陷，支持其作为前驱标志；而早发性抑郁可能通过共享遗传易感或慢性炎症通路起作用。抑郁还与快速眼动睡眠行为障碍、自主神经功能障碍和嗅觉减退共存，并涉及IL-17A、sIL-2R及α-突触核蛋白聚集等汇聚机制。作者据此认为，近端晚发性抑郁综合征是较可靠的前驱标志，远端或早发性抑郁则标识长期风险升高人群，但目前尚无试验检验治疗前驱期抑郁能否改变表型转化风险。

papers.title: Characterizing post-stroke changes in brain microstructure using the mean apparent propagator model.
papers.authors: Vega RJ, Richerson WT, Krucoff MO, Schmit BD.
papers.abstract: This study investigated regional and whole-brain microstructural alterations following stroke using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and Mean Apparent Propagator MRI (MAP-MRI). Multi-shell diffusion and T1-weighted MRI data were analyzed from participants with chronic stroke and healthy controls. DTI-derived fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD), and MAP-MRI-derived return-to-origin (RTOP), return-to-axis (RTAP), and return-to-plane (RTPP) probabilities were quantified across 13 predefined regions in native diffusion space. Regional group differences were assessed using participant-level median values with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) correction across all 65 ROI × diffusion-metric comparisons and age- and sex-adjusted sensitivity analyses. Complementary lesion-relative whole-brain analyses used nonparametric permutation testing with threshold-free cluster enhancement and family-wise error correction. MAP-MRI demonstrated widespread regional abnormalities, with significant group differences in 11 of 13 regions for RTOP, 12 of 13 for RTAP, and 10 of 13 for RTPP, compared with 8 of 13 for FA and all 13 regions for MD. After adjustment for age and sex, significant differences remained in 11, 10, and 9 regions for RTOP, RTAP, and RTPP, respectively, compared with 6 for FA and all 13 for MD. Whole-brain analyses demonstrated significant corrected abnormalities across all five diffusion metrics, with RTOP and RTAP showing the most spatially extensive Control > Stroke effects, followed by RTPP and FA, whereas MD showed extensive effects in the opposite, Stroke > Control direction. Regional discrimination varied by anatomical region and metric, without a uniform advantage of MAP-MRI over DTI. Exploratory diffusion-function analyses identified several nominal associations, but none survived correction across all comparisons. These findings demonstrate complementary, region- and metric-specific sensitivity of MAP-MRI and DTI to chronic stroke-related microstructural abnormalities. MAP-MRI identified distributed abnormalities across regional and whole-brain analyses, while MD remained highly sensitive to widespread tissue differences. The differing spatial distributions and regional discriminative performance of MAP-MRI and DTI suggest that these approaches capture partially distinct features of the post-stroke diffusion environment. Together, these findings support their complementary use for characterizing distributed microstructural abnormalities following chronic stroke.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究比较了弥散张量成像（DTI）与平均表观传播子MRI（MAP-MRI）在刻画慢性卒中后脑微结构改变方面的敏感性，分析了慢性卒中参与者和健康对照者的多壳弥散及T1加权数据。结果显示，MAP-MRI指标在多数预设脑区检出组间差异，全脑分析中也呈现广泛异常，其中RTOP和RTAP的空间范围最广；DTI的平均弥散率（MD）同样对广泛组织差异高度敏感，而各向异性分数（FA）检出的区域相对较少。两种方法在不同脑区和指标上的区分能力各有高低，未显示MAP-MRI具有一致优势，提示二者捕捉的是卒中后弥散环境中部分不同的特征，可互补用于描述慢性卒中后的分布式微结构异常；探索性的弥散-功能关联则未能在多重比较校正后保留。

papers.title: Diagnostic classification of ASD improves with positively sparsified DTI inter-regional correlation and graph-theoretical artificial intelligence.
papers.authors: Ratnaik R, P SK, Selvaganesh L, Sengar SS, Ronickom JFA.
papers.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by impairments in social interaction and behavioral functioning. ASD diagnosis primarily relies on behavioral assessments and can vary across individuals. In this study, an ASD diagnostic model was developed using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) derived inter-regional correlations, graph-theoretical analysis and artificial intelligence. Initially, the DTI data from 283 individuals (154 ASD and 129 typically developing) were preprocessed using a standard pipeline. Subsequently, DTI-derived parameters were extracted from 50 white matter (WM) regions. Inter-regional correlations were computed between DTI-derived parameters using Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), Biweight midcorrelation coefficient, and Spearman rank correlation coefficient. The resulting fully correlated matrices were subsequently decomposed into positive and negative correlation matrices. These matrices were sparsified at different threshold levels to construct graph networks. Nine graph-theoretical features were calculated for each WM region, yielding 450 features, which were fed as input to artificial intelligence models, including logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), random forest, extreme gradient boosting, and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network. The highest average 5-fold classification accuracy of 90.47% was achieved using 75 features derived from a positively correlated PCC network thresholded at 0.2 and SVM. The most discriminative features were eigenvector and pagerank centrality of the cingulum (cingulate gyrus) left, and eigenvector centrality of the superior corona radiata left, inferior cerebellar peduncle right, and cingulum (cingulate gyrus) right. These findings indicate that positively sparsified DTI inter-regional correlation networks combined with graph-theoretical analysis and artificial intelligence provide a promising framework for accurate ASD classification.

papers.title: Altered language network microstructure links with impaired language function and development in very preterm/very low birth weight born adults.
papers.authors: Gambarte L, Wendt J, Hippen R, Daamen M, Boecker H, Bartmann P, Wolke D, Schmitz-Koep B, Hedderich DM, Sorg C, Menegaux A.
papers.abstract: Premature birth is associated with impaired language function. In premature-born children, language function has been linked with microstructural alterations of the language network.Whether these brain-language associations persist into adulthood remains unclear. We investigated the microstructural properties of major dorsal and ventral language pathways in very preterm/very low birth weight (VPT/VLBW) adults and their associations with language performance in adulthood and childhood. Sixty-three VPT/VLBW and eighty full-term-born adults (mean age 26.8 years) underwent diffusion-weighted imaging and language assessment. The arcuate fasciculus, superior longitudinal fasciculus, uncinate fasciculus and inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus were reconstructed using probabilistic tractography from which fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) measures were extracted. Adult language function was assessed via the Regensburg word fluency test, rapid automatized naming and verbal IQ; childhood language was assessed at the mean age of 8 using the Kaufman Assessment Battery for children. We observed altered language network microstructure in VPT/VLBW participants, illustrated by lower FA and higher MD in the SLF and UF. These microstructural alterations were associated with language function in adulthood, but also with language development in childhood. We found that the association between tract microstructure and language abilities differed between groups. Our results demonstrate altered language network microstructure in premature born adults, which links with impaired language function and development. These findings extend previous work by comprehensively characterizing the adult dorsal and ventral language network and relating its microstructural properties to language function across development. The selective follow-up sample may limit generalizability to the broader VPT/VLBW population.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察极早产/极低出生体重成人的语言网络微结构是否改变，以及这些改变是否与其成年期语言表现和童年期语言发展相关。研究对极早产/极低出生体重成人和足月出生成人进行弥散加权成像与语言评估，重建背侧和腹侧语言通路并提取微结构指标。结果显示，极早产/极低出生体重成人在上纵束和钩束表现出微结构改变，且这些改变与成年期语言功能及童年期语言发展均有关联，但通路微结构与语言能力之间的关联在两组间存在差异。作者据此认为，早产成人存在语言网络微结构改变，并与语言功能受损及发展相关；同时提示该随访样本的选择性可能限制结果外推。

papers.title: Atlas-assisted segment anything model for fetal brain MRI (FeTal-SAM).
papers.authors: Zeng Q, Liu W, Li B, Didier R, Grant PE, Karimi D.
papers.abstract: This paper presents FeTal-SAM, a novel adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) tailored for fetal brain MRI segmentation. Traditional deep learning methods often require large annotated datasets for a fixed set of labels, making them inflexible when clinical or research needs change. By integrating atlas-based prompts and foundation-model principles, FeTal-SAM addresses two key limitations in fetal brain MRI segmentation: (1) the need to retrain models for varying label definitions, and (2) the lack of insight into whether segmentations are driven by genuine image contrast or merely inferred by learned spatial priors. We leverage multi-atlas registration to generate spatially aligned label templates that serve as dense prompts, alongside a bounding-box prompt, for SAM's segmentation decoder. This strategy enables binary segmentation on a per-structure basis, which is subsequently fused to reconstruct the full 3D segmentation volumes. Evaluations on two datasets, the dHCP dataset and an in-house dataset demonstrate FeTal-SAM's robust performance across gestational ages. Notably, it achieves Dice scores comparable to state-of-the-art baselines which were trained for each dataset and label definition for well-contrasted structures like cortical plate and cerebellum, while maintaining the flexibility to segment anatomical structures that could be templated by compatible atlas image and label sample pairs. Although slightly lower accuracy is observed for subtle, low-contrast structures (e.g., hippocampus, amygdala), our results highlight FeTal-SAM's potential as a flexible atlas-conditioned segmentation framework without requiring a separately trained model for each supported parcellation. This method thus constitutes a promising step toward clinically adaptable fetal brain MRI analysis tools.

papers.title: Micro- and nanoplastics and potential perturbation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis.
papers.authors: Macedo DS, Lima JGV, Queiroz AIG, Cordeiro RA.
papers.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants increasingly investigated for their potential neurotoxicological relevance. This narrative review critically evaluates experimental and emerging human evidence linking plastic exposure to microbiota-gut-brain communication and brain-related vulnerability. MPs and NPs are considered separately because differences in particle size, surface properties, cellular uptake, barrier interactions, and biodistribution constrain toxicological extrapolation across particle classes. Controlled animal studies provide the strongest mechanistic evidence, reporting microbiota compositional and metabolic perturbations, intestinal barrier alterations, systemic inflammatory signaling, neurovascular effects, and neurobehavioral changes under defined exposure conditions. However, these findings are limited by heterogeneous particle characterization, frequent use of pristine model particles, uncertain dose relevance, variable study quality, and incomplete distinction between intrinsic particle effects and toxicity associated with additives or co-contaminants. Evidence for a sequential microbiota-barrier-lipopolysaccharide-neuroinflammation pathway remains incomplete, and individual components should be interpreted as interacting candidate mechanisms rather than an established causal cascade. Human evidence is substantially weaker and is dominated by biomonitoring, post-mortem detection, and early observational associations that cannot establish parenchymal brain exposure or causality for neuropsychiatric or neurodegenerative disease. Progress will require environmentally representative particle libraries, chronic low-dose and route-specific models, spatial validation of brain entry, harmonized contamination-controlled biomonitoring, longitudinal human cohorts, explicit causal frameworks, and validated multi-omic integration. Current evidence therefore supports MPs and NPs as candidate environmental modifiers of neurobiological vulnerability rather than established human neurotoxicants.

papers.title: When brain networks crash: connectivity, slow-wave activity and neural replay in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Pini L, Campuzano C, Zhang L, Imbimbo BP, Allegra M.
papers.abstract: Brain connectivity disruption is a hallmark of neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet how network breakdown gives rise to cognitive deficits remains unclear. Here, we review the evidence bearing on three interconnected processes that have been proposed to link molecular pathology to cognitive decline. First, we summarize evidence that misfolded proteins propagate along brain connectivity pathways, making the connectome the biological substrate for disease progression. Second, we discuss the divergent trajectory reported across the AD continuum, an initial compensatory hyperconnectivity followed by progressive hypoconnectivity and network collapse, together with the accompanying oscillatory changes (intrusion of slow-wave activity and suppression of fast oscillatory rhythms). Third, we examine the proposal that these oscillatory alterations compromise neural replay mechanisms, critical for memory consolidation, representing the potential link between network dysfunction and cognitive decline. By integrating evidence from human neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and animal models in the AD field, this framework offers new perspectives for therapeutic interventions targeting brain connectivity and replay mechanisms in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Phase-associated differences in perivascular and glymphatic-related MRI markers in AQP4-IgG-seropositive neuromyelitis Optica spectrum disorder: A cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Xu Y, Zhan Y, Zheng Z, Xu H, Zhao M, Cai Y, Zhao Y, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Background Perivascular and brain fluid-homeostasis-related MRI measures reflect distinct structural and diffusion-related features, but their phase-associated profiles in aquaporin-4 immunoglobulin G (AQP4-IgG)-seropositive neuromyelitis Optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) remain unclear. Methods In this single-center cross-sectional study, 78 participants were included, comprising 55 patients with AQP4-IgG-seropositive NMOSD (26 in the acute phase and 29 in remission) and 23 healthy controls. Basal ganglia perivascular space (BG-PVS) and white matter perivascular space (WM-PVS) volumes were quantified from T1-weighted images using automated segmentation, the bilateral mean diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index was derived from diffusion MRI, and total choroid plexus (ChP) volume was measured on three-dimensional T1-weighted images. Principal group comparisons were covariate-adjusted, and the four adjusted omnibus group tests were corrected for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) procedure. Results BG-PVS volume showed a significant covariate-adjusted group effect after BH-FDR correction (F(2, 72) =7.03; raw P = 0.00163; q = 0.00651). BG-PVS volume was higher in remission-phase AQP4+ NMOSD than in acute-phase AQP4+ NMOSD (geometric-mean ratio=1.389; 95% CI, 1.058-1.824; Tukey-adjusted P = 0.0139) and healthy controls (geometric-mean ratio=1.486; 95% CI, 1.126-1.960; Tukey-adjusted P = 0.0030), whereas no significant difference was observed between acute-phase NMOSD and healthy controls. WM-PVS volume, the bilateral mean DTI-ALPS index, and total ChP volume showed no significant covariate-adjusted group effects after BH-FDR correction. Conclusions Remission-phase AQP4-IgG-seropositive NMOSD was characterized by higher BG-PVS volume and a distinct peripheral immune profile compared with the acute phase. These findings suggest that glymphatic-related changes may emerge over the course of AQP4-IgG-seropositive NMOSD. Further prospective longitudinal studies are needed to validate these findings and clarify their temporal evolution.

papers.title: Unraveling myelin biogenesis: The hidden role in neuropsychiatric disorders.
papers.authors: Garcia Valdez K, Murambadoro AK, Punch KD, Martin BC, Mourão N, Szobody MW, Gullapalli S, Sayers T, Baldado L, Rodriguez IN, Bellamkonda A, Penmetcha N, Anand N, Belmares R, Potter-Baker K, Gadad BS.
papers.abstract: Glial cells in the central nervous system (CNS) are associated with signal transduction via myelination of neuronal axons, neural pathway formation, and neurotransmitter regulation. Specifically, myelination of axons is vital for electrical signal conduction, allowing the nervous system to perform its executive functions. Without these white-matter components, a variety of neuropsychiatric pathologies arise. This review details the current literature on myelin dysregulation in neuropsychiatric disorders, including major depressive disorder (MDD), suicide, chronic alcohol-use disorder (CAUD), schizophrenia (SCZ), and bipolar disorder (BD). An overview of myelin biogenesis and neuroimaging techniques is also discussed. These disorders present with similar pathologies involving decreased myelination in various brain regions. Studies on MDD report reduced myelination in the prefrontal cortex, upregulation of inflammatory cytokines, and decreased oligodendrocyte differentiation. In BD, decreased myelination was evident in the corpus callosum, left internal capsule anterior corona radiata, and the bilateral cingulum. Research into post-mortem brain tissue from suicide cases displayed altered expression of myelin-supporting genes, leading to destabilized myelin membranes and increased susceptibility to oxidative stress. Downregulation of oligodendrocyte structural genes has been noted in certain cases of SCZ, and ethanol has been shown to activate toll-like receptors in the CNS that similarly alter myelin-coupled gene expression. Current literature on myelin dysregulation within these disorders is limited in scope. Imaging techniques for visualizing myelination in vivo are similarly restricted. Further inquiry into the mechanism of demyelination within neuropsychiatric disorders and improvement of myelin imaging techniques could deepen understanding of disease pathology, specify diagnostic criteria, and allow for the development of advanced treatment options for vulnerable patient populations.

papers.title: Treatment-associated structural connectome reorganization following high-frequency rTMS in major depressive disorder: A low- and high-order connectivity study.
papers.authors: Guan M, Wang Z, Liu N, Tang N, Xie Y, Wang H.
papers.abstract: Background High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) of the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) is an established treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD), but associated changes in structural-connectome topology remains unclear. Specifically, higher-order structural connectivity (HOSC), defined by similarities between regional structural connectivity profiles, may provide information beyond direct low-order structural connectivity (LOSC). Methods Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data were acquired from 23 patients with MDD before and after 10-Hz rTMS and from 30 matched healthy controls (HCs). LOSC networks were constructed based on deterministic tractography, whereas HOSC networks were derived from similarities between regional LOSC profiles. Graph-theoretical analysis and network-based statistics were employed to characterize topological and subnetwork differences. Results Depressive symptoms decreased significantly after treatment. Global LOSC topology remained stable, whereas HOSC showed case-control differences in network segregation and post-treatment differences in small-world organization relative to HCs. Network-based analysis revealed focal strengthening of a left insula-hippocampal-inferior temporal component in LOSC and distributed HOSC variation involving cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuitry, particularly the thalamus and caudate. Nodal analyses further identified treatment-associated centrality changes involving the thalamus and hippocampus. Conclusion High-frequency rTMS treatment was associated with coordinated structural-connectome variation across low- and high-order network organization in MDD. These findings should be interpreted as treatment-associated changes rather than effects attributable specifically to rTMS and suggest that HOSC may provide a complementary representation of network variation accompanying clinical improvement.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨重度抑郁症患者接受左侧背外侧前额叶高频rTMS治疗后，结构连接组拓扑是否发生改变，并比较低阶结构连接与基于区域连接剖面相似性的高阶结构连接。研究对患者治疗前后及健康对照进行弥散张量成像，结合图论和网络统计分析。结果显示抑郁症状显著减轻，全局低阶拓扑保持稳定，而高阶网络在网络分离和小世界组织上呈现与对照的差异及治疗前后变化；网络层面可见低阶中左侧岛叶-海马-颞下成分的局部增强，高阶则涉及皮层-纹状体-丘脑-皮层环路的分布式变化，节点分析还提示丘脑和海马的中心性改变。作者强调这些应理解为与治疗相伴的变化，而非特异地归因于rTMS，并认为高阶连接可补充反映临床改善伴随的网络变化。

papers.title: Profiles of Chronic Pain and Cognitive Concerns: A Cluster Analysis Among Older Adults Enrolled in a Mind-body Activity Intervention.
papers.authors: Gnall KE, Boyd SM, Hooker JE, Yucebas D, Ritchie CS, Vranceanu AM.
papers.abstract: Chronic pain and cognitive concerns are highly comorbid, particularly among older adults, though the specific severity and symptom overlap may vary across individuals. We aimed to characterize distinct profiles of individuals with chronic pain and subjective cognitive concerns (concern of persistent cognitive decline, with or without objective cognitive deficits) and compare demographic/psychosocial variables between subgroups. We analyzed baseline data from an ongoing randomized controlled trial comparing a mind-body activity intervention to a health education control. As part of the larger study, older adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain and subjective cognitive concerns completed measures of pain severity (NRS), pain interference (PROMIS), and subjective (ECog-12) and objective cognitive dysfunction (RBANS). Participants also completed measures of mental health symptoms (anxiety, depression), general psychosocial factors (loneliness, mindfulness, self-compassion, coping skills), and pain-specific psychological factors (pain catastrophizing, kinesiophobia, pain self-efficacy). An exploratory hierarchical cluster analysis examined unique symptom profiles among participants with complete data (n=251) on the four pain/cognitive dysfunction variables, and multivariate logistic regression models examined cluster membership by demographic and psychosocial variables. We identified a three-cluster solution: (1) lowest symptom burden (n=101); (2) mixed symptom burden (n=93); and (3) highest symptom burden (n=57). Several demographic, mental health, and psychosocial factors significantly distinguished between subgroup membership. Results elucidate the heterogeneity in clinical presentations within these two overlapping conditions and suggest specific potential risk factors for experiencing greater symptom burden. Findings overall represent an important first step in identifying which older adults may benefit most from interventions for co-occurring chronic pain and cognitive concerns. PERSPECTIVE: This article characterizes distinct profiles of older adults with chronic pain and cognitive concerns and suggests potential risk factors for experiencing greater symptom burden. Findings can help inform which older adults are most likely to benefit from interventions targeting co-occurring chronic pain and cognitive concerns.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于一项正在进行的随机对照试验的基线数据，对患有慢性肌肉骨骼疼痛并伴有主观认知担忧的老年人进行探索性聚类分析，以识别不同的症状特征组合。分析在疼痛严重程度、疼痛干扰及主客观认知功能等指标上识别出三类人群：症状负担最低、症状负担混合以及症状负担最高。多项人口学、心理健康和社会心理因素能够区分这些亚组，提示某些因素可能与更高的症状负担相关。作者认为，这有助于理解慢性疼痛与认知担忧共病时的临床异质性，并为判断哪些老年人可能从相关干预中获益更多提供了初步线索，但结果尚属探索性，不能直接推断因果关系或干预效果。

papers.title: EEG-VTSFN: An enhanced approach for differentiating between unipolar and bipolar mood disorders.
papers.authors: Zhao X, Cui Y, Zhao T, Wang B, Wang Y, Chen F, Zhang H, Cui Y, Liu Y, Zhang Y, Sha S, Zhang L, Hong B, Lu B, Yan Y, Ren Y, Wang G.
papers.abstract: Accurate differentiation between Bipolar Disorder (BD) and Unipolar Depression (UD) is a significant clinical challenge due to overlapping manifestations and a lack of objective biomarkers. While EEG offers high temporal resolution, its psychiatric utility for diagnostic differentiation remains limited. To address this, we propose the Variational Autoencoder (VAE)-based Time-Space Fusion Network (VTSFN). VTSFN transforms complex EEG signals into latent-space representations to mitigate noise and construct stable latent co-activation patterns. By integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and attention mechanisms, the model captures temporal dynamics to identify discriminative patterns. Our results demonstrate that VTSFN achieved the highest accuracy and AUC point estimates among the evaluated models, with a test-set accuracy of 79.3% (95% CI, 65.5%-93.1%) and an AUC of 82.7% (95% CI, 63.2%-98.5%), without significant paired AUC differences at p < 0.01. Validation in a diagnostic-switch (tBD) cohort (n = 22) identified 17/22 converters (sensitivity, 77.3%; 95% CI, 59.1%-90.9%), requiring further longitudinal validation. Exploratory feature analysis revealed that, compared with UD patients, BD and tBD patients exhibited weaker latent co-activation in right parieto-temporal and temporo-occipital regions, alongside stronger latent co-activation in left frontal-right parietal and temporal regions. These model-derived channel similarity patterns require independent validation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对双相障碍与单相抑郁临床表现重叠、缺乏客观生物标志物而难以区分的问题，提出一种基于变分自编码器的时间—空间融合网络，将脑电信号转换为潜空间表示并结合时序与注意力机制提取判别特征。在受评估的模型中，该模型取得了最高的准确率和AUC点估计，并在一个诊断转换队列中识别出多数后来发生转换的个体，但作者强调仍需纵向验证。探索性特征分析显示，双相及转换组在右侧顶颞和颞枕区的潜共激活弱于单相抑郁组，而在左额—右顶及颞区更强；这些由模型导出的通道相似性模式尚需独立验证。

papers.title: Right putaminal gray matter change tracks psychomotor recovery after accelerated iTBS in melancholic treatment-resistant depression.
papers.authors: Mao D, Wu GR, Cavendish BA, De Smet S, De Witte S, Baeken C.
papers.abstract: Background Psychomotor retardation is a prominent and disabling feature of melancholic depression. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) may hasten antidepressant effects, but neural substrates of early symptom improvement remain unclear. Given the central role of frontostriatal circuitry in motivation and behavioral activation, structural alterations in the striatum may represent a possible neural substrate of early therapeutic change. Methods Structural MRI was acquired from 61 patients with melancholic TRD and 77 healthy controls, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess baseline striatal gray matter volume differences. Patients then underwent a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of left dorsolateral prefrontal aiTBS, comprising 20 sessions over four days. In 50 patients with complete pre- and post-treatment data, we tested whether GMV change in the baseline-identified striatal region was associated with clinical change in the active and sham groups (n = 25 each). Results Patients showed greater right putamen GMV than controls at baseline. After active aiTBS, greater right putamen GMV increase was associated with greater psychomotor retardation improvement. This association was absent after sham stimulation and was not observed for overall depression severity. Conclusion The right putamen appears structurally altered in melancholic TRD. After active aiTBS, short-term putamen GMV increase was associated with psychomotor rather than broader depressive improvement. This pattern should not be interpreted as structural normalization but may reflect a relationship between putaminal change and early psychomotor recovery.

papers.title: Multivariate connectivity deviations reveal task-evoked and clinical network reorganization.
papers.authors: Kröll JP, Abdelmotaleb M, Kocataş H, Müller V, Paas L, Meinzer M, Flöel A, Eickhoff S, Patil KR.
papers.abstract: Understanding how cognitive demands and pathology reshape functional connectivity (FC) requires multivariate, region-specific methods. Here, we introduce one-class SVM-based connectome anomaly recognition (OSCAR), which detects condition-related deviations in regional connectivity profiles. OSCAR learns region-to-whole-brain connectivity patterns from a reference state using one-class support vector machines and quantifies target-condition deviations based on outlier proportions. We validated OSCAR across three diverse cognitive tasks, in which it identified regions within networks associated with conflict processing, object-location memory, and lexical learning. In a clinical cohort that included individuals with early psychosis, OSCAR identified relevant regions, including thalamic and basal ganglia areas. Compared with permutation-based multivariate analysis of variance, OSCAR detected additional established task- and disease-relevant parcels, while its task-related findings were at least as close, and often closer, to independent activation findings. OSCAR thus provides an interpretable, region-centered approach for mapping multivariate FC reconfigurations across experimental and clinical conditions.

papers.title: Neuroplastic changes in functional connectivity associated with problematic smartphone use in a data-driven rs-fMRI study.
papers.authors: Arató Á, Darnai G, Dudás B, Szente AT, Alhour HA, Perlaki G, Orsi G, Nagy SA, Janszky J.
papers.abstract: Previous studies revealed altered functional connections in problematic smartphone use (PSU), but most of the studies used self-reported data to assess PSU. Therefore, in the current study, we investigated neuroplastic changes in functional connectivity (FC) associated with PSU and objectively measured smartphone screen time (OMST) using data-driven multivariate pattern analysis. Based on our results, OMST had no direct effect on FC, but the FC between the somatomotor and the frontoparietal networks was negatively, while the connection between the somatomotor and limbic networks was positively associated with PSU. In addition, the FC between the default mode network and the limbic system was negatively, while connectivity between the default mode and the somatomotor networks was also negatively associated with PSU. In light of our findings, PSU may impair higher level brain networks, although future studies are highly needed to determine which specific objectively measured screen time activities might affect brain functions.

papers.title: Cloning and expression of CRH genes in Epinephelus coioides and its potential application in stress resistance evaluation.
papers.authors: Liu S, Wang Z, Yu F, Lu Y, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) is a hypothalamic regulatory peptide that modulates the hypothalamic-pituitary-interrenal (HPI) axis and mediates stress responses in fish. Fluctuations in environmental factors such as temperature, ammonia nitrogen, and dissolved oxygen are among the most common triggers of fish stress, which can disrupt homeostasis, increase disease susceptibility and mortality, and thereby constrain the sustainable development of grouper aquaculture. To identify more suitable stress tolerance indicators for timely assessment of fish stress status in grouper farming, this study focused on CRH to evaluate its response characteristics under environmental stress and its feasibility as a candidate indicator. To this end, we cloned and characterized the CRH gene from orange spotted grouper (Epinephelus coioides) and examined its temporal expression patterns alongside serum physiological and biochemical parameters under 48 h acute challenges of high temperature, high ammonia, and low oxygen. The results showed that the open reading frame (ORF) of CRH is 516 bp in length, encoding 171 amino acids with a conserved CRF domain. Following acute stress, CRH expression in the gill, liver, and brain tissues exhibited significant stress responsive changes, but with distinct tissue specific patterns. Under high temperature and high ammonia stress, gill expression showed a bimodal fluctuation, liver expression rose initially then declined before stabilizing, and brain expression increased, then decreased, and rose again or continued to rise; under hypoxia, all three tissues displayed a unimodal pattern of initial increase followed by a decrease, with markedly smaller fluctuation amplitudes. The magnitude of stress response was positively correlated with stress intensity, and fish showed strong tolerance and adaptation to hypoxic conditions. This study clarifies the gene sequence and evolutionary conservation of CRH in E. coioides, reveals its response patterns to environmental stress, and preliminarily demonstrates that CRH has potential and feasibility as a stress tolerance evaluation indicator for grouper.

papers.title: Sex-divergent neurovascular and cognitive effects of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
papers.authors: Kirby BD, Clary BL, Burrage E, Chantler PD, Dakhlallah D, Karelina K, Brown CM, Simpkins JW.
papers.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion is the leading risk factor for the development of vascular dementia and is associated with white matter damage and cognitive impairment. Here, we assessed sex differences in vascular and neural pathology and cognitive impairment in the asymmetric carotid arterial stenosis (ACAS) mouse model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion. Thirty days of ACAS significantly reduced cerebral blood flow, increased microvascular permeability as evidenced by extravasation of IgG and fibrinogen into brain parenchyma, and impaired MCA vasodilation. ACAS also induced white matter damage in the hippocampus and corpus callosum, with greater damage in the corpus callosum of females compared to males. Spatial memory impairments on the Barnes maze were significantly greater in ACAS males than in females. Finally, miRNA analyses revealed upregulated angiogenic miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS females and upregulated neuroinflammatory miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS males. Together, these findings indicate that the ACAS model produces robust neuropathology and sex differences in spatial memory and miRNA profiles.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注慢性脑低灌注的神经血管与认知后果是否存在性别差异，采用不对称颈动脉狭窄小鼠模型，在持续低灌注后评估脑血流、微血管通透性、血管舒张、白质损伤、空间记忆及miRNA表达。结果显示，模型动物出现脑血流下降、微血管渗漏和血管舒张受损，海马与胼胝体白质受损，其中雌性胼胝体损伤更重，而雄性空间记忆损害更明显；雌性海马和皮层以促血管生成miRNA上调为主，雄性则以神经炎症相关miRNA上调为主。作者据此指出，该模型可稳定复现神经病理改变，并在空间记忆和miRNA谱上呈现性别分化，提示慢性脑低灌注的损伤机制和认知后果可能因性别而异。

papers.title: Dynamic roles of embryonic glial cells in octopus brain development.
papers.authors: Lassnig MA, Geslain E, Nguyen B, Abaffyová D, Styfhals R, Spanier K, Patel A, Gattamraju A, Poovathingal S, Wojno M, Van Dijck M, Almansa E, Rogers TF, Simakov O, Accorsi A, Seuntjens E.
papers.abstract: Coleoid cephalopods, such as octopus, squid, and cuttlefish, have evolved remarkably large nervous systems with neuron numbers comparable to those of small mammals. Despite this, little is known about how these nervous systems develop, which genetic programs drive the formation and diversification of their neural cells, and what factors contribute to evolutionary brain expansion. This study combined single-cell multi-omics with spatial expression analysis to uncover the cell types and the regulatory mechanisms underlying nervous system development and evolution in Octopus vulgaris. We discovered an early embryonic glial cell population that is distinct from neurogenic progenitors and defined by orphan nuclear receptor 4a (nr4a), distal-less homeobox (dlx), and prospero homeobox (pros) regulons. Their spatial distribution and dynamic transcriptional profile during embryogenesis indicated that these cells might orchestrate cell migration, axon guidance, and brain patterning before expressing neuronal markers or differentiating into mature glia. Comparison of embryonic glial transcriptional signatures across two cephalopods, a gastropod, and Drosophila revealed shared expression of nr4a, dlx, and pros in mollusks, while embryonic glia in Drosophila expressed pros, dlx, repo, ttk, and gcm but not nr4a. Intriguingly, the overall gene expression profile of cephalopod embryonic glia has diverged from that of Pomacea canaliculata (golden apple snail), whose glia do not express guidance or patterning genes. Together, these findings identified a conserved embryonic glial cell type in mollusks that might have acquired new functions in coleoid cephalopods to organize neuronal migration and wiring in their expanded brain.

papers.title: The effects of foreign accent syndrome on bilingual speech production: Multilevel evidence from a controlled-case study.
papers.authors: Contreras-Ruston F, Navarra J, Elvira-García W, Sierpowska J, Rico-Pons I, Paipa A, Peñaloza C.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
papers.abstract: Foreign Accent Syndrome (FAS) is a rare motor speech disorder with altered speech patterns perceived as a foreign accent. The effects of FAS on the first (L1) and second-acquired (L2) languages in bilinguals have not been examined in depth and knowledge about its neural correlates is limited. Additionally, possible disruptions in auditory-motor feedback processes supporting speech monitoring and voice adaptation are rarely assessed. This study reports on P1, an L1 Catalan- L2 Spanish bilingual with FAS. We sought to characterize FAS in her two languages using a multilevel approach combining perceptual, phonetic, neuropsychological, sensorimotor adaptation to auditory feedback and structural neuroimaging analyses. Results showed that P1's L1 and L2 speech production were perceived as foreign by native bilingual listeners. Phonetic analyses revealed segmental and suprasegmental disturbances in both languages resulting from focal left motor cortex damage. Voice adaptation to auditory noise revealed an abnormal pattern, with differences between L1 and L2, suggesting altered auditory-motor integration. Notably, P1's speech rate, fluency and eloquence were more affected in her L1, suggesting decreased automaticity in this language. She also presented domain-general executive control deficits and increased L1 to L2 switching, as she found L2 production easier. These findings suggest differential effects of FAS on the L1 and L2 speech production of P1, with increased L1-L2 switching as a potential compensatory strategy to decrease executive control burden in L1 production and facilitate more fluent communication. Our findings highlight a potential role for disrupted auditory-motor speech and voice integration in the manifestation of bilingual FAS.

papers.title: Assessing brain-behaviour coupling in non-invasive brain stimulation: Insights from reliable change indices and Monte Carlo simulations.
papers.authors: Fujiyama H, Wansbrough K, Lebihan B, Tan J, Levin O, Mathersul DC, Tang AD.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
papers.abstract: Non-invasive brain stimulation (NiBS) studies frequently report exploratory brain-behaviour correlations following the application of NiBS. However, these analyses are typically underpowered and rely on ratio-based change scores with known statistical limitations. We addressed these limitations by pooling individual data from three independent studies (N = 69) and combining empirical analysis with a Monte Carlo simulation framework. All studies applied 20 Hz transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) targeting the pre-supplementary motor area (preSMA) and right inferior frontal gyrus (rIFG) during a stop signal task. Changes in preSMA-rIFG EEG imaginary coherency (ImCoh) and stop-signal reaction time (SSRT) were quantified using reliable change indices (RCI), z-standardised within studies for pooled mixed-effects regression. We found no meaningful association between tACS-induced ImCoh change and SSRT change (r = .013, marginal R2 = .004), with project-wise correlations being small, non-significant, and directionally inconsistent. While sensitivity analysis using ratio-based change scores converged on the same null result (r = .014), the simulation framework revealed that ratio-based scores show near-complete failure to recover true brain-behaviour associations across all plausible effect sizes. Conversely, RCI-based scores preserved directional accuracy and provided well-calibrated Type I error control, despite moderate attenuation under realistic noise conditions. These results highlight the severe statistical limits of detecting individual-level brain-behaviour coupling following 20 Hz tACS. Rather than ruling out a true biological association, our findings demonstrate that standard sample sizes and typical measurement noise create substantial 'blindness' to realistic effect sizes, underscoring a broader need for more reliable metrics and adequately powered designs in NiBS research.

papers.title: Movement regimens drive region-specific humeral adaptation: whole-bone insights from an experimental animal model.
papers.authors: Bergren S, Jashashvili T, Dowdeswell M, Carlson KJ.
papers.abstract: Repetitive movements impose distinct loading regimens on long bones, potentially eliciting predictable osteogenic responses and morphological change. Cortical responses to such movements are seldom investigated along whole diaphyses as opposed to selected locations. Morphometric mapping is a technique that is well-suited for comprehensively examining whole diaphyses. To assess responses to different movement regimens, we evaluated humeri of thirty-five female C57BL/6J mice raised from weeks 4 to 20 post-birth in one of three scenarios: linear-dominated (n = 12), turning-dominated (n = 12), and open cage (n = 11) movements. We measured aspects of humeral structure such as diaphyseal cortical thicknesses (Ct.Th), second moments of area (SMA), and deltoid crest angles (DCA) on 3D models and 2D images of humeri generated from high-resolution (microCT) image data. Turning and open-cage individuals exhibited slightly greater Ct.Th than linear individuals in proximal shaft regions. Turning individuals were distinctive in mediolateral reinforcement (SMAs) in distal shaft regions. Individuals in the open cage group tended to exhibit overall greater SMAs than individuals in the other groups. Bayesian probabilities support mean DCA differences between the linear (25.0°) versus the open cage (20.9°) and turning (22.0°) groups. Ultimately, three different movement regimens elicited unique combinations of site- and direction-specific shaft reinforcements and muscle attachment orientations without any substantial differences in overall humeral bone mass. The generally overall greater SMAs of the open cage group suggest benefits to skeletal health (e.g., diversified shaft reinforcement) may be accrued in a non-pharmacological intervention strategy that would emphasize multidirectional rather than repetitive activities.

papers.title: Thalamocortical dysconnectivity shapes cortical hierarchy disruption across illness durations in schizophrenia.
papers.authors: Huang H, Palaniyappan L, Li H, Zhou J, Tang Y, Hou C, Liu Z, He H, Jiang S, Jin L, Yi Q, Tang Y, Wang J, Cui LB, Rodriguez-Labrada R, Chang X, Feng J, Jiang Y, Yao D, Luo C.
papers.abstract: Background Schizophrenia is increasingly conceptualized as a disorder of circuit-level dysfunction. However, how thalamocortical abnormalities differ across cohorts with varying illness durations and relate to large-scale cortical hierarchical organization remains unclear. Methods We analyzed resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 1,223 patients with schizophrenia and 1,224 matched healthy controls across 12 datasets. The datasets were grouped as early-, middle-, and late-stage cohorts. Connectivity gradient mapping was applied to characterize thalamocortical organization, and computational modeling evaluated simulated hierarchical changes after modifying thalamic-salience connectivity. Results We identified a schizophrenia-relevant sensorimotor-salience-association axis that captures systematic differences in thalamocortical abnormality profiles across the stage cohorts. Along this axis, case-control effects in association regions were positive in the early-stage cohort but negative in the middle- and late-stage cohorts, whereas sensorimotor regions showed the converse pattern. This cross-cohort pattern was accompanied by reduced cortical hierarchical separation in cohorts with longer illness duration. In contrast, salience-related thalamic regions showed negative case-control effects in all three stage cohorts, with larger effect sizes in the middle- and late-stage cohorts, and these alterations were associated with clinical symptoms. Computational modification of thalamic-salience connectivity increased simulated cortical hierarchical differentiation, particularly in the middle-stage cohort. Conclusions These findings indicate that thalamocortical dysconnectivity, centered on disrupted thalamic-salience interactions, is associated with systematic differences in cortical hierarchical organization across cohorts. The cross-cohort pattern of salience-related abnormalities highlights thalamic-salience coupling as a circuit-level link to cortical hierarchical differentiation and a candidate for future mechanistic and interventional investigation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注精神分裂症中丘脑-皮层连接异常如何随病程变化，以及其与皮层层级组织的关系。作者汇总多套静息态功能磁共振数据，比较早、中、晚病程患者与匹配健康对照，并用连接梯度刻画丘脑-皮层组织、以计算模型模拟改变丘脑-显著网络连接后的层级变化。结果显示，患者存在一条感觉运动-显著网络-联合皮层的异常轴：联合区与感觉运动区的病例对照效应方向在不同病程组间相反，病程较长组的皮层层级分离降低；丘脑显著网络相关区域的异常在各组均存在，中晚期更明显并与临床症状相关。模拟增强丘脑-显著网络连接可提高皮层层级分化，提示这一耦合可能是连接异常与层级组织差异的回路层面环节，但研究为横断面关联，尚不能说明因果或治疗作用。

papers.title: Simultaneous measurement of Midbrain and Striatal Dopamine in Schizophrenia using an agonist radiotracer.
papers.authors: Slifstein M, Gil R, Weinstein J, Van Snellenberg J, Horga G, Carson R, Huang Y, Nabulsi NB, Abi-Dargham A.
papers.abstract: Background Imaging studies showing greater amphetamine-induced dopamine release in patients with schizophrenia (SCZ) compared to matched healthy controls (HC) have been repeatedly replicated, but these studies all used radiotracers that were dopamine D2 receptor antagonists. A more recent study using an agonist radiotracer did not detect this increase, raising a question whether the difference in radiotracer pharmacology affected the result. Another study examining the extrastriatal response to the amphetamine challenge with an antagonist tracer observed a blunted effect in SCZ in the midbrain, suggesting mechanisms local to the striatum might have contributed to the striatal imaging results independent of midbrain dopamine availability. Here, we sought to address both of these questions by performing neuroimaging in SCZ and HC with the agonist tracer [11C]-(+)-PHNO that is quantifiable in striatum and extrastriatal brain regions including midbrain. Methods 28 SCZ and 29 HC were scanned at baseline and 3 hours after oral administration of 0.5 mg/kg d-amphetamine. Outcome measures were baseline binding (BPND ) and the percent change following amphetamine (ΔBPND ). Results There were no significant group differences in any of the outcome measures, but we observed trend level lower BPND and ΔBPND in SCZ compared to HC. Post-hoc analysis showed this was mainly driven by dorsal striatum subregions. Associations between ΔBPND in midbrain and striatal regions were modest in both groups. Conclusions Our results are consistent with the prior study using an agonist tracer that did not observe greater ΔBPND in SCZ.

papers.title: Driving Simulation Methods for Assessing Post-Injury Driving Performance After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Scoping Review.
papers.authors: Stevenson J, Rundus CRM, Yang J, Stavrinos D.
papers.abstract: Driving is a cognitively demanding task that involves the continuous integration of attention, executive control, visual processing, and motor coordination. Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) may disrupt these functions and affect driving performance during recovery. Driving simulation is increasingly used to examine post-mTBI driving performance, yet substantial heterogeneity exists in simulator platforms, task designs, and outcome selection. This scoping review characterized driving simulation methodologies used to assess post-mTBI driving performance and examined patterns of mTBI-related findings across reported outcomes. A systematic search of seven electronic databases identified 12 eligible publications between 2017 and 2026. Publications were synthesized by participant characteristics, time since injury, simulator platform, task demands, and outcomes. Across publications, mTBI-related findings were most frequently reported for vehicle control metrics, particularly lane position variability and speed regulation. mTBI-related differences were most often condition-specific, including differences during curves, hazard events, and manipulated cognitive load or dual-task conditions. Cognitive measures also demonstrated mTBI-related differences and associations to driving performance, particularly those assessing executive functioning and processing speed domains. Differences were observed across all post-injury intervals, including ≥ 15 days, with a small number of related publications reporting performance differences after symptom resolution. However, the predominantly cross-sectional evidence does not establish whether these differences persist over time within the same individuals. Findings suggest that driving simulation can provide a useful controlled method for examining functional driving performance following mTBI across varying road environments and task demands. Future work should prioritize standardizing simulator outcomes and validating simulator performance against on-road, naturalistic-driving, and crash-related outcomes.
papers.summary_zh: 该范围综述梳理了用于评估轻度创伤性脑损伤后驾驶表现的驾驶模拟方法，系统检索后纳入2017至2026年间的相关文献，并按参与者特征、伤后时间、模拟平台、任务需求和结局指标进行归纳。综述发现，轻度创伤性脑损伤相关差异最常出现在车道位置变异和速度调节等车辆控制指标上，且多具有情境特异性，如在弯道、危险事件及认知负荷或双任务条件下更为明显；执行功能和处理速度等认知测量也与驾驶表现相关。差异在包括伤后较长时间在内的各伤后区间均有报告，少数文献提示症状消退后仍存在表现差异，但以横断面为主的证据无法确定同一人身上这些差异是否持续存在。作者据此认为驾驶模拟可作为受控的功能评估手段，并呼吁统一模拟结局指标、将其与实车、自然驾驶及碰撞结局进行验证。

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for symptom assessment and patient-reported outcomes in neuro-oncology.
papers.authors: Yogendran LV, Avery C, Crooms RC, Ozair A, Siegel C, Guterman I, Rhee JY, Binder J, Minor M, Alder L, Davis J, Sharma A.
papers.abstract: Purpose Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) are critical tools for measuring how patients experience their illness and treatment. Neuropsychiatric symptoms, headaches, seizures, and neurological deficits evolve over time and impact quality of life. In this narrative review, we summarize current literature on PROs in neuro-oncology, extant artificial intelligence (AI) tools for PRO analysis, considerations for real-world application, and ethical implications. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Google Scholar for English-language articles published from January 2015 through April 2026, supplemented by reference-list reviews. Four themes were agreed upon, and authors were assigned to each theme. Authors conducted a literature review, selected articles, and synthesized the information under each of these themes. An initial 78 articles were narrowed down to 53 confirming eligibility if they reported PRO or symptom data in people with brain tumors or computational/AI methods were applied to PRO or symptom monitoring in oncology. Article selection was verified by two senior authors (L.V.Y, A.S.). Older, foundational studies were retained where they remain the primary evidence. Results The growing volume and complexity of PRO data present challenges for traditional analysis methods. Integrating AI, including machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), may help model longitudinal symptom trajectories to predict deterioration, extract symptoms from free-text clinical notes, and embed outputs in clinical decision support tools. Autonomy, informed consent, data security, bias, access, transparency and accountability should be considered. Conclusion Successful translation will require interpretable, electronic health record-integrated, bias-mitigating tools that allow for actionable insights and preserve patient consent, privacy, and autonomy in this highly vulnerable population. Clinical trial number Not applicable.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述梳理了神经肿瘤学中患者报告结局（PRO）与症状评估的现有文献，以及用于PRO分析的人工智能工具。作者指出，PRO数据数量和复杂性不断增加，给传统分析方法带来挑战；机器学习和大语言模型等AI手段可能有助于建模纵向症状轨迹以预测恶化、从自由文本临床记录中提取症状，并将输出嵌入临床决策支持工具。文章还讨论了自主性、知情同意、数据安全、偏倚、可及性、透明度和问责等伦理问题，并认为成功转化需要可解释、与电子健康记录整合且能减轻偏倚的工具，以在脆弱人群中保留患者同意、隐私和自主性。

papers.title: Real-world safety and efficacy of lecanemab in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Wu Y, Zhu L, Chen J, Liu J, Yin K, Yang X.
papers.abstract: Background Despite the approval of lecanemab for Alzheimer's disease (AD), evidence regarding its performance outside controlled trial settings remains scarce, leaving its real-world safety and clinical utility largely unknown. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science (through October 1, 2026) for real-world studies of lecanemab in AD. Outcomes included ARIA, discontinuation, infusion-related reactions, serious adverse events, MMSE, MoCA, CDR-SB, and amyloid PET. Random-effects models with REML and Hartung-Knapp adjustment were used. Subgroup analyses were stratified by region, APOE ε4 genotype, baseline CDR score, microhemorrhage, and white matter hyperintensity. Sensitivity analyses included leave-one-out and Egger's test. Scenario-based sensitivity analyses were also performed for overlapping cohorts. This study was registered with PROSPERO (No. CRD420261333493). Results Thirty-seven studies were included. For overlapping cohorts, the largest dataset per outcome was retained after prioritizing peer-reviewed reports. Pooled incidence of any ARIA was 15.1% (US vs Asian studies 19.5% vs 9.7%), ARIA-E 6.5% (10.6% vs 2.5%), ARIA-H 11.5% (15.2% vs 7.0%), and symptomatic ARIA 1.3% (3.3% vs 0.1%). APOE ε4 homozygotes showed the highest rates across all three subtypes (any ARIA 34.1%, ARIA-E 10.3%, ARIA-H 18.9%), followed by heterozygotes (14.5%, 4.7%, 12.0%) and non-carriers (11.0%, 2.9%, 6.7%). Baseline microhemorrhage was associated with higher any ARIA (23.4% vs 11.5%) and ARIA-H (19.3% vs 4.2%), but not ARIA-E (5.4% vs 5.7%). ARIA incidence did not differ significantly by baseline CDR severity or deep white matter hyperintensity burden. Except for MoCA at ≤ 3 months (MD 0.515, 95% CI 0.451-0.578; 2 studies), no statistically significant changes were observed in cognitive outcomes. Amyloid PET decreased at 6 months (Centiloid MD -28.453, 95% CI -37.708 to -19.198) and 12 months (SUVR MD -0.171, 95% CI -0.291 to -0.052). Discontinuation rates were 3.5% (ARIA-related), 6.2% (adverse event-related), and 12.2% (total); infusion-related reactions were 18.5% and serious adverse events 2.8%. Sensitivity analyses supported robustness. Conclusions This is the first large-scale systematic review and meta-analysis of real-world studies of lecanemab reporting safety and efficacy outcomes. Safety outcomes particularly ARIA may be influenced by APOE ε4 genotype and baseline microbleeds. Cognitive outcomes lacking control data cannot confirm efficacy and longer-term cross-regional controlled studies are needed.

papers.title: Neurotransmitter-defined cerebral vulnerability patterns in frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD).
papers.authors: Tahedl M, Toomey A, Mandal N, Mangan S, Siah WF, Tan EL, Hardiman O, Kleinerova J, McKenna MC, Hutchinson S, Lope J, Bede P.
papers.abstract: Background Frontotemporal dementia syndromes encompass a genetically, clinically and radiologically heterogeneous set of conditions with distinctive clinical and imaging characteristics. The main FTD phenotypes exhibit strikingly different disease burden patterns with a predilection to specific brain regions and relative sparing of others. The apparent selectivity of cerebral involvement in FTD has not been fully elucidated. Methods A prospective neuroimaging study has been undertaken with a uniform imaging protocol to characterise atrophy patterns in ALS-FTD, behavioural variant FTD, nonfluent variant primary progressive aphasia, and semantic variant primary progressive aphasia and evaluate associations with physiological neurotransmitter receptor expression maps. Anatomical correlations between focal volume loss and a large panel of neurotransmitters were systematically evaluated and associations ranked. Results Associations were noted with GABAergic, opioid, cannabinoid, microglial and acetylcholine systems in ALSFTD-C9NEG. Correlations were observed with opioid, glutaminergic, and synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A receptor populations in ALSFTD-C9POS. Atrophy in bvFTD showed predilection to serotonergic, glutaminergic, opioid, GABAergic and cannabinoid circuits. Volume loss in nfvPPA colocalised with GABAergic, opioid, microglial, serotonergic, cannabinoid, acetylcholine, glutaminergic and dopaminergic networks. A multitude of neurotransmitter populations are implicated in svPPA including opioid, serotonergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, and microglial systems. Discussion The distinctive neuroimaging signatures of FTD phenotypes exhibit spatial associations with physiological neurotransmitter receptor density maps. The propensity of atrophy to specific brain regions in FTD subtypes may be defined by neurotransmitter populations. Our findings indirectly support the notion of neurotransmitter-system defined connectivity-based disease propagation in FTD.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究采用统一影像协议的前瞻性神经影像方法，刻画肌萎缩侧索硬化-额颞叶痴呆（ALS-FTD）、行为变异型额颞叶痴呆、非流利变异型原发进行性失语和语义变异型原发进行性失语的脑萎缩模式，并系统评估其与生理性神经递质受体表达图谱的空间关联。结果显示，各表型的局灶性体积丢失与不同递质系统存在关联，涉及GABA能、阿片、大麻素、谷氨酸能、血清素能、胆碱能、多巴胺能及小胶质等系统，且关联组合随表型而异。作者据此提出，FTD亚型萎缩好发于特定脑区可能由神经递质群体所界定，并间接支持以神经递质系统定义的连接性病变传播假说；这些关联性发现尚不能说明因果关系。

papers.title: Multi-Parametric Phase-Cycled Balanced Steady-State Free Precession Brain Tissue Characterization in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.authors: Birk F, Bender B, Tesh H, Deshmane A, Fabian MM, Kowarik MC, Lindig T, Ernemann U, Scheffler K, Heule R.
papers.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
papers.abstract: Background Time-efficient phase-cycled balanced steady-state free precession (pc-bSSFP) imaging is a novel microstructure- and myelin-sensitive approach for multi-parametric brain tissue characterization not yet evaluated in demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis (MS). Purpose To evaluate quantitative relaxometry metrics in white matter (WM) and gray matter (GM) of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) and healthy control (HC) cohorts using a multi-parametric pc-bSSFP framework. Study type Prospective and retrospective, observational. Population Twenty RRMS patients (34.5 ± 5.9 years, female 15/20) and 10 HC subjects (33.4 ± 6.9 years, female 5/10). Field strength/sequence 3 T; T1 -weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo, T2 -weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery, pc-bSSFP, B1 + mapping, single-shot spin-echo echo-planar-imaging diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). Assessment R1 , R2 , and the bSSFP asymmetry index (AI) were compared between RRMS and HC across selected WM and GM regions of interest (ROIs). DTI-derived fiber-to-field angle, number of fiber orientations, and fractional anisotropy were used for parameter anisotropy analysis. Statistical tests Linear mixed-effects models tested group, ROI, and group-by-ROI effects for each metric. Anisotropy differences between cohorts were assessed with two-sided t-tests. ROI and anisotropy tests employed false discovery rate correction with significance set at pcorr < 0.05. Results Significant group, ROI, and group-by-ROI effects were found for R1 (β = -0.16) and R2 (β = -2.84). The ROI effect was significant for AI while the group (p = 0.450) and group-by-ROI (p = 0.747) effects were non-significant. Age and sex covariates did not reach significance (Age: p = [0.563, 0.705, 0.591], Gender: p = [0.839, 0.822, 0.179], for [R1 , R2 , AI]). Fourteen of 16 ROIs showed significantly lower R1 and R2 (d = -4.25 to -0.85) in RRMS than HC. All ROIs remained non-significant for AI. R2 (pcorr ≥ 0.055) and AI (pcorr ≥ 0.108) anisotropy comparison between RRMS and HC groups did not reach significance. Data conclusion Phase-cycled bSSFP relaxometry showed WM-predominant differences in RRMS, with additional whole-brain assessment including gray matter. Evidence level 2. Technical efficacy Stage 1.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究评估相位循环平衡稳态自由进动（pc-bSSFP）多参数成像能否刻画复发缓解型多发性硬化（RRMS）患者的脑组织特征，比较了RRMS患者与健康对照在白质和灰质感兴趣区的定量弛豫指标。结果显示，R1和R2存在显著的组别、脑区及组别与脑区交互效应，多数感兴趣区在RRMS中R1和R2更低，差异以白质为主，同时全脑评估也纳入了灰质；而bSSFP不对称指数在各脑区均未见组间差异，其各向异性比较也未达显著。作者据此认为，pc-bSSFP弛豫测量可反映RRMS中以白质为主的微结构改变，但该指标对灰质病变及组织各向异性的敏感性仍有限，尚属技术效能早期阶段的方法学证据。

papers.title: Semaglutide Remodels the Gut Microbiome Beyond Its Appetite-Suppressing Action: Sex-Specific Gut-Brain Axis Implications.
