The canonical views suggest that PTSD patients are characterized by hypocortisolemia and an enhanced negative glucocorticoid feedback (nGF), whereas major depression patients typically show hypercortisolemia and impaired nGF. Here, we critically review studies on the effects of different stress models on nGF, distinguishing between nGF under resting and stress conditions. The evidence that chronic stress exposure is associated with impaired nGF is weak, except for HPA activity under resting conditions. The evidence that a single exposure to severe stressors leads to enhanced nGF under stress conditions is controversial, and the studies supporting this present important limitations. In general, the major limitations of nGF studies are the lack of plasma ACTH data, the assessment of nGF using exposure to a stressor with which animals have prior experience, and the predominant use of dexamethasone instead of natural glucocorticoids. At the dexamethasone doses typically used, this drug acts mainly at the anterior pituitary rather than at the brain level, making it difficult to relate altered nGF with changes in brain corticosteroid receptors.

papers.title: Determining the turbulent energy spectrum tensor using multidimensional diffusion MRI.
papers.authors: Clarke D, Topgaard D.
papers.abstract: Turbulent flows are of interest for various engineering and medical applications. Pulsed field gradient diffusion encoding sequences quantify overall turbulent velocity fluctuations, but do not resolve spectral characteristics of the flow. Modulated gradient sequences have the potential to measure the diffusion spectrum but are limited by unidirectional encoding. In this article, we explore multidimensional diffusion encoding via the double-rotation of the q-vector as a tool to study anisotropic turbulent flow. We demonstrate that encoding durations beyond the mean correlation time were required to satisfy the assumption of a Gaussian phase distribution. The diffusion spectrum tensor was reconstructed with reasonable accuracy. However, the assumption of single-peak encoding spectra did not hold. The development of advanced data inversion protocols is required to derive detailed insights into turbulent flow phenomena.

papers.title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
papers.authors: Zuo J, Yang H, Tang Y, Wang X, Zhong K, Peng X, Luo J.
papers.abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints. We retrospectively evaluated our method on two diverse datasets: a proprietary 7.0 T dental MRI dataset (25 T2-weighted DESS sequences from 10 beagle dogs) and a public 5.0 T brain MRI dataset (Diff5T, 50 diffusion-weighted sequences). Image quality was quantified using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID. On the 7.0 T dental test dataset (2 subjects), our method achieved a PSNR of 27.31 [26.83, 27.79] dB and the lowest LPIPS of 0.19 [0.18, 0.20]. On the 5.0 T brain test dataset (10 subjects), the method achieved a PSNR of 27.15 ± 0.10 dB, an LPIPS of 0.14 ± 0.00 and an FID of 54.01, with lower perceptual metrics than the evaluated baselines. Ablation studies indicated that the proposed frequency-domain and structural constraints reduced LPIPS and FID, with trade-offs in PSNR and SSIM. In conclusion, the evaluated framework showed improvements in perceptual metrics by integrating targeted local processing with frequency-domain and structural regularization, accompanied by a trade-off in pixel-wise fidelity metrics, supporting the technical feasibility of addressing the resolution-time trade-off in high-field MRI. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and evaluating the framework in human dental cohorts to address anatomical differences between the current canine model and human dental anatomy.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对高场MRI空间分辨率与采集时间之间的权衡，提出一种自适应局部超分辨率方法，将计算资源集中于信息丰富区域，并用扩散模型结合频域与结构约束进行正则化。方法在7.0 T犬牙MRI和5.0 T脑MRI数据上回顾性评估，结果显示其感知指标（LPIPS、FID）优于所比较的基线，但像素级保真指标存在取舍；消融分析表明频域和结构约束可改善感知指标，同时伴随PSNR和SSIM的权衡。作者据此认为该框架在技术上可行，有助于缓解高场MRI的分辨率—时间矛盾，但尚需扩展数据并在人类牙科队列中验证。

papers.title: Prenatal exposure to PFAS and multimodal structural brain development across childhood.
papers.authors: Rocha S, Uy JP, Antonacci C, Buthmann JL, Tan AP, Chong YS, Fortier MV, Eriksson J, Gotlib IH.
papers.abstract: Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous environmental pollutants that are posited to be neurotoxic to the developing brain; however, the impact of prenatal exposure to PFAS - particularly to newer, short-chain PFAS - on brain development across childhood is unclear. Methods Concentrations of 9 PFAS were quantified in cord blood plasma of 452 infants (440 for the diffusion sample) who later participated in structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at ages 4.5, 6, 7.5, and 10.5 years, providing estimates of regional cortical thickness and surface area, subcortical volumes, and fractional anisotropy (FA) of key white matter tracts. Longitudinal mixed-effect models estimated associations of PFAS with age 4.5 brain metrics and their developmental trajectories across childhood after correcting for the false discovery rate within PFAS and outcome domains. Results Higher concentrations of PFNA and PFDA in cord blood were associated with lower model-estimated age 4.5 surface area of the right paracentral lobule. PFHpA was associated with faster surface area growth in the left rostral anterior cingulate and slower growth in the right caudal middle frontal gyrus from 4.5 to 10.5 years. The short-chain compound PFBS was linked with greater model-estimated age 4.5 FA in 12 white matter tracts, while PFOA and PFNA were linked with lower FA in the middle cerebellar peduncle and the left corticospinal tract, respectively. Associations of PFBS with FA attenuated with age in several tracts. Conclusions Prenatal exposure to PFAS was associated with altered development of frontal and paracentral regions and of white matter microstructure. These findings highlight the need for further research examining the long-term associations of prenatal exposure to PFAS with children's neurodevelopment.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于452名婴儿的脐血PFAS浓度及后续4.5至10.5岁多次结构磁共振与弥散磁共振数据，考察产前PFAS暴露与儿童期皮层厚度、表面积、皮层下体积及白质各向异性（FA）发育轨迹的关联。结果显示，脐血中PFNA和PFDA浓度较高与4.5岁时右侧中央旁小叶表面积估计值较低相关；PFHpA与左侧前扣带喙部表面积增长较快、右侧额中回后部增长较慢相关；短链PFBS与12条白质纤维束4.5岁时FA估计值较高相关，且这种关联随年龄增长在部分纤维束中减弱；PFOA和PFNA则分别与小脑中脚和左侧皮质脊髓束FA较低相关。作者认为，产前PFAS暴露与额叶、中央旁区域及白质微结构的发育改变相关，提示需进一步研究其与儿童神经发育的长期关联。

papers.title: Functional neural activity and connectivity deficits underlying vocal auditory feedback control in post-stroke aphasia: An fMRI study.
papers.authors: Behroozmand R, Venezia J, Sarmukadam K, Rorden C, Bonilha L, Hickok G, Fridriksson J.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: Objective This study investigated the functional neural activity and connectivity correlates of disrupted sensorimotor integration underlying vocal production and motor control deficits in post-stroke aphasia. Methods fMRI data were acquired from 15 aphasia and 15 control participants during vocalization of speech vowel sounds under altered auditory feedback with randomized ± 100-cents pitch-shift stimuli. Results We found that stroke-induced brain damage in aphasia was associated with diminished activation within left-hemisphere dorsal stream networks, including premotor and motor cortices, posterior superior temporal regions, and supramarginal gyrus. Functional connectivity analysis revealed reduced left-hemisphere coupling between posterior superior temporal gyrus (pSTG) and dorsal and ventral precentral speech areas (dPSA and vPSA) in aphasia, indicating disrupted auditory-motor integration. Aphasia participants exhibited reduced following and opposing (i.e., compensatory) vocal responses to pitch-shifted auditory feedback, reflecting impairments in both rapid feedforward and slower feedback-based control mechanisms. In addition, impaired vocal compensatory behavior was associated with reduced functional connectivity between pSTG and the left dorsal precentral speech areas (dPSA) as well as the right dorsal laryngeal motor cortex (dLMC), suggesting the critical role of these networks in auditory-feedback-based laryngeal motor control during vocal production and their stroke-induced impairment in aphasia. Conclusions Our data provide converging evidence of disrupted auditory-motor integration and impaired neural communications within dorsal stream networks in aphasia. Significance These findings emphasize that clinical interventions for aphasia therapy benefit from targeting sensorimotor mechanisms supporting vocal auditory feedback processing and control. Personalized interventions that strengthen sensorimotor integration pathways could further enhance recovery of fluent verbal communication.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨卒中后失语症患者发声听觉反馈控制缺陷背后的功能性神经活动与连接基础，采用fMRI比较失语症患者与对照组在音高偏移听觉反馈下发声时的脑活动与功能连接。结果显示，失语症患者左半球背侧通路网络（包括运动前区、运动皮层、后颞上区及缘上回）激活减弱，后颞上回与背侧、腹侧运动前言语区之间的左半球耦合降低，提示听觉—运动整合受损；患者对音高偏移的跟随性和补偿性发声反应均减弱，反映快速前馈与较慢反馈控制机制同时受损。补偿性发声行为受损还与后颞上回同左背侧运动前言语区及右背侧喉运动皮层的连接减弱相关。作者据此认为，失语症存在背侧通路网络内听觉—运动整合与神经通讯的破坏，并提示康复干预可着眼于支持发声听觉反馈处理的感觉运动机制。

papers.title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
papers.authors: Gao F, Nguyen TN, Wang A, Li R, Xu P, Chen Y, Nogueira RG, Fang S, Hu W.
papers.abstract: Background The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. Methods This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. Results Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. Discussion In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

papers.title: Animal models for investigating post-stroke cognitive impairment: A neurovascular trafficking perspective.
papers.authors: Kaewkaen P.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major cause of long-term disability after ischemic stroke, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely explained by infarct volume, lesion location, or conventional vascular risk factors alone. Animal models are indispensable for clarifying how ischemic injury evolves into delayed cognitive dysfunction and for determining which mechanisms are experimentally tractable, reproducible, and translationally relevant. This review examines PSCI from a neurovascular trafficking perspective, focusing on how laboratory animal models can be used to investigate secretory pathway stress, endolysosomal dysfunction, autophagy-lysosomal flux, extracellular vesicle signaling, blood-brain barrier disruption, glial reactivity, myelin debris clearance, white matter injury, and cognition-relevant behavioral phenotypes. Rodent models of transient or permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion, photothrombotic stroke, embolic stroke, chronic cerebral hypoperfusion, bilateral carotid artery stenosis, and subcortical white-matter injury each reproduce selected components of the human PSCI spectrum. No single model fully captures the temporal, vascular, cellular, and cognitive complexity of human PSCI; therefore, model selection should be driven by the mechanistic question, disease phase, vascular pathology, cellular compartment, cognitive domain, and welfare burden under investigation. The central argument is not that neurovascular trafficking failure is already a proven causal pathway, but that well-designed animal studies can test, refine, or falsify this hypothesis. Future studies should integrate model validity, translational rigor, and welfare refinement through longitudinal cognitive testing, multimodal imaging, cell-specific molecular profiling, extracellular vesicle phenotyping, intervention-based validation, randomization, blinding, sample-size justification, humane endpoints, perioperative care, and transparent reporting.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述从神经血管运输的角度梳理了用于研究卒中后认知障碍（PSCI）的动物模型，讨论这些模型如何帮助探究分泌通路应激、内体-溶酶体功能、自噬-溶酶体流、细胞外囊泡信号、血脑屏障破坏、胶质反应、髓鞘碎片清除、白质损伤及认知相关行为表型。作者指出，大鼠和小鼠的多种局灶缺血、栓塞、慢性低灌注及白质损伤模型各自只再现人类PSCI谱系的部分成分，没有单一模型能完整涵盖其时间、血管、细胞与认知复杂性，因此模型选择应取决于所研究的机制问题、疾病阶段和认知域等。文章的核心主张并非神经血管运输失败已被证实为因果通路，而是设计良好的动物研究可以检验、修正或证伪这一假说，并强调未来研究需兼顾模型有效性、转化严谨性与动物福利。

papers.title: Brain-thought states during movie-watching reflect shared sensory anchors and film- and person- specific processes in association cortex
papers.authors: Wallace RS, Hardikar S, Ketcheson S, Mulholland B, Goodall-Halliwell I, McKeown B, Chitiz L, Milham M, Xu T, Margulies DS, Ho N, Karapanagiotidis T, Poerio GL, Gonzalez Alam TRJ, Turnbull A, Skipper JI, Bernhardt BC, Leech R, Wammes JD, Jefferies E, Smallwood J.
papers.abstract: Naturalistic paradigms such as movie-watching have transformed functional neuroimaging by capturing cognitive dynamics during rich, real-world experiences. A fundamental challenge, however, is determining whether the neural signatures identified during these experiences reflect general principles of cognition or the specific contexts in which they are measured. To address this question, we combined fMRI data from participants watching eight diverse films with continuous reports of ongoing thought. We found that the generalizability of brain-thought relationships depends on the cognitive process being recruited. Neural signatures linked to sensory processing remained robust across films, whereas those involving memory-related association networks depended on how we modelled between-film variability, indicating that cognition becomes increasingly context-dependent along the cortical hierarchy from sensory to association cortex. Within default and limbic networks, we identified two contrasting memory-related states with opposite consequences for comprehension. One, reflecting the integration of prior knowledge with ongoing experience, predicted better narrative comprehension and was revealed only after accounting for between-film variability. The other, associated with stimulus-independent thought, predicted poorer comprehension and emerged only when between-film variability was not modelled. Together, these findings establish when brain-experience relationships measured during naturalistic paradigms can generalize across contexts and when they instead reflect interactions between cognition and the specific environments in which cognition unfolds. More broadly, the consistency of a given brain-experiential association may depend less on where it occurs in the brain and more on the viewer’s contextual experience: perceiving the film, drawing on memory to understand it, or drifting away. Significance statement Films have revolutionized how we study healthy and atypical brain activity by capturing synchronized, semi-unconstrained dynamics of real-world cognition. Yet experience is rarely measured alongside brain activity, and most studies use one or few films; thus, we do not know whether these neural and experiential responses generalize across films. By combining brain imaging with continuous reports of ongoing thought, we find a hierarchy: sensory processing is consistent across films, whereas memory-related processes in association cortex are uniquely sensitive to how film context is modelled. Two opposing memory states relate to comprehension. One draws on memory to support understanding; the other reflects stimulus-independent thought and impairs it. Identifying brain–experience relationships across films is crucial for developing and understanding naturalistic neuroscience.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究结合功能磁共振成像与观看电影时的持续思维报告，考察大脑活动与主观体验之间的关系能否在不同影片间推广。结果显示，这种可推广性随皮层层级而变化：与感觉加工相关的神经特征在不同影片间保持稳定，而涉及记忆的联合皮层特征则取决于如何建模影片间差异，说明认知越偏向联合皮层越依赖具体情境。在默认网络和边缘网络中，作者区分出两种方向相反的 memory 相关状态：一种整合先前知识与当前体验，仅在考虑影片间差异后显现，并预测更好的叙事理解；另一种与刺激无关思维有关，仅在未建模影片间差异时出现，并预测更差的理解。作者据此指出，自然情境下脑与体验关联能否推广，更多取决于观看者所处的具体体验状态，而非仅由脑区位置决定。

papers.title: Aging Is Associated with Reduced Topographic Differentiation Between Speaking and Silent Reading
papers.authors: Basciano A, Daliri A, Chao S, Rogalsky C.
papers.abstract: Aging affects how neural activity is organized and specialized, but its impact on neural differentiation across language tasks remains unclear. In this study, we investigated whether aging influences neural differentiation during speaking and silent reading. Fifteen young adults and 15 older adults completed speaking and silent-reading tasks in a delayed-response paradigm while we collected electroencephalography (EEG) data. We examined EEG signal strength using time-resolved global field power (GFP), spatial configuration using topographic analysis of variance (TANOVA), and task-specific neural differentiation using the global dissimilarity index (DISS). We also examined the relationship between neural and behavioral measures, including digit-span scores and speech onset time. We found that speaking was associated with higher GFP than silent reading in the 388–800 ms interval, with no significant effects of group or group × task interaction, indicating similar EEG strength across groups. TANOVA revealed age-related differences in scalp topography in the 229–334 ms and 377–538 ms intervals, a task effect in the 618–723 ms interval, and a group × task interaction in the 562–636 ms interval. Notably, young adults had greater DISS than older adults during the 508–629 ms and 660–800 ms intervals, reflecting more distinct neural configurations for speaking and reading. We did not find significant correlations between DISS or GFP and behavioral measures, and the two groups performed similarly on behavioral measures. Overall, aging was associated with reduced neural differentiation between speaking and silent reading, especially during later processing stages (e.g., motor command preparation), while preserving overall EEG activity and behavioral performance. These findings may suggest that aging reduces neural network specificity (as previously suggested) and alters spatial organization without necessarily impairing behavior.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察衰老是否影响说话与默读两种语言任务间的神经分化，比较了年轻人和老年人完成延迟反应任务时的脑电活动，并结合行为测量进行分析。结果显示，两组在脑电信号强度和行为表现上相近，但老年人区分说话与默读的神经活动模式差异较小，尤其在较晚加工阶段更为明显，提示衰老可能降低神经网络的特异性并改变空间组织，而不一定伴随行为受损。研究未发现神经分化指标与行为测量之间存在显著相关。

papers.title: NeuroMark dFNC: Transferable Dynamic-State Templates for Subject-Specific and Frequency-Resolved Chronnectomics
papers.authors: Esfahani MM, Seraji M, Salem S, Jensen KM, Fu Z, Adali T, Wang Y, Calhoun V.
papers.abstract: Dynamic functional network connectivity (dFNC) commonly identifies recurring connectivity states from resting-state fMRI, but states derived independently in each dataset lack guaranteed correspondence across studies and cannot be directly estimated in new participants. We introduce NeuroMark dFNC, which extends the NeuroMark principle of prior-guided network estimation to dynamic connectivity by using reproducible reference states as priors for estimating corresponding subject-specific states. Reference-state templates were derived from UK Biobank using windowed functional network connectivity and time-frequency moments (TFMs), with split-sample reproducibility evaluated for k-means, independent component analysis (ICA), and principal component analysis (PCA) template-generation approaches. Constrained ICA then used the templates to estimate subject-specific state patterns and continuous loadings in independent FBIRN schizophrenia and ADNI Alzheimer's disease cohorts. ICA loadings were calibrated by their contribution to reconstruction of the original feature matrix. Fractional occupancy and conditional mean dwell time were calculated from the state with the largest absolute calibrated loading at each observation. The predefined templates avoided the need for dataset-specific state discovery and post-hoc state matching. In both clinical cohorts, the analysis identified state-dependent, distributed edgewise differences and differences in selected temporal summaries. Nominal frequency-resolved findings varied across states and moment-frequency bins and were treated as exploratory. NeuroMark dFNC provides a common state space for cross-cohort comparison while retaining subject-specific connectivity patterns and continuous state expression.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出NeuroMark dFNC方法，将NeuroMark的先验引导网络估计思路扩展到动态功能网络连接，用可重复的参考状态模板约束个体状态估计，从而避免各数据集独立发现状态和事后匹配。参考模板来自UK Biobank，并比较了k-means、ICA和PCA三种模板生成方式的分样本可重复性；随后用约束ICA在独立的FBIRN精神分裂症和ADNI阿尔茨海默病队列中估计个体状态模式与连续载荷。两个临床队列均发现状态依赖的分布式边水平差异及部分时间摘要指标差异，而频率分辨结果随状态和频段变化，被作者视为探索性。该方法为跨队列比较提供共同状态空间，同时保留个体连接模式和连续状态表达。

papers.title: Source-Decomposed Multimodal Graph Connectivity: A Temporal Mixture-Manifold Pipeline for Tracking Ischemic Injury and Treatment
papers.authors: Park H, Lee J, Nimmagadda A, Llinas B, Ghahfarokhi MF, Musto A, Ryu S.
papers.abstract: To capture the complex, dynamic network reorganization following acute focal brain injuries that standard static or unimodal neuroimaging frameworks routinely miss, we present an open, reproducible computational multimodal pipeline that integrates resting-state functional MRI and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) into dynamic, source-decomposed graph networks. This framework preserves sub-voxel, multi-peak distributional dynamics over time by modeling regional blood-oxygen-level-dependent signals within sliding windows using a Gaussian mixture model, with model complexity dynamically optimized. The resulting pairwise similarities define time-varying edge weights across local, nonlocal, and DTI-supported structural sources, unifying them into a multimodal connectivity manifold that precisely quantifies node strength, topological turnover, and boundary modifications. Applied to a non-human primate model of photothrombotic ischemia, the methodology revealed severe post-injury disruptions, with 66 of 144 nodes (45.8%) fundamentally altering their connectivity across localized sources. Furthermore, coupling this architecture with an Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) allowed for the continuous tracking of a tissue “reversibility” coordinate, yielding earlier detection of metabolic state collapse than unimodal baselines and generating a forecast-divergence index as a rigorous early-warning signal. Extended across post-injury treatment boundaries to evaluate network recovery toward baseline, this interpretable, modality-aware framework establishes a standardized, shareable methodological foundation for tracking complex pathophysiological dynamics in neuroinformatics research.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对急性局灶性脑损伤后常规静态或单模态神经影像难以捕捉的动态网络重组，提出一套整合静息态功能磁共振与弥散张量成像的可重复多模态计算流程，将区域信号按时间窗建模为高斯混合分布，并据此构建随时间变化的多源图连接网络。在光血栓缺血的非人灵长类模型中，该方法显示损伤后多数节点在局部来源上的连接发生根本改变，并能连续追踪组织“可逆性”坐标，较单模态基线更早提示代谢状态崩溃，还可输出预测分歧指数作为早期预警信号。作者将该框架用于评估损伤后治疗过程中网络向基线的恢复，为神经信息学中追踪复杂病理生理动态提供了可解释、可共享的方法学基础。

papers.title: Overt and Covert Speech-State Classification from Tripolar Concentric Ring Electrode EEG: A 4 mm and 10 mm Configuration Study.
papers.authors: Memon PQ, Anderson CW, Memon S.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) speech-state classification is a noninvasive method to identify the brain's overt and covert behavior. The EEG achieved through the scalp is contaminated by artifacts and volume conduction and suffers from poor spatial resolution. We present the first application of small 4 mm tripolar concentric ring electrodes (TCREs) to record the overt and covert EEG signals. In addition, EEG signals were recorded for overt and covert behavior using a 10 mm TCRE as a reference. Data were recorded from 16 participants (4 mm, n=8; 10 mm, n=8). Each participant completed 200 picture-naming trials (100 overt and 100 covert). The analysis includes task-to-baseline root mean square ratios, power spectral density, time frequency representation analysis and participant-wise overt and covert classification using linear discriminant analysis, support vector machines, and EEGNet. The overt speech produced higher task-to-baseline ratios than covert speech. In addition, EEGNet achieved the highest mean accuracy (84.06±15.57%), followed by SVM (81.56±14.23%) and LDA (76.56±15.30%).

papers.title: The Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis in Obesity: Inflammation, Appetite Dysregulation, and Feeding Behavior.
papers.authors: Sandoval-Valenzuela C, Pacheco R.
papers.abstract: Obesity is increasingly recognized as a disorder of bidirectional communication among the gut microbiota, immune system, and neural circuits controlling energy balance and feeding behavior. This review examines the associations and potential mechanistic links between obesity-associated dysbiosis, chronic low-grade inflammation, and impaired appetite regulation through interconnected peripheral and central pathways. We discuss how these signals reach the central nervous system (CNS), and promote microglial and astrocytic activation, impair leptin and insulin signaling, and disrupt hypothalamic POMC and AgRP/NPY neuronal networks. We also examine how microbial metabolites and structural components influence appetite through enteroendocrine hormones, vagal afferents, blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and direct actions on neural and glial cells. Particular emphasis is placed on short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan-derived metabolites, bile acids, and lipopolysaccharide, as well as their effects on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), peptide YY (PYY), serotonergic signaling, and mesolimbic reward pathways. Together, these findings support a bidirectional framework in which diet, microbiota function, immune signaling, and neural regulation may reinforce one another during obesity progression. However, the directionality and causal relevance of many of these relationships, particularly in humans, remain incompletely understood. Clarifying these microbiota-gut-brain interactions may identify new targets for restoring appetite control and interrupting obesity progression.

papers.title: Knowledge, Confidence and Preparedness for Brain Death Determination Among Anaesthesiology and Reanimation Residents: A National Web-Based Survey with an Embedded Randomised Vignette.
papers.authors: Yanatma S, Kaya S.
papers.abstract: Background/objectives Under Turkish law, brain death is determined by two physicians, one of whom is a specialist in anaesthesiology and reanimation or intensive care, a responsibility residents assume soon after qualifying. We assessed whether residents' confidence matches their accuracy, and whether the decision to initiate determination is influenced by the family's attitude toward organ donation. Methods Cross-sectional web-based survey of a national convenience sample of anaesthesiology and reanimation residents in Türkiye. Ten knowledge statements and three clinical vignettes combined the answer and the respondent's confidence in one choice; the primary outcome was the high-confidence error rate. In an embedded participant-blinded randomised vignette, participants were allocated 1:1 to a medically identical scenario describing the family as favourable or opposed to donation. Results A total of 206 residents were analysed. They answered 80.9% of items correctly but endorsed only 64.2% with confidence; confident answers were correct in 90.8% of instances versus 63.3% of non-confident answers (p < 0.001). The mean high-confidence error rate was 5.9 ± 7.3%, yet 50.5% committed at least one such error, and these errors clustered in four domains. In this exploratory comparison, initiation of determination did not differ between arms (85.6% versus 87.4%; adjusted odds ratio 1.29, 95% CI 0.54-3.05). Only 18.0% felt prepared to serve on a determination board; in univariable and sensitivity analyses, preparedness was associated with case exposure and formal instruction but not with knowledge score. Conclusions Residents answered most items correctly and were appropriately cautious, yet fewer than one in five felt prepared; self-reported preparedness is not a measure of clinical competence. Supervised clinical exposure, correction of specific misconceptions and communication training are priorities for future intervention studies.

papers.title: 5-Aminolevulinic Acid-Guided Glioma Resection During Awake Craniotomy: Systematic Review of Functional Safety and Surgical Benefit.
papers.authors: Mofatteh M, Mashayekhi MS, Sinclair J, Ashkan K.
papers.abstract: Background: Maximal safe resection remains the cornerstone of glioma surgery, particularly in eloquent regions where oncologic gain must be balanced against functional preservation. While 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) fluorescence-guided surgery improves extent of resection in high-grade gliomas under general anesthesia, its role during awake craniotomy (AC) remains underdeveloped. We aimed to evaluate the oncologic and functional outcomes of 5-ALA-guided tumor resection during AC. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to February 2026 for studies reporting original data on AC using 5-ALA following PRISMA guidelines. Results: Across ten studies comprising 108 patients, fluorescence positivity was 79.2% in high-grade gliomas (Grade III-IV) and 24.1% in low-grade gliomas (Grade II), among the 83 patients with both grade and fluorescence data available (grade was not reported for 19 patients in one case series, and 6 patients in one cohort study did not receive 5-ALA and were excluded from grade- and fluorescence-stratified analyses). Gross total resection was achieved in 62.2% of patients with evaluable extent-of-resection data (56.5% of the full cohort), reaching 66.7% in the largest comparative cohort. Transient aphasia occurred in 32.6% of evaluable patients, while permanent aphasia and persistent hemiparesis were observed in 14.6% and 16.9%, respectively. In multiple studies, resection was intentionally halted despite persistent fluorescence when functional mapping identified an eloquent cortex, underscoring that mapping remained the decisive determinant of surgical boundaries. No study reported conversion to general anesthesia. Conclusions: 5-ALA-guided resection during AC appears feasible and clinically useful, particularly for high-grade gliomas in eloquent regions. Permanent neurological morbidity was observed in a minority of patients, within a range broadly consistent with awake glioma surgery generally, but the absence of a non-5-ALA comparator group means that functional safety relative to awake mapping alone cannot yet be established with confidence. Across the available literature, 5-ALA consistently enhances intraoperative tumor visualization, supports identification of residual fluorescent disease, and integrates well with cortical and subcortical mapping without clear evidence of increased permanent neurological morbidity. Although functional mapping remains the decisive determinant of the final resection boundary, the available evidence supports 5-ALA as a valuable complementary adjunct in onco-functional glioma surgery.

papers.title: Tractometric: A Diffusion Tractography Software Engine for Integration into a Neuronavigation System: Technical Development and Preliminary Clinical Feasibility.
papers.authors: Mendez W, Bohórquez A, Bohórquez X, Bohórquez O, Shelton WJ, Ordóñez-Rubiano EG.
papers.abstract: Background Diffusion MRI tractography can support patient-specific neurosurgical planning, but implementation may be limited by workflow complexity, software requirements, and resource constraints. We describe Tractometric® , a diffusion tractography software engine developed for integration with the Surgimetric® neuronavigation planning environment. Methods Tractometric® was developed through a multidisciplinary, iterative co-design process involving neurosurgeons and neuroimaging specialists. The software uses a modular Model-View-Controller architecture implemented in Python (version 3.11) and supports multiple diffusion reconstruction models, deterministic and probabilistic tracking, patient-specific and atlas-derived regions of interest (ROIs), visualization, and interoperable export. The present study was designed as a technical development and preliminary clinical feasibility report. Technical workflow characteristics were described retrospectively across 30 cases, while preliminary clinical feasibility was explored in 8 patients undergoing tractography-assisted surgical planning. Intraoperative direct cortical and subcortical electrical stimulation was used as a qualitative clinical reference rather than as a formal diagnostic-accuracy test. Results Tractometric® implemented a complete workflow from diffusion data loading and preprocessing to tract reconstruction, filtering, visualization, and export to Surgimetric® . The 30-case technical series illustrated variation in processing time and user interaction according to operator experience, reconstruction model, registration, ROI strategy, and manual cleaning. In 8 preliminary clinical cases, reconstructed motor and language pathways were qualitatively concordant with positive intraoperative stimulation findings. No formal sensitivity, specificity, spatial agreement, or test-retest reproducibility estimates were calculated. Conclusions Tractometric® provides an integrated technical workflow for diffusion tractography and neuronavigation planning and was feasible to implement in a preliminary clinical series. The current data support technical feasibility and workflow integration, but do not establish anatomical accuracy, reproducibility, clinical efficacy, or cost-effectiveness. Independent, prospective validation using standardized acquisitions, predefined tractography parameters, quantitative spatial metrics, and systematic intraoperative mapping is warranted.

papers.title: MTHFR C677T and Brain MRI Patterns Across Cognitive and Vascular Disorders: A Systematic Review.
papers.authors: Gogu AA, Axelerad A, Gogu AE, Benta M, Neda-Stepan O, Bredicean AC.
papers.abstract: Background: Elevated plasma homocysteine, arising from impaired one-carbon metabolism, has been implicated in cerebral microvascular injury and in neurodegeneration. The methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) C677T polymorphism is the commonest genetic determinant of homocysteine concentration, but whether it leaves a measurable structural footprint on the brain remains unresolved. We synthesised genotype-stratified structural MRI findings in Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and vascular cognitive disorders. Methods: Four sources (PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar) were searched up to 20 September 2026. Eligible reports gave C677T-stratified structural MRI outcomes in adults with clinically defined cognitive disorders. Quality was appraised with an adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and exploratory random-effects meta-analyses supplemented a narrative synthesis. Results: Thirteen studies (3880 participants across partly overlapping cohorts) were included. Moderate-to-severe white matter lesions were modestly more frequent in TT homozygotes, consistently across contributing studies, with no consistent excess in heterozygotes. Regional volume findings were inconsistent and largely confined to one cohort, whereas whole-brain atrophy rate, hippocampal and medial temporal measures, lacunes, microbleeds, and diffusion metrics showed no genotype-only association. Homocysteine was higher in T-allele carriers wherever measured. Conclusions: The evidence is more compatible with a modest association with vascular white matter injury than with a reproducible neurodegenerative imaging phenotype and does not support genotype-guided clinical decision-making. Longitudinal, biomarker-characterised cohorts with harmonised imaging, adequately powered genotype groups, and measured nutritional status are the main priorities.

papers.title: MRI-based intratumoral and peritumoral heterogeneity for predicting intracranial progression in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma patients with treatment-naive brain metastases receiving first-line third-generation EGFR-TKIs.
papers.authors: Deng G, Li H, Dai Z, Fan J, Song X, Pang G, Li Z, Zhao F.
papers.abstract: Purpose To develop and externally test a multiparametric MRI habitat-based framework integrating intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH), peritumoral heterogeneity (PTH), and clinical characteristics for predicting intracranial progression in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and de novo brain metastases receiving first-line third-generation (3rd-gen) EGFR-TKI monotherapy. Materials and methods This retrospective multicenter study included patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and de novo brain metastases who received first-line 3rd-gen EGFR-TKI monotherapy. Patients were assigned to an internal training cohort (n = 90) and an external testing cohort (n = 51). The binary prediction outcome was intracranial progression within 20 months after treatment initiation. Pretreatment contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging, T2-weighted imaging, and diffusion-weighted imaging were analyzed. The index brain metastasis and a 6-mm peritumoral region were segmented, followed by voxel-wise habitat clustering. Habitat-specific radiomic features were extracted and selected to construct ITH, PTH, and combined intratumoral-peritumoral habitat (PITH) signatures. Clinical predictors were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Support vector machine models were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic, decision curve, calibration, and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Results A total of 141 patients were analyzed, including 75 with progressive disease (PD) and 66 without PD (non-PD). Multivariable logistic regression identified EGFR mutation subtype (odds ratio [OR] = 2.390, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.187-4.811, P = 0.015) and the maximum diameter of the index brain metastasis as independent predictors (OR = 2.048, 95% CI: 1.204-3.483, P = 0.008). Models based on imaging heterogeneity features outperformed the clinical model overall. The clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.662, while the ITH, PTH, and PITH models achieved AUCs of 0.715, 0.724, and 0.758, respectively. The combined model showed favorable performance (AUC 0.795, accuracy 76.5%, sensitivity 70.4%, and specificity 83.3%). Patients classified by the combined model as high risk had significantly shorter intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS), than those classified as low risk (log-rank P = 0.019). Conclusion The proposed framework integrating ITH, PTH, and clinical features may provide a noninvasive approach for predicting intracranial progression risk and stratifying prognosis in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma with newly diagnosed BMs receiving first-line 3rd-gen EGFR-TKI monotherapy.

papers.title: Slow-wave sleep selectively amplifies network signatures of the presumed epileptogenic zone in focal epilepsy.
papers.authors: Nadig V, Heide EC, Yoshida-Stiksrud E, Segovia-Oropeza M, Riedel C, Flüh C, Malinova V, von der Brelie C, Schwiedrzik CM, Focke NKN.
papers.abstract: Study objectives Slow-wave sleep increases interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and seizures in focal epilepsy, but how sleep stages reshape epileptogenic tissue remains unclear. We assessed whether sleep stages selectively modulate network properties of the presumed epileptogenic zone (pEZ) relative to irritative (IZ) and non-involved (NIZ) zones. Methods We studied 22 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing pre-surgical intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG). IED-free resting-state epochs spanned four vigilance stages: wakefulness, non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep stages 2 and 3, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Spectral power, functional connectivity, graph-theoretic indices, and the 1/f exponent were quantified across seven frequency bands. Sleep stage and zone interactions were tested using permutation testing. pEZ electrodes were classified using elastic net logistic regression with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Results NREM3 selectively amplified within-pEZ gamma-band synchrony beyond surrounding zones (pEZ-NIZ: d=1.204, P=0.027). pEZ local efficiency and betweenness centrality rose in beta1 and gamma bands versus wakefulness. The aperiodic exponent steepened within the IZ versus NIZ during NREM3 and NREM2 (d =1.452 and 0.87, P < 0.001 and P=0.015). A three-feature classifier (NREM3 aperiodic exponent, beta2 connectivity, gamma local efficiency) localised the pEZ without ictal recordings (median AUC 0.859 pEZ vs. non-pEZ). Conclusions Slow-wave sleep selectively unmasks pEZ network properties via amplified power, synchrony and hub topology. NREM3-derived multimodal features may complement conventional pre-surgical biomarkers. Prospective validation in larger cohorts is needed to determine whether these markers improve surgical planning and outcome prediction.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注不同睡眠阶段是否会选择性地改变局灶性癫痫致痫组织的网络特征，利用耐药性局灶性癫痫患者的颅内脑电静息态数据，比较清醒、NREM2、NREM3和REM睡眠下致痫区与刺激区、非累及区的网络指标。结果显示，NREM3睡眠选择性地增强了致痫区内部的伽马频段同步，并提高了该区在贝塔1和伽马频段的局部效率与介数中心性；同时，刺激区的非周期指数在NREM2和NREM3下变陡。作者据此构建的三特征分类器可在无发作期记录的情况下定位致痫区，提示慢波睡眠能揭示致痫区的网络属性，相关特征或可补充传统术前生物标志物，但其对手术规划和预后判断的价值仍需更大样本的前瞻性验证。

papers.title: Sublexical compensatory reorganization of Chinese character recognition in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Liu B.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology
papers.abstract: Objective This study investigated the cognitive-functional shift in visual character recognition across the cognitive decline trajectory, ranging from healthy aging through Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) to Mild Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Specifically, it was hypothesized that as global semantic networks degrade, the reliance on rapid holistic processing decreases, prompting a compensatory shift toward sublexical features. Method Using a controlled unmasked priming lexical decision paradigm, this study evaluated behavioral performance across three distinct participant groups (N = 30 per group): healthy controls (HC), individuals with MCI, and patients with Mild AD. The experimental stimuli consisted of 80 Chinese phonograms matched across key psycholinguistic properties. This study utilized mixed-design Analyses of Variance (ANOVAs) alongside item-level hierarchical multiple regression (HMR) models to isolate the specific drivers of reaction times, assessing the predictive power of visual complexity, whole-character frequency, semantic transparency, and phonetic regularity. Results The analytical models revealed distinctly divergent psycholinguistic trajectories. The HC group demonstrated highly efficient holistic processing, with performance primarily driven by whole-character frequency. Conversely, the MCI group exhibited a unique transitional cognitive profile, characterized by a simultaneous reliance on both holistic whole-word access and analytic sublexical features. Crucially, in the Mild AD tgroup, the holistic processing advantage was entirely abolished. This functional disintegration triggered a compensatory reorganization toward bottom-up sublexical properties, with patients relying heavily on semantic transparency and phonetic regularity to achieve semantic access. Conclusions These findings demonstrate a linguistic Compensation-Related Utilization of Neural Circuits Hypothesis (CRUNCH) effect within the degenerating brain. As top-down lexical-semantic hubs deteriorate, reflected behaviorally in this paradigm by the loss of holistic processing advantages, the cognitive system actively compensates by upregulating bottom-up, sublexical pathways. Furthermore, the transitional sublexical dependency observed during the MCI stage highlights the translational potential of psycholinguistic variables as sensitive, noninvasive behavioral biomarkers for the early screening and monitoring of dementia.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察了从健康老化、轻度认知障碍（MCI）到轻度阿尔茨海默病（AD）过程中汉字识别所依赖的认知加工方式如何变化，采用无掩蔽启动词汇判断任务，比较三组被试在匹配 Psycholinguistic 属性汉字上的行为表现。结果显示，健康对照组主要依靠整字频率进行高效的整体加工；MCI 组同时依赖整体词通达和分析性亚词汇特征，呈现过渡性特征；轻度 AD 组的整体加工优势完全消失，转而更多依赖语义透明度和语音规则性等自下而上的亚词汇属性。作者据此提出，随着自上而下的词汇—语义枢纽退化，认知系统通过上调亚词汇通路进行补偿，并认为亚词汇依赖可能作为早期筛查和监测痴呆的敏感行为标记。

papers.title: Identification of two pathogenic guanidinoacetate methyltransferase variants in patients with intellectual disability: clinical and molecular insights.
papers.authors: Hashemi SR, Nejatizadeh A, Sheikhha MH, Moayedi AR, Daneshipour A, Firoozabadi SR, Mohammadi SA, Kalantar SM.
papers.abstract: Background Intellectual disability (ID) is a genetically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder with diverse underlying causes. Guanidinoacetate methyltransferase (GAMT) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disorder of creatine biosynthesis characterized by cerebral creatine depletion and accumulation of guanidinoacetate (GAA), resulting in a spectrum of neurodevelopmental manifestations, including intellectual disability. This study aimed to investigate the molecular basis of ID in individuals with suspected genetic etiologies and to characterize pathogenic GAMT variants. Methods Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed in 50 unrelated Iranian individuals with idiopathic ID. Variants were prioritized based on population allele frequency, predicted functional impact, and genotype-phenotype correlation. Candidate variants were confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and segregation analysis was performed to establish their inheritance patterns. Biochemical and cerebral magnetic resonance spectroscopy findings were also evaluated in individuals with pathogenic GAMT variants. Results Pathogenic biallelic GAMT variants were identified in two unrelated families. Patient 1 harbored the homozygous nonsense variant NM_000156.6:c.134G > A (p.Trp45Ter), whereas Patient 2 carried a novel homozygous four-base-pair deletion, NM_000156.6:c.373_376del (p.Pro125ThrfsTer35), predicted to result in premature protein truncation. Both variants were absent from the population databases examined and were classified as pathogenic according to ACMG/AMP criteria. Sanger sequencing confirmed homozygosity in the affected individuals and heterozygosity in their parents, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Both patients exhibited global developmental delay, intellectual disability, severe speech impairment, behavioral/autistic features, and a history of seizures. Elevated plasma GAA concentrations and reduced cerebral creatine levels further supported the diagnosis of GAMT deficiency. Conclusions This study expands the molecular spectrum of GAMT -related disease by identifying a novel pathogenic frameshift variant and provides additional clinical and biochemical characterization of GAMT deficiency in Iranian individuals with ID. The findings highlight the importance of considering GAMT deficiency among the potentially treatable causes of unexplained intellectual disability, particularly when neurodevelopmental manifestations are accompanied by biochemical evidence of disturbed creatine metabolism. Early molecular and biochemical recognition may facilitate appropriate clinical management and genetic counseling.

papers.title: Baseline MRI markers and clinical outcomes during anti-amyloid β therapy: A real-world study in a Japanese dementia center.
papers.authors: Kujuro Y, Saito M, Maruko M, Kamiyama K, Nakano A, Qian E, Okamura T, Ito D, Kageyama T, Sugiyama I, Ishihara E, Kuwahara T, Moritani K, Katai H, Hattori H.
papers.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
papers.abstract: Importance Predictors of decline and of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) during anti-amyloid β therapy in routine care are undefined. Objective To identify baseline predictors of cognitive, functional, and safety outcomes. Design, setting, and participants Retrospective cohort of 161 consecutive patients initiating anti-amyloid β therapy at a Tokyo dementia center, 2024 to 2026 (lecanemab, 89; donanemab, 72). Exposures Lecanemab or donanemab. Main outcomes and measures Change in MMSE and CDR-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB); baseline medial temporal atrophy (VSRAD Z score), amyloid PET burden, and microbleeds; ARIA. Results With lecanemab, MMSE and CDR-SB declined significantly at every assessment (CDR-SB +0.79, +1.10, +1.60 at 6, 12, 18 months); memory and orientation declined while language was preserved. Greater baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with greater 12-month CDR-SB worsening (r = 0.39; P = .01; n = 40); patients in the most severe standard category (Z ≥ 3) worsened by 2.62 versus 0.64 points (adjusted β = +2.18; P < .001). Atrophy was associated with older age (r = 0.19; P = .03) and with baseline memory-related measures - ADAS-Cog score (r = 0.32; P < .001) and the MMSE subdomains of delayed recall (β = -0.25; P = .006) and time orientation (β = -0.30; P = .04) - but not MMSE total score. Amyloid PET burden showed no significant association at most time points. All ARIA events were asymptomatic; ARIA-H occurred in 6 of 25 with microbleeds versus 3 of 136 without (odds ratio, 14.0; P < .001). Donanemab follow-up was 6 months. Conclusions and relevance Baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with functional decline and microbleeds with ARIA-H. Pretreatment MRI may provide prognostic and safety information during anti-amyloid β therapy.

papers.title: Investigating fatigability and cortical activation during prolonged foot tapping in multiple sclerosis.
papers.authors: Abasiyanik Z, Moumdjian L, Skorupa N, Kos D, Van Wijmeersch B, D'Haeseleer M, Zijdewind I, Feys P, Santinelli FB.
papers.abstract: People with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) often exhibit motor fatigability and reduced foot-tapping ability. However, the coupling between performance and cortical activity during fast, repetitive and prolonged ankle movements remains unexplored. We aimed to investigate the neural correlates of a prolonged foot-tap task (FTT) in pwMS and healthy controls (HC). Thirty-nine pwMS (EDSS 4[3.5], 55[14] years) and 18 HC (54.5[9.75) years) performed one 1-minute FTT for each foot. Wearable sensors and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) quantified motor performance and cortical activity, respectively. fNIRS covered bilaterally frontopolar, dorsolateral prefrontal (DLPFC), primary motor (M1) and supplementary motor area (SMA) cortices. Data were segmented into 10-second intervals and analysed via two-way ANOVA (group × time). Spearman's correlations evaluated associations between changes in cortical activity and performance (6th vs 1st segment). PwMS showed worse FTT performance with lower DLPFC activation compared to HC. On the other hand, comparable FTT performance decline over time were observed in both pwMS and HC. Cortical activity increased in SMA in HC (6 vs 2-3 intervals), but not in pwMS. In HC's, increased cortical activity across all cortical regions in the 6th interval was positive and moderately associated with less worsening in tapping performance. On the other hand, increased M1 activity was weakly associated with less foot tapping in pwMS. PwMS exhibited reduced foot-tap performance, accompanied by reduced DLPFC activation. While increased cortical activity leads to better performance in HC (i.e., a neural compensatory strategy), in pwMS increased activity was associated with worse performance (i.e., neural inefficiency).
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察多发性硬化患者在进行持续快速足部敲击任务时，运动表现下降与皮层活动之间的关系，并与健康对照比较；受试者完成一分钟足部敲击，同时用可穿戴传感器记录表现、用功能性近红外光谱测量皮层活动。结果显示，患者的敲击表现整体差于健康对照，且背外侧前额叶激活更低；两组在任务过程中表现随时间下降的程度相近，但健康对照的辅助运动区活动随任务推进而增加，患者则没有这种增加。相关分析提示，健康对照中多个皮层区域活动增加与表现下降较少相关，可能反映神经补偿；而在患者中，皮层活动增加反而与更差的表现相关，作者据此将其解释为神经低效。

papers.title: Precise modeling of task-related sensorimotor activation based on simultaneous surface electromyography.
papers.authors: Jasenská M, Hok P, Kojan M, Burkot O, Kolářová B, Holobar A, Hluštík P.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the relationship between motor control of ankle movements and actual motor performance using simultaneous functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and surface electromyography (EMG) in healthy individuals. Twenty participants performed dorsi-/plantarflexion of the ankle (Ankle) and gait imagery in a block design during fMRI. First-level models consisting of task regressors included either orthogonalized accelerometry (Acc) from the foot, EMG from the tibialis anterior, EMG with Acc, EMG split across conditions, or none. Each model was additionally evaluated either by default with or without a temporal derivative (TD) of the ankle movement task regressor. Voxel-wise and post-hoc region-of-interest (ROI) analyses revealed that both Acc and EMG explained fMRI signal in the primary sensorimotor cortices, while EMG was additionally associated with activation in the cerebellar vermis and the secondary somatosensory cortex. The two latter findings were, however, neither reproduced when separating the signal fluctuations during rest and gait imagery nor reflected in pairwise comparisons. Leaving out the TD reduced each model's performance by increasing unexplained variance, but resulted in more signal being explained by the EMG or Acc in the cerebellum, reflecting that it preferentially exhibited brief signal changes during transitions between conditions. Taken together, both EMG and Acc enabled capturing specific brain activity related to the movement variability; however, including the TD may significantly affect the ability to detect EMG- or Acc-related signal in regions with transient fMRI responses sensitive to changes in movement context, such as the cerebellum.

papers.title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
papers.authors: Holstein T, Sarrazin JC, Berberian B, Desantis A.
papers.abstract: Voluntary action shapes our perception through sensory predictions of its consequences. These predictions are thought to inhibit perceptual processing of predicted outcomes, leading to sensory attenuation. However, some studies have reported findings that contrast with this effect, suggesting that the influence of predictions may reflect, or interact with, attentional processes. Here, we investigated the interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention on early and late perceptual processing, with prediction and attention referring to the likelihood of a sensory event and its behavioral relevance, respectively. Electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded while participants viewed two sequential gratings. The orientation of the first was either predicted and self-generated or unpredicted and externally generated. Participants judged the tilt direction of the second grating relative to the first but responded only when the grating appeared in a task-relevant color. EEG analyses revealed no modulation of early visual potentials (N1a), but modulations at later processing stages. Specifically, the P3b exhibited reduced amplitude for predicted compared to unpredicted stimuli, but only when they were task-relevant, whereas task-relevance enhanced the P3b only for unpredicted stimuli. Interestingly, multivariate pattern analysis showed significant temporal clusters for decoding the grating's orientation exclusively for predicted and task-relevant stimuli, although decoding performance did not significantly differ between conditions. Furthermore, predicted and task-relevant stimuli elicited faster behavioral responses, with prediction-related P3b latency differences correlating with reaction-time differences. Overall, converging findings from the P3b, multivariate, time-frequency and behavioral analyses provide suggestive evidence that top-down attention and action-based prediction may jointly facilitate late perceptual and decision-related processing.

papers.title: Resting EEG as a condition-dependent ageing phenotype.
papers.authors: Du Y.
papers.abstract: Resting-state electroencephalography is increasingly proposed as a scalable marker of healthy brain ageing, yet its interpretability depends on distinguishing stable individual characteristics from condition-dependent measurement effects. This secondary analysis of an open lifespan dataset examined periodic alpha activity, alpha-peak detectability, aperiodic spectral structure, short-term repeatability, and longitudinal change under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions before and after an extended cognitive battery. Eye state strongly organised both whether a posterior alpha peak could be detected and the values of periodic and aperiodic measures. Age-related trajectories were prominent for the aperiodic exponent and full-sample alpha activity, whereas evidence that age modified post-battery change was weak. Across follow-up, detectable alpha frequency and the aperiodic exponent showed mean decreases, while alpha power was comparatively stable. Level measures demonstrated moderate-to-high repeatability and rank-order stability, but post-battery and difference-in-differences change scores were considerably less reliable. The findings position resting EEG as a condition-dependent ageing phenotype rather than a unitary baseline. They further show that peak detection, recording context, attrition, and the reliability of change must be modelled explicitly when resting EEG is used for lifespan inference or normative applications.

papers.title: Stage- and context-dependent modulation of fear memory by oxytocin: Neurobiological mechanisms and implications for PTSD.
papers.authors: Wei B, Li X, Che X.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a multifactorial psychiatric condition characterized by re-experiencing, avoidance, hyperarousal, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and disturbances in social and emotional functioning. Within this broader clinical syndrome, persistent traumatic memories and excessive fear generalization represent important mechanistic and therapeutic domains. Despite substantial advances in understanding its neurobiological basis, current treatments remain suboptimal, with limited efficacy and high dropout rates. The neuropeptide oxytocin (OXT), a key modulator of social behavior, stress regulation, and memory, has been investigated as a potential therapeutic target. Accumulating evidence indicates that severe trauma profoundly disrupts endogenous OXTergic signaling, whereas pharmacological studies suggest that exogenous OXT can modulate fear-memory processing through region-, dose-, route-, and context-dependent mechanisms. Evidence from fear-conditioning indicates that across acquisition, consolidation, retrieval, reconsolidation, and extinction, the direction of OXT's effects is heterogeneous rather than uniformly anxiolytic and pro-extinction. OXT may influence threat discrimination, fear expression, memory updating, and extinction by modulating specific neural circuits and neurochemical pathways. However, most preclinical models capture selected dimensions of PTSD rather than the full clinical disorder. Human studies further indicate that intranasal OXT can modulate neural, physiological, and social-cognitive processes relevant to PTSD, although evidence for consistent clinical efficacy remains limited and heterogeneous. This review synthesizes current findings on OXT and its synthetic analogs within a stage- and context-dependent framework to better investigate their heterogeneous effects and assess their potential relevance and translational limitations in PTSD.

papers.title: Cerebellar nuclei remain vulnerable to cuprizone-induced demyelination in adult and aged mice: A longitudinal multimodal MRI-histology study.
papers.authors: Shimshek DR, Zurbruegg S, Neuhaus A, Doelemeyer A, Beckmann N.
papers.abstract: Age is a major determinant of demyelination and remyelination capacity. Here, we investigated age-dependent brain responses to acute cuprizone exposure in female C57BL/6 mice using longitudinal multimodal Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and histological analyses. Our aim was to determine whether any brain region in very old animals remains susceptible to cuprizone-induced pathology. Adult (6-month-old) and aged (18-month-old) mice received 0.2% cuprizone in the diet for 5 weeks, followed by 4 weeks of recovery on normal chow, with in vivo MRI performed at baseline, during intoxication, and throughout recovery. Magnetization transfer ratio (MTR) and T2 -weighted signal were used as MRI surrogates of myelin integrity and neuroinflammation, respectively, whereas T1 -weighted signal was assessed as a potential marker sensitive to oxidative stress. In adult mice, cuprizone induced robust and region-specific pathology, including reduced MTR and increased T2 -weighted signal in the corpus callosum, accompanied by microgliosis, astrocytosis, and increased APP-positive dystrophic neurites. These abnormalities showed only partial recovery following cuprizone withdrawal. In contrast, cuprizone elicited little or no detectable change in these forebrain white-matter regions and in other brain areas in aged mice. However, the cerebellar nuclei remained susceptible at both ages, exhibiting persistent MTR decreases and T2 -weighted signal increases, corroborated by histological evidence of demyelination and gliosis. T1 -weighted signal increased broadly in adult, but not in aged, mice during intoxication, consistent with cuprizone-associated oxidative stress. Together, these findings demonstrate pronounced age- and region-dependent effects of cuprizone and identify the cerebellar nuclei as a sensitive target of demyelination across the lifespan. Moreover, the non-invasive nature of MRI enables efficient assessment of regional differences over time.

papers.title: A multimodal MRI-based study of early-stage Parkinson's disease across age-at-onset groups.
papers.authors: Liu G, Tian Y, Nan D, Shi Y, Sun P, Zhang H, Cui Y, Liu P.
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to investigate distinct iron deposition and neurite microstructural alterations in deep gray matter nuclei between early-onset Parkinson's disease (EOPD) and late-onset Parkinson's disease (LOPD) patients using quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI), and to evaluate the ability of these quantitative metrics to distinguish EOPD and LOPD from their corresponding healthy controls. Methods Fifty-three early-stage PD patients (15 EOPD and 38 LOPD) and 58 healthy controls (17 young healthy controls and 41 older healthy controls) underwent multimodal MRI. QSM-derived magnetic susceptibility and NODDI-derived parameters (NDI, Viso, ODI) were analyzed in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc), substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr), red nucleus (RN), globus pallidus (GP), putamen (PT), and caudate nucleus (CN). Results In EOPD, the iron content in deep gray matter nuclei was not significantly different from that in young healthy controls, but ODI was reduced in the left SNc. In LOPD, increased QSM values were observed in bilateral SNc, PT, and left CN, alongside decreased NDI and increased Viso in the left SNc, and reduced ODI in bilateral SNc and PT. Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that the combination of the NDI and ODI in the left SNc could effectively differentiate patients with EOPD from young healthy controls, whereas the optimal combination for distinguishing patients with LOPD from older healthy controls consisted of the NDI, ODI, and QSM in the left SNc. Conclusion Multimodal MRI revealed distinct spatial involvement patterns in early-stage EOPD and LOPD and showed potential for distinguishing PD patients from their corresponding healthy controls.
keywords: Neurite Orientation Dispersion And Density Imaging

papers.title: Multicenter external validation of a multimodal MRI deep-learning model to predict meningioma bone invasion.
papers.authors: Wei Z, Hu W, Tang F, Ren J, Zhou J, Liu M, Su L, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Background Preoperative detection of meningioma bone invasion lacks objective biomarkers and relies on subjective radiological assessment, posing a risk of excessive bone resection or residual tumor. We therefore developed and externally validated a parsimonious six-feature DenseNet121 signature derived from multiparametric MRI across two independent institutions. Methods In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 438 consecutive patients (mean age, 53 ± 11 years; 77% women) with histologically confirmed meningioma were allocated to training (n = 182), internal validation (n = 77), and external test (n = 179) sets. Following N4 bias-field correction and isotropic resampling, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted volumes were fed into a DenseNet121 architecture to extract a six-feature signature via nested cross-validation. Discrimination (area under the ROC curve, AUC), calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision-curve analysis) were evaluated. Results In the external cohort (prevalence 11%), the signature achieved an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.73-0.91), sensitivity 75%, specificity 77% and negative predictive value 96%, with an AUC improvement of 0.155 over conventional radiomics (95% CI, 0.01-0.30; p = 0.035). At a 20% risk threshold, decision-curve analysis confirmed a positive net clinical benefit, primarily driven by the high negative predictive value. SHAP analysis demonstrated the dominant and consistent contribution of low-ADC features. Conclusion The DenseNet121-derived six-feature signature serves as a reliable rule-out aid for preoperative meningioma bone invasion, with a high negative predictive value that may safely support decisions to avoid extensive bone resection in predicted-negative cases. Positive predictions require confirmatory CT or intraoperative biopsy to mitigate false positives. This tool could assist nurses and surgeons in preoperative planning, facilitating personalized patient care and potentially reducing operative time and complications.

papers.title: Altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics are associated with auditory hallucinations in patients with major depressive disorder.
papers.authors: He Y, Wu F, Liao F, Zhang Z, Wu J, Zhang X, Li H, Wu K, Zhao Y, Wang L, Huang Y.
papers.abstract: Background Auditory hallucination experiences are an understudied but clinically significant feature of major depressive disorder (MDD). Although EEG microstate abnormalities have been reported in MDD, their relationship with auditory hallucination experiences remains unclear. This study investigated resting-state EEG microstate dynamics associated with auditory hallucination experiences in first-episode MDD. Methods A total of 182 first-episode patients with MDD and 95 healthy controls underwent resting-state EEG recordings. Patients were classified according to lifetime history of auditory hallucination experiences into those with (AH+, n = 42) and without (AH-, n = 140) such experiences. Patients were either psychotropic medication-naïve or minimally medicated (<2 weeks of cumulative exposure). Microstate parameters were compared among groups. ANCOVA and hierarchical binary logistic regression were performed to examine associations with auditory hallucination experiences. Results Only microstate C occurrence was significantly higher in the AH+ group than in both the AH- and healthy control groups after multiple-comparison correction. This difference remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, education, and depression severity. Hierarchical logistic regression showed that higher microstate C occurrence was independently associated with auditory hallucination experiences (OR = 1.773, 95% CI: 1.211-2.595, p = 0.003), but not with hallucination severity. Its discriminatory ability was modest (AUC = 0.614, 95% CI: 0.516-0.711). Conclusions In first-episode MDD, a lifetime history of auditory hallucination experiences was associated with increased microstate C occurrence. This finding suggests that altered microstate C dynamics may represent an electrophysiological correlate of auditory hallucination experiences, warranting further investigation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注首发重性抑郁障碍患者中幻听体验与静息态脑电微状态动态的关系，比较了伴与不伴幻听史的患者及健康对照的微状态参数。结果显示，伴幻听史患者的微状态C出现频率高于不伴幻听史患者和健康对照，且在控制年龄、性别、教育程度和抑郁严重度后仍成立；分层回归中该指标与幻听体验独立相关，但与幻听严重度无关，区分能力有限。作者据此提出，微状态C动态改变可能是幻听体验的电生理相关特征，而非严重度指标，仍需进一步研究。

papers.title: Central neuroendocrine governance as a unifying framework for host-tumor interaction: From afferent sensing to therapeutic modulation.
papers.authors: Wang YF, Zhang ML, Jin WL.
papers.abstract: Cancer is not biologically confined to the tumor bed. Cachexia, fatigue, metabolic dysfunction, circadian disruption, and immune dysfunction reflect disturbances that local models alone cannot fully explain. The brain is well positioned to participate in these processes because it continuously samples circulating signals and coordinates endocrine and autonomic responses. Yet the afferent side of this communication has received less attention than its downstream consequences. Here, we synthesize evidence showing that cytokines, hormones, metabolites, and cargo carried by extracellular vesicles can engage central sensory interfaces and integrative regions, particularly circumventricular organs and hypothalamic and brainstem circuits. We use the term Endocriception to describe afferent humoral sensing and early central decoding of circulating biochemical signals, and focus here on how tumor- and host-associated changes engage this process in cancer. Central neuroendocrine governance refers to the subsequent integration of this information and the generation of autonomic and endocrine outputs. Persistent inflammation, stress, circadian disruption, and impaired feedback may gradually reconfigure this regulatory system. The resulting changes can affect systemic immunity, metabolism, behavior, and host tolerance of cancer. Evidence is strongest for a limited number of pathways, whereas many proposed links remain incomplete or dependent on tumor type and experimental context. We therefore present central neuroendocrine governance as a working framework for organizing current evidence and guiding mechanistic studies, biomarker development, and interventions aimed at restoring host physiology.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic efficacy, durability, and optimal parameters of rTMS for cognitive rehabilitation: A comprehensive meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Ali AMS, Gorter M, Zakaria R, Jenkinson MD, Frank B, Klein M, de Witt Hamer PC, Douw L.
papers.abstract: Aim Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) is a promising non-invasive neuromodulation technique for cognitive rehabilitation. We evaluated the cognitive effects of rTMS on neurological and psychiatric diseases to determine moderators of efficacy. Methods A meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) comparing real versus sham rTMS to July 2025 was performed. Objective cognition reported as primary or secondary outcomes were extracted and Hedges' g effect sizes computed. Univariate and multivariate three-level meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled effect sizes and assess moderator influence. Results 748 measures from 137 studies (5972 participants) were extracted. Real rTMS produced a significant cognitive enhancement (g = 0.28, p < 0.0001, I2 = 37.3%). This was durable over 2-52 weeks follow-up. There was efficacy across all cognitive domains (g > 0.20, I2 = 35.8). Neurodegenerative (g = 0.35) and focal (g = 0.44) conditions demonstrated stronger effects than psychiatric conditions (g = 0.20). Although stimulation target was not a significant moderator overall, the Inferior Frontal Gyrus showed the largest effect (g = 0.45), with significant effects also at the left and right DLPFC and left parietal cortex (g = 0.29-0.45), all nodes of the Frontoparietal Network. 1-Hz stimulation produced a significantly larger effect (g = 0.39) than the 10-Hz reference (g = 0.19); 5-Hz, 20-Hz and iTBS were also significantly positive (g = 0.30-0.49). In multivariate models, adding 10 rTMS sessions improved cognitive outcomes (Δg = +0.077), whereas increasing the number of pulses per session trended toward reduced efficacy. All effects were confirmed in a left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex subgroup analysis. Subjective cognition was measured in only 6% of studies. A multivariate prediction tool is introduced: https://amsali.shinyapps.io/tms_cognition_prediction/ CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis demonstrates the sustained efficacy of rTMS in enhancing cognitive function, with small-to-moderate effect sizes across diverse clinical populations and stimulation protocols. However, a significant gap remains regarding whether these objective neurocognitive gains translate into meaningful improvements in subjective cognition or functional outcomes.

papers.title: Vagal mechanoreceptors controlling gastrointestinal function.
papers.authors: Lowenstein ED, Birchmeier C.
papers.abstract: The vagus nerve innervates internal organs, in particular the gastrointestinal tract, and is a major communication route between the gut and brain. Most vagal fibers are viscerosensory, but vagal motor axons also travel with the nerve. Vagal sensory neurons can detect mechanosensory information arising from the gastrointestinal tract such as stretch or pressure, and transmit this information to the nucleus of the solitary tract in the brain. Recent technological advances have opened new routes for studying vagal mechanosensation. Single-cell transcriptomic atlases have revealed substantial heterogeneity among vagal sensory neurons and now guide targeted analysis of individual subtypes. Viral and genetic approaches based on molecular profiling enable anatomical tracing, electrophysiological recordings, and selective ablation, silencing, or activation of defined neuronal populations. Recent work has revealed subtypes of vagal mechanoreceptors defined by expression of Prox2, Runx3, Glp1r, and Oxtr, which form intraganglionic laminar endings in the muscle layer of the gut. These mechanoreceptors detect distension in the gastrointestinal tract, such as a bolus moving through the esophagus or the filling of the stomach, and initiate coordinated peristalsis. Together, these mechanosensory pathways enable precise monitoring of gastrointestinal mechanics to support digestive function.
keywords: Nodose Neurons Controlling Gut Stretch Or Distension

papers.title: MRI-based correlation of cry acoustic parameters and brain structural development in preterm infants.
papers.authors: Zhu X, Cao Q, Xu F, Duan Y, Huang M, Hua Z.
papers.abstract: Objective Infant crying conveys abundant information, including neurophysiological, pathological, and psychological aspects. However, the relationship between crying and brain structure remains poorly understood. Methods In this study, 154 preterm infants and 84 term infants were enrolled, and their cries were recorded for 1 min under similar stimulation conditions. MATLAB software was used to analyse the crying data, for statistical analyses, repeated cry-level observations were averaged within infant, and each infant contributed one value for each cry acoustic parameter. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in 43 preterm infants to measure the volumes of grey matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Results Preterm infants had longer cry cycle and inhale durations than term infants (P = 0.022 and 0.014). Among preterm infants, cry parameters did not differ significantly across gestational ages (all P > 0.05). In 43 preterm infants with MRI, grey and white matter volumes differed significantly across gestational age groups (P = 0.01 and 0.02), as did the grey matter/CSF and white matter/CSF ratios (P = 0.010 and 0.020). Correlations between cry parameters and brain volumes were generally weak. Multiple linear regression showed that cry parameters were associated with white matter volume (R2 = 0.38, P = 0.039) but not with grey matter or CSF volume. Conclusion This study identified associations between cry characteristics and MRI-derived brain volumes in infants across gestational ages. Although these findings suggest that cry characteristics may reflect certain aspects of brain development, the observed associations were generally weak and should be considered exploratory.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察早产儿哭声声学特征与脑结构发育之间的关系，比较了早产儿与足月儿的哭声参数，并对部分早产儿进行磁共振成像以测量灰质、白质和脑脊液体积。结果显示，早产儿哭声周期和吸气时长较足月儿更长，但在早产儿内部，哭声参数并未随胎龄呈现显著差异；脑体积指标则随胎龄分组存在差异。哭声参数与脑体积的相关总体较弱，回归分析仅提示哭声参数与白质体积存在关联，与灰质和脑脊液体积无关。作者据此认为，哭声特征可能反映脑发育的某些方面，但关联较弱，相关发现应视为探索性结果。

papers.title: MRI and proton MR spectroscopy in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a comprehensive imaging review.
papers.authors: Enokizono M.
papers.abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) remains a leading cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability. Although cranial ultrasound is widely used as a bedside screening tool, brain MRI has become central to diagnosis, injury pattern classification, timing estimation, and outcome prediction. Furthermore, proton MR spectroscopy (1 H-MRS) provides complementary metabolic biomarkers that enhance prognostication. This review focuses on MRI and 1 H-MRS in neonatal encephalopathy due to hypoxic-ischemic injury, addressing both term and preterm infants. The pathophysiologic determinants of injury distribution are summarized, the optimal timing of imaging and diffusion evolution is discussed, and practical acquisition protocols including recommended sequences and 1 H-MRS parameters are proposed. Key MRI phenotypes in term infants-basal ganglia-thalamus injury, watershed/parasagittal cortical-subcortical injury, and global or near-total injury patterns are reviewed with attention to common pitfalls such as diffusion pseudonormalization and evolving T1/T2 signal changes.
