Conclusion Reported GM alterations in IGE converge most robustly onto a subcortical normative functional network involving the thalamus and putamen, with additional DMN involvement observed primarily in the HCP discovery analysis. These findings provide preliminary, descriptive evidence that reported GM alterations in IGE are associated with a reproducible subcortical normative connectivity pattern across two connectome datasets, although the available analyses do not establish above-chance or disease-specific network convergence.

papers.title: Deep learning-accelerated contrast-enhanced 3D MRI for acute optic neuritis: faster acquisition and improved lesion conspicuity.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Liu WV, Wen Z, Lu M, Liu C, Li L, Chen T, Yang R, Zha Y.
papers.abstract: Objective To compare a deep learning-accelerated contrast-enhanced 3D T1-weighted sequence (T1-CUBE-DLS) with standard parallel imaging-accelerated T1-CUBE for detecting acute optic neuritis (ON). Methods This prospective study enrolled 59 patients with suspected acute ON (38 females; mean age 41.2 ± 12.8 years). All underwent contrast-enhanced whole-brain 3.0 T MRI including both T1-CUBE-DLS and standard T1-CUBE sequences. Two blinded neuroradiologists independently scored motion artifacts, subjective noise, and optic nerve clarity. Consensus readings recorded enhancement laterality, involved segments, and visual conspicuity. Enhancement length was measured per optic nerve, with inter-observer reliability assessed via intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Clinical diagnosis by a senior neuro-ophthalmologist served as the reference standard. Results Acute ON was confirmed in 43 of 59 patients (72.9%). T1-CUBE-DLS reduced acquisition time by 36.2%. Subjective noise was equivalent between sequences (p > 0.05), but T1-CUBE-DLS showed significantly fewer motion artifacts and superior optic nerve clarity (both p < 0.05). No significant difference was detected in diagnostic performance between the two sequences: sensitivity (88.4% vs. 86.0%), specificity (93.8% vs. 93.8%), and accuracy (89.8% vs. 88.1%; all p > 0.05). T1-CUBE-DLS demonstrated stronger visual conspicuity (p = 0.011) and slightly longer measured enhancement length (mean difference, 0.836 mm; p < 0.0001). ICC for length measurement was 0.91 for T1-CUBE-DLS vs. 0.83 for standard T1-CUBE, with narrower 95% limits of agreement (-1.37 to 1.51 mm vs. - 3.1 to 2.4 mm). Conclusion T1-CUBE-DLS reduces acquisition time by 36.2%, with no significant difference in diagnostic accuracy detected, while improving enhancement conspicuity and measurement reproducibility, supporting its potential as a practical and efficient alternative for ON evaluation.

papers.title: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing confirmed pseudorabies virus encephalitis complicated with central visual impairment: a case report.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Zhang X, Wei X, Yu W, Ma N, Liu W, Zheng Y, Jia H.
papers.abstract: Pseudorabies virus (PRV) is an alphaherpesvirus for which domestic swine serve as the sole natural reservoir. Human PRV infection has historically been regarded as extremely rare. Since 2017, however, an increasing number of severe human PRV encephalitis cases have been identified in China, pre-dominantly among individuals with occupational exposure to pigs or pork products. The condition has been associated with substantial morbidity and mortality and remains under recognized in clinical practice. We report a 53-year-old male dockworker who presented with a 9-day history of fever followed by progressive severe headache. PRV infection was confirmed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed signal abnormalities involving the right insular cortex, temporal lobe, hippocampus, and amygdala, consistent with encephalitis. The patient received intravenous acyclovir (500 mg every 8 h for 23 days), corticosteroids, and intravenous immunoglobulin. Although his level of consciousness gradually improved, he developed permanent bilateral blindness with no light perception. At 1-year follow-up, he remained alive but with persistent blindness; neuroimaging demonstrated encephalomalacia in the right temporal and insular regions. PRV can cause devastating human encephalitis with visual impairment as a frequent and serious complication, reported in up to 60% of published cases. Our case is notable in that bilateral blindness emerged after recovery of consciousness, without evidence of peripheral ocular pathology, suggesting a pre-dominantly central visual pathway injury. CSF mNGS has become a key tool for timely diagnosis of rare viral encephalitides. Clinicians should consider PRV encephalitis in patients with unexplained encephalitis and a history of swine exposure, and pursue early mNGS testing to facilitate prompt aetiological diagnosis and antiviral therapy.

papers.title: Angiography-derived fractional flow and clinical outcomes in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
papers.authors: Zheng W, Zou R, Wang M, Tang J, Chen R, Zheng C, Gong J, Gao Y, Wang N, Lu Y, Wu J, Fiehler J, Siddiqui AH, Xiang J, Wan S.
papers.abstract: Background To explore the association between fractional flow (FF) and clinical outcomes in patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS), and to evaluate its potential role in patient stratification. Methods This retrospective exploratory study included symptomatic ICAS patients hospitalized between March 2019 and May 2024. FF values were derived from digital subtraction angiography using an angiography-based computational method. Patients were stratified according to a pre-specified FF threshold of 0.76 and treatment modality (interventional vs. conservative). Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) at discharge and 12 months. Results Among patients with FF ≤ 0.76, no worsening in mRS between discharge and 12 months was observed in 96.3% of the interventional group and 78.6% of the conservative group (p = 0.017). In a post hoc analysis, improvement of at least one mRS point occurred in 46.3 and 17.9%, respectively; however, discharge mRS scores differed between groups, and the difference in improvement was not statistically significant when the analysis was restricted to patients with discharge mRS ≥ 1. No significant differences in mRS or NIHSS improvement were observed between treatment strategies in patients with FF > 0.76 (p > 0.05). In contrast, stratification based on degree of stenosis (DS% ≥ 70%) did not differentiate clinical outcomes between treatment groups. These findings suggest that FF-based stratification may be associated with differences in functional outcomes across treatment strategies. Conclusion FF may provide additional information for risk stratification in symptomatic ICAS patients and may help identify clinically relevant subgroups for further evaluation. However, these findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Intraoperative asymmetry of thalamic stimulation mapping in Essential Tremor: specificity of first hemisphere implantation and transitory lesioning effect.
papers.authors: Bucciarelli V, Vogel D, Coste J, Chaix R, Hemm S, Lemaire JJ.
papers.abstract: Introduction Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) effectively reduces symptoms in Essential Tremor (ET). Clinical benefit depends on modulation of distributed neural circuits with still undeciphered mechanisms. Furthermore, the lesioning effect observable intraoperatively following the implantation of the DBS lead in the first brain hemisphere has received little attention. We hypothesize that hemispheric differences exist in the spatial organization of improvement and adverse effects, related to the sequential implantation of electrodes and a transitory lesioning effect. Methods We investigated this hemispheric asymmetry with a data-driven, probabilistic mapping approach, linking simulated stimulation volumes [Volumes of Tissue Activated (VTAs)] to symptom improvement (imp) and side effects (se) for each hemisphere. Intraoperative data from 23 ET patients undergoing DBS lead implantation in the ventrointermediate nucleus of thalamus (Vim) were retrospectively analyzed. The left hemisphere was systematically implanted first. Stimulation spots (positions) were categorized using therapeutic window values and side effect occurrence. Hemisphere-specific probabilistic effect volumes of imp (PVimp) and se (PVse) derived from VTAs, and clusters of stimulation spots grouped by category were computed. They were topographically analyzed in relation to structures of the Vim region, and compared within hemispheres and across hemispheres. Results In the first implanted hemisphere, PVimp was in the infero-posterior part of Vim reaching the subthalamic tegmental fields, whereas the PVse was above, posterior and lateral to the PVimp, spanning Vim and the ventrocaudal nucleus of thalamus (VC). In the right one, PVimp and PVse overlapped, intersecting Vim and VC, in the intermediate part of both. The stimulation spots clusters, in the left hemisphere, were located around the intermediate part, slightly lateral of Vim and VC to a lesser extent. In the right one, they were located in the intermediate and superior parts of Vim. Discussion Significant hemispheric asymmetries were observed, revealing a lesioning effect subsequent to the first DBS lead implantation in the left hemisphere. This led to a broader distribution of optimal positions with a larger PVimp largely overlapping with the PVse in the contralateral right hemisphere. The combined mapping and categorization framework yields hemisphere-specific insights on the transitory lesioning and bi-hemispheric modulation which could guide future DBS strategies.

papers.title: E-MDD: an evidence-guided explainable framework for EEG-based depression recognition.
papers.authors: Huang J, Zhang Z, Cao Y, Zhao Z, Niu L.
papers.abstract: Introduction An evidence-guided explainable framework, E-MDD, is developed to integrate high-dimensional EEG representations, neurophysiological biomarkers, and large language models for the recognition of EEG-based depression with concise and evidence-based textual explanations. Methods The proposed E-MDD framework consists of three stages: classification, evidence construction, and evidence-guided inference. In the classification stage, two parallel feature extraction branches are employed to extract Electroencephalography latent features and neurophysiological biomarkers, which are subsequently fused and fed into a lightweight multilayer perceptron for the recognition of depression. In the evidence construction stage, the latent feature dimensions of the EEG are aligned with neurophysiological biomarkers, and the model's decision basis is identified to construct structured evidence supporting the classification results. In the evidence-guided inference stage, structured evidence and the proposed evidence-guided prompt are used to guide the large language model in generating concise textual explanations. Results The experimental results on the Mumtaz dataset show that E-MDD achieves an AUC of 0.8472 and an F1-score of 0.8421. Meanwhile, the generated short-text explanations can effectively describe the basis of the model's decision-making for its predictions, demonstrating a high degree of faithfulness. The proposed framework also demonstrates consistent evidence-guided explanation performance across EEGNet and EEGConformer. Discussion Overall, this study proposes a neurophysiologically interpretable framework for EEG-based deep learning models, which effectively enhances the interpretability of deep learning models for depression detection and provides a new perspective for understanding their decision-making mechanisms.

papers.title: Concordance and Association of Kidokoro MRI Scores at 32 and 40 Weeks Postmenstrual Age with Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Very Preterm Infants.
papers.authors: Bonezzi L, Biagioni T, Fiori S, Luke C, George JM, Colditz PB, Fripp J, Ware RS, Pannek K, Boyd RN.
papers.abstract: Background and purpose Early identification of neurodevelopmental risk in very preterm infants is critical for timely intervention. The Kidokoro MRI scoring system offers a semiquantitative approach to evaluating brain abnormalities. This study aimed to assess the agreement of Kidokoro scores obtained in the same infants at 32 and 40 weeks postmenstrual age, and their association to cognitive, language, and motor outcomes at 24 months corrected age. Materials and methods A cohort of 187 very preterm infants (median 28+5 weeks gestational age; 55% boys) underwent structural MRI at 2 time points: early (median 32+2 weeks) and term-equivalent age (TEA; median 40+5 weeks), using 3T scanners. Scans were scored independently using a modified version of the Kidokoro system. Bland-Altman analysis assessed agreement between early and TEA scores. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed at 24 months using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Third Edition (Bayley-III). Multivariable linear regression models evaluated the predictive value of MRI scores, adjusting for sex, gestational age, birth weight centile, and socioeconomic status. Results Early MRI scores were consistently higher than TEA scores (mean difference: 1.9; 95% CI, 1.6-2.2), with WM scores showing the largest discrepancy (mean difference: 1.68; 95% CI, 1.46-1.90), primarily due to the myelination delay item. Excluding this item reduced the difference to 0.32 (95% CI, -0.01 to 0.64). Early and TEA Kidokoro Global Brain Abnormality Score (GBAS) were negatively associated with Bayley-III cognitive and motor, but not language scores. Higher GBAS were associated with lower cognitive (early: β = -0.67 [95% CI, -1.23 to -0.11], partial R 2 = 0.03; TEA: β = -0.60 [95% CI, -1.15 to -0.06], partial R 2 = 0.03) and motor scores (early: β = -1.04 [95% CI, -1.67 to -0.41], partial R 2 = 0.06; TEA: β = -1.18 [95% CI, -1.78 to -0.58], partial R 2 = 0.08). Reduction in GBAS from early to TEA correlated with higher motor scores (β = 1.02 [95% CI, 0.03-2.02], partial R 2 = 0.02). WM abnormalities were linked to poorer motor outcomes at both time points. Conclusions Kidokoro scores at early and term-equivalent time points are associated with neurodevelopmental outcomes at 24 months. Global abnormalities and WM scored at either time points, or their longitudinal changes are significantly linked to motor outcomes. Refinement of the scoring system for the early assessment may enhance clinical utility.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在极早产儿中比较了纠正胎龄32周与足月等效年龄两次结构MRI的Kidokoro评分一致性，并分析其与24月龄认知、语言和运动结局的关联。结果显示，早期评分整体高于足月等效年龄评分，差异主要来自髓鞘化延迟条目；两个时间点的整体脑异常评分均与认知和运动评分呈负相关，而与语言评分无关，白质异常与运动结局相关，评分随发育下降也与更好的运动表现相关。作者提示早期评分系统仍需完善，这些关联尚不能直接视为临床预测或干预依据。

papers.title: Novel Neuroimaging Biomarker of Cortical Gray/White Border Integrity in Blast-Related Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.authors: Andreu Arasa VC, Fortenbaugh FC, Knoff AA, Fortier CB, Milberg WP, Salat DH.
papers.abstract: Background and purpose Recent studies suggest that blast or mid-impact neurotrauma are characterized by scar-border forming astrogliosis at the gray-white matter junction. Individuals with mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) and blast trauma have increased neuroinflammation and impairment of axonal remyelination on postmortem histopathology. However, there are currently only limited methodologies to use in the assessment of the cortical gray/white interface using in vivo neuroimaging. The purpose was to investigate the gray-white matter contrast (GWC) at the gray-white matter junction that may be linked to neuroinflammation/astrogliosis in the setting of blast exposure and/or mTBI, through 3D T1-weighted MPRAGE images. Materials and methods Post-9/11 veterans (n =723) from the Translational Research Center for TBI and Stress Disorders completed MRI. Participants were grouped into 4 categories: participants with a history of blast-related mTBI (blast-mTBI), participants with a history of mTBI due to other mechanical forces (blunt-mTBI), participants with a history of close blast exposure but no mTBI, and those without a history of lifetime mTBI or close blast exposure. MRI data processing for morphometry and cortical surface mapping was done using FreeSurfer image analysis. Signal intensities in gray and white matter along the cortical and white matter interface were used to calculate mean GWC value. Results Veterans in the blast-mTBI group showed diffuse patterns of increased GWC relative to the other groups, particularly in the frontotemporal lobes. This effect was driven primarily by a greater number of high GWC regions in the blast-mTBI group compared with the no-neurotrauma and blunt-mTBI groups. Conclusions There was diffuse increased GWC on MR in the blast-mTBI group compared with the no-neurotrauma, close blast exposure, and blunt-mTBI groups. These findings may be linked to astrogliosis and neuroinflammation in patients with blast-mTBI. Histopathologic correlation with imaging findings will be necessary to better understand these effects.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注爆炸相关轻度创伤性脑损伤是否在皮层灰白质交界处留下可被在体神经影像捕捉的异常，利用三维T1加权MPRAGE图像计算灰白质对比度，比较了有爆炸相关mTBI、其他机械力所致mTBI、仅有近距离爆炸暴露以及无创伤暴露的退伍军人。结果显示，爆炸相关mTBI组的灰白质对比度呈弥漫性升高，以额颞叶较为明显，且主要由该组高对比度区域数量增多所驱动。作者认为这一影像特征可能与星形胶质细胞增生和神经炎症有关，但强调尚需组织病理学与影像的对照研究来验证，因此目前只能视为有待确认的候选生物标志物。

papers.title: The Effects of Cognitive Load on Intergroup Empathy Biases [Registered Report Stage 1, Version 2]
papers.authors: Franks JE, Gutsell JN.
papers.abstract: Accurate and quick judgments of others’ mental and emotional states are crucial for social interaction. However, these judgments can be compromised by social biases, especially while cognitive demands are high and cognitive resources are low. Empathy is not always allocated to everyone equally, especially when the target is considered an outgroup member. One factor that may exacerbate such empathy biases is cognitive load, as cognitive load has been shown to increase ingroup biases and impair empathizing. This study investigates whether high cognitive load and racial outgroup membership interact, potentially worsening behavioral and self-reported indicators of empathy bias. To our knowledge, the present work is the first to directly manipulate cognitive load during intergroup empathizing, examining its effects on two distinct, yet interacting, routes of empathy—experience sharing and mentalizing. Mentalizing (cognitive empathy) and affective experience sharing (emotional empathy) activate different brain networks but interact during social situations, necessitating separate examination within the same paradigm. Using an empathy task designed to test racial empathy biases, we integrate behavioral and self-report measures to capture empathy dynamics in response to naturalistic stimuli. This approach allows us to test how group biases and cognitive load independently and jointly affect mentalizing and experience sharing.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨高认知负荷与种族外群体成员身份是否交互影响共情偏差，并首次在组间共情过程中直接操纵认知负荷，分别考察心理化与情绪分享这两条相互作用的共情路径。研究采用共情任务，结合行为与自我报告指标，测量对自然情境刺激的共情反应。摘要仅说明研究设计与目的，未报告结果，因此无法概述具体发现及其含义。

papers.title: Baroreflex control of heart rate at rest and during exercise in microgravity conditions.
papers.authors: Perrone MA, Caminiti G, Aracri M, Volterrani M, Iellamo F.
papers.journal: The Journal of sports medicine and physical fitness
papers.abstract: One of the most important features of prolonged weightlessness is a progressive impairment of muscular function. Physiological modifications related to exposure to microgravity, e.g. altered blood volume distribution, impaired myocardial function, and a decrease in stroke volume, in addition to the alterations in muscular function, contribute to the reduced physical exercise capacity commonly reported after space flight. The interplay between muscular, hemodynamic and body fluid modifications occurring in microgravity could alter also the neural mechanisms of cardiovascular regulation both in resting conditions and during exercise in comparison to those that are normally operating on the ground. Indeed, an impairment in arterial baroreflex control of heart rate has been reported in the resting state during spaceflight. Moreover, cardiovascular and autonomic responses to exercise have been reported to be either impaired or preserved after simulated or actual microgravity conditions. Differences in results might depend on different experimental settings: the majority of studies on exercise in microgravity have been conducted using handgrips as a convenient model of muscular exercise. However, microgravity-induced muscular impairment involves mainly the antigravity muscles, i.e. leg muscles, which are those primarily involved in the reduced exercise capacity and hence are more representative of the marked changes in the musculoskeletal system induced by microgravity. This brief review aims to summarize current knowledge on baroreflex control of heart rate in resting and exercise conditions in microgravity.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述聚焦微重力环境下静息和运动时心率压力反射控制的研究现状。作者指出，太空飞行中静息状态下的动脉压力反射控制已报告受损，而运动时的心血管与自主神经反应在模拟或真实微重力条件下结果不一，可能与实验设置差异有关，多数运动研究用手握力作为肌肉运动模型，但微重力主要影响抗重力腿肌，后者更代表肌肉骨骼系统的显著变化。文章据此梳理现有知识，提示需结合更贴近微重力肌肉损伤特点的运动模型来理解压力反射调节。

papers.title: Exploring the Neural Mechanisms of Acupuncture Stimulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Multimodal Neuroimaging Trial.
papers.authors: Sim J, Choi KS, Lee DH.
papers.abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by restricted and repetitive behaviors and disturbances in social communication and interaction. Currently, there is no fundamental treatment for ASD, with only a few medications available for use on a limited basis to manage concomitant neuropsychiatric symptoms. The primary therapeutic goal of such treatments is to alleviate symptoms while maximizing the functional independence and quality of life of affected individuals. Many complementary and alternative medicine therapies have been reported to have effects on ASD symptoms; however, evidence is insufficient to confirm their clinical effectiveness. Acupuncture has traditionally been used as a complementary intervention to manage various neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases, including ASD, in East Asia. However, how acupuncture stimulation modulates neural activity at the macroscale level in individuals with ASD remains largely unknown. Objective This study aims to elucidate disease-related brain alterations and explore the acute neural mechanisms underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD and in typically developing (TD) individuals, using a multimodal neuroimaging approach. Methods This study was designed as a randomized, sham-controlled trial. In this stratified 2×2 design, 70 participants, including individuals with ASD (n=35) and TD controls (n=35), will each be randomly assigned to either the verum or sham acupuncture group, resulting in 4 groups. The verum acupuncture group will receive stimulation at specific acupoints clinically indicated for ASD, eliciting a deqi sensation. The sham acupuncture group will receive superficial needling at nonacupoints unrelated to ASD symptoms. Each group will undergo clinical assessments and multimodal neuroimaging measurements, including functional near-infrared spectroscopy and electroencephalography, before and after acupuncture stimulation. The primary outcome will be differences in resting state network metrics and relative band power in frontal areas by disease status. Secondary outcomes will include differences in these neural markers following acupuncture stimulation between the verum and sham groups, reflecting the group × intervention interaction. Exploratory outcomes will focus on identifying neural markers that correlate with clinical indicators of ASD. Results Recruitment began in April 2025. To date, 23 individuals with ASD and 21 TD individuals have participated in this study. The recruitment process is expected to continue until December 2026. Conclusions ASD presents a significant socioeconomic burden, with no definitive treatment established to date. Although acupuncture is a widely applied intervention for various neurological conditions, including ASD, its large-scale neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. By using multimodal neuroimaging, the present study aims to investigate the immediate neural substrates underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD. These findings are expected to provide a robust neurobiological foundation for future longitudinal research and the development of evidence-based integrative strategies.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究方案针对自闭症谱系障碍缺乏根本性治疗、针灸虽被用作补充干预但其宏观神经机制尚不清楚的问题，设计了一项随机假对照试验，纳入自闭症患者与典型发育个体，在真针灸或假针灸刺激前后进行临床评估及多模态神经影像测量。研究以疾病状态相关的静息态网络指标和额区相对频带功率差异为主要结局，并比较真、假针灸刺激后的神经标记变化，探索与自闭症临床指标相关的神经标记。作者希望借此揭示针灸刺激在自闭症患者中的即时神经基础，为后续纵向研究和循证整合干预策略提供依据；目前招募仍在进行，尚未报告结果。

papers.title: Effective Connectivity and Clinical Correlates in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.authors: Han KI, Bae JH, Jo HJ, Park JM, Yeo Y, Park TS, Park DW, Kim TH.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.abstract: Background Cognitive impairment is a substantial comorbidity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the neural mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This study aimed to assess alterations in effective connectivity (EC) in patients with COPD and investigate their relationships with clinical measures. Methods Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (RS-fMRI) was performed in 38 patients with COPD and 30 healthy controls. EC was estimated using vector autoregressive (VAR) modelling combined with Granger causality analysis across 26 prespecified brain regions of interest derived from our previous functional connectivity study of the same cohort. Between-group differences in directed connectivity were assessed using Welch's t -tests. Associations between EC measures showing between-group differences and clinical measures were evaluated using age-adjusted partial Pearson correlations. Results At the nominal two-sided p < 0.05 level, 37 directed connections showed between-group differences in effective connectivity, and the mean vector autoregressive coefficients for 35 of these connections lay on opposite sides of zero between the COPD and control groups. Among the connections showing between-group differences, age-adjusted associations in patients with COPD involved pulmonary function, systemic oxygenation, cognition, affect, and health status. These associations involved distributed cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions, with several directed connections showing convergence across multiple clinical domains. Conclusion Resting-state VAR-based EC revealed distributed between-group differences in direction-sensitive BOLD temporal organization in COPD. Several of these EC measures were associated with pulmonary function, SpO2 , respiratory and COPD symptom burden, cognition, affect, and health status after age adjustment. These findings extend the functional connectivity profile of COPD by linking directed temporal relationships to its multidimensional clinical burden.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）患者认知等临床负担背后的神经机制，对患者与健康对照进行静息态功能磁共振成像，并用向量自回归建模结合格兰杰因果分析估计预设脑区间的有效连接。结果显示，两组在多个方向性连接上存在差异，且部分连接的方向性模式在两组间呈相反走向；在患者中，这些有效连接指标与肺功能、血氧、认知、情绪及健康状况等临床测量相关，涉及分布广泛的皮层、皮层下和小脑区域。作者认为，这从方向敏感的时间组织层面扩展了COPD的功能连接特征，并将其与多维临床负担联系起来；但相关分析不能说明因果关系。

papers.title: EEG microstate-source coupling is spatially preserved in ALS
papers.authors: Metzger M, Costa G, Dukic S, McMackin R, Giglia E, Mitchell M, Bista S, Tadjine Y, Sirenko V, Plaitano S, Coffey A, Sharp AF, Mehra P, Suleyman N, Woods E, Heverin M, Bede P, Muthuraman M, Pender N, Hardiman O, Nasseroleslami B.
papers.abstract: Abstract EEG microstates are thought to reflect rapid transitions between brain-wide states and show disrupted temporal dynamics across neurological and psychiatric conditions, including ALS, yet the neural sources generating these states remain incompletely understood. Here, we introduce a source-resolved framework that links time-resolved microstate activations to estimated regional brain signals, enabling estimation of the neural sources underlying canonical microstate classes. Resting-state EEG from a large cohort of healthy controls (HC, n = 122) and individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, n = 121) was analysed. Canonical microstates were derived from pooled data, and time-resolved microstate activation time series were estimated via projection-based decomposition of scalp potentials. In parallel, EEG source activity was reconstructed using beamformer-based inverse modelling and parcellated into 90 cortical regions. Microstate-source coupling was quantified using ridge regression linking microstate activations to reconstructed regional timecourses, producing spatially resolved coupling maps for each microstate class. In HC, reproducible and spatially distinct microstate-source coupling patterns were observed, consistent with structured mapping between scalp-defined brain states and distributed neural systems. Spatial reproducibility was confirmed using permutation-based null models that preserved temporal autocorrelation within microstate sequences and accounted for spatial dependence across regions. In HC, microstate-source coupling was spatially reproducible across independent subgroups for the four canonical microstates (A-D; r ≥ 0.90, q < 0.05). In ALS, coupling topography was preserved relative to HC for all four microstate classes (r ≥ 0.90, q < 0.05), and cluster-based permutation testing revealed no significant group differences in coupling magnitude for any microstate class, a null result robust to sex and riluzole status. Microstate-source coupling was preserved, suggesting stability of canonical microstate organisation across sensor and source space. Overall, these findings demonstrate that canonical EEG microstates have stable, reproducible coupling with distributed brain sources, and that this coupling organisation is preserved in ALS despite known alterations in microstate temporal characteristics. This dissociation suggests that spatial and temporal organisation of microstates may be governed by partially independent mechanisms, with spatial organisation buffered against ALS-related change, potentially through degeneracy or local compensatory mechanisms, while temporal engagement remains more directly sensitive to disease.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出一个源分辨框架，将脑电微状态的瞬时激活与估计的区域脑信号联系起来，以考察经典微状态类别背后的神经来源；研究分析健康对照与肌萎缩侧索硬化（ALS）患者的静息态脑电，并用束流形成器逆建模重建源活动、以岭回归量化微状态与脑源的耦合。结果发现，健康对照中四种经典微状态均呈现可重复且空间上彼此区分的耦合模式，独立亚组间高度一致；ALS患者的耦合空间拓扑与健康对照相比同样保持稳定，各微状态类别的耦合强度未见显著组间差异，且该零结果对性别和利鲁唑使用状态稳健。作者据此指出，经典脑电微状态与分布式脑源之间存在稳定、可重复的耦合，这种空间组织在ALS中得以保留，尽管已知微状态的时间特征发生改变；空间与时间组织可能受部分独立的机制调控，空间组织或受到缓冲保护，而时间参与则对疾病更敏感。

papers.title: The hypothalamic orexin-medial prefrontal cortex pathway modulates susceptibility to depression in the learned helplessness paradigm in male mice.
papers.authors: Mi T, He Z, Yu B, Li Q, Lu G, Hao J, Niu J, Ma S, Rong W, Niu J.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Depression is a prevalent psychiatric disorder primarily characterized by behavioral despair and helplessness. The orexinergic system plays a crucial role in stress-induced depression; however, the precise mechanisms remain unclear. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a major target of orexinergic projections, is essential for emotional regulation. This study suggests that impaired orexinergic input to the mPFC underlies depression-like behaviors in murine models. In the learned helplessness (LH) paradigm, the majority of male mice subjected to inescapable foot shocks developed depression-like behaviors (classified as LH-susceptible), whereas a subset displayed resilience (classified as LH-resilient). LH-susceptible mice exhibited a reduced number of orexin+ neuronal somata in the hypothalamus, along with decreased expression of prepro-orexin mRNA Correspondingly, the mPFC of these mice displayed decreased density of orexinergic terminals and lower Orexin A levels. In contrast, LH-resilient mice maintained stable hypothalamic orexin neuron counts, exhibited increased prepro-orexin mRNA expression, and preserved orexinergic terminal density in the mPFC. Chemogenetic activation of the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway alleviated depression-like behaviors in LH-susceptible mice through Orexin A signaling. Conversely, inhibition of this pathway induced depression-like behaviors in LH-resilient mice. Additionally, LH-susceptible mice showed decreased excitatory synaptic transmission in layer V pyramidal neurons of the mPFC, which was improved by activation of hypothalamic orexinergic inputs; this improvement was attenuated by administration of an orexin receptor 1 (OX1R) antagonist. Collectively, these findings implicate the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway as a pivotal regulator of excitatory synaptic transmission and suggest its involvement in modulating individual variability in susceptibility and resilience to depression.Significance statement Depression is a highly prevalent emotional disorder characterized by behavioral despair and helplessness under stress. This study demonstrates that the orexinergic system is critical for modulating resilience to aversive stimuli. Using the learned helplessness (LH) mouse model, we found that LH-susceptible mice, but not LH-resilient mice, show compromised hypothalamic orexinergic projections to the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), together with decreased excitatory synaptic transmission in layer V pyramidal neurons. Activation of the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway alleviates depression-like behaviors in susceptible mice through Orexin A, while inhibition of this pathway induces depression-like phenotypes in resilient mice. These findings identify orexinergic signaling as a promising therapeutic target for depression.

papers.title: A novel nitric oxide (NO)-dependent 'molecular switch' mediates LTP in the Octopus vulgaris brain through persistent activation of nitric oxide synthase (NOS).
papers.authors: Turchetti-Maia AL, Shomrat T, Bidel F, Koren I, Stern-Mentch N, Nesher N, Hochner B.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Cephalopod mollusks provide a striking example of the independent evolution of advanced cognitive abilities in invertebrates. In octopuses, learning and memory are mediated by the vertical lobe (VL), whose visual input synapses undergo robust activity-dependent long-term potentiation (LTP). Here, we used Octopus vulgaris of either sex to show that persistent activation of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) mediates both LTP expression and maintenance, independently of de novo protein synthesis. Contrary to the prevailing view, NO signaling is not required for LTP induction, as LTP can still be induced in the presence of NOS inhibitors. Remarkably, however, NOS inhibitors blocked presynaptic LTP expression, while NO donors induced only short-term potentiation, together suggesting that LTP expression depends on persistently elevated NO levels. The effective NO concentrations, estimated both pharmacologically and amperometrically, were more than three orders of magnitude higher than those required for activation of the canonical sGC-cGMP pathway, suggesting that NO acts through direct covalent modification of proteins, such as S-nitrosylation. In a subset of synapses, the NOS inhibitor L-NNA rapidly and completely erased established LTP; however, following washout, full potentiation could be reinstated by renewed tetanic stimulation. We therefore propose a 'molecular switch' mechanism in which an NO-dependent positive feedback loop persistently reactivates NOS, thereby maintaining LTP. These findings reveal an unprecedented form of convergent evolution in which molecular innovations equip the octopus VL network with the computational properties required for associative learning.Significance Statement Long-term potentiation (LTP) is a central cellular mechanism of learning and memory. While extensively studied in vertebrates, its mechanisms in octopuses-animals that independently evolved sophisticated cognitive abilities-remain poorly understood. Here, we uncover a novel form of LTP involving activity-dependent activation of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) in the postsynaptic cell. The produced nitric oxide (NO) mediates LTP maintenance through persistent NO-dependent reactivation of NOS (a "molecular switch") and simultaneously mediates LTP expression by retrogradely facilitating presynaptic transmitter release. These findings reveal a striking example of convergent evolution in which distinct molecular mechanisms independently evolved to implement associative (Hebbian) learning rules within a neural network.

papers.title: Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit: Simulated datasets and quality metrics for dynamical models of neural activity.
papers.authors: Versteeg C, McCart JD, Ostrow M, Zoltowski DM, Washington CB, Driscoll L, Codol O, Michaels JA, Linderman SW, Sussillo D, Pandarinath C.
papers.abstract: A primary goal of systems neuroscience is to discover how ensembles of neurons transform inputs into goal-directed behavior, a process known as neural computation. A powerful framework for understanding neural computation uses neural dynamics - the rules that govern how neural activity evolves over time - to explain how goal-directed input-output transformations occur. As dynamical rules are not directly observable, we need computational models that can infer neural dynamics from recorded neural activity. We typically validate such models using synthetic datasets with known ground-truth dynamics, but unfortunately existing synthetic datasets don't reflect fundamental features of neural computation and may therefore be poor proxies for neural systems. Further, the field lacks validated metrics for quantifying the accuracy of the dynamics inferred by models. The Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit (CtDToolkit) addresses these critical gaps by providing: 1) synthetic datasets that reflect computational properties of biological neural circuits, 2) interpretable metrics for quantifying model performance, and 3) a standardized pipeline for training and evaluating models with or without known external inputs. In this manuscript, we demonstrate how CtDToolkit can help guide the development, tuning, and troubleshooting of neural dynamics models. In summary, CtDToolkit provides a necessary framework for model developers to better understand and characterize neural computation through the lens of dynamics.

papers.title: Functional and Structural Imaging Features of Cognitive Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.authors: Jain K, Valsasina P, Mistri D, Meani A, Preziosa P, Filippi M, Rocca MA.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Cognitive impairment affects 40%-70% of patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). Although recent hypothesis-driven and data-driven efforts have identified cognitive phenotypes, functional substrates underlying impairment in such phenotypes are still not clear. Our objective was to identify distinct cognitive phenotypes using clustering in a large cohort of patients with MS and characterize their associated clinical, structural MRI, and resting-state (RS) functional connectivity (FC) features. Methods We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study with right-handed patients with MS and age-matched and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) who underwent neurologic and neuropsychological evaluation (Brief Repeatable Battery of Neuropsychological tests). Latent profile analysis on cognitive test Z-scores identified MS cognitive phenotypes. 3.0T MRI was used to derive atrophy measures and RS FC within default mode network (DMN I/II), executive control network (ECN), left/right fronto-parietal, language, and salience networks. Linear regression models compared structural MRI and RS FC across cognitive phenotypes and HCs, while polynomial contrasts assessed RS FC patterns across groups. Results Three hundred and sixty-nine patients with MS and 168 HCs were enrolled. Four cognitive phenotypes were detected: preserved cognition ([PC], n = 67[18.2%]), mild single-domain verbal fluency involvement (MSD-VF, n = 37[10.0%]), mild single-domain attention involvement (MSD-A, n = 197[53.4%]), and severe multidomain (SMD) involvement (SMD, n = 68[18.4%]). At corrected threshold, PC patients showed decreased deep gray matter (GM) volumes (p < 0.001-0.001) and similar RS FC vs HCs, whereas MSD-VF exhibited no significant atrophy and no differences in RS FC vs HCs. MSD-A displayed lower cortical/deep GM volumes vs HCs (p < 0.001-0.005), whereas SMD had worse clinical and atrophy features (p < 0.001-0.04), as well as decreased DMN II RS FC (p = 0.01-0.04) vs other groups. Polynomial contrast analyses revealed significant quadratic patterns with increased RS FC in MSD-VF vs HC/PC groups, followed by decrease in MSD-A and SMD, within DMN II (p = 0.005), ECN (p = 0.005), and language network (p < 0.001). Discussion PC exhibited intact RS FC, whereas SMD presented widespread structural and DMN RS FC damage. These findings advance our understanding of cognitive heterogeneity in MS by revealing distinct structural and functional neuroimaging profiles across cognitive phenotypes, encouraging future longitudinal and multimodal investigations to improve disease characterization and prognostic stratification.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注多发性硬化患者认知损害的异质性，用聚类方法在患者中识别认知表型，并比较各表型与健康对照在脑结构萎缩和静息态功能连接上的差异。结果发现四种认知表型：认知保留、轻度单域言语流畅性受损、轻度单域注意力受损和严重多域受损。认知保留者虽有深部灰质体积下降但功能连接与健康对照相近，轻度言语流畅性受损者无明显萎缩和功能连接差异，轻度注意力受损者皮层及深部灰质体积较低，而严重多域受损者临床和萎缩表现更差且默认网络II功能连接降低。作者据此指出，不同认知表型对应不同的结构与功能影像特征，认知保留者功能连接相对完整，严重受损者则呈现广泛的结构和默认网络功能连接损害，这有助于理解多发性硬化认知异质性，但相关发现仍需纵向和多模态研究验证。

papers.title: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
papers.authors: Łoś K, Waszkiewicz N.
papers.journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
papers.abstract: Background The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data represents a burgeoning frontier in schizophrenia diagnostics. However, the inferential validity of findings is frequently compromised by methodological heterogeneity. This systematic review rigorously evaluates the diagnostic efficacy and methodological robustness of AI-generated EEG biomarkers by implementing the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for Artificial Intelligence (PROBAST+AI). Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 43 primary studies encompassing 3,420 patients with schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis and 3,164 healthy controls (total N = 6,584). Methodological quality and validation strategies were assessed using the 34 signaling questions of the PROBAST+AI framework. Results The aggregate mean diagnostic accuracy across the literature was 93.38%, with deep learning architectures demonstrating superior metrics relative to classical machine learning (96.83% vs. 87.68%). Critically, external validation was restricted to 4.7% of the included studies. A pronounced performance discrepancy was observed between subject-wise (88.22%) and segment-wise (98.14%) validation protocols, indicating pervasive data leakage. Overall, 76.7% of the analyzed studies were characterized by a high risk of bias, predominantly stemming from suboptimal data partitioning and inadequate independent verification. Conclusions Contemporary diagnostic accuracies appear to be artifactually elevated due to structural methodological deficiencies and data leakage. Consequently, current evidence does not support the immediate clinical implementation of AI-EEG biomarkers in schizophrenia. To facilitate translational progress, we propose a standardized methodological framework optimizing validation strategies.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述系统评估了基于静息态脑电的人工智能精神分裂症诊断标志物，纳入多项原始研究，并用PROBAST+AI工具评价其方法学质量与验证策略。汇总结果显示文献报告的诊断准确率整体很高，深度学习模型高于经典机器学习，但外部验证研究极少，且按被试划分与按片段划分验证之间存在明显性能落差，提示数据泄漏普遍存在。多数研究被判定为高偏倚风险，主要源于数据划分不当和缺乏独立验证。作者据此认为，现有准确率可能被人为抬高，当前证据尚不足以支持这类标志物直接进入临床使用，并提出标准化方法学框架以改进验证策略。

papers.title: Development of the social perception pathway across the third trimester of gestation and perinatal transition.
papers.authors: Chawarska K, Scheinost D, Constable RT, Lacadie C, Sun H, Chang J, Ment LR.
papers.abstract: Babies display social perceptual skills within hours of birth which may indicate that the neural predecessors of such skills have prenatal origins. However, the putative fetal neural infrastructure supporting these skills remains unexplored. Data from 497 participants scanned between 28-44 weeks postmenstrual age were examined to map the development of intrinsic functional connectivity (iFC) within the proto social pathway (pSP), encompassing the superior temporal sulcus (STS), a region implicated in processing multimodal social stimuli later in development, and the proto ventral pathway (pVP), including the fusiform face area (FFA), a region associated with static face processing in older children and adults. IFC was greater than 0 in the bilateral pSP and pVP by 28 weeks and increased significantly in the left and right pSP and left pVP but not in the right pVP between 28 and 44 weeks. By 44 weeks, both pathways exhibited robust right-dominance. By 40 weeks, iFC for the right and left pSP was significantly higher than in the corresponding pVPs. Lastly, the right posterior STS (pSTS) and the right FFA coupling became positive by 40 and 44 weeks and the left pSTS-FFA coupling became negative by 44 weeks. These findings demonstrate that neural architecture supporting social perception later in life is present in the third trimester and undergoes rapid development across the pre- to postnatal transition. The strengthening of intrinsic connectivity, emergence of right-hemisphere dominance, and early differentiation of putative social perception and face-processing circuitry indicate that key features of the social brain begin to assemble before birth, providing a developmental scaffold for later social development.

papers.title: Evidence for hierarchical representations of written and spoken words from an open-science human neuroimaging dataset.
papers.authors: Banerjee S, Jin K, Nikolov P, Cho P, Pendri VR, Chang L, Damera SR, Riesenhuber M.
papers.abstract: Reading and speech recognition rely on multi-level processing that builds from basic visual or sound features to complete word representations, yet details of these processing hierarchies (in particular those for spoken words) are still poorly understood. We re-analyzed the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data provided in the Mother Of all Unification Studies (MOUS) open-science dataset by using parametric regressions of word frequency and sublexical unit (bigram or syllable) frequency during reading and speech listening tasks in order to elucidate lexical and sublexical processing stages in the visual and auditory modalities. We first validated our approach in the written word domain, where the technique identified significant correlations for word frequency in the left mid-fusiform cortex (at the location of the Visual Word Form Area) and a left occipital region tracking bigram frequency, compatible with prior reports. During listening, activity in a left mid-superior temporal region consistent with the recently described Auditory Word Form Area (AWFA) showed a lexical frequency effect, while a more posterior region of the superior temporal gyrus was sensitive to syllable frequency. Activation in the left inferior frontal gyrus correlated with both written and spoken word frequencies. These findings suggest analogous posterior-to-anterior hierarchical organizations in the anteroventral visual and auditory streams, with modality-specific posterior sublexical and more anterior lexical representations that converge in higher-order language areas.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究重新分析开放科学脑成像数据，用词汇与亚词汇频率的参数回归比较阅读和听词的加工层级。结果在书写词中复现了视觉词形区的词汇频率效应及枕区对双字母组合频率的追踪；听词时听觉词形区呈词汇频率效应，更后部颞上回对音节频率敏感，左额下回与两种词频均相关。作者据此提出视觉与听觉腹侧通路存在类似的后到前层级组织，后部加工亚词汇、前部加工词汇，并在高级语言区汇聚。

papers.title: Validating the standard model of diffusion MRI in white matter with numerical substrates.
papers.authors: Nguyen-Duc J, Uhl Q, Oliveira R, Rafael-Patiño J, Jelescu IO.
papers.abstract: The non-invasive estimation of intra- and extracellular microstructural parameters using biophysical models has been a major focus in brain microstructure imaging with MRI. The Standard Model (SM) of diffusion in white matter (WM) provides a unifying framework for various modelling approaches, representing axons as impermeable sticks embedded within a locally anisotropic extra-axonal space. However, the SM relies on simplifying assumptions that may not hold in realistic WM tissue, as they do not take into account axonal undulations, beading, the presence of glial cells, or membrane permeability. In this work, we investigate how SM parameter estimates, derived using the Standard Model Imaging (SMI) framework, behave when the model is applied to realistic numerical WM substrates generated by the CATERPillar tool. Specifically, we vary (i) axonal morphological features such as beading and undulations, (ii) axonal packing density, (iii) orientation dispersion, (iv) membrane permeability of axons and astrocytes separately, (v) myelin volume fraction, and (vi) diffusion time. In each part of the analysis, different noise levels are introduced. Our findings enable users to identify potential biases introduced by varying conditions and to adjust their interpretations accordingly.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究检验白质扩散磁共振标准模型在更接近真实组织的数值底物上是否仍能给出可靠参数估计。作者用数值工具生成白质底物，改变轴突形态、堆积密度、方向弥散、膜通透性、髓鞘体积分数和扩散时间，并加入不同噪声水平，考察标准模型成像所得参数如何随之偏移。结果显示，这些简化假设未覆盖的因素会引入可识别的估计偏差，提示使用者需结合具体条件解读参数，而非将其直接视为真实微观结构的无偏读数。

papers.title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Liu Y, Hu Y, Zhang Z, Du J, Cui L, Liu Q, Zhong L, Xin Y, Chai R, Deng L, Pan J, Schiller J, Xu NL.
papers.abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

papers.title: Altered prefrontal suppression of striatal activity during intrusive images in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
papers.authors: Vandevelde A, Dollfus S, Gagnepain P.
papers.abstract: Background Current models of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) emphasize dysfunction in frontostriatal circuits that support flexible behavioral control, leading to impulsive and compulsive actions. However, how these disruptions contribute to obsessions and intrusive thoughts remains poorly understood. Clarifying these mechanisms is essential for understanding cognitive control deficits in OCD. Method We examined intrusive memories elicited by emotional and neutral scenes in individuals with OCD (N = 24) and healthy controls (N = 21). Participants learned scene-cue associations and were later instructed to suppress memory retrieval when presented with reminder cues. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) measured neural activity during suppression. Generalization of findings with alternative materials was assessed in larger samples of healthy controls (N = 73) and individuals with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD; N = 55). Results fMRI analyses showed preserved activity in frontoparietal, basal ganglia, and limbic regions in individuals with OCD, even during emotional intrusion suppression. However, unlike healthy controls, individuals with OCD failed to suppress striatal activity during intrusive memory, regardless of emotional content. Connectivity analyses indicated that this hyperactivity reflected reduced top-down inhibitory control, a disruption associated with greater obsessive symptom severity. Test of generalizability confirmed the role of frontostriatal downregulation in controlling intrusive thoughts and showed that this alteration was specific to OCD. Conclusions These findings emphasize the central role of frontostriatal circuits in regulating intrusive thinking. Obsessions in OCD may result from disrupted inhibitory mechanisms that normally restrict access to striatal-dependent information, contributing to persistent intrusive thoughts.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注强迫症中侵入性思维为何难以抑制，比较了强迫症患者与健康对照在抑制情绪性和中性场景所诱发侵入记忆时的脑活动，并在健康人和创伤后应激障碍个体中检验结果的推广性。影像分析显示，强迫症患者额顶、基底节和边缘区域活动基本保留，但无论记忆内容是否带情绪色彩，他们都未能像健康对照那样抑制纹状体活动；连接分析提示这种过度活动反映自上而下的抑制控制减弱，且与强迫症状严重程度相关。作者据此认为，强迫症中的强迫观念可能源于额纹状体抑制机制失调，使本应受限制的纹状体依赖信息持续进入意识，而该改变在对照检验中表现出对强迫症的特异性。

papers.title: Neuronavigated dual-target transcranial magnetic stimulation for schizophrenia negative symptoms.
papers.authors: Wei Y, Wang J, Tang X, Qian Z, Xu L, Cui H, Song Y, Zhu H, Ju M, Long B, Zhai W, Zeng L, Jiao X, Lan X, Wei X, Tang Y, Wang J, Zhang T.
papers.abstract: Negative symptoms in schizophrenia severely impair function and quality of life, yet respond poorly to current therapies. This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial aimed to investigate the efficacy of neuronavigated dual-target repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (rDLPFC) and cerebellum for improving negative symptoms in early-stage psychosis (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04853485). Participants with first-episode schizophrenia or clinical high-risk for psychosis were enrolled from Shanghai Mental Health Center and Suzhou Guangji Hospital. Participants were randomly assigned to either a real or sham group under MRI-guided neuronavigation, targeting rDLPFC with 1Hz at 100% motor threshold(MT), cerebellar with intermittent theta burst stimulation(iTBS) at 120% MT for 20 consecutive days. Clinical assessments were conducted at baseline(T0), 10-session(T1), 20-session(T2) and one month after the intervention(T3). Cognition and MRI were evaluated at T0 and T2. The primary outcome was change of negative subscale score of the Positive and Negative Symptoms Scale(PANSS), while secondary outcomes included alterations in other PANSS subscale scores and fronto-cerebellar circuit functional connectivity. In total, 75 participants were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (36 active, 39 sham). The pre-specified primary linear mixed-effects analysis revealed a non-significant group-by-time interaction for PANSS negative subscale scores (F(3,174.6)=1.45, p=0.230). At the 4-week endpoint (T2), the nominal unadjusted between-group p-value was 0.049; after Sidak correction for multiple comparisons, the adjusted mean difference was -2.48 points (95% CI -4.99 to 0.03, adjusted p=0.150, Cohen's d=-0.51). Descriptive uncorrected t-tests indicated greater negative-symptom reductions in the active group at T1 and T2, and the 4-week negative-symptom response rate (≥50% reduction) was higher under real rTMS (χ2=9.5, p=0.002). A significant group-by-time interaction was observed for PANSS positive subscale scores (F(3,172.0)=3.26, p=0.023). Both groups exhibited substantial within-group symptom improvement. Resting-state fMRI demonstrated group-by-time interactions within cerebello-temporal, parahippocampal, caudate, and parietal networks (FWE-corrected p<0.05), and negative-symptom change correlated with cerebello-caudate connectivity (r=0.33, p=0.026). These findings suggest neuronavigated dual-target rTMS over rDLPFC and cerebellum may be associated with numerical improvements in negative symptoms in early-stage psychosis.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注导航下右侧背外侧前额叶与小脑双靶点重复经颅磁刺激能否改善早期精神病（首发精神分裂症或精神病临床高危）的阴性症状，采用多中心随机双盲假对照设计，真刺激组接受1Hz rDLPFC与iTBS小脑刺激共20天，主要结局为PANSS阴性分量表评分变化。意向性分析纳入75人（真刺激36、假刺激39），预设线性混合模型未发现显著的组×时间交互（p=0.230）；4周终点经Sidak校正后组间差异亦不显著（校正p=0.150），仅未校正检验和应答率提示真刺激组降幅更大，且两组均有明显组内改善。静息态fMRI显示小脑-颞叶、海马旁回、尾状核及顶叶网络存在组×时间交互，阴性症状变化与小脑-尾状核连接相关。作者据此仅提示该双靶点方案可能与阴性症状的数值性改善相关，未确立疗效。

papers.title: Pupil dilation as an index of episodic processing when remembering, imagining, and thinking creatively.
papers.authors: Thakral PP, Madore KP, Devitt AL.
papers.abstract: Prior research indicates that the cognitive and neural systems supporting the recall of specific past experiences (episodic memory) also play a key role in imagining novel and specific future experiences (episodic simulation), and divergent creative thinking. In particular, constructive memory processes (e.g. retrieval and recombination of specific episodic details) are thought to benefit episodic simulation and divergent thinking. In the current study, we provide a novel test of this hypothesis using eye-tracking. We capitalized on prior eye-tracking and neuroimaging evidence demonstrating that pupil dilation and hippocampal activity are enhanced when memory is associated with the retrieval of episodic detail relative to non-episodic detail. We tracked pupil dilation as participants recalled past experiences, imagined novel future experiences, engaged in divergent thinking, or performed a non-episodic/semantic retrieval task. Pupil dilation tracked divergent thinking ability and the number of episodic details generated during episodic memory and simulation. No relationship was observed between pupil dilation and performance in the semantic memory task, or the generation of non-episodic details during episodic memory and simulation. In contrast, fixation counts tracked performance in the semantic retrieval task. In line with prior findings, we interpret the results as reflecting the retrieval of specific information during episodic memory, simulation, and divergent thinking. At a broader level, these findings suggest that examining pupillometry is a promising direction for identifying common episodic processes.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究用眼动追踪考察瞳孔扩张能否作为情节性加工的共同指标，让参与者在回忆过去经历、想象新颖未来经历、进行发散性思维或完成非情节性语义提取任务时同步记录瞳孔变化。结果显示，瞳孔扩张与发散思维能力以及情节记忆和想象中生成的情节细节数量相关，而与语义记忆任务表现及非情节细节的生成无关；相比之下，注视次数与语义提取任务表现相关。作者据此认为，瞳孔扩张反映了情节记忆、想象和发散思维中对特定信息的提取，并提示瞳孔测量是识别共同情节性加工的有前景方向。

papers.title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder.
papers.authors: Li X, Zuo F, Cheng Y, Perkins K, Cao F.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD-TD connectivity differences. Cluster 1 was marked by consistent hypoconnectivity across ages, suggesting a stable neural signature of ASD. Cluster 2 was characterized by hypoconnectivity in childhood that gradually diminished with age, suggesting a temporary delay profile. These clusters were systematically organized along the sensory-association axis. Cluster 1 mainly involved lower-rank sensory and sensorimotor cortices, while Cluster 2 mainly involved higher-rank association cortices. Brain-behavior analyses revealed greater and broader ASD symptom associations across ages in the consistent hypoconnectivity profile than the delay profile. Further subtype analyses suggested that social-affect symptoms were associated with greater hypoconnectivity than repetitive behavior symptoms in both clusters. Spatial correlation analyses with neurotransmitter maps revealed associations of Cluster 1 with mGluR5 and of Cluster 2 with GABAA α5, providing insight into the neurobiological basis of the two clusters. In a cross-disorder validation analysis, applying the same analytic framework to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder did not reveal comparable results. Together, these findings suggest that ASD-related functional connectivity alterations are developmentally heterogeneous and organized along the cortical hierarchy, providing a developmental perspective for understanding the neurobiology of ASD.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究利用多中心静息态功能磁共振横断面数据，考察5至64岁孤独症谱系障碍者与典型发育者之间功能连接差异如何随年龄变化。数据驱动分析识别出两个空间分布的皮层区域簇：一簇在各年龄段均表现为稳定的连接减弱，另一簇的连接减弱主要在童年出现并随年龄逐渐消退，呈延迟特征；两簇沿感觉—联合皮层轴组织，且稳定减弱簇与症状的关联更广更强。作者据此提出，孤独症相关功能连接改变在发育上具有异质性，并沿皮层等级组织。

papers.title: Mechanistic versus descriptive interpretation of brain activity pattern reconstruction.
papers.authors: Jung K, Eickhoff SB, Patil KR.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: The geometric eigenmodes, derived from the shape of the cortical surface, have been suggested as a better model for explaining brain function due to their high accuracy in reconstructing patterns of both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked brain activity patterns captured by functional MRI, when contrasted with alternative models including structural connectome derived bases. While a descriptive representation offers valuable utility for neuroimaging studies, it is necessary to examine the extent to which it supports a mechanistic explanation for human brain function. Although the observation that geometric eigenmodes accurately fit brain activity is intriguing, we argue that accepting them as a model of brain function risks conflating descriptive and mechanistic interpretations. While a representation that effectively describes the underlying geometry is inherently adept at fitting patterns within that geometric space; it does not necessarily shed light on mechanisms that give rise to the brain's functional attributes. To this end, we provide two lines of empirical results: a) geometric eigenmodes demonstrate a high flexibility when fit to a range of manipulated patterns, and b) localized parcel-based representations can reconstruct activity patterns as well. Based on those results, theoretical considerations, and previous data, we argue that more consideration is needed regarding the complementary roles of descriptive representation and mechanistic explanation in neuroimaging research. While we recognize the potential role of the brain's geometry in influencing its dynamics, assertions regarding its efficacy should be weighed against its inherent lack of specificity, biological interpretability, and anatomical evidence.
papers.summary_zh: 该文讨论用皮层表面几何本征模态重建脑活动模式时，描述性表征与机制性解释之间的混淆问题。作者以两项实证结果说明：几何本征模态对多种人为操纵的模式也能灵活拟合，而基于局部脑区的表征同样可重建活动模式。作者据此指出，几何本征模态拟合精度高并不等于揭示了脑功能的产生机制，其特异性、生物学可解释性和解剖学证据均有限，呼吁神经影像研究更审慎地区分描述与机制解释。

papers.title: Towards a unified biology of vertebrate number sense.
papers.authors: Zanon M, Messina A, Butterworth B, Vallortigara G, Brennan CH, Torres-Pérez JV, Miletto-Petrazzini ME.
papers.abstract: Number sense, the ability to estimate and compare numerical quantities, emerges early in development and is widespread across species. Despite decades of work on behavioural and neural correlates of numerosity, the genetic and mechanistic foundations remain poorly integrated. We propose a review and perspective that brings together evidence from vertebrates. Our unique focus relies on how genetic variation, brain lateralisation, and neural circuit organisation across development shape number cognition. We highlight zebrafish (Danio rerio) and chicks (Gallus gallus) as complementary comparative models that can uncover conserved principles and novel mechanisms, opening new avenues for studying the biological bases of numerical cognition and its disorders from the very early developmental stages.

papers.title: 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin.
papers.authors: Baker JJ, Kogan E, Ma S, Lu J, Zuo Y.
papers.abstract: It is unclear how serotonin 2A receptors (5-HT2A Rs) in cortical layer 5 pyramidal neurons differentially contribute to psilocybin-induced hallucinations versus neuroplasticity. Here we show that psilocybin promotes synapse formation and maturation while accelerating the elimination of pre-existing synapses. Cell type-specific manipulation further demonstrated that 5-HT2A R signaling in cortical layer 5 pyramidal neurons is necessary and sufficient for psilocybin-induced synaptic remodeling but dispensable for the head-twitch response, a rodent proxy of hallucination.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal AI-based modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain using Seal.
papers.authors: Hao Y, Park CY, Theesfeld CL, Troyanskaya OG.
papers.abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation in the developing human brain remains a central challenge in neuroscience, particularly in transient cell types and developmental stages where data are limited. We present Seal, an interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) transfer learning framework for genome-based modeling of gene expression and variant effects with spatiotemporal resolution across 26 regions, 30 cell types and 7 developmental stages. Seal predictions provide mechanistic interpretation by linking variants to transcriptional regulators in a spatiotemporal context. Applying Seal to genome-wide association studies, we identify shared and distinct regulatory architectures across six neuropsychiatric conditions that align with clinical trajectories. In the Simons Simplex Collection autism cohort whole-genome data, Seal uncovers a significant burden of de novo regulatory variants in transient fetal excitatory neurons, revealing cell-type-specific and stage-specific effects. By connecting genetic variation to spatiotemporal regulatory programs, Seal offers a general framework for uncovering mechanisms of human brain development and disease.

papers.title: An aging-sensitive secreted phospholipase confers neuroprotection and cognitive resilience.
papers.authors: Vicidomini C, Goode TD, Yu R, Mehta I, McAvoy KM, Beveridge CH, Randolph CE, Iyer SN, Victor MB, Leary N, Evans L, Steinbaugh MJ, Lai ZW, Lyon MC, San Silvestre MRF, Tosoni G, Ayyildiz D, Ho Sui S, Yamamoto K, Murakami M, Salta E, Tsai LH, Chopra G, Sahay A.
papers.abstract: Cognitive reserve theory posits that compensatory mechanisms during aging stave off cognitive decline and lower risk for Alzheimer's disease. Here, in a screen for hippocampal dentate granule cell (DGC) synapse loss-induced factors in mice, we identified a secreted phospholipase, Pla2g2f, whose expression increases in DGCs during aging and is associated with cognitive resilience in humans. Pla2g2f deletion in DGCs exacerbates aging-associated pathophysiological changes, including synapse loss, inflammatory microglia, reactive astrogliosis, impaired neurogenesis, lipid dysregulation, lipid droplet accumulation and hippocampal-dependent memory loss. Conversely, boosting Pla2g2f in DGCs during aging is sufficient to prevent these pathophysiological alterations in hippocampal-cortical circuits, protect memory and prophylactically modify trajectory of cognitive decline. Mutagenesis of the catalytic site of PLA2G2F prevented lipid droplet mobilization and reduction of reactive gliosis and inflammatory microglia. Neuronal PLA2G2F mediates intercellular signaling to decrease lipid droplet and cholesterol ester load in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia. Our findings implicate PLA2G2F as a compensatory neuroprotective broadcast signal that maintains lipid homeostasis to counteract aging-associated cognitive decline.

papers.title: Periventricular gradient pathology is linked to ependymal reactivity and cell adhesion disruption in multiple sclerosis.
papers.authors: Groh AMR, Afanasiev E, Thevakumaran R, Creeggan F, Callahan-Martin L, Bigotte M, Yaqubi M, Gertsvolf J, Pei J, Wu H, de Vos J, Aalders MCG, Zandee S, Prat A, Rudko DA, Stratton JA.
papers.abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-adjacent brain areas are especially vulnerable to diffuse degeneration in multiple sclerosis (MS). Surface-in gradients arising from CSF-borne cytotoxic factors have been proposed to predict disease relapses independent of white matter lesions. Yet, whether such factors disrupt ependymal cells to penetrate the ventricular border in MS remains unknown. Here, using ultra-high-field magnetic resonance imaging-guided histology, electron microscopy and single-nucleus multiomics, we found that ependymal pathology correlates with periventricular gradients and involves an immune-reactive state marked by transporter and junctional protein dysregulation. We further defined the gene regulatory networks underpinning the MS ependymal state and predicted ligands known to be enriched in MS CSF that could drive the emergence of this state. One of the candidates, IFNγ, increased murine ependymal permeability in vivo, indicating that CSF ligands can modulate ependymal function and regional inflammation. These findings identify CSF-driven ependymal dysfunction as a contributor to periventricular pathology in MS.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注多发性硬化中脑室周围区域易受弥漫性退变影响的机制，特别是脑脊液来源因素是否通过破坏室管膜细胞而参与这一过程。作者结合超高场磁共振引导的组织学、电子显微镜和单核多组学方法，分析多发性硬化组织中的室管膜病理状态及其与脑室周围梯度的关联。研究发现室管膜病理与脑室周围梯度相关，表现为转运蛋白和连接蛋白失调的免疫反应状态，并构建了相应的基因调控网络、预测了脑脊液中可能驱动该状态的配体。候选配体IFNγ在体内可增加小鼠室管膜通透性，提示脑脊液配体能够调节室管膜功能与局部炎症，但该研究主要基于关联和组织/动物实验，尚不能确立临床因果关系。

papers.title: Polygenic scores for longevity in relation to brain MRI measures in a cohort of 70-year-olds.
papers.authors: Seidu NM, Lindberg O, Kern S, Rydén L, Wahlund LO, Waern M, Mohanty R, Cedres N, Zetterberg H, Blennow K, Erhag HF, Zettergren A, Westman E, Holstege H, Skoog I.
papers.abstract: Population-based studies on the relation between polygenic longevity scores (PGLSs) and specific brain regions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are few. We aimed to investigate this relationship in a population of 70-year-olds from Gothenburg, Sweden (N = 675). We constructed two PGLSs (one with and one without the APOE locus) using longevity GWAS summary statistics. MRI outcomes included total grey matter, white matter (WM), WM hyperintensities (WMHs), subcortical volumes, small vessel disease (SVD) score, cortical thicknesses, and fractional anisotropy (FA) fibre tracts. We adjusted for sex, age, principal components, and sex interactions, and corrected for multiple comparisons. We found no associations in the total sample. In males, both PGLSs were associated with smaller WMHs volume and lower SVD burden, and a thicker cortex of pars triangularis, pars opercularis, and insula. Our findings suggest a possible link between genetic propensity for longevity and lower cerebrovascular burden and certain cortical grey matter areas in males.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于瑞典哥德堡一批70岁人群的队列数据，考察长寿多基因评分与脑磁共振成像指标之间的关系，并分别构建了包含和不包含APOE位点的两种评分。结果显示，在全样本中未发现评分与任何脑影像指标相关；但在男性中，两种评分均与较小的白质高信号体积、较低的小血管病负担以及额下回三角部、岛盖部和岛叶皮层较厚相关。作者据此提示，长寿遗传倾向可能与男性较低的脑血管负担及部分皮层灰质特征存在联系，但这一关联具有性别特异性，且研究为观察性设计，尚不能说明因果关系。

papers.title: Predicting individual differences in social functioning from functional connectomes in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.authors: Li A, Zhang J, Yu C, Tan L, Yi A, Xiao Y.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by profound heterogeneity in social functioning. While previous studies using group-level comparisons and predefined regions of interest have identified neural correlates of social deficits in ASD, the neural basis of individual differences in social functioning remains unclear. Here, we applied connectome-based predictive modeling to resting-state functional MRI data from 65 children with ASD aged 1.5-8 years (mean age = 4.23 years) to predict individual differences in social functioning assessed by the personal-social subscale of the Griffiths Development Scales (GDS). Results showed that whole-brain functional connectivity significantly predicted personal-social scores. The positive predictive network was dominated by connections within the default mode network, with the left precuneus emerging as a core hub. In contrast, the negative predictive network mainly involved inter-network connections, particularly between the frontoparietal and sensorimotor networks. In an independent cohort of 27 children with ASD aged 1.25-8 years (mean age = 3.31 years), the positive-edge model showed a significant association with personal-social scores, whereas the negative-edge and combined models did not. These findings suggest that intrinsic large-scale brain network organization is associated with individual differences in social functioning in children with ASD, highlighting the potential of network-level approaches for characterizing neurodevelopmental heterogeneity and supporting future precision-oriented research.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注孤独症谱系障碍儿童社会功能的个体差异能否由静息态功能连接预测，采用连接组预测建模分析孤独症儿童的功能磁共振数据，并以格里菲斯发育量表个人-社会分量表评估社会功能。结果显示，全脑功能连接能够显著预测个人-社会得分；正向预测网络以默认网络内部连接为主，左侧楔前叶为核心节点，负向预测网络则主要涉及网络间连接，尤其是额顶网络与感觉运动网络之间。在一个独立的孤独症儿童队列中，仅正向边模型与个人-社会得分显著相关，负向边模型和合并模型均未显示显著关联。作者据此认为，内在大规模脑网络组织与孤独症儿童社会功能的个体差异相关，网络层面的方法有助于刻画神经发育异质性，但相关结果尚不能说明因果关系或临床效用。

papers.title: A comparative study of modified suanzaoren decoction versus estazolam in chronic insomnia disorder: Clinical outcomes and thalamocortical network changes.
papers.authors: Wang R, Han Y, Chen L, Lv D, Yao P, Guo Z, Guo W.
papers.abstract: Chronic insomnia disorder (CID) is associated with widespread abnormalities in thalamic functional connectivity (FC). For CID patients with the yin-deficiency and fire-excess syndrome, Modified Suanzaoren Decoction (MSZRD) and estazolam are common treatments, but their longitudinal associations with thalamic networks remain unclear. This study was a non-randomized, patient-preference controlled trial. Eighty-two CID patients with yin-deficiency and fire-excess syndrome received a 6-week treatment with either MSZRD or estazolam based on preference. Additionally, 54 healthy controls (HCs) were recruited for baseline comparison. Clinical scales, polysomnography, and resting-state fMRI data were collected pre- and post-treatment. Using the Human Brainnetome Atlas, the thalamus was parcellated into eight subregions. We examined baseline group differences and longitudinal FC changes, and identified genes associated with the baseline FC alterations for enrichment analysis. At baseline, CID patients showed significantly increased FC in pathways involving the medial pre-frontal thalamus, posterior parietal thalamus, lateral pre-frontal thalamus, and caudal temporal thalamus with multiple cortical regions. After treatment, the MSZRD group showed greater improvement than the estazolam group on subjective and objective measures. While FC decreased in the MSZRD group between the left occipital thalamus and right middle frontal gyrus, and between the right occipital thalamus and right angular gyrus, it increased in the estazolam group for these connections. Enrichment analysis of genes associated with baseline FC alterations identified pathways related to synaptic organization, cytoskeletal stability, and metabolism. These findings provide preliminary evidence that CID is associated with enhanced thalamocortical connectivity consistent with the thalamus-centric hyperarousal model, and that MSZRD and estazolam show different clinical and neural correlates. However, due to the non-randomized design and baseline FC differences, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in future randomized mechanistic studies.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究比较改良酸枣仁汤与艾司唑仑治疗阴虚火旺型慢性失眠障碍的临床结局及丘脑皮层网络变化，采用非随机、患者偏好对照设计，结合临床量表、多导睡眠监测和静息态功能磁共振，并纳入健康对照作基线比较。基线时患者丘脑多个亚区与皮层区域的功能连接增强，符合以丘脑为中心的高唤醒模型；治疗后改良酸枣仁汤组在主客观指标上改善优于艾司唑仑组，且两药在部分丘脑皮层连接上变化方向相反。作者提示，受非随机设计和基线连接差异限制，结果仅为初步、假设生成性的，尚需随机机制研究验证。

papers.title: Peripheral pathway rerouting shapes whole-brain functional network.
papers.authors: Hu JJ, Xiang YT, Huo BB, Zuo YF, Peng CY, He-Wang, Wu JJ, Zheng MX, Xu JG.
papers.abstract: Pathway rerouting is critical for severe peripheral nerve injury (PNI), which induces widespread neuroplastic alterations within the central nervous system, yet whether different rerouting approaches differentially affect whole-brain functional networks remains unknown. The present study investigated alterations in brain network organization following different peripheral pathway rerouting after PNI. Adult Sprague-Dawley rats underwent complete left brachial plexus transection and were assigned to nerve repair, end-to-end nerve transfer, end-to-side nerve transfer, or untreated PNI groups. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging was acquired 7 months after surgery. Whole-brain functional connectivity matrices were constructed, and graph theoretical analysis was performed to assess global and nodal network properties, including global efficiency, nodal efficiency, and small-world characteristics. Rich-club, feeder, and local connections were further analyzed to characterize patterns of network reorganization. The results revealed significant differences in global efficiency, nodal efficiency, small-world organization and feeder connection among the four groups. Compared with the other reconstruction procedures, end-to-end nerve transfer showed reduced global efficiency, impaired small-world organization, lower nodal efficiency in subcortical regions, and increased functional connectivity and feeder connections, indicating reduced efficiency of large-scale information processing. In contrast, end-to-side nerve transfer preserved global efficiency, nodal efficiency, and small-world properties to a greater extent and was accompanied by more extensive increases in functional connectivity. These findings suggest that end-to-end nerve transfer appears to have a negative effect on the order of the whole-brain network, whereas end-to-side nerve transfer better preserves and restores network stability.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注严重周围神经损伤后不同神经通路改道方式是否会对全脑功能网络产生不同影响。作者在大鼠左侧臂丛完全切断模型上比较了神经修复、端端神经转位、端侧神经转位与未处理损伤组的静息态功能连接和网络拓扑属性。结果显示，端端转位组整体效率、小世界组织和皮层下节点效率下降，功能连接及馈送连接增多，提示大规模信息处理效率降低；端侧转位则较大程度保留了整体效率、节点效率和小世界特性，并伴随更广泛的功能连接增强。作者据此认为，端端转位可能不利于全脑网络秩序，而端侧转位更有利于维持和恢复网络稳定性，但结论来自动物模型，尚需进一步验证。

papers.title: Rightward saccades distort the scaffold of spatial working memory in ADHD.
papers.authors: Moussaoui S, Frost A, Niemeier M.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is typically characterized by executive dysfunction, yet emerging evidence points to spatially asymmetrical features of cognition.
