We examined whether transsaccadic working memory (tWM), the mechanism that integrates visual and motor signals across eye movements, shows directional vulnerability in ADHD. Participants with ADHD completed a spatial tWM task in which memory arrays (one or three items) were presented before leftward, rightward, or fixation trials, and repositioned a probe to the remembered target location. For comparison, data from a previously tested neurotypical sample were included in group-level analyses. Errors were decomposed into systematic and unsystematic components. Compared to controls, ADHD participants showed a modest but reliable rightward-saccade disadvantage, with greater systematic distortions after rightward than leftward eye movements. Saccades disrupted working memory in both groups, but the typical load-dependent increase in unsystematic error observed in neurotypical participants was absent in ADHD. Two complementary interpretations may account for this asymmetry. The integration-imbalance hypothesis attributes it to weakened right-hemisphere contributions to spatial working memory, which impair integration of left-hemisphere oculomotor and right-hemisphere spatial signals during rightward saccades. Alternatively, the anchoring-disruption hypothesis suggests that rightward eye movements destabilize the spatial scaffold anchoring remembered locations, producing geometric distortions without increased error. Together, these findings identify a direction-specific fragility of visuomotor-cognitive coupling in ADHD not explained by general capacity limits. More broadly, they reveal a partial neglect-like pattern of transsaccadic vulnerability: selective impairment for rightward saccades without a left-field deficit, highlighting the utility of oculomotor paradigms for revealing hidden spatial asymmetries in neurocognitive function.

papers.title: A brainstem module for backward locomotion reveals direction-selective premotor circuits.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Lu L, Di R, Cui Y, Liu Y, Ren Q, Dai R, Wu W, Wang R, Luo M.
papers.abstract: Smooth locomotion requires precise directional control, yet the neural circuits governing navigational transitions remain elusive. Here, we identify the pontine backward locomotion center (PBLC) as a key brainstem node for backward locomotion in mice. PBLC glutamatergic neurons are preferentially recruited during backward locomotion; their activation elicits robust backward walking with naturalistic gait features, whereas their inhibition suppresses backward movement across multiple behavioral contexts. PBLC neurons send ascending projections to the peri-fasciculus retroflexus and descending projections to the paramedian reticular nucleus (PMn). Activating spinal-projecting PMn glutamatergic neurons evokes backward locomotion, whereas PMn ablation suppresses PBLC-evoked backward movement. The PBLC lies within an anteroposteriorly organized set of brainstem regions that includes the cuneiform nucleus, ventral laterodorsal tegmental nucleus, and lateral parabrachial nucleus, associated with forward locomotion, ipsilateral turning, and locomotor arrest, respectively. Together, these findings define a supraspinal circuit for backward locomotion and reveal neighboring brainstem modules associated with distinct locomotor actions.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在小鼠中寻找控制后退行走的脑干环路，并识别出脑桥后退运动中心（PBLC）这一关键节点。PBLC的谷氨酸能神经元在后退时优先被招募，激活它们可诱发步态自然的后退行走，而抑制它们则在多种行为情境下削弱后退运动。PBLC通过上行投射到后屈束周围区、下行投射到旁正中网状核（PMn）组织环路，激活向脊髓投射的PMn谷氨酸能神经元同样能诱发后退，损毁PMn则阻断PBLC激活所诱发的后退。作者进一步指出，PBLC与楔形核、腹侧被盖背外侧核及外侧臂旁核等邻近脑干模块相邻，这些模块分别与前进、同侧转向和运动停止相关，从而勾勒出一套方向选择性的超脊髓运动控制架构。

papers.title: Achieving detailed medial temporal lobe segmentation with upsampled isotropic training from implicit neural representation.
papers.authors: Li Y, Khandelwal P, Jena R, Xie L, Duong MT, Denning AE, Brown CA, Wisse LEM, Das SR, Wolk DA, Yushkevich PA.
papers.abstract: Imaging biomarkers in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are important tools for diagnosing, tracking and treating Alzheimer's disease (AD). Neurofibrillary tau pathology in AD is closely linked to neurodegeneration and generally follows a pattern of spread in the brain, with early stages involving subregions of the medial temporal lobe (MTL). Accurate segmentation of MTL subregions is needed to extract granular biomarkers of AD progression. MTL subregions are often imaged using T2-weighted (T2w) MRI scans that are highly anisotropic due to constraints of MRI physics and image acquisition, making it difficult to reliably model MTL subregions geometrically and extract morphological measures, such as thickness. In this study, we propose a segmentation framework for MTL subregions in isotropic space, in which an implicit neural representation is used to construct the isotropic training atlas from the anisotropic low-resolution T2w data, with T1w MRI as an auxiliary modality to support the INR and segmentation. In an independent test set, the morphological measures extracted using this isotropic model showed stronger effect sizes than those from models trained on anisotropic data in distinguishing participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from cognitively unimpaired individuals. In the test-retest analysis, the morphological measures extracted using the isotropic model showed greater stability than those from the anisotropic segmentation. This study demonstrates improved reliability of MRI-derived MTL subregion biomarkers without additional atlas annotation effort, which may more accurately quantify and track the relationship between AD pathology and brain atrophy for monitoring disease progression.

papers.title: From gut microbiome to aging brain: Butyrate as a neurogeroscience effector.
papers.authors: Mitrea L, Calinoiu LF, Martau GA, Teleky BE, Cocean AM, Odocheanu R, Stefanescu BE, Vodnar DC.
papers.abstract: Aging-related cognitive decline is increasingly linked to disruption of the microbiome-gut-brain axis, in which age-associated dysbiosis progressively reduces butyrate production, a short-chain fatty acid and central neuroactive metabolite generated by bacterial fermentation of dietary fiber. Experimental studies indicate that butyrate can influence multiple processes relevant to brain aging, including histone deacetylase activity, neuroinflammatory signaling, microglial phenotypes, blood-brain barrier integrity, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis. Through these mechanisms, butyrate may modulate several molecular and cellular processes involved in brain aging, although evidence for direct causal effects in the human brain remains limited. Preclinical studies report neuroprotective effects across several models of aging and neurological disease; however, direct evidence in humans remains limited and largely associative or indirect. Therefore, this review critically synthesizes current evidence on microbiome-derived butyrate in brain aging, encompassing its microbial production and age-related alterations, molecular and cellular mechanisms, associations with neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric conditions, and emerging strategies for therapeutic modulation and delivery. It examines emerging biotechnological strategies - including prodrug design, nanoparticle- and liposomal-based delivery systems, gut-targeted formulations, and microbiome engineering - all developed to overcome the blood-brain barrier and restore therapeutically relevant butyrate concentrations in the aging brain. By bridging fundamental microbiome biology and translational neuroscience, this review positions butyrate as a mechanistically grounded neurogeroscience effector and charts a roadmap for its application in promoting brain health across the aging continuum.

papers.title: Longitudinal associations of screen time with brain development and expressive language skills in early childhood.
papers.authors: Choi EJ, Nichols ES, Tomfohr-Madsen L, Giesbrecht GF, Manning KY, Lebel CA, Duerden EG.
papers.abstract: Screen-based media may reduce reciprocal social interactions that support expressive language development, but little is known about how early language abilities, later screen use, and brain structure are related during toddlerhood. We examined 70 toddlers with structural magnetic resonance imaging and standardized developmental assessments at age 2, along with parent-reported screen time at ages 2 and 3. Greater weekday and weekend screen time at age 2 were associated with poorer concurrent expressive language skills. Right pars triangularis volume did not explain additional variance in these cross-sectional associations. Longitudinally, right pars triangularis volume moderated the association between expressive language skills at age 2 and screen time at age 3. Among toddlers with relatively smaller right pars triangularis volumes, poorer expressive language skills were associated with greater subsequent weekday and weekend screen time. These findings support guidance to limit screen use during toddlerhood, a sensitive window for language and brain development.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注幼儿期屏幕使用、脑结构与表达性语言能力之间的关系，对幼儿在2岁时进行结构磁共振成像和标准化发育评估，并收集2岁和3岁时的家长报告屏幕时间。结果发现，2岁时工作日和周末屏幕时间较多与同期表达性语言能力较差相关，而右侧三角部体积并未解释这一横断面关联的额外变异。纵向来看，右侧三角部体积调节了2岁表达性语言能力与3岁屏幕时间之间的关联：在右侧三角部体积相对较小的幼儿中，2岁语言能力较差者随后工作日和周末屏幕时间更多。作者据此支持限制幼儿期屏幕使用的建议，并强调这是语言和脑发育的敏感窗口；但上述关联为观察性结果，不能直接推断屏幕使用导致语言或脑结构变化。

papers.title: Cortical substrates of perceptual confusion between pitch and timbre.
papers.authors: Ou Y, Allen EJ, Kay KN, Oxenham AJ.
papers.abstract: Pitch and timbre, two fundamental perceptual attributes of sound, are critical for both speech and music. Although governed by different acoustic parameters, pitch, and brightness (one of the primary dimensions of timbre) can be perceptually confused. Here, we identify potential neural substrates of this well-known illusion by independently manipulating pitch and brightness while measuring fMRI responses. First, we show that the preferred pitch of individual voxels within auditory cortex decreases systematically as stimulus brightness increases, and vice versa , consistent with predictions from perceptual confusion. Second, we demonstrate that pitch and brightness share a common tuning gradient across auditory cortex, implying a shared trajectory of cortical activation for changes in each dimension. The pattern of results at both local and global cortical levels are consistent with the principle of efficient coding, with the brain exploiting correlations between pitch and brightness in natural sounds via a shared neural code.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注音高与音色（以明亮度为主要维度）在知觉上相互混淆这一现象，试图找出其背后的皮层基础。作者用fMRI独立操纵音高与明亮度，发现听觉皮层中单个体素的偏好音高会随刺激明亮度升高而系统性降低，反之亦然，与知觉混淆的预期一致；同时两者在听觉皮层上共享同一条调谐梯度，提示两个维度沿共同的皮层激活轨迹变化。作者认为，局部与整体层面的结果都符合高效编码原则，即大脑利用自然声音中音高与明亮度的相关性，以共享的神经编码加以表征。

papers.title: Diffusion MRI processing in the HEALthy Brain and Child Development study: Innovations and applications.
papers.authors: Cieslak M, Irfanoglu MO, Meisler SL, Salo T, Raikes AC, Cook PA, Chung AW, Lee EG, Li R, Li X, Pecheva D, Fair DA, Smyser CD, Harms MP, Landman BA, Wisnowski JL, Huang H, Alexander AL, Satterthwaite TD.
papers.abstract: The landmark ongoing HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) study will longitudinally chart brain development in a large sample (projected n = 7200) of infants through age 10 years with multimodal neuroimaging that includes an advanced diffusion MRI (dMRI) acquisition. Here, we detail advances in dMRI image processing developed for HBCD, incorporated into the widely used QSIPrep pipeline. Major changes to preprocessing include improvements in infant brain extraction, distortion correction, and normalization to infant-specific templates. Additionally, we describe a new software package - QSIRecon - that yields rich derived data including diverse maps of tissue microstructure as well as person-specific white matter bundles. Using dMRI data from a subset of the HBCD 1.0 release where age information was available (n = 529 sessions across two time points), we observe critical improvements in data quality with preprocessing and see expected developmental patterns. Moving forward, the publicly-available data from HBCD will rapidly grow to become the largest study of brain development in infancy and early childhood using dMRI. QSIPrep and QSIRecon are openly available and can be applied to other infant and pediatric dMRI datasets.

papers.title: Mucoromycotina fine root endophyte engages in a nutritionally mutualistic symbiosis with Arabidopsis thaliana.
papers.authors: Prout J, Burgess J, Williams A, Morales V, Pressel S, Ton J, Field KJ.
papers.abstract: Arabidopsis thaliana, a widely used genetic model species, is considered incapable of forming mycorrhizal associations, which support nutrient acquisition in most other land plants. Mucoromycotina "fine root endophytes" (MFREs) are a recently characterized group of mycorrhizal fungi capable of forming nutritional mutualisms with a wide range of plants, supplying nitrogen and phosphorus to host plants and gaining access to photosynthetically derived carbon. Here, we demonstrate that a wild-isolated MFRE strain, Lyc-1, successfully colonizes Arabidopsis roots under monoaxenic conditions without affecting plant growth. Using a combination of conventional light and epifluorescence microscopy, we demonstrate extensive extra- and intraradical colonization of the root cortex. Stable- and radio-isotope tracing further revealed bidirectional nutrient exchange between the host plant and the fungus. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a functional, mycorrhiza-like nutritional mutualism in Arabidopsis. As Arabidopsis lacks a complete set of common symbiosis signaling pathway genes, our findings suggest that Arabidopsis-Lyc-1 symbiosis may be controlled by an alternative, so far uncharacterized, symbiotic pathway. Thus, our study not only supports the existence of multiple evolutionary routes to plant-fungal nutritional mutualisms but also establishes Arabidopsis as a genetically tractable model to study plant-fungal symbiosis, thereby opening new opportunities to dissect the molecular basis and evolution of mycorrhizal symbioses.

papers.title: Neural coordination of wing and leg movements during a terrestrial threat display.
papers.authors: Cao S, Anderson DJ.
papers.abstract: In most flying species, legs and wings mediate earthbound vs. aerial locomotion, respectively. During terrestrial social displays such as threat or courtship, however, species-typical movements of these appendages are coordinated in a stereotyped manner. How such appendicular control is integrated is poorly understood. Threat behavior in Drosophila consists of four types of leg and wing actions, which can be performed singly or in combination. Using a large-scale functional screen, we previously identified a cluster of 4-5 AIP (CL062) neurons whose optogenetic activation can evoke all threat actions and which are essential for natural threat displays. To understand how this threat command module functions, we have mapped AIP neurons into the male fly connectome and identified split-GAL4 drivers for four major downstream targets, whose functional connectivity and behavioral roles we have tested. Surprisingly, we find that distinct threat-specific actions are not controlled by parallel connections from different subsets of AIP cells to different action-specific descending neurons (DNs), a parsimonious circuit architecture. Rather, AIP neurons collectively activate two parallel downstream modules comprising pairs of neurons that control wing vs. leg movements, respectively. Wing movements are controlled via direct projections to two specialist DNs that act synergistically, while leg movements are controlled indirectly via two interneurons that act antagonistically to pattern the activity of multiple DNs, which are likely used in other locomotor contexts. These data elucidate a hierarchical circuit for appendicular coordination during a terrestrial social display and provide insight into how the brain has repurposed appendage-specific locomotor control for social communication, a form of exaptation.

papers.title: The legible body and the language of cognition.
papers.authors: Mainen ZF.
papers.abstract: Neural activity moves the body to act on the world, and the world returns through the body to shape neural activity. Systems neuroscience built tasks to cut this loop, isolating low-dimensional, task-related signals and discarding the rest. Tasks suited cognition as classically conceived: general-purpose machinery between sensation and action, performing latent computations abstracted from specific behaviors. With recording techniques limited to tracking individual neurons and discrete actions, it took tasks to make cognition legible by supplying meaning within a limited but generalizable frame. That constraint has been lifting: brain-wide neural recording and rich video tracking of the body can now read neurons and behavior as two facets of one dynamical system. Together they reveal cognitive primitives - decision variables, expected values, hidden states - distributed not only in brain activity but also in subtle face and body movements long dismissed as noise. Cognition, it turns out, is not confined to higher-order cortex; it surfaces in incidental movements carrying latent variables the brain computes - even ones it never acts on. It keeps its hold on the body, as emotion keeps its expressions. Backed by normative theories, noninvasive video recordings can divulge not only the syntax of behavior but also its semantics, opening the study of cognition in the wild beyond tasks. The potential is perhaps greatest in our own species, where the promise of reading the mind noninvasively - to treat and to understand - is mirrored by the threat of laying it bare.
papers.summary_zh: 该文是一篇观点性文章，讨论系统神经科学如何通过任务设计让认知变得“可读”，以及这一限制正在如何被打破。作者指出，以往研究用任务隔离与认知相关的低维信号、舍弃其余活动，从而在有限框架内赋予认知意义；而全脑记录与对身体运动的丰富视频追踪，正把神经活动和行为视为同一动力系统的两个方面。由此，决策变量、期望值、隐藏状态等认知基元不仅分布于脑活动，也体现在曾被当作噪声的细微面部和身体动作中，说明认知并不局限于高级皮层。作者进一步提出，在规范性理论支持下，无创视频记录有望同时揭示行为的语法与语义，把认知研究拓展到任务之外的真实情境，并提醒这种“读心”能力在治疗与理解之外也伴随暴露风险。

papers.title: Cross-cohort transfer of clinical Alzheimer's EEG signatures to cognitively healthy APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 risk carriers using differentiable logic gate networks.
papers.authors: Dharia SY, Valderrama CE, Smith SD.
papers.abstract: Neural alterations associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) may emerge years before clinical diagnosis, and genetic risk factors such as APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 may identify individuals vulnerable to these shifts. We tested whether electroencephalography (EEG) signatures learned from clinically diagnosed AD patients transfer to cognitively healthy middle-aged adults carrying these variants. Differentiable logic gate networks (Diff-Logic) and neural baselines were trained on log-relative power spectral density features from a clinical cohort of AD patients and cognitively normal (CN) controls. These models were then applied without retraining to an independent genetic-risk cohort of neutral-risk non-carriers (N), APOE-ε4-only carriers (A+P-), and dual APOE-ε4/PICALM G-allele carriers (A+P+), yielding a continuous AD-like EEG signature score per participant. Diff-Logic matched neural baselines in clinical classification (balanced accuracy 0.809±0.028; AUROC 0.845±0.023) while enabling edge inference with a 7.4× model-size reduction and 0.22 ms model-only latency on a 7 W single-core CPU. In the genetic-risk cohort, scores were highest in A+P+ participants (0.393±0.167) relative to N (0.296±0.154) and A+P- (0.285±0.143; subject-level mean ± SD). This elevation was nominally significant before correction (A+P+ vs. A+P-, punc =0.036) but did not survive Holm correction (pHolm =0.109), and the cohort carried no AD pathology or conversion ground truth; the association was therefore exploratory. Integrated gradients attribution of the trained model showed genetic-risk relevance in delta, theta, and alpha, partially overlapping clinical AD topography. These findings support the feasibility of zero-shot EEG transfer in genetically at-risk individuals and highlight the need for replication in larger cohorts. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/Shyamal-Dharia/ad-difflogic-transfer.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究检验从临床确诊阿尔茨海默病患者学到的脑电特征能否不经重训练迁移到携带APOE-ε4和PICALM rs3851179风险变异的认知健康中年成人。作者用可微逻辑门网络和神经基线模型基于功率谱密度特征进行分类，再将其零样本应用于独立遗传风险队列，得到每人的类AD脑电评分。结果显示，双重携带者的评分相对最高，但该差异在多重校正后不显著，且该队列缺乏AD病理或转化金标准，因此作者将关联定位为探索性，并强调需在更大队列中重复验证。

papers.title: Caffeine Consumption and Adolescent Mental Health: The Role of Sleep and Brain Structure.
papers.authors: Zheng J, Rakesh D.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Background Caffeine is a widely consumed psychoactive substance, with use beginning during adolescence, a sensitive period of neurodevelopment. Despite its widespread, unregulated use, links between caffeine consumption and adolescent brain structure and mental health remain poorly understood. Methods We examined the association between caffeine intake and brain structure in 9632 adolescents aged 9-11 years. Caffeine consumption (intake of coffee, tea and soft drinks) and mental health were assessed via self-report. Cortical thickness and surface area were derived from structural MRI scans. Linear mixed-effects models tested associations between caffeine intake and brain measures. Structural equation modeling was used to test whether sleep duration and brain structure mediated the association between caffeine intake and mental health outcomes assessed at the 6-month and 18-month follow-up. Results Higher total caffeine intake was associated with lower total cortical surface area (B=-0.03,SE=0.01,p=.001) and lower surface area in 22 regions across four lobes, driven largely by soft drink consumption, with some additional associations emerging for coffee and espresso intake with cortical thickness. All associations were evident at consumption levels as low as one cup per week. Shorter sleep duration and lower surface area sequentially mediated the association between higher caffeine intake and greater mental health problems in the future. Conclusion Findings highlight the need for evidence-based guidelines on adolescent caffeine consumption to support neurodevelopment and mental health.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于近万名9至11岁青少年的自我报告咖啡因摄入量、结构磁共振脑影像及随访心理健康数据，考察咖啡因摄入与青少年脑结构和心理健康之间的关联，并用中介模型检验睡眠时长与脑结构的作用。结果显示，咖啡因摄入越多，皮层总表面积及多个脑区表面积越小，这一关联主要来自软饮料，咖啡和浓缩咖啡摄入还与皮层厚度存在部分关联，且每周一杯的低摄入水平即可观察到。更重要的是，较短睡眠时长与较小皮层表面积依次中介了较高咖啡因摄入与日后更多心理健康问题之间的关联。作者据此强调，需要为青少年咖啡因消费制定循证指南，以支持其神经发育和心理健康；但该研究为观察性关联，尚不能确立因果。

papers.title: Air-jet Pneumodissection in Neuroanatomy: a new method for the study of White Matter anatomy in the Human Brain.
papers.authors: Marrone S, Scalia G, De Notaris M, Corrivetti F, Umana GE.
papers.abstract: Traditional white matter (WM) dissection techniques, such as the Klingler method, employ wooden or metal instruments that may cause myelin wear and limit fine anatomical separation. Inspired by clinical water-jet applications, we investigated the feasibility of an air-jet dissector (pneumodissection) for WM dissection, leveraging the Coandă effect to gently separate contiguous fiber tracts while preserving their integrity. A portable air compressor was modified with an extended tube and an 18G blunt needle tip. A left cerebral hemisphere, prepared according to a modified Klingler freeze-thaw protocol, was dissected under exoscope magnification. Airflow was delivered at pressures between 0.8 and 3 bar. Dissection followed Klingler's stepwise protocol, adapted to the ergonomics and dynamics of the air-jet device. The air-jet dissector enabled progressive detachment of pia-arachnoid membranes, cortex and U-fibers, with clear exposure of commissural, projection, and association bundles. Low-pressure flow (0.8-1.2 bar) was used for delicate superficial planes and U-shaped fibers, whereas transient increases up to 3 bar were used for more resistant cortical or deep tissue planes. During this feasibility experiment, the air jet reduced broad direct instrument-tissue contact and helped clear loose debris and surface fluid from the operative field. Vessel-fiber interfaces and anatomical cleavage planes were sharply delineated. The device's portability and pressure modulation allowed both blunt and sharp dissection functions through a single tool. Air-jet dissection is a novel and complementary technique for white matter study. The present study does not establish superiority or reduced tissue damage compared with conventional manual tools because no matched quantitative comparison or histological assessment was performed. Further replicated and standardized studies are required to define reproducibility, tissue effects, and any objective advantage over established dissection methods.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探索能否用喷气分离装置（气动分离）替代传统木质或金属器械进行人脑白质解剖，装置由改装便携空压机、延长管和钝针头组成，利用柯恩达效应在显微镜下按Klingler流程逐步分离纤维束。可行性实验显示，气流能渐进剥离软脑膜-蛛网膜、皮层和U形纤维，清晰暴露连合、投射和联络纤维束，低压用于浅表精细层面、短时升压用于较坚韧的皮层或深部层面，并可减少器械与组织的直接接触、清除碎屑和表面液体，使血管-纤维界面和解剖分离面更清晰。作者强调这只是新型辅助技术，未做配对定量比较或组织学评估，因此不能说明其优于传统手工器械或能减少组织损伤，可重复性、组织效应和客观优势仍需后续标准化研究确认。

papers.title: Longitudinal motor recovery trajectories in brainstem glioma associated with preoperative DTI-based corticospinal tract involvement patterns.
papers.authors: Zhang M, Xie L, Zhou H, Jiang K, Jiang Z, Wu W, Sun T, Wang L, Wu Z, Zhang J, Zhang P, Zhang L.
papers.abstract: Purpose Despite the high risk of postoperative motor dysfunction from corticospinal tract (CST) involvement, no preoperative system integrates CST-tumor interactions to stratify the prognosis in brainstem gliomas (BSGs). Methods We enrolled 180 BSG patients who underwent craniotomy between 2020 and 2023. Preoperative DTI tractography classified CST-tumor relationships as displacement, infiltration, and traverse types. Clinical, pathological, and follow-up data (KPS, mRS, MRC, OS) were systematically collected at predefined intervals. Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models; survival was assessed by Kaplan-Meier. Results The cohort comprised 51 displacement (28.3%), 83 infiltration (46.1%), and 46 traverse (25.6%) cases, with excellent inter-rater reliability (κ = 0.93). Tumor biology, CST fractional anisotropy (FA), and preoperative functional status demonstrated clear gradients across subtypes. The traverse type was predominantly high-grade (97.8%), exhibited the lowest FA (0.424 ± 0.055), and had the poorest preoperative KPS/mRS (all P < 0.001). Conversely, the displacement type was mostly low-grade (74.5%), showed the highest FA (0.45 ± 0.038), and had superior functional status; infiltration was intermediate. FA correlated positively with preoperative muscle strength (ρ = 0.238, P = 0.001). Longitudinal trajectories differed significantly (P_FDR < 0.05): displacement patients recovered rapidly, traverse patients showed minimal recovery with late decline, and infiltration was intermediate. Median OS was not reached for displacement, versus 15.3 months for infiltration and 12.0 months for traverse; all pairwise comparisons were significant. Conclusion This DTI-based CST-tumor classification system effectively stratifies BSG patients preoperatively and is associated with distinct recovery trajectories, providing a hypothesis-generating framework for surgical planning.

papers.title: Improved diffusion tensor parametric maps in the brain from reduced-direction acquisitions using a deep learning approach.
papers.authors: Tucksinapinunchai N, Boonsuth R, Rodkong A, Saokhieo P, Peragine DE, Skorska MN, Thurston LT, Hu DZ, Supindham T, Kaewthip O, Wantanajittikul K, Saekho S, Chariyalertsak S, Angkurawaranon S, VanderLaan DP, Yarach U.
papers.abstract: Objectives This study implements and evaluates a deep learning approach to enhance FA, MD, AD, and RD maps derived from 16-direction DTI to approximate corresponding maps derived from 32-direction DTI, with the aim of reducing acquisition time while maintaining quantitative accuracy. Materials and methods A modified 8-layer 3D convolutional neural network was trained using scalar DTI-derived maps from 16-direction acquisitions as input and corresponding 32-direction maps as reference targets. Model performance was evaluated on an independently acquired evaluation cohort (n=33) using PSNR, %NRMSE, SSIM, Bland-Altman analysis, and tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS), with BM4D and AONLM as comparators. Results The DL model reduced noise and improved PSNR, %NRMSE, and SSIM compared with raw ND16, BM4D, and AONLM (p < 0.05). DL-derived FA, MD, and AD showed the smallest deviations from the ND32 reference among the evaluated methods, although statistically significant mean differences remained. TBSS showed localized differences for FA and AD, but no significant differences for MD or RD (p > 0.05). Discussion The proposed map-domain DL approach improved scalar DTI-derived maps from 16-direction acquisitions while reducing diffusion acquisition time by approximately 1.8-fold. The findings demonstrate improved agreement with 32-direction reference maps, while remaining quantitative differences and generalizability require further validation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究开发并评估了一种深度学习方法，用16方向扩散张量成像（DTI）数据生成FA、MD、AD和RD参数图，使其接近32方向采集的结果，目的是在保持定量准确性的同时缩短采集时间。模型以16方向导出的标量图为输入、对应的32方向图为参考进行训练，并在独立队列中与原始16方向图及两种去噪方法比较。结果显示，深度学习方法降低了噪声，在多项图像质量指标上优于对照，生成的FA、MD和AD与32方向参考的偏差也较小，但平均差异仍具统计学显著性；基于纤维束的空间统计仅在FA和AD上发现局部差异，MD和RD未见显著差异。作者认为，这种在图域进行的深度学习处理可在约缩短1.8倍采集时间的情况下改善16方向DTI参数图，但与32方向参考图之间仍存在定量差异，其泛化性也需进一步验证。

papers.title: Impact of sedation on the reliability of magnetoencephalographic language mapping in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.authors: Song T, Song RR, Bodden C, Deleon R, Cordova J, Huang M, Calley C.
papers.abstract: Objective Magnetoencephalography (MEG) language mapping in pediatric epilepsy frequently requires sedation, which may alter cortical physiology and compromise the reliability of language lateralization. We hypothesized that sedation disrupts coupling between early auditory processing and higher order language networks, reducing the interpretability of laterality metrics. Methods Sixty-nine pediatric patients undergoing presurgical MEG evaluation were analyzed, including 32 nonsedated and 37 sedated participants. Auditory evoked field responses were quantified using the M200/M100 amplitude ratio and interhemispheric asymmetry. Language laterality indices (LIs) were derived from a continuous recognition memory paradigm, and source localization was performed using Fast-VESTAL. Results Sedation preferentially suppressed late auditory responses, reflected by a significant reduction in the M200/M100 ratio (p < .001) and increased interindividual variability. Despite preserved early sensory responses, auditory-language coupling was numerically attenuated under sedation. Notably, low M200/M100 ratios were frequently associated with highly lateralized LI values, suggesting reduced physiological reliability and the potential for "false certainty" in language lateralization. Source imaging demonstrated preserved primary auditory cortical activity with reduced recruitment of higher order association networks in sedated participants. Significance Sedation compromises the physiological reliability of MEG language lateralization by disrupting late auditory and association-level processing. The M200/M100 ratio provides a practical physiological marker for identifying cases in which laterality results should be interpreted with caution. These findings support a physiology-informed framework for improving the clinical interpretation of MEG language mapping in sedated pediatric patients, with direct implications for presurgical planning in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注镇静是否会影响儿童癫痫术前脑磁图语言定位的可靠性，比较了镇静与非镇静患儿在听觉诱发反应和语言偏侧化指标上的差异。结果显示，镇静主要压制较晚的听觉反应，使M200/M100比值降低且个体差异增大，同时高级联合网络参与减少；低比值常伴随高度偏侧化的语言指数，提示这种偏侧化可能并不反映可靠的生理状态。作者据此提出，M200/M100比值可作为识别需谨慎解读偏侧化结果的实用生理标记，以改进镇静患儿脑磁图语言定位的临床解释。

papers.title: Extensive Parenchymal Brain Calcification in a Patient With Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease and Stage 5 Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.authors: Khan N, Streicher N.
papers.abstract: Extensive parenchymal brain calcification is uncommon in chronic kidney disease (CKD): intracranial vascular calcification affects up to 10% of uremic patients, but widespread Fahr-type parenchymal deposits are rare and, where reported, have occurred in patients with a coexisting hypoparathyroid or parathyroid-hormone (PTH)-resistant state. We describe a man in his 50s with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) and Stage 5 CKD who presented with word-finding difficulty, gait imbalance, and myoclonus and was found to have extensive symmetric calcification of the basal ganglia, thalami, dentate nuclei, and subcortical white matter. He carried an unverified childhood diagnosis of pseudohypoparathyroidism made at age 13. At presentation, total calcium was 6.1-6.3 mg/dL, phosphate 5.8 mg/dL, intact PTH 194 pg/mL, creatinine 6.21 mg/dL, and alkaline phosphatase normal. Over the following 10 months, intact PTH fell rather than rose, reaching 56 pg/mL during treatment with calcium, calcitriol, sevelamer, and hemodialysis, all of which lower PTH whatever the underlying cause. The calcium-phosphate product was low at presentation (36.5 mg2 /dL2 ) but rose to 58-62 mg2 /dL2 later, and single values cannot exclude earlier CKD-related mineral abnormality. No pathogenic variant was identified on an 866-gene panel. Neither the product nor the PTH trajectory separated renal from non-renal contributions. We present this as a diagnostic-reasoning case that raises, but cannot resolve, the question of causation and suggest that such calcification should not be attributed to CKD-mineral and bone disorder by default.
papers.summary_zh: 本文报告一例患常染色体显性多囊肾病并处于5期慢性肾脏病的五十多岁男性，因找词困难、步态不稳和肌阵挛就诊，影像发现基底节、丘脑、齿状核及皮层下白质广泛对称钙化。作者结合其童年疑似假性甲状旁腺功能减退的诊断及钙磷、甲状旁腺激素等指标变化进行诊断推理，但指出这些指标无法区分肾脏与非肾脏因素对钙化的贡献，基因panel也未检出致病变异。文章因此提出，此类广泛脑实质钙化不应默认归因于慢性肾脏病相关矿物质与骨异常，其因果关系仍待明确。

papers.title: Cross-state stability and maturational similarity of the social brain connectome in children and adolescents
papers.authors: Lee J, Eilbott J, Kelly C, Todd R, Vanderwal T.
papers.abstract: The intra-individual stability of functional connectivity (FC) across two or more scans and the inter-individual similarity of FC patterns relative to peers capture developmental variability in functional brain organization. Despite their different referents, these measures are strongly coupled at the whole brain level; however, it remains unclear whether this relationship emerges in development, whether it extends to the social brain, and whether it differs by sex. Based on the importance of social development in this age range, we hypothesized that known developmental relationships and sex-specific effects would be more pronounced in the social brain relative to the whole brain. Using a large psychiatrically enriched sample of 769 youth ages 6-21 (female N = 327, mean age = 12.27 years), we computed FC during rest and movie-watching scans and quantified stability across scans as well as similarity to mature subjects (n=36) within each condition. We then tested whether sex-dependent age relationships were captured by these measures or by the strength of their coupling. Our results showed that cross-state stability and maturational similarity are strongly coupled in development, and that this coupling is enhanced in the social brain relative to the whole brain. Furthermore, the strength of stability-similarity coupling increased as a function of age in females, while males showed the opposite effect. When assessing relationships between age and each FC measure independently, no individual effects were significant after FDR correction. However, our multivariate age-prediction models fared much better, demonstrating that edgewise stability and maturational similarity measures can capture spatially heterogeneous developmental effects that are lost when collapsing across edges. Together, these results support the emerging idea that the degree of FC stability across scans is related to how closely an individual’s functional architecture aligns to a shared template. Here, we newly show that this stability-similarity coupling is stronger in the social brain and varies with age in sex-specific ways. Future longitudinal work is needed to establish whether these cross-sectional relationships also characterize within-person developmental change.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注儿童青少年社会脑功能连接组在跨扫描状态下的稳定性与向成熟模式趋近的相似性之间的关系，并检验这种关系是否随年龄和性别变化。研究基于大样本青少年在静息和观影条件下的功能连接，计算个体跨状态稳定性及其与成熟被试的相似性。结果显示，稳定性与成熟相似性在发育中紧密耦合，且社会脑中的耦合强于全脑；女性中这种耦合随年龄增强，男性则相反。逐边分析未发现各指标与年龄的独立关联，但多变量模型能捕捉空间异质的发育效应。作者据此提出，功能连接的跨扫描稳定性与个体功能架构接近共享模板的程度相关，并强调需纵向研究验证这些横断面关系是否反映个体内发育变化。

papers.title: Virtual Brain Modelling Reveals Altered Network Dynamics and Predicts Symptom Severity in Schizophrenia: Relevance to Antipsychotic Treatment Response and Resistance
papers.authors: Vitacca M, Pischedda D, Ciccarelli M, Pontillo G, De Simone G, Cocozza S, Ćipranić F, Monteverdi A, Fusar-Poli P, Gandini Wheeler-Kingshott CAM, Palesi F, de Bartolomeis A, D’Angelo E.
papers.abstract: Background Schizophrenia (SZ) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by positive, negative, cognitive and disorganisation symptoms, with pleomorphic phenotype and poorly understood aetiology. Dopamine dysregulation represents the most replicated in vivo pathophysiology finding. However, accumulating evidence suggests altered large-scale brain connectivity and excitation/inhibition balance disruption. While quantifying these alterations would help clarify SZ neurophysiology and guide therapy, single-patient identification remains impractical. This is particularly relevant for treatment-resistant SZ (TRS) whose pathophysiology remains unclear. Methods Using virtual brain modelling, we simulated large-scale brain dynamics from functional and structural MRI data in 43 healthy controls and 33 SZ patients, stratified into TRS and non-TRS. We used the Wong-Wang model to derive four network parameters reflecting GABAergic and NMDA receptor-mediated glutamatergic transmission: global coupling (G), local inhibitory (J i ) and excitatory (J NMDA ) coupling, and recurrent excitation (w + ). We performed simulations in the whole brain and in resting-state networks, compared model parameters between groups and tested their association with Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) scores. Results Compared to non-TRS, TRS patients showed increased J NMDA and decreased w + at the whole-brain level, increased J NMDA and G in the dorsal attention network, lower G in the limbic network and increased w + in the visual network. Moreover, J i in the default mode network predicted negative symptom severity while J NMDA in the limbic and ventral attention networks predicted total PANSS scores and disorganisation. Conclusions These findings suggest that TRS is characterized by network-specific alterations in excitation/inhibition profiles and support the use of personalised multiscale modelling to identify symptom biomarkers.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注精神分裂症尤其是难治性患者的脑网络兴奋/抑制失衡问题，利用虚拟脑建模，从功能与结构磁共振数据模拟大规模脑动力学，并估计反映GABA能与NMDA能传递的网络参数。结果显示，与非难治性患者相比，难治性患者在全局及多个静息态网络中表现出兴奋/抑制参数的特异性改变，且默认网络、边缘网络和腹侧注意网络的部分参数与阴性症状、总体症状及紊乱症状的严重程度相关。作者据此认为，难治性精神分裂症具有网络特异的兴奋/抑制改变，个体化多尺度建模有望用于识别症状生物标志物；这些关联属于预测性发现，尚不能说明因果或临床疗效。

papers.title: Biologically inspired alignment reveals distributed and directionally asymmetric correspondence between rat and human cortices
papers.authors: Dong X, Luo Q, Cai A, Jin Z, Mu C, Wang F, Shan H.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rodent models enable causal interrogation of brain circuits, but translating their systems-level organization to humans requires correspondence beyond one-to-one anatomical homology. Guided by the view that cortical areas are characterized by their relationships within distributed functional networks, we developed BrainMapping, a biologically inspired framework for aligning rat and human cortex using resting-state functional MRI. The framework combined a shared representation with optimal transport to derive probabilistic, bidirectional maps. These alignments revealed distributed, many-to-many correspondences that generalized to held-out subjects and preserved functional connectivity architecture, cortical gradients, and graph topology. Organizational preservation was directionally asymmetric. Human-to-rat mapping preserved organization more uniformly across rat cortical systems, whereas rat-to-human mapping showed stronger preservation in human association-related networks than in primary sensory and motor networks. The maps recovered literature-consistent default-mode and salience-system correspondences and generated testable non-canonical predictions. These findings provide a framework for expressing rat functional organization in human functional-network coordinates.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出BrainMapping框架，利用静息态功能磁共振数据，将大鼠与人类皮层在分布式功能网络层面进行对齐，而非依赖一对一的解剖同源关系。结果显示，两者之间存在分布式的多对多对应关系，这些对应能泛化到留出个体，并保留功能连接结构、皮层梯度和图拓扑特征。组织结构的保留呈现方向不对称：人到大鼠的映射在大鼠各皮层系统中保留得更为均匀，而大鼠到人的映射在人类联合相关网络中保留得更好，在初级感觉和运动网络中则较弱。这些映射还复现了与文献一致的默认网络和突显系统对应，并给出可检验的非经典预测，为用人类功能网络坐标表达大鼠功能组织提供了框架。

papers.title: Differential subcortical-cortical circuit reorganization in autism and ADHD
papers.authors: Zhou G, Xie K, Ngo A, Ding R, Cabalo DG, Wang Y, Smith M, Nakamura M, Royer J, Serediuc N, Toussaint PJ, Mottron L, Martino AD, Milham MP, Hong S, Evans AC, Bernhardt BC.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often co-occur and share symptoms as well as genetic risk factors. While subcortical-cortical networks have been implicated in both conditions, particularly involving thalamic and striatal circuits, patterns of shared and diverging disruptions remain unclear. Here we integrated resting-state functional connectivity (FC) and regression dynamic causal modeling (rDCM) across a transdiagnostic multi-site cohort. We used statistical group comparisons and individualized normative deviation mapping to map network deviations in ASD and ADHD relative to neurotypical controls and against one another. Multivariate associative techniques examined associations to clinical and cognitive phenotypes. Our transdiagnostic analyses revealed significant differentiation of ASD and ADHD across subcortical-cortical circuits. While ASD was characterized by widespread thalamocortical hyperconnectivity and bidirectional elevated coupling across thalamic subdivisions, ADHD exhibited a focal pattern of striatocortical disruption, anchored predominantly within the caudate. Multivariate analyses identified shared and disorder-specific brain-behavior associations. Across both conditions, aberrant striatocortical signaling was associated with reduced overall intelligence measures. Clinically, ASD-related thalamocortical connectivity disruptions mapped onto generalized cognitive impairment, whereas ADHD-related subcortical alterations tracked hyperactive and inattentive symptom dimensions. Our findings differentiate ASD and ADHD through distinct patterns of functional and directional subcortical-cortical dysregulations.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）与注意缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）在皮层下-皮层环路中是否存在共享及分化的异常模式，整合静息态功能连接与回归动态因果模型，在多站点跨诊断队列中比较两组相对神经典型对照及彼此的偏差。结果显示，ASD以广泛的丘脑-皮层功能连接增强及丘脑各亚区间的双向耦合升高为特征，ADHD则表现为以尾状核为主的局灶性纹状体-皮层环路紊乱，提示两者在皮层下-皮层环路上存在可区分的功能与方向性失调。多变量分析还发现共享和疾病特异的脑-行为关联：纹状体-皮层信号异常与整体智力水平降低相关，ASD相关丘脑-皮层连接异常对应一般性认知受损，而ADHD相关皮层下改变则与多动和注意不集中症状维度相关。这些结果支持将两种障碍区分为不同的环路失调模式，但关联性发现尚不能说明因果或治疗效应。

papers.title: Human Hippocampal Theta-Gamma Phase-Amplitude Coupling Signals the Distance to Remembered Goals
papers.authors: Huang Z, Goumas P, Bisby JA, Rodionov R, Diehl B, McEvoy AW, Walker MC, Vivekananda U, Burgess N, Bush D.
papers.abstract: In mammals, flexible navigation is believed to rely on a cognitive map of known locations supported by the hippocampus and surrounding medial temporal lobe structures. Hippocampal place cells typically exhibit spatial firing fields within a given environment. Moreover, their firing is modulated by the movement-related theta rhythm such that ‘theta sweeps’ of place cell activity encode the trajectory towards a hidden reward location during goal-directed navigation. Here, we attempted to detect signatures of theta sweeps in the human hippocampal local field potential (LFP) recorded with intracranial EEG. Specifically, we hypothesised that sequences of locations along a planned trajectory encoded by distinct cell assemblies are associated with gamma activity at successive theta phases. To test this hypothesis, we asked N=9 patients with epilepsy to perform a spatial navigation task in desktop virtual reality while we recorded LFP signals from depth electrode contacts implanted across the medial temporal lobe. Consistent with our predictions, we found an increase in hippocampal theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, a decrease in gamma power, and theta phase precession of gamma activity as hidden goal locations were approached and the sequence of locations remaining to be traversed became shorter. This suggests that goal-directed hippocampal theta sweeps during navigation are reflected in LFP theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, and that these neural mechanisms of model-based planning are conserved across species.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨人类海马局部场电位中是否存在类似“theta扫掠”的目标导向导航信号，即不同细胞集群编码的路径位置序列是否随theta相位依次激活。作者让癫痫患者在接受颅内脑电记录时完成桌面虚拟现实空间导航任务，并分析海马theta-gamma相位-幅值耦合。结果显示，当受试者接近隐藏目标、剩余路径变短时，海马theta-gamma相位-幅值耦合增强，gamma功率下降，gamma活动出现theta相位进动。作者据此认为，目标导向的海马theta扫掠可在人类局部场电位的相位-幅值耦合中体现，并提示这种基于模型的规划机制可能跨物种保守。

papers.title: Beyond High-Amplitude Events: Amplitude-Resolved Spatial and Temporal ICA Representations in fMRI
papers.authors: Vu D, Calhoun V.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Functional MRI analyses commonly reduce high-dimensional brain activity using predefined spatial summaries, such as region-of-interest (ROI) averages, or temporally selective representations, such as co-activation patterns (CAPs) and high-amplitude events. These approaches provide useful summaries but do not explicitly characterize information distribution across the continuous magnitude of spatial and temporal network expression. We introduce an amplitude-resolved framework for systematically interrogating this continuum using independent component analysis (ICA). Resting-state fMRI data in the FBIRN dataset were decomposed using spatially-constrained ICA with NeuroMark. For the temporal representation, time points were stratified according to global ICA amplitude and frequency bands, with functional network connectivity (FNC) estimated for each amplitude range. For the spatial representation, we introduce an approach that stratifies voxels according to ICA loading magnitude and generates amplitude-specific spatial similarity matrices. Linear support vector machine (SVM) classification of schizophrenia (SZ) and healthy control (HC) participants was used to probe the information retained by each representation. Discriminative information varied non-monotonically across amplitude: intermediate ranges frequently matched or exceeded the highest amplitudes, while combinations of amplitude ranges further improved classification. These findings demonstrate that informative fMRI structure is distributed across the ICA expression continuum and motivate representations that complement fixed ROI summaries and high-amplitude approaches.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出一种按幅度分层的独立成分分析框架，用静息态fMRI数据分别考察空间和时间网络表达在不同幅度区间上的信息分布，并以精神分裂症患者与健康对照的分类表现检验各层表示所保留的判别信息。结果显示，判别信息随幅度呈非单调变化，中等幅度区间常与最高幅度相当甚至更优，而多个幅度区间的组合还能进一步提升分类表现。作者据此指出，有信息量的fMRI结构分布在ICA表达的整个连续幅度范围内，提示需要发展能补充固定ROI汇总和高幅度事件方法的表示方式。

papers.title: Language-associated brain representations covary with disruption of selfhood under psilocybin
papers.authors: Cooper G, Stoliker D, Astl Delgado VS, Blackburne G, Novelli L, Green DW, Das R, Razi A, Skipper JI.
papers.abstract: Language helps organise experience into an idiosyncratic, temporally extended sense of self. We therefore used fMRI to investigate whether greater similarity between subjects in the activity of language-associated brain regions accompanied psilocybin-induced loss of selfhood using fMRI. Participants heard music and viewed moving clouds at baseline and after 19 mg psilocybin. At each brain location and time point, we tested whether similarity increased with each pair’s summed rank on the Ego Dissolution Inventory (EDI; N=43). We grouped independent components of these associations by time course and decoded each group’s map with Neurosynth. Elementary visual imagery (SI; N=49) and baseline activity served as comparators. Under psilocybin, one group formed a distributed, left-lateralised frontotemporal network matching the Neurosynth language map (r=.382, spatial-null p<.001, q=.003), nearly twice the largest comparator estimate (SI: r=.208, p=.004, q=.028; baseline: r≤.12). In exploratory analyses, resting-state connectivity of this network decreased with posterior visual cortex and increased with thalamic and frontal regions. Participants with higher EDI scores showed larger changes (ρ=.455, Bonferroni-adjusted p=.048; SI: ρ=.008), most strongly for items describing loss of ego or identity (ρ=.43–.51; other items, ρ=.22–.33). We propose that language-associated systems incorporate each person’s semantic and autobiographical context into experience, and that disrupting them contributes to loss of ego and identity.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究用fMRI考察裸盖菇素引起的自我感丧失是否伴随语言相关脑区活动在个体间相似性的变化：参与者在基线和服药后听音乐、观看移动云朵，并分析这种相似性与自我消解量表得分的关系。结果显示，服药后出现一个与语言网络图谱匹配的左侧化额颞分布式网络，其相似性明显高于视觉表象和基线对照；该网络与后部视觉皮层的静息连接减弱，与丘脑和额叶区域的连接增强，且自我消解得分越高者变化越大，尤以描述自我或身份丧失的条目最为突出。作者据此提出，语言相关系统将个人的语义和自传体背景纳入体验，其受扰动可能促成自我与身份的消解；相关分析属探索性，尚不能确立因果。

papers.title: Tablet-Camera Iris Landmarks and EEG/PPG-Derived Arousal Indices During Naturalistic Reading: Geometric Confounding and Exploratory Within-Subject Associations.
papers.authors: Ko S, Park J, Whang M, Kim D, Kim M.
papers.abstract: Arousal, the activation dimension of the valence-arousal circumplex, indexes alertness and engagement independently of pleasantness. We evaluated whether MediaPipe FaceLandmarker iris landmark distances from a tablet camera estimate electroencephalography (EEG)- and photoplethysmography (PPG)-derived arousal markers during naturalistic reading. Recordings from 48 participants yielded 43,923 thirty-second windows. Raw iris distances correlated with EEG alpha (r=+0.118) and theta (r=+0.076), but face scale explained 93% of their variance. After face-width normalisation, alpha remained associated (r=+0.076), whereas theta was not statistically significant. Further adjustment for ocular luminance and head pose rendered alpha nonsignificant (r=+0.021, p=0.33). Circular-shift testing identified alpha coupling in 11/48 participants under full control, versus 28/48 using uncorrected Pearson tests. Within-subject Ridge regression, with no raw sample shared between the training and test windows, yielded a nonsignificant group mean correlation (r=+0.078, p=0.07); 13/48 participants had individually significant prediction-reference associations (11 positive), fewer when the PPG term was restricted to filter-consistent beats. Both counts are exploratory, nominal and uncorrected across participants, and come from different analyses. Neither establishes prospective monitoring performance, and the study does not validate the landmark distance as a pupil measure.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Electrically Guided Drug Transport Toward Morphology-Specific Brain Tumor Treatment.
papers.authors: Lee S, Lee K, Lee S, Park J, Choy YB, Im CH.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Iontophoresis employs an applied electric field to induce electromigration, enabling the active and directional transport of drug molecules. This study presents the first computational investigation of iontophoretic drug delivery targeting human brain tumors. The objective was to evaluate the feasibility of this approach and to determine how electrode configurations influence drug transport across different tumor morphologies. Methods: A realistic finite element head model was constructed from T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data. Two representative glioblastoma morphologies were considered: a spherical tumor in the left hemisphere and a butterfly-shaped tumor extending across the corpus callosum. Six electrode configurations spanning three categories (scalp electrodes, combined catheter and scalp electrodes, and catheter electrodes) were systematically evaluated. The electric field distribution was computed by solving the quasi-static Laplace equation, and the spatiotemporal distribution of gadobutrol was obtained using the Nernst-Planck equation. Drug delivery performance was quantified in terms of tumor coverage and targeting efficiency. Results: Under the simulated conditions, iontophoresis markedly enhanced drug delivery compared with passive diffusion, increasing tumor volume coverage from 13% to 84% in the spherical tumor model. Scalp electrode configurations resulted in the lowest tumor coverage in both tumor models. The combined catheter-scalp configuration generated radial drug transport from the catheter and achieved the highest coverage in the spherical tumor. In the butterfly-shaped tumor model, a three-catheter configuration enabled bilateral delivery along the tumor axis, achieving a tumor coverage of 49% and a targeting efficiency of 82%. The maximum electric field magnitude across all configurations was 49.26 V/m, remaining below reported axonal activation thresholds for deep brain stimulation. Conclusions: These findings support the feasibility of iontophoretic drug delivery to human brain tumors and demonstrate that the effective electrode configuration depends on tumor morphology. This study provides a computational foundation for morphology-specific planning of iontophoretic drug delivery to brain tumors.

papers.title: Dietary Vitamin Intake and Cognitive Performance in Adults with Long COVID: The BioICOPER Study.
papers.authors: Arjol D, Arroyo-Romero S, García DR, Navarro-Matías E, Navarro-Cáceres A, Suárez-Moreno N, Domínguez-Martín A, Gómez-Marcos MA, Gómez-Sánchez M, Gómez-Sánchez L, BioICOPER Investigators Group.
papers.abstract: Background: Long COVID (LC) is associated with persistent cognitive symptoms, frequently described as brain fog, and with inflammatory, immunometabolic, and energetic mechanisms potentially involved in cognitive functioning. Vitamins participate in biological processes relevant to brain function, but the relationship between habitual dietary vitamin intake and cognitive performance in LC remains poorly studied. Objective: To analyze the relationship between dietary vitamin intake and cognitive performance in adults with LC, considering both objective performance and self-reported cognition. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 304 adults with LC. Vitamin intake from foods and beverages was estimated using the EVIDENT seven-day dietary record, previously compared with a validated food-frequency questionnaire. Objective cognitive performance was assessed using normative scores from the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and the Memory Index Score (MIS), as well as MoCA domains and items. Self-reported cognition was assessed using the 30-item Memory Failures of Everyday Questionnaire (MFE-30) and the cognitive subscale of the Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (MFIS). Primary global associations were examined using multiple linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors, whereas bounded MoCA domains were analyzed using proportional-odds ordinal regression and binary item-level outcomes using logistic regression. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied within prespecified families of contrasts. Results: No associations between vitamin intake and global normative cognitive performance remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Median MoCA and MIS scores were 24.00 (IQR, 21.00-26.00) and 11.00 (IQR, 9.00-13.00), respectively. Normative MoCA and MIS scores showed medians of -0.32 (IQR, -0.82 to 0.19) and -0.32 (IQR, -0.76 to 0.14), respectively. Most participants (95.1%) met the dietary reference value for vitamin B3. In secondary ordinal analyses, higher vitamin B3 intake was associated with better MoCA language performance in the fully adjusted model (OR per 1 SD = 2.18, 95% CI 1.45-3.27, p < 0.001, q = 0.0116). No associations remained significant after FDR correction for everyday cognitive complaints, cognitive fatigue, or MoCA Memory and MoCA Multiple scores. Conclusions: In adults with LC, the primary analyses did not identify FDR-significant associations between habitual dietary vitamin intake and global normative cognitive performance. The secondary vitamin B3-language association requires independent confirmation and does not establish a cognitive benefit of higher intake or supplementation. These findings require confirmation in longitudinal studies incorporating nutritional biomarkers, information on supplementation, and broader neuropsychological assessment.

papers.title: Profiling Amino Acid Substitutions in Proteomic Datasets of Alzheimer's Disease Reveals Biological Significance.
papers.authors: Zhao P, Lai S, Dai S, Zhou C, Li N, Yu W.
papers.abstract: Background : Amino acid (AA) substitutions in Alzheimer's disease (AD) have been studied almost exclusively at the DNA and RNA levels, and the proteome-level substitution landscape remains largely uncharacterized. Methods : We applied an open-search substitutomics pipeline (PIPI-C with Comet re-scoring, 1% PSM-level FDR) to two independent AD brain proteomic datasets, the AMP-AD superior temporal gyrus cohort (244 individuals) and PXD013753, excluding substitutions whose mass shifts coincide with common post-translational modifications. Results : We quantified 789 substitution-bearing peptidoforms from 185 proteins, corresponding to 784 protein-level substitution events. N > M was the most frequent N > X substitution in both datasets. In an institution-stratified case-control meta-analysis, 138 peptidoforms were more and 142 less abundant in AD than in neuropathological controls. Of 774 genome-mappable events, 710 (91.7%) were recorded in neither UniProt nor gnomAD, and only five matched a population variant with allele frequency ≥ 0.1%. The unrestricted search recovered six literature-reported sites in GFAP, ACTG1, and HBB. Conclusions : Proteome-level profiling reveals substitution events in AD brains that catalogued germline variation does not explain; their molecular origin requires orthogonal validation.

papers.title: Advancing the Translational Pipeline: From In Vivo and In Vitro 2D Models to Next-Generation Cell Culture Models for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Modelling and Drug Discovery.
papers.authors: Carata E, Mariano S, Tenuzzo BA, Panzarini E.
papers.abstract: Background : Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is still a global health challenge, as there is no effective treatment due to the inadequacy of conventional experimental platforms for comprehending pathogenic mechanisms and developing therapy. Objectives : This review details the recent progress and clinical utility of next-generation iPSC-derived 3D in vitro systems integrated with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, multi-omics readouts, and AI-based machine learning, which are emerging as transformative platforms for recapitulating key ALS pathological hallmarks. Methods : A literature search was performed using PubMed and Web of Science, including only English-language publications. All the published papers collected covered the period from January 2015 to June 2026. Results : Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) cerebral organoids, assembloids, and organ-on-a-chip technologies are revolutionizing research into ALS by providing a way to model the complex spatial organization, cellular heterogeneity, and neural network dynamics of the human brain. Moreover, recent bioengineering advancements enable the inclusion of functional neurovascular units, the integration of resident immune cells (microglia), and the use of 3D bioprinting to accelerate the functional maturation of age-related phenotypes. CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, OMICS, and machine learning improve tools for studying ALS and identifying therapeutic targets. Conclusions : Novel cell culture models may bridge the gap between preclinical animal models and human clinical trials and reduce the duration and costs of translation. Future work is likely to integrate bioprinting with organ-on-chip microfluidics, CRISPR-based genetic editing, and multi-omics readouts to build increasingly faithful, patient-specific ALS models for both basic research and precision therapeutics.

papers.title: Case Report: Presumptive subdural hemorrhage as a rare neurological manifestation of primary immune-mediated thrombocytopenia in a dog.
papers.authors: Hong HP, Kei TG, Gagnon NA, Scrivani PV.
papers.abstract: A 10-year-old female spayed mixed-breed dog was presented with a history of seizures and acute progressive intracranial signs. The neurological examination was consistent with multifocal brain disease. Clinical examination revealed ecchymoses, petechiae, and bilateral retinal hemorrhage. Clinicopathological evaluation identified severe thrombocytopenia [a platelet count of 9 × 103 /μL without clumps on manual smear evaluation] with an increased mean platelet volume. Coagulation testing (activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time) and fibrinolysis markers (D-dimers, quantitative fibrinogen), infectious disease screening, and thoracic and abdominal imaging were within normal limits, establishing a diagnosis of primary immune-mediated thrombocytopenia (ITP). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain showed minimally expanded, bilateral crescent-shaped, extra-axial fluid accumulations overlying both cerebral hemispheres. Based on T1-weighted and T2-weighted hyperintensities and peripheral susceptibility artifact on T2*-weighted gradient-recalled echo (GRE) imaging, a late subacute subdural intracranial hemorrhage was diagnosed. Despite initial uneventful anesthesia and recovery, the dog experienced acute neurological deterioration and suffered cardiopulmonary arrest, suspected due to ongoing hemorrhage or brain herniation. This report describes a rare neurological manifestation of primary ITP in a dog. While canine ITP generally carries a favorable prognosis, life-threatening secondary intracranial hemorrhage can occur. Primary ITP should be considered as a differential diagnosis for an acute, progressive neurological presentation until a normal platelet count is confirmed.

papers.title: Case Report: Solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) of cerebellum: report of 2 cases.
papers.authors: Guo G, Ma Z, Zhao L, Gao T, Sun Y, Liu Z, Liu Y, Li C.
papers.abstract: Objective To elucidate the neuroradiological characteristics, clinical manifestations, and surgical outcomes of intracranial cerebellar solitary fibrous tumors (SFTs) to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic strategies. Method A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of two histopathologically confirmed cases of cerebellar SFT, supplemented by a review of the relevant literature. Results Both patients underwent total surgical excision followed by postoperative radiotherapy. At the latest follow-up, neither patient showed radiological evidence of tumor recurrence (Case 1: 18 months; Case 2: 12 months]). Given the potential for late recurrence in SFTs, long-term surveillance is mandatory. Conclusion Intracranial cerebellar SFTs are rare neoplasms that are frequently misdiagnosed despite exhibiting distinctive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. Definitive diagnosis relies on histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses. In this study, MRI demonstrated T1-weighted imaging (T1WI) hypointensity or isointensity, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) heterogeneity, and inconsistent post-contrast enhancement. Immunohistochemical evaluation revealed positivity for CD34, CD99, and STAT6. Prompt surgical intervention accompanied by adjuvant therapy was associated with a favorable prognosis.

papers.title: Projecting the real through active inference: a unified model of reality construction from neuronal dynamics to social consensus a neuroscientific framework for psychopathology.
papers.authors: G P, P P.
papers.abstract: How does the brain transform a chaotic stream of sensory signals into a stable, shared experience of reality? This theoretical paper proposes that the brain does not passively receive the world, but actively projects it - it continuously generates predictions about sensory inputs and updates its internal model when predictions fail, a process formally described by the free energy principle and active inference. We argue that this process can be understood through an analogy with quantum decoherence - the collapse of multiple possibilities into a single actuality. By integrating insights from this analogy with active inference, we show how the brain resolves sensory uncertainty into a coherent projection of reality. A central question we address is whether projecting reality changes it. We argue that it does: a strong, coherent projection reduces uncertainty, while a weak or fragmented one amplifies prediction errors, and a distorted one - diverging from social consensus - leads to alternative realities that resist correction. This projection operates in discrete, rhythmic cycles governed by brain waves and is fine-tuned by neurochemicals that determine how much we "trust" our predictions versus new sensory data. The Default Mode Network - the brain's inner "sea" of self-awareness, memories, and context - acts as a central hub that integrates and updates these projections. Crucially, individual projections are stabilized into a shared, "solid" reality through social interaction, language, and culture - a process we call collective active inference. Within this framework, psychiatric disorders are understood as disorders of projection - distortions in how the brain generates and stabilizes its model of reality. This perspective reverses the traditional explanatory gradient: psychopathology is not merely a sensory or chemical problem, but a fundamental disruption of the brain's capacity to project a coherent world. This unifying framework offers a new foundation for both pharmacological and psychotherapeutic interventions, grounding them in a common computational logic.

papers.title: Reality stabilization: a unified framework for psychosis and post-psychotic depression.
papers.authors: Panov G, Panova P.
papers.abstract: Both quantum mechanics and cognitive neuroscience challenge the classical view of a passively perceived reality. Instead, they suggest that reality arises through a process of selection and stabilization from a field of possibilities. This article proposes that this "reality stabilization" framework can unify our understanding of psychosis and post-psychotic depression-two conditions that are currently studied as distinct phenomena, and which existing models of predictive coding, dopaminergic dysregulation, and network neuroscience rarely integrate into a single account. We conceptualize psychosis as a failure of neurocognitive decoherence, in which competing perceptual and interpretative states cannot be reduced to a single, coherent reality. Post-psychotic depression, in contrast, is framed as a compensatory hyperstabilization, in which a rigid, negatively valenced reality is restored, possibly mediated by altered DMN activity. The framework suggests that effective intervention must move beyond dopaminergic blockade to include strategies that promote adaptive network coherence and cognitive integration. The model remains hypothetical, and direct empirical evidence for decoherence-like processes, network changes, and the proposed temporal progression is limited. Future work should focus on empirical testing of stabilization and hyperstabilization mechanisms, longitudinal assessment across illness stages, and their possible therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Traumatic brain injury, neurobiology of aggression and antisocial behavior: from large-scale brain networks to anatomical and molecular substrates.
papers.authors: Berretta E, Manni L, Soligo M.
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a dynamic pathological cascade that often culminates in chronic neuropsychiatric sequelae, such as reactive aggression and antisocial behavior. While these debilitating manifestations severely impair social reintegration and quality of life, their heterogeneous nature complicates clinical and forensic characterization. This review addresses this challenge through an integrated, multiscale framework that bridges macro-scale network desynchronization with micro-circuit pathology. We illustrate how the mechanical disruption of major white matter tracts decouples large-scale neurocognitive networks, leaving subcortical emotional anchors in a state of unmodulated hyper-reactivity stripped of prefrontal inhibitory control. The macroscopic untethering operates in synergy with localized cellular failures within specific amygdalar subnuclei, where chronic neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and ascending neuromodulatory alterations durably shift the affective circuitry toward a hyperexcitable state. By mapping these dimensional neurobiological substrates directly onto the DSM-5-TR taxonomic framework, we spark a new neuroforensic debate regarding criminal responsibility, considering the boundaries of volitional control and the contemporary debate on free will in organically compromised patients. This translational perspective guides the evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies, shifting the paradigm away from non-specific pharmacological sedation toward personalized, state-dependent neuromodulation capable of exogenously restoring circuit synchrony and patient clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Review on unobtrusive estimation of team processes underlying team situation awareness: shared mental models and team coordination.
papers.authors: Zhecheva E, Groen E, Haselager P, Brouwer AM.
papers.abstract: Introduction Team situation awareness (SA) is essential for effective team performance. Yet, current methods rely on potentially biased self-reports and obtrusive tools such as task probes. Objective, unobtrusive, and continuous methods for monitoring team SA could support its improvement. In contrast to individual SA, unobtrusive measures of team SA have not been systematically reviewed. Because team SA is an umbrella concept, we adapted a framework proposed by Salmon et al., identifying two components that can potentially be measured unobtrusively: shared mental models (SMMs) and team coordination. This systematic review examines behavioural and physiological technologies that may enable unobtrusive measurement of these components. Methods We conducted a systematic literature review of studies investigating behavioural technologies, such as verbal communication and eye-tracking, and physiological technologies, such as electroencephalography, for unobtrusive measurement of team SMMs and coordination. We searched Web of Science (May and July 2025) for relevant literature published between 2000 and 2025. We included peer-reviewed articles published in English. In total, 19 studies addressing team SMMs and 33 addressing team coordination were included. We extracted sample and team size, task environment, operationalisation of team SMMs and coordination, and their relationship with unobtrusive measures. Results Cardiac measures (42%) and verbal communication (47%) were most popular for estimating team SMMs, while functional near-infrared spectroscopy (27%) and cardiac measures (30%) were most popular for estimating team coordination. Interpersonal synchrony-the temporal contiguity and interdependence of physiological and/or behavioural activity between teammates-was applied in 70% of team coordination studies. Studies covered diverse tasks and settings, from laboratory-based cognitive tasks and controlled physical tasks to real-world environments, including surgery. Various methods were used to operationalise SMMs and coordination, including participant experience, expert assessment, and self-reports. Discussion Findings suggest that team SMMs and coordination cannot be measured as single, unified constructs using one unobtrusive measure. Instead, different measures may provide information about specific aspects of these processes. Future research should begin with task analysis to identify relevant aspects of team SA and derive appropriate measures for the specific task environment. Task-related behavioural actions also represent a potentially valuable, yet often overlooked, category of unobtrusive measures. A key limitation is the substantial variation in how SMMs and coordination were operationalised and measured, making direct comparisons difficult. Future work should investigate how identified measures relate directly to team SA using validated measures.

papers.title: Combining pharmacological and non-invasive brain stimulation strategies to promote remyelination in multiple sclerosis.
papers.authors: Scheinok TJ, De Bundel D, Vanmierlo T, Van Schependom J.
papers.abstract: Remyelination in multiple sclerosis (MS) fails for several, partly overlapping reasons. The differentiation of oligodendrocyte precursor cells into myelin-producing oligodendrocytes is impaired both by intrinsic factors and by the surrounding lesion environment, which becomes increasingly inflammatory and senescent with age. Pharmacological strategies acting on a single target to promote oligodendrocyte lineage progression have been successful in animal models but have yet to produce meaningful clinical benefit in people with MS (pwMS). In this perspective paper, we argue that simultaneously targeting several of the mechanisms underlying this failure is a more promising route to repairing myelin lesions in pwMS. We outline how non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) might be leveraged to shift the glial microenvironment towards a pro-regenerative, remyelinating state, and how this can be paired with targeted pharmacological agents that enhance oligodendrocyte differentiation. We also discuss how the expected effect of such a combination may depend on age and lesion stage. This framework may offer a rational route beyond the translational failures of single-target remyelination therapies.

papers.title: Exercise-related brain remodeling through bidirectional brain-body crosstalk: an integrative narrative review.
papers.authors: Yin D, Luo C, Hu J, Bi SZ.
papers.abstract: Exercise is associated with favorable brain and cognitive outcomes, yet the supporting evidence spans molecular, cellular, organ, neural-circuit, imaging, and behavioral levels that differ substantially in causal strength. This narrative review develops an integrative framework across biological levels in which exercise-related brain remodeling emerges from bidirectional brain-body crosstalk rather than from a single peripheral factor or a one-way endocrine pathway. The framework links central motor commands, sensory feedback, autonomic regulation, and cerebral hemodynamics with signal generation by skeletal muscle, liver, adipose tissue, bone, the gut microbiome, and the circulating immune-vascular milieu. Metabolites, secreted factors, extracellular vesicles, and neural afferents may influence the central nervous system through blood-brain and blood-cerebrospinal fluid interfaces, circumventricular organs, cerebral endothelium, and brainstem-hypothalamic networks. Candidate central responses include neurotrophic and synaptic signaling, glial-state regulation, adult hippocampal neurogenesis, and neurovascular adaptation, which may correspond to group-level changes in brain structure, functional connectivity, and cognition. However, direct causal mediation across the complete human pathway remains largely untested: many cellular mechanisms derive from animal or in vitro studies, whereas human biomarker and neuroimaging findings are often indirect and process-nonspecific. Age, sex and hormonal state, genotype, disease stage, baseline function, exercise dose, recovery, and adherence further shape response heterogeneity. A stronger translational evidence base will require preregistered longitudinal interventions, source-resolved and time-resolved biomarker sampling, cross-species validation, multimodal target-engagement measures, and externally validated prediction models.

papers.title: Caregiver perspectives on participation in pediatric neuroimaging research: insights from qualitative focus groups.
papers.authors: Olson S, Thellman CR, Demetri B, Sholar B, Shultz S.
papers.abstract: Infant functional and structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is increasingly used in research to identify early emerging biomarkers of neurodevelopmental conditions. Although these methods hold promise for advancing discovery, pediatric MRI research protocols, which often require infants to be scanned during natural sleep, can present a range of challenges for infants and their caregivers. Yet little is known about caregivers' experiences participating in non-clinically indicated MRI studies with their infants. This study explored caregivers' motivations for participating in infant MRI research, their experiences during participation, and their suggestions for improving infant MRI protocols. Three semi-structured focus groups were conducted with caregivers of 0-6-month-old infants who participated in a longitudinal MRI study. Thematic analysis revealed that caregivers were primarily motivated by contributing to science and helping other families. Many experienced performance anxieties while attempting to help their infants fall asleep for a scan, but supportive communication from research staff helped reduce these concerns. Caregivers recommended flexible scheduling, clearer procedural expectations, and pre-visit materials to improve preparedness. These findings underscore the importance of family-centered communication in infant neuroimaging protocols.

papers.title: Altered attention network dynamics in resting-state fMRI of individuals with high smartphone addiction scores.
papers.authors: Watters H, Rashid AA, Suppiah S, LaGrow TJ, Hlinka J, Keilholz S.
papers.abstract: Introduction Altered attention network activity has been consistently reported in recent neuroimaging literature of smartphone addiction and problematic smartphone use. However, many functional imaging studies have relied on traditional static functional connectivity analyses, which cannot capture time-varying or recurrent dynamics of attention networks. Methods Given the importance of temporal and spatial dynamics for attentional processing, we applied two complementary dynamic functional connectivity approaches: functional connectivity-based attractor networks (fcANN), which characterize transitions between discrete attractor states related to internal-external context and action-perception dynamics, and cPCA-based quasi-periodic pattern (QPP) analysis, which captures phase relationships between cortical networks including the default mode network, dorsal attention network, and frontoparietal control network. Results In a resting-state fMRI dataset comparing participants with High and Low SAS-M scores (SAS-M: Smartphone addiction scale-Malay version questionnaire), we observed context-dependent differences in DMN-attention-network relationships across attractor states.
