The most consistent effects emerged during transitions between internal and external attractor states, where subjects with high smartphone addiction (SPA) scores showed greater DMN dominance relative to attention-related networks. For DMN-FPN, these differences correlated with subject SAS-M scores. Discussion Overall, these findings provide preliminary evidence that smartphone addiction may be associated with altered large-scale attentional dynamics at rest, warranting further investigation in larger and more diverse samples.

papers.title: Grey matter atrophy signatures and their genetic associations: a trans-disease study of Alzheimer's disease and multiple sclerosis.
papers.authors: Zhao Y, Sun J, Reheman B, Bai X, Zhang C, Ding W, Zou B, Zhang H, Zhang Z, Zhang N.
papers.abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) and multiple sclerosis (MS) share neuroimmune mechanisms that drive neurodegeneration. Current clinical interventions are largely confined to a single-disease approach, owing to the absence of trans-disease diagnostic markers and common therapeutic targets. Objective To map common and disease-specific grey matter (GM) atrophy patterns in AD and MS and identify their genetic correlations. Methods We performed a trans-disease meta-analysis in large-sample neuroimaging data from 2001 to 2024 (2,070 MS versus 1,625 healthy control, and 1,624 AD versus 1,607 healthy control) to map GM atrophy regions. The cross-sample partial least squares regression was applied to integrate gene expression profiles from the Allen Human Brain Atlas with region-specific GM atrophy patterns, achieving cross-scale analysis of identify neurodegeneration-associated genes. Results MS-specific atrophy localized to the bilateral dorsomedial thalamic nucleus and precentral gyrus, whereas AD-specific atrophy centered on bilateral hippocampus-amygdala complex in age-unadjusted comparisons. The common atrophy patterns were found in the bilateral superior temporal gyrus, insulae, posterior cingulate cortex, amygdalae, and striatal components. We identified 834 genes whose spatial expression patterns were associated with the common GM atrophy pattern in AD and MS, including PLS2 + and PLS2- subsets, which encompass biological processes such as immunological homeostasis imbalance, cellular stress response, and neurometabolic/functional regulation. Conclusion Findings establish shared cortical-limbic-striatal atrophy as pivotal neurodegeneration nexus in AD and MS. The identified gene-imaging signatures provide insights into potential pathway-specific mechanisms and may inform future therapeutic target discovery for dual-disease intervention.

papers.title: Advances in artificial intelligence for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis of neurological diseases: a systematic literature review.
papers.authors: Omarov B.
papers.abstract: Background Brain imaging is central to the structural, functional, metabolic, and neurophysiological characterization of neurological disease, yet interpretation remains constrained by heterogeneity in acquisition, annotation, expertise, and clinical context. Objective This systematic literature review evaluates recent artificial intelligence approaches for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis, with emphasis on methods, modalities, neurological diseases, diagnostic tasks, datasets, validation practices, and translational limitations. Methods The review followed PRISMA 2020 and covered peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2020 through June 2026. Eight information sources were searched using database-specific terms for artificial intelligence, neuroimaging, neurological disease, and diagnostic analysis. The search identified 1,078 records; 236 duplicates were removed, 842 unique records were screened, 258 full texts were assessed, and 123 studies were included after a record-level eligibility re-audit. Heterogeneous evidence was synthesized narratively and by descriptive mapping rather than meta-analysis. Results MRI was frequently represented in the included studies and auxiliary mapping data; CT was commonly used in acute stroke and intracranial hemorrhage; PET supported selected molecular and differential-diagnosis studies; fMRI and diffusion imaging were used for network and white-matter analysis; and EEG extended the scope to neurophysiological diagnosis. CNN and three-dimensional networks were commonly reported, while attention, Transformer, graph, self-supervised, generative, multimodal, and foundation-model approaches appeared in selected recent studies. Stroke, dementia, and brain tumors were frequently represented, but heterogeneous populations, outcomes, and incomplete validation extraction precluded ranking diseases, modalities, architectures, or validation strategies. Conclusion The evidence suggests movement from task-specific pattern recognition toward multimodal and context-rich decision support in selected settings, but it does not establish uniform methodological superiority or clinical maturity. Dependable translation requires patient-level data governance, transparent reporting, uncertainty estimation, independent multicenter testing, prospective workflow evaluation, and clinically meaningful endpoints.

papers.title: A two-stage RAG-LLM pipeline for roadmapping neuroscience research in operational environments.
papers.authors: Spencer CA.
papers.abstract: Introduction Neuroscientific research and applications in real world environments are often constrained by limited access, equipment limitations, and high costs. Consequently, robustly selecting constructs to focus effort on is a high-impact task. Method This study introduces a two-stage large language model (LLM) pipeline that generates research roadmaps from existing real-world data to inform research priorities in the field, given the state of the art. Stage 1 uses retrieval-augmented generation on operational logs to identify candidate psychological, social, and neurocognitive constructs and map their co-occurrence. Stage 2 evaluates how well these constructs are represented in the literature across four dimensions that commonly inform prioritization: ecological validity, neural correlates, biosensor protocols, and brain computer interface readiness, producing an evidence gap matrix. Pipeline evaluation combined human review, deterministic computations, and human-LLM alignment analysis. Results Applying the pipeline to Mars Desert Research Station logs, Stage 1 identified 19 constructs. Stage 2 highlighted critical gaps in neuroimaging and measurement protocols, particularly for social domains, thereby identifying potential research priorities and risks. Discussion This methodology offers a generalizable starting point for synthesizing operational logs into actionable research roadmaps, but the evaluation showed it still required human scrutiny.

papers.title: Clinically low-risk features do not exclude diffusion-weighted imaging-positive lesions in suspected transient ischemic attack.
papers.authors: Mann L, Ern K, Stahn S, Hildner M, Hattingen E, Keil FC.
papers.abstract: Introduction Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) is essential for distinguishing tissue-negative transient ischemic attack (TIA) from MRI-defined minor stroke. When MRI capacity is limited, clinical features could help estimate DWI lesion yield. While features associated with DWI positivity are well established, it remains uncertain whether clinically low-risk presentations identify patients with a sufficiently low probability of DWI-positive lesions. We investigated clinical features associated with DWI-positive lesions in patients presenting with suspected TIA and assessed whether clinically low-risk constellations reliably excluded DWI-positive lesions. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 418 patients presenting with suspected TIA who underwent a standardized MRI protocol within 6 h of admission. The study endpoint was an acute DWI-positive lesion, defined by DWI hyperintensity with corresponding apparent diffusion coefficient reduction. Univariate analyses and exploratory multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to examine clinical, neurological, and cardiovascular features associated with DWI positivity, with particular emphasis on clinically low-risk presentations. Results DWI-positive lesions were detected in 118/418 patients (28.2%). Motor symptoms (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.683, p < 0.001), NIHSS 1-5 (aOR 1.940, p = 0.007), and acute symptom onset (aOR 1.999, p = 0.025) were associated with DWI positivity in the clinical-neurological analysis, while cardiovascular risk factors showed the strongest association in the extended analysis (aOR 3.959, p < 0.001). Conversely, subacute onset, non-specific accompanying symptoms, NIHSS 0, and dizziness were associated with lower odds of DWI positivity. Importantly, DWI-positive lesions remained present in 13/133 patients (9.8%) with ≥2 and 2/48 (4.2%) with ≥3 low-risk features. Discussion Clinically low-risk presentations did not reliably exclude DWI-positive lesions, supporting MRI-based evaluation. Clinical and cardiovascular features may help estimate the likelihood of DWI positivity; whether they can inform MRI prioritization requires prospective validation.

papers.title: FLAIR vascular hyperintensities in acute ischemic stroke: from collateral-related imaging findings to a candidate dynamic hemodynamic imaging phenotype.
papers.authors: Qin M, Wang L, Han G.
papers.abstract: With advances in reperfusion therapies for acute large vessel occlusion (LVO), stroke imaging evaluation has progressively shifted from time-based treatment selection toward comprehensive assessment of tissue status and hemodynamic adaptation. However, current imaging approaches primarily characterize vascular patency, perfusion status, and tissue injury, while remaining limited in their ability to directly capture the dynamic regulatory processes of cerebral circulation after arterial occlusion. In patients with LVO, ischemic tissue outcome is determined not only by the occlusion site and time to reperfusion but also by collateral circulation capacity, cerebral hemodynamic status, and tissue tolerance to ischemia. Therefore, imaging biomarkers capable of reflecting cerebral circulatory adaptation under ischemic conditions are of substantial research interest. FLAIR vascular hyperintensities (FVHs) are MRI findings characterized by linear or serpentine hyperintense signals along the cortical surface, within cortical sulci, or along the Sylvian fissure on fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences. They are generally associated with reduced distal blood flow velocity, prolonged blood transit time, and hemodynamic alterations mediated by leptomeningeal collateral pathways. In recent years, numerous studies have investigated the role of FVHs in the diagnosis of acute ischemic stroke, evaluation of reperfusion therapy, and prediction of clinical outcomes. However, the clinical significance of FVHs remains incompletely understood. Some studies have suggested that FVHs are associated with favorable collateral status and smaller infarct volumes, whereas others have demonstrated that FVHs may also occur in patients with more pronounced hemodynamic impairment. These discrepancies suggest that FVHs may not simply represent favorable collateral circulation or ischemic severity, but may instead reflect the dynamic hemodynamic response of the cerebral circulation to reduced perfusion following arterial occlusion. From the perspective of precision stroke imaging, this review systematically summarizes the mechanisms underlying FVH formation, their biological significance, and clinical implications. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationships between FVHs and collateral circulation, FVHs-DWI mismatch, ischemic tissue status, and potential benefit from reperfusion therapy. Furthermore, current challenges related to FVH standardization and clinical translation are discussed, with particular emphasis on their potential role as a candidate dynamic hemodynamic imaging phenotype reflecting physiological hemodynamic adaptation.

papers.title: The HALF-IT score: proposing a simplified mechanical thrombectomy triage tool for basilar artery occlusion.
papers.authors: Jones AM, Tariq Z, Ashouri Y, Chaudhari A, AlMajali M, Ezzeldin M, Kareem MA, Awwad AR, Wong G, Molaie AM, Sanz Cuesta B, Saver JL, Limaye K, Zaidat OO.
papers.abstract: Background Basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is a devastating subtype of stroke with poor prognosis. Current patient selection tools for endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) are multi-tiered with interrater variability and limited validation studies. The HALF-IT score is a novel, simplified, dichotomized triaging tool focusing solely on the brainstem level. This study investigated the utility of the HALF-IT score to predict functional outcomes of EVT in patients with BAO. Methods We conducted a multicenter, retrospective, cohort study including patients with acute BAO presenting to four comprehensive stroke centers between 2021-2025. Acute infarction of ≥50% of any brainstem section on any axial or coronal slice of MRI was considered HALF-IT positive, whereas < 50% was considered HALF-IT negative. The primary efficacy outcome was a favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days; functional independence (mRS 0-2) was analyzed as a secondary outcome. Reperfusion was graded with the modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) scale. Primary safety endpoints included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage at 24 h and all-cause mortality at 90 days. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of the primary efficacy outcome. Results 37 patients (23 HALF-IT negative; 14 HALF-IT positive) met the inclusion criteria. The rate of 90-day mRS 0-3 was significantly lower in the HALF-IT positive compared with HALF-IT negative group [14.3% vs. 68.2%, OR 0.08 (0.01-0.45), p = 0.004]. HALF-IT positive status remained associated with a lower rate of 90-day mRS 0-3 after adjusting for age, initial NIHSS, onset-to-reperfusion time, intravenous thrombolysis administration complete reperfusion (final mTICI 3) [adjusted OR 0.02, 95% CI 0-0.84, p = 0.02]. Safety events were numerically higher in the HALF-IT positive group but the difference did not reach statistical significance. The two groups differed substantially at baseline in age, presenting NIHSS, and intravenous thrombolysis exposure, whereas stroke etiology (p = 0.28) and level of basilar occlusion (p = 0.63) were similarly distributed. Conclusion In this small, retrospective, hypothesis-generating cohort, HALF-IT positivity was associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes after EVT for BAO. Further prospective validation in larger cohorts is required before the score can inform treatment decisions.

papers.title: Neurologist-focused workflows for immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome in CAR T-cell therapy and CD3-engaging bispecific antibodies.
papers.authors: Alesefir W, Hejazi M, Alashger B, Abodahab A, Abdelrazek M, Abouelnaga K, Koudeimati S, Alshibani A, Aljohani L.
papers.abstract: Objective To synthesize current evidence into a neurologist-focused workflow for early recognition, bedside monitoring, diagnostic triage, mitigation, and therapy-specific surveillance of immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar were searched in English from inception through 25 March 2026. Of 201 records, 18 duplicates were removed, 183 were screened, 157 full texts were assessed, and 26 studies were included in a narrative synthesis. The selection process was reported using applicable PRISMA 2020 elements and the narrative presentation was evaluated using SANRA. Results Evidence supports early neurologic co-management in selected high-risk patients, serial language- and attention-sensitive bedside assessment, and clinically triggered rather than routine electroencephalography. Pilot neurocognitive data suggest that subtle decline may precede deterioration on the Immune Effector Cell-Associated Encephalopathy (ICE) score. Bispecific-antibody programs generally show lower neurotoxicity burdens than many CAR T-cell platforms but create repeated risk windows around step-up dosing and outpatient transition. Delayed B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-associated movement and neurocognitive syndromes remain an important safety signal, although therapeutic evidence is largely observational or case based. Conclusion The evidence supports documenting a baseline neurologic phenotype, performing serial bedside monitoring, deploying electroencephalography and neuroimaging when results may change management, and maintaining product-specific vigilance for delayed syndromes. Tiered pathways are needed for community and resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Association of endovascular treatment versus intravenous thrombolysis in mild stroke across occlusion subgroups.
papers.authors: Xing GP, Li XL, Wang TT, Chen HS.
papers.abstract: Background The benefit of endovascular treatment (EVT) vs. intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is uncertain in minor stroke patients (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] ≤ 5) with anterior large vessel occlusion (LVO). Methods The pooled cohort consisted of patients with NIHSS ≤ 5 and internal carotid artery (ICA), M1 or M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) from the DETECT2-China study and the Early antiplatelet for minor stroke following thrombolysis (EAST) trial. The primary efficacy outcome was excellent functional outcome, defined as a mRS 0-1 at 90 days. The primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). Subgroup analyses were performed using interaction terms in logistic regression models to assess effect modification by baseline variable. To further explore the subgroup findings, analyses were repeated separately in patients with ICA/MCA-M1 occlusion and those with MCA-M2 occlusion. Results A total of 237 patients were enrolled, including 105 (44.3%) with the IVT group, 132 (55.7%) with the EVT group. Compared to the IVT group, the EVT group had a similar proportion of excellent functional outcome (73.5% vs. 75.2%, aOR = 0.749, 95% CI = 0.392-1.433, p = 0.383), a numerically higher proportion of sICH (1.9% vs. 6.1%, aOR = 4.158, 95% CI = 0.819-21.127, p = 0.086). Subgroup analysis revealed that a numerically increased odds of excellent functional outcome was found in patients with ICA or MCA-M1 occlusion who received EVT vs. IVT (79.4% vs. 67.2%, aOR = 1.491, 95% CI: 0.693-3.211; p = 0.307), whereas significantly less probability of excellent functional outcome in those with MCA-M2 occlusion who received EVT vs. IVT (53.3% vs. 86.4%, aOR = 0.250, 95% CI: 0.057-0.980, p = 0.050). A significant interaction effect was identified between treatment (EVT vs. IVT) and excellent functional outcome (p for interaction = 0.008). Conclusion In this exploratory analysis, the association between reperfusion strategy and functional outcome differed according to occlusion site. Patients with proximal occlusions (ICA or MCA-M1) in the EVT cohort had numerically better outcomes, whereas those with M2 occlusions in the EVT cohort had worse outcomes compared with the IVT cohort.

papers.title: Tongxinluo is associated with neurovascular changes following rt-PA-treated ischemic stroke: associations with inflammation, vascular remodeling, and neural plasticity.
papers.authors: Xiao M, Ding W, Zuo X, Tao H.
papers.abstract: Background Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) is the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke but is often limited by microvascular obstruction and reperfusion injury. Tongxinluo (TXL) has demonstrated neuroprotective potential, yet its association with neurovascular responses during rt-PA-associated reperfusion remains incompletely characterized. Methods Because reperfusion was achieved by filament withdrawal before rt-PA administration, this model evaluates TXL-associated effects during mechanically induced reperfusion with rt-PA exposure rather than enhancement of rt-PA-mediated thrombolysis. Animals were randomized into Sham, MCAO, MCAO + rt-PA, and MCAO + rt-PA + TXL (low/high dose) groups. Neurological outcomes were assessed longitudinally. Cerebral perfusion was monitored using laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI). Mechanistic analyses included assessments of blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, oxidative stress, microglial activation, angiogenesis, mitochondrial function, apoptosis, and synaptic plasticity markers (BDNF, GAP-43, and Synapsin I) using histological, biochemical, and molecular techniques. Results Adjunctive TXL treatment was associated with improved neurological outcomes and reduced infarct volume compared with rt-PA alone, with dose-dependent trends observed. TXL was associated with improved cortical microvascular perfusion and reduced severity of the no-reflow phenomenon. Mechanistically, TXL suppressed microglia-mediated neuroinflammation (downregulating TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) and preserved BBB integrity. This anti-inflammatory environment facilitated angiogenic maturation, evidenced by increased microvessel density and lumen formation. Furthermore, TXL stabilized mitochondrial function, inhibited neuronal apoptosis, and upregulated BDNF, GAP-43, and Synapsin I, leading to significant restoration of dendritic spine density. Conclusion TXL may provide adjunctive neuroprotective effects in the context of rt-PA treatment by modulating inflammatory, vascular-associated, and neuronal recovery responses. These findings support further investigation of TXL as a complementary therapy following reperfusion. By concurrently suppressing neuroinflammation and promoting vascular and synaptic reconstruction, TXL translates multi-target modulation into robust functional recovery, supporting its potential as a strategic combination therapy for acute ischemic stroke.

papers.title: Diagnostic value of susceptibility-based imaging and apparent diffusion coefficient for differentiating multiple system atrophy-Parkinsonian type from Parkinson's disease.
papers.authors: Moon B, Won SY, Youn J, Seo Y, Youn J, Kim EY, Lee J, Sohn B.
papers.abstract: Objective To characterize the diagnostic performance of susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI), χ-separation-derived paramagnetic susceptibility (χpara ), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) for differentiating multiple system atrophy-Parkinsonian type (MSA-P) from Parkinson's disease (PD). Materials and methods This retrospective case-control study included 27 drug-naïve patients with MSA-P and 27 age- and sex-matched drug-naïve patients with PD. Clinical diagnosis by board-certified neurologists served as the reference standard. χpara maps were generated from multi-echo gradient-recalled echo images using χ-separation, and ADC maps were derived from diffusion-weighted imaging. Two blinded radiologists qualitatively assessed SWI and ADC images using prespecified putaminal criteria. Quantitative analyses included voxel-wise group comparison and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis using mean region-of-interest (ROI) values. Candidate logistic-regression models were assessed using leave-one-out cross-validation. Results Qualitative assessment yielded sensitivity (85.2%), specificity (100%) and accuracy (92.6%) for SWI; the corresponding ADC assessments were 70.4%, 77.8% and 74.1%, respectively. Voxel-wise χpara analysis revealed a rim-shaped susceptibility increase in the posterior putamen, whereas ADC differences were localized to cerebellar white matter, including the middle cerebellar peduncle (MCP). In ROI-based classification, putaminal χpara yielded a sensitivity of 92.6% and ADC of the MCP showed a specificity of 96.3%. An exploratory model combining putaminal χpara and ADC in the MCP yielded a leave-one-out cross-validation AUC of 0.927. Conclusion By evaluating susceptibility-based imaging and ADC in the same cohort, this study characterized their respective regional imaging features and diagnostic performance for differentiating MSA-P from PD. χpara revealed an observed rim-shaped susceptibility pattern in the posterior putamen, supporting further evaluation of this pattern as a candidate imaging finding in MSA-P.

papers.title: Association between red blood cell count and cortical functional connectivity in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients residing at high altitude: resting-state fMRI study in the Tibetan Plateau.
papers.authors: Meng J, Gao Y, Li H, Feng L, Li X, Zhou Z, Hu X, Li H, He Y, Guo Y, Luo X, He W, Wu Y, Huang X.
papers.abstract: Background Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with cognitive dysfunction and emotional disturbances, in which the hippocampus and amygdala are key limbic structures. We investigated hippocampal and amygdala functional connectivity (FC) in Tibetan patients with T2DM residing in a high-altitude hypoxic environment and examined associations with clinical and biochemical measures. Methods We included 87 Tibetan patients with T2DM and 63 healthy controls (HC) from the Tibetan Plateau. Seed-based resting-state FC analysis was used to compare whole-brain hippocampal and amygdala FC between groups. Associations between altered FC and biochemical indices, emotional symptoms, and cognitive performance were assessed using Pearson or Spearman correlation analyses. Results Compared with HC, Tibetan patients with T2DM showed increased FC between the right hippocampus and the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC)/superior frontal gyrus and between the left amygdala and the right orbitofrontal cortex (OFC)/right DLPFC. Within the T2DM group, hippocampal FC was positively associated with red blood cell (RBC) count and visuospatial memory scores, whereas amygdala FC was positively associated with visuospatial memory scores and Mini-Mental State Examination scores. Conclusion Tibetan patients with T2DM showed increased hippocampal and amygdala FC, which was associated with RBC count and memory-related cognitive performance. No significant associations were observed between altered FC and blood glucose measures. These findings characterize limbic-prefrontal connectivity alterations and their clinical associations in this high-altitude Tibetan T2DM cohort.

papers.title: White matter differences in adults with developmental language disorder
papers.authors: Abbott N, Banel S, Cler GJ.
papers.abstract: Developmental language disorder is a highly common yet underdiagnosed neurodevelopmental disorder which impacts receptive and/or expressive language abilities and cannot be attributed to another etiology such as hearing loss or a lack of early exposure to language. There is very little research into the brain differences that characterize developmental language disorder, especially in adult populations In this study, we used diffusion MRI to determine whether adults with DLD show differences in white matter microstructure of the brain when compared to adults with typical language. Participants included 23 adults identified as meeting criteria for developmental language disorder, as well as a group of 26 adults with typical language. White matter microstructure was examined with fractional anisotropy via diffusion tensor imaging and precise biophysical models of intra-axonal signal fraction and orientation coherence via the Standard Model of diffusion imaging, using tractometry to evaluate microstructure differences along white matter tracts. Analysis showed reduced myelin integrity in DLD in the corpus callosum, but increased myelin integrity in the left superior longitudinal fasciculus. It is yet unclear whether differences exist in childhood and are retained into adulthood, are a result of different language environments during childhood, or are a result of behavioral and neural compensation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注成人发展性语言障碍（DLD）是否存在脑白质微结构差异，采用弥散MRI比较了DLD成人与典型语言成人的白质纤维束特征。结果显示，DLD组在胼胝体处髓鞘完整性降低，而左侧上纵束的髓鞘完整性反而升高，提示白质差异并非单一方向的普遍异常。作者指出，目前尚不清楚这些差异是童年期已存在并延续至成年，还是源于童年语言环境不同或行为与神经代偿的结果，因此相关发现仍需谨慎解读。

papers.title: Humanizing AI-generated exemplars: Human-source framing facilitates group creative ideation
papers.authors: Xiaoyong S, Lu Y, Liu Y, Ge Y, Ruan Q, Jiang K, KelongLu.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated creative exemplars are increasingly used as scalable digital instructional resources in creativity education. However, it remains unclear whether labeling identical exemplars as human- or AI-generated shapes how learners engage in group creative activities. We tested this possibility in 113 dyads using an fNIRS hyperscanning group creative ideation paradigm. Dyads completed creative ideation tasks before, during, and after exemplar-stimulation. During stimulation, the human- and AI-attribution groups received identical exemplars labeled as produced by human or AI, whereas the control group received no exemplar. Human attribution increased idea uniqueness during stimulation relative to both the other phases and the AI-attribution and control groups. AI attribution temporarily increased switching among ideation pathways. Neither behavioral effect persisted after exemplar withdrawal. The two attribution groups did not differ in exemplar-category overlap or nearest-exemplar semantic distance, but human-attribution dyads rated the exemplars as more helpful. Human attribution also increased interbrain synchronization (IBS) in bilateral premotor and supplementary motor cortices during stimulation, whereas AI attribution was associated with decreased IBS in the left supramarginal gyrus and right frontopolar cortex from pre- to post-stimulation. Thus, exemplar-source attribution shapes the process and outcome of group creative ideation, revealing an important social-contextual factor in AI-supported creativity education.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察将相同的AI生成创意范例标注为人类或AI来源，是否会改变小组创造性构思的过程与结果。研究以双人小组完成构思任务，并在范例呈现前后及期间进行测量。结果显示，标注为人类来源时，范例呈现期间想法的独特性高于其他阶段及AI标注组和对照组，且被试认为范例更有帮助；AI标注则暂时增加构思路径间的切换。两种行为效应在范例撤除后均未持续，两组在范例类别重叠和语义距离上也无差异。脑间同步方面，人类标注组在范例呈现期间运动前区和辅助运动区的同步增强，AI标注组则在后测阶段出现部分脑区同步下降。作者据此认为，来源标注这一社会情境因素会影响AI辅助创意教育中的小组构思。

papers.title: MRI-Guided High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound in Movement Disorders: Targeting Pathologic Brain Circuits With Precision Imaging, From the AJR Special Series on Critical Anatomy.
papers.authors: Asturias A, Saez-Calveras N, Yu J, Feltrin F, Jha M, Sharma V, Maldjian JA, O'Suillebhain P, Shah BR.
papers.abstract: MRI-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (MRgHIFU) has emerged as an alternative to other neuromodulatory interventions for patients with medically refractory movement disorders, including open surgery, radiosurgery, and deep brain stimulation. Microelectrode recordings permit refinement of indirect targets during open procedures for movement disorders. However, their use is not possible during incisionless procedures, including MRgHIFU. Traditional MRgHIFU using indirect targets yields limited efficacy or adverse effects from anatomic or functional variability. Furthermore, the clinical efficacy associated with indirect targeting of subcortical gray matter structures is increasingly recognized as resulting from circuitwide neuromodulation distributed along white matter pathways. Additionally, diffusion tensor imaging tractography and white matter-nulled sequences (e.g., fast gray matter acquisition T1 inversion recovery) now enable patient-specific targeting of pathologic brain circuits. These developments are prompting growing interest in MRgHIFU for direct targeting of disease-specific white matter tracts. In essential tremor, dentatorubrothalamic tract targeting by MRgHIFU has shown high tremor suppression with few adverse effects; in Parkinson disease, pallidothalamic tract targeting has likewise emerged as a promising intervention. These tract-based approaches can leverage patient-specific targeting to improve precision, efficacy, and safety. Future developments, including artificial intelligence-driven approaches, are expected to enhance MRgHIFU targeting and broaden its role in personalized movement disorder therapy.
papers.summary_zh: 该文综述了磁共振引导高强度聚焦超声（MRgHIFU）在药物难治性运动障碍中的靶向策略进展。文章指出，传统间接靶点因解剖与功能变异而疗效有限或带来不良反应，且皮层下灰质靶点的临床效果日益被认为源于沿白质通路分布的环路调控；弥散张量成像纤维束示踪与白质抑制序列使患者个体化的病理环路直接靶向成为可能。在特发性震颤中靶向齿状核-红核-丘脑束、在帕金森病中靶向苍白球-丘脑束已显示出较好前景，这类基于纤维束的方法有望借助个体化靶向提升精准性、疗效与安全性，未来人工智能驱动的方法可能进一步拓展其应用。

papers.title: Severe Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy and Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Following Accidental Butane Exposure: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Tiburzi SP, Nistico' R, Stivala V, De Luca A, Justiz-Pérez I, Putignano A, Vescio V.
papers.abstract: Background Butane is a highly lipophilic aliphatic hydrocarbon widely used as a domestic fuel and aerosol propellant. Acute exposure in enclosed environments may cause severe neurological and cardiovascular toxicity through oxygen displacement, respiratory depression, myocardial sensitisation to catecholamines, and potentially direct toxic effects. Case presentation A 45-year-old woman was found unconscious in a small, closed studio apartment, while her husband was found deceased in the same environment. Subsequent inspection by the judicial authorities identified deterioration of the gas tubing associated with a gas leak. The patient presented in deep coma (Glasgow Coma Scale score 5) and required tracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation. Initial carboxyhaemoglobin was 16.9% and progressively normalised during oxygen therapy. Brain imaging demonstrated extensive cortical, deep grey matter, brainstem, cerebellar, and white-matter abnormalities consistent with severe hypoxic-ischaemic injury. Cardiac evaluation showed mild ST-segment elevation, increased cardiac biomarkers, and severe transient Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction (LVEF 25%) with a pattern highly suggestive of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy; LVEF subsequently improved to 44%. Severe neurological impairment persisted, and the patient was transferred to neurological rehabilitation. She died approximately six months after the index event; reliable documentation of the precise cause of death was unavailable. Conclusion This case illustrates the severe neurological and cardiovascular consequences that may follow accidental butane exposure in an enclosed environment. The coexistence of extensive hypoxic- ischaemic brain injury and transient stress-related ventricular dysfunction highlights the importance of integrated neurological, cardiological, and toxicological assessment.
papers.summary_zh: 该病例报告描述一名45岁女性在密闭房间内意外暴露于泄漏丁烷后深度昏迷，需气管插管和机械通气，其丈夫在同一环境中死亡。脑影像显示广泛皮层、深部灰质、脑干、小脑及白质异常，符合严重缺氧缺血性损伤；心脏评估见轻度ST段抬高、心肌标志物升高及短暂严重左室收缩功能障碍，表现高度提示Takotsubo心肌病，左室射血分数随后有所改善。患者严重神经功能损害持续存在，转至神经康复，约六个月后死亡，但确切死因记录不可靠。作者据此提示密闭环境丁烷暴露可同时造成严重缺氧缺血性脑损伤和短暂应激相关心室功能障碍，强调神经、心脏与毒理综合评估的重要性。

papers.title: Mechanistic Disruption of the Blood-Brain Barrier and Neurovascular Unit by Lead, Manganese, and Cadmium: A WHO-WHY-WHAT-WHEN-WHERE-HOW Structured Review.
papers.authors: Lara-Estrada R, Molina-Gonzalez M, González-Santoyo I, Diaz-Ruiz A, Rios C, Horton M, Roldan-Valadez E.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposure to lead (Pb), manganese (Mn), and cadmium (Cd) damages the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) and the Neurovascular Unit (NVU) through a combination of pathways, including endothelial and astrocyte remodeling, transport dysregulation, oxidative and inflammatory signaling, and altered astrocyte-pericyte control of capillary tone. These changes lead to impaired neurovascular coupling and reduced cerebral blood flow. We collated and synthesized mechanistic evidence from experimental and clinical studies conducted over the 30 years from 1995 to 2025, focusing on studies that reported quantitative environmental exposure data and measured neuroimaging correlates of NVU/BBB injury. Cognitive deficits are associated with low-level blood lead levels (<5-10 μg/dL); blood manganese (Mn) levels of 4-15 μg/L are associated with neurodegeneration. Cadmium (Cd) is a cumulative neurotoxicity biomarker linked to cognitive deficits. Hair Mn tracks chronic inhalation exposure more closely than blood Mn does, and the gap between the two measures suggests that cerebral targets receive more manganese than systemic concentrations imply. Neuroimaging corroborates these mechanistic pathways, documenting region-specific cortical and subcortical volume loss, altered brain perfusion, and changes consistent with inflammatory signaling and with endothelial and astrocyte remodeling. Pallidal T1-weighted MRI and Arterial Spin-Labeling (ASL) perfusion MRI both perform well as neuroimaging biomarkers. Multimetal exposure biomarkers are more indicative of the mixture effect than single metal biomarkers. Longitudinal, mechanistic, and quantitative analyses indicate potential to develop interventions in exposed populations.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述梳理了1995至2025年间实验与临床研究中的机制证据，聚焦铅、锰、镉暴露如何通过内皮与星形胶质细胞重塑、转运失调、氧化与炎症信号以及星形胶质细胞—周细胞对毛细血管张力的调控改变，破坏血脑屏障和神经血管单元，进而损害神经血管耦合、降低脑血流。作者指出，低水平血铅、一定范围的血锰以及作为累积性神经毒性标志物的镉均与认知缺陷相关，而发锰比血锰更能反映慢性吸入暴露，提示脑内锰负荷可能高于系统浓度所显示的水平。神经影像结果与上述通路相印证，并显示钯部T1加权MRI和动脉自旋标记灌注MRI可作为表现较好的影像标志物；多种金属暴露标志物比单一金属标志物更能反映混合暴露效应。综述据此认为，纵向、机制性和定量分析为在暴露人群中开发干预措施提供了可能。

papers.title: Cellular senescence changes and their association with brain structure in schizophrenia and major depressive disorder
papers.authors: Okada N, Seitz-Holland J, Ikegame T, Omileke F, Kiyota M, Shoji E, Mori S, Morita S, Koshiyama D, Satomura Y, Koike S, JINDE S, Yagishita S, Kamiya K, Abe O, Shenton M, Kubicki M, Kasai K.
papers.abstract: Abstract Individuals with schizophrenia (SZ) and major depressive disorder (MDD) may experience accelerated biological aging, potentially linked to cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). While the SASP index has been reported to be elevated in MDD, its status in SZ and its relationship with brain structure remain unclear. This study investigated whether the SASP index, a composite biomarker-based measure, is elevated in SZ and MDD, and examined its associations with brain-predicted age difference (brain-PAD) and regional brain morphology across SZ, MDD, and healthy controls (HCs). A total of 119 subjects (29 individuals with SZ, 40 individuals with MDD, and 50 HCs) underwent both peripheral blood collection and MRI scanning. First, across all subjects, the effects of diagnostic groups on SASP indices were assessed. Second, associations between age-adjusted SASP indices and brain-PAD were examined within each diagnostic group. Third, exploratory analyses tested associations between SASP indices and subcortical volumes as well as cortical thickness and surface area in each diagnostic group. We found a significant main effect of diagnostic group on SASP indices and significantly elevated SASP indices in both SZ and MDD. Although no significant associations were observed between SASP indices and brain-PAD in any diagnostic group, negative associations were identified in SZ between SASP indices and the surface area of the left transverse temporal gyrus and the right inferior frontal gyrus pars triangularis, regions that play pivotal roles in auditory and language processing alterations observed in SZ. These findings suggest that SASP-related processes may contribute to the neural underpinnings of SZ through localized, rather than global, alterations in brain structure.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究比较精神分裂症患者、重性抑郁障碍患者与健康对照者的衰老相关分泌表型（SASP）综合指标，并考察其与脑预测年龄差及局部脑形态的关系。结果发现，两种患者组的SASP指标均显著高于健康对照，但该指标与脑预测年龄差在任何组中均无显著关联。在精神分裂症患者中，SASP指标与左侧颞横回及右侧额下回三角部皮层表面积呈负相关，这些区域与听觉和语言加工有关。作者据此提出，SASP相关过程可能通过局部而非全局的脑结构改变，参与精神分裂症的神经基础；相关发现尚属关联性，不能推断因果。

papers.title: Beyond Gray Matter: White Matter Functional Network Signatures of Major Depressive Disorder Track Symptom Severity
papers.authors: Calhoun V, Sridhar M, Baker B.
papers.abstract: Abstract Resting-state neuroimaging studies in major depressive disorder (MDD) have consistently identified abnormalities across large-scale gray matter (GM) networks, including the default mode, salience, and sensorimotor systems. Although prior work has primarily focused on GM, evidence suggests that white matter (WM) hemodynamic signals are meaningful and reliable, supporting an active role for WM in brain function. A key gap remains in understanding WM functional network connectivity (FNC) and spectral characteristics in MDD. We used resting-state fMRI scans from the MDD-DIRECT phase II study, comprising 1,944 participants across 13 sites, to examine WM FNC and spectral characteristics in individuals with MDD and healthy controls using a spatially constrained independent component analysis (ICA) framework. This hybrid framework leverages ICA’s ability to identify spatially robust, functionally meaningful brain networks guided by replicable spatial priors to examine WM (1) FNC differences and (2) spectral power alterations between MDD and healthy participants. MDD was characterized by reduced long-range integrative connectivity alongside increased localized and limbic–sensorimotor coupling within WM networks, highlighting a systems-level imbalance in neural communication that may underlie core cognitive, affective, and somatic symptoms of depression. We also observed reduced low-frequency spectral power within frontal and subcortical WM systems involved in cognitive control, emotional regulation, and decision-making. Notably, both functional and spectral alterations were associated with clinical measures of depression and anxiety, with opposing associations observed for frontal connectivity patterns. Studying WM function alongside GM may provide a more comprehensive understanding of functional pathology in depression.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注重性抑郁障碍中白质功能网络连接与频谱特征是否异常，利用静息态功能磁共振数据，在白质空间先验引导下用独立成分分析比较患者与健康对照。结果显示，患者白质网络表现为长程整合连接减弱、局部及边缘系统—感觉运动耦合增强，提示系统层面的神经通讯失衡；同时，参与认知控制、情绪调节和决策的额叶及皮层下白质低频功率降低。这些功能与频谱改变同抑郁和焦虑的临床测量相关，且额叶连接模式呈现方向相反的关联。作者认为，结合白质与灰质功能有助于更全面地理解抑郁的功能病理，但相关发现尚属关联层面。

papers.title: Frequency-Specific Age Associations in EEG Microstate Dynamics Across the Adult Lifespan
papers.authors: Sanjar K, Tarailis P, Griskova-Bulanova I.
papers.abstract: Abstract EEG microstates are conventionally derived from broadband signals, although their temporal dynamics may differ across frequency ranges. Whether age associations in conventional voltage microstates are similarly frequency specific remains unclear. We examined resting-state EEG from 60 healthy adults aged 20–78 years and derived microstates separately from broadband (1–30 Hz), delta (1–4 Hz), theta (4–8 Hz), alpha (8–12 Hz), and beta (15–30 Hz) activity. The number of microstates was selected independently for each band using the Krzanowski–Lai criterion, yielding four classes for broadband, delta, alpha, and beta, and five for theta. Age associations were tested for duration, occurrence, coverage, global explained variance, observed transition probabilities, and transitions adjusted for those expected from class prevalence, with false-discovery-rate correction. Age associations showed a marked spectral dependence. Of 84 state-level tests, 13 survived correction: one in broadband, six in delta, one in theta, none in alpha, and five in beta. In delta, increasing age was associated with greater expression of MS B and reduced expression of MS C across duration, occurrence, and coverage. In beta, age was associated with greater MS A expression and reduced MS C expression. All significant state-level associations remained after adjustment for sex, education, and band-specific spectral power. Eight observed transition associations survived correction, all in broadband and delta, but only three remained after accounting for transitions expected from state prevalence. These findings indicate that age-related variation in EEG microstate dynamics is strongly frequency-specific and is expressed primarily through redistribution of state expression rather than through widespread alteration of transition preference. Frequency-resolved microstate analysis, hence, reveals age associations that are not evident in conventional broadband analysis.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察健康成人静息态脑电微状态的年龄关联是否随频段而异，分别从宽带及delta、theta、alpha、beta频段提取微状态，并检验其多项动态指标与年龄的关系。结果显示年龄关联具有明显的频谱依赖性：显著结果主要集中在delta和beta频段，表现为不同微状态表达量的此消彼长，而非转移偏好的普遍改变；这些关联在控制性别、教育程度和频段功率后仍存在。作者据此指出，分频段分析能揭示传统宽带分析未显现的年龄差异，提示微状态动态的年龄变化需结合频率成分理解。

papers.title: Rapid parameter-efficient calibration for cross-session intracortical speech decoding across multiple datasets
papers.authors: Roy D, Tabassum F, Mozumder R.
papers.abstract: Abstract Intracortical speech brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) can restore communication for people who cannot speak, but longitudinal neural variability can degrade decoding across sessions. We implemented a parameter-efficient cross-session calibration framework using separate recurrent connectionist temporal classification (CTC) decoders for two public intracortical speech datasets (T12 and T15). Adaptation was restricted to a 256 × 256 affine transformation and bias at the neural input, while the recurrent encoder and CTC classifier remained frozen. Sessions were split chronologically; the calibration protocol was selected only on T12 validation sessions, frozen before later T12 testing, and transferred unchanged to T15. Only 65,792 parameters (<0.05% of either model) were updated using 40 or 80 labeled trials. On T12, macro phoneme error rate improved by 11.37% and 15.51%, with all six held-out sessions improving under all three seeds. On T15, improvements were 2.72% and 10.05%, revealing greater session dependence. Extending prior work on high-performance and rapidly calibrating speech neuroprostheses, this study tests a fixed lightweight calibration rule across two independent datasets under a validation-locked protocol. These findings provide a leakage-resistant cross-dataset evaluation of rapid longitudinal recalibration and show that input-space adaptation can recover a substantial, but not universal, component of cross-session mismatch.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对皮层内语音脑机接口在跨会话使用中因神经信号变化而解码性能下降的问题，提出一种参数高效的校准框架，并在两个公开数据集上检验其效果。方法上，作者冻结循环编码器和CTC分类器，仅用少量标注试次更新神经输入端的仿射变换和偏置，且校准方案先在一个数据集上选定并锁定，再原样迁移到另一数据集。结果显示，该校准在两个数据集上均能改善音素错误率，但改善幅度因会话而异，说明输入空间适配只能恢复跨会话失配中的一部分而非全部。作者据此强调，这是一种避免信息泄漏的跨数据集评估，支持轻量校准的实用价值，同时保留了其效果不具普遍性的限定。

papers.title: The Application of Video‑Electroencephalographic Monitoring Combined with Multimodal Imaging in Surgical Management of Secondary Epilepsy in Children
papers.authors: Jing X, Yao C, Zhang W, Zhou J, Wang C.
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective To explore the clinical value of video‑electroencephalography (VEEG) coupled with multimodal imaging for pre‑surgical epileptogenic‑zone localization, surgical planning and prognostic evaluation in children with drug‑resistant epilepsy. Methods : A retrospective analysis was performed on 42 pediatric patients who underwent epilepsy surgery. Pre‑operative workup included brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), long‑term scalp VEEG, and PET‑CT for selected participants. For diagnostically challenging cases, stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) depth electrodes or electrocorticography (ECoG) cortical electrodes were implanted to refine epileptogenic‑zone identification. Cortical electrical stimulation (CES) and somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) were applied to map eloquent brain regions. Intra‑operative cortical electrophysiological monitoring guided lesion resection. Individualized surgical strategies were adopted according to lesion characteristics. Post‑operative follow‑up spanned 1‑4 years, and seizure outcomes were assessed using the modified Engel classification. Results : ① Pre‑operative brain MRI revealed heterogeneous epileptogenic etiologies, most frequently temporal‑lobe signal abnormalities (17 cases) and focal cortical developmental anomalies (12 cases). ② Long‑term VEEG allowed detailed recording of background electroencephalographic rhythms; sleep markedly elevated the yield of interictal epileptiform discharges. Interictal discharges were captured in 35 patients, and spontaneous clinical seizure discharges were successfully recorded in 15 patients. ③ Among 21 patients receiving PET‑CT, focal hypometabolism was observed within most lesion territories. ④ Combined long‑term VEEG with intracranial SEEG/ECoG electrodes precisely delineated discharge onset zones, while functional‑mapping techniques ensured operative safety. ⑤ Ten distinct individualized surgical protocols were implemented tailored to underlying pathology. Intra‑operative ECoG detected sharp‑wave activity in 35 patients, informing the extent of surgical resection. ⑥ Integrating MRI findings with post‑surgical histopathology clarified the etiological diagnosis for all patients. ⑦ After 1‑4 years of follow‑up, 33 patients attained Engel class I outcomes, indicating satisfactory overall seizure control. Note: Developmental anomalies encompass structural malformations and signal alterations, collectively termed cortical developmental abnormalities herein. Conclusions :Video‑electroencephalography combined with multimodal imaging including MRI and PET‑CT enables reasonably accurate (though not absolute) dual anatomical‑electrophysiological localization of epileptogenic zones. This multimodal framework provides robust evidence for individualized surgical planning and bears considerable clinical utility.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究回顾性分析了42例接受手术的儿童药物难治性癫痫患者，探讨视频脑电图联合多模态影像在致痫区定位、手术规划及预后评估中的临床价值。术前检查包括脑磁共振、长程头皮视频脑电图及部分患者的PET-CT，对定位困难者进一步植入颅内电极，并结合皮层电刺激和体感诱发电位进行功能区定位。结果显示，长程视频脑电图可记录发作间期放电，睡眠明显提高其检出率，部分患者还捕捉到自发临床发作放电；联合颅内电极能较精确地勾勒放电起始区，术中皮层脑电图则有助于确定切除范围。术后随访1至4年，多数患者达到Engel I级，提示该多模态框架可为个体化手术方案提供依据，但作者强调其定位并非绝对精确。

papers.title: Effects of Metformin on Resting-State EEG and Associations with Adaptive Behaviors in Fragile X Syndrome
papers.authors: Lippé S, Buckser R, Davoudi S, Arutiunian V, Knoth ISK, Thurman A, Bélanger A, Martin C, Proteau-Lemieux M, Santos E, Rubanarayana K, Pham T, Whitlock K, Bennett J, Tassone F, Kim K, Biag H, Hessl D, Schneider A, Abbeduto L, Jacquemont S, Bolduc F, Hagerman R.
papers.abstract: Abstract Metformin has emerged as a candidate drug for Fragile X Syndrome (FXS) after promising results in animal studies and small-scale trials. A three-site registered clinical trial (RCT) demonstrated effects of metformin on behavioral symptoms in FXS in participants aged 6–11. Resting state electroencephalography (RS-EEG) was also collected during the RCT. We present results from analyses of RS-EEG and associated adaptive behavior measures. We observed significant metformin treatment effects on EEG measures associated with cortical excitation/inhibition balance (periodic gamma), brain maturation (periodic alpha), and signal complexity. Significantly affected EEG measures moved toward values associated with typical development. We also observed associations between more typical EEG activity and improved adaptive behavior scores in the treatment group. Additional significant effects and associations were observed when considering only participants without molecular mosaic. Results confirm metformin’s potential as a treatment option and encourage further research into its effects on functional brain activity.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于一项多中心注册临床试验，分析二甲双胍对6至11岁脆性X综合征儿童静息态脑电及适应性行为的影响。结果显示，二甲双胍显著改变了与皮层兴奋/抑制平衡、脑成熟和信号复杂度相关的脑电指标，且这些变化朝向典型发育的方向；在治疗组中，更典型的脑电活动与适应性行为评分的改善相关。仅纳入无分子嵌合体的参与者时，还观察到其他显著效应和关联。作者认为这些结果支持二甲双胍作为潜在治疗选择，并提示需进一步研究其对脑功能活动的作用。

papers.title: Machine Learning Based Dyslexia Screening Using Multimodal Tests
papers.authors: Kawtikwar V, Hegde S, Pal AT, Pimpale H, Soni C.
papers.abstract: Dyslexia is a common problem that affects how people read and write. It is not because they are not smart. Because their brain works a little differently. It is really important to find out if someone has dyslexia so we can help them with their reading and writing. The problem is that the ways we have now to figure out if someone has dyslexia are not very good. They take a lot of time. Are not always right. In this paper we are talking about a way to find out if someone has dyslexia. This way uses computers to look at how people write and talk. We use something called Natural Language Processing to look at the words and sentences that people write. We also use something called Sequence-to-Sequence to look at the patterns in their writing. This helps us to see if someone has dyslexia or not. We tried out our way with some tests and it worked pretty well. It was able to tell if someone had dyslexia or not 63 percent of the time. This is really good because it means that we can use this way to help kids who have dyslexia. It is also a way because it is not too expensive. This means that teachers and parents can use it to help kids with dyslexia. Dyslexia is a problem that we can help with if we can just find out who has it. Our new way is a step, in the right direction. Dyslexia detection is important. Our system can help with dyslexia detection.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注如何更省时、准确地筛查阅读障碍，提出用计算机分析个体的书写和口语表现，借助自然语言处理考察用词与句子，并用序列到序列方法捕捉书写模式，据此判断是否存在阅读障碍。作者报告该方案在测试中的判别准确率约为63%，认为这一结果说明基于多模态语言特征的筛查具有可行性，且成本较低，便于教师和家长使用。需要留意的是，摘要未交代受试人群、测试规模与对照设置，63%的准确率也不足以支持其作为独立诊断工具，其实际筛查价值仍需进一步验证。

papers.title: Uncovering Latent Cognitive, Metacognitive, and Neural Bases of Problem-Solving Deficits in Children with Developmental Dyscalculia.
papers.authors: Lasnick OHM, Park Y, Mistry P, Menon V.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Developmental dyscalculia (DD) affects 7-10% of children and is characterized by persistent difficulties in arithmetic problem-solving, which depends on the dynamic interplay between cognitive and metacognitive control processes governing strategy execution and selection. Conventional behavioral and neuroimaging approaches do not simultaneously quantify these latent processes and link them to distributed neural mechanisms, leaving the neurocognitive and metacognitive underpinnings of DD insufficiently characterized. We integrated Bayesian computational modeling with whole-brain decoding to uncover cognitive, metacognitive, and neural bases of problem-solving deficits in DD using a sample of 68 children aged 8-10 years (38 female). Children with DD showed deficits across all problem-solving strategies (counting, retrieval, and decomposition), indicating reduced strategy execution efficiency. They also exhibited significant metacognitive impairments: longer baseline switching times between strategies, reduced sensitivity to problem difficulty, and lower adaptivity in selecting optimal strategies. Whole-brain Elastic Net decoding accurately distinguished DD from TA peers based on distributed activation patterns across frontoparietal cortex, hippocampus, and ventral-visual regions, whereas univariate approaches did not. Linear multivariate brain-behavioral analyses and nonlinear transformer-based predictions converged in showing that these distributed signatures predicted counting efficiency and switching sensitivity. Notably, brain-behavior relations reversed in direction between groups, positive in TA children but negative in DD, most strikingly in the hippocampus. These findings demonstrate that arithmetic difficulties in DD arise from deficits in both strategy execution efficiency and metacognitive control, reflecting an altered mapping between distributed neural activity, and highlight the power of integrating computational modeling with brain-wide decoding to understand learning disabilities.

papers.title: Time<sup>2</sup>: A Framework for the Neural Dynamics of Visual Perception.
papers.authors: Caplette L, Gosselin F.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Whenever we look at an object, we seem to perceive it immediately. However, this is not the case for two reasons. First, it takes hundreds of milliseconds for the brain to process visual information reaching the retina. Second, perceiving an object requires fixating it for some duration-typically hundreds of milliseconds-during which the retina continuously receives new visual information. These facts together imply that visual information is both processed and received through time. These two temporal facets of perception, which we term processing time and stimulus time, are often conflated in the literature, and rarely considered together in experiments. Here, we argue that, to obtain a more complete portrait of visual perception and further constrain models of vision, it is essential to consider and measure both temporal facets simultaneously. We present a new method designed to do so that is based on reverse correlation: Time2 We show that this method allows us to precisely characterize many neural phenomena, including rhythmic perception, predictive processing, and coarse-to-fine sampling.

papers.title: Context-Dependent Functional Diversity of Dorsomedial Posterior Parietal Neurons Revealed by Single-Unit FMRI Mapping during Naturalistic Viewing.
papers.authors: Zhou X, Wang L, Tam SKE, Ortiz-Rios M, Yin D, Kwok SC.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The dorsomedial posterior parietal cortex (dmPPC) plays an important role in episodic processing by integrating sensory, cognitive, and motor information across distributed brain systems. However, how individual dmPPC neurons participate in large-scale functional organization during naturalistic experience remains poorly understood. To address this question, we combined single-unit electrophysiology and awake fMRI in five rhesus macaques of both sexes viewing identical naturalistic video stimuli. Using single-unit fMRI mapping, we generated whole-brain neuron-BOLD functional maps by correlating individual neuronal activity with voxel-wise fMRI signals across the brain. We found that neuron-BOLD functional maps exhibited strong context-dependent organization, with neurons recorded during the same video context showing substantially greater similarity than neurons recorded during different video conditions. Compared with neuronal spiking activity or critical fMRI frames alone, neuron-BOLD functional maps more robustly captured contextual structure. Despite this shared large-scale organization, a substantial subset of neighboring neurons recorded simultaneously from the same electrode displayed markedly distinct whole-brain association patterns, revealing substantial local functional heterogeneity within the dmPPC. This local heterogeneity was not readily explained by waveform-based putative cell class or by opposing neuronal firing dynamics. In addition, distributed cortical and medial temporal regions exhibited highly context-dependent neuron-BOLD association patterns during naturalistic viewing. Together, these findings demonstrate that dmPPC neurons participate in dynamic and heterogeneous large-scale functional organization during naturalistic episodic processing. More broadly, this study establishes single-unit fMRI mapping as a framework for linking single-neuron activity to distributed whole-brain dynamics across contextual conditions.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注背内侧后顶叶皮层单个神经元在自然观看中如何参与全脑功能组织。作者在猕猴观看视频时结合单细胞电生理与清醒fMRI，将神经元活动与全脑BOLD信号相关。结果显示神经元-BOLD映射呈情境依赖组织，同一情境下记录的神经元相似性更高，且比单独放电或关键帧更能反映情境结构；但同一电极上相邻神经元的全脑关联模式差异明显，提示局部功能异质性，且难以由波形分类或放电动态解释。

papers.title: Cerebellar climbing fibers signal flexible, rapidly adapting reward predictions.
papers.authors: Vignali C, Mutersbaugh M, Hull C.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Classical models of cerebellar computation posit that climbing fibers (CFs) operate according to supervised learning rules, correcting movements by signaling the occurrence of motor errors. However, recent findings suggest that in some behaviors, CF activity can exhibit features that resemble the instructional signals necessary for reinforcement learning, namely reward prediction errors (rPEs). Despite these initial observations, many key properties of reward-related CF responses remain unclear, thus limiting our understanding of how they operate to guide cerebellar learning. Here, we have measured the postsynaptic responses of CFs onto cerebellar Purkinje cells using two-photon calcium imaging in mice of both sexes to test how CFs respond to learned stimuli that either do or do not predict reward. We find that CFs can develop generalized responses to similar cues of the same modality, regardless of whether they are reward predictive. However, the extent of this generalization depends on temporal context, and generalization does not extend across sensory modalities. Further, learned CF responses are flexible, and can be rapidly updated according to new reward contingencies. Together these results reveal two properties of learned CF responses: their generalization across similar cues is graded by the temporal and sensory context in which the cues are learned, and, when reward contingencies are reversed, they update rapidly to track new learning rules.Significance Statement The cerebellum is best known for coordinating movement, and the climbing fiber teaching signals thought to instruct cerebellar motor learning were long thought to report movement errors exclusively. Recent work has shown that these instructional signals can also convey information about reward. Here, by recording from these climbing fiber inputs in mice learning which cues predict reward, we find that they carry flexible, context-sensitive reward predictions. Notably, these signals do not simply track which cue an animal should respond to: they generalize across similar cues depending on context, and they rapidly reorganize when reward associations change. These properties resemble those of midbrain dopamine neurons, the brain's canonical reward system. These findings reframe how cerebellar teaching signals contribute to reward-guided learning.

papers.title: Voluntary movement initiation is associated with cardiac input in Libet's task.
papers.authors: Germanova K, Studenova A, Bredikhin D, Gippert M, Kapralov N, Klucharev V, Villringer A, Herrojo Ruiz M, Nikulin V.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: ​​The relationship between motor intention and initiation of voluntary movement remains a fundamental topic in neuroscience, originating from the seminal framework of B. Libet, introduced in 1983. Libet's paradigm significantly influenced discussions on intentionality, motor control, and free will. However, methodological critiques continue to challenge its interpretations, specifically the accuracy and validity of the 'urge to move' phenomenon. One understudied factor in this debate is the potential influence of interoceptive signals-such as cardiac activity-in shaping the experience of motor intention and movement initiation. In our study, we addressed this gap by examining whether cardiac signals modulate participants' experience of the 'urge to move', using behavioural and electrophysiological measures in 39 healthy human participants (17 males and 22 females) performing Libet's task. Crucially, when participants were asked to follow the 'urge to move', their button press timings were predominantly aligned with the diastolic phase of the cardiac cycle, indicating cardiac modulation of movement initiation. However, analysing heart evoked potential (HEP) amplitudes as a measure of cardiac input perception, we observed no differences in HEP amplitudes associated with changes in introspective demands during the task in both source and sensor spaces. Our results suggest that implicit perception of cardiac signals biases voluntary action initiation in Libet's task, independently of cortical interoceptive markers. These findings have implications for models of motor preparation, intentionality, and the bodily basis of voluntary action, challenging conventional interpretations of motor intention and informing debates on volition and interoception.Significance Statement Our study provides evidence that implicit perception of cardiac signals influences movement initiation in Libet's task. We demonstrate, for the first time, that when attending to the 'urge to move', participants tended to initiate voluntary movements during the diastolic phase of the cardiac cycle. These findings challenge traditional views on factors affecting motor initiation in Libet's task, suggesting the relevance of interoceptive processing. By highlighting the role of cardiac input in experiencing motor intention, our findings expand on existing debates on volition, agency, and free will, further underscoring the importance of integrating bodily signals into these theoretical frameworks.

papers.title: Dynamic Reduction of Neural Uncertainty Shapes Perceptual Decisions in a Bayes-Optimal Manner.
papers.authors: Rangelov D, Bitzer S, Mattingley JB.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Fast and accurate decisions are fundamental for adaptive behavior. Theories of decision-making posit that evidence in favor of different choices is gradually accumulated until a critical value is reached. It remains unclear, however, which aspects of the neural code get updated during evidence accumulation. Here we investigated whether evidence accumulation relies on a gradual increase in the precision of neural representations of sensory input (i.e., a decrease in neural uncertainty). Healthy human volunteers (N = 32, 24 females) discriminated global motion direction over a patch of moving dots, and their brain activity was recorded using electroencephalography. Time-resolved neural uncertainty was estimated using multivariate feature-specific analyses of brain activity. Behavioral measures were modeled using iterative Bayesian inference (BI) either on its own (i.e., the full model) or by swapping free model parameters with neural uncertainty estimates derived from brain recordings. The neurally restricted model was further refitted using randomly shuffled neural uncertainty. The full model and the unshuffled neural model yielded very good and comparable fits to the data, whereas the shuffled neural model yielded worse fits. Taken together, the findings reveal that the brain relies on reducing neural uncertainty during decision-making. They also provide neurobiological support for BI as a fundamental computational mechanism in support of decision-making.

papers.title: Individualized Network Topography in Pre-adolescent Children and Adults Using Naturalistic Precision fMRI.
papers.authors: Rai S, Godfrey KJ, Graff K, Tansey R, Merrikh D, Yin S, Feigelis M, Demeter DV, Vanderwal T, Greene DJ, Bray S.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Group-averaged network definitions, commonly used in developmental functional connectivity research, limit our understanding of how network topography may change with age and can lead to inaccurate estimates of age effects on intra- and inter-network functional connectivity. Here, we collected a precision fMRI dataset from 24 parent-child pairs (children 6-8 years, 13 females; adults 33-47 years, 12 females) during passive video viewing and derived individual template-matched functional network maps from 60 min of motion-censored data per participant. Overall, large-scale network architecture was broadly shared between children and adults, with no age effects observed for network-level surface area, few age differences in network boundaries, and generally lower assignment confidence in children. Considering interindividual similarity in network topography, association networks showed stronger within-family similarity and no overall effect of age on similarity of networks between pairs of individuals. We further asked how individualized network definitions might impact estimates of age effects on dense functional connectivity. While all approaches pointed to greater within-network functional connectivity in adults, we found that individualized approaches had larger age effects and lower sensitivity to head motion. Together, our results suggest that, relative to adults, preadolescent children show reduced network assignment confidence and weaker within-network connectivity but limited differences in network borders and size and underscore the value of individualized mapping for improving topographic reliability and increasing sensitivity to age effects.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究用自然观看视频的精准fMRI数据，为24对亲子（6至8岁儿童与33至47岁成人）构建个体化功能网络图谱，考察网络拓扑是否随年龄变化，以及个体化定义如何影响年龄效应估计。结果显示，儿童与成人的大规模网络架构大体共享，网络面积无年龄差异，边界差异很少，但儿童网络归属置信度较低；成人网络内连接更强。作者指出，个体化图谱可提高拓扑可靠性并更敏感地检出年龄效应，同时提示组平均定义可能低估发育差异。

papers.title: Microglial Presenilin-1 modulates neuronal function and memory-associated behaviors.
papers.authors: Frost PDS, Martinez CA, Millet A, McWhirt J, Cheng J, Bamkole M, Kim Y, Silva HM, Lafaille JJ, Azevedo EP, Stevens B, Ledo JH.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Microglial cells, the macrophages of the brain parenchyma, are increasingly recognized to play a key role in synaptic plasticity and function. Presenilin 1 (PS1) is an essential protein involved in learning and memory; the loss of neuronal Presenilin function causes cognitive deficits and impaired synapse plasticity in mice. Here we show memory enhancement in male mice lacking PS1 in microglia (PS1ΔMG ). Leveraging high-throughput RNA sequencing with single-cell deconvolution-analysis, we estimate that PS1ΔMG increases Cd52-lo microglial population, a proliferative group enriched in AP-1 responsive genes; and increases chemokines Ccl7 and Ccl8 In silico prediction of binding partners showed that microglial CCL7 may act via inhibition of neuronal CCR5, a receptor known to negatively regulate learning and memory. By profiling active neuronal populations via PhosphoTRAP the data showed a non-autonomous cell effect of microglial PS1 by modulating genes involved in neuronal excitability and synaptic plasticity. Ex vivo electrophysiology and in vivo calcium imaging in freely behaving mice confirm these effects with functional changes in CA1 hippocampus as seen by increased NMDA/AMPA ratios and increased amplitude of neuronal Ca2+ transients in freely behaving animals, respectively. Remarkably, PS1ΔMG mice exhibited increased memory retention in contextual fear conditioning and novel object recognition. Together, these data suggest a novel mechanism where microglial PS1 negatively regulates neuronal activity through modulation of NMDAR and memory-associated behaviors.Significance Statement Microglia are increasingly recognized as active regulators of neuronal function, yet the molecular mechanisms that constrain their influence on synaptic activity remain incompletely defined. This study identifies microglial Presenilin-1 (PS1) as a key regulator of neuron-microglia signaling that shapes synaptic transmission and learning. We show that loss of microglial PS1 shifts microglia toward a transcriptional and signaling state that enhances NMDA receptor-dependent synaptic activity and improves memory, demonstrating that microglial molecular programs can directly modulate neuronal excitability. These findings establish microglial PS1 as a physiological brake on circuit plasticity and reveal that altering microglial signaling alone is sufficient to influence cognition. Targeting microglial regulatory pathways may therefore provide new strategies to enhance synaptic resilience and cognitive function in brain disorders.

papers.title: Late Cross-Modal Biases in Neural Spatial Representations Revealed by EEG Decoding.
papers.authors: Buhmann Z, Robinson AK, Mattingley JB, Rideaux R.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: During audiovisual perception, spatial information from vision and audition is combined, often producing biases such as the ventriloquist effect. While these interactions are well documented behaviorally, it remains unclear when cross-modal information begins to alter modality-specific spatial representations in the brain. Here we used cross-generalized inverted encoding modeling of electroencephalography (EEG) data to track the temporal evolution of spatial representations during a spatial ventriloquist task. Human participants (both sexes) localized audiovisual stimuli with horizontally offset auditory and visual components. Decoders trained on unisensory EEG responses were applied to audiovisual trials to estimate whether and when spatial representations of one modality were biased toward the other. Behaviorally, participants integrated cues but showed slight visual overweighting. Neural decoding revealed robust spatial representations for both modalities, with early unisensory encoding remaining unaffected by cross-modal input. Cross-modal biases emerged only later (from ∼200 ms onward), within a generalized representational window, and occurred sequentially: auditory representations were biased earlier than visual. These findings indicate that multisensory spatial integration arises via recurrent feedback during later processing stages, while early sensory-specific representations remain independent, providing a neural basis for the temporal dynamics underlying the ventriloquist effect.

papers.title: A Parietal Grid-Like Code Rotates with Cognitive Maps But Lags Rapid Behavioral Transfer.
papers.authors: Yu LQ, Vaidya AR, Akhmetzhanova AA, Bruinsma S, Nassar MR.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The neural grid code has been proposed to provide a mechanism for generalization and transfer of relational knowledge between situations enabling rapid adaptation of behavior in novel circumstances. However, to date, very little is known about the dynamics with which grid representations change at context transitions or how such dynamics relate to downstream behavioral adaptation. Here we tested whether grid representations measured with fMRI rotate to match behavioral goals at context transitions and whether such rotations underlie knowledge transfer. Human participants (25 females and 23 males) performed a task that included unsignaled state changes at which the position of multiple target locations abruptly and synchronously rotated by the same degree. After state changes, participants were able to leverage the relative positions of the targets to rapidly infer locations, even novel ones, constituting a form of zero-shot transfer. We observed a cognitive grid-like code in the right posterior parietal cortex with a consistent phase angle that rotated with the relative positions of the targets. However, this rotation was too slow to account for rapid improvements in performance after a state change, and instead these improvements were more closely related to representations of the identity and location of spatial targets in the frontoparietal and orbitofrontal cortex, respectively. Our results highlight the ability of humans to rapidly transfer knowledge and demonstrate that a parietal grid-like code rotates into behaviorally relevant reference frames but indicate that alternate neural mechanisms support rapid knowledge transfer.

papers.title: Short-term subjective and EEG responses following cervical rotatory manipulation are not reproduced by simulated cracking sound: A randomized controlled study.
papers.authors: Lin Y, Zhong W, Yu M, Yu Y, Tang L, Xue F, Wei J, Li J, Li Y.
papers.abstract: Background Cervical rotatory manipulation (CRM) is commonly used for neck-related symptoms and is often accompanied by a cracking sound. Whether a simulated cracking sound can reproduce the short-term subjective and neurophysiological responses to the complete CRM remains unclear. Objective This study compared short-term subjective and electroencephalography (EEG) responses to CRM with those following sham manipulation with or without a simulated cracking sound. Methods In this randomized controlled trial with three parallel groups and a single intervention session, 54 healthy volunteers were allocated to CRM, sham manipulation, or sham + simulated sound. Positive affect, negative affect, comfort, satisfaction, and eyes closed resting state EEG were assessed before and after the intervention. Prespecified EEG derived outcomes included frontal alpha power, frontal alpha/beta ratio, occipital individual alpha frequency, and alpha band frontoparietal and frontotemporal functional connectivity. Results CRM produced greater improvements in positive affect, comfort, and satisfaction than sham manipulation or sham + simulated cracking sound, whereas no clear difference among groups was observed for negative affect. Differences among groups were also observed in frontal alpha/beta ratio and alpha band frontoparietal and frontotemporal functional connectivity. Sham + simulated sound did not reproduce the overall pattern of subjective and EEG responses observed after CRM. Conclusions CRM produced greater improvements over the short-term in positive affect, comfort, and satisfaction and was accompanied by differences in selected resting state EEG outcomes compared with sham manipulation with or without simulated cracking sound. Adding simulated cracking sound to sham manipulation did not reproduce this pattern. Because CRM differed from the control conditions in several procedural components, the specific component or combination of components responsible for these differences could not be determined. Trial registration The trial was registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (URL: https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn; ITMCTR2025001112).
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注颈椎旋转手法（CRM）伴随的弹响声能否单独解释其短期主观与脑电反应，采用三组平行随机对照设计，在健康志愿者中比较真实手法、假手法及假手法加模拟弹响声的效果。结果显示，真实手法在积极情绪、舒适感和满意度上的改善大于两个对照条件，消极情绪则未见组间差异；部分静息态脑电指标（如额区α/β比值及α频段额顶、额颞功能连接）也出现组间差异，而模拟弹响声未能复现真实手法的主观与脑电反应模式。作者指出，由于真实手法与对照条件在多个操作成分上不同，尚无法确定具体是哪个成分或成分组合导致了这些差异。

papers.title: Neuroimmune-oligovascular signaling shapes oligodendrocyte precursor cell fate and repair after ischemic stroke.
papers.authors: Li B, Ming R, Wu Z, Pan S.
papers.abstract: Background Ischemic stroke causes neuronal and oligodendroglial injury, axonal and myelin damage, and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) are lifelong progenitors that generate oligodendrocytes while receiving and transmitting signals within neural, immune, and vascular microenvironments. This review examines how neuroimmune-oligovascular communication and intracellular signaling shape OPC survival, recruitment, state transitions, differentiation, and remyelination after ischemic stroke. Main body We first define OPC lineage identity, functional heterogeneity, and signaling interfaces with neurons, microglia/macrophages, astrocytes, endothelial cells, and pericytes. We then examine how excitotoxic, metabolic, redox, inflammatory, vascular, extracellular-matrix, and regulated cell-death signals converge on OPCs across lesion compartments and disease phases. Severe core ischemia depletes the progenitor pool, whereas partially perfused peri-infarct tissue permits reactive proliferation and migration. During the subacute phase, intercellular signals within the post-ischemic niche influence whether recruited OPCs adopt inflammatory, angiogenic, differentiation-competent, or arrested states.
