Neuroimaging, including quantitative susceptibility mapping, synthetic MRI, cranial ultrasound and molecular or myelin-sensitive imaging, provides complementary but indirect information on the structural and maturational consequences of these processes, whereas omics approaches may characterize their molecular environment. Radiomics similarly provides indirect tissue-level biomarkers rather than cell-specific measures of glial biology. Dysglycaemia further illustrates the dependence of developing white matter on coordinated cellular energy handling and the potential relevance of immature astrocyte-oligodendrocyte interactions during metabolic instability. Evidence from very early development suggests that oligodendrocyte maturation occurs within a changing cellular environment in which astroglial maturation, neuronal and vascular processes, and immune and metabolic mechanisms coexist. The Crossword and Foil Effects are proposed as hypothesis-generating frameworks to organize these intersecting developmental, metabolic, cellular, imaging and molecular dimensions rather than as experimentally validated causal models. Overall, no single cellular substitute for mature astrocytic functions is identified; instead, oligodendrocyte maturation appears to emerge within a developmentally changing division of metabolic, homeostatic and signaling labour across astroglial, neuronal, vascular and immune compartments.

papers.title: Dihydromyricetin and Neuroinflammation: Implications for CNS Disorders and Therapeutic Development.
papers.authors: Skinner SG, Aleman EG, Berges AN, Kim KJ, Kantilal D, Asatryan L, Davies DL.
papers.abstract: Dihydromyricetin (DHM) is a bioactive polyphenol with broad therapeutic potential, including strong anti-inflammatory activity. Importantly, DHM has been shown to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB), enabling pharmacological activity within the central nervous system (CNS) and positioning it as a candidate for CNS disorders in which neuroinflammation plays a central role, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and stroke. Therapeutics such as DHM, which address neuroinflammation, are of increasing interest. Across CNS disease models, DHM's effects show recurring convergence on NF-κB suppression, NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition, and autophagy regulation, alongside context-specific mechanisms involving oxidative stress, ferroptosis, neurotrophic signaling, and peripheral gut-CNS communication. This review examines the evidence for DHM as a neuroinflammatory modulator, focusing on the mechanisms by which it exerts its therapeutic effects. By doing so, we aim to support its translational potential as a natural product for improving human health.

papers.title: Predicting MCI-to-Alzheimer's Conversion: A Systematic Benchmark of Classical, Machine Learning, and Deep Survival Models.
papers.authors: Santa NA, Daza-Santacoloma G, Serna WS.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting time-to-conversion from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a critical clinical challenge. Most survival analyses rely on static baseline variables, ignoring the temporal dynamics of serial neuroimaging. We benchmark seven survival model families using a novel temporal MRI descriptor pipeline on ADNI. Methods: A cohort of 661 MCI patients (250 conversion events, 37.8%, median follow-up 42.0 months) was constructed from ADNI. FreeSurfer volumetrics of six brain regions were summarised into three time-based descriptors each (atrophy rate, trajectory variability σ, and time-weighted cumulative mean μ) under strict anti-leakage constraints, yielding 18 neuroimaging features which, combined with six clinical variables (age, sex, education, MMSE, ADAS-13, and APOE-ε4), form a 24-dimensional covariate vector. Cox PH, Weibull AFT, Exponential, RSF, GBST, DeepSurv, and DeepHit were evaluated under stratified 5-fold cross-validation and assessed on an independent OASIS-3 cohort (n=78) as an exploratory analysis. Results: All seven models achieved C-index 0.853-0.863 (Δ=0.010), with Cox PH reaching 0.863±0.027 using only routine structural MRI. Time-dependent AUC ranged from 0.856 (12 months) to 0.938 (48 months). Risk stratification by quartile yielded highly separated Kaplan-Meier curves (log-rank p<0.001). On OASIS-3 (n=78, exploratory), classical models showed preliminary cross-cohort consistency (Weibull AFT 0.760±0.063, RSF 0.759±0.049), while deep learning degraded substantially (DeepSurv 0.551±0.116); these results are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as confirmatory given the small per-fold sample size (EPV ≈ 1). Conclusions: The temporal MRI descriptor pipeline achieves a C-index of 0.863 using only routine structural MRI, without PET or CSF biomarkers, demonstrating strong discriminative performance on ADNI MCI-to-AD conversion. The narrow performance band (Δ=0.010) suggests that, within this feature-engineering paradigm, no clear performance separation was observed among the evaluated model architectures; this convergence may reflect feature-level rather than architecture-level constraints, although the underlying cause cannot be established from discriminative performance alone. Classical models showed more stable cross-cohort behaviour under data-scarce conditions; prospective validation on larger cohorts with full covariate parity is required before clinical translation can be considered.

papers.title: Language and Cognitive Performance in Children with Well-Controlled Asthma: Associations with Serum pNF-H and Neurogranin.
papers.authors: Savaş M, Kahraman Beğen S, Akbayır E, Yücel E, Kıykım A, Dilek F, Tüzün E, Temizyürek A, Dumur S, Elgormus Y, Uzun H.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Childhood asthma is increasingly viewed as a systemic condition that may also affect neurodevelopmental processes. We examined language and cognitive performance and their associations with serum biomarkers of neuroinflammation, neuroaxonal integrity and synaptic function in school-aged children with clinically well-controlled asthma. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 67 children (33 with asthma and 34 healthy controls) underwent the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Revised (WISC-R), the Turkish Nonword Repetition Test (TAST), the Turkish School-Age Language Development Test (TODİL), sleep and psychosocial scales, and audiometric screening. Serum interleukin-4 (IL-4), IL-13, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 13 (CXCL13), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), nerve growth factor (NGF), chitinase-3-like protein-1 (YKL-40/CHI3L1), triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), synaptosomal-associated protein 25 (SNAP-25), neurogranin, and phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNF-H) were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Groups were compared with Mann-Whitney U and chi-square/Fisher tests and with age- and sex-adjusted regression using HC3 robust standard errors, with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction within predefined outcome families; within the asthma group, biomarkers were related to language and cognitive outcomes in exploratory multiple regression. Results: Serum pNF-H was higher in the asthma group (p = 0.001; pFDR = 0.012), remained higher after age and sex adjustment (p = 0.002), and was robust to outlier handling. Neurogranin was higher in the unadjusted comparison (p = 0.012), marginal after panel-level FDR (pFDR = 0.065), and significant after adjustment (p = 0.003). Several WISC-R indices, most clearly full-scale IQ, were lower in the asthma group, favoring controls. Within the asthma group, neurogranin was positively associated with WISC-R vocabulary and picture completion and TODIL organizing. Conclusions: Even in well-controlled asthma, specific language and cognitive domains may differ from those of healthy peers, alongside higher peripheral biomarkers related to neuroaxonal and synaptic processes. These findings are exploratory and require confirmation in larger, longitudinal samples.

papers.title: Neural Representation of Chinese Word Classes: An ALE Meta-Analysis of Noun and Verb Processing.
papers.authors: Luo X, Deng Y, Sun Y.
papers.abstract: Whether nouns and verbs rely on distinct neural systems remains debated, particularly in Chinese, which has limited inflectional morphology and flexible word-class use. We used activation likelihood estimation in GingerALE 3.0.2 to synthesize task-based fMRI/PET studies identified from three databases. Twenty-three publications contributed 28 experiment-level contrast entries. The primary analyses compared 8 noun-versus-baseline and 15 verb-versus-baseline entries, using a pooled 23-entry reference; the original mixed inputs of 9 noun-associated and 19 verb-associated entries were retained as additional analyses. Input maps used cluster-level family-wise error inference at p = 0.05, and final between-set contrasts used p = 0.05 with a 200 mm3 minimum cluster size. Noun-related convergence was concentrated in the left parietal region, whereas verb-related convergence involved frontal and posterior regions. The primary comparison identified greater noun-related convergence in the left parietal and right claustral/insular regions and greater verb-related convergence in bilateral frontal and right posterior regions. The baseline-only conjunction yielded no suprathreshold cluster, while the additional analyses showed a broadly comparable pattern. Together, these findings support partly differentiated neural processing of nouns and verbs in Chinese.

papers.title: Safe and efficient intracellular delivery of functional antibodies into cultured neural cells shows a role for Alzheimer's-relevant tau phosphorylation in cell integrity.
papers.authors: Viola KL, Chromy BA, Nowar R, Lambert MP, Klein WL.
papers.abstract: Introduction Protein proteoforms generated by post-translational modification are increasingly recognized as important regulators of neuronal function and neurodegenerative disease. However, methods for acutely interrogating specific intracellular proteoforms in living neuronal populations remain limited. We evaluated cationic liposomal delivery (CLD) as a strategy for introducing full-length functional antibodies into living neurons and used this approach to investigate the role of a phosphorylated tau proteoform recognized by the monoclonal antibody PHF-1. Methods Cationic liposomes composed of DOPC+ were complexed with antibodies or molecular probes and applied to cultured neuronal cell lines and primary mouse cortical neurons. Intracellular delivery, cellular localization, viability, and biological activity were assessed using fluorescence microscopy and live-cell imaging. Results CLD efficiently delivered full-length antibodies and molecular probes into living neuronal cells and primary neurons without detectable toxicity. Internalized antibodies retained target specificity, producing intracellular staining patterns consistent with the known localization of tau, vinculin, paxillin, and Fyn. Delivery was observed across essentially all cells in treated cultures and remained effective under standard culture conditions. Intracellular delivery of PHF-1 produced a rapid and striking morphological response characterized by neurite retraction and cell-body rounding within hours of treatment. These effects were not observed with heat-inactivated PHF-1, vehicle controls, or other intracellular antibodies, supporting a specific effect of intracellular engagement of PHF-1-reactive tau species. Discussion These findings establish CLD as a practical platform for the intracellular delivery of functional full-length antibodies into living neuronal populations. Beyond validating a delivery technology, the study demonstrates that acute intracellular engagement of PHF-1-reactive phosphorylated tau rapidly alters neuronal morphology, suggesting that this tau proteoform contributes to the maintenance of neurite integrity. CLD provides a versatile approach for probing the function of intracellular proteoforms that are difficult to study using conventional genetic or biochemical methods.

papers.title: ConvNeXt-KAN: a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network head for robust multi-class staging of Alzheimer's disease from brain MRI.
papers.authors: Islam K, Hossen B, Manjar MTA, Sultana S.
papers.abstract: Introduction Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder for which accurate, stage-wise classification from structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can support earlier intervention. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) dominate this task, but their classifier heads rely on fixed activation functions and linear weights, which constrain the modelling of the subtle, highly non-linear atrophy and texture patterns that separate dementia stages. In addition, the widely used Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS) collection is severely imbalanced, and two common practices-undersampling every class to the smallest one, and splitting at the image (slice) level-respectively discard most of the data and inflate reported accuracy. Methods We propose ConvNeXt-KAN, a hybrid model that couples a transfer-learned ConvNeXt-Tiny feature extractor with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) classification head whose edges are learnable spline activations implemented efficiently with Gaussian radial basis functions. The model is trained with a robustness-oriented recipe (MixUp and CutMix, label smoothing, decoupled weight decay, a cosine learning-rate schedule with warm-up, and test-time augmentation) and a data strategy that caps abundant classes and oversamples only the training partition, while evaluating on a fixed, balanced, leakage-controlled test set. Results On the held-out test set the model attains 94.5% accuracy, a macro-averaged F1 of 0.944, and a mean one-vs.-rest ROC-AUC of 0.991, with an ablation confirming that pre-trained features and expanded data are the main drivers of performance. A head-to-head comparison under a matched protocol shows that the KAN and MLP heads are statistically indistinguishable (McNemar p = 0.52), while the proposed image-space resampling strategy outperforms focal loss, class-balanced cross-entropy and feature-space SMOTE. Evaluated without any fine-tuning on an independent four-class Alzheimer's MRI collection distributed on Kaggle, test-time-augmented accuracy is 61.6% with a macro-averaged F1 of 0.565. Discussion The learnable-activation head improves the discrimination of the difficult non-demented vs. very-mild-demented boundary at negligible runtime cost, and the efficient formulation keeps the approach practical in standard deep-learning frameworks. A class-wise analysis of the external evaluation shows that moderate dementia continues to be recognized perfectly while the two clinically intermediate stages absorb most of the domain-shift error. We further quantify the impact of the evaluation protocol and argue that subject-level validation and multi-site external testing are essential before clinical claims.

papers.title: Reduced causal connectivity in multiple resting-state networks in autism spectrum disorder detected by convergent cross mapping.
papers.authors: Zhang H, He L, Wang D, Yan Y, He Y, Zhang Y, Shi Y, Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Background This study investigates alterations in causal connectivity within resting-state brain functional networks in patients with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using the Convergent Cross Mapping (CCM) method. Methods Data were obtained from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE I) public database. To minimize variability, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) data were restricted to the NYU site, comprising 52 ASD patients and 52 matched typically developing controls. Based on the AAL template, time series were extracted from five resting-state networks: attention network, default mode network, sensorimotor network, visual network, and subcortical network. The CCM method was employed to analyze causal connectivity among these brain regions. Additionally, a support vector machine (SVM) classifier was utilized to assess the discriminative potential of the identified causal connectivity patterns. Results Significant differences in causal connections were observed, particularly in the default mode network, which exhibited the most pronounced alterations. Overall, ASD patients showed a general decrease in causal connectivity across networks, accompanied by some localized increases. The SVM classifier accurately differentiated individuals with ASD from controls based on the causal connectivity patterns derived from resting-state brain networks. Conclusion These findings elucidate dynamical network mechanisms underlying ASD pathophysiology and highlight candidate neurobiological markers with potential translational relevance.

papers.title: Applications of functional ultrasound brain-computer interfaces in neurological diseases: research progress based on neurovascular coupling.
papers.authors: Zhang C.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) bypass peripheral nerves and muscles to establish direct information pathways between the brain and external devices, providing novel approaches for motor function reconstruction, communication assistance, and neurorehabilitation in patients with neurological disorders. However, conventional non-invasive BCIs relying on modalities such as electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), or functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) exhibit limitations in spatiotemporal resolution, portability, or real-time capability. Functional ultrasound (fUS), an emerging neuroimaging technology based on neurovascular coupling (NVC), detects cerebral blood volume changes at a spatial resolution of approximately 100 μm; its imaging frame interval is 200-500 ms, whereas its effective temporal resolution, limited by the hemodynamic response, is 1-2 s, offering a potential solution to overcome these constraints. This review comprehensively analyzed NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces from the dimensions of technical principles, clinical applications, future directions, and challenges. fUS has demonstrated significant clinical value in stroke assessment, epilepsy monitoring, and early identification of neurodegenerative diseases. Emerging technologies such as transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation, sonogenetics, and intravascular ultrasound are driving the evolution of fUS from single-signal "acquisition" toward bidirectional "acquisition-modulation" closed-loop systems, which remain at the proof-of-concept stage. However, the hemodynamic response latency relative to neural electrical activity (1-2 s), the yet-unclear biosafety of chronic ultrasound exposure, and insufficient decoding reliability under pathological conditions remain critical bottlenecks requiring urgent resolution. In conclusion, NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces provide a novel tool for precision diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases. Future efforts should focus on conducting multicenter clinical trials and enhancing the robustness of decoding algorithms.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.authors: H F T, Jacob JE.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approaches in deep learning-driven EEG analysis for the diagnosis of neurological diseases. It includes recent advances in deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), hybrid configurations, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), Large Language Models (LLM), autoencoders, and transformer-based models, with a focus on their capacity to model spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal dynamics in EEG signals. This is applicable in diagnosing major neurological disorders such as Epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease (AD), Encephalopathy, Parkinson's disease (PD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), sleep disorders, and developmental brain disorders. Furthermore, we discuss essential preprocessing strategies and denoising techniques, showing how removing biological artifacts prevents diagnostic models from confusing noise with actual signs of disease. Key challenges such as limited data availability, lack of model interpretability, inter-subject variability, and difficulty in clinical translation are identified and critically discussed. Finally, key emerging trends and future research directions are identified to support the development of clinical applications of EEG-based disease diagnostic systems.

papers.title: Emerging roles of apolipoprotein E4 in cerebral small vessel disease-related cognitive impairment: mechanistic insights and therapeutic perspectives.
papers.authors: Li M, Zhang Y, Lü P, Li J, Zhang Y, Wang S, Bai Y, Wang Y.
papers.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major contributor to cognitive decline and vascular cognitive impairment in the elderly. However, the extent to which apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) contributes to sporadic, non-amyloid CSVD remains unclear. Previous literature has often inferred CSVD mechanisms from Alzheimer's disease (AD) research, carrying the risk of overstating disease-specific causal relationships. Therefore, this narrative review re-evaluates the relationship between ApoE4 and CSVD using a CSVD-centric hierarchy of evidence. Population-based imaging and epidemiological data suggest that "APOE" ε4 may alter susceptibility to white matter injury and cognitive impairment; however, the effect sizes are generally small or context-dependent, and associations are influenced by factors such as age, hypertension, diabetes, total vascular risk burden, AD pathology, ancestry, sex, and "APOE" gene dosage. Evidence is stronger for cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA)-which involves mechanisms distinct from sporadic arteriolosclerotic CSVD-and thus warrants separate discussion. At the mechanistic level, direct evidence regarding CSVD supports endothelial dysfunction, BBB leakage, neurovascular unit (NVU) instability, and white matter injury as core pathological processes. Among the evidence specific to ApoE4, models involving impaired neurovascular regulation and chronic hypoperfusion are the most compelling; conversely, mechanisms such as the cyclophilin A-MMP-9 pathway, TREM2-ApoE signaling, insulin receptor trafficking, reelin-related synaptic effects, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and autophagy currently rely primarily on AD research or preclinical evidence. Two recently proposed specific hypotheses-the brain-heart-kidney axis hypothesis and the microglial lipid droplet model-offer valuable conceptual frameworks but should be viewed as testable theories rather than established mechanisms. To date, no ApoE4-targeted therapies have been proven effective for CSVD-related cognitive impairment future research should prioritize genotype-stratified longitudinal CSVD cohorts, standardized imaging studies, adjustment for Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarkers, analysis of interactions between vascular risk factors, studies on human white matter tissue, and the development of ApoE4 disease models that integrate chronic hypoperfusion and vascular comorbidities.

papers.title: Generative enhancement of suboptimally opacified cerebral CT angiography for large-vessel occlusion detection: a multireader study.
papers.authors: Tu Y, Wang M, Sun Z, Zeng Y, Li Y, Tang Y, Yang Y, Cao Z, Hu S, Wang D, Li Y.
papers.abstract: Background Rapid identification of proximal anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion (LVO) on CT angiography (CTA) is essential for thrombectomy triage. Suboptimal arterial phase timing can obscure the intracranial arteries, prompting repeat CTA, additional contrast exposure, and treatment delay. We evaluated whether deep-learning-generated vascular images from a single suboptimally opacified acquisition improved LVO detection. Methods This retrospective study included 626 patients. RescueCTA, a paired 2.5D conditional generative model, was developed in 391 patients using last-frame CT perfusion (CTP) as the simulated acquisition-failure input and same-session CTA as the target. Evaluation included 194 primary cases with simulated inputs and 41 exploratory cases with genuinely underopacified CTA. RescueCTA was compared with three generative baselines. Two radiologists assessed image quality. Four readers compared source images alone with source images plus RescueCTA for target LVO detection in the primary cohort; two also evaluated the exploratory cohort. The primary endpoint was the multireader multicase (MRMC) area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); exploratory analyses were descriptive. Results In the primary cohort, RescueCTA image quality was higher than that of all three baselines (3.90 ± 0.81). Combined reading improved AUC from 0.850 to 0.933 (ΔAUC = 0.083 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.025-0.141]; p = 0.007), while paired CTA reached 0.948 (p = 0.594 vs. combined reading). Strict AUC improved from 0.756 to 0.880 (p < 0.001) but remained lower than that of paired CTA (0.935; p = 0.019). In the exploratory cohort, combined reading yielded a higher AUC than underopacified CTA alone (0.981 vs. 0.889). Conclusion Deep-learning-generated vascular images improved LVO detection under simulated underopacification and showed preliminary feasibility in genuinely underopacified CTA. Larger real-world cohorts are needed to establish diagnostic performance after suboptimal arterial phase CTA.

papers.title: Social support and cognition in a racially and ethnically diverse cohort: the role of neighborhood disadvantage.
papers.authors: Rhoads T, Neale AC, Cobos K, Stypulkowski K, Wong CG, O'Bryant SE, Kind AJH, Miller JB.
papers.abstract: Background Social support is positively associated with cognitive health, but which dimensions of support matter most and how this relationship varies across environmental contexts remains under-explored. This study examined whether neighborhood disadvantage, measured by the Area Deprivation Index (ADI), moderates the relationship between social support and cognition in an ethnocracially diverse cohort of adults aged 50 and older. Methods Data were analyzed from the Health and Aging Brain Study-Health Disparities (HABS-HD), which used community-based participatory research methods to recruit Non-Hispanic Black (NHB), Hispanic, and Non-Hispanic White (NHW) participants across the cognitive spectrum (normal, mild cognitive impairment, dementia). Neighborhood disadvantage was dichotomized as low versus high, and three Interpersonal Support Evaluation subscales (Tangible, Companion, and Emotional Support) were assessed. For each racial/ethnic group, a social support × ADI interaction term was tested as the primary analysis. Pooled and ADI-stratified associations between each subscale and cognition (Mini-Mental State Exam; MMSE) were examined as secondary, exploratory analyses. Results The interaction test did not provide evidence that neighborhood disadvantage moderates the association between social support and cognition in any racial/ethnic group (all p > 0.23). Independent of neighborhood disadvantage, Tangible Support was significantly and positively associated with cognition across all three groups, while Emotional Support was significantly associated with cognition among NHB and Hispanic individuals. In exploratory subgroup analyses stratified by neighborhood disadvantage, Tangible and Emotional Support were significant among NHB and Hispanic individuals in lower-disadvantage areas (ADI 1-4), and Tangible Support among NHW individuals in this stratum. No subscale predicted cognition in the highest-disadvantage areas. Conclusion Tangible Support, and to a lesser extent Emotional Support, showed positive associations with cognition across ethnoracial groups, with the most consistent associations observed among NHB and Hispanic individuals in lower-disadvantage neighborhoods, though these associations attenuated in several sensitivity analyses. In exploratory subgroup analyses, significant associations were not observed among individuals residing in the most disadvantaged neighborhoods, though these findings should be interpreted cautiously given unequal strata sample sizes and warrant confirmation in future studies.

papers.title: Altered hippocampal morphology and its association with gait impairment in idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.authors: Kim J, Jeong SY, Lee SW, Yoon U, Kang K.
papers.abstract: Background and purpose: This study aimed to characterize structural alterations of the hippocampus associated with idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus (INPH), and to explore their relationship with gait disturbances in affected patients. Methods A total of 48 patients with INPH and 25 β-amyloid-negative healthy controls underwent MRI-based, vertex-wise three-dimensional hippocampal shape analysis. Additionally, all participants received 18F-florbetaben positron emission tomography to assess amyloid status. Results Hippocampal shape analysis revealed marked bilateral deformation in the INPH group compared to controls. Both hippocampi exhibited elongation and narrowing, with the middle and posterior regions showing upward curvature, indicating vertical displacement from the hippocampal body to the tail. The normalized hippocampal volume was significantly smaller in INPH patients. No substantial volumetric or morphological differences were observed between amyloid-positive and amyloid-negative individuals within the INPH group. Notably, localized shape deformities correlated with performance on the Timed Up and Go and 10-meter walk tests, more prominently in the right hippocampus. Bilateral inward deformations at the superomedial tail and inferior body of the hippocampus were consistently linked to worse gait performance. Furthermore, smaller right normalized hippocampal volumes were negatively associated with gait test outcomes. Conclusion These findings indicate that INPH is associated with characteristic hippocampal shape abnormalities. The observed associations between hippocampal morphology and gait disturbances suggest that the hippocampus may contribute to gait and postural control in INPH.

papers.title: Heterogeneous progression of AT(N) biomarkers in data-driven subtypes of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Teng Z, Hu M, Zhang Z, Zhou M, Yin P, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.
papers.abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits substantial heterogeneity in brain atrophy patterns and progression rates. Data-driven subtyping based on the Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) model has identified distinct MRI-derived subtypes, but the longitudinal dynamics of these subtypes within the AT(N) framework remain unknown. Methods This study included 1,576 participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) with at least two visits. SuStaIn was applied to volumetric measurements of 11 brain regions to identify imaging-based subtypes. Within each subtype, we fitted a Bayesian latent time longitudinal joint mixed-effects model incorporating six biomarkers: amyloid PET (A), CSF p-tau (T), hippocampal volume, cingulate volume, thalamic volume (N), and ADAS-Cog13 (X), with APOE ε4 as a covariate. Results The three subtypes exhibited distinctly different longitudinal patterns. Subtype 1 showed early elevation of amyloid, followed by a sharp decline in hippocampal volume, which was tightly coupled with cognitive deterioration. Subtype 2 featured early involvement of cortical regions such as the cingulate cortex, with hippocampal changes occurring at a similar timing to Subtype 1 but accompanied by earlier cortical and thalamic involvement. Subtype 3 exhibited early rapid hippocampal atrophy that later plateaued, and demonstrated the strongest hippocampus-cognition coupling. The association of APOE ε4 with biomarker trajectories was subtype-dependent: its effect estimates were largest for amyloid and p-tau in Subtype 1, whereas in Subtype 3 the effect estimates were significant for nearly all biomarkers, with the largest estimate for cognition. Conclusion This study demonstrates that AD subtypes defined by spatial atrophy patterns also differ fundamentally in temporal biomarker dynamics and APOE ε4 association, supporting subtype-stratified modeling of disease progression.

papers.title: Future of cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging: a bibliometric analysis.
papers.authors: Wu X, Yang Y, Xu Y, Wu Z, Liu H, Chen R.
papers.abstract: Background Cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (cDMRI) has become a valuable noninvasive tool for assessing cardiac microstructure. Objective To perform a systematic and comprehensive bibliometric analysis of cDMRI to explore current status, research hotspots and potential future directions. Material and methods A systematic search of Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and PubMed was conducted to identify articles on cDMRI published between 2005 and 2024. All retrieved records were independently screened by two reviewers to exclude the articles unrelated to the topic about cDMRI. Co-citation, collaboration networks, burst keywords, and reference analyses were performed. Results There were 359 articles searched in WoSCC and 88 articles in PubMed. Finally, 367 articles met the search criteria in both databases. The cardiac "diffusion tensor imaging" (cDTI) emerged as the most prominent keyword, with the highest occurrence count (191.0) and strongest citation bursts (6.8). The study by Nielles-Vallespin et al. showed the strongest citation burst (26.17), accumulating 163 total citations and an average of 20.38 citations per year, highlighting its substantial influence on the development of cDMRI research. The top-cited articles with the strongest citation bursts concentrated on the clinical application of cDTI, its sequence design, and cardiac electrophysiology based on cDTI. The trend topic analysis further revealed "deep learning" as an emerging research focus in cDMRI since 2022. Conclusions To our knowledge, this is the first dedicated bibliometric analysis focusing on cDMRI. By systematically analyzing the current status, research hotspots, and future trends of cDMRI, it provided valuable insights to guide future investigations in this field.

papers.title: KAT6B::KANSL1 fusion-positive uterine mesenchymal neoplasm with hybrid endometrial stromal and smooth muscle features: a case report.
papers.authors: Li Q, Wu M.
papers.abstract: KAT6B/A::KANSL1 fusion-positive uterine mesenchymal neoplasms are rare and may show overlapping endometrial stromal and smooth muscle features. We report a 47-year-old woman with regular menses, no dysmenorrhea, and a 7-year history of a presumed uterine fibroid. She underwent laparoscopic myomectomy at an outside hospital in November 2024. The fragmented specimen was interpreted as an endometrial stromal tumor with smooth muscle differentiation, but the tumor-myometrium interface could not be assessed, and an endometrial stromal nodule could not be distinguished from low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma. Subsequent pelvic magnetic resonance imaging showed postoperative changes, possible residual leiomyomas, and heterogeneous enhancement at the uterine fundus. Pelvic computed tomography showed heterogeneous uterine enhancement without definite extrauterine disease. Because the original specimen was fragmented and a potentially malignant uterine mesenchymal neoplasm could not be excluded, completion hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy was performed. The hysterectomy specimen contained multiple residual intramyometrial nodules with marked regional heterogeneity. One component showed fascicular smooth muscle morphology and diffuse desmin and h-caldesmon expression, whereas other nodules showed tongue-like myometrial infiltration, focal intravascular growth, spiral arteriole-like vessels, and diffuse ER, PR, CD10, and SMA expression. Whole-transcriptome sequencing identified an in-frame KAT6B::KANSL1 fusion involving KAT6B exon 3 and KANSL1 exon 11. Because the tumor expressed ER and PR, postoperative letrozole was administered for 30 days, after which surveillance was selected following review of the final pathologic and molecular findings. At 8 months after completion surgery, no clinical or radiologic recurrence was detected; this limited follow-up does not permit conclusions regarding long-term biological behavior or endocrine treatment benefit.

papers.title: Tablet-Based Neurocognitive Tests for Ugandan Adolescents Living With HIV: Cross-Sectional Validation Study.
papers.authors: Robbins RN, Nanteza A, Gumikiriza-Onoria JL, Santoro A, Ferraris CM, Karungi C, Tsapalas D, Asiedu N, Kirsch C, Tan M, Liu J, Familiar-Lopez I, Musiime V, Dirajlal-Fargo S.
papers.abstract: Background Adolescents living with perinatally acquired HIV (PHIV) remain at risk of neurocognitive difficulties, yet access to valid neurocognitive tests is limited in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where most of this population resides. Tests that can be administered by nonspecialist personnel are culturally and linguistically appropriate for SSA's diverse populations and are brief enough for routine use are needed to expand access, but few such tools exist. Objective We adapted NeuroScreen , a brief tablet-based neurocognitive test battery, into Luganda and evaluated its validity and acceptability for use among Ugandan adolescents with PHIV. Methods In this cross-sectional validation study, 100 Ugandan adolescents aged 11 to 20 years (50 with PHIV; 50 HIV-negative controls) completed the Luganda- or English-language NeuroScreen battery and a commonly used traditional test battery. Participants were recruited from an existing longitudinal cardiovascular cohort at the Joint Clinical Research Centre in Kampala, Uganda. We examined convergent validity with correlations between the 2 batteries' individual and global z -scores, known-groups validity with unadjusted and age-adjusted group comparisons, criterion validity by examining classification agreement between the 2 batteries quantified with Cohen κ, and acceptability through self-reported technology use and ease of use. Results NeuroScreen and the traditional battery global z -scores were strongly correlated (r =0.75; P <.001). Correlations between tests assessing similar domains were generally small to moderate, and were strongest for processing speed, attention, and working memory. Adolescents with PHIV scored significantly lower than controls on global scores for both NeuroScreen (P =.008) and the traditional battery (P =.003), even after adjusting for age. Agreement between batteries in classifying participants ≤1 SD (κ=0.56) and ≤2 SD (κ=0.66) below the global z -score mean was moderate, with both batteries classifying more adolescents with PHIV than controls below these thresholds. Although fewer than half of participants (42/97, 43%) had previously used a tablet, most rated NeuroScreen as easy to use, and prior tablet experience was not independently associated with NeuroScreen performance after age adjustment. Conclusions The Luganda-adapted NeuroScreen demonstrated convergent, known-groups, and criterion validity in Ugandan adolescents with PHIV. By delivering automated administration, automated scoring, and standardized multimedia instructions in the local language on a portable tablet, NeuroScreen addresses several persistent barriers to neurocognitive assessment in low-resource settings, including shortages of specialist personnel, the time burden of traditional batteries, and the scarcity of culturally and linguistically appropriate tools. The NeuroScreen battery was found to be highly acceptable among adolescents with little or no prior tablet experience. These findings add to a growing body of evidence supporting tablet-based assessment as a practical and scalable mobile health approach to expanding access to neurocognitive testing. Future research should evaluate test-retest reliability, sensitivity to change over time, normative benchmarks, and implementation within real-world clinical workflows.
papers.summary_zh: 该横断面验证研究将简短的平板电脑神经认知测验组合NeuroScreen改编为卢干达语，并在乌干达11至20岁围产期感染HIV的青少年与HIV阴性对照中，考察其效度与可接受性。结果显示，NeuroScreen与传统测验的整体z分数高度相关，在加工速度、注意和工作记忆等相近领域相关相对较强；感染HIV的青少年在两种测验上的整体得分均低于对照，且年龄调整后依然如此，两套测验对低于常模阈值的分类一致性为中等。多数参与者认为该测验易于使用，既往平板使用经验与测验表现无独立关联。作者认为，这种自动化施测与评分的本地语言平板测验有助于缓解低资源地区专业人员和合适工具不足的问题，但重测信度、纵向敏感性、常模及实际流程中的实施仍有待研究。

papers.title: Comparison of performance of an LLM Council of LFM2.5-1.2B, Qwen3-4B-2507 and Phi-4-Mini- reasoning and Meta LLaMa 3.1 8B against MedGemma 4B on extraction and classification of free-text radiology reports
papers.authors: Mathur V, Aggarwal B, Aman A.
papers.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated growing potential for clinical natural language processing (NLP) [1–4], including radiological report analysis, while recent studies have explored both domain-specialised medical models and multi-LLM approaches [7,8] for improving reliability and reasoning. However, the comparative performance of LLM Councils and specialised medical LLMs on structured radiological tasks remains underexplored. This study evaluated an LLM Council framework against MedGemma 4B for radiological report analysis. The Council comprised Qwen3-4B-2507, LFM2.5-1.2B, and Phi-4 Mini Reasoning, with LLaMa 3.1 8B as chairman. We hypothesised that MedGemma would outperform the Council due to its specialised medical training. A total of 783 anonymised mammography, hip-knee-ankle (HKA), and brain magnetic resonance (MR) reports from Max Healthcare Saket were analysed for BI-RADS and ACR extraction, pre- versus post-operative HKA classification, and normal versus abnormal brain MR classification. Performance was assessed using accuracy, F1 score, and task-specific metrics. MedGemma achieved higher overall accuracy than the Council (88.72% vs. 83.56%; weighted F1: 0.8653 vs. 0.7389), with significant differences overall (p = 0.0129) and for HKA classification (p = 0.0011), but not mammography or brain MR. However, Qwen3-4B-2507 independently achieved the highest accuracy across all tasks: 91.89% in mammography, 92.93% in HKA, and 90.25% in brain MR, yielding 91.69% overall accuracy and a weighted F1 of 0.8902. Notably, the Council achieved 72.22% HKA accuracy compared with 85.86% for MedGemma. These findings suggest that strong general-purpose reasoning may outperform both consensus-based and specialised approaches for clinical NLP under the conditions evaluated.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究比较了由多个小型语言模型组成的LLM Council框架与医学专用模型MedGemma 4B在放射报告结构化提取和分类任务上的表现，数据为乳腺钼靶、下肢力线及脑磁共振报告。结果显示，MedGemma总体准确率高于Council，差异主要来自下肢力线分类，而在乳腺钼靶和脑磁共振任务上两者差异不显著；但Council中的Qwen3-4B-2507单独使用时在所有任务上准确率最高。作者据此认为，在所评估的条件下，强通用推理模型可能优于共识式组合和专用医学模型，但这一结论仍需更多任务验证。

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Geometry HCFIM features for data-limited EEG screening of Alzheimer’s disease and Frontotemporal Dementia
papers.authors: Rojas-Pescio H.
papers.abstract: Abstract Resting-state EEG is a scalable modality for neurophysiological screening, but conventional spectral descriptors capture only part of the signal organization altered in neurodegenerative disease. This study evaluates a reproducible information-theoretic geometry framework based on entropy (H), statistical complexity (C) and Fisher Information Measure (FIM) for data-limited EEG characterization of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Using the public OpenNeuro resting-state EEG dataset comprising 29 healthy controls, 36 AD patients and 23 FTD patients, preprocessed eyes-closed 19-channel recordings were segmented into epochs, transformed into finite probability distributions, projected into HC and HFIMplanes and HCFIMspace, and aggregated at subject level. Synthetic signal regimes were first used to verify the behavior of the probability-domain geometry. Regional and lateralized cortical schemas were then compared against PSD baselines using leakage-aware subject-level validation. Then, various machine learning classification models were applied to distinguish between healthy and neurologically affected individuals. In the regional schema, the most consistent AD-related geometric displacement was found in temporal alpha rhythms, using Permutation entropy with m = 4, τ = 1 (inter/intra ratio = 0.847; silhouette = 0.141), while in FTD it was found in temporal broadband (inter/intra ratio = 1.140; silhouette = 0.073); both silhouette values indicate modest, overlapping group geometry rather than well-separated clusters. For AD classification, PSD + HCFIM with Extra Randomized Trees achieved ROC AUC = 0.818 and balanced accuracy = 0.803; adding lateralized differences increased ROC AUC to 0.832 and sensitivity to 0.833, with lower specificity. For FTD, regional HCFIM-only features achieved the highest ROC AUC (0.810), while regional PSD + HCFIM achieved the best balanced accuracy (0.740). Lateralization highlighted left temporal broadband displacement in FTD but did not improve classification. These results support HCFIM as an interpretable, reproducible complement to spectral EEG features for preclinical methodological research, while emphasizing the need for independent validation before clinical or device-specific claims.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对静息态脑电在神经退行性疾病筛查中常规频谱特征信息有限的问题，评估了一套基于熵、统计复杂度和Fisher信息测度的信息论几何框架，并在公开脑电数据上比较其与功率谱基线对阿尔茨海默病和额颞叶痴呆的区分能力。结果显示，两类疾病各自最一致的几何偏移分别出现在颞区alpha节律和颞区宽带，但组间几何重叠明显、分离程度有限；将HCFIM与频谱特征结合后分类表现有所提升，侧化特征对阿尔茨海默病略有帮助，对额颞叶痴呆则未改善分类。作者据此认为HCFIM可作为频谱脑电特征的可解释补充，用于临床前方法学研究，但强调在临床或设备相关应用前仍需独立验证。

papers.title: Whole-Brain, Region-Specific Astrocyte Reactivity and Morphological Remodeling After Diffuse Traumatic Brain Injury in A Gyrencephalic Ferret Model
papers.authors: Bagherian A, Perez C, Kosub A, Gonzales RCY, Patterson A, Bieniek K, Seidi M, Memar M.
papers.abstract: Abstract Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers pathological cascades that evolve across acute, subacute, and chronic phases. Astrocytes play a central role across these phases, and astrocyte reactivity is commonly evaluated using glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) immunolabeling. However, in many TBI studies GFAP changes are characterized qualitatively or with manual or simple threshold-based measures on a small set of sections, limiting throughput and constraining analysis of region-specific heterogeneity in astrocyte responses. To overcome these limitations, we employed a ferret model of diffuse TBI (5 TBI, 5 sham), leveraging the ferret's gyrencephalic cortex, human-like regional fractional brain volumes, and astrocyte features that more closely resemble the human brain than rodent models. An AI-driven segmentation model validated for GFAP-stained ferret histology was integrated with atlas-based mapping to achieve whole-brain, region-resolved quantification of astrocyte reactivity over an average of 10 coronal slices per animal. Morphometric analysis using a custom SMorph-based pipeline characterized branching complexity and spatial domain features across defined regions. At seven days post-injury, TBI animals showed elevated astrocyte reactivity and hypertrophic remodeling, with significant expansion of convex hull area and elongation of secondary branches at the whole-brain level, most pronounced in the atlas-defined gray-matter region and cerebellum and brain-stem subregions, whereas white-matter showed a similar but less marked trend. Morphological changes were also detected in the hippocampus that did not show significant increases in astrocyte reactivity, indicating that structural remodeling represents a partially independent dimension of the astroglial response. These regional patterns are consistent with expected large tissue deformation and axonal strain in brainstem-cerebellar pathways and gray-matter at gray-white junctions in sagittal rotation, motivating future computational studies to quantify these links more directly. By combining region-resolved GFAP mapping with large-scale morphometry, this work provides a scalable framework for region-specific astrocyte mapping to support future multimodal, computational, and targeted neuroprotective studies.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对弥漫性创伤性脑损伤后星形胶质细胞反应难以在全脑范围内定量刻画区域异质性的问题，在雪貂模型中结合经验证的AI分割模型与脑图谱映射，对GFAP染色切片进行全脑分区定量，并用形态学流程分析分支复杂度和空间域特征。伤后七天，损伤组星形胶质细胞反应性升高并出现肥大性重塑，全脑层面凸包面积扩大、二级分支延长，以灰质及小脑、脑干亚区最明显，白质呈类似但较弱的趋势；海马虽有形态改变却未见反应性显著升高，提示结构重塑是星形胶质细胞反应中部分独立的维度。作者认为这些区域分布与脑干-小脑通路及灰白质交界处所受组织变形和轴突应变相符，但仅为一致性推测，尚需计算研究直接验证。

papers.title: Potential links between PCOS/PMOS and Alzheimer disease and related dementias.
papers.authors: Amiri M, Kakavand Hamidi A, Farkas DL, Buyalos RP, Azziz R.
papers.abstract: Background Polycystic ovary syndrome/polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PCOS/PMOS) is a common endocrine disorder with significant metabolic and reproductive implications. Increasing attention has focused on its potential long-term neurological consequences, including possible links to cognitive impairment and Alzheimer disease (AD), through overlapping biological pathways. Methods We conducted a comprehensive PubMed search, from inception through October 2025, identifying studies on cognitive performance, brain structure and function, neurodegenerative biomarkers, and dementia risk in PCOS/PMOS patients. Results Evidence supports multiple potential mechanistic pathways that could connect PCOS/PMOS to AD-relevant biology, such as insulin resistance (IR), chronic inflammation, hormonal dysregulation, and cardiovascular dysfunction. These pathways converge on neurodegeneration processes such as impaired Aβ clearance, tau hyperphosphorylation, oxidative stress, and cerebral metabolic deficits. Clinically, PCOS/PMOS patients exhibit mild but reproducible impairments in executive function and memory, alongside structural and functional brain alterations, including hippocampal and white matter changes, and altered network connectivity. However, these findings are influenced by coexisting metabolic dysfunction, and direct epidemiological evidence linking PCOS/PMOS to increased dementia incidence remains limited and inconsistent. Conclusion Current evidence indicates that any association between PCOS/PMOS and AD risk is likely mediated by metabolic comorbidities, particularly IR and obesity, rather than an independent effect of PCOS/PMOS itself. However, clinical evidence for increased PCOS/PMOS risk for cognitive vulnerability and dementia remain inconsistent and cognitive benefits from PCOS/PMOS-specific interventions are lacking. Clinical focus should therefore remain on optimizing metabolic health, while longitudinal and interventional studies are required to clarify long-term neurological relationships and outcomes.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述通过检索PubMed相关文献，梳理了多囊卵巢综合征/多内分泌代谢性卵巢综合征（PCOS/PMOS）与阿尔茨海默病及相关痴呆之间可能存在的联系。作者指出，胰岛素抵抗、慢性炎症、激素失调和心血管功能障碍等通路可能汇聚于Aβ清除受损、tau过度磷酸化等神经退行性过程；临床上PCOS/PMOS患者表现出轻度但可重复的执行功能和记忆损害，并伴有海马、白质及网络连接改变。不过，这些发现受共存的代谢功能障碍影响，将PCOS/PMOS与痴呆发病率升高直接联系起来的流行病学证据仍然有限且不一致。作者据此认为，任何关联更可能由代谢共病（尤其是胰岛素抵抗和肥胖）介导，而非PCOS/PMOS本身的独立效应，目前也缺乏针对该人群的特异性干预能改善认知的证据，临床重点仍应放在优化代谢健康上。

papers.title: The late positive component in recognition memory is linked to mnemonic evidence accumulation.
papers.authors: Sun J, Feuerriegel D, Nightingale M, Osth AF.
papers.abstract: Recognising objects from memory requires an integration of sensory and mnemonic information. This process has been theorised to occur via a stochastic evidence accumulation process implemented within the parietal cortex. Recent electroencephalographic (EEG) evidence indicates that the widely studied parietal Late Positive Component (LPC) shows characteristics of such a mnemonic accumulation signal. Here, we formally investigated this hypothesis using generative computational modelling that links a trial-level memory strength variable in the Diffusion Decision Model (DDM) with LPC amplitudes prior to the time of the decision. We recorded EEG from 24 participants making recognition judgements based on either studied or novel words. Each participant completed up to three testing sessions. We replicated recent findings that the LPC ramps up and peaks around the time of the decision and corresponding motor response. LPC amplitudes also covaried with accuracy and response time, as expected of a neural correlate of memory strength. By fitting DDMs to LPC amplitudes and behavioural data using specialised neural network tools, we demonstrate that LPC amplitudes are selectively associated with the rate of evidence accumulation, signifying memory strength. This association was stronger for previously studied words compared to novel words, and strongest at the time window immediately prior to the recognition decision. Our findings, therefore, recast the LPC as a neural signature of mnemonic strength linked to the rate of evidence accumulation during recognition memory decisions.

papers.title: A clinically interpretable model for Parkinson's disease: insights from complementary MRI modalities.
papers.authors: Zheng Q, Wen J, Yuan W, Qin J, Duanmu X, Wu H, Zhu Z, Guo T, Wu C, Zhou C, Wu J, Chen J, Fang Y, Zhu B, Yan Y, Tian J, Zhang B, He H, Zhang M, Guan X, Xu X.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of Parkinson's disease may remain challenging in certain clinical scenarios, highlighting the need for a clinical decision-support model based on complementary MRI modalities. The case-control study included 462 participants, split into training [247 Parkinson's disease, 122 normal controls (NC)] and testing (60 Parkinson's disease, 33 NC) cohorts to construct and validate a clinical decision-support model. We employed least absolute shrinkage and selection operator and logistic regression analysis to develop the model utilizing quantitative susceptibility mapping, arterial spin labelling and T1-weighted images. The model was assessed for calibration, discrimination and clinical utility, with individual predicted scores correlated to Parkinson's disease clinical symptoms. The model's performance was also evaluated independently in multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy and essential tremor, with DeLong test comparisons. The model was trained in the training cohort (Parkinson's disease: 61.39 ± 8.06 years old, 134 males; NC: 61.29 ± 7.56 years old, 54 males) with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.842 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.798-0.883] and 0.771 (95% CI 0.657-0.870) in the testing cohort, whose clinical utility was confirmed. The predicted scores were positively correlated with Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale II (P = 0.034) and III (P = 0.015), while negatively correlated with the Purdue Pegboard total (P = 0.010) and assembly scores (P = 0.007). When discriminating each disease group from NC, the model's performance to identify multiple system atrophy and progressive supranuclear palsy with AUC values of 0.881 and 0.895 was superior than essential tremor with an AUC of 0.709 before false discovery rate correction (multiple system atrophy-NC versus essential tremor-NC: P = 0.041; progressive supranuclear palsy-NC versus essential tremor-NC: P = 0.010). The model based on complementary MRI modalities was an objective clinical decision-support measure for Parkinson's disease with potential applications in other parkinsonisms (multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy).

papers.title: Human-artificial intelligence collaboration for comanaging epilepsy in real time.
papers.authors: Goldblum Z, Shi H, Xu Z, Ojemann WKS, Aguila CA, Long K, Xie K, Nix KC, Walsh KG, Chang E, Lavelle SB, Bach B, Davis KA, Sinha N, Hammer LH, Conrad EC, Litt B.
papers.abstract: One-third of the world's 70 million people with epilepsy have seizures uncontrolled by medication, and implantable devices are a promising treatment. These devices can detect impending seizures, missed medication and impaired cognition, but, like most medical devices, they cannot share this information with patients in real time. This is a missed opportunity for devices to learn from clinical events and teach patients how their behaviors affect their health. Here we present a device platform that converses with patients to help them manage their epilepsy. The inpatient prototype links scalp and intracranial electroencephalography (EEG) to a secure, large language model-based artificial intelligence (AI) that communicates bidirectionally through a smartphone app. The AI processes biomarkers of sleep, medication, cognition and seizure probability, notifies patients of clinical events and trends, records symptoms and responses, and uses their feedback to retrain its seizure detector, reducing false alarms. We validated this platform in 13 patients who are undergoing video-EEG monitoring for epilepsy (scalp, n = 11; intracranial, n = 2). In a pseudoprospective simulation, seizure detectors improved precision from patient feedback alone, without expert intervention. We propose this system as a scalable, safeguarded platform for medical devices that can rapidly adapt to patient and provider needs across epilepsy and other medical conditions.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对植入式癫痫设备无法与患者实时共享信息的问题，开发了一套连接头皮与颅内脑电、基于大语言模型的人工智能平台，通过智能手机应用与患者双向交流，处理睡眠、用药、认知和发作概率等生物标志物，并记录患者反馈以重新训练发作检测器。研究在13名接受视频脑电监测的癫痫患者中验证了该平台，模拟结果显示仅凭患者反馈即可提高检测精确度、减少误报，无需专家干预。作者据此提出，这一系统可作为可扩展且有防护的医疗设备平台，快速适应癫痫及其他疾病中患者和医护人员的需求。

papers.title: Openness to experience modulates the neural dynamics of semantic processing.
papers.authors: Li B, Huang CM, Lin Q, Huang HW.
papers.abstract: Personality fundamentally shapes language processing, yet the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying this relationship remain poorly understood. Openness to experience (Openness), as measured by the NEO Five-Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI), has been associated with enhanced creativity and engagement with novel semantic information. This study examined how openness modulates the neural dynamics of semantic processing using event-related potentials (ERPs) during a semantic category verification task. Participants evaluated category relatedness across the four levels of semantic structure, including high typicality (HT), low typicality (LT), related violations (RV), and nonrelated violations (NRV). Neural responses exhibited the expected graded pattern, with N400 amplitudes becoming more negative as semantic relatedness decreased. Critically, higher Openness was associated with greater N400 differentiation between related and nonrelated violations, an effect uniquely predicted by Openness beyond the remaining four personality traits. Follow-up analyses revealed that this differentiation was primarily driven by enhanced N400 responses to nonrelated violations rather than by reduced responses to related violations. This pattern is inconsistent with a simple facilitation account in which higher Openness uniformly eases semantic processing. Instead, it suggests that Openness is associated with heightened sensitivity to semantic mismatch or more sustained semantic evaluation when incoming information is incompatible with an activated context. Behavioral performance was comparable across participants; the observed neural differences were not accompanied by detectable differences in task success. Together, these findings establish that Openness is systematically related to variation in the neural dynamics of semantic processing, while highlighting the need to clarify the underlying cognitive mechanisms and contributions of other individual differences.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察开放性人格如何调节语义加工的电生理动态，采用语义类别验证任务并记录事件相关电位，比较不同语义关联水平下的神经反应。结果发现，语义关联性越低，N400波幅越负，呈预期的梯度模式；开放性较高者对相关违反与非相关违反之间的N400差异更大，且这一效应在其余四种人格特质之外仍由开放性独立预测。后续分析显示，该差异主要来自对非相关违反的N400反应增强，而非对相关违反的反应减弱，因而不支持开放性普遍促进语义加工的简单解释，更可能反映对语义不匹配的敏感性提高或语义评估更持续。行为表现在各参与者间相当，神经差异未伴随可检测的任务成绩差异，作者据此强调仍需厘清其认知机制及其他个体差异的作用。

papers.title: Effects of intensive sensorimotor rehabilitation in resting state functional connectivity in a rodent model of Cerebral Palsy.
papers.authors: Sanches E, Schirmbeck G, Mairesse J, Ho D, Dennez C, Baud O, Sizonenko S.
papers.abstract: Background Sensorimotor stimulation has been shown to protect against brain damage and function impairments following experimental Cerebral Palsy (CP). Functional ultrasound (fUS) gives valuable information about brain connectivity at unprecedented spatial and time resolutions with high translational potential. We tested brain function and connectivity using fUS following experimental CP and the effects of early sensorimotor rehabilitation in the model. Methods Pregnant Wistar rats were exposed to maternal immune challenge at E18-19. Pups received perinatal anoxia at postnatal day 0 (P0) and restriction of the hindlimbs from P2 to P21. Rehabilitation (EETT) used environmental enrichment (EE) and Treadmill Training (TT) from P21 to P28. At P29, fUS was performed to access brain connectivity and graph theoretic analysis was used to distinguish patterns of brain connectivity. Results CP increased intrinsic brain functional connectivity compared to Controls and EETT animals. Connectivity was increased in CP animals in cortical areas related to sensorimotor function and subcortical myelinated structures. EETT animals showed levels of brain connectivity similar to Controls. Conclusions Sensorimotor stimulation changed brain hyperconnectivity profile induced by CP. Brain connectivity pattern alterations can be detected using fUS with high accuracy, suggesting great potential to be used as earlier biomarker for neurodevelopmentalal disorders such as CP.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在实验性大鼠脑瘫模型中考察早期感觉运动康复对静息态脑功能连接的影响，采用功能超声成像结合图论分析评估脑连接模式。结果显示，脑瘫模型动物皮层感觉运动区及皮层下髓鞘化结构的固有功能连接较对照组升高，而接受环境丰富化与跑台训练联合康复的动物，其连接水平与对照组相近，提示感觉运动刺激可改变脑瘫引起的脑连接过度增强。作者认为功能超声能较准确地检测连接模式改变，有望作为脑瘫等神经发育障碍的早期生物标志物，但这一应用潜力尚待进一步验证。

papers.title: Default mode network mechanisms of trait rumination in treatment-resistant depression and rTMS: evidence from source-localized EEG.
papers.authors: Chu SA, Valles TE, Citrenbaum CC, Leuchter MK, Shamas M, Leuchter AF, Corlier J.
papers.abstract: Background Rumination is a transdiagnostic feature of multiple psychiatric disorders and is a critical risk factor for more severe episodes and poor treatment outcomes in treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) ameliorates both depressive and ruminative symptoms in TRD. While prior literature has linked rumination to abnormal default mode network (DMN) connectivity, the electrophysiological correlates of rumination in the DMN are not well understood. Methods Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data were examined in a cohort of 66 TRD subjects who underwent 30 sessions of rTMS treatment for TRD administered to left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). We employed source-localization and calculated four metrics of functional connectivity (Amplitude Envelope Correlation [AEC], weighted Phase Lag Index [wPLI], magnitude-squared coherence, and Spectral Correlation Coefficient [SCC]) across five frequency bands within the DMN to identify the neural correlates of rumination in TRD. Correction for multiple comparisons was performed using the Network Based Statistic (NBS). Results Baseline severity of rumination and depression were positively correlated, but AEC alpha band connectivity was positively associated only with baseline rumination severity and not depression. Rumination severity prior to treatment was not associated with any other connectivity metric. Severity of rumination and depression decreased following rTMS treatment, but alpha AEC connectivity did not charge after 30 sessions of rTMS treatment. Conclusion Higher DMN connectivity, as measured by alpha-band AEC, is a stable trait-like neurophysiological marker of rumination that is not significantly affected by rTMS administered to left DLPFC.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注难治性抑郁症中反刍思维与默认模式网络电生理特征的关系，以及重复经颅磁刺激治疗对其的影响。研究对接受左侧背外侧前额叶rTMS治疗的难治性抑郁症患者进行静息态脑电溯源分析，计算默认模式网络内多个频段的功能连接指标。结果发现，基线反刍严重程度与抑郁严重程度正相关，但仅alpha频段的振幅包络相关连接与基线反刍严重程度正相关，而与抑郁无关；其他连接指标均无此关联。治疗后反刍和抑郁症状均减轻，但该alpha频段连接未随治疗改变。作者据此认为，较高的默认模式网络alpha频段连接可能是反刍思维一种稳定的、特质样的神经生理标记，且不受左侧背外侧前额叶rTMS的显著影响。

papers.title: Neurophysiological signatures underlying preserved lexical-semantic proficiency in healthy aging.
papers.authors: Nurmi P, Ala-Salomäki H, Renvall H, Liljeström M.
papers.abstract: Although semantic cognition remains behaviorally stable with age, neuroimaging studies report age-related alterations in response to semantic context. To address these inconsistent findings, we combined behavioral and magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures and examined the neural mechanisms underlying lexical-semantic processing in healthy aging. Forty-six Finnish-speaking adults across younger (22 - 32 years) and older (62 - 69 years) cohorts performed a semantic congruency judgment task on word pairs. Both age groups performed the task with high accuracy, with older adults responding faster than younger. While task performance was retained in older adults, MEG revealed a shift in the neural activation patterns with advancing age. Younger participants exhibited the canonical N400 effect in the left temporal cortex 300 - 400 ms post-stimulus, followed by a late semantic effect, whereas older adults showed less pronounced congruency effects, and the activation distribution was shifted toward frontal and bilateral regions. Despite the absence of the canonical N400 effect in older participants, multivariate time-resolved decoding demonstrated that the congruency effect was decodable from the MEG activation patterns in both groups from ~300 ms post-stimulus, indicating preserved sensitivity to congruency with age. Decoding performance further correlated with response times, suggesting that greater neural separation between semantic concepts, indicated by higher decodability, is associated with rapid decision-making. Critically, age groups were distinguishable based on their neural responses 300 - 800 ms post-stimulus, indicating a functional reorganization of semantic processing in older adults. Overall, our findings suggest that healthy aging involves a reconfiguration of neural systems associated with preserved semantic proficiency, despite broader age-related cognitive changes.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究结合行为测量与脑磁图，考察健康老龄化中词汇语义加工保持稳定的神经机制。行为上两组均能准确完成任务，老年人反应更快；但脑磁图显示，老年人虽缺乏典型的N400效应，语义一致性信息仍可从约300毫秒起的激活模式中解码，且解码表现与反应时相关。研究还发现两年龄组的神经反应在刺激后300至800毫秒可区分，提示老年人语义加工存在功能重组，从而在更广泛的认知变化背景下维持语义能力。

papers.title: Parallel development and maturation of GABAergic interneurons and corticotrophin-releasing factor signaling within the amygdala complex.
papers.authors: Demaestri C, Delevich K, Gourley SL, Tseng KY.
papers.abstract: The amygdala complex is known to play a critical role in supporting adaptive behaviors in response to environmental stimuli, particularly during sensitive periods of brain development. Through its connections, the amygdala modulates hippocampal and striatal-dependent memories and shapes distinct cortical function within the emotional and cognitive domains. Major neural circuit remodeling is known to occur in the amygdala during postnatal development through adolescence, which includes the maturation of its excitatory connectivity and the progressive organization of local GABAergic inhibitory interneurons. Thus, the goal of this paper is to review current knowledge on how developmental trajectories of distinct GABAergic interneuron populations within the amygdala are temporally staggered to enable successive sensitive periods during which environmental input impacts amygdala-dependent emotional learning, threat processing, and social behavior. This review will discuss the early emerging somatostatin and neuropeptide Y interneurons, later maturing parvalbumin-positive interneurons, and developmental changes in stress-responsive corticotrophin-releasing factor signaling. We examine how these trajectories may shape age-appropriate behavior and sensitivity to early life adversity as GABAergic circuits within the amygdala mature.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Psychobiology.
papers.authors: Andreazza AC, Behnke A, Bolanos JP, Juan-Sanz J, Epel E, Evans MK, Barrett LF, Gyllenhammer LE, Hirabayashi Y, Hirano M, Hollis F, Kelly DP, Kempes C, Kolassa IT, Lane N, Lobo MK, Mujica-Parodi LR, O'Donovan A, Ongur D, Picard M, Pressman SD, Sandi C, Shirihai O, Trumpff C, Oudenhove LV, Wager TD.
papers.abstract: A field that uses mitochondria to unify biological and psychological sciences and to better understand the basis of health has emerged-Mitochondrial Psychobiology. Mitochondria are the body's cellular hubs for energy transformation and signaling. Mitochondria regulate functions as diverse as metabolism, gene expression, and stress adaptation; consequently, their dysregulation is linked to most chronic illnesses and aging. Here, we propose that mitochondria provide a mechanistic bridge between body and the measurable functions of the mind, including perception, cognition, emotion, and behavior. From this perspective, mitochondria provide a scientifically tractable interface through which bioenergetic processes relate to subjective experiences and behaviors. We outline foundational principles for Mitochondrial Psychobiology, discuss the key gaps that the field needs to address to advance our understanding of mind-mitochondria relationships across the lifecourse, and review emerging approaches to probe the mind-mitochondria connection across levels. This stimulating scientific challenge is a unique opportunity to train the next generation of interdisciplinary scientists, resolve conceptual and technical challenges spanning temporal and spatial scales, and develop a more accurate, holistic model of health. Rooted in general energetic principles, mitochondrial psychobiology is poised to productively steer biomedicine over the coming decades.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic reductions in glymphatic-related perivascular diffusion across psychiatric disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Pascucci A, Saccaro LF, Forrer S, Marenco G, Merola PG, Linares AE, Gracia IV, Sandini C, Delavari F, Piguet C, Van De Ville D, Eliez S.
papers.abstract: Background The glymphatic system, a perivascular pathway supporting cerebrospinal and interstitial fluid exchange and clearance, has been implicated in neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders. Diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) provides a non-invasive proxy for glymphatic-related processes, yet its role in psychiatric conditions remains uncertain. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, PsycNET, and Embase for articles published up to September 25th, 2025. The protocol was pre-registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251155430). Studies reporting diffusion-based indices of glymphatic function in psychiatric populations were included. Standardised mean differences (Hedges' g) were calculated for patient-control comparisons and pooled using random-effects models. Heterogeneity, methodological moderators, and risk of bias were assessed. Results Thirty-two studies met inclusion criteria for the systematic review, covering major psychiatric groups including mood disorders, autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, psychosis, sleep disorders, and substance-related conditions. Twenty-four studies (n = 2855; 1503 patients, 1352 controls) reporting bilateral DTI-ALPS measures were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled random-effects model revealed a significant transdiagnostic reduction in DTI-ALPS index in psychiatric populations compared with healthy controls (Hedges' g = -0.78, 95% CI -1.01 to -0.55, p < 0.0001). Between-study heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 86.3%), and there was evidence of small-study effects. Conclusions Bilateral DTI-ALPS index showed a robust but heterogeneous reduction across psychiatric disorders. These results suggest that impairments of perivascular diffusion, as indexed by DTI-ALPS, may reflect a shared transdiagnostic pattern across psychiatric conditions. Harmonised imaging pipelines and multimodal validation are needed to clarify the biological and clinical significance of these findings.

papers.title: Dual-mode dynamics in hippocampal populations enable rapid and precise spatial coding.
papers.authors: Ren M, Feng S, Chen Q, Lin L, Xu J.
papers.abstract: Hippocampal spatial representations emerge within minutes of first exposure to novel environments, challenging models based solely on gradual synaptic plasticity. Here, we show that CA1 spatial coding is organized according to a dual-mode architecture comprising a pre-organized backbone and an experience-dependent component. Backbone cells expressing immediately emerging place fields form a stable spatial scaffold and dominate positional decoding from the first traversal, whereas experience-dependent cells bearing gradually emerging fields are progressively incorporated to refine spatial representations. Analyses of ensemble activity further reveal that offline dynamics prospectively organize future spatial coding. In backbone cells, latent tuning aligns with their future place fields prior to task engagement, while in experience-dependent cells this alignment strengthens before overt place-field expression. Together, these findings identify a dual-mode organization of hippocampal populations in which offline dynamics pre-organize network activity to enable rapid and precise spatial coding in novel environments.

papers.title: Anterior cingulate feedback facilitates rapid global context modulation in primary visual cortex.
papers.authors: Peterka DS, Imai F, Ross JM, Bastos G, Hornick MA, Rachmany L, Gallimore CG, Hockley A, Hamm JP.
papers.abstract: Context modulates sensory processing. Recent proposals claim early areas like primary visual cortex (V1) are only influenced by "local" context (e.g., recent stimulus history), while "global" context (e.g., learned patterns and probabilities) modulates only higher areas. We tested this using a global/local oddball paradigm: mice viewed repeating five-item sequences (AAAA-B), where B is deviant from local context but typical in global context. Using two-photon imaging and local field potential (LFP) recording in mouse V1, we found that global predictability normalized responses to B stimuli. This effect emerged after fewer than 10 sequence repetitions, demonstrating rapid learning. When a globally deviant "C" stimulus replaced B or when B occurred at unpredictable intervals (i.e., standard oddball), V1 showed strong response enhancement. This global context modulation in V1 required top-down feedback from anterior cingulate area. However, when B was replaced by an A (AAAA-A), responses were mixed, suggesting that stimulus-specific adaptation can constrain prediction-error signals in V1.

papers.title: Diffusion MRI assessment of white matter microstructure and free-water fraction in drug-naïve children with SeLECTS.
papers.authors: Zhou X, Chen Y, Luo Y, Kuang Y, Deng C, Lai H.
papers.abstract: Background Self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) is a common childhood-onset focal epilepsy syndrome. Although seizures are typically self-limited, some children may show neurodevelopmental or cognitive vulnerability. Diffusion MRI may provide insight into white matter alterations in SeLECTS. Objective To evaluate white matter diffusion differences in newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS using tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) and white matter free-water fraction (FW-WM), and to explore within-patient associations with selected seizure-related and cognitive variables. Methods Fifty-three newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS and 53 healthy controls with a similar age and sex distribution were prospectively enrolled in this cross-sectional case-control study. Diffusion MRI was acquired at 3.0 T, and white matter diffusion differences were assessed using TBSS and FW-WM analyses. Voxelwise between-group differences in fractional anisotropy (FA) were tested with age and sex as covariates and corrected using threshold-free cluster enhancement-based family-wise error correction. FW-WM was compared between groups using age- and sex-adjusted general linear models, with additional adjustment for years of education in a sensitivity analysis. Exploratory within-patient associations between imaging measures and selected clinical or cognitive variables were assessed using partial Spearman correlations with false-discovery-rate correction. Results Children with SeLECTS showed lower FA than healthy controls in multiple TBSS-defined white matter regions after correction for multiple comparisons, mainly involving commissural, projection, and association pathways. No between-group differences in mean, axial, or radial diffusivity survived correction for multiple comparisons. FW-WM was higher in the SeLECTS group after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted mean difference = 0.0085; 95% CI, 0.0023-0.0147; P = 0.008), with similar results after additional adjustment for education. In exploratory cluster-level analyses, mean FA in a left-sided cluster involving the posterior internal capsule, posterior thalamic radiation, and sagittal stratum was inversely associated with disease duration after FDR correction (r = -0.413; P = 0.003; q = 0.010). No imaging-cognition or within-patient FW-WM-FA association survived FDR correction. Conclusions Newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS showed white matter diffusion differences, including lower FA in distributed TBSS-defined regions and higher FW-WM. These findings support diffusion MRI-based characterization of white matter alterations at diagnosis, before antiseizure treatment. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their clinical and developmental relevance.
papers.summary_zh: 该横断面病例对照研究考察了初诊未用药的SeLECTS患儿白质微结构是否存在弥散MRI可见的差异，并与年龄性别分布相近的健康儿童比较，采用基于纤维束的空间统计和自由水分数分析。结果显示，患儿在多个白质区域各向异性分数低于对照组，且平均自由水分数更高，而平均、轴向和径向弥散系数未见组间差异。探索性分析中，左侧一簇区域的平均各向异性分数与病程呈负相关，但影像与认知指标及自由水分数与各向异性分数之间未见经校正的关联。作者认为这些发现支持在抗癫痫治疗前用弥散MRI刻画白质改变，其临床和发育意义仍需纵向研究澄清。

papers.title: State-specific dynamic functional connectivity disturbances in spinal cord injury-related neuropathic pain.
papers.authors: Sun C, Xin H, Wang L, Chen Q, Wang Y, Yang B, Chen X, Li F, Lu J, Chen N.
papers.abstract: This exploratory study aimed to characterize dynamic functional network connectivity (dFNC) alterations in spinal cord injury-induced neuropathic pain (SCI-NP) and dFNC-related metrics as biomarkers for treatment guidance. A total of 23 SCI individuals with NP (SCI-NP), 20 SCI individuals without NP (SCI-N), and 20 healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled. SCI-NP individuals were predominantly chronic (≥12 months post-injury), whereas SCI-N individuals were predominantly acute/subacute (<12 months post-injury). Resting-state fMRI data were analyzed using independent component analysis (ICA) combined with a sliding-window approach to characterize dFNC. Recurring connectivity states were identified using clustering algorithms. Group differences were assessed using ANCOVA, adjusting for age and sex.
