Behavioral analyses revealed a significant Group × Target Type interaction. For the less common [1+3] pattern, low synchronizers exhibited reliable rhythmic priming, whereas high synchronizers showed little or no priming benefit. In contrast, priming effects for the dominant [2+2] pattern were modest and comparable across groups. Furthermore, higher theta-band CACoh was associated with smaller priming effects for [1+3] targets, indicating that stronger neural synchronization predicted reduced behavioral facilitation. These findings suggest that the influence of auditory rhythm on speech production depends jointly on individual neural synchronization capacity and the rhythmic structure of the planned utterance. The results provide new evidence that auditory-motor interactions in speech production are shaped by both listener-specific and utterance-specific factors.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察个体神经同步差异如何调节听觉节律对言语产生的启动效应，以及这种调节是否随目标句的节律结构而变化。86名母语为普通话的参与者完成四音节言语产生任务，目标为常见的[2+2]和较少见的[1+3]两种节律模式，并记录脑电与纯音节律包络的脑-声耦合及反应时。结果发现，神经同步水平与目标类型存在交互：对较少见的[1+3]模式，低同步组表现出明显的节律启动，而高同步组几乎没有获益；对常见的[2+2]模式，两组的启动效应都较小且相近。此外，较高的theta频段脑-声耦合与[1+3]目标更小的启动效应相关。作者据此认为，听觉节律对言语产生的影响同时取决于个体神经同步能力和计划话语的节律结构，提示言语产生中的听觉-运动交互受听者特征与话语特征共同塑造。

papers.title: Beyond Ophthalmoplegia: Wernicke Encephalopathy with Anisocoria.
papers.authors: Ito Y, Hayashi K, Kurihara H, Nakaya Y, Sato M.
papers.abstract: A 69-year-old man with a history of heavy alcohol consumption and poor nutrition presented with disorientation and gait instability. The cognitive assessment was severely affected, with the Hasegawa Dementia Scale-Revised score was 4. Neurological examination revealed anisocoria (right 4.0 mm, left 2.0 mm) with sluggish light reflexes, gaze-evoked horizontal nystagmus, and vertical gaze restrictions. He exhibited disorientation and limb ataxia; deep tendon reflexes were normal. Brain MRI showed bilateral thalamic hyperintensities on diffusion-weighted imaging and periaqueductal high signal on T2 FLAIR. Laboratory testing confirmed a severely reduced serum thiamine level of 10.5 ng/mL, establishing Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) based on Caine's criteria. Immediately upon admission (Day 1), high-dose thiamine therapy was initiated at 700 mg/day (300 mg/day intravenous drip plus 400 mg/day oral) for 7 days, followed by 400 mg/day oral. Despite prompt, high-dose thiamine administration, the 2.0 mm anisocoria persisted consistently throughout the 19-day hospitalization, whereas cognitive function and ataxia partially improved. The 2.0 mm interocular difference confirmed pathologic anisocoria, indicating asymmetric autonomic disruption involving descending sympathetic pathways in the periaqueductal gray matter. While neuro-ophthalmic signs in WE are typically reversible, this case demonstrates that autonomic deficits may persist despite comprehensive thiamine therapy, highlighting WE as a critical metabolic mimic of life-threatening structural brainstem disorders.

papers.title: Enteral Feeding Progression Trajectories in the First Two Postnatal Weeks Are Associated with Motor Neurodevelopment at 24 Months in Preterm Infants: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
papers.authors: Di Chiara M, Terrin G, Van Reet V, Van Grambezen B, Dito L, Regoli D, Caravale B, De Groote A, Piersigilli F.
papers.abstract: Background/objectives Preterm infants are at substantial risk of neurodevelopmental impairment. Current guidelines recommend gradual advancement of enteral feeds during the first postnatal weeks, but the rate that is optimal for the individual infant remains uncertain. We modeled the day-by-day balance between enteral and parenteral nutrition during the first two postnatal weeks as longitudinal trajectory phenotypes and examined their association with neurodevelopment at 24 months of corrected age. Methods Retrospective multi-center observational cohort of preterm infants (gestational age < 32 completed weeks or birth weight < 1500 g) from two centers managed under closely aligned nutritional protocols. The daily enteral-to-total-energy ratio on postnatal days 0-7 and 14 was clustered by K-means (K = 3) into parenteral-dominant (C0), moderate-progression (C1) and rapid-progression (C2) phenotypes. The primary outcome was the Bayley-III Motor composite at 24 months; Cognitive and Language composites at 24 months and the Motor composite at 12-18 months were additional outcomes. Linear mixed-effects models were adjusted for gestational age, birth-weight z-score and sex, with a random intercept for center. Results Among 260 infants, three trajectory phenotypes were identified. At 24 months, the moderate-progression cluster had a higher Motor composite than the parenteral-dominant cluster (adjusted mean difference + 4.96 points; 95% CI, +1.51 to +8.41; p = 0.005; n = 194). In exploratory analyses of the other two domains, the unadjusted differences favoring the moderate cluster (cognitive + 7.1 points, p = 0.022; language + 6.9 points, p = 0.009) were abolished by adjustment for maturity (cognitive + 0.17 points, p = 0.94; language + 1.80 points, p = 0.45), whereas the motor difference remained statistically significant; the confidence intervals for these two domains do not exclude clinically relevant differences. The rapid-progression cluster did not differ significantly from either the parenteral-dominant or the moderate cluster, yielding a non-monotonic pattern. The motor association remained statistically significant after adjustment for baseline illness severity and was attenuated only marginally by downstream morbidities or the proportion of human milk. Conclusions A moderate-progression enteral trajectory during the first two postnatal weeks was associated with better motor neurodevelopment at 24 months, whereas rapid advancement did not differ from parenteral dominance, so that the association was confined to a graded progression rather than to either extreme. The moderate-progression association was homogeneous across gestational-age strata (cluster × gestational age interaction, p = 0.23). These real-world findings are compatible with previously divergent evidence within a single non-monotonic dose-response framework.

papers.title: Association of Diagnosis Age with Clinical Characteristics and MRI Findings in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.authors: Mirmosayyeb O, Aghajanian S, Mohammadifard F, Zabeti A, Shaygannejad V.
papers.abstract: Background Age at multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis may be associated with clinical course, inflammatory activity, and disability accrual, but evidence across the full age spectrum remains limited. We compared clinical and radiological features, phenotype distribution, and time to first post-diagnosis relapse across early-onset MS (EOMS), adult-onset MS (AOMS), and late-onset MS (LOMS). Methods This observational study included patients with MS treated at two tertiary centers in Isfahan, Iran, combining a retrospective review of clinical records with a cross-sectional assessment at the most recent study visit. Patients were categorized as EOMS (MS diagnosis at ≤18 years), AOMS, or LOMS (diagnosis at or after 50 years) according to age at diagnosis. Demographic, clinical, MRI, and comorbidity data were compared across groups. Time to first post-diagnosis relapse was analyzed in RRMS using Cox regression, and continuous age effects were explored with spline models. Results Among 3994 patients, 257 had EOMS, 3587 had AOMS, and 150 had LOMS. EOMS had a higher hazard of first post-diagnosis relapse (adjusted HR: 1.27, 95% CI: 1.05-1.54) and more frequent enhancing brain lesions. LOMS had a more progressive phenotype, higher EDSS at diagnosis and qualitative brain atrophy, and more age-associated comorbidities. The adjusted LOMS relapse estimate (HR: 0.58, 95% CI: 0.34-0.99) was borderline significant. Progressive MS became more common with increasing diagnosis age, largely reflecting PPMS, although unequal follow-up and last-visit classification limit causal interpretation. Female predominance persisted across all groups but was less pronounced in LOMS. Conclusions Age at diagnosis was associated with clinical and radiological differences across the MS spectrum from a more relapsing phenotype to a more progressive, disability-associated phenotype. These findings should be verified in prospective studies based on symptomatic onset age.

papers.title: Temporal Change: Evaluation of Brain Atrophy in Patients with Radiologically Isolated Syndrome Using volBrain.
papers.authors: Akkoç F, Alagöz AN, Bünül SD, Alparslan B, Efendi H.
papers.abstract: Background and Objective: Radiologically isolated syndrome (RIS) is characterized by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings suggestive of multiple sclerosis (MS) in individuals without a history of clinical demyelinating events. Increasing evidence indicates that structural brain abnormalities may be present in RIS before the development of overt neurological symptoms. However, most previous studies have employed cross-sectional designs, limiting the ability to characterize the temporal evolution of neurodegenerative changes. This study aimed to investigate longitudinal changes in global, regional, and lobar brain volumes in individuals with RIS using serial MRI examinations obtained at least six months apart. Methods: Patients with RIS who had undergone two 3 Tesla (3T) brain MRI examinations separated by an interval of at least six months were retrospectively identified. Three-dimensional (3D) T1-weighted MRI scans obtained at both time points were analyzed using the volBrain pipeline of the volBrain platform to quantify global, regional, and lobar brain volumes. Longitudinal volumetric changes were expressed as annualized percentage volume changes. The number of T2 lesions and total T2 lesion volume were additionally assessed, and their associations with longitudinal brain volume changes were investigated. Results: A total of 28 patients with RIS were included. After correction for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure, significant annual volume loss was observed in total brain volume (p = 0.043), total cerebrum volume (p = 0.033), right cerebrum volume (p = 0.033), left cerebrum volume (p = 0.044), total thalamic volume (p = 0.033), right thalamic volume (p = 0.047), and left thalamic volume (p = 0.043). No significant associations were observed between annualized brain volume changes and follow-up duration, total or regional T2 lesion counts, or total T2 lesion volume. Similarly, annualized brain volume changes did not differ significantly between subgroups defined according to MRI progression, the presence of gadolinium-enhancing lesions, or the presence of spinal cord lesions. Conclusions: Longitudinal volumetric analysis demonstrated progressive brain volume loss involving both global and regional structures in patients with RIS. These findings provide further evidence of measurable longitudinal structural brain changes in RIS before the development of clinically overt demyelinating disease. Larger longitudinal studies incorporating appropriate control groups are warranted to further characterize the temporal trajectory of volumetric changes in RIS.

papers.title: Cognitive Reserve: White Matter, Microvascular, Glymphatic and Cholinergic Dysfunction in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.authors: Wood PL.
papers.abstract: Late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD) is a cognitive disorder that leads to the requirement of full-time care. The ever-increasing growth of the LOAD population demands that more research be dedicated to the discovery/design of effective therapeutics. The two major hypotheses that have been evaluated in the clinic include the cholinergic and the amyloid hypotheses. Unfortunately, the therapeutics that have resulted from research in these areas have minimal clinical impact. These are, respectively, the cholinesterase inhibitors and the anti-amyloid therapies. Clearly, a new path forward is needed. To this end, a number of genetic approaches and biochemical investigations are currently being employed to provide new insights into the pathophysiology of dementia. While there currently is a diverse array of dysfunctions that have been reported in LOAD subjects, white matter (WM) dysfunction may be a nodal point that is critical to the pathophysiology of cognitive decline. In this review, I present our current knowledge of WM dysfunction in LOAD. This addresses the potential contributions of microvascular dysfunction to WM abnormalities and neuronal dysfunction. This knowledge base has the potential to lead to a new approach for treating cholinergic dysfunction in cognitive disorders.

papers.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for 3D Medical Imaging: A Scoping Review of Volumetric Attribution Methods.
papers.authors: Bhati D, Nahata MR, Neha F, Bellan R, Bhati D.
papers.abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods developed for two-dimensional images may not preserve spatial context when applied to volumetric medical imaging. This scoping review map attribution methods for 3D medical images and examines how dimensionality is preserved across model inference, attribution generation, and visualization. Following PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched IEEE Xplore, PubMed, ACM Digital Library, Semantic Scholar, and arXiv for studies published from January 2018 to May 2026. We mapped 32 selected studies by attribution method, imaging modality, clinical task, evaluation approach, and dimensionality paradigm. Grad-CAM and its variants were the most frequently reported method family. Within the selected corpus, two studies were classified as P2 boundary cases, 29 as P3, and one as P4. Most studies using volumetric inference presented explanations through two-dimensional views, and quantitative evaluation of attribution quality was uncommon. These findings identify a gap between volumetric model inference and explanation presentation and motivate improved volumetric visualization and more consistent evaluation.

papers.title: A Survey on U-Net with Variants and Their Applications in Two-Dimensional Medical Image Segmentations.
papers.authors: Wu T, Ullah S, Yu B, Ullah F, Wang J, Gao Z, Yoshigoe K, Zhao Y.
papers.abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a critical role in computer-assisted diagnosis, treatment planning, surgical navigation, and quantitative medical image analysis. Among deep learning-based segmentation architectures, U-Net has become one of the most influential frameworks because of its encoder-decoder structure and skip connections for integrating semantic and spatial information. This review focuses on U-Net and representative variants for two-dimensional medical image segmentation. We systematically analyze their architectural evolution, including attention-based designs, enhanced skip connections, deformable convolutions, and Transformer-based extensions and discuss their advantages, limitations, and application boundaries. Quantitative performance results are synthesized from published studies rather than reproduced through new benchmarking experiments; direct numerical comparisons are restricted to models evaluated within the same study or under clearly defined benchmark settings. We further relate architectural modifications to modality-specific challenges in MRI, CT, ultrasound, fundus imaging, dermoscopy, and microscopy. Finally, current challenges in computational efficiency, cross-domain generalization, data scarcity, interpretability, and clinical deployment are discussed, together with promising directions for future research.

papers.title: β-Catenin Knockout in the Olfactory Bulb and Hippocampus Reveals Dual Roles in Olfactory Discrimination and Working Memory.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Kong M, Jin H, Chu TL, Lim LW, Cheah KSE.
papers.abstract: Mice rely heavily on their sense of smell to provide crucial environmental information. The intricate organization of neural circuits within the olfactory bulb (OB) and the communication across the OB-hippocampus network in mice underpin their ability to discriminate and adapt to odors and perform odor-guided behaviors. Wnt/β-catenin signaling has been shown to regulate neural stem cell proliferation and migration during embryogenesis and adult neurogenesis. However, the potential role of β-catenin in adult OB and hippocampus in olfaction, odor-guided behavior and working memory is not known. Here, we report the unexpected expression of collagen, type X, alpha 1 (Col10a1 ), in the postnatal mouse OB and the hippocampus starting at approximately postnatal day 14. We exploited this finding to generate OB and hippocampus conditional Ctnnb1 knockout (Ctnnb1 cKO ) mice. We found Ctnnb1 cKO mice displayed impaired odor habituation and discrimination abilities, whereas food foraging ability was unaffected. Surprisingly, Ctnnb1 cKO mice displayed modestly improved working memory in the Radial Arm Maze test. Together, these findings identify behavioral phenotypes associated with Col10a1 -Cre-driven Ctnnb1 deletion and establish this mouse line as a useful tool for studying β-catenin function in adult OB-hippocampal circuits.

papers.title: Ectopic Adrenal Cortical Tissue in the Ovary: A Rare Incidental Histopathologic Finding.
papers.authors: Song DH, Cho IA, Baek JC.
papers.abstract: Ectopic adrenal cortical tissue (EACT) is an uncommon developmental heterotopia and is exceptionally rare in the ovary of adult women. A 52-year-old woman, 6 years after menopause, was evaluated for progressive enlargement of a uterine leiomyoma and postmenopausal spotting. Transvaginal ultrasonography and pelvic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multiple uterine leiomyomas but no adnexal mass or endometrioma. During total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, dense adhesions between the sigmoid colon and posterior cul-de-sac were unexpectedly encountered. Histopathologic examination of the adhesion-related tissue revealed neither endometriosis nor significant inflammatory change. Microscopic examination of the ovary identified a 1.9 mm, sharply circumscribed nodule composed of clear, vacuolated zona fasciculata-like cells and compact eosinophilic zona reticularis-like cells. The lesional cells showed diffuse Melan-A immunoreactivity and focal-to-patchy inhibin-α positivity, supporting adrenocortical differentiation. The findings established a diagnosis of ovarian EACT. This case emphasizes that microscopic ovarian adrenal rests may be radiologically occult and should be distinguished from ovarian steroidogenic neoplasms by integrating clinical, morphologic, and immunohistochemical findings.

papers.title: Non-Invasive Assessment of SMAD4 Expression Status in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Diagnostic Value of T1ρ-Weighted Imaging Combined with Clinical Parameters.
papers.authors: Li K, Guo R, Li J, Wu Q, Liu X, Chen J, Wang X, Chen W.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives : Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a malignancy with poor prognosis, where SMAD4 protein loss is closely associated with increased tumor aggressiveness and metastatic potential. Current assessment of SMAD4 expression relies on IHC of tumor tissue obtained by biopsy or resection, in which limited sampling may not represent intratumoral heterogeneity. T1ρ-weighted imaging, an emerging functional MRI technique, shows promise in characterizing tumor microstructural properties. This study aimed to evaluate the value of T1ρ imaging combined with conventional MRI sequences and clinical parameters for non-invasive prediction of SMAD4 protein expression status in PDAC. Methods : This retrospective single-center study included 57 patients with histologically confirmed PDAC who underwent pretreatment MRI with T1ρ imaging between September 2024 and May 2025. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed SMAD4 intact in 28 tumors (49.1%) and SMAD4 loss in 29 tumors (50.9%). T1ρ values were measured and compared between SMAD4 intact and SMAD4 loss tumors. A multiparametric predictive model incorporating T1ρ values, lymph node metastasis status, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) levels was developed. Results : SMAD4 intact tumors demonstrated significantly higher T1ρ values compared to SMAD4 loss tumors (96.34 ± 14.12 vs. 71.93 ± 10.24 ms, p < 0.001). T1ρ achieved an AUC of 0.901 (95% CI: 0.817-0.986), with 82.14% sensitivity and 89.66% specificity, for predicting SMAD4 expression status. A multiparametric model combining T1ρ values, lymph node metastasis status, and CA19-9 levels yielded a numerically higher AUC of 0.932 (95% CI: 0.862-1.000), although the difference from T1ρ alone was not statistically significant (DeLong test, p > 0.05). Conclusions : T1ρ imaging showed potential for predicting SMAD4 status in PDAC.

papers.title: Aphasia with Anomia in Mandarin Chinese: An Exploratory Pilot Study Based on Phonological Awareness Therapeutic Strategies.
papers.authors: Chen J, Wang Y, Li Y, Huang J, Fang F, Wan Q.
papers.abstract: Anomia, a pivotal symptom of aphasia, impedes functional communication. In tonal languages such as Mandarin, phonological awareness plays a critical role in lexical retrieval. This study developed and evaluated a phonological awareness-based intervention for anomia in Mandarin-speaking people with aphasia (PWA). Ten post-stroke Mandarin-speaking PWA with left-hemisphere damage and anomia (5M/5F; 4 non-fluent, 6 fluent aphasia) received a three-stage phonological awareness intervention (phoneme-nonword-real word). Pre- and post-intervention assessments covered naming ability, phonological awareness, and initial consonant articulation. After treatment, phonological awareness improved significantly across all measures (adjusted p < 0.05; partial η2 = 0.733-0.932). Both groups showed significant pre-to-post improvements in rhyme, alliteration, tone, phoneme awareness, syllable decoding, and syllable plausibility judgments (all adjusted p < 0.05); syllable awareness improved significantly only in the FA group (MD = 41.67, 95% CI = 24.85-58.48, adjusted p = 0.002). For naming accuracy, both groups improved significantly on trained words (FA: MD = 25.76, 95% CI = 13.08-38.44, adjusted p = 0.006; NFA: MD = 38.64, 95% CI = 29.30-47.98, adjusted p = 0.002). On the standardised test and untrained generalization words, only the FA group improved significantly (MD = 8.33, 95% CI = 4.05-12.62, adjusted p = 0.008; and MD = 11.37, 95% CI = 6.36-16.37, adjusted p = 0.004, respectively). Initial consonant articulation accuracy improved significantly in both groups (FA: MD = 17.46, 95% CI = 7.14-27.78, adjusted p = 0.014; NFA: MD = 25.00, 95% CI = 8.20-41.80, adjusted p = 0.036). Regarding naming errors, NFA showed significantly higher pre-treatment omission errors (median = 20.00% vs. 6.67%, adjusted p = 0.010) and phonological errors (median = 11.67% vs. 3.33%, adjusted p = 0.020) than FA on the standardized test; on trained words, NFA had higher pre-treatment omission errors (median = 15.91% vs. 6.82%, adjusted p = 0.048), while FA had higher post-treatment word formation errors (median = 9.09% vs. 0.00%, adjusted p = 0.038). No significant treatment-related changes in the occurrence rate of naming errors were detected on untrained generalization words. In conclusion, this exploratory pilot study provides preliminary evidence that a phonological awareness-based intervention may improve phonological awareness and trained-word naming ability in Mandarin-speaking PWA. Improvements on untrained words were limited and observed only in the FA group. Therefore, the intervention's generalization remains uncertain. These findings cautiously support a language-specific rehabilitation approach attuned to Mandarin phonology.

papers.title: Clinical reasoning in canine meningoencephalitis of unknown origin and glioma: the role of signalment, history and neurological examination.
papers.authors: Spohn F, Abani S, Dickinson PJ, Vernau KM, Toedebusch CM, Woolard KD, Beineke A, Volk HA, Nessler JN.
papers.abstract: Introduction Meningoencephalitis of unknown origin (MUO) is a group of presumed immune-mediated inflammatory diseases of the central nervous system (CNS) in dogs. Differentiating MUO from intracranial diseases such as glioma can be challenging based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis. Because glioma represents an important differential diagnosis in dogs clinically suspected to have MUO, distinguishing these diseases is relevant for diagnostic reasoning, therapeutic planning, and owner communication. This study assessed whether readily available clinical variables contribute to clinical reasoning in dogs with histopathologically confirmed MUO or glioma. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 138 dogs with histopathologically confirmed MUO or glioma. Medical history, signalment, and neurological examination findings were compared between groups. Binary logistic regression was used to identify clinical variables associated with diagnosis. Results Seventy dogs were diagnosed with MUO and 68 dogs with glioma. Dogs with MUO had a lower median body weight (10.50 kg vs. 23.90 kg; p = 0.0007) and age (5.00 years vs. 7.04 years; p = 0.0007) than dogs with glioma. In the final multivariable model, disease onset was associated with the distinction between MUO and glioma (p = 0.0282), while lower body weight and head tilt were associated with MUO. Increasing body weight was associated with lower odds of MUO (OR: 0.910; 95% CI: 0.861 - 0.961; p = 0.0007). Dogs without head tilt were less likely to be diagnosed with MUO than dogs with head tilt (OR: 0.249; 95% CI: 0.062 - 0.998; p = 0.0497). An exploratory, cohort specific body weight cut-off of ≤ 7.70 kg yielded 40.6% sensitivity and 95.6% specificity for MUO. Discussion Readily available clinical variables may provide supportive information when MUO and glioma are differential diagnoses, particularly when MRI and CSF findings are equivocal. However, overlap between groups and limited discriminatory performance of individual variables indicate that these findings should not be used as standalone criteria. Instead, signalment, history, and neurological examination findings should be interpreted as part of an integrated assessment together with MRI, CSF analysis, and infectious testing.

papers.title: Case Report: Surgical treatment of feline pituitary apoplexy in 3 cases.
papers.authors: van Schaik MA, van Stee LL, Grinwis GCM, Meij BP.
papers.abstract: Background Surgical treatment of feline pituitary apoplexy has not been previously described. Objectives To describe the clinical course and follow-up of 3 cases of feline pituitary apoplexy. Methods Cases were selected based on histopathological confirmation of pituitary masses with haemorrhagic lesions, following transsphenoidal hypophysectomy. Details of physical examination, diagnostic test results, treatment and follow-up course were retrospectively acquired by review of medical and imaging records. Results Two cats were presented with acute onset of neurologic signs (case 1 and 2), and one cat showed subacute endocrinological dysfunction (case 3). All cases underwent successful transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, followed by intensive care hospitalization and successful discharge. Pituitary apoplexy was identified by histopathological examination of the excised pituitary glands in cases 1, 2, and 3. Imaging findings compatible with pituitary apoplexy were present in all 3 cases, although only case 3 was imaged with a hemorrhage-sensitive sequence, providing unequivocal evidence of intralesional hemorrhage. Case 1 had a survival time at least 716 days, underwent a second transsphenoidal surgery because of tumor recurrence and was subsequently lost to follow-up. Case 2 had a survival time of at least 1,098 days and is still alive at the time of writing this manuscript. In case 3, tumor recurrence was identified radiologically (MRI) at 365 days, and it died during a course of radiation therapy 612 days after transsphenoidal hypophysectomy. Conclusion and clinical importance Pituitary apoplexy is a rare condition that also affects cats with large pituitary adenomas. Overall, the cats experienced acceptable clinical recovery and postoperative survival, supporting the feasibility of transsphenoidal hypophysectomy as a therapeutic option for cats with pituitary tumors affected by apoplexy. Notably, a favorable outcome was observed even in the presence of remnant pituitary tissue, as illustrated by the cat that later developed pituitary tumor recurrence.

papers.title: Case Report: An MDT-guided multimodal protocol for large-area stroke plateau - integrating neuromodulation with multimodal assessment.
papers.authors: Wu XL, Xia XQ, Ye CQ, Wang YL, Li XZ, Liu LX, Hang FB, Liu JS, Song YC, Zhang Y, Du XX.
papers.abstract: Objective This case report investigates the feasibility and potential value of an individualized precision rehabilitation protocol for large-area stroke, integrating multimodal neuromodulation under the guidance of a multidisciplinary team (MDT) and dynamic assessment. Methods A 38-year-old male with right hemiplegia and global aphasia following large left hemispheric infarction underwent an 8-month MDT-managed program. A closed-loop "assess-decide-intervene-re-assess" framework was implemented, featuring periodic multimodal evaluations (clinical scales, DTI, fMRI, EEG, 3D gait analysis). The intervention dynamically combined conventional therapy with staged neuromodulation: repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) for aphasia and intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation (iTBS) for motor disorder, Brain-Computer Interface (BCI)-robotic training and task-oriented Virtual Reality (VR) for upper limb function, and biomechanical correction with custom insoles based on gait analysis. Results Notable functional improvements were observed: LOTCA increased by 16 points, CRRCAE subscale improved by 60%-90%, FMA increased from 20 to 56, FMA-B reached 12, and MBI improved from 40 to 91. Neuroimaging revealed increased fractional anisotropy (FA) in the corpus callosum and right corticospinal tract, and elevated ALFF/ReHo in right frontal-temporal areas. Event-related desynchronization (ERD) decreased during BCI training, and gait parameters improved. Conclusion In this patient with large-area stroke who showed limited response to conventional rehabilitation, an MDT-guided, dynamically adjusted multimodal intervention was temporally associated with concurrent recovery across cognitive, language, motor, and daily living domains. The concomitant neural changes suggest possible trans-hemispheric network reorganization. These observations are hypothesis-generating and, while limited by the single-case design, provide a preliminary rationale for future investigations into precision neurorehabilitation approaches in similar complex cases. Clinical trial registration ChiCTR2300069203.
papers.summary_zh: 本病例报告针对大面积脑梗死后常规康复反应有限的患者，采用多学科团队指导、动态评估驱动的个体化多模态神经调控方案，并观察其可行性与潜在价值。经过约8个月的闭环“评估—决策—干预—再评估”流程，患者在认知、语言、运动和日常生活能力等多个维度均出现明显改善，影像与电生理指标也提示跨半球网络重组可能同步发生。作者强调，这些变化仅为时间上的伴随关系，单例设计无法确立因果，结果属于假设生成性质，为今后在类似复杂病例中探索精准神经康复提供了初步依据。

papers.title: Influence of self-reported vascular health and physical activity level on intravoxel incoherent motion imaging response to exercise in chronic low back pain.
papers.authors: Dupuis F, Berry DB, Lau A, Havandjian L, Brumm Z, Anand A, Zavareh A, Ward SR, Raiszadeh K, Shahidi B.
papers.abstract: Introduction In individuals with chronic low back pain (CLBP), degenerative changes in paraspinal muscles, such as fatty infiltration and reduced vascularization, may impair muscles' physiological response to exercise, limiting recovery potential. Intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) imaging enables assessment of muscle microvascular perfusion (D*) and intracellular diffusion (D) in response to exercise. Previous work demonstrated that individuals with chronic LBP exhibit attenuated IVIM responses to exercise, and that these responses predict clinical improvement following rehabilitation. Yet the mechanisms underlying these alterations remain unclear. Vascular comorbidities, frequently reported in individuals with CLBP, may impair exercise-induced vasodilation and limit microvascular perfusion in lumbar muscles, while reduced physical activity (PA) levels, also commonly observed, may contribute to alterations in muscle microstructure. This study investigated whether systemic vascular health and PA level moderate lumbar paraspinal IVIM responses to acute exercise in individuals with CLBP. Methods Seventy-nine participants with CLBP underwent lumbar IVIM imaging before and after a lumbar extension exercise. IVIM parameters D, D* and perfusion fraction (f) were measured for paraspinal muscles. Participants were classified as having a known vascular condition (n=26) or no vascular condition (n=53), and stratified into High (n=42), Moderate (n=23), or Low PA (n=14) groups based on the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Linear mixed models examined the moderating roles of vascular health and PA on IVIM parameters, controlling for age, BMI and relative resistance as between-groups differences were observed. Results There was a significant main effect of Vascular condition on D (p=0.01), with the Vascular group having lower absolute values pre and post-exercise. There was a significant Time x Vascular interaction for D* (p=0.02): the Vascular group showed an attenuated response compared to the No vascular group. There was no main effect of PA on IVIM parameters, nor interactions with Time, except a trend for PA main effect on f (p=0.06). Discussion Vascular health moderates lumbar paraspinal intracellular diffusion and microvascular responses to acute exercise in CLBP. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the physiological significance of lumbar muscle IVIM parameters in chronic LBP.

papers.title: Cannabidiol preserves astrocyte viability and attenuates injury-induced glial stress responses across zebra finch song control nuclei.
papers.authors: Marshall DA, Litwa KA, Soderstrom K.
papers.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation following traumatic brain injury (TBI) increases the risk of affective disorders and early-onset dementias. Existing anti-inflammatory therapies are limited by systemic side effects with chronic use and by poor brain penetration of newer biologics. Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-euphorigenic phytocannabinoid with a favorable safety profile and multi-target neuroprotective actions, is a promising alternative. Using a songbird microlesion model of learned vocal recovery after targeted damage to the premotor nucleus HVC, we previously showed that systemic CBD (10 mg/kg/day) reduces vocal disruption, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, and synaptic loss. Here we tested the hypothesis that these benefits involve astrocytes. CBD (10 mg/kg/day IM for 7 days) preserved astrocyte viability, attenuated injury-induced lysosomal stress, suppressed reactivity markers (C3, S100A10, aromatase), and upregulated key metabolic and antioxidant transcripts (glutamine synthetase and GCLM) across the interconnected song-control nuclei HVC, RA, and Area X. These changes were accompanied by reduced neuronal apoptosis in lesioned HVC. The results identify astrocyte-associated responses as a candidate cellular substrate of CBD's circuit-wide protective effects and support its translational potential to mitigate secondary injury and communication deficits after TBI.

papers.title: Case Report: A severe case of human parechovirus encephalitis in a neonate.
papers.authors: Grimm AM, Heep A, Sentner CP, Fiedler KM.
papers.abstract: Introduction Human parechovirus is a common pathogen causing respiratory and gastroenterological symptoms. Symptoms range from asymptomatic courses to rare encephalitis or sepsis-like symptoms. Studies regarding neurodevelopment after parechovirus encephalitis in infants are conflicting with indications of possible short or long term neurodevelopmental impairments. In this case report we describe an especially severe course of human parechovirus infection. Case A two-week-old infant presented with fever and developed seizures and apneic episodes after admission. Laboratory tests revealed leukopenia. A lumbar puncture revealed parechovirus via polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Recurrent seizures required extensive anticonvulsive therapy. Invasive ventilation for four days was necessary due to apneic episodes. Cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed white matter involvement. Discussion In neonates with a sepsis-like presentation and largely unremarkable laboratory and cerebrospinal fluid findings, parechovirus encephalitis is an important differential diagnosis. In this case, follow-up examinations showed age-appropriate neurodevelopment. However, owing to the severe clinical presentation and extensive neuroimaging abnormalities, long-term neurodevelopmental monitoring is warranted.
papers.summary_zh: 这是一篇病例报告，描述一名两周龄新生儿感染人副肠孤病毒后出现特别严重的病程：入院后发生惊厥和呼吸暂停，脑脊液PCR检出病毒，头颅MRI显示白质受累，需反复抗惊厥治疗和数日有创通气。作者据此提示，对表现为脓毒症样症状而实验室和脑脊液检查基本无异常的新生儿，应将副肠孤病毒脑炎纳入重要鉴别诊断。该患儿随访时神经发育与年龄相符，但鉴于临床表现严重且神经影像异常广泛，仍需长期监测神经发育。

papers.title: Clinical and radiological features of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome in children: a retrospective study.
papers.authors: Huang H, Jiang S, Xu H, Zhang J, Qin D.
papers.abstract: Background Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is an uncommon but critical neurological emergency in children. Data on Chinese pediatric cohorts remain limited. Objective To analyze the clinical features, imaging findings, and treatment of PRES in children to improve early diagnosis and management. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 10 children diagnosed with PRES from March 2016 to January 2025. Results The patients included 7 males and 3 females, aged 3-13 years (mean 7.5 years). The main underlying diseases were acute lymphoblastic leukemia (3 cases) and nephrotic syndrome (3 cases). Eight children (80%) had hypertension, 6 (60%) had hypoalbuminemia, and 8 received glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants. The main symptoms were headache, seizures, impaired consciousness, and visual disturbances. Cranial MRI showed symmetrical long T1 and long T2 signals in bilateral posterior cerebral white matter. After comprehensive treatment including antihypertensive, anticonvulsant, and dehydration therapy, all symptoms resolved and lesions disappeared on follow-up imaging without sequelae. Conclusion Pediatric PRES is an acute reversible disorder associated with hypertension and immunosuppressive therapy. Early MRI diagnosis and prompt intervention can significantly improve prognosis.
papers.summary_zh: 该回顾性研究分析了儿童后可逆性脑病综合征（PRES）的临床与影像特征，纳入一家医院十年间确诊的10例患儿，年龄3至13岁。患儿多有急性淋巴细胞白血病或肾病综合征等基础疾病，多数伴高血压、低白蛋白血症，并曾接受糖皮质激素或免疫抑制治疗；主要症状为头痛、癫痫发作、意识障碍和视觉异常，头颅MRI显示双侧后部脑白质对称性异常信号。经降压、抗惊厥和脱水等综合治疗后，症状均缓解，复查影像病灶消失且未留后遗症。作者据此认为，儿童PRES是一种与高血压和免疫抑制治疗相关的急性可逆性疾病，早期MRI诊断和及时干预有助于改善预后。

papers.title: Effect of epidural spinal cord stimulation combined with personalized neurorehabilitation in chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury: study protocol for the phase II single-arm feasibility RESTORES (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) trial.
papers.authors: Wan KR, Ng ZYV, Wee SK, Misbaah F, Lui WL, Phua MW, Plunkett T, Robinson N, Phyo Wai AA, Guan C, Sidarta A, So RQY, Premchand B, Susanto K, Cocchi L, Saffari SE, Ker RXJ, Ng WH.
papers.abstract: Background Chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury (SCI) results in profound neurological disability with minimal prospects for functional recovery using conventional rehabilitation strategies. Emerging evidence suggests that epidural spinal cord stimulation (eSCS) can activate dormant spinal locomotor networks and restore volitional and autonomic functions when combined with intensive activity-based training. However, systematic evaluation of multimodal neuromodulation approaches integrating advanced rehabilitation and computational neurophysiology remains limited. Methods The RESTORES trial (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) is a prospective, single-arm Phase II feasibility study enrolling 15 adults with chronic (≥1 year) motor-complete SCI (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment scale (AIS) A or B) between C5 and T12. Participants will undergo implantation of an epidural spinal cord stimulator followed by a 24-week program of structured stimulation-coupled personalised neurorehabilitation (five sessions per week). Clinical outcomes will be evaluated using standardized neurological and functional measures including the AIS motor score, Spinal Cord Independence Measure version III (SCIM-III), Walking Index for Spinal Cord Injury II (WISCI-II), and Trunk Assessment Scale (TASS). Autonomic function and quality of life will also be assessed. Multimodal neurophysiological measurements-including surface electromyography (sEMG), electroencephalography (EEG), resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI), and computer-vision-based movement analysis-will be performed to investigate neural recovery mechanisms and inform the development of adaptive neuromodulation systems. Study outcomes The primary outcome is the safety of epidural spinal cord stimulation implantation, defined as the absence of device explantation for safety-related reasons within 6 months following implantation. Secondary outcomes include changes in AIS motor score, functional outcomes (SCIM, WISCI-II, TASS), autonomic function, quality of life, and neurophysiological biomarkers. Discussion This study integrates neuromodulation, advanced rehabilitation technologies, and multimodal computational neurophysiology to evaluate both clinical efficacy and neural mechanisms of recovery following chronic SCI. Findings from the RESTORES trial will provide critical safety and feasibility data to inform future multicenter trials and the development of closed-loop spinal cord stimulation systems. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier NCT05644171.
mesh_terms: Clinical Trials, Phase II as Topic
papers.summary_zh: 该研究是一项单臂II期可行性试验方案，计划纳入慢性运动完全性脊髓损伤成人，评估硬膜外脊髓电刺激植入后联合个体化神经康复的安全性与可行性。主要结局为植入后6个月内未因安全原因取出设备，次要结局涵盖运动评分、功能量表、自主神经功能、生活质量及多模态神经生理标志物。研究旨在为后续多中心试验和闭环刺激系统开发提供初步数据，尚不能据此判断临床疗效。

papers.title: Treatment of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD): acute attacks, relapse prevention, and symptomatic care.
papers.authors: Mahler JV, Vilardo M, Silva GD, Vishnevetsky A, Bilodeau PA, Levy M, Matiello M.
papers.abstract: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a distinct inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system, and its diagnosis is guided by the 2023 International MOGAD Panel criteria. Its clinical spectrum includes optic neuritis, transverse myelitis, acute disseminated encephalomyelitis, and brainstem or cortical encephalitis, with a phenotype distribution that is strongly age-dependent. Although attacks are typically steroid-responsive and recovery is often good, roughly half of adults relapse, and it is the accumulation of incompletely recovered attacks, rather than a progressive phase, that drives long-term disability. Management therefore has three aims: to abort and reverse the acute attack, to prevent relapses in patients at risk, and to relieve residual symptomatic disability. This review synthesizes current evidence for acute treatment (high-dose corticosteroids, therapeutic plasma exchange, and intravenous immunoglobulin), the corticosteroid taper, and maintenance immunotherapy, with attention to when treatment should be started and when it may reasonably be stopped. We summarize comparative data favoring maintenance intravenous immunoglobulin, the emerging evidence for interleukin-6 receptor blockade, the more variable performance of B-cell depletion relative to AQP4-IgG-seropositive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, and the first phase 3 trials in the field (satralizumab and rozanolixizumab). We give particular attention to children, in whom acute disseminated encephalomyelitis predominates and in whom cognitive, academic, growth and skeletal outcomes must shape treatment decisions, and to the real-world availability of antibody testing and therapy outside high-income settings. Finally, we address symptomatic care: visual rehabilitation, neuropathic and spasticity-related pain, fatigue, bladder dysfunction, cognition, and mood.

papers.title: A robust adversarial learning framework for EEG emotion recognition.
papers.authors: Yang H, Chen L, Gao J, Zhang J, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Introduction Electroencephalography (EEG) provides an objective means of capturing neural patterns associated with emotion, but substantial inter-subject variability limits the ability of existing models to generalize to unseen subjects. Methods We propose a robust adversarial domain generalization framework for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition. In the first stage, long short-term memory-based encoders are jointly trained to learn domain-invariant and domain-specific representations using reconstruction, emotion classification, and adversarial domain objectives. This process preserves emotion-relevant information while suppressing subject-specific distribution shifts. In the second stage, the invariant encoder and emotion classifier are further refined through distributionally robust optimization with gradient-guided feature augmentation. Theframework is evaluated on the AMIGOS and DREAMER datasets using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Results The proposed method achieves mean accuracies of 69.94% and 68.97% and F1 scores of 0.59 and 0.65 on AMIGOS and DREAMER, respectively, outperforming the comparison methods on both datasets. Ablation results further show that adversarial learning provides the primary improvement in cross-subject generalization, while distributionally robust optimization offers complementary robustness. Discussion These findings indicate that combining representation learning that is invariant across domains with distributionally robust optimization effectively reduces distribution shifts across subjects and improves EEG emotion recognition for unseen subjects.

papers.title: VB-ROI-focused segmentation-to-morphometry workflow for vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia assessment on MRA.
papers.authors: Guan J, Liu Z, Qiu H, Chen C, Yang S, Cui J, Dai Z, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Introduction Vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia (VBD) is closely associated with posterior circulation infarction; however, reliable MRA-based morphometric quantification is hindered by the challenges of delineating the basilar artery (BA) and bilateral vertebral arteries (R-VA and L-VA). These vessels are characterized by their thin, elongated structure, spatial localization, and high sensitivity to boundary deviations, endpoint instability, and centerline discontinuity, which render generic full-image vessel segmentation suboptimal for VBD-oriented morphometric analysis. Methods In this study, we address this clinical-computational mismatch using a vertebrobasilar region-of-interest (VB-ROI)-focused segmentation-to-morphometry workflow. Initially, a full-image nnU-Net is employed for coarse anatomical localization, from which a prediction-derived VB-ROI is generated. Subsequently, a second nnU-Net performs fine segmentation of the BA/R-VA/L-VA within this anatomically focused field of view, and the restored full-size mask is utilized for segmentation evaluation and downstream morphometric quantification. Results Compared to the direct full-image nnU-Net, the proposed two-stage VB-ROI workflow improved the mean Dice coefficient from 0.7974 to 0.9681, the mean Intersection over Union (IoU) from 0.7145 to 0.9412, and the mean centerline Dice from 0.7398 to 0.9206, while reducing the Hausdorff Distance at 95th percentile (HD95) from 8.6245 mm to 1.1709 mm. The prediction-derived VB-ROI demonstrated performance comparable to the ground-truth-based ROI setting without necessitating test-time ground truth, thus supporting the robustness of the localization strategy. Morphometric analysis indicated strong agreement in diameter-related measurements, while length, displacement, tortuosity, and curvature-related indices exhibited greater sensitivity to centerline extraction and endpoint definition. Discussion These findings illustrate the technical feasibility of VB-ROI-focused segmentation for MRA-based vertebrobasilar morphometric quantification and provide a methodological foundation for future studies on VBD and posterior circulation infarction.

papers.title: Regional spontaneous brain activity abnormalities in ischemic stroke patients with motor dysfunction: protocol for an AES-SDM coordinate-based meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Zhao J, Rao Y, Wu J, Zeng M, Zhang J, Ni J, Xu H, Zhao Z, Zheng Y, Wang C, Shan C.
papers.abstract: Introduction Most ischemic stroke survivors experience motor deficits, yet the underlying patterns of spontaneous brain activity change remain unclear. Individual rs-fMRI studies on this population have yielded contradictory findings, likely due to small sample sizes and between-study differences in lesion profiles, stroke stage, rehabilitation history, and imaging pipelines. These inconsistencies have not been resolved by existing reviews, many of which combine ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke, pool conceptually distinct rs-fMRI metrics without sufficient stratification, or focus on functional connectivity rather than local spontaneous activity. This protocol plans a coordinate-based meta-analysis restricted to ischemic stroke and local rs-fMRI metrics to address that gap. Methods and analysis This study will systematically identify and synthesise whole-brain rs-fMRI studies that compared ALFF, fALFF, or ReHo between adult ischemic stroke patients with motor dysfunction and healthy controls. We will search PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library up to 6 February 2026. To be included, a study must report whole-brain voxel-wise group comparisons and provide stereotactic peak coordinates in MNI or Talairach space. Studies will be excluded if they are non-original reports, case reports or case series, use task-state fMRI or ROI-only analyses, lack extractable standard-space coordinates, involve duplicate or overlapping datasets, include hemorrhagic or mixed stroke without separable ischemic-stroke data, or do not provide clearly extractable motor dysfunction-related data. Two reviewers will independently screen, extract, and assess methodological quality. Using anisotropic effect-size seed-based d mapping (AES-SDM), the quantitative synthesis will pool coordinates to detect convergent patterns of both increased and decreased regional spontaneous activity. Where data allow, we will conduct subgroup analyses, jackknife sensitivity testing, heterogeneity assessment, and meta-regression. The protocol follows the PRISMA-P statement, and the completed review will adhere to PRISMA 2020. Conclusion This protocol outlines a systematic review and AES-SDM coordinate-based meta-analysis aimed at synthesizing regional spontaneous activity abnormalities in ischemic stroke patients with motor dysfunction. The results should identify convergent areas of local functional alteration, generating testable predictions for future research on post-stroke motor-network reorganization and rehabilitation. Clinical trial registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261359426, identifier CRD420261359426.
papers.summary_zh: 这是一篇针对缺血性脑卒中伴运动功能障碍患者的系统综述与坐标元分析方案，计划纳入比较患者与健康对照的ALFF、fALFF或ReHo全脑静息态fMRI研究，并用AES-SDM合并坐标。作者指出，既往单项研究结果不一致，现有综述又常混合出血性与缺血性卒中、未充分区分不同指标或侧重功能连接，因此本方案限定于缺血性卒中和局部自发活动指标。预期结果将识别局部功能改变的汇聚脑区，为卒中后运动网络重组与康复研究提供可检验的预测，但方案本身尚未给出实际合并结果。

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms underpinning cognitive reserve and resilience.
papers.authors: Chen A, Bhuvaneshwaran S, Akkara Y, Burke T, Perneczky R, Sastre M.
papers.abstract: The concept of cognitive reserve (CR) and resilience originates from clinicopathological observations that amyloid-β deposition, tau pathology and neurodegeneration do not uniformly translate into clinical dementia, highlighting inter-individual differences in the brain's capacity to tolerate pathology. Although CR and resilience lack a single accepted definition, they broadly describe the ability to maintain cognition in the presence of age-related or pathological brain changes. This review synthesises current molecular, cellular, and brain network mechanisms of cognitive reserve and critically examines key controversies. We also identify convergent biological pathways across multiple levels of organisation. Available evidence implicates that CR is not attributable to a single factor but reflects interactions among environmental exposures, genetic background, epigenetic regulation, cellular homeostasis, glial function, and large-scale brain network organisation. Lifestyle factors are associated with reduced pathology accumulation, preserved brain structure, and maintenance of cognition despite pathology, depending on the mechanism and outcome considered and are understood to exert their effects through epigenetic modulation of neuroplasticity, neurotrophic signalling, metabolic regulation, and inflammatory pathways. At the cellular level, preservation of dendritic spine integrity, synaptic signalling balance, mitochondrial energetic flexibility, and adult hippocampal neurogenesis supports efficient circuit function under pathological stress. Glial cells play central roles in mediating adaptive plasticity, neuroinflammatory control, and metabolic support, with dysregulation accelerating cognitive decline. Collectively, these findings frame CR as an emergent property of coordinated biological processes operating across molecular, cellular, and network scales, with important implications for developing reserve-enhancing therapeutic and lifestyle-based interventions that complement traditional pathology-focused approaches.

papers.title: A SynNotch-PiggyBac gene circuit for inflammation-responsive IL-10 delivery in Alzheimer's disease: a hypothesis and design framework.
papers.authors: Gupta S, Gupta R.
papers.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation driven by sustained microglial and astrocyte activation contributes to Alzheimer's disease progression, yet no therapeutic strategy addresses it with precision or durability in the brain. Interleukin-10 occupies an unresolved position in this problem. Constitutive interleukin-10 overexpression in amyloid precursor protein transgenic mice increased plaque burden by suppressing microglial phagocytic activity, while interleukin-10 deletion has been reported to restrict amyloidosis in one setting and to worsen tau hyperphosphorylation in another. We interpret this pattern as evidence that interleukin-10 carries opposite signs on the two principal pathologies of Alzheimer's disease, so that any therapy holding it at a fixed concentration is committed in advance to being wrong about one of them. We therefore propose a falsifiable hypothesis: conditional, inflammation-gated interleukin-10 expression may suppress damaging inflammatory signaling while limiting the impairment of microglial phagocytosis associated with continuous exposure. We present a design framework for a synthetic gene circuit combining an adeno-associated viral vector for delivery to the central nervous system, a synthetic Notch receptor that detects membrane-bound tumor necrosis factor alpha on activated microglia through juxtacrine contact, and a PiggyBac transposon intended to integrate the circuit into the astrocyte genome. Receptor engagement is expected to release a transcription factor that drives interleukin-10 from a synthetic promoter, with transcription ceasing as the stimulus is withdrawn. We provide a quantitative packaging analysis showing that the circuit requires a compacted vector design to fit within viral capacity, and we identify three unvalidated assumptions: the recognition domain does not yet exist, ligand surface density on activated microglia is unmeasured, and shed soluble tumor necrosis factor alpha is predicted to act as a competitive inhibitor of receptor activation. A computational analysis of simulated resting-state electroencephalography, in which 45 of 171 electrode pairs differed after false discovery rate correction, is presented as a fully specified analysis workflow for delta-band connectivity as a secondary outcome measure rather than as evidence of effect, and yields effect sizes indicating that a rodent study would need roughly 11 animals per group. A four-arm validation plan is specified that separates the contribution of conditional regulation from that of genomic integration.
papers.summary_zh: 该文是一篇提出假设与设计框架的文章，而非实验研究。作者围绕白细胞介素-10在阿尔茨海默病神经炎症中的矛盾作用展开：摘要指出，持续过表达会抑制小胶质细胞吞噬并加重斑块负荷，而缺失白细胞介素-10在不同情境下对淀粉样变性和tau磷酸化影响不一，因此固定浓度的白细胞介素-10治疗可能顾此失彼。作者据此提出可证伪假设，即由炎症信号门控的白细胞介素-10表达或可在抑制有害炎症信号的同时，减少持续暴露对吞噬功能的损害，并给出由腺相关病毒载体、识别活化小胶质细胞膜结合肿瘤坏死因子α的合成Notch受体和PiggyBac转座子组成的基因回路设计框架。作者明确列出识别结构域尚不存在、配体表面密度未测、可溶性肿瘤坏死因子α可能竞争性抑制受体激活这三项未经验证的假设，并将模拟静息态脑电分析定位为次要结局的流程示例而非疗效证据。

papers.title: Concurrent Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses in a woman: a case report of a diagnostic challenge.
papers.authors: Hu J, Dong L, Sun L, Su H.
papers.abstract: Background Bartholin gland abscess and perianal abscess are common suppurative infections involving anatomically adjacent regions of the female perineum. Because both conditions may present with localized pain and swelling, distinguishing their respective origins and determining the extent of infection can be challenging. The concomitant occurrence of these two abscesses is uncommon, and its diagnostic and therapeutic considerations remain poorly characterized. We report a rare case of concomitant Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses and describe the diagnostic process and multidisciplinary surgical management. Case presentation An 18-year-old woman presented with progressive perineal and perianal pain and swelling. Pelvic computed tomography demonstrated abscess formation involving the perianal and left perineal soft tissues, and a possible communication between the two lesions was initially suspected. Emergency surgery was performed. The perianal abscess was incised and drained, and an infected anal gland was identified and excised, with bridge drainage established between the drainage incisions. Intraoperative exploration revealed no communication between the perianal abscess and the adjacent perineal lesion. Following gynecological consultation, the separate left vulvar abscess was drained and treated with Jacobi ring fistulization. Culture of the perineal abscess grew Escherichia coli, whereas the perianal abscess culture showed no bacterial growth. Follow-up magnetic resonance imaging 1 month after surgery demonstrated a cystic lesion in the anatomical region of the left Bartholin gland, supporting the Bartholin gland origin of the previously drained perineal abscess. The patient showed satisfactory clinical recovery, with complete healing of the perianal and perineal wounds at 4 months and no evidence of recurrent abscess during the available follow-up. Conclusion Concomitant Bartholin gland and perianal abscesses may be difficult to distinguish because of their overlapping clinical manifestations and anatomical proximity. Clinicians should consider the possibility of multiple independent or potentially related infectious foci and systematically evaluate adjacent anatomical regions. Careful physical examination, appropriate imaging, intraoperative assessment, and timely multidisciplinary collaboration can facilitate accurate diagnosis and individualized surgical management.

papers.title: Association of Serum GDF-15 with Bone and Muscle Parameters in Community-Dwelling Individuals.
papers.authors: Profili NI, Makrogiannis S, Castelli R, Benelli M, Orrù V, Marongiu M, Fiorillo E, Cucca F, Delitala AP.
papers.abstract: Introduction Muscle mass and bone mineral density decrease with aging, although following different patterns among males and females. Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) is a stress-induced cytokine and has emerged as a key biomarker for inflammation, tissue injury, and metabolic stress. We tested the association between GDF-15 and specific bone and muscle parameters in a large cohort of community-dwelling subjects. Methods The SardiNIA survey included 4,842 subjects (2,795 females). All underwent a detailed medical visit and laboratory testing. Peripheral quantitative computed tomography at the tibia was performed to evaluate volumetric bone mineral density and bone microstructure as well as muscle mass. Results Multivariate regression analysis showed that GDF-15 was negatively associated with cortical bone density (Beta -0.042, p < 0.001) in females. In males, total bone density and trabecular bone density at 4% site and cortical bone area at 38% site were negatively associated with GDF-15 levels (respectively, Beta -0.016, p = 0.027, Beta -0.014, p = 0.039, and Beta -0.022, p = 0.002). Multivariate regression analysis for muscle parameters showed that GDF-15 was negatively associated with muscle density (Beta -0.002 in females and males, p < 0.001 for all) and muscle area (Beta -0.338, p = 0.003, Beta -0.744, p < 0.001). Conclusions Higher circulating GDF-15 levels were independently associated with lower volumetricBMD and poorer muscle parameters in both women and men. These findings support the potential role of GDF-15 as a biomarker of age-related musculoskeletal decline, although longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether GDF-15 contributes to the development of these changes or simply reflects the underlying biological processes.

papers.title: Glioblastoma stem cell-immune microenvironment crosstalk: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.authors: Xu C, Chai L, Yuan W.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most aggressive and treatment-resistant primary brain malignancies, with limited improvement in long-term survival despite advances in multimodal therapy. Glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) are central to tumour initiation, recurrence and therapeutic resistance, but their malignant properties are not determined by intrinsic programmes alone. Increasing evidence indicates that reciprocal interactions between GSCs and the tumour immune microenvironment (TIME) establish a dynamic ecosystem that promotes stemness, immune escape and treatment resistance. In this review, we summarise the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying GSC - TIME crosstalk, with emphasis on tumour-associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, T cells, regulatory T cells, natural killer cells, B cells, plasma cells and neutrophils. We highlight major signalling and metabolic networks, including B2M/TGF-β1, IL8/CXCR2, IFI35/NF-κB, lactate/lactylation, IgG/FcγRIIA and m6A/LOXL2 signalling, as well as extracellular vesicle-mediated communication. We further discuss how these interactions sustain GSC stemness, facilitate metabolic adaptation, promote immune escape and contribute to resistance to radiotherapy, temozolomide and targeted therapies. Emerging therapeutic approaches-including tumour-associated macrophage/myeloid-derived suppressor cell (TAM/MDSC) reprogramming, metabolic and epigenetic intervention, immune checkpoint blockade, bispecific antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor T/natural killer (CAR-T/NK) cell therapy and extracellular vesicle-based delivery-are also evaluated. Finally, we discuss the importance of spatial heterogeneity, blood-brain barrier limitations and rational combination strategies. Understanding GSC-TIME crosstalk may provide a framework for developing more effective and biologically informed precision therapies for GBM.

papers.title: Brain network changes in patients with glioma-related epilepsy after frontal resection.
papers.authors: Fang S, Wang J, Zhang Z, Li Y, Sun Z, Zhou C, Wang Y, Fan X, Jiang T.
papers.abstract: Objective Clinical factors such as IDH status, preoperative seizures, and frontal tumor location influence the prognosis of postoperative glioma-related epilepsy (GRE), but the underlying network-level mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify network-based predictors of postoperative GRE. Methods The authors retrospectively analyzed 109 patients with frontal glioma (76 left sided). All patients underwent preoperative and 1-week postoperative resting-state functional MRI and diffusion tensor imaging. Changes in network characteristics, including structural-functional coupling and functional connectivity (FC), were evaluated. Using the left-sided cohort as the training set, Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was applied to identify network-based risk factors for postoperative GRE and construct a predictive model. The right-sided cohort served as a validation set. Results Patients with postoperative GRE showed reduced structural-functional coupling between the dorsal attention network (DAN) and the frontoparietal network (FPN), along with decreased FC within and between these networks. Increased DAN-FPN coupling and higher FC between the lesional-hemisphere prefrontal thalamus and the whole brain were protective against postoperative GRE. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.785 in the training cohort and 0.922 in the validation cohort (both p < 0.0001). Conclusions Altered structural-functional coupling and FC between attention-related networks are associated with postoperative GRE in frontal glioma. Enhanced DAN-FPN coupling and thalamocortical connectivity may serve as protective network markers.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注额叶胶质瘤患者术后胶质瘤相关癫痫（GRE）的网络层面机制，回顾性分析了额叶胶质瘤患者术前及术后早期静息态功能MRI和弥散张量成像，考察结构-功能耦合与功能连接的变化，并以左、右侧队列分别建模和验证。结果显示，术后出现GRE的患者背侧注意网络（DAN）与额顶网络（FPN）之间的结构-功能耦合降低，网络内及网络间功能连接也减弱；而DAN-FPN耦合增强以及病灶侧前额丘脑与全脑功能连接较高与术后GRE风险降低相关。作者据此认为，注意相关网络的结构-功能耦合和功能连接改变与术后GRE相关，增强的DAN-FPN耦合和丘脑皮层连接可能作为保护性网络标志，但预测模型性能不等同于临床干预效果。

papers.title: MBB-AVR: a mind-brain-body dataset with dynamic affective states in immersive virtual reality
papers.authors: Fourcade A, Ciston AB, Roellecke L, de Mooij J, Leos H, Villringer A, Carletto S, Malandrone F, Gaebler M.
papers.abstract: We present MindBrainBody-AffectiveVR (MBB-AVR), a multimodal dataset capturing continuous affective experience and both central and peripheral physiological responses during naturalistic emotional stimulation in immersive virtual reality. Forty-seven healthy adults (24 female, 22 male, 1 non-binary; age = 27.1 ± 5.4) viewed a 23-minute stereoscopic 360° video sequence, composed of computer-generated, language-free content designed to elicit high affective variability over time, presented via a head-mounted display (HTC Vive Pro Eye). While immersed, participants continuously rated their momentary valence and arousal using a previously validated rating tool with real-time visual feedback. Synchronized recordings include 64-channel EEG, ECG, respiration, photoplethysmography, galvanic skin response, and head and eye tracking with pupillometry. Participants additionally completed questionnaires including interoceptive sensibility and alexithymia. The dataset is organized following the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) and includes extracted low-level audio and video features of the stimulus. It may support research on the temporal dynamics of affect, multimodal physiological correlates of emotion, and affective computing. The dataset is available at https://gin.g-node.org/fourcade_a/mbb-avr.
papers.summary_zh: 该数据集研究在沉浸式虚拟现实中呈现自然主义情绪刺激时，如何同步采集连续情感体验与中枢、外周生理反应。47名健康成人观看约23分钟的立体360°视频，并实时连续评定效价和唤醒度，同时记录脑电、心电、呼吸、皮电、眼动与瞳孔等多种信号，另收集内感受敏感性和述情障碍问卷。数据按BIDS组织并附刺激的低层音视频特征，可用于情感时间动态、情绪的多模态生理关联及情感计算研究。

papers.title: fMRI hyperscanning reveals widespread neural coupling during natural conversations
papers.authors: Mwilambwe-Tshilobo L, Tsoi L, Speer S, Zada Z, Burns SM, Falk EB, Tamir D.
papers.abstract: Conversation is one of the most powerful tools that people have for building and maintaining social connections. How does conversation bring two minds together? Here we tracked the neural dynamics between dyads during real-time conversation using fMRI hyperscanning, where both people were scanned simultaneously, to explore whether and how conversation aligns brains. Dyads engaged in natural, free-flowing conversation as they co-constructed the content of their dialogue. In a control condition, partners read aloud scripted dialogue from another dyad’s conversation, preserving the turn-taking structure while removing the co-construction. To examine neural alignment, we compared whole-brain intersubject correlation between partners in each condition, assessing both synchronous and predictive neural dynamics. Results showed that naturalistic conversation led to significant widespread neural alignment across brain regions implicated in attention, audition, affect, executive control, and social cognition, compared to scripted conversation. Temporally refined analyses showed that during naturalistic conversation, relative to scripted conversation, both speakers and listeners anticipated each other within a short temporal window, with brain activity preceding their partner’s in the same neural systems. These findings show that live, turn-taking conversations align neural activity well beyond passive or asynchronous communication, providing a foundation for future research examining how spontaneous, co-constructed dialogue allows people to communicate effectively.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究用fMRI超扫描同时记录成对参与者在自然即兴对话和朗读他人脚本对话时的脑活动，比较两种条件下双方的全脑人际相关，并区分同步与预测性的神经动态。结果显示，自然对话比脚本对话引发更广泛的神经对齐，涉及注意、听觉、情绪、执行控制和社会认知等系统；时间分析还表明，说者和听者会在短时间窗内相互预测，其脑活动先于对方。作者据此认为，实时、轮流且共同建构的对话能使双方神经活动对齐，其范围超出被动或非同步交流，为理解自发对话如何支持有效沟通提供了基础。

papers.title: Increasing cerebellar beta rhythms shifts cerebral oscillatory signatures of context-driven language processing
papers.authors: Ambichler S, Portier T, Piai V, Klaus J.
papers.abstract: While there is growing consensus that the cerebellum is part of the cerebrally centred network underlying language processing, the direct nature of its contribution to comprehension and production remains unknown. In particular, while both processes require lexical access, production additionally involves motor processes linked to articulatory planning, which has fuelled the view that the cerebellum is primarily involved in motor control in language production. Cortically, both lexical access and articulatory planning are known to be driven by alpha-beta power decreases. To disentangle cerebellar involvement in language, this study investigated the modulatory effect of transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) over the right cerebellum on context-driven language comprehension and production. In a cross-over, double-blind, sham-controlled within-participants design, 32 healthy volunteers received 20 minutes of 20-Hz tACS (2 mA peak-to-peak) targeting the right posterior cerebellum. Immediately afterwards, they performed a context-driven language task while EEG was recorded from 32 channels. In the task, visually presented lead-in sentences creating a constraining or unconstraining context were followed by a picture depicting the final word of the sentence. Participants were instructed to name the picture (production) or judge its animacy (comprehension). Responses became slower overall following active compared to sham tACS, and this increase was more pronounced in the comprehension task. In line with previous work, reliable context-related oscillatory power decreases were observed in response to the context manipulation, but exhibited a different pattern across tasks and stimulation conditions. For production, beta-centred power decreases following sham shifted to temporally and spatially extended alpha power decreases following active tACS. By contrast, alpha-centred power decreases following sham tACS in the comprehension task increased following active tACS. Increasing beta activity in the right posterior cerebellum thus affected early stages of context-driven language processing linked to lexical access in both language domains. The stimulation-induced spectral, spatial and temporal shifts suggest recruitment of alternative cortical resources as a consequence of cerebellar network modulation. This interpretation is consistent with the cerebellum functioning as a network node coordinating temporal dynamics across distributed language regions.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨右侧小脑是否以及如何参与语境驱动的语言理解与产出，采用交叉、双盲、假刺激对照设计，对健康志愿者右侧后小脑施加20 Hz经颅交流电刺激，并在刺激后同步记录脑电完成语言任务。结果显示，主动刺激后整体反应变慢，且理解任务中的变慢更明显；语境操作仍引起可靠的振荡功率下降，但其任务与刺激条件下的模式不同：产出任务中，假刺激下以beta为中心的功率下降在主动刺激后转为时间与空间上更延展的alpha功率下降，而理解任务中原本以alpha为中心的下降在主动刺激后增强。作者据此认为，提高右侧后小脑beta活动影响了两个语言领域中与词汇通达相关的早期语境加工阶段，刺激诱发的频谱、空间和时间变化提示小脑网络调制后大脑皮层动用了替代资源，这与小脑作为协调分布式语言网络时间动态的节点这一解释相符。

papers.title: Neural Correlates of Beat Processing in Infancy and Their Association With Later Grammar Development: Evidence for the Atypical Rhythm Risk Hypothesis
papers.authors: Ladanyi E, Nayak S, Bush CT, Wang Y, Woynaroski TG, Lense MD, Leonard MK, Gordon RL.
papers.abstract: Infants show evidence of beat processing from birth, but its neural correlates in infancy remain poorly understood. Moreover, although rhythm and grammar abilities are closely linked in older (school-aged) children, it is not known whether individual differences in infant beat processing lay the foundations for those associations. This longitudinal EEG study examined neural correlates of beat processing in 6–12-month-old infants (N=37) and their relation to sentence comprehension skills in the same children at 4 years. We analyzed infants’ evoked time–frequency responses to rhythmic tone–tone–rest sequences presented in physically accented conditions and in inferred-beat conditions, in which accents were removed after an initial exposure phase.. Analyses revealed a significant increase in power to physically accented beats (9–24 Hz, p < .001). Individual differences in this response were positively associated with receptive grammar performance at age 4, assessed with the TROG-2 (r = .48, p = .005), and remained significant after controlling for infant age, parent education, and home music environment (β = .45, p = .011). The inferred beat effect was not related to later sentence comprehension performance. These findings indicate that infant neural activity tracks beat structure, with neural correlates broadly similar to those reported in adults, and that early neural sensitivity to beat is associated with later grammar development, supporting the Atypical Rhythm Risk Hypothesis.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察6至12个月婴儿的节拍加工神经相关活动，以及这些活动是否与同一批儿童4岁时的句子理解能力相关，采用纵向脑电分析婴儿对节奏声音序列的诱发时频响应。结果显示，婴儿对物理重音节拍出现明显的神经功率增强，且这一反应的个体差异与4岁时的接受性语法成绩呈正相关，在控制婴儿年龄、父母教育和家庭音乐环境后仍成立；而对推断节拍的效应则与后来的句子理解无关。作者据此认为，婴儿神经活动能够追踪节拍结构，其模式与成人报道大致相似，早期对节拍的神经敏感性可能与后续语法发展相关，从而为“非典型节律风险假说”提供支持。需注意这是纵向关联证据，尚不能说明因果关系。

papers.title: Music-Based Interventions for Cognition and Brain Health: the ARM framework
papers.authors: Loui P, Peelle JE, Grahn JA.
papers.abstract: Music-based interventions (MBIs) have shown promise in addressing cognitive, motor, and language impairments across neurological and neurodevelopmental conditions. Despite an increasing number of controlled studies that have assessed the potential rehabilitative effects of music, neural mechanisms underlying therapeutic benefits remain poorly understood. Here we present the ARM framework: a neurobiologically-informed model integrating three key systems: Auditory processing networks that encode temporal and spectral features; Reward circuitry activated by musical pleasure and prediction, and Motor systems engaged through auditory-motor coupling and rhythmic entrainment. We examine how specific MBIs leverage these systems to varying degrees and show how understanding these mechanisms is essential for predicting individual treatment response, personalizing interventions, and developing next-generation therapeutic approaches that optimize engagement of specific neural systems.

papers.title: Pooled versus structured inhibition drives stimulus competition across distinct spatial scales in the superior colliculus.
papers.authors: Banerjee A, Kothari NB, Mysore SP.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Competitive stimulus interactions across the space map of the midbrain superior colliculus (SC) are critical for spatial decision-making among multiple options. Here, using electrophysiological recordings from the intermediate and deep layers of the SC (SCid) in mice of either sex, we discovered that the rules and spatial profiles of these competitive interactions are different between local within-receptive field (RF), versus global across-RF-boundary, spatial scales. When one visual stimulus was centered in the RF and a second one was located within the RF's classical inhibitory surround, we found that stimulus interactions followed an averaging rule. This classical surround was spatially restricted, and the strength of inhibition underlying these within-RF interactions decreased with distance from the RF center. By contrast, when the second stimulus was located outside the RF, stimulus interactions followed a divisive rule. Strikingly, this extra-classical inhibitory surround was spatially global, and the strength of competitive inhibition underlying these across-RF-boundary interactions was distance-invariant while being dependent on the relative strengths of the competing stimuli. Computational modeling revealed that whereas within-RF interactions are well-explained by a normalization-like mechanism driven by pooled inhibition, across-RF-boundary interactions are not, and instead, are well-explained by a winner-take-all-like mechanism driven by structured, donut-like inhibition. Combined, our results reveal the mechanistic logic of stimulus competition across the space-map of mammalian SCid.Significance statement Selecting one target among many is essential for diverse cognitive functions, and requires neural circuits to compare priorities of competing stimuli. Using electrophysiological recordings in the mouse superior colliculus, a critical brain area for spatial decision-making, we show that stimulus competition follows fundamentally different rules at local versus distant spatial scales. Nearby stimuli within a receptive field (RF) engage spatially restricted, decaying inhibition, enacting an averaging rule. By contrast, distant stimuli separated by the RF boundary engage spatially global, distance-invariant inhibition, enacting a divisive, relative strength-dependent rule. Computational modeling reveals that local interactions are explained by a pooling normalization mechanism, whereas global interactions are explained by a donut-like winner-take-all mechanism. Results resolve long open questions about stimulus competition in the SC.

papers.title: Revisiting post-stimulus theta activity: evidence for a broadband rather than narrowband spectral origin.
papers.authors: Vanneau T, Quiquempoix M, Voytek B, Gyurkovics M, Molholm S.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: The aperiodic, 1/f-like component of electrophysiological activity is increasingly recognized as a meaningful feature of neural function rather than background noise. Meanwhile, many EEG studies interpret transient post-stimulus changes in oscillatory power as signatures of attention, salience, or cognitive control.
