The experience of acute stress might impair the ability to select actions in line with personally valued long-term goals in situations where a conflict between short-term and long-term action consequences arises. In this fMRI study, we examined the effects of experimentally induced acute stress on neural and behavioral substrates of self-controlled decision-making in a large sample (n = 175). We showed that acute stress was associated with increased modulation of activation in the ventromedial PFC by anticipated action short-term consequences, suggesting that acute stress might alter the degree to which short-term consequences are incorporated into the neural valuation process, but not with decreased modulation by long-term consequences. In addition, acute stress reduced functional connectivity between ventromedial and dorsolateral PFCs during self-control conflict possibly indicating weakened recruitment of cognitive control. However, despite group differences on the neural level, acute stress did not affect the impact of anticipated short-term or long-term action consequences on behavioral decisions or participants' self-control performance. Several factors might have contributed to the results reported here, for instance, potential compensatory mechanisms employed by stressed participants. Future work is needed to address these systematically.

papers.title: Expanding the toolkit: OPMs for studying the developing brain.
papers.authors: Taylor MJ, Rhodes N.
papers.abstract: Tremendous maturation in brain structure and function, underlying very rapid cognitive development, occurs in the early years of life, yet it has been difficult to obtain reliable measures of brain function over this period. A major challenge has been the difficulty of acquiring reliable neuroimaging data from awake young children, who often struggle to tolerate conventional imaging environments or remain still during scanning. Existing approaches each involves important compromises between spatial and temporal resolution, movement tolerance and practicality for use in early childhood. Optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs), a recent advance in magnetoencephalography (MEG) technology, are expanding the developmental neuroimaging toolkit. By enabling adaptable, wearable, and movement-tolerant MEG systems, OPMs retain the excellent spatial and temporal resolution of conventional cryogenic MEG technology while improving suitability for infants, toddlers, and young children. In this commentary, we briefly review the current functional neuroimaging toolkit used across development and discuss how OPMs are transforming the study of the developing brain. We highlight recent applications of OPMs to study early life, their potential for investigating brain-behaviour relationships and social interaction, and their promise for improving inclusion of clinical populations traditionally underrepresented in neuroimaging research. We also outline remaining technical and methodological challenges that should be addressed as the field continues to grow.

papers.title: Iterative delay correction improves breath-hold cerebrovascular reactivity mapping in clinical populations.
papers.authors: Clements RG, Geranmayeh F, Parkinson NV, Bright MG.
papers.abstract: Cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR), the ability of cerebral blood vessels to dilate or constrict in response to a vasoactive stimulus, is an important measure of cerebrovascular health. Accurate CVR estimation requires accounting for the time required for the vasoactive stimulus to reach each brain region and the time it takes for local arterioles to modulate cerebral blood flow. The temporal search range used to calculate this spatially varying offset can substantially impact CVR estimates, and the appropriate search range may vary across populations, acquisition protocols, and even brain regions. Here, we present an iterative approach for automatically determining the appropriate maximum shift, using breath-hold fMRI data acquired in a cohort of stroke survivors. This approach selectively expands the delay search range only for voxels with estimated delays at the boundary (i.e., near the minimum or maximum shift) until the estimated delay is no longer at the boundary or a predefined value is reached. In the context of stroke, among voxels initially at the boundary, this approach significantly increased the number of voxels with statistically significant CVR (i.e., having a relationship between end-tidal CO2 and the BOLD signal that is unlikely to be due to random chance). It also resulted in CVR polarity reversals in voxels originally at the early-response boundary and amplified negative CVR values in voxels originally at the late-response boundary, suggesting that using an iterative maximum shift can critically impact CVR interpretation. This approach is broadly applicable beyond stroke, but careful parameter tuning is required, as illustrated by our demonstration of the parameter tuning process for a participant with Moyamoya disease. Together, these findings suggest that iterative delay correction allows for improved CVR assessments in clinical populations.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注屏气fMRI计算脑血管反应性（CVR）时，延迟搜索范围如何影响估计结果，并提出一种迭代方法，对延迟落在搜索边界上的体素逐步扩大搜索范围，直至延迟不再位于边界或达到预设上限。研究以卒中幸存者的屏气fMRI数据为对象，发现该方法能增加延迟最初处于边界的体素中获得统计显著CVR的比例，同时使原本位于早反应边界的体素出现CVR极性反转，并放大原本位于晚反应边界的体素中的负CVR值，提示搜索上限的设定会实质影响CVR的解释。作者还以一例烟雾病患者的参数调优过程说明该方法可推广至卒中以外，但需谨慎设定参数。总体而言，迭代延迟校正有望改善临床人群的CVR评估。

papers.title: [Higher Brain Dysfunction Caused by Left Frontal Brain Retraction Injury and Infarction of the Left Genu of the Internal Capsule and Anterior Thalamus: A Case Report of Transient Gerstmann Syndrome Due to Multifocal Lesions].
papers.authors: Sawaki M, Yoshida M, Saito O, Yamauchi T, Yamamoto M.
papers.journal: Brain and nerve = Shinkei kenkyu no shinpo
papers.abstract: We herein report a case of subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by the rupture of a cerebral aneurysm that was treated by clipping surgery. The patient was a right-handed woman in her 40s who presented with attention disorder and transient Gerstmann syndrome, including left-right disorientation, finger agnosia, acalculia, and agraphia, associated with brain retraction injury in the left inferior frontal gyrus and perforating branch infarction of the horizontal segment of the left anterior cerebral artery. Diffusion tensor tractography was performed to investigate the underlying pathophysiological mechanism of transient Gerstmann syndrome. White matter fibers connecting the frontal lobe to the other lobes such as the left superior longitudinal fasciculus/arcuate fasciculus (SLF/AF), inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (IFOF), and uncinate fasciculus were compressed by vasogenic and cytotoxic edema without evidence of disconnection. The left thalamic-prefrontal peduncle (TPP), connecting the thalamus and inferior frontal gyrus, was not visualized, whereas left parietal angular-to-supramarginal U-fibers were preserved. These findings suggested that connectional diaschisis involving SLF/AF and IFOF, together with TPP damage, contributed to the development of transient Gerstmann syndrome. Early clinical improvement was expected due to the preservation of multiple association fibers from the frontal lobe to the other lobes without definite disconnection. (Received February 20, 2026; Accepted June 30, 2026; Published October 1, 2026).
papers.summary_zh: 本文报告一例右侧大脑前动脉动脉瘤夹闭术后出现注意障碍和短暂性Gerstmann综合征的右利手女性病例，影像显示左侧额下回牵拉损伤及左侧前动脉水平段穿支梗死。作者用弥散张量纤维束成像分析其病理生理机制，发现连接额叶与其他脑叶的多种白质纤维束虽受水肿压迫但未见明确离断，而连接丘脑与额下回的丘脑-前额脚未显影。作者据此提出，涉及上纵束/弓状束和额枕下束的连接性失联络，连同丘脑-前额脚损伤，可能共同促成了短暂性Gerstmann综合征，而多组联络纤维的保留或有助于早期临床改善。

papers.title: First glowing cuttlefish marks a genetic engineering milestone.
papers.authors: Reardon S.
papers.abstract: Breakthroughs in manipulating cephalopod embryos pave way for new studies of perception, brain evolution, and more.

papers.title: Inducing Interpersonal Closeness: Effects on Inter-Brain Synchrony and Collaborative Performance.
papers.authors: Fornari L, Janssen TWP, Davidesco I, Krabbendam L, van Atteveldt NM.
papers.abstract: Feeling close to another person is widely assumed to facilitate collaboration. However, causal evidence that interpersonal closeness improves collaborative behavior remains limited, and it is unclear whether any such influence is accompanied by increased synchrony at the neural level. Previous studies comparing inter-brain synchrony (IBS) and collaborative performance across relationship types (e.g., friends vs. strangers) have reported better collaboration and higher IBS in closer relationships, but these effects are confounded by familiarity and shared interaction history. To address these limitations, we experimentally manipulated interpersonal closeness in 123 dyads of strangers (N = 246) to test its causal influence on IBS and collaborative performance. Dyads were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: No Interaction, Small Talk, or a closeness-generating conversation. After the manipulation, dyads completed a collaborative task while undergoing mobile EEG hyperscanning. The manipulation was effective: perceived closeness increased significantly between the No-Interaction, Small-Talk, and closeness-generating conversation conditions. However, induced closeness did not affect collaborative performance or IBS during collaboration. These findings suggest that the better collaboration and higher IBS often reported for pre-existing relationships in previous studies may originate from factors beyond momentary feelings of closeness, such as familiarity derived from prior interaction. Interestingly, across all dyads, we observed a negative association between central delta IBS and collaborative performance, with IBS explaining unique variance beyond self-reported measures. This negative link is consistent with the idea that, in this context, IBS reflects speech-tracking and increased cognitive demands during coordination, rather than coordination efficiency.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究以陌生人为对象，通过实验操纵人际亲近感，并结合移动脑电超扫描考察其对脑间同步与协作表现的影响。结果发现，操纵确实提升了被试感知到的亲近程度，但并未改变协作表现或协作过程中的脑间同步。这提示，以往在既有关系中观察到的更好协作与更高脑间同步，可能更多源于熟悉度和既往互动经验，而非当下的亲近感受。此外，所有被试中中央区delta频段脑间同步与协作表现呈负相关，作者认为该同步可能反映言语追踪与协调时的认知负荷，而非协调效率。

papers.title: Social Anxiety Predicts Enhanced Electrocortical Sensitivity to the Mental State Meanings Revealed by Gaze Patterns.
papers.authors: Melani I, Berg MK, Glazer J, Kitayama S.
papers.abstract: Social anxiety-a fear of social interaction and negative evaluation-may be accompanied by heightened vigilance toward others' mental states, particularly those conveyed through gaze, as they provide cues about how one is being evaluated. We thus investigated whether individual differences in social anxiety predict neural sensitivity to the mental-state meanings conveyed by gaze patterns. Fifty-seven European American young adults varying in social anxiety viewed different gaze patterns, immediately followed by a mental-state word that was either congruent or incongruent with the culturally recognized meaning of the gaze, while their electroencephalogram (EEG) was monitored. Our focus was N400-an event-related potential (ERP) component indexing semantic expectation violations. We found the N400 amplitude to be more negative for incongruent (vs. congruent) mental-state words. Notably, this N400 incongruity effect increased significantly with social anxiety. Moreover, the social anxiety effect was specific to mental state inference and was not observed in a comparable N400 incongruity effect involving animal stereotypes (n = 50). These findings suggest that social anxiety may confer enhanced neural sensitivity during the inference of others' mental states from gaze, even in the absence of overt performance differences. We discuss the implications of these findings with respect to the potential functional benefits of social anxiety.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察社交焦虑的个体差异是否预测人对注视模式所传达心理状态含义的神经敏感性。研究让社交焦虑程度不同的年轻成人观看不同注视模式，随后呈现与注视含义一致或不一致的心理状态词，同时记录脑电，并以反映语义预期违背的N400成分为指标。结果显示，不一致词引发更负的N400，且这一不一致效应随社交焦虑升高而增强；该效应仅见于心理状态推断，未出现在动物刻板印象的类似任务中。作者据此认为，社交焦虑可能伴随对他人心理状态推断的更强神经敏感性，即便外显表现没有差异，并讨论了社交焦虑可能具有的功能性益处。

papers.title: Delivery and Attitude Modulate Shared Neural Processing of Speech Through Distinct Frequency Channels.
papers.authors: Atia B, Berson Y, Goldstein A.
papers.abstract: Listeners' brains align when they attend to the same speech, but what determines how strongly they align is not well understood. We asked whether that alignment tracks the communicative relation between a listener and a message, manipulating it from the speaker's side and from the listener's, and bounding the account with a manipulation that alters the social setting while leaving the relation intact. In two magnetoencephalography experiments, we measured inter-subject correlation of band-limited envelopes, which resolves shared processing by frequency rather than treating it as a single quantity. In Study 1, 40 listeners watched the same actor deliver the same speech charismatically and non-charismatically, so that content and identity were held constant. Charismatic delivery raised correlation most strongly in the beta band, and after regression of the acoustic and visual features, the surviving effect was concentrated in right perisylvian cortex. In Study 2, listeners read a favorable or unfavorable description of a speaker they had never encountered and watched a second speaker either with or without a minimal cue that an audience was present. A newly formed attitude raised correlation in alpha and theta within the same right perisylvian region, whereas the audience cue, which left both the message and the listener's disposition unchanged, produced no detectable change in any band. Correlation also proved partly dispositional: how strongly a listener synchronized on one task predicted their synchrony on the other, specifically in alpha and independently of personality. Delivery and attitude thus converge on a common substrate for the speaker's expressive signal, reaching it through separate frequency channels.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注听者之间神经反应同步的强弱由什么决定，用两项脑磁图实验考察说话者的表达方式与听者对说话者的态度如何影响共享的言语加工。研究以分频段包络的受试者间相关为指标，将同步性按频率拆解。结果发现，富有魅力的表达主要在beta频段提高同步，且该效应在回归声学与视觉特征后集中于右侧外侧裂周皮层；新形成的态度则在alpha和theta频段提高同一区域的同步，而仅提示有观众在场未改变任何频段的同步。听者在一个任务上的同步程度还能预测其在另一任务上的同步，尤其在alpha频段。作者据此认为，表达方式与态度经由不同频率通道汇聚到说话者表达信号的共同神经基础，且同步性部分具有倾向性成分。

papers.title: Early Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in Type 1 Fucosidosis: Reversal of Central Tegmental Tract Abnormalities.
papers.authors: Palaz M, Taşkın A, Özpınar E, Topçu Y, Yaman Y, Kılıç B, Aydın K.
papers.abstract: Background Fucosidosis is an ultra-rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency, leading to progressive neurodegeneration and multisystem involvement. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) has emerged as a potential disease-modifying therapy, particularly when performed early in the disease course. However, neuroradiological reversibility after HSCT remains insufficiently documented. Methods We report a male infant diagnosed with Type 1 fucosidosis at 6 months of age based on enzymatic and genetic analyses. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) demonstrated characteristic abnormalities, including central tegmental tract involvement. The patient underwent allogeneic HSCT at 14 months of age and was followed clinically and radiologically. Results Following HSCT, the patient demonstrated stabilization and gradual improvement of neurological functions. Follow-up neuroimaging revealed marked regression of white matter abnormalities and reversal of central tegmental tract hyperintensities. Developmental progression improved after transplantation, and no major transplant-related neurological complications occurred. Conclusion Early HSCT was accompanied by clinical improvement and resolution of central tegmental tract abnormalities in this patient. These imaging changes may help assess treatment response, though larger cohorts and longer follow-up are needed to evaluate long-term outcomes.
papers.summary_zh: 该病例报告描述一名男婴在6个月时经酶学和基因分析确诊为1型岩藻糖苷贮积症，脑MRI和MRS显示包括中央被盖束受累在内的特征性异常，随后在14个月时接受异基因造血干细胞移植并进行了临床与影像随访。移植后患儿神经功能趋于稳定并逐渐改善，随访影像显示白质异常明显消退、中央被盖束高信号逆转，发育进程也有所进步，且未出现重大移植相关神经系统并发症。作者据此认为早期移植伴随临床改善和中央被盖束异常的消退，这些影像变化或有助于评估治疗反应，但尚需更大样本和更长随访来确定长期结局。

papers.title: Neurophysiological Correlates of Pain-Related Cognitive-Affective Dysregulation in Adolescent Depression.
papers.authors: Li H, Wen Y, Cheng W, Zhuang L, Liu Z.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by altered processing and regulation of negative emotional and bodily experiences. Pain lies at the interface of sensory and cognitive-affective processing, encompassing both perceptual sensitivity and appraisal of pain-related experiences. Yet, how pain catastrophizing, a pain-specific cognitive-affective pattern characterized by rumination, magnification, and helplessness, relates to depressive severity and neurophysiological dynamics during adolescence remains poorly understood. In this cross-sectional case-control study, we recruited 140 participants aged 12-23 years with and without MDD and investigated behavioral and electrophysiological correlates of pain-related cognitive-affective dysregulation using clinical assessments and resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). Structural equation modeling revealed a significant indirect association between pain catastrophizing and depressive severity through anxiety, highlighting anxiety-related processes within this relationship. Compared with healthy controls, adolescents with MDD exhibited increased δ- and θ-band power and altered EEG microstate dynamics, characterized by greater temporal involvement of microstate B, reduced temporal persistence of microstate D, and increased bidirectional B-C transitions. EEG-informed path models further linked microstate features to the indirect relationship between pain catastrophizing, anxiety, and depressive severity. Together, these findings identify convergent behavioral and neurophysiological correlates of pain-related cognitive-affective dysregulation and highlight dynamic EEG features for further investigation in adolescent MDD.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注青少年重性抑郁障碍中疼痛相关认知-情感失调的神经生理关联，采用横断面病例对照设计，结合临床评估与静息态脑电，比较伴与不伴抑郁的青少年。结构方程模型显示，疼痛灾难化与抑郁严重程度之间通过焦虑存在间接关联，提示焦虑相关过程在其中起作用。与健康对照相比，抑郁青少年的δ和θ频段功率升高，脑电微状态动态也发生改变，表现为微状态B的时间占比增加、微状态D的持续时间缩短以及B-C双向转换增多；脑电信息路径模型进一步将这些微状态特征与上述间接关系联系起来。作者据此认为，这些行为与神经生理指标共同反映了疼痛相关认知-情感失调，并提示动态脑电特征值得在青少年抑郁中进一步研究。

papers.title: Evolutionary Background of Precise Vocal-Respiratory Temporal Coordination in Human Infants.
papers.authors: Takahasi M, Mazuka R.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Human infants acquire speech through prolonged postnatal development. Sequential vocalizations, including speech, can be viewed as motor patterns consisting of alternating sound and silence. This temporal structure depends on the coordination of respiratory airflow and laryngeal activity, yet relatively little attention has been paid to how such timing control develops in infancy. In this review, we examine the development of vocal timing across two contexts: spontaneous vocalizations produced in nonsocial settings and vocal exchanges during face-to-face interactions. We highlight a developmental transition around the second half of the first year, in which vocal timing first becomes relatively stabilized in relation to respiratory maturation and is then increasingly used flexibly in social interaction. To place this transition in an evolutionary context, we review comparative findings from songbirds and marmosets and consider swallowing as another vital behavior requiring tight laryngeal-respiratory coordination. In humans, rapid postnatal brain growth may promote early complementary feeding, increasing the need for flexible regulation of swallowing timing, while laryngeal descent may heighten the need for airway protection. These pressures may have provided a physiological background for the later elaboration of flexible vocal timing control.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述关注人类婴儿发声与呼吸的时间协调如何发展，梳理了非社会情境下的自发发声和面对面互动中的发声交流两类情境。作者指出，婴儿在出生后第一年下半年出现一个发展转折：发声时序先随呼吸系统成熟而相对稳定，随后在社交互动中被越来越灵活地运用。为放入演化背景，文章还比较了鸣禽和狨猴的研究，并把吞咽视为另一种需要喉部与呼吸紧密协调的重要行为。作者提出，人类出生后脑的快速生长可能促使早期补充喂养，从而增加灵活调节吞咽时序的需求，而喉部下降可能加大气道保护的需要，这些压力或为日后灵活发声时序控制的精细化提供了生理基础。

papers.title: Epidemiology of Irritable Bowel Syndrome Among Chilean Adults: Differences Across Healthcare Settings and Urban-Rural Populations.
papers.authors: von Muhlenbrock C, Pacheco N, Santos N, Carbone F, Tack J, Madrid AM, Vanuytsel T.
papers.abstract: Introduction Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is one of the most prevalent disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs), with an estimated global prevalence ranging from 4.1% to 17%. However, prevalence data remain largely unknown in many countries and across different populations. Aim The aim of this study was to characterize IBS among Chilean adults using Spanish-validated Rome diagnostic criteria across healthcare and community-based settings, including public and private gastroenterology outpatient populations and urban and rural/Mapuche community populations. Methods IBS was assessed using standardized, Spanish-validated Rome questionnaires, with Rome IV criteria applied to available symptom data in the outpatient cohorts (public and private) and the official Spanish-language Rome IV Diagnostic Questionnaire used in the community-based populations (urban and rural/Mapuche). Data were analyzed using chi-squared, Mann-Whitney U, and multivariable logistic regression, with analyses performed using GraphPad Prism. Results We evaluated the proportion of gastroenterology outpatients meeting Rome IV criteria for IBS and IBS subtypes in 8717 patients, as well as IBS prevalence in 896 urban and rural/Mapuche community participants. The proportion of gastroenterology outpatients meeting Rome IV criteria for IBS was higher in the public than private hospital (36.2% vs. 23.3%; p < 0.0001) and in urban females versus males (30.5% vs. 20.5%; p = 0.0015). Rural/Mapuche and urban populations showed comparable IBS prevalence (30.9% vs. 25.7%; p = 0.26), and rural/Mapuche residence was not significantly associated with IBS after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted OR 1.18, 95% CI 0.68-2.05; p = 0.56). The rural/Mapuche population had a different subtype distribution, with a higher proportion of IBS-M. Conclusions IBS symptoms compatible with Rome IV criteria were common across the evaluated Chilean adult populations, with differences observed according to healthcare setting and sex. Although IBS prevalence did not differ significantly between the urban and rural/Mapuche populations, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given differences in age and recruitment methods. Larger population-based studies are needed to confirm these findings in rural and Indigenous populations. These data provide novel insights into IBS epidemiology in a Latin American country with marked socioeconomic heterogeneity and may inform future population-based and mechanistic studies in diverse settings.

papers.title: Cortical Morphology and Susceptibility to Fall-Related Fractures: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Study.
papers.authors: Yang XL, Zhao QH, Xiao MZ, Ma YZ, Hong YM.
papers.abstract: Aim Injurious falls and low-energy fractures after a simple fall cause substantial morbidity in older adults; observational brain-structure associations are vulnerable to confounding and reverse causation. To test whether predicted regional cortical thickness or surface area causally influences falls and fractures after a simple fall, and to evaluate reverse causality. Methods Bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization used cortical morphology across 34 regions (> 51 000 Europeans). Outcomes were falls/tendency to fall and simple-fall fractures. Independent genome-wide significant instruments (p < 5 × 10-8 ) were clumped at r2 = 0.001 within a 10 000 kb window, retained if SNP-level F statistics were > 10, and analyzed using inverse-variance weighted MR with sensitivity methods, pleiotropy/directionality checks, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Estimated bone mineral density (eBMD) was explored as a potential mediator. Results After FDR correction and pleiotropy screening, larger caudal anterior cingulate surface area was associated with lower odds of fracture resulting from a simple fall (OR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98; pFDR = 0.0159), whereas larger insula surface area was related to higher odds of fracture resulting from a simple fall (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.08; pFDR = 0.0037). Associations with the broader falls/tendency-to-fall phenotype were not robust. Reverse MR showed no evidence that falls or simple-fall fractures altered cortical traits, and exploratory eBMD analyses did not support mediation. Conclusions Genetically predicted surface area in the caudal anterior cingulate and insula was associated with susceptibility to fractures resulting from simple falls. These findings require replication and functional validation before specific neurobiological mechanisms or clinical applications can be inferred.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究用双向两样本孟德尔随机化，检验预测的皮层厚度或表面积是否因果影响跌倒及简单跌倒后骨折，并评估反向因果。经多重比较校正和敏感性分析后，较大的尾侧前扣带表面积与简单跌倒后骨折风险降低相关，而较大的岛叶表面积与风险升高相关；与更宽泛的跌倒倾向表型的关联不稳健。反向分析未发现跌倒或骨折改变皮层特征的证据，探索性骨密度分析也不支持中介作用。作者强调这些关联需重复验证和功能研究，尚不能推断具体神经机制或临床应用。

papers.title: Multimodal Neuroimaging and Behavioral Characterization of Aged Female APOE4 Knock-In Rats Reveals a Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease Phenotype.
papers.authors: Cavallaro NJ, Maheswari A, Chukwuemeka T, Koganov A, Sundararaj N, D'Argenio S, Stotland H, Weiss D, Botelho G, Kulkarni PP, Ferris CF.
papers.abstract: The apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (APOE4) is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer's disease (AD) and confers disproportionate risk in women, particularly after reproductive senescence. The brain changes preceding overt neurodegeneration in APOE4 carriers remain incompletely characterized. We conducted neuroimaging and behavioral studies in aged (18-month) female APOE4 humanized knock-in rats and APOE3 controls. Regional brain volumes across 197 areas were quantified by voxel-based morphometry (VBM); white and gray matter microstructure by diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), yielding fractional anisotropy (FA) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Spatial memory was assessed with the Barnes maze and motor coordination with the beam walk. APOE4 rats showed significantly larger regional brain volumes than APOE3 controls. DTI revealed increased FA in the thalamus, brainstem, and white matter tracts, and reduced FA in the sensorimotor cortex. Across most regions elevated FA was accompanied by reduced ADC, an inverse relationship consistent with cytotoxic edema. Behaviorally, APOE4 rats were significantly impaired on the Barnes maze. Aged female APOE4 knock-in rats exhibit a preclinical AD phenotype: widespread volumetric enlargement across white matter, sensorimotor, and limbic circuits, with microstructural alterations (elevated FA in brainstem, thalamus, and white matter; reduced FA in sensorimotor cortex). This mirrors the imaging and cognitive profile of cognitively normal human APOE4 carriers in preclinical AD and validates the model as a translationally relevant platform for investigating early APOE4-driven pathophysiology and testing preventive interventions.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在18月龄雌性APOE4人源化敲入大鼠与APOE3对照中，结合体素形态学、弥散张量成像及行为测试，考察阿尔茨海默病临床前阶段的表现。结果显示，APOE4大鼠多个脑区体积增大，丘脑、脑干和白质纤维束各向异性升高而感觉运动皮层降低，且多数区域各向异性升高伴随弥散系数下降，提示细胞毒性水肿；行为上空间记忆受损。作者认为这再现了认知正常人类APOE4携带者的影像与认知特征，支持该模型用于研究早期APOE4相关病理及预防干预，但结论基于动物模型，尚不能直接推及临床。

papers.title: Neural Cell Models of Specific Reading Disabilities: Identification of Cellular and Transcriptome Alterations.
papers.authors: Barr CL, Wigg KG, Feng Y, Blokland K, Wilkinson M, Kerr EN, Guger SL, Lovett MW, Strug LJ, Oefner R, Benassi S, Gage FH, Marchetto MC.
papers.abstract: Based on post-mortem studies, a long-standing hypothesis on the biological bases of specific reading disabilities (RD) has been that alterations in neuronal migration alter language neural circuits. However, there are questions concerning the original studies (small sample size, comorbidities). Further, this idea has not been strongly supported by current genetic studies. In this study, we test altered neural cell phenotypes using cells derived from two pairs of siblings strongly discordant for reading-probands with severe RD and their strong-reader siblings. We observed significant differences in neurosphere outgrowth between the neural precursor cells (NPCs) from the probands compared to their strong-reader siblings. Transcriptome analyses of adherent NPCs and neurons derived from the NPCs identified genes differentially expressed between the probands and siblings, including genes previously identified in neurodevelopmental disorders. Of note was the overexpression of the hormone IGF1 and the transcription factor OTX2, responsible for the opening and closing of critical windows in development and predicted to be involved in critical windows for language acquisition. Our results support altered transcriptome and cellular phenotypes in RD neural cells and suggest possible molecular mechanisms underlying the changes.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对特定阅读障碍的生物学基础，用两对阅读能力高度不一致的兄妹（阅读障碍者与阅读能力强者）来源的神经前体细胞和神经元，检验细胞表型与转录组改变。结果显示，患者神经前体细胞的神经球生长存在差异，且前体细胞和神经元中有多个基因表达不同，包括既往在神经发育障碍中报道的基因；其中激素IGF1和转录因子OTX2过表达尤为突出，二者与发育关键期的开启和关闭有关，被推测可能涉及语言习得的关键期。作者据此认为，阅读障碍神经细胞存在转录组和细胞表型改变，并提示了可能的分子机制，但相关发现仍需进一步验证。

papers.title: Associations Between the Brain Care Score and Structural Brain Changes and Cognitive Impairment Using Data From the Hamburg City Health Study.
papers.authors: Schellin J, Sehner S, Neumann M, Petersen M, Nägele FL, Singh SD, Rosand J, Schumacher N, Zyriax BC, Twerenbold R, Cheng B, Thomalla G, Jensen M.
papers.abstract: Background The Brain Care Score (BCS) was designed to engage patients in behavior change targeting modifiable risk factors for dementia, stroke, and depression. We investigated its associations with structural brain changes and cognitive function to evaluate its utility for early prevention. Methods We analyzed data from the population-based Hamburg City Health Study (participants aged 45-74 years). A modified BCS (range 0-18) was derived from physiological, lifestyle, and social factors. Brain MRI including diffusion tensor imaging provided markers of neurodegeneration, vascular brain damage, and structural brain network organization. Cognitive function was assessed using the MMSE and CERAD-Plus subtests. Results Among 2453 participants (mean age 63.8 years, 44% women, median BCS 11), a higher BCS was associated with less vascular brain damage: a 5-point-increase was associated with lower white matter hyperintensity burden (relative increase 0.81; 95% CI [0.75, 0.87]) and lower Peak Width of Skeletonized Mean Diffusivity (relative increase 0.97; 95% CI [0.96, 0.98]). A higher BCS was also associated with better structural connectivity (higher global efficiency, lower clustering coefficient). Regarding cognition, a 5-point-increase was associated with faster processing speed (relative increase 0.96, 95% CI [0.94, 0.98]), better executive function (relative increase 0.94, 95% CI [0.91, 0.97]), and improved verbal fluency (absolute increase 0.57, 95% CI [0.05, 1.10]). Conclusion The BCS represents a simple score capturing modifiable risk factors for common age-related brain disease, adaptable to large population-based cohorts. Higher scores are associated with healthier brain structure, network organization, and better cognitive function, supporting its role in guiding preventive interventions. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03934957.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于汉堡城市健康研究的群体数据，考察改良版脑健康评分（涵盖生理、生活方式和社会因素）与脑结构改变及认知功能之间的关联。结果显示，评分较高者血管性脑损伤标志物负担较低，结构性脑网络组织更优，并在加工速度、执行功能和言语流畅性等认知测验上表现更好。作者认为，这一简便评分可用于大型人群队列，并可能有助于指导针对年龄相关脑病的早期预防，但研究为横断面关联分析，尚不能说明评分改善会带来脑结构或认知获益。

papers.title: Continuous Versus Routine EEG in Critically Ill Patients Without Primary Neurologic Condition: Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Lepeu G, Novy J, Alvarez V, Schindler KA, Rüegg S, Rossetti AO.
papers.abstract: Introduction Continuous EEG (cEEG) is increasingly used in critically ill patients, driven by its superior seizure detection sensitivity over routine EEG (rEEG). However, cEEG is resource-demanding, and whether its use translates into improved clinical outcomes in patients without primary neurologic conditions remains unknown. Methods This is a post hoc analysis of the multicenter randomized CERTA trial, in which critically-ill adults were randomized 1:1 to cEEG or two rEEG recordings. Six-month mortality represented the primary outcome, while exploratory outcomes included functional outcome (Cerebral Performance Categories, CPC), detection of seizures/status epilepticus, ictal-interictal continuum features, medication changes, and infections within 4 weeks. Analysis was restricted to patients without primary neurologic injury. Results Among 364 enrolled patients, 76 lacked a primary neurologic condition (cEEG: n = 34, rEEG: n = 42). Continuous EEG was not associated with mortality (p = 0.970) or functional outcome (CPC 1-2; p = 0.893). No seizures or status epilepticus were detected in either group. Rates of EEG periodic patterns, ictal-interictal continuum features, medication changes, and infections were comparable between groups. Conclusion In critically ill adults without a primary neurologic condition, cEEG was not associated with measurable benefits in survival, neurological recovery, or epileptiform activity detection compared with repeated rEEG, in a cohort without detected electrographic seizures or status epilepticus. Pending larger, ideally prospective comparative studies, repeated routine EEG may represent a reasonable alternative in resource-limited settings.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于CERTA随机试验的事后分析，聚焦无原发性神经系统疾病的危重成人，比较持续脑电图（cEEG）与两次常规脑电图（rEEG）在临床结局上的差异。结果显示，两组在六个月死亡率、功能结局以及癫痫发作或癫痫持续状态的检出上均无差异，周期性模式、发作间期-发作期连续谱特征、用药调整和感染等探索性结局也相近。作者据此认为，在这一未检出电graphic癫痫发作或癫痫持续状态的队列中，cEEG未见可测量的生存、神经功能恢复或癫痫样活动检测获益，资源有限时重复常规脑电图可能是合理替代，但尚需更大规模、最好为前瞻性的比较研究加以验证。

papers.title: Structural Brain Correlates of Digit-Span Performance in Adults: A Narrative Review of Evidence From Lesion and MRI Studies.
papers.authors: Carnemolla SE, Chau M.
papers.abstract: The digit-span task is a widely used measure of working memory in clinical and research contexts. Although numerous studies have examined its neuroanatomical correlates, research findings are heterogeneous, and a clear synthesis of structural evidence is warranted. This review aimed to synthesise existing evidence linking structural integrity of brain regions (volume or lesion) with digit-span performance in adults, using findings from 23 peer-reviewed studies. Functional imaging studies, composite digit-span scores and paediatric/adolescent samples were excluded. PubMed search supplemented by citation tracking identified 23 eligible studies (17 lesion and six structural MRI) published until December 2025. Six regions were related to both forward and backward digit-span task performance (left inferior parietal, left insula, bilateral supplementary motor, bilateral cerebellum, left middle temporal and left thalamus regions). Forward span was uniquely associated with six left-hemisphere regions including the left superior temporal, caudate, putamen, superior frontal, inferior temporal and precuneus. Backward span was uniquely associated with the bilateral superior parietal, bilateral hippocampus, left sensorimotor, right precuneus and right posterior cingulate regions. Dorsolateral prefrontal and inferior frontal findings were mixed. Partially distinct neuroanatomical profiles between forward and backward digit-span tasks likely reflect differences between attentional control/storage demands and higher executive/manipulation demands, respectively. In conclusion, digit-span performance is related to a distributed neural network spanning cortical, subcortical and cerebellar regions. While forward and backward digit-span tasks share common substrates, distinct regions are also recruited, consistent with differing cognitive demands. These findings may inform clinical interpretation and targeted cognitive interventions for prevention and rehabilitation of working memory deficits.

papers.title: Beyond Dissemination: From Critical Science Literacy to Citizen Neuroscience.
papers.authors: Raschle NM, Federici E, Hauser T, Dresler M.
papers.abstract: Neuroscience increasingly informs education, mental health, and public policy, yet its real-world impact remains limited, with misunderstandings and neuromyths persisting. We argue that the societal impact of neuroscience communication depends less on the volume of information disseminated than on whether it cultivates critical science literacy, namely, the ability to evaluate how neuroscientific knowledge is generated, modeled, and constrained and to understand the inferential steps linking data to conclusions and their limits of generalization. In the context of neuroscience, we refer to this as critical neuroscience literacy to emphasize the domain-specific challenges of interpreting brain-based evidence. The primary barrier is not insufficient dissemination alone, but systematic misinterpretation of neuroscientific inference once findings leave the laboratory. We advance three claims: first, that public misunderstandings often reflect limited insight into scientific reasoning and practice rather than simple information deficits about scientific results; second, that citizen science and dialogical engagement function as mechanisms for practicing such reasoning rather than as outreach add-ons; and third, that neuroscientists share responsibility for shaping the interpretive conditions under which findings are translated, particularly in education, health, and policy. Importantly, this self-referentiality is not merely descriptive. Interpretations are associated with beliefs, expectations, and environments that may themselves be linked to neural and behavioral change. We outline implications for training, incentives, and professional norms within the neuroscience community.

papers.title: Motoric Cognitive Risk Syndrome as a Predementia Marker: Insights From a Bibliometric and Visual Analysis.
papers.authors: Zhao B, Yang Z, Shen Y, Zhu J, Cao M, Yu Q, Hou X, Zou Z.
papers.abstract: Motoric cognitive risk syndrome (MCR)-characterized by subjective cognitive complaints and slow gait in people without dementia or mobility disability-is an emerging predementia stage. To characterize the evolution, collaboration structure, and thematic organization of MCR research, we performed a bibliometric and visual analysis using Web of Science Core Collection records published between January 1, 2013, and July 30, 2026. Following dual-investigator screening, 238 English-language original articles and reviews (from 308 records) were analyzed using VOSviewer (v1.6.19) and CiteSpace (v 6.4.R2). Annual publication volume accelerated post-2020, peaking at 56 records in 2025. China led in total publication volume, whereas the United States demonstrated the highest country-level network connectivity. Thematic mapping revealed a core focus on cognitive impairment, dementia, gait, and older-adult research, with recent shifts toward neuroimaging and physical activity interventions. Citation-burst analysis highlighted a progression from foundational cohort studies to definition harmonization and multidomain research. While bibliometric mapping reflects academic output rather than clinical validity, these findings underscore the need for standardized diagnostic criteria, prospective validation, and scalable multidisciplinary studies.

papers.title: Structuring the World: Statistical Learning From the Top and From the Bottom.
papers.authors: Tabas A, Fiser J, Lengyel M, de Hoz L.
papers.abstract: Statistical learning is the brain's primary strategy for transforming continuous, noisy, and ambiguous sensory inputs into structured internal representations. This process is studied through a diverse array of perspectives spanning different species, sensory systems, levels of analysis, and methodological frameworks. Here, we present four such perspectives. Two of them approach the problem from the bottom, examining the neural substrates of the biological implementation. The first line describes implicit contextual learning in the rodent auditory midbrain, showing how neuronal frequency tuning adapts to predictable statistical regularities over days. The second line shows that explicit knowledge modulates belief updating as early as the human auditory midbrain and thalamus, revealing a functionally specialized subcortical inferential hierarchy. The other two research lines approach it from the top, examining the computations the brain performs. The third line compares statistical computations across species and human development, uncovering fundamental differences in probabilistic chunking strategies between honeybees, human infants, and adults. The fourth line provides a computational framework for continual learning in which experience is organized into structured internal models through ongoing contextual inference. We then examine what each line can contribute to the others. We argue that, if the brain evolved statistical learning under pressure to behave optimally, this optimality must have been achieved globally through the constraints and synergies that emerge from the interplay between subsystems and levels of analysis. The neuronal mechanisms implementing a computation are shaped by the computation they perform, while that computation is itself constrained by the available physiology: a mutual dependence that can only be understood by bridging across perspectives.

papers.title: Mismatch Responses to Prosodic Changes in Children With Developmental Language Disorder: A Longitudinal Approach.
papers.authors: Themas L, Schaadt G, Lippus P, Padrik M, Kask L, Vaher U, Männamaa M, Kreegipuu K.
papers.abstract: Developmental language disorder is characterized by difficulties in auditory processing and prosody discrimination. Estonian word prosody features a unique three-way quantity distinction, characterized by changes in syllable duration and pitch contour, which differentiate word meaning and grammatical cases. In this study, we examined the Mismatch Responses longitudinally in 23 children with developmental language disorder and 25 age and biological sex matched typically developing peers (age at first measurement 4;6-6;5 years; age at second measurement 5;6-7;5 years). A multifeature paradigm was used in which all stimuli were meaningful words; two deviants differed from the standard, one in syllable duration and the other in both syllable duration and pitch contour. We also tested the discrimination of these prosodic features with behavioral tasks at both measurements. For duration discrimination, an early positive mismatch response diminished from first to second measurement, while a subsequent negative mismatch response increased. Significant longitudinal changes were observed in the typically developing group but not in children with developmental language disorder, while direct comparisons of maturational trajectories did not reveal significant group differences. For the duration and pitch contrast, in both groups and at both assessments, no mismatch response was detected. Additionally, no association was observed at the individual level between maturational changes in mismatch responses and behavioral discrimination at either measurement. These findings provide insights into the maturation of prosodic change detection processes and contribute to a better understanding of developmental language disorder and its manifestations.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究追踪比较了发育性语言障碍儿童与典型发育同伴对爱沙尼亚语词韵律变化的失匹配反应及其行为辨别能力，采用纵向多特征范式，以真实词为刺激考察音节时长及时长加音高轮廓两类偏差。结果显示，仅时长偏差诱发了失匹配反应：早期正波随年龄减弱、随后负波增强，这种纵向变化在典型发育组显著，而在发育性语言障碍组不明显，但两组成熟轨迹的直接比较未达显著差异；时长加音高偏差在两组两次测量中均未引出失匹配反应。个体层面，失匹配反应的成熟变化与行为辨别成绩无关联。作者据此讨论韵律变化检测的成熟过程及其对理解发育性语言障碍表现的意义，结果尚不能说明组间成熟差异具有统计可靠性。

papers.title: Towards a Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) for Improving Phonological Processing in Developmental Dyslexia: An Exploratory Study.
papers.authors: Zheng X, Araújo J, Busson Q, Goswami U.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have immense potential regarding the provision of therapies for disorders of development, but to date have typically been created for non-linguistic disorders such as ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder). Here, we present a BCI designed to improve linguistic phonological processing during natural speech listening, aimed at participants with developmental dyslexia. Phonological 'deficits' are considered a core feature of dyslexia across languages and are present from infancy in those later diagnosed with dyslexia. Here, a non-invasive EEG-BCI relying on auditory inputs and visual feedback was developed to optimise brain patterns related to phonological development in infants and children. The BCI focused on neural patterns identified using Temporal Sampling theory, which has found the theta/delta ratio during natural speech listening to be a key neural associate of impaired phonology. As a first step, the BCI was tested with adults. Adults with and without dyslexia played the BCI for 16 sessions and received pre- and post-testing regarding phonological awareness and single word and non-word reading skills. Learning was assessed both online, as in most BCI studies, and offline, enabling removal of a greater number of potential EEG artefacts. Significant associations between offline BCI scores (a measure of BCI learning) and improvements in non-word reading were found for all participants who learned the BCI, both dyslexic and control. BCI learning also showed significant associations with improvements in real word reading and amplitude rise time discrimination. The data are interpreted with respect to Temporal Sampling theory.
papers.summary_zh: 该探索性研究开发了一种基于脑电、以听觉输入和视觉反馈构成的脑机接口，旨在通过自然言语聆听训练与语音发展相关的脑活动模式，目标人群为发展性阅读障碍者，并首先在成人中测试。有阅读障碍和无阅读障碍的成人接受了多次训练及前后测。结果显示，在学会使用该脑机接口的参与者中（无论有无阅读障碍），离线脑机接口学习分数与无词阅读改善存在显著关联，该分数也与真词阅读和上升时间辨别改善相关。作者结合时间采样理论解读这些关联，但摘要未报告对照比较或因果证据，因此结果应视为初步关联而非治疗效果。

papers.title: Altered Timing of Self-Voice Processing in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.authors: Contreras-Ruston F, Criscuolo A, Callén A, Cucurell D, Navarra J, Kotz SA.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) affects voice and speech production, often resulting in reduced vocal intensity and monotonous speech. Recent studies suggest that these changes can be partially explained by altered sensory feedback processing in speech production: individuals with PD (IwPD) may fail to monitor and adapt sensory feedback when producing speech. We investigated PD voice production using a voice playback paradigm and focused on the sensory attenuation typically observed in event-related responses (ERPs) to the self-generated voice. When sensory feedback is intact, the P50, N100, and P200 responses to a self-generated voice are attenuated compared to an externally generated voice. Twenty-three IwPD and 23 matched healthy controls (HCs) completed the voice playback study with three conditions: self-generated voice (auditory-motor [AMC]), externally generated voice (auditory-only [AOC]), and motor-only. Linear mixed models assessed group differences in ERP morphology. Groups differed in the N100 latency response: IwPD showed a greater shift in latency between AMC and AOC than healthy controls. Regarding the P200, a significant group-by-condition interaction indicated that IwPD, unlike healthy controls, produced larger amplitudes for the self-generated than the passively listened to voice. Taken together, these findings suggest that the processing of one's own voice in IwPD is altered in terms of temporal precision rather than in the N100 suppression effect per se. This effect was accompanied by an enhanced P200 attentional response. These response patterns in IwPD are indicative of likely progressing difficulties in regulating one's own voice, characteristic of Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注帕金森病患者的自我语音加工，采用语音回放范式比较患者与匹配健康对照在听觉-运动、纯听觉和纯运动条件下的脑电反应，以考察自我生成语音通常出现的感觉衰减。结果显示，两组在N100潜伏期上存在差异：患者自我生成与外部生成语音之间的潜伏期偏移大于健康对照；P200上则出现组别与条件的交互，患者对自我生成语音的波幅反而大于被动聆听时，而健康对照并非如此。作者据此认为，患者自我语音加工的改变主要体现在时间精确性而非N100抑制本身，并伴随增强的P200注意反应，可能反映其调控自身语音的困难。

papers.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of VR Rehabilitation Systems for ASD: A Focus on Embodied Interaction and Longitudinal Impact.
papers.authors: Qu J, Bu L, Zhang Q, Zhang K, Liu N, Li M, Pang X.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics
papers.abstract: With the increasing rehabilitation needs of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and the development of virtual reality (VR) systems in rehabilitation, VR training systems based on embodied interaction have received growing research attention. However, evaluating rehabilitation-related changes during long-term VR training and improving the use of multi-source feedback remain important challenges. This study aims to explore the longitudinal effects of a VR training and assessment system based on embodied interaction and multi-source interactive feedback for children with ASD. The system integrates brain function evaluation using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), behavioral pattern analysis using Kinect, VR task performance records, and subjective questionnaires. Guided by human-centered design principles, a one-month longitudinal study was conducted in a hospital rehabilitation setting with nine children with ASD. Participants completed 20 VR training sessions, and data were collected before the first training session, after the tenth session, and after the twentieth session. The results provide preliminary support for the feasibility of the system and show positive changes in several rehabilitation-related indicators, including task performance, subjective user experience indicators, selected brain function measures, and upper limb movement patterns. The multi-source feedback approach provides complementary objective information for interpreting rehabilitation-related changes. These findings offer references for applying VR technology in ASD rehabilitation and for designing longitudinal training cycles in future studies.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注基于具身交互和多源反馈的虚拟现实康复系统能否在较长期训练中用于自闭症谱系障碍儿童，并在医院康复环境中对9名儿童开展了为期一个月、共20次训练的纵向研究，在训练前、中、后采集数据。结果显示，该系统具有初步可行性，任务表现、主观体验、部分脑功能指标和上肢运动模式等康复相关指标出现积极变化，多源反馈也为解释这些变化提供了互补的客观信息。作者据此认为，这些发现可为VR技术用于自闭症康复及未来设计纵向训练周期提供参考，但结果仍属初步，尚不能据此推断临床疗效。

papers.title: Neural Signatures and Multi-Cognitive Decoding of EEG Signals Induced by Shared Stimulus: A Paradigm Study.
papers.authors: Ju J, Li H.
papers.abstract: Multi-task decoding from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals is valuable for brain-computer interface (BCI) applications in naturalistic settings. Most existing studies focus on decoding distinctly different tasks, leaving the diversity of cognitive responses elicited by a single stimulus underexplored. We introduced a novel experimental paradigm where a common visual stimulus elicits five distinct cognitive processes: single reach, interception reach, sequence reach, attention reach, and inhibition reach. EEG signatures were analyzed using temporal and spectral methods. A regularized linear discriminant analysis (RLDA) classifier was employed for decoding, utilizing both temporal and event-related spectral perturbation (ERSP) features. Significant neural activation differences (p < 0.05) were observed across tasks and brain regions. The RLDA classifier achieved high decoding accuracy: 91.72% ± 6.10% for classifying the five cognitive states using ERSP features. Furthermore, for the sequence reach task, temporal features enabled classification of normal versus catch trials with 77.96% ± 7.03% accuracy. All these results demonstrate the potential for EEG-based BCI applications to distinguish diverse cognitive states elicited by identical stimuli, offering new insights for improving the naturalness and intelligence of BCI systems. Future work will focus on enhancing decoding performance and extending this research to online applications.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出一种新实验范式，让同一视觉刺激诱发单次伸够、拦截伸够、序列伸够、注意伸够和抑制伸够五种认知过程，并用脑电的时域与频谱特征分析其神经标记。结果显示，不同任务和脑区之间存在显著的神经激活差异；基于事件相关频谱扰动特征的分类器对五种认知状态的解码准确率较高，而时域特征也能区分序列伸够任务中的正常试次与捕捉试次。作者认为，这表明脑电能区分由相同刺激诱发的多种认知状态，为提升脑机接口在自然情境下的适用性提供了依据，但解码性能与在线应用仍有待后续研究。

papers.title: MSHANet: A Multiscale Hybrid Attention Network for Motor Imagery EEG Decoding.
papers.authors: Zhao Y, Cao D, Yu H, Liang G, Chen Z.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology has significant applications in neurorehabilitation and motor function restoration, especially for patients with stroke or spinal cord injury. Motor imagery electroencephalography (MI-EEG) is widely used in BCIs, but its nonlinear dynamics and inter-subject variability limit decoding accuracy. In this paper, a multiscale hybrid attention network (MSHANet) for MI-EEG decoding, which consists of spatiotemporal feature extraction (STFE), talking head self-attention (THSA), dynamic squeeze-and-excitation attention (DSEA), and a temporal convolutional network (TCN), is proposed. MSHANet was evaluated via within-subject experiments using BCI Competition IV Datasets 2a and 2b, as well as EEGMMID, achieving decoding accuracies of 83.56%, 89.75%, and 75.66%, respectively. In cross-subject experiments on the three datasets, the model attained accuracies of 69.93% on BCI-2a, 81.85% on BCI-2b, and 79.67% on EEGMMID. In addition, we propose an electrode spatial structure-aware encoder. This technique encodes the spatial positions of electrodes in the original data, enabling the model to obtain richer spatial electrode information at the input stage. In within-subject and cross-subject tasks on BCI-2a, this encoding improved the decoding performance by 2.83% and 2.91%, respectively. Visualization was also employed to elucidate feature distributions and the effectiveness of its attention mechanisms. Experimental results demonstrate that MSHANet performs exceptionally well in MI-EEG decoding tasks and has high potential for clinical applications, particularly in neurorehabilitation and motor function reconstruction.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对运动想象脑电信号因非线性动态和个体差异导致解码准确率受限的问题，提出一种多尺度混合注意力网络MSHANet，融合时空特征提取、自注意力、动态通道注意力和时间卷积网络，并引入电极空间结构感知编码。模型在三个公开数据集上分别开展被试内与被试间实验，被试内解码准确率整体较高，跨被试时性能有所下降；电极空间编码在被试内和跨被试任务中均带来一定提升。可视化结果用于说明特征分布和注意力机制的作用。作者据此认为该网络在运动想象解码上表现良好，并对其在神经康复和运动功能重建中的临床应用潜力作出展望，但摘要未提供临床验证证据。

papers.title: Multimodal Spiking Neural Network With Generalized Distributive Law for Biosignal and Sensory Fusion.
papers.authors: Huang Z, Guo B, Xu H, Ruan H, Guo D.
papers.abstract: Multimodal signal fusion is a cornerstone of biomedical engineering and intelligent sensing, enabling holistic analysis of heterogeneous sources such as electroencephalography (EEG), peripheral signals, speech, and imaging data. However, integrating diverse modalities in a computationally efficient and biologically plausible manner remains a significant challenge. Transformer-based fusion architectures rely on global cross-attention to integrate multimodal information but incur high computational costs. In contrast, STDP-driven fully connected layers adopt local learning rules, which restrict their ability to autonomously form efficient sparse topologies for complex multimodal tasks. To address these issues, we propose a novel end-to-end framework-the Multimodal Spiking Neural Network (MSNN)-featuring a fusion module grounded in the Generalized Distributive Law (GDL). This principled mechanism provides an efficient and interpretable means of integrating heterogeneous biomedical and sensory signals. The MSNN further incorporates structure-adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire (SALIF) neurons, enabling dynamic optimization of sparse connectivity to enhance fusion efficiency. The proposed MSNN is validated on a range of datasets, demonstrating strong versatility: it achieves binary classification accuracies of 92.29% (valence) and 91.08% (arousal) on the DEAP dataset for affective state decoding and 99.77% on the WESAD dataset for stress detection, while delivering state-of-the-art performance on standard pattern recognition tasks (MNIST & TIDIGITS: 99.01% ) and event-driven neuromorphic datasets (MNIST-DVS & N-TIDIGITS: 99.98% ). These results demonstrate that MSNN offers an effective and energy-efficient solution for multimodal sensor fusion in biomedical and intelligent sensing applications.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对多模态生物与传感信号融合中计算效率与生物合理性难以兼顾的问题，提出一种基于广义分配律融合模块的多模态脉冲神经网络框架，并引入结构自适应漏积分放电神经元以动态优化稀疏连接。作者在情感状态解码、压力检测及多个模式识别与神经形态数据集上验证了该框架，报告了较高的分类准确率，并将其定位为一种有效且节能的多模态融合方案。需要说明的是，这些结果来自作者所选数据集的分类性能评估，尚不能直接等同于临床或实际应用中的效果。

papers.title: RUNet: A Zero-Calibration Framework for Cross-Domain EEG Decoding via Riemannian and Unsupervised Representation Learning.
papers.authors: Jin J, Wang C, Xu R, He X, Wu X, Li J, Chen W, Wang X, Cichocki A.
papers.abstract: Objective Inter-session and inter-subject variability in electroencephalography (EEG) signals, resulting from individual differences and environmental factors, poses a major challenge for neural decoding in brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. Methods To address this issue, we propose RUNet, a zero-calibration motor imagery EEG decoding framework based on Riemannian manifold learning and unsupervised representation learning. RUNet incorporates a multi-scale spatiotemporal convolutional module that jointly captures local-global spatial and multi-resolution temporal dynamics features. To enhance the robustness of EEG features against non-stationarity, a polysynergistic covariance optimization module is employed, which strengthens the covariance matrix representation through multiple regularizations and adaptive fusion. In addition, RUNet integrates the Riemannian Affine Log Mapping layer, based on Affine-Invariant Transformation and Log-Euclidean Mapping, in an end-to-end manner to mitigate cross-domain covariance drift and enhance domain-invariant feature learning. A transfer learning framework is further integrated into RUNet: during pre-training, an unsupervised contrastive loss is applied to resting-state EEG data to learn domain-invariant spatiotemporal features; during retraining, task-specific data are used to enhance discriminability and feature disentanglement. Conclusion Experimental results on the BCI Competition IV 2a, 2b datasets and a self-collected laboratory dataset show that RUNet achieves average cross-session accuracies of 87.19%, 88.03% and 85.45%, and cross-subject accuracies of 68.09%, 78.29% and 87.25%, respectively. On the PhysioNet dataset, a cross-subject accuracy of 78.14% is achieved. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of RUNet's unified pipeline and its robust cross-domain generalization.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对脑电信号在跨会话、跨被试场景下因个体差异和环境因素导致的变异性问题，提出零校准运动想象解码框架RUNet，融合黎曼流形学习与无监督表征学习。该框架通过多尺度时空卷积联合提取局部与全局空间特征及多分辨率时间动态，利用多重正则化与自适应融合优化协方差矩阵表示，并以端到端的黎曼仿射对数映射层缓解跨域协方差漂移；预训练阶段在静息态脑电上采用无监督对比损失学习域不变特征，重训练阶段再用任务数据增强判别性与特征解耦。在多个公开数据集和自采数据上的实验显示，该框架取得较高的跨会话与跨被试解码准确率，表明其统一流程具有较好的跨域泛化能力，但结果仍属离线实验验证，尚不能直接等同于临床或实际BCI应用效果。

papers.title: Fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF) changes in children with anisometropic amblyopia: A resting-state fMRI study.
papers.authors: Yu X, Zhao L, Lu W, Chen D, Li D, Li X, Nie S, Wang Y, Wang B.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to explore changes in spontaneous brain activity in children with anisometropic amblyopia (CAA) using the fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF) analysis method and to determine whether anisometropic amblyopia is associated with changes in brain function. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data were collected from 16 children with anisometropic amblyopia (CAA group) and 10 healthy children (HC group). fALFF was used to assess spontaneous brain activity. Group differences in fALFF were analyzed using a two-sample t test, with age, sex, and head motion included as covariates. The statistical threshold was set at a voxel-level P < .001 (uncorrected), combined with a cluster-level family-wise error correction at P < .05. Partial Pearson correlation analyses, controlling for age and sex, were used to examine the relationships between fALFF values in regions showing significant group differences and clinical measures (best-corrected visual acuity of the amblyopic eye and magnitude of anisometropia) in the CAA group. Given the exploratory nature of the study, no correction for multiple comparisons was applied. Compared with the HC group, the CAA group showed higher fALFF values in the right middle occipital gyrus and left paracentral lobule. The fALFF value in the left middle frontal gyrus was lower in the CAA group than in the HC group. There were no significant correlations between clinical information and mean fALFF values in the CAA group. This study suggests that CAA may exhibit aberrant spontaneous brain activity within visual and frontal networks, as measured by fALFF. The absence of a direct correlation with standard clinical measures suggests that fALFF may capture distinct, network-level neural alterations in amblyopia. However, whether fALFF can serve as a reliable neuroimaging biomarker remains hypothetical and requires confirmation in larger, well-powered studies with comprehensive visual-function assessments.

papers.title: Mapping and visualizing global research trends in gut microbiota and autism spectrum disorder: A bibliometric analysis (2015-2024).
papers.authors: He Y, Lin F, Huang H, Chen Q.
papers.abstract: Background Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder with increasing research interest in its association with the gut microbiota. However, the knowledge structure and development of this field have not been systematically analyzed. Methods We conducted a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of English-language publications related to ASD and gut microbiota from 2015 to 2024 using the Web of Science Core Collection. We used the bibliometrix package in R, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace for analysis, focusing on publication trends, geographic and institutional contributions, prominent authors and journals, citation patterns, keyword dynamics, and thematic clusters. Results A total of 1309 publications were included, involving corresponding authors from 64 countries or regions. The annual number of publications steadily increased from 2015 to 2022, followed by a slight decline in 2023 and a partial rebound in 2024, with the US and China contributing the most. Leading authors and teams were primarily based in North America and Europe. Thematic evolution revealed a shift from early mechanistic research to intervention-focused topics, such as short-chain fatty acids, fecal microbiota transplantation, and probiotics. Conclusion Research on ASD and gut microbiota is progressing from theoretical exploration toward early-stage translational research, with increasing investigation of potential clinical applications. Future studies should emphasize multi-omics integration, mechanistic validation, and international collaboration. This bibliometric analysis offers a comprehensive overview to inform and guide future research in this rapidly evolving field.

papers.title: Central retinal artery occlusion preceding hemispheric ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy: A case report.
papers.authors: Wen X, Guo B, Zeng X, Xiang Z, Deng Z, Yuan Z.
papers.abstract: Rationale Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) is a form of ischemic stroke that may signal underlying cerebrovascular or cardiac disease. Patient concerns A 52-year-old man developed sudden, painless vision loss in the right eye. Nine days later, he presented with left-sided weakness and speech difficulty, with a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 8. His medical history included dilated cardiomyopathy, and electrocardiography revealed atrial fibrillation. Diagnoses Ophthalmologic examination and fluorescein angiography supported right CRAO. Computed tomography (CT) angiography at neurological presentation showed right internal carotid artery occlusion from its origin. CT perfusion demonstrated estimated infarct core and penumbral volumes of 37 and 186 mL, respectively. Interventions Emergency mechanical thrombectomy with aspiration and adjunctive balloon angioplasty achieved expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade 2c reperfusion. Outcomes The NIHSS score improved to 2 at discharge, 7 days after admission. At 3 months, the modified Rankin Scale score was 1, although right-eye visual loss persisted. Lessons CRAO warrants prompt cerebrovascular and cardiac evaluation, with reassessment when new neurological deficits develop. The nine-day interval between retinal symptoms and thrombectomy does not establish the duration of carotid occlusion or cerebral ischemia. The favorable individual outcome does not establish the efficacy of thrombectomy beyond 24 hours.

papers.title: Stroke and brain white/gray matter alterations: A Mendelian randomization investigation.
papers.authors: Wu X, Yang L, Xu W, Guan H.
papers.abstract: Disruptions or abnormalities in white and gray matter (WM/GM) microstructure are closely associated with the severity of neurological impairment and long-term prognosis and are often regarded as pathological sequelae in stroke patients. Still, their direct causal linkage remains to be elucidated. This study obtained genome-wide association study (GWAS) data of 5 stroke phenotypes from the MEGASTROKE consortium, as well as the GWAS data of 283 structural imaging-derived phenotypes (IDPs), including intracellular volume fraction (ICVF), isotropic/free water volume fraction (ISOVF), orientation dispersion index (ODI), and gray matter volume (GMV) from the UK Biobank. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was conducted to examine causal interactions between stroke phenotypes and IDPs. In forward MR results, any stroke was positively associated with ISOVF in the genu of the corpus callosum, while any ischemic stroke was positively associated with ISOVF in the body of the corpus callosum and the right superior corona radiata. Small-vessel stroke (SVS) was positively associated with ODI in the right superior cerebellar peduncle. In inverse MR results, GMV in the left planum polare was negatively associated with SVS, while ISOVF in specific brain regions was positively associated with SVS. This study systematically elucidated the causal relationships between stroke and brain structure involving WM/GM from the perspective of MR, which suggested that stroke-related genetic liability may causally contribute to white matter injury; genetically determined structural abnormalities in specific brain regions may causally increase the risk of SVS; GM atrophy may be an upstream causal factor for SVS, rather than merely a consequence.

papers.title: Two siblings presented with spastic paraplegia and psychomotor retardation with or without seizures with HACE1 variants: A case report and literature review.
papers.authors: Deng J, Gao Y.
papers.abstract: Rationale Spastic paraplegia and psychomotor retardation with or without seizures (SPPRS) is a rare autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder caused by biallelic HACE1 variants. Its long-term clinical course and genotype-phenotype spectrum remain incompletely characterized. Patient concerns Two siblings from a nonconsanguineous Chinese family presented with infantile-onset hypotonia, global developmental delay, markedly delayed motor milestones, gait impairment, language delay, and dysarthria. The older sister experienced recurrent febrile seizures, whereas her younger brother had no seizures. Diagnoses Whole-exome sequencing followed by Sanger validation identified compound heterozygous HACE1 variants in both siblings: c.1303C > T (p.Gln435Ter), inherited from the father, and c.2158_2159insG (p.Glu720GlyfsTer17), inherited from the mother. Both variants were considered disease-causing after clinical, segregation, database, and ACMG-based assessment. Interventions Both patients received symptomatic rehabilitation and underwent long-term neurological and developmental follow-up. Outcomes At the last follow-up, at 25 and 16 years of age, respectively, both siblings could walk independently with a waddling and unstable gait but remained unable to run. Both could understand basic instructions and communicate using short phrases, although dysarthria and substantial cognitive impairment persisted. An updated literature review demonstrated marked clinical heterogeneity among patients with HACE1-associated SPPRS, with hypotonia, developmental impairment, spasticity, speech disturbance, seizures, and structural brain abnormalities occurring at variable frequencies. Lessons These cases expand the genotypic spectrum of HACE1-associated SPPRS and demonstrate that a relatively mild and gradually improving clinical course may occur. Early molecular diagnosis can facilitate individualized rehabilitation, genetic counseling, and prenatal diagnostic planning.
keywords: Spastic Paraplegia And Psychomotor Retardation With Or Without Seizures
papers.summary_zh: 该病例报告结合文献回顾，报道了一对非近亲结婚的中国家庭兄妹，二人均因HACE1基因复合杂合变异而患伴或不伴癫痫的痉挛性截瘫与精神运动发育迟缓（SPPRS），通过全外显子测序及Sanger验证确认变异分别来自父母。两人均表现为婴儿期肌张力低下、全面发育迟缓、运动里程碑明显落后、步态异常、语言迟缓和构音障碍，姐姐有反复热性惊厥而弟弟无癫痫发作。长期随访至成年早期时，两人可独立行走但步态摇摆不稳、不能跑，能理解基本指令并用短语交流，构音障碍和明显认知损害持续存在。作者据此指出该病临床异质性显著，并提示存在相对较轻且逐渐改善的病程可能；早期分子诊断有助于个体化康复、遗传咨询和产前诊断规划。

papers.title: Functional brain network stability reflects individual resilience during sleep deprivation.
papers.authors: Cha J, Negelspach D, Huskey A, Kennedy KER, Katz J, Forger DB, Killgore WDS.
papers.abstract: Study objectives Sleep deprivation is known to impair cognitive performance, but individuals differ in their ability to maintain function under sleep loss. This study examined the neural mechanisms that support such resilience by tracking changes in resting-state functional connectivity during prolonged wakefulness. Materials and methods Six resting-state fMRI sessions obtained during approximately the first 32 hours of a 39-hour total sleep deprivation protocol were analyzed in 16 healthy adults, enabling unusually dense longitudinal sampling of brain network dynamics during prolonged wakefulness. Functional connectivity changes were analyzed using network-based statistics as the primary approach for analyzing pairwise functional connectivity, with nodal strength used as a secondary node-level follow-up analysis in relation to a behavioral resilience index derived from psychomotor vigilance performance. Results Two NBS-defined subnetworks, referred to here as the thalamocortical and perceptual-memory subnetworks, showed significant interactions between time awake and resilience, indicating that the trajectory of functional connectivity across prolonged wakefulness differed as a function of behavioral resilience. Participants with higher resilience showed less negative connectivity trajectories within these networks, particularly in the thalamus, globus pallidus, and visual cortex. In contrast, participants with lower resilience exhibited progressive declines in connectivity. Conclusion The ability to withstand the cognitive effects of sleep deprivation appears to be associated with less negative connectivity trajectories within thalamocortical and perceptual-memory subnetworks. These patterns may represent state-dependent neural correlates of resilience during sleep deprivation and may be relevant to future fatigue-state monitoring. Statement of Significance People differ widely in how well they stay alert and perform when they lose sleep, but the brain basis of this resilience is still not well understood. By repeatedly measuring brain activity during extended wakefulness, we found that people who performed better also showed stronger connectivity in brain systems linked to alertness and higher-level visual processing. Those who remained more resilient kept these brain systems working together more effectively, while those who were more vulnerable showed a greater loss of coordination and poorer performance over time. These findings contribute to understanding why some people maintain performance better than others during sleep loss and may support future efforts to monitor fatigue and protect performance in high-demand settings.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注睡眠剥夺下认知功能维持能力存在个体差异的神经基础，对健康成人进行长时间清醒期间的多次静息态功能磁共振扫描，并结合精神运动警觉任务得出的行为韧性指标分析功能连接变化。结果显示，丘脑皮层与知觉—记忆两个子网络的功能连接随时间变化的轨迹随韧性水平不同：韧性较高者这些网络连接下降较少，韧性较低者则逐步下降。作者据此认为，睡眠剥夺中较好的认知表现可能与这些网络连接轨迹较不负面相关，并提示其或可用于疲劳状态监测，但这只是关联性发现，尚不能说明因果或直接应用。

papers.title: Efficacy of Personalizing Cognitive Remediation for Schizophrenia by Targeting Impairments in Early Auditory Processing.
papers.authors: Medalia A, Saperstein AM, Javitt DC, Qian M.
papers.abstract: Background and hypotheses Early auditory processing (EAP) deficits are common but not universal in schizophrenia, are linked to impairments in higher cognitive functions and when improved are associated with downstream cognitive improvements. Assessment of baseline EAP training need provides an opportunity for cognitive remediation (CR) programs to personalize treatment and optimize impact. This confirmatory efficacy study examined the differential benefit of EAP training for those with and without baseline EAP deficits. Hypotheses were: (1) Only EAP impaired (EAP-) patients would benefit more from CR that included EAP training, (2) cognitive gains made by EAP- patients during CR that included EAP training would mediate the relationship between gains in EAP and functional capacity. Study design 184 outpatient adults diagnosed with schizophrenia were classified as having intact (n = 91) or impaired (n = 81) EAP and randomized to CR with restorative exercise plans that either included EAP training (n = 89) or did not (n = 83). Cognitive and functional outcomes were measured post-treatment and 3 months later. Study results Across CR treatment conditions, cognitive gain effect size was moderate. Treatment condition did not significantly impact EAP, cognitive, or functional outcomes for either EAP group at final endpoint. EAP improved significantly but modestly for EAP- patients across conditions. Cognitive gains did not mediate the relationship between EAP gains and functional capacity. Conclusions These findings support the value of CR for people with schizophrenia, demonstrate that EAP deficits are malleable, and that cognitive and functional gains can occur for EAP impaired patients, regardless of whether EAP training is provided.

papers.title: Neuroanatomical Subtypes of Schizophrenia Reveal Divergent Atrophy Trajectories and Distinct Associations with Long-Term Clozapine Use.
papers.authors: Chang X, Jiang Y, Lin BD, Xiang S, Zhang J, Collin G, Wirsching P, Schlagenhauf F, Zhao Y, Gong H, Zheng Y, Cui LB, Wang J, Jia T, Heinz A, Luykx JJ, Feng J, Zhangjiang International Brain Biobank (ZIB) Consortium.
papers.abstract: Background and hypothesis Schizophrenia is a heterogeneous disorder, and biology-informed stratification may provide insights into individual differences in disease course and treatment response. We hypothesized that neuroimaging-based subtyping could reveal biologically distinct subgroups characterized by divergent brain atrophy trajectories and unique clinical profiles. Study design We applied the Subtype and Stage Inference framework to baseline structural MRI data from the 6-year longitudinal Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis cohort (n = 467), including patients, unaffected siblings and healthy controls. We characterized subtype-specific longitudinal brain atrophy and medication profiles. Subtype-specific atrophy patterns were correlated with external molecular maps of neurotransmitter density and schizophrenia-related gene expression. Study results Two distinct neuroanatomical subtypes were identified: subtype 1 (65.5%), characterized by widespread cortical volume loss at baseline, and stable volume decrease over 6-year follow-up. Conversely, subtype 2 (34.5%) showed baseline volume decrease confined in the hippocampus and amygdala, but accelerated volume loss over follow-up. Clinically, subtype 1 patients had a significantly higher prevalence of clozapine use than subtype 2 (36% vs. 17%; chi2 = 5.62, P = 0.02), and brain atrophy of subtype 1 mirrored patterns observed in clozapine users. The two subtypes showed divergent spatial associations with neurotransmitter systems and risk-gene expression profiles. Conclusions We identified two neuroanatomical subtypes of schizophrenia showing divergent brain atrophy over 6-years. The subtypes may represent biologically distinct forms of schizophrenia, as they show different medication profiles and associations with molecular signatures. Our results provide a candidate framework for parsing disease heterogeneity and may offer insights for future stratified treatment strategies.

papers.title: Risk Indicator Aggregation and Cluster Stability Across Developmental Domains from Early to Middle Childhood in Children at Familial High-Risk of Schizophrenia or Bipolar Disorder and Population-Based Controls.
papers.authors: Krantz MF, Hoffmann AG, Hemager N, Gregersen M, Weye N, Søndergaard A, Burton B, Brandt J, Greve A, Knudsen CB, Andreassen AK, Veddum L, Jepsen JRM, Mors O, Thorup AAE, Ekstrøm CT, Nordentoft M.
papers.abstract: Background and hypotheses Children of parents with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder are at increased risk of developing a mental disorder, including psychosis. While domain-specific developmental risk indicators have been identified, studies examining the accumulated risk distribution are lacking. Hypothesizing heterogeneity, we aimed to identify clusters with differential risk indicator load across known risk domains, and to examine cluster stability across early to middle childhood in children at familial high-risk of schizophrenia (FHR-SZ) or bipolar disorder (FHR-BP). Study design A total of 441 children at FHR-SZ or FHR-BP and population-based controls were examined across multiple domains including neurocognition, social behavior, motor function, emotion regulation, language, and psychopathology at ages 7 and 11. Data from age 7 were clustered using k-means clustering and data from age 11 were clustered using the same cluster centers. Study results Four clusters were identified and named Best outcome profile, Intermediate outcome profile, Selectively affected profile, and Broadly affected profile. The clusters showed marked heterogeneity regarding child performance and functioning across domains, and associations with family and caregiver functioning were shown across groups. From age 7 to 11, 60% stayed in the same cluster. Conclusions Our findings of partially stable clusters with differential risk profiles for later onset of psychotic disorders evidence the need to consider risk heterogeneity in preventive interventions targeting offspring at FHR-SZ or FHR-BP, since some children have profiles with serious impairments across multiple domains while others have profiles with few or no impairments and therefore may be more resilient.

papers.title: Identifying Neurophysiological Subtypes in Clinical High Risk for Psychosis Using Functional Connectome Profiling.
papers.authors: Hou G, Feng J, Wang Y, Dong D.
