papers.abstract: Background and hypothesis The clinical high-risk (CHR) state already harbors substantial heterogeneity. Delineating homogeneous subgroups at this stage is critical for elucidating disease mechanisms and advancing precision psychiatry. However, the neurobiological heterogeneity among individuals at CHR and its clinical relevance remain poorly understood. Study Design: We applied Heterogeneity Through Discriminative Analysis to resting-state functional connectome profiling to identify potential neurophysiological subtypes within a large multicenter CHR dataset (N = 838) compared to healthy controls (HC) (N = 244). Study results The results revealed 2 distinct neurophysiological subtypes within the CHR population. Subtype 1 exhibited widespread reductions in overall functional connectivity-particularly within the sensorimotor network and the salience network-whereas Subtype 2 showed widespread increases within these networks. Compared with HC and Subtype 1, Subtype 2 showed poorer performance in sustained attention and verbal learning/memory. However, Subtype 1 did not differ significantly from HC in these domains. Conclusions These findings provide robust evidence for neurophysiological subtypes among individuals at CHR and further suggest that patterns of aberrant brain network organization have already diverged during the CHR stage, accompanied by dissociable cognitive profiles.

papers.title: Keratan sulfate proteoglycan is not expressed in human fetal cerebellar system except pontine nuclei and transitory vermal septa or in fasciculi caudal to the internal capsule.
papers.authors: Sarnat HB, Yu W, Flores-Sarnat L.
papers.journal: Journal of neuropathology and experimental neurology
papers.abstract: We determined spatial/temporal expression of keratan sulfate proteoglycan (KS) in the developing cerebellar system, fasciculi, and dysgeneses. KS is an extracellular molecule secreted by astrocytes that forms a template for neuroblastic migration and axonal fascicles and creates perineural nets. We studied KS immunoreactivity in cerebellar cortex, deep cerebellar, inferior olivary, red and pontine nuclei, and white matter of 25 control human fetuses 12-41 weeks gestation and 16 cerebellar dysgeneses. Dentate, inferior olivary, and red nuclei were nonreactive at all ages. Pontine nuclei were positive from the early second trimester. Bergmann glia and cerebellar white matter pathways were nonreactive throughout fetal and postnatal life. Transitory KS septa demarcated the vermal/hemispheric boundary. KS was not expressed in Dandy-Walker or Chiari malformations, cerebellar hypoplasia, heterotopia, pontocerebellar hypoplasia, or rhombencephalosynapsis. Axonal fascicles caudal to the internal capsule did not exhibit KS. The absence of hindbrain KS contrasts with strong forebrain immunoreactivity. Lack of KS expression in typically developing cerebellum and associated brainstem nuclei (except pontine), or in dysgeneses, implies that KS does not contribute to cerebellar system malformation pathogenesis. Transitory KS septa define early vermal margins similar to neuromeric segmentation septa. The intense KS template of the internal capsule does not extend caudally into brainstem fascicles.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究通过免疫组化观察了25例妊娠12至41周人类胎儿及16例小脑发育异常标本中小脑系统与轴突束的硫酸角质素蛋白聚糖表达。结果显示，齿状核、下橄榄核和红核在各时期均不表达，小脑皮质、Bergmann胶质细胞及小脑白质通路也始终阴性，仅脑桥核自妊娠早期第二 trimester 起呈阳性，暂时性中隔则标记蚓部与半球边界。作者据此认为，KS在正常发育的小脑及相关脑干核团（脑桥核除外）和各类小脑发育异常中均缺乏表达，提示其不参与小脑系统畸形的发病；内囊处强阳性模板也未向尾侧延伸至脑干轴突束。

papers.title: Maternal lifestyle risk factors and human embryonic morphologic development using 3D ultrasound: a population-based prospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Graafland N, Posthumus AG, Mulders AGMGJ, Gaillard R, Koning AHJ, Jaddoe VWV, Steegers EAP, Rousian M.
papers.abstract: Study question Are periconception maternal modifiable lifestyle factors (i.e. smoking, alcohol consumption, caffeine intake, folic acid supplement use, and physical activity) associated with embryonic morphologic development and growth in a large population-based cohort study? Summary answer Inadequate folic acid supplement use and insufficient serum folate levels were associated with delayed embryonic morphologic development and reduced growth, while no associations were observed for smoking, alcohol, caffeine intake, or physical activity. What is known already Modifiable maternal lifestyle factors during the periconception period may influence embryonic growth and development. Prior studies suggest associations between smoking, folic acid use, and first trimester growth, but evidence on morphologic development remains limited. Study design, size, duration This study was embedded in the Generation R Next Study, a population-based periconception cohort in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, conducted between 2017 and 2021. Of the 2173 included spontaneous singleton pregnancies, 993 had reliable pregnancy dating, 3D ultrasound data up to 10 + 2 weeks of gestation, and available information on periconception lifestyle risk factors. Participants/materials, setting, methods Embryonic development and growth were assessed in vivo at 7 and 9 weeks of gestation using 3D transvaginal ultrasound and virtual reality techniques. Morphologic development was determined using the Carnegie staging system based on limb position, embryonic curvature, and brain morphology; crown-rump length (CRL) was used to assess growth. Periconception lifestyle factors, including smoking, alcohol and caffeine intake, physical activity, and folic acid supplement use, were assessed using early pregnancy questionnaires. Linear mixed models were used to examine the association between lifestyle factors and embryonic Carnegie stages and CRL. Analyses were adjusted for gestational age at ultrasound, maternal age, ethnicity, education level, parity, fetal sex, and the other lifestyle factors. Main results and the role of chance Inadequate folic acid supplement use was associated with a 0.51-day delay in embryonic development and a 0.72-mm reduction in CRL (-1.6%) at 10 + 2 weeks of gestation. Insufficient serum folate levels (<25.5 nmol/l) were associated with a 1.01-day developmental delay and a 1.24-mm reduction in CRL (-3.7%). No significant associations were observed for smoking, alcohol or caffeine intake, or physical activity. Results remained robust after adjustment for confounders. Limitations, reasons for caution Lifestyle exposures were self-reported, which may have introduced recall or social desirability bias. Gestational age determination was based on the last menstrual period, which can result in dating discrepancies due to variability in cycle length or inaccurate recall, but strict inclusion criteria were applied to minimize misclassification. The relatively healthy study population could limit the generalizability of our results to higher-risk groups. Wider implications of the findings Our findings emphasize the importance of initiating folic acid supplementation in the preconception period to ensure sufficient maternal folate levels, which may support optimal embryonic morphologic development and growth during the first trimester. These results reinforce public health recommendations advocating timely folic acid supplementation to promote healthy early embryonic development. Study funding/competing interest(s) The Generation R Next Study is financially supported by the Erasmus University Medical Centre Rotterdam, the Erasmus University Rotterdam, and the Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development. R.G. received funding from the Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development (NWO, ZonMw VIDI 09150172110034, and NWO, ZonMW, grant number 05430052110007) and an European Research Council Starting Grant (ERC-2024-STG 101161004). V.W.V.J. received a grant from the Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development (NWO, ZonMw 05430052110007) and a European Research Council Consolidator Grant (ERC-2014-CoG-648916). The authors declare no conflicts of interest. Trial registration number N/A.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究基于荷兰一项人群前瞻性队列，纳入自然单胎妊娠，在孕7周和9周用三维阴道超声结合虚拟现实技术评估胚胎形态发育（Carnegie分期）和头臀长，并考察孕前母亲吸烟、饮酒、咖啡因摄入、体力活动及叶酸补充等可改变生活方式因素与胚胎发育的关联。结果显示，叶酸补充不足与胚胎形态发育延迟和生长减小相关，血清叶酸水平不足者延迟和减小更明显；而吸烟、饮酒、咖啡因摄入和体力活动未见显著关联。作者据此强调孕前及时补充叶酸、维持充足叶酸水平对早期胚胎发育的意义，但生活方式为自报、人群相对健康，结果外推需谨慎。

papers.title: Lateralized Gene Splicing in the Brain is Associated With Lateralized Feeding Behavior in an Asymmetrical Scale-eating Cichlid Fish.
papers.authors: Tian X, Meyer A.
papers.abstract: Lateralized behavior ("handedness") is a trait observed across all vertebrates, including humans. As an adaptive trait involved in both intraspecific and interspecific interactions, it holds broad evolutionary significance. However, the molecular basis of its brain regulation-particularly post-transcriptional regulation-remains poorly understood. Perissodus microlepis, a textbook example in evolutionary biology and an endemic scale-eating cichlid fish from Lake Tanganyika, displays pronounced lateralized feeding behavior that is complemented by its asymmetric head, by which it bites the scales preferentially from only one side or the other side of its prey. Based on data from two previous studies, we investigated the patterns of alternative splicing-an important yet understudied regulatory mechanism-across multiple brain regions in both resting and predatory states of L-eft or the R-ight morphs of this species. We found that the telencephalon, the cognitive center of the vertebrate brain, shows enrichment in functions related to microtubule and neural development in both states. Compared to the resting state, brain regions in the predatory state exhibited more consistent functional profiles, exhibiting pronounced enrichment in the nervous system. We identified several genes whose proportion of alternatively spliced transcripts was strongly correlated with behavioral laterality, establishing a potentially causal link between alternative splicing and handedness. Our findings underscore the significant role of alternative splicing in important adaptive traits, such as lateralized behavior and present a set of candidate genes for further investigation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究以具有明显偏侧取食行为的坦噶尼喀湖鳞食性慈鲷为对象，基于既往两项研究的数据，分析左右型个体在静息与捕食状态下多个脑区的可变剪接模式，以探讨行为偏侧化的转录后调控基础。结果显示，端脑在两种状态下均富集微管和神经发育相关功能，捕食状态下各脑区的功能谱更为一致并明显富集于神经系统；若干基因的可变剪接转录本比例与行为偏侧性高度相关。作者据此提出可变剪接与“利手”之间可能存在因果联系，并给出待进一步验证的候选基因，但相关证据尚不能确立因果关系。

papers.title: Brain structure links extraversion to shyness in late adolescence.
papers.authors: Yu Y, Liu W, Wang S.
papers.abstract: Shyness is a prevalent psychological construct that can lead to psychopathology and negative developmental outcomes, yet its neurostructural substrates remain poorly understood, particularly during adolescence-a critical period for social and emotional development. This study examined the brain gray matter volume correlates of shyness and the potential mediating role of basic personality traits in 228 normal adolescents (aged 16-20 years). Participants underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging and completed the Cheek and Buss Shyness Scale and NEO Five-Factor Inventory. Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and cross-validation prediction analyses revealed a positive association between shyness and gray matter volume in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, a key region implicated in cognitive control and emotion regulation. Among the Big Five traits, only extraversion correlated with right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex gray matter volume and showed a significant indirect association with the gray matter volume-shyness link. Specifically, higher right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex gray matter volume was associated with lower extraversion, which in turn was associated with greater shyness; this indirect association was partial and remained significant after controlling for other personality traits. These results highlight the importance of integrating neural and personality factors in understanding shyness during this critical developmental period and offer potential targets for early identification and intervention.

papers.title: Sleep after motor learning enhances post-movement beta synchronization.
papers.authors: Bernier MF, Hoyer RS, Lecaignard F, Nicolas A, Bertrand O, Albouy P, Albouy G.
papers.abstract: The neural substrates supporting the beneficial effect of sleep on motor memory consolidation are well described. However, less is known about brain oscillatory dynamics underlying these processes. We characterized the oscillatory dynamics associated with motor sequence learning and their modulation by post-learning sleep using magnetoencephalography (MEG) in young healthy adults. After learning a motor sequence task while their brain activity was recorded with MEG, participants were distributed in two groups according to whether they slept or were totally sleep deprived during the first post-training night. Consolidation was assessed with a retest in the MEG three days later. Behaviorally, performance improved over the consolidation interval irrespective of whether sleep was afforded during the first night. MEG results showed that initial motor sequence learning was characterized by a decrease in beta event-related desynchronization (ERD, 18 to 25 Hz) over bilateral motor areas from early to late training. Interestingly, while practice-related modulations of beta ERD were not influenced by the sleep status, post-learned-movement beta event-related synchronization (ERS) over bilateral parietal areas increased over the consolidation interval in the sleep, compared to the sleep deprived, group. These results extend current models of motor memory consolidation by identifying ERS as an oscillatory marker of sleep-dependent consolidation.

papers.title: Global feature-based suppression without local target competition.
papers.authors: Christopher G, Matthias M M.
papers.abstract: Feature-based attention (FBA) enables the prioritization of behaviorally relevant stimulus features across the visual field by enhancing processing of attended and suppressing unattended information. While global amplification of attended features is well established, it remains unclear whether suppression of unattended features reflects a global mechanism or depends on local spatial competition with attended stimuli. Here, we tested whether suppression of unattended colors requires direct local competition with the attended color. Participants performed a feature-based attentional shifting task while viewing centrally task-relevant and peripherally task-irrelevant, frequency-tagged random-dot kinematograms. By systematically varying the combination of attended and unattended colors in the periphery, we isolated the conditions under which suppression emerges. Steady-state visual evoked potentials were used to track neural modulations in early sensory processing. As expected, cueing a particular color led to robust global amplification of the attended color. Critically, unattended colors were suppressed globally irrespective of whether they were presented together with the attended color. These findings demonstrate that suppression of unattended features does not require direct competition with the attended feature. FBA operates via global allocation of attentional resources that enhances attended features while suppressing non-attended features, consistent with accounts combining feature-similarity gain and biased competition.

papers.title: Dissociable contributions of cortical thickness and surface area to cognitive aging: evidence from multiple longitudinal cohorts.
papers.authors: Demetriou I, Correia M, Vidal-Piñeiro D, Fisher SE, Eising E, Escott-Price V, Bracher-Smith M, Apšvalka D, Attaheri A, Emery T, Henson RN.
papers.abstract: Cortical volume, a widely-used marker of brain aging, is the product of two genetically and developmentally dissociable morphometric features: thickness and area. However, it remains unclear whether these two features have dissociable consequences for cognitive aging. To address this, we analyze cross-sectional and longitudinal neuroimaging and cognitive data from one discovery cohort (Cam-CAN) and two independent, pre-registered replication cohorts (OASIS-3 and HABS-HD), leveraging wide age ranges across adulthood, different follow-up intervals and diverse population backgrounds. We show that thickness declines more steeply with age than does area, and shows stronger associations with longitudinal change in fluid cognitive abilities, fairly uniformly across the cortex. Cognitive change is also dependent on baseline thickness, independent of thickness change and independent of baseline cognitive ability. In contrast, area is comparatively stable across adulthood, at least until old age, and shows weaker and more heterogeneous associations with cognitive change. Together, these findings help to reconcile inconsistencies in the literature, and indicate that thickness provides a more sensitive marker of dynamic neurobiological processes underlying cognitive aging, whereas area seems to reflect primarily stable, trait-like variation in cognitive ability.

papers.title: Reaping what you grow: rethinking apoptosis in cortical folding.
papers.authors: Barresi M, Tolcos M.
papers.abstract: Cortical folding is a defining feature of mammalian brain evolution widely attributed to spatially patterned cell proliferation, neuronal differentiation, and migration that drive regional expansion of the cerebral cortex. Growth-centric models have dominated theories of gyrification for decades; however, cortical morphogenesis is not governed by expansion alone. In this hypothesis-driven review, we reconceptualize cell death as a potential driver of cortical folding. We synthesize evidence indicating that apoptosis is spatiotemporally regulated during healthy brain development, influences cortical size and structure when perturbed, and functions differently in cell type- and layer-specific contexts. Apoptosis has been largely overlooked as an instructive contributor to gyral and sulcal formation. We explore the possibility that spatially patterned apoptosis may directly modulate cell density, radial units, and cortical topology, acting in concert with, rather than a consequence of, proliferation and migration to sculpt the developing brain. We propose that this is a substantial area of investigation given the limited data on spatially patterned apoptosis and gyrification and the evidence that would be required to substantiate this hypothesis. Recognizing the potential for apoptosis as a candidate driver of gyrification expands current developmental models and provides a new testable framework for interpreting both evolutionary cortical expansion and malformations.

papers.title: Laplace-based cortical thickness without volumetric discretisation.
papers.authors: Snell A, Reutens D, Du J, Vegh V.
papers.abstract: Laplace-based methods define cortical thickness as the length of a streamline connecting the pial and white surfaces, but existing implementations discretize the volume and lose accuracy in tight folds. Surface-based methods use Euclidean inter-surface distances that cannot enforce orthogonal, non-crossing correspondences. We solve Laplace's equation on the cortical surface itself using a boundary element method, with pial and white surfaces as Dirichlet boundaries and the surrounding edge Neumann boundaries; thickness is the length of a streamline traced along the analytic gradient field. We tested 8044 streamlines across analytical shapes, synthetic gyral patches, and real cortices; reciprocal paths returned within 0.05 mm of their origin, with 95th-percentile asymmetry below 0.68%. On folded patches with known ground truth, length-normalized bias was 0.0003 mm/mm independent of curvature. Streamline validity remained near-complete above a mean triangle shape quality of 0.90 and degraded sharply below 0.80, defining a practical mesh threshold. In three focal cortical dysplasia patients, each imaged at 3 T and 7 T, the method resolved focal thickening at the lesion site, with contralateral cortex mapped alongside as a visual reference. Vertex-wise comparison against FreeSurfer on identical surfaces showed differences scaling with local curvature. The observed bias is over an order of magnitude below preclinical Alzheimer's thinning rates.

papers.title: The functional lateralization of white matter with sex differences.
papers.authors: Cai ZY, Hu K, Linli ZQ.
papers.abstract: Numerous studies indicate that the brain demonstrates functional lateralization with distinct patterns between males and females, but they primarily have focused on gray matter, with only a handful considering white matter (WM) and sex differences. Utilizing rs-fMRI from the Southwest University Longitudinal Imaging Multimodal (SLIM) dataset, we quantified lateralization of WM as the difference in each region's synchronization with the left versus right hemisphere, and examined its temporal fluctuations and sex differences. Then, the Louvain community detection algorithm clustered lateralization patterns, and sex differences within each cluster were analyzed. We established the functional connectivity network, assessed its properties, and utilized correlation analysis to examine the relationship between lateralization and network. Our analyses revealed that WM demonstrated a left-lateralized trend in the left hemisphere and a right-lateralized trend in the right hemisphere. Moreover, functional lateralization was more pronounced in males than females. We also categorized the regions into three spatial clusters, revealing sex differences in the lateralization patterns within each cluster. Additionally, lateralization patterns are intricately associated with the functional connectivity network. These findings provide insights into functional lateralization and sex differences, and may inform future investigations of the neural mechanisms associated with functional specialization, cognition, behavior, and neurological disorders.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注白质的功能偏侧化及其性别差异，利用静息态功能磁共振数据，以各脑区与左右半球同步性的差异来量化白质偏侧化，并考察其时间波动。结果显示，白质在左半球呈左偏侧化趋势、右半球呈右偏侧化趋势，且男性的功能偏侧化比女性更明显；脑区可归为三个空间聚类，各聚类内的偏侧化模式也存在性别差异。偏侧化模式还与功能连接网络存在关联。这些发现提示白质功能组织同样具有偏侧化和性别差异，可为后续功能特化及相关神经机制研究提供参考，但摘要未涉及临床或因果层面的结论。

papers.title: Cortical folding and reduced connection distances in the human brain.
papers.authors: Rolls ET, Huang Y, Huang CC.
papers.abstract: Why do sulci occur in the human brain in particular parts of the cortical sheet? To obtain quantitative evidence on how folding may help to reduce the amount of white matter involved in connecting cortical regions, we measured the geodesic distance (GD) across the cortical white-matter surface, and the length of the connections and the number of streamlines (SN), between 180 cortical regions in the Human Connectome Project (HCP) Multimodal Parcellation atlas using diffusion tractography at 7 T in 178 HCP participants. For relatively long connections (GD >90 mm), we quantify how in many cases the connection distance is much shorter than the geodesic distance, with the presence of folding making this possible. We show how sulci can help to reduce the wiring cost defined as the length of the streamlines multiplied by the number of streamlines between all cortical regions. The wiring cost function may be minimized in evolution by utilizing factors such as the "tension" between cortical regions caused by the number of streamlines and the distance that could be saved arising from having sulci in particular locations in the cortical sheet. The cortical folding may also bring key hierarchically organized cortical processing streams closer together to minimize conduction time.

papers.title: Reduced social brain coupling to others' face threats in narcissism.
papers.authors: Piispanen M, Tuominen J, Wuolio M, Henttonen P, Harjunen VJ, Koskinen E, Krusemark E, Glerean E, Rinne P, Sams M, Peräkylä A, Salmi J.
papers.abstract: Although several studies have linked narcissism to reduced empathy, the neural mechanisms underlying narcissistic behavior in socially complex, naturalistic contexts remain poorly understood. This study investigated how grandiose narcissistic traits are associated with neural dynamics in empathy-related areas of the "social brain" when participants observed another person receiving face-threatening feedback. We hypothesized that individuals with high narcissistic traits would exhibit lower intersubject correlation (ISC), indicating less synchronized neural responses across participants, in the anterior insula (aINS), dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) in response to face threats directed at others. Participants with high (n = 28) and low (n = 30) scores in grandiose narcissism watched videos during functional magnetic resonance imaging in which another person received face-threatening feedback to a personal story. Consistent with our hypothesis, highly narcissistic individuals exhibited reduced ISC in the dlPFC and PCC. In aINS, the effect did not reach statistical significance. The present findings suggest that trait narcissism reduces convergence in empathic responses particularly in areas related to cognitive empathy when witnessing social threats targeted at others. These findings further indicate that ecologically relevant experimental designs may help clarify how personality traits are expressed in neural responses to socially meaningful events.

papers.title: Temporal brain dynamics and fluid reasoning after extreme prematurity.
papers.authors: Padilla N, Escrichs A, Del Agua E, Kringelbach M, Donaire A, Deco G, Åden U.
papers.abstract: Extremely preterm (EPT) birth (<28 weeks' gestation) disrupts brain maturation and increases later neurodevelopmental and mental health vulnerability. Temporal irreversibility quantifies directional brain dynamics, capturing the temporal organization of brain function. We examined whether EPT birth alters temporal irreversibility at 10 years and its association with cognition at 12 years. Resting-state functional MRI was acquired at 10 years of age in 33 children born EPT and 26 term-born controls. At 12 years of age, 29 children born EPT and 21 term-born controls underwent cognitive assessment using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fifth edition (WISC-V). Temporal irreversibility was quantified globally, across large-scale functional networks (visual, somatomotor, dorsal attention, salience, limbic, control, and default mode [DMN]), and at the node level using the INSIDEOUT framework. Children born EPT showed reduced temporal irreversibility globally and in higher-order association networks (control and DMN, P < 0.01; dorsal attention and salience, P < 0.05). Node-level analyses identified two association-network parcels that remained significant after false discovery rate correction (left precuneus and right dorsomedial frontal cortices). Within the EPT group, fluid reasoning was the only WISC-V domain significantly associated with temporal irreversibility, with higher global irreversibility associated with poorer fluid reasoning. These findings may inform future neurodevelopmental monitoring and intervention strategies after prematurity.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察极早产是否改变儿童大脑功能的时间不可逆性，以及这种改变与日后认知的关系。研究者对10岁儿童进行静息态功能磁共振扫描，并在12岁时评估认知，比较极早产儿童与足月出生儿童。结果发现，极早产儿童在全脑及控制网络、默认模式网络等高级联合网络中的时间不可逆性降低，部分联合网络脑区在多重比较校正后仍显著。在极早产组内，时间不可逆性仅与流体推理相关，且全脑不可逆性越高，流体推理表现越差。作者认为，这些发现或可为早产后的神经发育监测和干预提供参考，但关联性结果尚不能说明因果。

papers.title: Sleep neurophysiology as a biological correlate of infant temperament.
papers.authors: Reicher V, Markovic A, Beaugrand M, Mühlematter C, Schoch SF, Gácsi M, Kurth S.
papers.abstract: Temperament, characterized as individual differences in reactivity and self-regulation, influences our behavior in everyday situations. It is apparent as early as infancy and shaped by genetic and environmental factors. A neurophysiological marker of temperament has been quantified during the waking state; however, it remains unknown how these associations manifest in sleep. To address this gap, we assessed nighttime sleep in 29 6-month-old infants (Mage = 6.145 months, SD = 0.399, 48% males) using a portable high-density electroencephalography. Temperament was assessed using a parent-rated questionnaire, focusing on 2 scales: negative affectivity and orienting/regulatory capacity. The correlation analyses included: (i) frontal asymmetry and (ii) whole-brain, electrode-wise correlations with temperament. The predefined frontal asymmetry correlation revealed that increased left-hemispheric slow-wave activity (SWA) corresponded to higher orienting/regulatory capacity scores. The whole-brain correlation showed that higher theta power across an array of electrodes over the prefrontal regions was associated with decreased negative affectivity scores. Local sleep depth over frontal and temporal brain areas, as reflected by SWA asymmetry and theta power, serves as a marker of self-regulatory abilities and affective traits, which, in turn, reflect differences in temperament. Our findings reveal that sleep neurophysiology is a biological correlate of temperament during preverbal stages.

papers.title: Age-related differences in behavior-driven activity in LEC but not MEC.
papers.authors: Lister JP, Comrie AE, Barnes CA.
papers.abstract: The hippocampus integrates spatial information from medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) with non-spatial sensory information from lateral entorhinal cortex (LEC) to form episodic memories. While age-related memory dysfunction is linked to several changes in neuronal function within hippocampal subfields, the effects of aging on MEC and LEC cellular activity patterns are less well-characterized. Here, we investigated MEC and LEC population activity in adult versus aged rats by monitoring the expression of the immediate early gene Arc across two behavioral task sessions with olfactory stimuli separated by a rest period. Aging did not affect the percentage of activated neurons in MEC or their consistent Arc expression patterns across sessions, consistent with stably coding repeated spatial experiences. In contrast, fewer LEC neurons were activated during behavior in aged than adult rats, indicating a specific age-associated hypoactivity in LEC. Additionally, regardless of group, more LEC neurons were activated during the second session compared to the first, which may reflect temporally sensitive LEC neuronal activity increasingly engaged across episodes of experience. These results indicate that aging affects input to the hippocampus in a region-specific manner and are also consistent with observations that suggest that some LEC neurons may provide a temporal tag for episodic memories.

papers.title: Distinct electroencephalography alpha-band rhythms map macroscale brain gradients.
papers.authors: Gunko I, Doesburg SM, Medvedev G, Moiseev A, Vakorin VA.
papers.abstract: Brain gradients provide a low-dimensional framework for describing cortical organization, linking functional connectivity, anatomy, development, and transcriptional architecture. Whether this macroscale organization also structures fast electrophysiological dynamics remains less clear. Here we used the longstanding observation that alpha-band activity is not unitary, and that some individuals exhibit multiple alpha peaks, as an entry point for examining cortical gradients in resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). We analyzed source-reconstructed EEG from 608 adults, comprising 3,255 recordings acquired across eyes-open and eyes-closed rest before and after cognitive testing. Within individuals, parcel-wise alpha peak frequencies frequently departed from unimodality, revealing 2 separable alpha-frequency components in 38.3% of recordings. These components were not spatially arbitrary: frequency-defined clusters aligned with canonical functional networks, most prominently separating visual and somatomotor systems, although their relative frequency ordering varied across individuals. Low-dimensional analysis of cluster network composition further identified 2 principal axes: a sensory-differentiation axis contrasting visual and somatomotor contributions, and a sensorimotor-association axis resembling established functional-connectomic gradients. These findings suggest that split alpha reflects multiple sensory-anchored oscillatory modes embedded within macroscale cortical gradients, linking a classical EEG phenomenon to the brain's hierarchical architecture.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究以静息态脑电中部分个体存在多个α峰这一现象为切入点，用源重建脑电数据考察宏观皮层梯度是否也组织快速电生理动态。作者发现，个体内许多脑区的α峰频率偏离单峰分布，相当一部分记录可分出两个可分离的α频率成分；这些成分并非空间随机分布，而是与经典功能网络对齐，最突出地分离视觉与躯体运动系统，但其相对频率顺序因人而异。进一步的低维分析识别出感觉分化轴和感觉运动—联合轴两条主轴，后者类似已有的功能连接组梯度。作者据此提出，分裂的α反映嵌入宏观皮层梯度中的多个感觉锚定振荡模式，从而把这一经典脑电现象与脑的层级组织联系起来。

papers.title: Altered connectivity and network efficiency in preterm infants.
papers.authors: Stemberger K, Lasić D, Pecco N, Canini M, Grizelj R, Ćaleta T, Judaš M, Kostović I, Radoš M, Ozretić D, Božek J, Lennartsson F, Della Rosa PA, Radoš M.
papers.abstract: Preterm birth is associated with altered maturation of large-scale functional brain networks during the neonatal period. Acquisition and preprocessing variability across neonatal resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) studies limits cross-site comparability and may obscure prematurity-related alterations. We combined rs-fMRI data from 90 local preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age (TEA) with data from 160 infants in the Developing Human Connectome Project (100 term-born and 60 preterm) to evaluate cross-site harmonization and characterize edge-wise functional connectivity and network efficiency. Data were preprocessed using an identical pipeline in SPM and CONN toolbox, harmonized with neuroCombat, and analyzed using per-edge analysis of covariance for connectivity and linear mixed-effects models for graph efficiency. Harmonization substantially reduced site-related variance and improved cross-site comparability. Relative to term-born controls, preterm infants showed widespread edge-wise hypoconnectivity, with only limited focal hyperconnectivity. Graph-theoretical analysis revealed reduced local alongside modestly increased global network efficiency in preterm infants, whereas regional connection-class composition did not interact with group. These findings support the feasibility of harmonizing multi-site neonatal rs-fMRI data and suggest that prematurity at TEA is characterized by widespread functional hypoconnectivity and a shift in the balance between local network segregation and large-scale functional integration.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注早产儿在足月等效年龄时大规模功能脑网络的成熟改变，并尝试解决多中心新生儿静息态fMRI数据可比性差的问题。作者将本地早产儿数据与公开数据集中的足月儿和早产儿数据合并，采用统一流程预处理并以神经ComBat进行跨站点协调，再分析逐边功能连接和网络效率。结果显示，协调显著降低了站点相关方差、改善了跨站点可比性；与足月儿相比，早产儿表现为广泛的逐边低连接，仅见有限的局灶性高连接，同时局部网络效率降低而全局网络效率略有升高。作者据此认为，足月等效年龄的早产儿以广泛功能低连接以及局部分离与大规模整合之间平衡的偏移为特征，并提示多站点新生儿数据协调具有可行性。

papers.title: Lower engagement of cognitive control in children on ChatGPT.
papers.authors: Horowitz-Kraus T, Kenett YN, Link-Sourani D, Ashqar E, Farah R.
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can scaffold idea generation, but how it engages control, attention, and memory systems in the developing versus mature brain, and how this relates to creativity, remains unclear. We compared 6-7-yr-old children and adults during a naturalistic 5-min co-creative dialog with ChatGPT using the same prompt, in-scanner conversation, undergoing functional magnetic resonance imaging scanning and their dialogs were recorded. Functional connectivity was computed within and between seven large-scale networks: cingulo-opercular, default mode, memory retrieval, frontoparietal (FP), salience, ventral attention, and dorsal attention (DAN). Creativity scores, assessed outside of the scanner, did not differ between groups. Adults showed stronger within-network connectivity in control/attention systems, most robustly in FP, with additional effects in salience and DAN. Adults also exhibited greater cross-network integration, particularly FP-salience and FP-DAN couplings, alongside broader adult-greater effects among memory- and attention-related pairs. During a co-creative AI-assisted conversation, children exhibit a less coherent and integrated control-attention-memory architecture than adults. The combination of similar creativity scores with divergent neural profiles suggests that developmental differences in the implementation of creative cognition may be more pronounced than baseline capacity. This highlights FP-centric pathways and their salience-gated interactions as candidate substrates by which creativity supports goal-directed co-creative dialog with AI.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究比较6至7岁儿童与成人在与ChatGPT进行同一提示的自然对话共创作时的脑功能连接，并结合扫描外评估的创造力表现。结果显示，两组创造力得分相近，但成人在控制与注意系统内的连接更强，尤其在前额顶网络，且跨网络整合更明显；儿童的控制—注意—记忆架构则相对不够连贯和整合。作者据此认为，创造性认知在发育中的实现方式差异可能比基线能力差异更突出，并提示前额顶相关通路及其与凸显网络的交互可能是支持目标导向AI共创作的候选神经基础。

papers.title: Gratitude mediates the link of precuneus volume to depression in older women.
papers.authors: Jiang J, Qiu H, Suo X, Liu J, Gao J, Wu D, Wang S.
papers.abstract: Depression in older people is a major contributor to global disease burden and functional impairment. While trait gratitude, a stable tendency to appreciate others' help, has been shown to alleviate depressive symptoms across populations, less is known about its neuroanatomical substrates and protective neuropsychological mechanisms against depression symptoms in aging populations. Here, we investigated the structural neural correlates of trait gratitude in 120 community-dwelling older women using voxel-based morphometry analysis of T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data. First, the whole-brain correlation analysis identified a negative association between trait gratitude and regional gray matter volume (GMV) in the right precuneus. Mediation analyses further suggested that trait gratitude could mediate the impact of regional GMV in right precuneus on depression symptoms. Critically, supplemental analyses showed that the results persisted even after controlling for anxiety and stress symptoms, as well as general personality traits. Our study presents novel evidence for the neuroanatomical basis of trait gratitude in general older women and highlights a brain-personality-symptom pathway for protecting against depression in which GMV affects depressive symptoms via trait gratitude. These findings deepen understanding of gratitude's protective role in late-life mental health while highlighting potential neurostructural markers for resilience against depression.

papers.title: Linked multimodal brain alterations in depression with suicidal risk.
papers.authors: Wang M, Yan Y, Tao Y, Amos TJ, Wei J, Zhao L, Ni R, Yang X, Ma X.
papers.abstract: Suicidal ideation and behavior (SIB) represent a major clinical challenge in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet the multimodal brain structural signatures associated with SIB and their relationships with cognitive dysfunction remain poorly understood. We acquired multimodal neuroimaging measures, including gray matter volume, cortical thickness, pial area (PA), white matter fractional anisotropy, together with neurocognitive measures from 61 MDD patients with SIB (MDD-SIB), 38 without SIB (MDD-nSIB), and 142 healthy controls (HC). Linked independent component analysis (LICA) was used to identify covarying multimodal structural brain patterns, followed by group comparisons and exploratory association analyses. LICA identified distinct multimodal structural patterns related to SIB status, with IC1, IC9, and IC14 differing between MDD-SIB and HC, and IC12 between MDD-SIB and MDD-nSIB. Spatial working memory (SWM), visual memory, sustained attention, and cognitive flexibility also differed significantly across groups, with the MDD-SIB group showing poorer performance across these cognitive domains. Within the MDD-SIB group, IC1, a fronto-temporal-cingulate structural covariance pattern characterized predominantly by PA alterations, was associated with both SWM strategy performance and depressive symptom severity. These findings identify distributed multimodal structural signatures associated with SIB in MDD and highlight a fronto-temporal-cingulate neural correlate linking cognitive dysfunction with depressive symptom severity.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注伴自杀意念与行为的重性抑郁障碍患者是否存在多模态脑结构改变，以及这些改变与认知功能的关系。作者采集了伴自杀风险、不伴自杀风险的患者及健康对照的灰质体积、皮层厚度、软膜面积、白质各向异性和神经认知数据，用关联独立成分分析提取共变的多模态结构模式。结果发现若干结构模式在伴自杀风险患者与健康对照之间、以及伴与不伴自杀风险患者之间存在差异，伴自杀风险者在空间工作记忆、视觉记忆、持续注意和认知灵活性上表现更差。在伴自杀风险组内，一个以软膜面积改变为主、涉及额颞扣带的结构协变模式与空间工作记忆策略表现和抑郁症状严重程度相关，提示这一神经相关物可能连接认知功能障碍与症状严重程度。上述关联为探索性结果，尚不能说明因果关系。

papers.title: Neural signatures of serial order access in verbal working memory.
papers.authors: Cristoforetti G, Xu Y, Viganò S, van Dijck JP, Bottini R, Fias W.
papers.abstract: Serial order working memory allows information to be maintained as structured sequences, yet the neural formats supporting access to serial position remain unclear. Behavioral evidence suggests that temporal order can be recoded into spatial representations, but serial order may also rely on representations that generalize beyond the spatial configuration of encoding. Here, participants memorized digit sequences presented either left-to-right or right-to-left, thereby reversing the mapping between ordinal position and external space while keeping retrieval cues centrally presented during fMRI. Behaviorally, spatial coding during retrieval was modulated by encoding direction. Multivoxel pattern analysis revealed direction-specific decoding in lateral parietal cortex: left inferior parietal cortex encoded serial position after left-to-right encoding, whereas right inferior parietal cortex did so after right-to-left encoding. In contrast, cross-direction decoding revealed direction-invariant effects in left supramarginal and precentral regions, suggesting serial-position information that generalized across spatial layouts. Finally, univariate parametric modulation revealed activity scaling with serial position in bilateral posterior parietal cortex, left anterior hippocampus, and action-control regions. Together, these findings indicate that serial order access in working memory relies on multiple neural signatures, including spatially context-dependent representations, direction-invariant ordinal codes, and graded process-related activity.

papers.title: EEG reflects subjective but not behavioral hearing in noise performance.
papers.authors: Liu J, Stohl J, Overath T.
papers.abstract: Ever since the first description of the "cocktail party problem" in 1953, much effort and progress have been devoted to understanding the factors that contribute to hearing difficulties in noise. Hearing difficulties in noise are multifold, and as such have been assessed using a range of objective and subjective measures. Here, we explored three distinct measures of hearing in noise: tone-in-noise (TIN) detection, speech reception threshold (SRT) in noise, and the self-reported Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ). We evaluated how these measures relate to auditory brainstem response, cortical electroencephalogram (EEG), behavioral (e.g., frequency modulation, FM detection), and self-reported factors. FM detection threshold emerged as a common factor across the predictive models for TIN, SRT, and SSQ, consistent with the possibility that temporal fine structure sensitivity is broadly related to different aspects of hearing in noise. In contrast, EEG P3 amplitude was only retained in the SSQ model and not in the TIN or SRT models, suggesting that cortical EEG measures may be more closely related to subjective than objective hearing in noise outcomes. Together, these findings suggest that different measures of hearing in noise capture partially distinct aspects of auditory function.

papers.title: Global organization of structural covariance networks derived from parcellated cortical surface area in atypical populations.
papers.authors: Roseby W, Racey C, Ward J.
papers.abstract: Higher-order features of brain organization are powerful measures for understanding the relationship between brain and experience. In particular, the global arrangement of structural features of the cortex provides insight into neurodevelopmental processes that underlie individual differences in perception and cognition. Structural covariance networks (SCNs), which capture regional coordination of brain morphometry, are an efficient method to derive global cortical properties. However, their interpretation relies on an array of methodological choices that are often inconsistent between studies. Using a hierarchically clustered version of the Human Connectome Project (HCP) atlas, we constructed SCNs of regional cortical surface area for groups with four different conditions-synesthesia, autism, early psychosis, and anxiety or depression-and compared global network properties with those of age- and sex-matched controls. SCNs for synesthesia and autism showed globally stronger connectivity, with specific increases at moderate cortical distances, as well as lower network complexity. Conversely, the SCN for early psychosis showed a globally lower connectivity and a greater complexity, while depression and anxiety showed few differences compared with controls. The results for autism and depression were replicated across two datasets each. These findings support the notion that synesthesia and autism share neurodevelopmental mechanisms, while psychosis may involve a diverging process.

papers.title: Cortico-striatal network architecture shapes rhythmic biases in music.
papers.authors: Lumaca M, van der Werff J, Keller PE, Kotz SA, Baggio G, Rosso M, Kakihara M, Martin M, Vuust P, Ravignani A.
papers.abstract: Why is human music rhythmically structured the way it is? One hypothesis is that the human brain is intrinsically wired to favor specific rhythmic organizations. To test this, we collected diffusion and resting-state functional MRI (fMRI) data from musically untrained participants and, weeks later, asked them to imitate randomly generated drumming sequences using finger taps. These imitations exhibited systematic biases toward temporal structures widespread in human music: predictable patterns characterized by isochronous organization (1:1) and other small integer ratios (2:1 and 3:1). Functional connectome analyses linked the increased rhythmic predictability of reproduced rhythms to intrinsic interactions between networks implicated in auditory timing (auditory basal ganglia) and executive control (task-positive and task-negative networks). Notably, the tendency toward isochrony-a feature highly conserved across species-was selectively associated with increased fiber density within a cortico-basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical network previously implicated in the perception and production of a metronomic pulse from music (the "beat"). Our findings reveal how stable neural architecture predisposes humans to produce rhythmically structured patterns. This evidence links intrinsic brain circuitry to individual cultural expressions, supporting the account of human symbolic systems, including music, as biocultural hybrids.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察人脑内在连接结构是否使人在无音乐训练背景下更倾向于产生特定节奏组织。研究者采集无音乐训练参与者的弥散与静息态功能磁共振数据，数周后让其用手指敲击模仿随机生成的鼓点序列，发现模仿普遍偏向等时组织和2:1、3:1等小整数比这类人类音乐中常见的时间结构。功能连接分析显示，节奏可预测性提高与听觉计时相关网络和执行控制网络之间的内在交互有关，而偏向等时性则选择性关联于皮层-基底节-丘脑-皮层环路内更高的纤维密度。作者据此认为，稳定的神经架构可能预先塑造了人产生有节奏结构模式的倾向，并将内在脑回路与个体文化表达联系起来，支持音乐等人类符号系统是生物与文化混合产物的观点。

papers.title: Multi-molecular adaptations of long-term opioid use in chronic pain.
papers.authors: Baliki MN, Vigotsky AD, Rached G, Jabakhanji R, Huang L, Branco P, Barroso J, Cong O, Centeno M, Cermak S, Griffith J, Wasan AD, Schnitzer TJ, Apkarian AV.
papers.abstract: Millions of chronic pain patients are managed with opioids, yet the neuropsychological implications of stable long-term daily opioid consumption remain unknown. Here, we contrasted the psychosocial profiles and brain structure and function of 70 chronic back pain patients prescribed opioids (CBP+O, average current daily opioid exposure of 7.8 years) with tightly matched 70 opioid-naïve patients (CBP-O) and 30 healthy subjects. Despite CBP+O exhibiting only modestly worse psychosocial profiles and small differences in brain morphology relative to CBP-O, CBP+O showed stark differences in brain activity (ALFF). A large portion (38% of the variance) of this pattern was captured by a model using 19 receptor/transporter distributions. The patients' (across all 140 CBP) psychosocial profiles were summarized by three principal components (PCs, explaining 70% of variance): functional disability, pain quality, and negative affect. These PCs were respectively associated with serotonergic (5HT1a and 5HT6) and opioidergic (mu-opioid receptor, MOR) receptor-related activities. In additional analyses and new data, 5HT1a- and MOR-related activities tracked opioid dose, abstinence status, and tapering success, while 5HT6-related activity tracked pain intensity. Overall, our findings uncover molecularly defined brain circuits in opioid use and chronic pain.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注慢性疼痛患者长期稳定使用阿片类药物对心理社会和脑功能的影响，比较了长期用药的慢性背痛患者、未用过阿片类药物的匹配患者及健康对照的脑结构与功能。结果显示，长期用药患者心理社会状况仅略差、脑形态差异也较小，但脑活动模式差异明显，且该模式很大一部分可由多种受体与转运体分布解释；患者的心理社会特征可归纳为功能残疾、疼痛性质和负性情绪三个成分，并分别与血清素能和阿片受体相关活动有关。后续分析提示部分受体相关活动与用药剂量、戒断状态及减量成败相关，另一类则与疼痛强度相关，作者据此提出阿片使用与慢性疼痛中由分子特征界定的脑环路。

papers.title: Rethinking cortical hypertrophy in temporal lobe epilepsy.
papers.authors: Cossette-Roberge H, Nguyen BT, Fadaie F, Deacon C, Bernhardt BC, Schaper FLWVJ, Giampiccolo D, Larivière S.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is one of the most common chronic neurological disorders, and temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is its most prevalent form in adults. Although TLE is classified as a focal epilepsy, it has traditionally been defined by hippocampal and extra-hippocampal atrophy. However, several studies also report regions of increased cortical thickness, or cortical hypertrophy, in TLE, challenging the notion that structural change in epilepsy is unidirectional. In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence for cortical hypertrophy in TLE and place these findings in a broader neurobiological context. We provide an overview of cortical thickness and MRI approaches used to measure it, highlighting differences between surface-based, volume-based and voxel-based methods. We then review MRI studies reporting cortical hypertrophy in TLE, noting variability in affected regions, patient populations and analytical techniques. We discuss potential mechanisms that may underlie cortical hypertrophy, including seizure-related structural remodelling, glial or inflammatory processes, compensatory neuroplasticity, network effects and methodological limitations. Finally, we outline key gaps and controversies regarding the biological validity, temporal dynamics and clinical relevance of cortical hypertrophy in TLE. We conclude that consideration of both cortical atrophy and hypertrophy may improve broader understanding of TLE as a disorder involving brain remodelling rather than isolated regional atrophy.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述重新审视颞叶癫痫中常被忽视的皮质增厚现象。作者梳理了基于MRI的皮质厚度测量方法及其差异，并汇总报告颞叶癫痫患者存在皮质增厚的影像学研究，指出受累区域、患者群体和分析技术存在较大差异。文章进一步讨论增厚可能涉及的机制，包括癫痫相关的结构重塑、胶质或炎症过程、代偿性神经可塑性、网络效应以及方法学局限，并指出其在生物学有效性、时间动态和临床相关性方面仍存争议与空白。作者认为，同时关注皮质萎缩与增厚，有助于将颞叶癫痫理解为涉及全脑重塑的疾病，而非局限于区域性萎缩。

papers.title: The entropic brain today.
papers.authors: Carhart-Harris RL.
papers.abstract: Introduced in 2014 and revised in 2018, the entropic brain hypothesis has accrued a wealth of supportive evidence. The hypothesis states that-along a dimension of 'the size of phenomenal consciousness'-expansive states reliably exhibit increased brain entropy, whereas the inverse applies for states of no or reduced consciousness. Examples of expansive states include expert meditation, flicker-light stimulation, near-death-like experiences, atypical breathing, REM sleep, the pre-ictal aura, unmedicated early psychosis and psychedelic drug states. Examples of states of no or reduced consciousness with low brain entropy, include disorders of consciousness, deep sleep, the anaesthetized state, seizure, post-stroke, ageing, cognitive impairment and neurodegenerative illness. It is shown that the entropic brain has convergent, correlative, predictive, discriminative and external validity. Regarding its predictive validity, increased brain entropy under psilocybin (in a supportive context) predicts subsequent improvements in mental health (improved well-being 1-month post-dose). Regarding its discriminative validity, changes in brain entropy selectively index the 'breadth of subjective experience' versus alternative dimensions, such as arousal. Regarding portability/external validity, an entropy-related function is applied in generative artificial intelligence. In conclusion, the entropic brain is a useful model of conscious states.

papers.title: Clinical markers of disease progression in the prodromal to overt alpha-synucleinopathy continuum.
papers.authors: Roascio M, Antelmi E, Baldelli L, Biscarini F, Bonanni E, Brunetti V, Capriglia E, Geromino C, Casoni F, Cirillo F, Della Marca G, Di Laudo F, Ferini-Strambi L, Fernandes M, Figorilli M, Galbiati A, Gigli GL, Guarnieri B, Hoxhaj D, Lanza G, Liguori C, Maestri Tassoni M, Maio S, Malomo G, Marelli S, Mattioli P, Mulas M, Orso B, Pardini M, Plazzi G, Provini F, Pellitteri G, Puligheddu M, Terzaghi M, Pelletier A, Postuma RB, Arnulfo G, Arnaldi D, FARPRESTO consortium.
papers.abstract: Clinical progression from prodromal to overt stages of alpha-synucleinopathies is highly heterogeneous, and there is an urgent need for reliable clinical progression markers. Exploiting the Disease Course Mapping (DCM) model, we investigated how clinical signs evolve in patients with idiopathic/isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD), extracting clinical progression measures for use at the single-subject level. Furthermore, we correlated them with both established and innovative neurodegeneration biomarkers. We trained a DCM model using cognitive and motor scores of a longitudinal cohort of 766 patients with iRBD (166 female, 67.9 ± 7.4 years). We personalized the model by extracting three parameters to describe the single subject in comparison to the averaged population data. We tested the model on a blind set of 49 patients with iRBD (seven female, 68.5 ± 7.1 years) who underwent both longitudinal clinical evaluations and instrumental evaluation at the first observation. In the blind set, we correlated the individual model parameters with presynaptic dopaminergic impairment, an established biomarker of substantia nigra neurodegeneration, and cortical electrophysiological dysfunction-measured by high-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG)-an innovative neurodegeneration biomarker. We identified three individual clinical markers reflecting early/late (time-shift, τ) and fast/slow (acceleration factor, α) disease progression, as well as the individual clinical trajectory (i.e. earlier motor or cognitive impairment, intermarker spacing, ω). The individual model parameters are significantly associated with phenoconversion, with a 73% chance of distinguishing between clinically stable patients (non-converters) and those converting during the longitudinal observation to an overt alpha-synucleinopathy (converters). Motor scores progress 35% faster than cognitive scores in our iRBD cohort. Converter iRBD patients exhibited a faster and earlier disease progression than non-converters, and on average, they showed an earlier worsening of motor scores than cognitive scores, regardless of the clinical diagnosis of overt parkinsonism. Patients with iRBD who developed parkinsonism worsened earlier than those who developed dementia. At baseline, an earlier progression was related to presynaptic dopaminergic impairment and higher phase synchronization in the theta band (4-8 Hz). Higher synchronization in the theta band was also associated with an earlier worsening of motor scores than cognitive scores. In this study, we investigated a large longitudinal iRBD cohort, applying an advanced disease progression model. We found three individual clinical markers that were able to monitor disease progression and showed significant association with both established and innovative neurodegeneration biomarkers. We suggest that these clinical markers could be used as efficacy end points in disease-modifying clinical trials.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注特发性/孤立性快速眼动睡眠行为障碍（iRBD）向显性α-突触核蛋白病进展过程中，如何刻画个体化的临床进展。作者用患者的认知与运动评分训练疾病进程映射模型，并在独立样本中提取反映进展早晚、快慢及运动/认知损害先后顺序的个体化指标。这些指标与表型转化显著相关，能在一定程度上区分临床稳定者与转化者；转化者的进展更快、更早，且运动评分恶化通常早于认知评分，发展为帕金森病者又早于发展为痴呆者。基线时进展较早与突触前多巴胺能受损及θ波段同步性较高相关。作者据此提出，这些临床标志物有望作为疾病修饰试验的疗效终点，但尚需进一步验证。

papers.title: White matter lesions disrupt cholinergic pathways important for cognition in Parkinson's disease.
papers.authors: Carli G, Brown T, Michalakis F, Biddix A, Roytman S, Vangel R, Van Hout A, Kanel P, Scott PJH, Albin RL, Bohnen NI.
papers.abstract: White matter lesions are associated with cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease, but the underlying neurobiological mechanisms remain unclear. One hypothesis is that strategically located white matter lesions disrupt long-range white matter pathways crucial for cognitive functioning, particularly cholinergic projections from the basal forebrain, contributing to cognitive decline. Using volumetric measures of basal forebrain nuclei (T1 MRI proxy for brain cholinergic projection nuclei), quantitative white matter lesion assessments (fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI) and a presynaptic cholinergic marker (18F-FEOBV PET), we tested a mechanistic model of white matter lesion effects on basal forebrain cholinergic projections and nuclei, and how these disruptions relate to cognition. We analysed data from 127 mid-to-advanced-stage patients with Parkinson's disease without dementia. Periventricular and deep white matter lesion burdens were quantified with the UBO Detector pipeline. Cognitive function was assessed across five domains using z-scores from a control group matched for age and education. Voxel-wise analyses examined associations between white matter lesion burden and cholinergic synaptic density, followed by mediation analyses testing whether cholinergic alterations mediated the relationship between white matter lesions and cognition, while correcting for sex, levodopa equivalent dose and disease duration. Voxel-wise analyses revealed that higher periventricular lesions burden was associated with reduced 18F-FEOBV uptake in an insular-limbic-frontal-cingulum cluster, while deep lesions showed more topographically limited associations that disappeared after adjusting for periventricular burden. Periventricular lesions affected lateral and external Ch4 cholinergic projection pathways (81%-88% of patients), more frequently than deep white matter lesions (25%-47% of patients), except for the external capsule, which was equally affected by both. Cognitive performance (global cognition, memory, executive function and attention) was associated with both periventricular lesion burden and 18F-FEOBV uptake within the insular-limbic-frontal-cingulum cluster, as well as with basal forebrain volume. Mediation analyses indicated that periventricular lesions had a direct effect on cortical terminal integrity (18F-FEOBV) and an indirect, presumably retrograde degeneration effect via basal forebrain atrophy. The effect of periventricular lesions on insular-limbic-frontal-cingulum cholinergic terminal density was a strong mediator of the association between lesion burden and cognitive performance. A weaker mediation effect via the basal forebrain emerged for global cognition, whereas mediation was more robust for memory and executive functioning. Our findings indicate that periventricular white matter lesions contribute to cognitive vulnerability in Parkinson's disease without dementia through impacts on basal forebrain cholinergic projections. White matter lesion burden may represent a mechanistically meaningful biomarker for predicting cognitive trajectories and informing targeted interventions in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究在127名无痴呆的中晚期帕金森病患者中，结合脑室旁和深部白质病变的MRI定量评估、基底前脑核团体积测量及胆碱能突触密度PET成像，检验白质病变是否通过破坏基底前脑胆碱能投射影响认知。结果显示，脑室旁病变负担越重，岛叶-边缘-额叶-扣带回区域的胆碱能末梢密度越低，且脑室旁病变比深部病变更常累及外侧和外部Ch4胆碱能通路；该区域胆碱能末梢密度是病变负担与整体认知、记忆、执行功能和注意力关联的重要中介，基底前脑萎缩则构成一条较弱的间接通路。作者据此提出，脑室旁白质病变可能通过影响基底前脑胆碱能投射增加帕金森病患者的认知脆弱性，病变负担或可作为预测认知轨迹的候选生物标志物，但相关机制仍属模型推断，尚需进一步验证。

papers.title: Precision dynamics of predictive coding in functional neurological disorder.
papers.authors: Lyndon S.
papers.abstract: Functional neurological disorder (FND) presents disabling symptoms that fluctuate, migrate across systems and yet routinely show preserved structural integrity-features that can frustrate diagnosis and patient education. Crucially, these symptoms are genuine and reflect altered brain regulation across multiple systems rather than tissue damage or conscious control. This paper offers a clinically usable account of these puzzles by reframing FND as a disorder of precision control within predictive coding. The brain's confidence (precision) in its own predictions is modelled as a dynamic quantity that can surge with arousal, settle back towards baseline and slowly recalibrate over longer periods. Placing this mechanism in a four-level hierarchy (affective, interoceptive, proprioceptive, spinal) shows how arousal can temporarily make an unhelpful expectation dominate, suppress corrective feedback, and produce motor, sensory, cognitive or visceral symptoms-often in combination. The same dynamics explain rule-in positive signs such as distractibility, entrainment and give-way weakness, and clarify the lived experience of reduced agency without implying wilfulness or malingering. For clinicians, the framework provides an intuitive way to explain symptoms to patients ('a temporary gain miscalibration that overweights predictions and underweights sensory feedback'), and to justify why physiotherapy (amplifying proprioceptive feedback), psychotherapy (reducing arousal) and mindfulness or biofeedback (raising the effective threshold for arousal-driven 'gain spikes') can all help by recalibrating that weighting. The framework also yields concrete, falsifiable tests, linking bedside observation to measurable biomarkers and offering ways to refine it further. By centring dynamic precision, the account unifies diagnosis, communication and treatment planning, and provides a mechanistic foundation for precision-guided care in FND.

papers.title: The Wnt5a-PKCδ-GluA1 axis controls synapse-specific plasticity in HIV-1 gp120-induced pain pathogenesis.
papers.authors: Chen X, Spurgat M, Liu X, Maurelli M, Dibua A, Sha C, Wollmuth LP, Tang SJ.
papers.abstract: Imbalance of excitatory and inhibitory neuronal activity (E/I imbalance) plays a critical role in pain pathogenesis. Recent studies have identified a novel form of E/I imbalance in the spinal dorsal horn of animal models of HIV-associated pain, manifesting as increased spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic current (sEPSC) frequency in excitatory neurons alongside decreased sEPSC frequency in inhibitory neurons and hence termed neural circuitry polarization. However, how the opposite forms of synaptic plasticity in neural circuitry polarization are coordinated in the pain neural circuit is unclear. Here, we show that in the spinal dorsal horn of a mouse model of HIV-associated pain, potentiation of excitatory synapses on excitatory neurons (ESE) and depression of excitatory synapses on inhibitory neurons (ESI) employ distinct mechanisms to support their expression. We found the increase of sEPSC frequency in excitatory neurons induced by HIV-1 gp120 was mediated by a postsynaptic mechanism, whereas decrease of sEPSC frequency in inhibitory neurons was mediated by a presynaptic mechanism. Our studies showed that pharmacological inhibition of calcium-permeable AMPA (CP-AMPA) receptors selectively attenuated potentiation of ESE without significantly affecting ESI depression. We also observed that GluA1 was upregulated in excitatory but not inhibitory neurons, indicating selective CP-AMPA receptor formation in excitatory neurons. Furthermore, we identified a new pain-related signalling pathway in ESE: Wnt5a-PKCδ-GluA1. We elucidated that the GluA1 upregulation and ESE potentiation were controlled by neuronal Wnt5a signalling via protein kinase C delta (PKCδ). Our findings reveal that ESE and ESI in the spinal dorsal horn of HIV pain models use distinct synaptic and molecular mechanisms to support their expression in neural circuitry polarization, demonstrating specialized regulatory pathways for the plasticity of excitatory synapses targeting different neuron types during the pain pathogenesis.

papers.title: Hippocampal growth and function are reduced in the newborn following fetal growth restriction.
papers.authors: White TA, Camm EJ, Rock CR, Sutherland AE, Pham Y, Castillo-Melendez M, Dudink I, Ahmadzadeh E, Dean J, Palmer KR, Malhotra A, Guo T, Allison BJ, Miller SP, Miller SL.
papers.abstract: The rate of human brain growth is greatest in mid-to-late fetal gestation, corresponding to peak neuronal dendritogenesis. In pregnancies complicated by fetal growth restriction (FGR) caused by placental dysfunction, brain development is adversely impacted, with evidence of reduced total and hippocampal brain volume in childhood and cognitive deficits. The cellular basis for hippocampal maldevelopment and dysfunction in FGR is unknown. In this study we employed complementary preclinical and clinical investigations of hippocampal developmental trajectory in growth-restricted neonates to address this knowledge gap. In the preclinical study (FGR n = 18, control n = 19), FGR was induced in fetal sheep via surgical induction of placental insufficiency at 89 days' gestational age (dGA, term is 148 dGA), and after near-term birth (136 dGA), postnatal memory function was measured over 4 weeks. Neuronal dendritogenesis (dendrite length, branching, complexity) was assessed using Golgi-Cox staining of individual hippocampal cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) neurons at two neonatal time points, newborn age at 24 h after birth and 4 weeks of age, to compare the trajectory of hippocampal neuron development in FGR and control lambs. Results show that, in control lambs, total dendrite length and branching of CA1 hippocampal neurons significantly increased between newborn age and 4 weeks. In FGR lamb brains, neither dendrite length nor branching increased over this period, and dendrite deficits were worse in FGR lambs at 4 weeks, corresponding to reduced hippocampal area. In 4-week-old lambs, we observed a significant correlation between total dendrite length of CA1 neurons and memory function. Hippocampal growth trajectory and function deficits were corroborated in small-for-gestational-age (SGA) infants born very preterm. MRI was performed in very preterm infants in early life and repeated at term-equivalent age, showing that the trajectory of anterior hippocampal growth was significantly reduced in SGA infants (n = 20) compared to appropriate-for-gestational age (n = 139) infants. Within the SGA infant cohort, reduced anterior hippocampal volume was significantly associated with lower Bayley Cognitive Composite scores at 18 months corrected age, controlling for gestational age at birth and infant sex. Together, these findings demonstrate that the trajectory of hippocampal growth is significantly impaired in SGA/FGR infants, caused by disturbed neuronal dendritogenesis that is programmed by an adverse fetal environment and persists, or worsens, after birth. Results in the clinical cohort provide the critical link between programming of reduced dendritogenesis, hippocampal volume deficit and cognitive dysfunction in SGA infants.

papers.title: A novel mouse model of cerebral microbleeds by targeted Col4a1 editing in adult brain microvessels.
papers.authors: Kim H, Seo Y, Kho H, Singh SS, Lee J, Lee H, Hwang JW, Riew TR, Koh S, Choi JY, Roh HW, Son SJ, Kim GT, Cho SK, Jin HS, Jeong SY, Lee KI, Lee JY, Kim BG.
papers.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease is a leading cause of cognitive decline and stroke in the elderly, with cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) serving as a key imaging biomarker. Despite their clinical significance, the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying cerebral small vessel disease remain poorly understood owing to a lack of appropriate animal models. We performed targeted deletion of Col4a1 in brain microvessels of adult mice using brain endothelium-specific adeno-associated virus (AAV)-BR1 vectors with clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/CRISPR-associated protein 9 (CRISPR/Cas9). Eight-week-old Cas9 transgenic mice received retro-orbital injections of AAV-BR1 containing single guide RNA (sgRNA) targeting Col4a1 or control Rosa26 sequences. Animals underwent longitudinal behavioural testing, including novel object recognition, Y-maze and rotarod tests, over 6 months. Brain pathology was assessed using T2*-weighted MRI, histological analysis and electron microscopy. For human studies, we analysed MRI and genomic data from 836 participants from the BICWALZS biobank, examining associations between genetic variants and CMB burden using linear regression and χ2 analyses. T2*-weighted MRI revealed numerous CMBs with distributions remarkably similar to human CMBs, appearing within 3 months post-injection. CMB burden increased progressively over 6 months in a dose-dependent manner. Behaviourally, mice exhibited progressive cognitive decline and motor incoordination. Histological examinations revealed haemosiderin deposits corresponding to MRI-detected CMBs, without macroscopic intracerebral haemorrhage or white matter changes. Ultrastructural analysis demonstrated significant basement membrane thinning in Col4a1-depleted microvessels. CMB accumulation was associated with widespread astrocytic reactivity extending beyond microbleed sites, whereas microglial activation remained localized. In human subjects, we identified significant associations between four genetic variants of TIMP2, an endogenous inhibitor of the matrix-degrading enzyme MMP2 and CMB burden, with odds ratios of 1.50-1.96 for increased microbleed susceptibility. This work provides the first animal model demonstrating that selective disruption of collagen IV in adult brain microvessels is sufficient to generate CMBs with high penetrance and dose-dependent tunability. Our findings establish that basement membrane integrity is critical for preventing microbleed formation and suggest that dysregulated collagen IV homeostasis underlies sporadic human CMB development.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究旨在解决脑小血管病缺乏合适动物模型、微出血机制不清的问题，通过脑内皮特异性AAV联合CRISPR/Cas9在成年小鼠脑微血管中靶向敲除Col4a1，并结合行为学、影像与组织学检查，同时分析人群遗传数据。结果显示，敲除后小鼠在数月内出现分布与人类相似的脑微出血，且随敲除剂量递增，伴随进行性认知下降和运动失调；组织学见相应含铁血黄素沉积，超微结构显示基底膜变薄，星形胶质细胞反应范围超出出血灶。人群数据中，TIMP2的若干遗传变异与微出血负荷相关。作者据此提出，基底膜完整性对防止微出血形成至关重要，胶原IV稳态失调可能参与散发性人类微出血的发生；这些关联性证据尚不能确立因果关系。

papers.title: Study of blood linear RNA nominates CD55 and DLD as early-stage biomarkers for Parkinson's disease.
papers.authors: Beric A, Sahin S, Sanchez S, Yang Z, Kumar R, Alfradique-Dunham I, Sanford J, Western D, Phillips B, Budde JP, Perrin RJ, Kotzbauer PT, Perlmutter JS, Norris SA, Cruchaga C, Ibanez L.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second leading neurodegenerative disease, pathologically characterized by the accumulation of alpha-synuclein in the brain and the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. Despite the intensive efforts to identify diagnostic biomarkers for PD and nominating prospective candidates such as such as CSF α-synuclein seed amplification assay or α-/β-synuclein ratio, establishment of minimally invasive biomarkers remains the focus of PD research. We leveraged transcriptomic data from 4343 participants from four independent datasets to robustly identify PD-associated transcripts. Following the differential abundance analyses, we integrated our findings with several brain transcriptomic, CSF proteomic, plasma proteomic and genomic data to add biological context. We further leveraged our findings to develop predictive models that could differentiate between PD and healthy controls. We identified 296 differentially expressed transcripts, 28 of which were transcribed from known PD-associated loci. Furthermore, we found a significant overlap between our findings and transcripts dysregulated in brain, as well as proteins that differentially accumulate in CSF. Our results suggested that expression of the identified transcripts was affected by genetic background, including ancestry and PD-related mutations, and nearly half of the identified transcripts were dysregulated before symptom onset. The differentially expressed transcripts were utilized to develop three predictive models that distinguished PD from healthy controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.727-0.733. The predictive models detected transcriptomic PD signatures even before symptom onset. Overall, two transcripts, DLD and CD55, showed particular promise as early stage, minimally invasive PD biomarkers. DLD was significantly related to PD in the expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) analyses, and we identified a putative eQTL for CD55. Their protein products differentially accumulated in CSF, and both DLD and CD55 were included in all three predictive models. Having performed the largest transcriptomic study of PD to date, we demonstrate that the transcriptome can be leveraged to develop minimally invasive biomarkers that may aid in diagnosing the disease.
keywords: Parkinson’s Disease; Blood Transcriptomics; Cd55; Dld; Biomarkers

papers.title: Extracardiac imaging biomarkers of cardiovascular health: a comprehensive review.
papers.authors: Ahn WJ, Choi IY, Shim E, Yeom SK, Hwang SH, Yong HS, Lee YH, Kim C.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading global cause of morbidity and mortality. Beyond clinical risk factors and cardiac imaging, extracardiac imaging biomarkers provide complementary insight into cardiometabolic health. Routine non-cardiac imaging often depicts the liver, kidneys, pancreas, lung, brain, adipose tissue, muscle, vasculature, breast, and bone, enabling opportunistic risk assessment. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), detectable on MRI, CT, and ultrasound, independently predicts major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Chronic kidney disease-related markers including kidney size, vascular calcification, and renal resistive index also correlate with adverse outcomes. Reduced pancreas volume is similarly associated with cardiovascular disease. CT-quantified emphysema and lung hyperinflation are associated with coronary artery disease and cardiovascular mortality. Cerebral small vessel disease markers, such as white matter hyperintensities and silent brain infarcts, demonstrate associations with cardiovascular events. Ectopic adiposity and sarcopenia quantified by CT, MRI, and ultrasound add prognostic value beyond body mass index. Extracardiac vascular and skeletal biomarkers, such as breast arterial calcification and low bone mineral density, further associate with cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Collectively, these markers improve risk stratification and enable screening without added cost or radiation. Future priorities include standardization, external validation, and integration into risk prediction models to advance precision cardiovascular medicine.
papers.summary_zh: 该综述梳理了心脏以外器官的影像生物标志物与心血管健康之间的关联，涵盖肝脏、肾脏、胰腺、肺、脑、脂肪组织、肌肉、血管、乳腺和骨骼等常规非心脏影像可见的结构。作者指出，脂肪肝、肾脏相关指标、胰腺体积减小、肺气肿与肺过度充气、脑小血管病标志、异位脂肪与肌少症，以及乳腺动脉钙化和低骨密度等，均与心血管事件或死亡风险相关，并可能在不增加费用或辐射的情况下改善风险分层。文章强调，这些多为关联性证据，未来需推进标准化、外部验证并纳入风险预测模型。

papers.title: BRAINet: a brain-region-aware interaction network for EEG-based diagnosis of disorders of consciousness.
papers.authors: Chen H, Zhao S, Yu J, Wang J, Bai Y, Xu C, Li S, Luo B, Pan G.
papers.abstract: Objective. Reliable assessment and stratification of disorders of consciousness (DOC) is essential for patient care and clinical treatment planning. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive approach to measure neural activity and has shown promise in DOC assessment. However, most existing EEG-based approaches focus on binary unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS)/minimally conscious state (MCS) classification and often process EEG channels as a whole, without explicitly modeling anatomical brain-region organization. In this study, our goal is to distinguish among UWS, minimally conscious state minus (MCS), and minimally conscious state plus (MCS) using resting-state EEG signals.Approach. We propose BRAINet, a brain-region-aware EEG framework for three-class DOC classification. BRAINet partitions EEG channels into five anatomical brain regions, extracts region-specific spatiotemporal and spectral features, models cross-region interactions using a Transformer-based attention module, and fuses the learned representations with approximate entropy features for final classification. We evaluated BRAINet on a clinical resting-state EEG dataset comprising 22 UWS, 24 MCS, and 15 MCSpatients using patient-wise five-fold cross-validation and comparisons with representative machine-learning and deep-learning baselines. Statistical comparisons were based on paired patient-level out-of-fold (OOF) predictions.Main results. BRAINet achieved the highest numerical performance among the compared methods. Across the five folds, its mean balanced accuracy (BA) was 54.07% at the epoch level and 59.89% at the subject level. Based on pooled patient-level OOF predictions, BRAINet achieved significantly higher BA than the best-performing baseline, Conformer (two-sided paired permutation test, Holm-adjusted).Significance. These results suggest that brain-region-aware EEG modeling may provide useful information for fine-grained UWS/MCS/MCSclassification. BRAINet provides an interpretable framework for exploring region-specific EEG representations in DOC and may support future studies on patient stratification and prognostic assessment.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究针对意识障碍（DOC）的细粒度分层问题，提出BRAINet框架，将静息态脑电通道按五个解剖脑区划分，分别提取时空与频谱特征，并用基于Transformer的注意力模块建模跨脑区交互，再融合近似熵特征，以区分无反应觉醒综合征、微意识状态减和微意识状态加三类患者。在临床静息态脑电数据上采用患者级交叉验证并与代表性机器学习和深度学习基线比较，BRAINet取得了数值上最高的平均平衡准确率，且基于汇总的患者级折外预测，其平衡准确率显著高于表现最好的基线Conformer。作者认为，脑区感知的脑电建模可为细粒度意识障碍分类提供有用信息，并提供一个可解释的框架，供后续患者分层与预后评估研究参考；但当前准确率水平仍有限，其临床效用尚待进一步验证。

papers.title: Atypical late neurosyphilis presenting as status epilepticus: diagnostic and screening implications.
papers.authors: Pollet S, Ernon L, Meeuwissen J, Boogaerts H, Willaert X, Oris E, Fivez T, Hubloue I, Boer W.
papers.abstract: Objectives Neurosyphilis is a serious complication of poorly treated syphilis due to Treponema pallidum invasion of the central nervous system. Symptoms vary from silent infection to severe neurological deficits. Despite progress in diagnostics and treatment, the diagnosis is frequently missed because it is not considered, particularly in atypical presentations and in patients with no evident risk factor. . Methods A 45-year-old man presented with confusion, speech difficulties, and left-sided weakness following subtle behavioral changes. In the emergency department, he had a witnessed focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizure starting with head deviation to the left and tonic posturing of the left arm. Brain CT was normal, while MRI revealed right thalamic and bilateral temporal FLAIR hyperintensities with diffusion restriction in the thalamus.
